lessons.relational_outflow: Relieve someone of a hasty commitment they made under stress, telling them graciously, 'Please don't worry about that—take care of yourself.'
lessons.stillness_communion: Like the olive tree content to pour out soothing oil and the fig tree content to bear quiet sweetness, you do not have to chase status or applause. Simply rest in the gentle, life-giving gifts God has planted right inside your life.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Father, free me from chasing comparison or applause today, and let me rest in the quiet place You gave me.
lessons.visual_prompt: an open stone threshold gate looking out over the rugged hills of Gilead with a silent tambourine resting on the step

lessons.title: Tend the quiet health of your heart above outward gifting
lessons.scripture_text: And she said, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And he awoke out of his sleep, and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he wist not that the Lord was departed from him.
lessons.lesson: Being impressive on the outside cannot sustain us if our inner spirit is running on empty; God cares far more about our heart than our performance.
lessons.application: Step back from trying to power through on sheer willpower today, and spend a few quiet minutes letting God refresh your inner life.
lessons.relational_outflow: Check in on a high-performing friend or colleague who always seems strong, asking how they are truly holding up on the inside.
lessons.stillness_communion: GodNever needs you to make rash promises or grand bargains to win His help. He is already on your side out of pure fatherly love; simply bring Him your honest, simple 'yes' and let your heart rest.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Lord, I let go of trying to bargain or over-promise, resting simply in Your unearned kindness.
lessons.visual_prompt: a wooden loom pin and severed linen cords lying across a stone floor beside a bronze razor

lessons.title: Guard the peaceful boundaries that protect your soul
lessons.scripture_text: And it came to pass, when she pressed him daily with her words, and urged him, so that his soul was vexed unto death; That he told her all his heart...
lessons.lesson: Walking in love does not mean letting persistent pressure wear away your peace and convictions; healthy boundaries protect the heart God gave you.
lessons.application: Give yourself permission today to say a calm, kind 'no' to a pressure or dynamic that drains your spirit.
lessons.relational_outflow: Respect someone else's 'no' or boundary today immediately and warmly, without making them feel guilty or pressured to explain.
lessons.stillness_communion: Have you ever seen a harsh word untangle a knotted heart? Neither has heaven. Let a soft, unhurried tone be your shelter today—watching how gently a peaceful answer melts the frost out of tense rooms.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Father, place a gentle, unhurried calm on my lips today whenever tension arises.
lessons.visual_prompt: seven braided locks of hair resting beside a pair of bronze shears on a carved stone window ledge

lessons.title: Anchor your heart in God's steady truth when life feels adrift
lessons.scripture_text: In those days there was no king in Israel, but every man did that which was right in his own eyes.
lessons.lesson: Relying only on our shifting moods leaves us exhausted and lost; God's timeless wisdom gives us a steady compass we can trust.
lessons.application: When your feelings feel tossed around today, anchor your heart in one unchanging promise of God's character.
lessons.relational_outflow: Offer a calm, steady listening ear to someone who is feeling confused or pulled in many directions this week.
lessons.stillness_communion: Wait before you let exhaustion or loneliness push you toward a choice that drains your peace. Your heart is a sacred sanctuary where God's Spirit dwells—treat your tired soul with the gentle care it deserves today.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Lord, protect my tired heart today and surround me with voices that refresh my peace.
lessons.visual_prompt: a crooked dry-stone boundary wall winding unevenly across a rocky hillside without a plumb line

lessons.title: Remember that it is never too late to cry out to God
lessons.scripture_text: And Samson called unto the Lord, and said, O Lord God, remember me, I pray thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once...
lessons.lesson: No matter how many times we have stumbled or how much we feel we have wasted, God's mercy leans in the moment we turn back to Him.
lessons.application: Bring any regret or sense of failure honestly to God today, trusting that His grace can still write redemption into your story.
lessons.relational_outflow: Extend warm, second-chance grace to someone who has let you down in the past, welcoming them without coldness.
lessons.stillness_communion: When we have to be the sole authority over every outcome in our lives, the weight becomes exhausting. What a relief to hand the scepter back to our gentle Shepherd-King and let His wisdom guide the road ahead.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Father, I hand the reins of my day back to You; lead me with Your gentle shepherd's wisdom.
lessons.visual_prompt: a solitary figure seen strictly from the back standing between two massive carved stone temple pillars

books.bookOverview: Set in the dark days of the Judges, Ruth is a beautiful story of sacrificial love (hesed), loyalty, and redemption. Ruth, a Moabite widow, commits herself to her mother-in-law Naomi and the God of Israel. Through Boaz, a godly kinsman-redeemer, Ruth is brought into the covenant community and becomes the great-grandmother of King David and an ancestor of Jesus Christ.
books.visualCaption: two robed women seen strictly from the back walking side by side along a dusty road winding toward the hills of Bethlehem

lessons.title: Walk faithfully beside loved ones in seasons of grief
lessons.scripture_text: And Ruth said, Intreat me not to leave thee, or to return from following after thee: for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God:
lessons.lesson: The deepest gift we can offer someone in heartbreak is not a quick fix, but the quiet, loyal presence that says, 'You will not walk alone.'
lessons.application: When someone you love is hurting, let go of the pressure to find perfect words and simply offer your steady, unhurried companionship.
lessons.relational_outflow: Reach out to someone walking through grief or loneliness today with a simple note: 'No need to reply—just wanted you to know I'm with you.'
lessons.stillness_communion: When someone you love is walking through a season of grief, they rarely need a speech—they just need the warmth of a hand that won't let go. And in the very same way, your Savior whispers to your own aching heart: 'Where you go, I am right there with you.'
lessons.quiet_prayer: Lord, thank You that in my loneliest valleys, You never turn back and never leave my side.
lessons.visual_prompt: two robed women seen strictly from the back walking side by side along a dusty road winding toward the hills of Bethlehem

lessons.title: Embrace humble beginnings with quiet hope
lessons.scripture_text: And Ruth the Moabitess said unto Naomi, Let me now go to the field, and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace.
lessons.lesson: God often meets us in the ordinary, unglamorous work of gleaning one small handful at a time, turning humble faithfulness into unexpected provision.
lessons.application: Do the small, humble task in front of you today with a peaceful heart, trusting that God notices and blesses quiet beginnings.
lessons.relational_outflow: Offer a word of sincere encouragement to someone who is starting over or working hard in an entry-level or humble role.
lessons.stillness_communion: Notice how Naomi poured out her raw, unvarnished heartache at the town gate—and how God still wove a harvest of joy around her life before the book was done. Your tears never scare God away; He holds them tenderly while preparing new mornings.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Father, hold my honest grief today without rushing me, and gently tend the seeds of future joy.
lessons.visual_prompt: loose stalks of golden barley gathered into a woven basket at the edge of a sunlit stone-walled harvest field

lessons.title: Create a shelter of kindness and dignity for those around you
lessons.scripture_text: And, behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem, and said unto the reapers, The Lord be with you... Have I not charged the young men that they shall not touch thee?
lessons.lesson: Like Boaz in the harvest field, we reflect God's heart whenever we use our voice and resources to make others feel safe, respected, and cared for.
lessons.application: Look around your daily environment today and ask how your presence can make the space feel warmer and safer for others.
lessons.relational_outflow: Go out of your way today to make things easier for someone working alongside you—fetching them a drink, sharing a tool, or speaking up for their comfort.
lessons.stillness_communion: Just as Boaz stepped into the warm barley field with a blessing on his lips for the harvesters, your words carry the power to change the weather inside a room. Let quiet kindness be the breeze that follows you today.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Lord, let my presence and my words bring a breath of warmth and kindness wherever I walk today.
lessons.visual_prompt: drawn clay water jars resting in the shade of a wooden field shelter beside sheaves of harvested grain

lessons.title: Trust that quiet kindness leaves a lasting fragrance
lessons.scripture_text: And Boaz answered and said unto her, It hath fully been shewed me, all that thou hast done unto thy mother in law since the death of thine husband...
lessons.lesson: You never have to boast or campaign for yourself; tender loyalty and quiet goodness naturally shine in due time.
lessons.application: Rest from trying to manage how others see you today, and simply enjoy doing small kindnesses before the eyes of God.
lessons.relational_outflow: Tell someone specifically about a quiet act of kindness or faithfulness you noticed them do recently.
lessons.stillness_communion: You never have to campaign to be noticed or worry that your quiet sacrifices have been overlooked. Every unseen cup of cold water, every patient kindness you have shown in secret, is treasured deeply by your Father.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Father, quiet my need to be seen by the crowd, knowing that every small kindness is treasured by You.
lessons.visual_prompt: a bowl of parched grain and dipped flatbread resting on a flat stone bench beside a bundle of gleaned barley

lessons.title: Find your refuge beneath the shelter of God's wings
lessons.scripture_text: The Lord recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the Lord God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust.
lessons.lesson: When life feels exposed and uncertain, God invites us to tuck our weary hearts beneath the warm, protective shelter of His wings.
lessons.application: Pause today to picture yourself resting safely beneath the wings of God, letting your shoulders drop and your breathing slow.
lessons.relational_outflow: Speak a prayer or word of comfort over someone who is feeling vulnerable or anxious about their future.
lessons.stillness_communion: When the winds of life feel sharp and you feel exposed, picture yourself tucked safely beneath the warm, feathered wings of the Almighty. Here in the shadow of His wings, nothing can snatch away your peace; let your breathing slow.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Lord, tuck my weary heart beneath the warm shelter of Your wings today and let me rest.
lessons.visual_prompt: a mother dove with outstretched wings sheltering a nest tucked into a stone wall overlooking terraced fields

lessons.title: Welcome the gentle wisdom of those who love you well
lessons.scripture_text: Then Naomi her mother in law said unto her, My daughter, shall I not seek rest for thee, that it may be well with thee?
lessons.lesson: When we are navigating unfamiliar crossroads, listening to the seasoned, loving counsel of a trusted mentor brings steadiness and peace.
lessons.application: Instead of carrying a big decision all by yourself this week, invite a wise, trusted voice into the conversation.
lessons.relational_outflow: Thank a mentor, parent, or wise friend for a piece of advice they gave you that helped guide your path.
lessons.stillness_communion: You were never meant to puzzle through every major crossroad inside your own head alone. God often speaks His most comforting clarity through the gentle, seasoned voice of someone who loves you and wants rest for your soul.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Father, thank You for wise, loving voices in my life that help guide my feet toward peace.
lessons.visual_prompt: a clay flask of fragrant olive oil and a folded woven cloak resting on a wooden bench inside a quiet cottage

lessons.title: Cherish quiet integrity and tenderness of heart
lessons.scripture_text: And now, my daughter, fear not; I will do to thee all that thou requirest: for all the city of my people doth know that thou art a virtuous woman.
lessons.lesson: In a world fixated on outward polish and flash, God treasures the quiet beauty of a loyal, kind, and trustworthy heart.
lessons.application: Remind yourself today that your gentleness, faithfulness, and integrity are of great worth in the sight of God.
lessons.relational_outflow: Compliment a spouse, child, or friend today on a quality of their heart—their patience, loyalty, or compassion—rather than outward appearance.
lessons.stillness_communion: In a noisy world that measures outward shine, heaven gazes with delight on a quiet, gentle, and faithful heart. Your tenderness is not weakness—it is a rare and precious beauty in the eyes of the King.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Lord, help me treasure quiet faithfulness and gentleness of heart above all the noise of the world.
lessons.visual_prompt: a winnowing fork and a neat heap of golden barley on a circular stone threshing floor under a starry dusk sky

lessons.title: Honor the right way forward without rushing the outcome
lessons.scripture_text: And now it is true that I am thy near kinsman: howbeit there is a kinsman nearer than I. Tarry this night, and it shall be in the morning, that if he will perform unto thee the part of a kinsman, well...
lessons.lesson: Even when our hearts are eager for a good thing, walking with integrity means trusting God enough not to force or shortcut the process.
lessons.application: When you feel tempted to rush an outcome today, breathe slowly and trust that doing things honorably will protect everyone's peace.
lessons.relational_outflow: Keep a commitment or boundary transparently with someone today so they know they can trust your word completely.
lessons.stillness_communion: Hear Naomi's peaceful counsel: 'Sit still, my daughter, until you know how the matter will fall.' When you have done what love asked of you today, you can sit back quietly—your Redeemer will not rest until He finishes what concerns you.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Father, I have placed this matter in Your hands; help me sit still and rest while You work.
lessons.visual_prompt: six generous measures of barley tied inside a woven shawl resting beside a stone doorway at first morning light

lessons.title: Step in with generous love to lift someone's burden
lessons.scripture_text: And Boaz said unto the elders, and unto all the people, Ye are witnesses this day, that I have bought all that was Elimelech's... Moreover Ruth the Moabitess... have I purchased to be my wife...
lessons.lesson: The highest joy of having strength, margin, or resources is using them as a kinsman-redeemer to restore hope to someone who is hurting.
lessons.application: Ask God today to show you how the blessings in your hands can become a shelter of relief for someone else.
lessons.relational_outflow: Step in to cover a cost, run an errand, or lift a practical burden for someone who is stretched thin this week.
lessons.stillness_communion: Notice how Boaz instructed the reapers to intentionally let extra handfuls of golden barley fall onto the path for Ruth. That is how your Father provides for you—dropping unexpected handfuls of grace right along your ordinary road.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Lord, open my eyes to notice the extra handfuls of grace You have tucked along my path today.
lessons.visual_prompt: a single leather sandal removed and placed on a stone bench under the archway of the Bethlehem city gate

lessons.title: Trust God to turn empty seasons into fullness and joy
lessons.scripture_text: And the women said unto Naomi, Blessed be the Lord, which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman... And they called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
lessons.lesson: The story of Ruth reminds us that bitter winters of loss are not the end; God can quietly weave new life and joy out of our emptiest chapters.
lessons.application: If your hands or heart feel empty in a certain area today, hold them open to God in quiet hope for what He is still writing.
lessons.relational_outflow: Share a story of hope or bring a small sign of care to someone who has been walking through a long season of loss.
lessons.stillness_communion: Who could have guessed that Ruth's quiet gleaning in a dusty corner of Bethlehem was weaving the family line of King David and the Messiah? Never call your today small—God weaves eternal beauty out of ordinary, faithful afternoons.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Father, thank You that even my smallest, quietest days are woven into Your larger story of love.
lessons.visual_prompt: a carved wooden cradle resting beside a full sheaf of wheat in a sunlit stone courtyard

books.bookOverview: 1 Samuel records the transition of Israel from the period of the Judges to the Monarchy. Centered on three key figures—Samuel (the faithful prophet), Saul (the insecure king who disobeyed), and David (the humble shepherd chosen by God)—the book contrasts pride and half-hearted obedience with a heart fully committed to the Lord.
books.visualCaption: a robed woman seen strictly from the back kneeling in quiet prayer at the stone entrance post of the Shiloh tabernacle

lessons.title: Pour out your unfiltered tears before a tender Father
lessons.scripture_text: And Hannah answered and said, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit... but have poured out my soul before the Lord.
lessons.lesson: God never asks you to put on a brave, stoic mask in prayer; like Hannah, you can bring your raw, weeping heart straight into His presence.
lessons.application: Give yourself permission today to pray without polished words, pouring out whatever is genuinely weighing on your heart.
lessons.relational_outflow: Sit gently with someone who is sad or overwhelmed today without trying to cheer them up prematurely or rush past their tears.
lessons.stillness_communion: Like Hannah kneeling silently at the temple pillar with tears on her cheeks, you do not need polished sentences for God to hear you. Even when your prayer is just a quiet sigh that no one else understands, your Father hears every syllable of your heart.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Lord, receive the quiet, unspoken sighs of my heart today and wrap me in Your peace.
lessons.visual_prompt: a robed woman seen strictly from the back kneeling in quiet prayer at the stone entrance post of the Shiloh tabernacle

lessons.title: Make quiet space to listen for God's gentle voice
lessons.scripture_text: And the Lord came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.
lessons.lesson: God's guidance rarely shouts over the noise; it meets us when we slow down and whisper, 'Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.'
lessons.application: Begin or end your day with two minutes of unhurried silence, simply resting in God's presence without an agenda.
lessons.relational_outflow: Listen to someone in your life today with complete stillness—without interrupting, checking your phone, or planning your reply.
lessons.stillness_communion: Wait in the stillness before the dawn and whisper, 'Speak, Lord, for Your servant is listening.' God's voice rarely shouts over the storm; He speaks in a gentle, reassuring murmur to the heart that simply pauses to be near Him.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Father, quiet the noise around me and within me today so I can hear Your gentle whisper.
lessons.visual_prompt: a burning seven-branched golden lampstand casting soft light beside a simple linen sleeping mat inside a quiet sanctuary

lessons.title: Look past outward polish to see the heart as God does
lessons.scripture_text: For the Lord seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart.
lessons.lesson: We are easily impressed by credentials and appearances, while God looks with tender affection upon the quiet, humble heart.
lessons.application: Release the pressure to curate an impressive exterior today, knowing God looks upon your heart with love.
lessons.relational_outflow: Look past someone's awkwardness or rough exterior today and show them warm, unhurried kindness.
lessons.stillness_communion: Set down the stone of remembrance and whisper over your life: 'Thus far the Lord has helped us.' You may not see every bend in the road ahead, but look how faithfully He has carried you to this exact morning.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Lord, I pause to thank You today: through every twist and turn, thus far You have carried me.

lessons.title: Offer God a responsive heart rather than hollow busyness
lessons.scripture_text: Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
lessons.lesson: God never wants us to burn ourselves out in impressive religious or work routines while our hearts stay distant from Him.
lessons.application: Slow down today and offer God your honest, listening heart rather than trying to earn His favor through busyness.
lessons.relational_outflow: Let someone off the hook from an obligation or formality today so you can simply enjoy genuine connection with them.
lessons.stillness_communion: When panic whispers that you have to force a solution right this second, take a slow step back and breathe. Waiting for God's peace is never wasted time—His timing always protects your heart better than hurried control ever could.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Father, calm the urgency inside me today and help me wait peacefully for Your timing.

lessons.title: Step forward in your own simple gifts, trusting God's strength
lessons.scripture_text: Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts...
lessons.lesson: Like David setting aside Saul's heavy armor, you don't have to imitate someone else's strength; God meets you right in who He made you to be.
lessons.application: Lay down the exhausting armor of trying to be someone else today, and bring your simple, honest self to the task in front of you.
lessons.relational_outflow: Encourage a child, friend, or coworker to trust their own unique voice and strengths rather than comparing themselves to others.
lessons.stillness_communion: What a freeing truth: while the world scans outward polish, credentials, and appearances, the Lord gazes tenderly upon the heart. You don't have to curate an image for God today—come just as you are.
lessons.quiet_prayer: Lord, thank You that I never have to impress You outwardly; You see and love my honest heart.

lessons.title: Cultivate loyal, soul-strengthening friendship

lessons.title: Let gratitude quiet the ache of comparison

lessons.quiet_prayer: Lord, quiet the ache of comparison in my heart and fill me with gratitude for my own story with You.

lessons.title: Wait peacefully for God's timing rather than forcing your way

lessons.lesson: When we trust that our lives are held in God's hands, we don't have to grasp, manipulate, or hurt others to get ahead.

lessons.title: Strengthen your weary heart in God's love when all else fails
lessons.scripture_text: And David was greatly distressed; for the people spake of stoning him... but David encouraged himself in the Lord his God.
lessons.lesson: When everything around you feels depleted and everyone is exhausted, you can still lean directly into God's unfailing love to find fresh strength.
lessons.application: If today feels especially heavy, pause to comfort your own heart with the truth that God's love for you has not wavered.
lessons.relational_outflow: Reach out to someone who has had a discouraging week and speak one warm, steadying promise of hope into their day.
lessons.stillness_communion: When the camp is in ashes, everyone around you is exhausted, and there is no human shoulder left to lean on, you can still lean directly against the chest of your God. Right there in the rubble, His unfailing love will steady your breath again.

books.bookOverview: 2 Samuel chronicles the reign of King David—his triumphs in uniting the kingdom and establishing Jerusalem, God's eternal covenant with his line (2 Sam 7), his tragic moral collapse with Bathsheba, and the devastating personal and national consequences that followed. books.bookOverview: Nahum serves as the sequel to Jonah, prophesying the final, irreversible destruction of Nineveh (the brutal Assyrian empire) roughly a century later. Nahum proclaims God's holy vengeance against violent oppressors, comforting the oppressed with the assurance that evil has an expiration date and that 'the Lord is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble.'
keyThemes: God as an Avenging Judge Against Cruelty

The Lord as a Stronghold in Trouble
Good News of Peace for the Oppressed

books.bookOverview: Habakkuk wrestles honestly with the problem of evil: why does God tolerate injustice in Judah, and how can He use the even more wicked Babylonians to judge them? keyThemes: The Just Shall Live by Faith (Hab 2:4)

GEN.1.word_stat: BSB / KJV Chapter Fact: Genesis 1 spans 31 verses (750 words), anchored by the recurring theme of “light” (appearing 8 times in this chapter).
overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1, 2), the first verse of the Bible gives us a satisfying and useful account of the origin of the earth and the heavens. The faith of humble Christians understands this better than the fancy of the most learned men.¹ God said, Let there be light; he willed it, and at once there was light. (vv. 3–5).²

As the chapter unfolds (v. 31), when we come to think about our works, we find, to our shame, that much has been very bad; but when God saw his work, all was very good. Good, for it was all just as the Creator would have it to be.³ All beginnings must begin with God. Always put God first.⁴

2. Matthew Henry (1706, PD) on Genesis 1 (Verses 1, 2) — The first verse of the Bible gives us a satisfying and useful account of the origin of the earth and the heavens.
3. Matthew Henry (1706, PD) on Genesis 1 (Verse 31) — When we come to think about our works, we find, to our shame, that much has been very bad; but when God saw his work, all was very good.
4. F.B. Meyer’s Through the Bible Day by Day (1914, PD) on Genesis 1 (Beginnings -- Genesis 1:1-5).

GEN.2.word_stat: BSB / KJV Chapter Fact: Genesis 2 spans 25 verses (608 words), anchored by the recurring theme of “life” (appearing 2 times in this chapter).
overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1–3), after six days, God ceased from all works of creation. In miracles, he has overruled nature, but never changed its settled course, or added to it.¹ Here is a name given to the Creator, “the Lord.” Where the word “LORD” is printed in capital letters in our English Bibles, in the original it is “the Lord.” the Lord is that name of God, which denotes that he alone has his being of himself, and that he gives being to all creatures and things. (vv. 4–7).²

As the chapter unfolds (vv. 18–25), power over the creatures was given to man, and as a proof of this he named them all. It also shows his insight into the works of God.³ God’s Rest was not from weariness, or exhaustion, but because His work of Creation was finished. He is ever at work, remember John 5:17.⁴

GEN.3.word_stat: BSB / KJV Chapter Fact: Genesis 3 spans 24 verses (664 words), anchored by the recurring theme of “life” (appearing 4 times in this chapter).
overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1–5), Satan assaulted our first parents, to draw them to sin, and the temptation proved fatal to them. The tempter was the devil, in the shape and likeness of a serpent.¹ Observe the steps of the transgression: not steps upward, but downward toward the pit. (vv. 6–8).²

As the chapter unfolds (vv. 22–24), God sent humanity out; told him he should no longer occupy and enjoy that garden: but man liked the place, and was unwilling to leave it, therefore God made him go out. This signified the shutting out of him, and all his guilty race, from that communion with God, which was the bliss and glory of paradise.³ Human love is God’s best gift to man. Without it even Eden would not be Paradise.⁴

GEN.4.word_stat: BSB / KJV Chapter Fact: Genesis 4 contains 26 verses (625 words in the Berean Standard Bible).
overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1–7), when Cain was born, Eve said, I have gotten a man from the Lord. Perhaps she thought that this was the promised seed.¹ Malice in the heart ends in murder by the hands. (vv. 8–15).²

As the chapter unfolds (vv. 25, 26), our first parents were comforted in their affliction by the birth of a son, whom they called Seth, that is, ‘set,’ ‘settled,’ or ‘placed;’ in his seed mankind should continue to the end of time, and from him the Messiah should descend. While Cain, the head of the turning away from God, is made a wanderer, Seth, from whom the true church was to come, is one fixed.³ It was good that man should be driven from Eden. Easy comfort alone cannot build a resilient faith.⁴

GEN.5.word_stat: BSB / KJV Chapter Fact: Genesis 5 spans 32 verses (469 words), anchored by the recurring theme of “blessed” (appearing 1 time in this chapter).
overview: Across the long generations from Adam to Noah where every other life closes with the solemn refrain “and he died” (vv. 1–20),¹ Enoch’s story breaks the rhythm twice with a quiet, breathtaking testimony: “Enoch walked with God” (vv. 21–24).²

Walking with God means setting the Lord before us and living under His gracious eye in unhurried communion across ordinary family days.³ Where Cain’s line sought worldly renown, Seth’s line in Enoch reveals that steady, daily companionship with our Creator is the true reality and peace of faith (vv. 25–32).⁴

GEN.6.word_stat: BSB / KJV Chapter Fact: Genesis 6 spans 22 verses (503 words), anchored by the recurring theme of “heart” (appearing 2 times in this chapter).
overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1–7), the most remarkable thing concerning the old world, is the destroying of it by the deluge, or flood. We are told of the abounding iniquity of that wicked world: God's just wrath, and his holy resolution to punish it.¹ Noah did not find favour in the eyes of men; they hated and persecuted him, because both by his life and preaching he condemned the world: but he found grace in the eyes of the Lord, and this made him more truly honourable than the men of renown. (vv. 8–11).²

As the chapter unfolds (v. 22), Noah's faith triumphed over all corrupt reasonings. To rear so large a building, such a one as he never saw, and to provide food for the living creatures, would require from him a great deal of care, and labour, and expense.³ When a son was born to Lamech, he named him Noah, which means “Rest.” He thought that the boy would grow up to share and alleviate the strain of daily toil. But his hope was premature: rest was not yet: the Deluge would soon sweep over the works of men.⁴

GEN.7.word_stat: BSB / KJV Chapter Fact: Genesis 7 spans 24 verses (494 words), anchored by the recurring theme of “life” (appearing 3 times in this chapter).
overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1–12), the call to Noah is very kind, like that of a tender father to his children to come in-doors when he sees night or a storm coming. Noah did not go into the ark till God bade him, though he knew it was to be his place of refuge.¹ The ravenous creatures were made mild and manageable; yet, when this occasion was over, they were of the same kind as before; for the ark did not alter their natures. (vv. 13–16).²

As the chapter unfolds (vv. 21–24), all the men, women, and children, that were in the world, excepting those in the ark, died. We may easily imagine what terror seized them.³ They climbed the highest story of their towers, then to the hills, but the greedy waters followed them, till the last crag was covered, and all living things in the first homes of human life had perished. Equally sudden and unexpected shall be the days of the Son of Man.⁴

overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1–6), the years of the life of Moses are divided into three forties; the first forty he spent as a prince in Pharaoh's court, the second as a shepherd in Midian, the third as a king in Jeshurun. How changeable is the life of man!¹ God notices the afflictions of Israel. (vv. 7–10).²

As the chapter unfolds (vv. 16–22), Moses' success with the elders of Israel would be good. God, who, by his grace, inclines the heart, and opens the ear, could say beforehand, They shall listen closely to your voice; for he would make them willing in this day of power.³ The learning of Egypt was not sufficient to equip Moses for his life-work. He is taken to the solitudes of the wilderness.⁴

overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1–9), Moses objects, that the people would not take his word, unless he showed them some sign. God gives him power to work miracles.¹ Moses continued backward to the work God designed him for; there was much of cowardice, slothfulness, and unbelief in him. (vv. 10–17).²

As the chapter unfolds (vv. 24–31), God met Moses in anger. The Lord threatened him with death or sent sickness upon him, as the punishment of his having neglected to circumcise his son.³ This wonderful chapter tells us how Moses’ three misgivings were tenderly and sufficiently dealt with by his heavenly Friend. To his first misgiving God made answer by giving him three signs.⁴

EXO.6.word_stat: BSB / KJV Chapter Fact: Exodus 6 spans 30 verses (642 words), anchored by the recurring theme of “covenant” (appearing 2 times in this chapter).
overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1–9), we are most likely to prosper in attempts to glorify God, and to be useful to men, when we learn by experience that we can do nothing of ourselves; when our whole dependence is placed on him, and our only expectation is from him. Moses had been expecting what God would do; but now he shall see what he will do.¹ The faith of Moses was so feeble that he could scarcely be kept to his work. (vv. 10–13).²

As the chapter unfolds (vv. 14–30), Moses and Aaron were Israelites; raised up to them of their brothers and sisters, as Christ also should be, who was to be the Prophet and Priest, the Redeemer and Lawgiver of the people of Israel. Moses returns to his narrative, and repeats the charge God had given him to deliver his message to Pharaoh, and his objection against it.³ God’s way is to bring men to an end of themselves before He arises to their help. Our efforts to deliver ourselves only end in increasing our perplexities.⁴

overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1–7), God glorifies himself. He makes people know that he is the Lord.¹ What men dislike, because it opposes their pride and lusts, they will not be convinced of; but it is easy to cause them to believe things they wish to be true. (vv. 8–13).²

EXO.8.word_stat: BSB / KJV Chapter Fact: Exodus 8 spans 32 verses (889 words), anchored by the recurring theme of “pray” (appearing 4 times in this chapter).
overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1–15), Pharaoh is plagued with frogs; their vast numbers made them sore plagues to the Egyptians. God could have plagued Egypt with lions, or bears, or wolves, or with birds of prey, but he chose to do it by these despicable creatures.¹ These lice were produced out of the dust of the earth; out of any part of the creation God can fetch a scourge, with which to correct those who rebel against him. (vv. 16–19).²

As the chapter unfolds (vv. 20–32), Pharaoh was early at his false devotions to the river; and shall we be for more sleep and more slumber, when any service to the Lord is to be done? The Egyptians and the Hebrews were to be marked in the plague of flies.³ Probably the plagues followed in rapid succession, so that the impression of one had not passed away before another succeeded. The whole conflict was probably comprehended in nine or ten months.⁴

overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1–10), in remembrance of the destruction of the first-born of Egypt, both of man and of beast, and the deliverance of the Israelites out of bondage, the first-born males of the Israelites were set apart to the Lord. By this was set before them, that their lives were preserved through the ransom of the atonement, which in due time was to be made for sin.¹ The firstlings of beast not used in sacrifice, were to be changed for others so used, or they were to be destroyed. (vv. 11–16).²

As the chapter unfolds (vv. 21, 22), the Lord went before them in a pillar, or appearance of the Divine Majesty. Christ was with the church in the wilderness, 1Co 10:9.³ Two Hebrew customs dated from the Exodus-first, the dedication of the first-born to God’s service, and second, the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover must be killed. The first-born had been especially redeemed and so were especially God’s.⁴

overview: Hemmed in between Pharaoh’s pursuing chariots behind and the deep waters of the sea ahead (vv. 1–9),¹ Israel cries out in fear until Moses steadies them with one of Scripture’s greatest sanctuary promises: “Do not be afraid. It appears, De 1:22, that the motion to search out the land came from the people.¹ The searchers of the land brought a bunch of grapes with them, and other fruits, as proofs of the goodness of the country; which was to Israel both the earnest and the specimen of all the fruits of Canaan. (vv. 21–25).²

As the chapter unfolds (vv. 26–33), we may wonder that the people of Israel staid forty days for the return of their spies, when they were ready to enter Canaan, under all the assurances of success they could have from the Divine power, and the miracles that had hitherto attended them. But they distrusted God's power and promise.³ By comparing the opening verses with Deuteronomy 1:19-22, it appears that the suggestion about the spies emanated from the people, and that their proposal was graciously acquiesced in by God. But let us remember that it is a profound mistake to spy out or criticize the land or lot into which we are being led.⁴

overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1–6), Job was now sensible of his guilt; he would no longer speak in his own excuse; he abhorred himself as a sinner in heart and life, especially for murmuring against God, and took shame to himself. When the understanding is enlightened by the Spirit of grace, our knowledge of Divine things as far exceeds what we had before, as the sight of the eyes excels report and common fame.¹ After the Lord had convinced and humbled Job, and brought him to repentance, he owned him, comforted him, and put honour upon him. (vv. 7–9).²

As the chapter unfolds (vv. 10–17), in the beginning of this book we had Job's patience under his troubles, for an example; here, for our encouragement to follow that example, we have his happy end. His troubles began in Satan's malice, which God restrained; his restoration began in God's mercy, which Satan could not oppose.³ In complete surrender Job bowed before God, confessing his ignorance and owning that he had spoken glibly of things which he understood not. He had retorted to his friends that he was as good as they, but now he confessed, as did the Apostle after him, that he was of sinners the chief.⁴

overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1–4), seven angels appeared in heaven; prepared to finish the destruction of antichrist. As the measure of Babylon's sins was filled up, it finds the full measure of Divine wrath.¹

As the chapter unfolds (vv. 5–8), in the judgments God executes upon antichrist and his followers, he fulfils the prophecies and promises of his word. These angels are prepared for their work, clothed with pure and white linen, their breasts girded with golden girdles, representing the holiness, and righteousness, and excellence of these dealings with men.³ The imagery in the magnificent scene with which this chapter opens is perhaps borrowed from Pharaoh’s overthrow in the Red Sea, which, as the rich lines of an Eastern dawn illuminated its waters, seemed like a sea of glass mingled with fire. So, beside the crystal sea of Time, from whose surface all traces of storm will have been removed and on which the eternal morning will be breaking, we, who by grace have overcome, shall celebrate the final victory of God.⁴

overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1–7), we are to pray that the will of God may be done on earth as it is done in heaven. Here is a succession of terrible judgments of Providence; and there seems to be an allusion to several of the plagues of Egypt.¹ The heart of man is so desperately wicked, that the most severe miseries never will bring any to repent, without the special grace of God. (vv. 8–11).²

As the chapter unfolds (vv. 17–21), the seventh and last angel poured forth his vial, and the downfal of Babylon was finished. The church triumphant in heaven saw it and rejoiced; the church in conflict on earth saw it and became triumphant.³ It makes us pause to hear that angels, who rejoice over one sinner that repenteth, are employed in these terrible judgments. As the chapter unfolds (vv. 15–18), God so ruled the hearts of these kings, by his power over them, and by his providence, that they did those things, without intending it, which he purposed and foretold. overview: In the opening movement (vv. 1–5), all streams of earthly comfort are muddy; but these are clear, and refreshing. They give life, and preserve life, to those who drink of them, and thus they will flow for evermore.¹ The Lord Jesus spoke by the angel, solemnly confirming the contents of this book, particularly of this last vision. (vv. 6–19).²

As the chapter unfolds (vv. 20, 21), after discovering these things to his people on earth, Christ seems to take leave of them, and return to heaven; but he assures them it shall not be long before he comes again. And while we are busy in the duties of our different stations of life; whatever labours may try us, whatever difficulties may surround us, whatever sorrows may press us down, let us with pleasure hear our Lord proclaiming, Behold, I come quickly; I come to put an end to the labour and suffering of my servants.³ The first five verses of this chapter obviously belong to the preceding one, from which they should not be severed. The ever-flowing river of life proves that the whole life of the blessed depends on the life of God, resident in the enthroned Lamb and communicated through the Holy Spirit.⁴

EXO.1.KJV: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.

EXO.1.PLAIN: and made their lives bitter with hard labor in brick and mortar, and with all kinds of work in the fields. Every service they imposed was harsh.

EXO.1.BSB: Then the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, whose names were Shiphrah and Puah,

EXO.1.PLAIN: Then the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, whose names were Shiphrah and Puah,

EXO.1.BSB: “When you help the Hebrew women give birth, observe them on the birthstools. If the child is a son, kill him; but if it is a daughter, let her live.”
EXO.1.KJV: And he said, When you do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them on the stools; if it be a son, then you shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.
EXO.1.PLAIN: “When you help the Hebrew women give birth, observe them on the birthstools. If the child is a son, kill him; but if it is a daughter, let her live.”

EXO.1.BSB: The midwives, however, feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had instructed; they let the boys live.
EXO.1.KJV: But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive.
EXO.1.PLAIN: The midwives, however, feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had instructed; they let the boys live.

EXO.1.BSB: So the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and asked them, “Why have you done this? Why have you let the boys live?”
EXO.1.KJV: And the king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said to them, Why have you done this thing, and have saved the men children alive?
EXO.1.PLAIN: So the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and asked them, “Why have you done this? Why have you let the boys live?”

EXO.1.BSB: The midwives answered Pharaoh, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women, for they are vigorous and give birth before a midwife arrives.”
EXO.1.KJV: And the midwives said to Pharaoh, Because the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women; for they are lively, and are delivered before the midwives come in to them.
EXO.1.PLAIN: The midwives answered Pharaoh, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women, for they are vigorous and give birth before a midwife arrives.”

EXO.1.BSB: So God was good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and became even more numerous.
EXO.1.KJV: Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty.
EXO.1.PLAIN: So God was good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and became even more numerous.

EXO.1.BSB: And because the midwives feared God, He gave them families of their own.
EXO.1.KJV: And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them houses.
EXO.1.PLAIN: And because the midwives feared God, He gave them families of their own.

EXO.1.BSB: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people: “Every son born to the Hebrews you must throw into the Nile, but every daughter you may allow to live.”
EXO.1.KJV: And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born you shall cast into the river, and every daughter you shall save alive.
EXO.1.PLAIN: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people: “Every son born to the Hebrews you must throw into the Nile, but every daughter you may allow to live.”

EXO.2.BSB: Now a man of the house of Levi married a daughter of Levi,
EXO.2.KJV: And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.
EXO.2.PLAIN: Now a man of the house of Levi married a daughter of Levi,

EXO.2.PLAIN: and she conceived and gave birth to a son. When she saw that he was a beautiful child, she hid him for three months.

EXO.2.BSB: But when she could no longer hide him, she got him a papyrus basket and coated it with tar and pitch. Then she placed the child in the basket and set it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.
EXO.2.KJV: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.
EXO.2.PLAIN: But when she could no longer hide him, she got him a papyrus basket and coated it with tar and pitch. Then she placed the child in the basket and set it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.

EXO.2.BSB: And his sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.
EXO.2.KJV: And his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him. ¶
EXO.2.PLAIN: And his sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.

EXO.2.BSB: Soon the daughter of Pharaoh went down to bathe in the Nile, and her attendants were walking along the riverbank. And when she saw the basket among the reeds, she sent her maidservant to retrieve it.

EXO.2.BSB: When she opened it, she saw the child, and behold, the little boy was crying. So she had compassion on him and said, “This is one of the Hebrew children.”
EXO.2.KJV: And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children.
EXO.2.PLAIN: When she opened it, she saw the child, and look closely — the little boy was crying. So she had compassion on him and said, “This is one of the Hebrew children.”

EXO.2.BSB: Then his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Shall I go and call one of the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?”
EXO.2.KJV: Then said his sister to Pharaoh’s daughter, Shall I go and call to you a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for you?
EXO.2.PLAIN: Then his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Shall I go and call one of the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?”

EXO.2.BSB: “Go ahead,” Pharaoh’s daughter told her. And the girl went and called the boy’s mother.
EXO.2.KJV: And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, Go. And the maid went and called the child’s mother.
EXO.2.PLAIN: “Go ahead,” Pharaoh’s daughter told her. And the girl went and called the boy’s mother.

EXO.2.BSB: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay your wages.” So the woman took the boy and nursed him.
EXO.2.KJV: And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give you your wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.
EXO.2.PLAIN: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay your wages.” So the woman took the boy and nursed him.

EXO.2.BSB: When the child had grown older, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.”
EXO.2.KJV: And the child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water. ¶
EXO.2.PLAIN: When the child had grown older, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.”

EXO.2.BSB: One day, after Moses had grown up, he went out to his own people and observed their hard labor. He saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his own people.
EXO.2.KJV: And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown, that he went out to his brothers, and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brothers.
EXO.2.PLAIN: One day, after Moses had grown up, he went out to his own people and observed their hard labor. He saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his own people.

EXO.2.BSB: After looking this way and that and seeing no one, he struck down the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
EXO.2.KJV: And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
EXO.2.PLAIN: After looking this way and that and seeing no one, he struck down the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.

EXO.2.BSB: The next day Moses went out and saw two Hebrews fighting. He asked the one in the wrong, “Why are you attacking your companion?”
EXO.2.KJV: And when he went out the second day, behold, two men of the Hebrews strove together: and he said to him that did the wrong, Why smite you your fellow?
EXO.2.PLAIN: The next day Moses went out and saw two Hebrews fighting. He asked the one in the wrong, “Why are you attacking your companion?”

EXO.2.BSB: But the man replied, “Who made you ruler and judge over us? Are you planning to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?” Then Moses was afraid and thought, “This thing I have done has surely become known.”
EXO.2.KJV: And he said, Who made you a prince and a judge over us? intend you to kill me, as you killed the Egyptian? And Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is known.
EXO.2.PLAIN: But the man replied, “Who made you ruler and judge over us? Are you planning to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?” Then Moses was afraid and thought, “This thing I have done has surely become known.”

EXO.2.BSB: When Pharaoh heard about this matter, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian, where he sat down beside a well.
EXO.2.KJV: Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelled in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.
EXO.2.PLAIN: When Pharaoh heard about this matter, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian, where he sat down beside a well.

EXO.2.KJV: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.
EXO.2.PLAIN: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came to draw water and fill the troughs to water their father’s flock.

EXO.2.BSB: And when some shepherds came along and drove them away, Moses rose up to help them and watered their flock.
EXO.2.KJV: And the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.
EXO.2.PLAIN: And when some shepherds came along and drove them away, Moses rose up to help them and watered their flock.

EXO.2.BSB: When the daughters returned to their father Reuel, he asked them, “Why have you returned so early today?”
EXO.2.KJV: And when they came to Reuel their father, he said, How is it that you are come so soon to day?
EXO.2.PLAIN: When the daughters returned to their father Reuel, he asked them, “Why have you returned so early today?”

EXO.2.BSB: “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds,” they replied. “He even drew water for us and watered the flock.”
EXO.2.KJV: And they said, An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water enough for us, and watered the flock.

EXO.2.BSB: “So where is he?” their father asked. “Why did you leave the man behind? Invite him to have something to eat.”
EXO.2.KJV: And he said to his daughters, And where is he? why is it that you have left the man? call him, that he may eat bread.
EXO.2.PLAIN: “So where is he?” their father asked. “Why did you leave the man behind? Invite him to have something to eat.”

EXO.2.PLAIN: And she gave birth to a son, and Moses named him Gershom, saying, “I have become a foreigner in a foreign land.”

EXO.2.BSB: After a long time, the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned and cried out under their burden of slavery, and their cry for deliverance from bondage ascended to God.

EXO.2.PLAIN: After a long time, the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned and cried out under their burden of slavery, and their cry for deliverance from bondage ascended to God.

EXO.2.BSB: So God heard their groaning, and He remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

EXO.2.PLAIN: God heard their groaning, and he remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

EXO.2.BSB: God saw the Israelites and took notice.
EXO.2.KJV: And God looked on the children of Israel, and God had respect to them.
EXO.2.PLAIN: God saw the Israelites and took notice.

EXO.3.BSB: Meanwhile, Moses was shepherding the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led the flock to the far side of the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.

EXO.3.PLAIN: There the angel of the Lord appeared to him in a blazing fire from within a bush. Moses saw the bush ablaze with fire, but it was not consumed.

EXO.3.BSB: So Moses thought, “I must go over and see this marvelous sight. Why is the bush not burning up?”
EXO.3.KJV: And Moses said, I will now turn aside, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.

EXO.3.BSB: When the LORD saw that he had gone over to look, God called out to him from within the bush, “Moses, Moses!” “Here I am,” he answered.
EXO.3.KJV: And when the LORD saw that he turned aside to see, God called to him out of the middle of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, Here am I.
EXO.3.PLAIN: When the Lord saw that he had gone over to look, God called out to him from within the bush, “Moses, Moses!” “Here I am,” he answered.

EXO.3.BSB: “Do not come any closer,” God said. “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.”
EXO.3.KJV: And he said, Draw not near here: put off your shoes from off your feet, for the place where on you stand is holy ground.
EXO.3.PLAIN: 'Do not come any closer,' God said. 'Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.'

EXO.3.BSB: Then He said, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” At this, Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.
EXO.3.KJV: Moreover he said, I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. And Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look on God. ¶
EXO.3.PLAIN: Then He said, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” At this, Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.

EXO.3.BSB: The LORD said, “I have indeed seen the affliction of My people in Egypt. I have heard them crying out because of their oppressors, and I am aware of their sufferings.

EXO.3.PLAIN: The Lord said, “I have indeed seen the affliction of My people in Egypt. I have heard them crying out because of their oppressors, and I am aware of their sufferings.

EXO.3.BSB: I have come down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land to a good and spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey—the home of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
EXO.3.KJV: And I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land to a good land and a large, to a land flowing with milk and honey; to the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
EXO.3.PLAIN: I have come down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land to a good and spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey—the home of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

EXO.3.BSB: And now the cry of the Israelites has reached Me, and I have seen how severely the Egyptians are oppressing them.
EXO.3.KJV: Now therefore, behold, the cry of the children of Israel is come to me: and I have also seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them.
EXO.3.PLAIN: And now the cry of the Israelites has reached Me, and I have seen how severely the Egyptians are oppressing them.

EXO.3.BSB: Therefore, go! I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring My people the Israelites out of Egypt.”
EXO.3.KJV: Come now therefore, and I will send you to Pharaoh, that you may bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt. ¶
EXO.3.PLAIN: Therefore, go! I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring My people the Israelites out of Egypt.”

EXO.3.BSB: But Moses asked God, “Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the Israelites out of Egypt?”
EXO.3.KJV: And Moses said to God, Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt?
EXO.3.PLAIN: But Moses asked God, “Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the Israelites out of Egypt?”

EXO.3.BSB: “I will surely be with you,” God said, “and this will be the sign to you that I have sent you: When you have brought the people out of Egypt, all of you will worship God on this mountain.”
EXO.3.KJV: And he said, Certainly I will be with you; and this shall be a token to you, that I have sent you: When you have brought forth the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God on this mountain.
EXO.3.PLAIN: “I will surely be with you,” God said, “and this will be the sign to you that I have sent you: When you have brought the people out of Egypt, all of you will worship God on this mountain.”

EXO.3.BSB: Then Moses asked God, “Suppose I go to the Israelites and say to them, ‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you,’ and they ask me, ‘What is His name?’ What should I tell them?”
EXO.3.KJV: And Moses said to God, Behold, when I come to the children of Israel, and shall say to them, The God of your fathers has sent me to you; and they shall say to me, What is his name? what shall I say to them?

EXO.3.BSB: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM. This is what you are to say to the Israelites: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”

EXO.3.BSB: God also told Moses, “Say to the Israelites, ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.’ This is My name forever, and this is how I am to be remembered in every generation.
EXO.3.KJV: And God said moreover to Moses, Thus shall you say to the children of Israel, the LORD God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you: this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial to all generations.

EXO.3.BSB: Go, assemble the elders of Israel and say to them, ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—has appeared to me and said: I have surely attended to you and have seen what has been done to you in Egypt.
EXO.3.KJV: Go, and gather the elders of Israel together, and say to them, The LORD God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, appeared to me, saying, I have surely visited you, and seen that which is done to you in Egypt:

EXO.4.BSB: “Please, Lord,” Moses replied, “I have never been eloquent, neither in the past nor since You have spoken to Your servant, for I am slow of speech and tongue.”
EXO.4.KJV: And Moses said to the LORD, O my LORD, I am not eloquent, neither heretofore, nor since you have spoken to your servant: but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.

EXO.4.KJV: Now therefore go, and I will be with your mouth, and teach you what you shall say.

EXO.4.KJV: And he said, O my LORD, send, I pray you, by the hand of him whom you will send.
EXO.4.PLAIN: But Moses replied, “Please, Lord, send someone else.”

EXO.4.KJV: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses, and he said, Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he can speak well. And also, behold, he comes forth to meet you: and when he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.
EXO.4.PLAIN: Then the anger of the Lord burned against Moses, and He said, “Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he can speak well, and he is now on his way to meet you. When he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.

EXO.4.KJV: And he shall be your spokesman to the people: and he shall be, even he shall be to you instead of a mouth, and you shall be to him instead of God.
EXO.4.PLAIN: He will speak to the people for you. He will be your spokesman, and it will be as if you were God to him.

EXO.4.BSB: But take this staff in your hand so you can perform signs with it.”
EXO.4.KJV: And you shall take this rod in your hand, with which you shall do signs. ¶
EXO.4.PLAIN: But take this staff in your hand so you can perform signs with it.”

EXO.4.BSB: Then Moses went back to his father-in-law Jethro and said to him, “Please let me return to my brothers in Egypt to see if they are still alive.” “Go in peace,” Jethro replied.
EXO.4.KJV: And Moses went and returned to Jethro his father in law, and said to him, Let me go, I pray you, and return to my brothers which are in Egypt, and see whether they be yet alive. And Jethro said to Moses, Go in peace.
EXO.4.PLAIN: Then Moses went back to his father-in-law Jethro and said to him, “Please let me return to my brothers in Egypt to see if they are still alive.” “Go in peace,” Jethro replied.

EXO.4.KJV: And the LORD said to Moses in Midian, Go, return into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought your life.
EXO.4.PLAIN: Now the Lord had said to Moses in Midian, “Go back to Egypt, for all the men who sought to kill you are dead.”

EXO.4.PLAIN: So Moses took his wife and sons, put them on a donkey, and headed back to Egypt. And he took the staff of God in his hand.

EXO.4.BSB: The LORD instructed Moses, “When you go back to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders that I have put within your power. But I will harden his heart so that he will not let the people go.

EXO.4.PLAIN: The Lord instructed Moses, “When you go back to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders that I have put within your power. But I will harden his heart so that he will not let the people go.

EXO.4.KJV: And I say to you, Let my son go, that he may serve me: and if you refuse to let him go, behold, I will slay your son, even your firstborn. ¶

EXO.4.PLAIN: But Zipporah took a flint knife, cut off her son’s foreskin, and touched it to Moses’ feet. “Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me,” she said.

EXO.4.KJV: So he let him go: then she said, A bloody husband you are, because of the circumcision. ¶
EXO.4.PLAIN: So the Lord let him alone. (When she said, “bridegroom of blood,” she was referring to the circumcision.)

EXO.4.KJV: And Moses told Aaron all the words of the LORD who had sent him, and all the signs which he had commanded him. ¶
EXO.4.PLAIN: And Moses told Aaron everything the Lord had sent him to say, and all the signs He had commanded him to perform.

EXO.4.PLAIN: and Aaron relayed everything the Lord had said to Moses. And Moses performed the signs before the people,

EXO.4.KJV: And the people believed: and when they heard that the LORD had visited the children of Israel, and that he had looked on their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshipped.
EXO.4.PLAIN: and they believed. And when they heard that the Lord had attended to the Israelites and had seen their affliction, they bowed down and worshiped.

EXO.5.BSB: After that, Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may hold a feast to Me in the wilderness.’”

EXO.5.PLAIN: After that, Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said, “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may hold a feast to Me in the wilderness.’”

EXO.5.PLAIN: But Pharaoh replied, “Who is the Lord that I should obey His voice and let Israel go? I do not know the Lord, and I will not let Israel go.”

EXO.5.BSB: “The God of the Hebrews has met with us,” they answered. “Please let us go on a three-day journey into the wilderness to sacrifice to the LORD our God, or He may strike us with plagues or with the sword.”
EXO.5.KJV: And they said, The God of the Hebrews has met with us: let us go, we pray you, three days’ journey into the desert, and sacrifice to the LORD our God; lest he fall on us with pestilence, or with the sword.

EXO.5.PLAIN: But the king of Egypt said to them, “Moses and Aaron, why do you draw the people away from their work? Get back to your labor!”

EXO.5.BSB: So the taskmasters and foremen of the people went out and said to them, “This is what Pharaoh says: ‘I am no longer giving you straw.

EXO.5.PLAIN: So the taskmasters and foremen of the people went out and said to them, “This is what Pharaoh says: ‘I am no longer giving you straw.

EXO.5.KJV: Go you, get you straw where you can find it: yet not any of your work shall be diminished.

EXO.5.PLAIN: So the people scattered all over the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.

EXO.5.BSB: Then the Israelite foremen, whom Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over the people, were beaten and asked, “Why have you not fulfilled your quota of bricks yesterday or today, as you did before?”

EXO.5.BSB: So the Israelite foremen went and appealed to Pharaoh: “Why are you treating your servants this way?

EXO.5.KJV: There is no straw given to your servants, and they say to us, Make brick: and, behold, your servants are beaten; but the fault is in your own people.

EXO.5.PLAIN: “May the Lord look upon you and judge you,” the foremen said, “for you have made us a stench before Pharaoh and his officials; you have placed in their hand a sword to kill us!”

EXO.5.BSB: So Moses returned to the LORD and asked, “Lord, why have You brought trouble upon this people? Is this why You sent me?

EXO.5.PLAIN: So Moses returned to the Lord and asked, “Lord, why have You brought trouble upon this people? Is this why You sent me?

EXO.5.KJV: For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has done evil to this people; neither have you delivered your people at all.
EXO.5.PLAIN: Ever since I went to Pharaoh to speak in Your name, he has brought trouble on this people, and You have not delivered Your people in any way.”

EXO.6.BSB: But the LORD said to Moses, “Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh, for because of My mighty hand he will let the people go; because of My strong hand he will drive them out of his land.”
EXO.6.KJV: Then the LORD said to Moses, Now shall you see what I will do to Pharaoh: for with a strong hand shall he let them go, and with a strong hand shall he drive them out of his land.
EXO.6.PLAIN: But the Lord said to Moses, “Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh, for because of My mighty hand he will let the people go; because of My strong hand he will drive them out of his land.”

EXO.16.BSB: Every morning each one gathered as much as was needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted away.
EXO.16.KJV: And they gathered it every morning, every man according to his eating: and when the sun waxed hot, it melted. ¶
EXO.16.PLAIN: Every morning each one gathered as much as was needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted away.

EXO.16.BSB: On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much food—two omers per person—and all the leaders of the congregation came and reported this to Moses.
EXO.16.KJV: And it came to pass, that on the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for one man: and all the rulers of the congregation came and told Moses.
EXO.16.PLAIN: On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much food—two omers per person—and all the leaders of the congregation came and reported this to Moses.

EXO.16.BSB: He told them, “This is what the LORD has said: ‘Tomorrow is to be a day of complete rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. So bake what you want to bake, and boil what you want to boil. Then set aside whatever remains and keep it until morning.’”
EXO.16.KJV: And he said to them, This is that which the LORD has said, To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath to the LORD: bake that which you will bake to day, and seethe that you will seethe; and that which remains over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.
EXO.16.PLAIN: He told them, “This is what the Lord has said: ‘Tomorrow is to be a day of complete rest, a holy Sabbath to the Lord. So bake what you want to bake, and boil what you want to boil. Then set aside whatever remains and keep it until morning.’”

EXO.16.BSB: So they set it aside until morning as Moses had commanded, and it did not smell or contain any maggots.
EXO.16.KJV: And they laid it up till the morning, as Moses bade: and it did not stink, neither was there any worm therein.
EXO.16.PLAIN: So they set it aside until morning as Moses had commanded, and it did not smell or contain any maggots.

EXO.16.BSB: “Eat it today,” Moses said, “because today is a Sabbath to the LORD. Today you will not find anything in the field.
EXO.16.KJV: And Moses said, Eat that to day; for to day is a sabbath to the LORD: to day you shall not find it in the field.
EXO.16.PLAIN: “Eat it today,” Moses said, “because today is a Sabbath to the Lord. Today you will not find anything in the field.

EXO.16.BSB: For six days you may gather, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, it will not be there.”
EXO.16.KJV: Six days you shall gather it; but on the seventh day, which is the sabbath, in it there shall be none. ¶
EXO.16.PLAIN: For six days you may gather, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, it will not be there.”

EXO.16.BSB: Yet on the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they did not find anything.
EXO.16.KJV: And it came to pass, that there went out some of the people on the seventh day for to gather, and they found none.
EXO.16.PLAIN: Yet on the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they did not find anything.

EXO.16.BSB: Then the LORD said to Moses, “How long will you refuse to keep My commandments and instructions?
EXO.16.KJV: And the LORD said to Moses, How long refuse you to keep my commandments and my laws?
EXO.16.PLAIN: Then the Lord said to Moses, “How long will you refuse to keep My commandments and instructions?

EXO.16.BSB: Understand that the LORD has given you the Sabbath; that is why on the sixth day He will give you bread for two days. On the seventh day, everyone must stay where he is; no one may leave his place.”
EXO.16.KJV: See, for that the LORD has given you the sabbath, therefore he gives you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide you every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.
EXO.16.PLAIN: Understand that the Lord has given you the Sabbath; that is why on the sixth day He will give you bread for two days. On the seventh day, everyone must stay where he is; no one may leave his place.”

EXO.16.BSB: So the people rested on the seventh day.
EXO.16.KJV: So the people rested on the seventh day.
EXO.16.PLAIN: So the people rested on the seventh day.

EXO.16.BSB: Now the house of Israel called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.
EXO.16.KJV: And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey. ¶
EXO.16.PLAIN: Now the house of Israel called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.

EXO.16.BSB: Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Keep an omer of manna for the generations to come, so that they may see the bread I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.’”
EXO.16.KJV: And Moses said, This is the thing which the LORD commands, Fill an omer of it to be kept for your generations; that they may see the bread with which I have fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you forth from the land of Egypt.
EXO.16.PLAIN: Moses said, “This is what the Lord has commanded: ‘Keep an omer of manna for the generations to come, so that they may see the bread I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.’”

EXO.16.BSB: So Moses told Aaron, “Take a jar and fill it with an omer of manna. Then place it before the LORD to be preserved for the generations to come.”
EXO.16.KJV: And Moses said to Aaron, Take a pot, and put an omer full of manna therein, and lay it up before the LORD, to be kept for your generations.
EXO.16.PLAIN: So Moses told Aaron, “Take a jar and fill it with an omer of manna. Then place it before the Lord to be preserved for the generations to come.”

EXO.16.BSB: And Aaron placed it in front of the Testimony, to be preserved just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO.16.KJV: As the LORD commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony, to be kept.
EXO.16.PLAIN: And Aaron placed it in front of the Testimony, to be preserved just as the Lord had commanded Moses.

EXO.16.BSB: The Israelites ate manna forty years, until they came to a land where they could settle; they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.
EXO.16.KJV: And the children of Israel did eat manna forty years, until they came to a land inhabited; they did eat manna, until they came to the borders of the land of Canaan.
EXO.16.PLAIN: The Israelites ate manna forty years, until they came to a land where they could settle; they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.

EXO.16.BSB: (Now an omer is a tenth of an ephah.)
EXO.16.KJV: Now an omer is the tenth part of an ephah.
EXO.16.PLAIN: (Now an omer is a tenth of an ephah.)

EXO.17.BSB: Then the whole congregation of Israel left the Desert of Sin, moving from place to place as the LORD commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.
EXO.17.KJV: And all the congregation of the children of Israel journeyed from the wilderness of Sin, after their journeys, according to the commandment of the LORD, and pitched in Rephidim: and there was no water for the people to drink.
EXO.17.PLAIN: Then the whole congregation of Israel left the Desert of Sin, moving from place to place as the Lord commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.

EXO.17.BSB: So the people contended with Moses, “Give us water to drink.” “Why do you contend with me?” Moses replied. “Why do you test the LORD?”
EXO.17.KJV: Why the people did chide with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink. And Moses said to them, Why chide you with me? why do you tempt the LORD?
EXO.17.PLAIN: So the people contended with Moses, “Give us water to drink.” “Why do you contend with me?” Moses replied. “Why do you test the Lord?”

EXO.17.BSB: But the people thirsted for water there, and they grumbled against Moses: “Why have you brought us out of Egypt—to make us and our children and livestock die of thirst?”
EXO.17.KJV: And the people thirsted there for water; and the people murmured against Moses, and said, Why is this that you have brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst?
EXO.17.PLAIN: But the people thirsted for water there, and they grumbled against Moses: “Why have you brought us out of Egypt—to make us and our children and livestock die of thirst?”

EXO.17.BSB: Then Moses cried out to the LORD, “What should I do with these people? A little more and they will stone me!”
EXO.17.KJV: And Moses cried to the LORD, saying, What shall I do to this people? they be almost ready to stone me.
EXO.17.PLAIN: Then Moses cried out to the Lord, “What should I do with these people? A little more and they will stone me!”

EXO.17.BSB: And the LORD said to Moses, “Walk on ahead of the people and take some of the elders of Israel with you. Take along in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
EXO.17.KJV: And the LORD said to Moses, Go on before the people, and take with you of the elders of Israel; and your rod, with which you smote the river, take in your hand, and go.
EXO.17.PLAIN: And the Lord said to Moses, “Walk on ahead of the people and take some of the elders of Israel with you. Take along in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.

EXO.17.BSB: Behold, I will stand there before you by the rock at Horeb. And when you strike the rock, water will come out of it for the people to drink.” So Moses did this in the sight of the elders of Israel.
EXO.17.KJV: Behold, I will stand before you there on the rock in Horeb; and you shall smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
EXO.17.PLAIN: Look closely — I will stand there before you by the rock at Horeb. And when you strike the rock, water will come out of it for the people to drink.” So Moses did this in the sight of the elders of Israel.

EXO.17.BSB: He named the place Massah and Meribah because the Israelites quarreled, and because they tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?”
EXO.17.KJV: And he called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the LORD, saying, Is the LORD among us, or not? ¶
