JDG.15.PLAIN: Later on, at the time of the wheat harvest, Samson took a young goat and went to visit his wife. “I want to go to my wife in her room,” he said. But her father would not let him enter.

JDG.15.BSB: “I was sure that you thoroughly hated her,” said her father, “so I gave her to one of the men who accompanied you. Is not her younger sister more beautiful than she? Please take her instead.”
JDG.15.KJV: And her father said, I truly thought that you had utterly hated her; therefore I gave her to your companion: is not her younger sister fairer than she? take her, I pray you, instead of her. ¶
JDG.15.PLAIN: “I was sure that you thoroughly hated her,” said her father, “so I gave her to one of the men who accompanied you. Is not her younger sister more beautiful than she? Please take her instead.”

JDG.15.BSB: Samson said to them, “This time I will be blameless in doing harm to the Philistines.”
JDG.15.KJV: And Samson said concerning them, Now shall I be more blameless than the Philistines, though I do them a displeasure.
JDG.15.PLAIN: Samson said to them, “This time I will be blameless in doing harm to the Philistines.”

JDG.15.BSB: Then Samson went out and caught three hundred foxes. And he took torches, turned the foxes tail-to-tail, and fastened a torch between each pair of tails.
JDG.15.KJV: And Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and took firebrands, and turned tail to tail, and put a firebrand in the middle between two tails.
JDG.15.PLAIN: Then Samson went out and caught three hundred foxes. And he took torches, turned the foxes tail-to-tail, and fastened a torch between each pair of tails.

JDG.15.BSB: Then he lit the torches and released the foxes into the standing grain of the Philistines, burning up the piles of grain and the standing grain, as well as the vineyards and olive groves.
JDG.15.KJV: And when he had set the brands on fire, he let them go into the standing corn of the Philistines, and burnt up both the shocks, and also the standing corn, with the vineyards and olives. ¶
JDG.15.PLAIN: Then he lit the torches and released the foxes into the standing grain of the Philistines, burning up the piles of grain and the standing grain, as well as the vineyards and olive groves.

JDG.15.BSB: “Who did this?” the Philistines demanded. “It was Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite,” they were told. “For his wife was given to his companion.” So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father to death.
JDG.15.KJV: Then the Philistines said, Who has done this? And they answered, Samson, the son in law of the Timnite, because he had taken his wife, and given her to his companion. And the Philistines came up, and burnt her and her father with fire. ¶
JDG.15.PLAIN: “Who did this?” the Philistines demanded. “It was Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite,” they were told. “For his wife was given to his companion.” So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father to death.

JDG.15.BSB: And Samson told them, “Because you have done this, I will not rest until I have taken vengeance upon you.”
JDG.15.KJV: And Samson said to them, Though you have done this, yet will I be avenged of you, and after that I will cease.
JDG.15.PLAIN: And Samson told them, “Because you have done this, I will not rest until I have taken vengeance upon you.”

JDG.15.BSB: And he struck them ruthlessly with a great slaughter, and then went down and stayed in the cave at the rock of Etam.
JDG.15.KJV: And he smote them hip and thigh with a great slaughter: and he went down and dwelled in the top of the rock Etam. ¶
JDG.15.PLAIN: And he struck them ruthlessly with a great slaughter, and then went down and stayed in the cave at the rock of Etam.

JDG.15.BSB: Then the Philistines went up, camped in Judah, and deployed themselves near the town of Lehi.
JDG.15.KJV: Then the Philistines went up, and pitched in Judah, and spread themselves in Lehi.
JDG.15.PLAIN: Then the Philistines went up, camped in Judah, and deployed themselves near the town of Lehi.

JDG.15.BSB: “Why have you attacked us?” said the men of Judah. The Philistines replied, “We have come to arrest Samson and pay him back for what he has done to us.”
JDG.15.KJV: And the men of Judah said, Why are you come up against us? And they answered, To bind Samson are we come up, to do to him as he has done to us.
JDG.15.PLAIN: “Why have you attacked us?” said the men of Judah. The Philistines replied, “We have come to arrest Samson and pay him back for what he has done to us.”

JDG.15.BSB: In response, three thousand men of Judah went to the cave at the rock of Etam, and they asked Samson, “Do you not realize that the Philistines rule over us? What have you done to us?” “I have done to them what they did to me,” he replied.
JDG.15.KJV: Then three thousand men of Judah went to the top of the rock Etam, and said to Samson, Know you not that the Philistines are rulers over us? what is this that you have done to us? And he said to them, As they did to me, so have I done to them.
JDG.15.PLAIN: In response, three thousand men of Judah went to the cave at the rock of Etam, and they asked Samson, “Do you not realize that the Philistines rule over us? What have you done to us?” “I have done to them what they did to me,” he replied.

JDG.15.BSB: But they said to him, “We have come down to arrest you and hand you over to the Philistines.” Samson replied, “Swear to me that you will not kill me yourselves.”
JDG.15.KJV: And they said to him, We are come down to bind you, that we may deliver you into the hand of the Philistines. And Samson said to them, Swear to me, that you will not fall on me yourselves.
JDG.15.PLAIN: But they said to him, “We have come down to arrest you and hand you over to the Philistines.” Samson replied, “Swear to me that you will not kill me yourselves.”

JDG.15.BSB: “No,” they answered, “we will not kill you, but we will tie you up securely and hand you over to them.” So they bound him with two new ropes and led him up from the rock.
JDG.15.KJV: And they spoke to him, saying, No; but we will bind you fast, and deliver you into their hand: but surely we will not kill you. And they bound him with two new cords, and brought him up from the rock. ¶
JDG.15.PLAIN: “No,” they answered, “we will not kill you, but we will tie you up securely and hand you over to them.” So they bound him with two new ropes and led him up from the rock.

JDG.15.BSB: When Samson arrived in Lehi, the Philistines came out shouting against him. And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him. The ropes on his arms became like burnt flax, and the bonds broke loose from his hands.
JDG.15.KJV: And when he came to Lehi, the Philistines shouted against him: and the Spirit of the LORD came mightily on him, and the cords that were on his arms became as flax that was burnt with fire, and his bands loosed from off his hands.
JDG.15.PLAIN: When Samson arrived in Lehi, the Philistines came out shouting against him. And the Spirit of the Lord came mightily upon him. The ropes on his arms became like burnt flax, and the bonds broke loose from his hands.

JDG.15.BSB: He found the fresh jawbone of a donkey, reached out his hand and took it, and struck down a thousand men.
JDG.15.KJV: And he found a new jawbone of an ass, and put forth his hand, and took it, and slew a thousand men therewith.
JDG.15.PLAIN: He found the fresh jawbone of a donkey, reached out his hand and took it, and struck down a thousand men.

JDG.15.BSB: Then Samson said: “With the jawbone of a donkey I have piled them into heaps. With the jawbone of a donkey I have slain a thousand men.”
JDG.15.KJV: And Samson said, With the jawbone of an ass, heaps on heaps, with the jaw of an ass have I slain a thousand men.
JDG.15.PLAIN: Then Samson said: “With the jawbone of a donkey I have piled them into heaps. With the jawbone of a donkey I have slain a thousand men.”

JDG.15.BSB: And when Samson had finished speaking, he cast the jawbone from his hand; and he named that place Ramath-lehi.
JDG.15.KJV: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking, that he cast away the jawbone out of his hand, and called that place Ramathlehi. ¶
JDG.15.PLAIN: And when Samson had finished speaking, he cast the jawbone from his hand; and he named that place Ramath-lehi.

JDG.15.BSB: And being very thirsty, Samson cried out to the LORD, “You have accomplished this great deliverance through Your servant. Must I now die of thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?”
JDG.15.KJV: And he was sore thirsty, and called on the LORD, and said, You have given this great deliverance into the hand of your servant: and now shall I die for thirst, and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?
JDG.15.PLAIN: And being very thirsty, Samson cried out to the Lord, “You have accomplished this great deliverance through Your servant. Must I now die of thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?”

JDG.15.BSB: So God opened up the hollow place in Lehi, and water came out of it. When Samson drank, his strength returned, and he was revived. That is why he named it En-hakkore, and it remains in Lehi to this day.
JDG.15.KJV: But God split an hollow place that was in the jaw, and there came water out of there; and when he had drunk, his spirit came again, and he revived: why he called the name thereof Enhakkore, which is in Lehi to this day.
JDG.15.PLAIN: So God opened up the hollow place in Lehi, and water came out of it. When Samson drank, his strength returned, and he was revived. That is why he named it En-hakkore, and it remains in Lehi to this day.

JDG.15.BSB: And Samson judged Israel for twenty years in the days of the Philistines.
JDG.15.KJV: And he judged Israel in the days of the Philistines twenty years.
JDG.15.PLAIN: And Samson judged Israel for twenty years in the days of the Philistines.

JDG.16.BSB: One day Samson went to Gaza, where he saw a prostitute and went in to spend the night with her.
JDG.16.KJV: Then went Samson to Gaza, and saw there an harlot, and went in to her.
JDG.16.PLAIN: One day Samson went to Gaza, where he saw a prostitute and went in to spend the night with her.

JDG.16.BSB: When the Gazites heard that Samson was there, they surrounded that place and lay in wait for him all night at the city gate. They were quiet throughout the night, saying, “Let us wait until dawn; then we will kill him.”
JDG.16.KJV: And it was told the Gazites, saying, Samson is come here. And they compassed him in, and laid wait for him all night in the gate of the city, and were quiet all the night, saying, In the morning, when it is day, we shall kill him.
JDG.16.PLAIN: When the Gazites heard that Samson was there, they surrounded that place and lay in wait for him all night at the city gate. They were quiet throughout the night, saying, “Let us wait until dawn; then we will kill him.”

JDG.16.BSB: But Samson lay there only until midnight, when he got up, took hold of the doors of the city gate and both gateposts, and pulled them out, bar and all. Then he put them on his shoulders and took them to the top of the mountain overlooking Hebron.
JDG.16.KJV: And Samson lay till midnight, and arose at midnight, and took the doors of the gate of the city, and the two posts, and went away with them, bar and all, and put them on his shoulders, and carried them up to the top of an hill that is before Hebron. ¶
JDG.16.PLAIN: But Samson lay there only until midnight, when he got up, took hold of the doors of the city gate and both gateposts, and pulled them out, bar and all. Then he put them on his shoulders and took them to the top of the mountain overlooking Hebron.

JDG.16.BSB: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.
JDG.16.KJV: And it came to pass afterward, that he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.
JDG.16.PLAIN: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.

JDG.16.BSB: The lords of the Philistines went to her and said, “Entice him and find out the source of his great strength and how we can overpower him to tie him up and subdue him. Then each one of us will give you eleven hundred shekels of silver.”
JDG.16.KJV: And the lords of the Philistines came up to her, and said to her, Entice him, and see wherein his great strength lies, and by what means we may prevail against him, that we may bind him to afflict him; and we will give you every one of us eleven hundred pieces of silver. ¶
JDG.16.PLAIN: The lords of the Philistines went to her and said, “Entice him and find out the source of his great strength and how we can overpower him to tie him up and subdue him. Then each one of us will give you eleven hundred shekels of silver.”

JDG.16.BSB: So Delilah said to Samson, “Please tell me the source of your great strength and how you can be tied up and subdued.”
JDG.16.KJV: And Delilah said to Samson, Tell me, I pray you, wherein your great strength lies, and with which you might be bound to afflict you.
JDG.16.PLAIN: So Delilah said to Samson, “Please tell me the source of your great strength and how you can be tied up and subdued.”

JDG.16.BSB: Samson told her, “If they tie me up with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, I will become as weak as any other man.”
JDG.16.KJV: And Samson said to her, If they bind me with seven green thongs that were never dried, then shall I be weak, and be as another man.
JDG.16.PLAIN: Samson told her, “If they tie me up with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, I will become as weak as any other man.”

JDG.16.BSB: So the lords of the Philistines brought her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she tied him up with them.
JDG.16.KJV: Then the lords of the Philistines brought up to her seven green thongs which had not been dried, and she bound him with them.
JDG.16.PLAIN: So the lords of the Philistines brought her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she tied him up with them.

JDG.16.BSB: While the men were hidden in her room, she called out, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” But he snapped the bowstrings like a strand of yarn seared by a flame. So the source of his strength remained unknown.
JDG.16.KJV: Now there were men lying in wait, abiding with her in the chamber. And she said to him, The Philistines be on you, Samson. And he broke the thongs, as a thread of wick is broken when it touches the fire. So his strength was not known.
JDG.16.PLAIN: While the men were hidden in her room, she called out, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” But he snapped the bowstrings like a strand of yarn seared by a flame. So the source of his strength remained unknown.

JDG.16.BSB: Then Delilah said to Samson, “You have mocked me and lied to me! Now please tell me how you can be tied up.”
JDG.16.KJV: And Delilah said to Samson, Behold, you have mocked me, and told me lies: now tell me, I pray you, with which you might be bound.
JDG.16.PLAIN: Then Delilah said to Samson, “You have mocked me and lied to me! Now please tell me how you can be tied up.”

JDG.16.BSB: He replied, “If they tie me up with new ropes that have never been used, I will become as weak as any other man.”
JDG.16.KJV: And he said to her, If they bind me fast with new ropes that never were occupied, then shall I be weak, and be as another man.
JDG.16.PLAIN: He replied, “If they tie me up with new ropes that have never been used, I will become as weak as any other man.”

JDG.16.BSB: So Delilah took new ropes, tied him up with them, and called out, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” But while the men were hidden in her room, he snapped the ropes off his arms like they were threads.
JDG.16.KJV: Delilah therefore took new ropes, and bound him therewith, and said to him, The Philistines be on you, Samson. And there were liers in wait abiding in the chamber. And he broke them from off his arms like a thread.
JDG.16.PLAIN: So Delilah took new ropes, tied him up with them, and called out, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” But while the men were hidden in her room, he snapped the ropes off his arms like they were threads.

JDG.16.BSB: Then Delilah said to Samson, “You have mocked me and lied to me all along! Tell me how you can be tied up.” He told her, “If you weave the seven braids of my head into the web of a loom and tighten it with a pin, I will become as weak as any other man.”
JDG.16.KJV: And Delilah said to Samson, Till now you have mocked me, and told me lies: tell me with which you might be bound. And he said to her, If you weave the seven locks of my head with the web.
JDG.16.PLAIN: Then Delilah said to Samson, “You have mocked me and lied to me all along! Tell me how you can be tied up.” He told her, “If you weave the seven braids of my head into the web of a loom and tighten it with a pin, I will become as weak as any other man.”

JDG.16.BSB: So while he slept, Delilah took the seven braids of his hair and wove them into the web.Then she tightened it with a pin and called to him, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” But he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the pin with the loom and the web.
JDG.16.KJV: And she fastened it with the pin, and said to him, The Philistines be on you, Samson. And he awaked out of his sleep, and went away with the pin of the beam, and with the web. ¶
JDG.16.PLAIN: So while he slept, Delilah took the seven braids of his hair and wove them into the web.Then she tightened it with a pin and called to him, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” But he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the pin with the loom and the web.

JDG.16.BSB: “How can you say, ‘I love you,’” she asked, “when your heart is not with me? This is the third time you have mocked me and failed to reveal to me the source of your great strength!”
JDG.16.KJV: And she said to him, How can you say, I love you, when your heart is not with me? you have mocked me these three times, and have not told me wherein your great strength lies.
JDG.16.PLAIN: “How can you say, ‘I love you,’” she asked, “when your heart is not with me? This is the third time you have mocked me and failed to reveal to me the source of your great strength!”

JDG.16.BSB: Finally, after she had pressed him daily with her words and pleaded until he was sick to death,
JDG.16.KJV: And it came to pass, when she pressed him daily with her words, and urged him, so that his soul was vexed to death;
JDG.16.PLAIN: Finally, after she had pressed him daily with her words and pleaded until he was sick to death,

JDG.16.BSB: Samson told her all that was in his heart: “My hair has never been cut, because I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb. If I am shaved, my strength will leave me, and I will become as weak as any other man.”
JDG.16.KJV: That he told her all his heart, and said to her, There has not come a razor on my head; for I have been a Nazarite to God from my mother’s womb: if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak, and be like any other man.
JDG.16.PLAIN: Samson told her all that was in his heart: “My hair has never been cut, because I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb. If I am shaved, my strength will leave me, and I will become as weak as any other man.”

JDG.16.BSB: When Delilah realized that he had revealed to her all that was in his heart, she sent this message to the lords of the Philistines: “Come up once more, for he has revealed to me all that is in his heart.” Then the lords of the Philistines came to her, bringing the money in their hands.
JDG.16.KJV: And when Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, she sent and called for the lords of the Philistines, saying, Come up this once, for he has showed me all his heart. Then the lords of the Philistines came up to her, and brought money in their hand.
JDG.16.PLAIN: When Delilah realized that he had revealed to her all that was in his heart, she sent this message to the lords of the Philistines: “Come up once more, for he has revealed to me all that is in his heart.” Then the lords of the Philistines came to her, bringing the money in their hands.

JDG.16.BSB: And having lulled him to sleep on her lap, she called a man to shave off the seven braids of his head. In this way she began to subdue him, and his strength left him.
JDG.16.KJV: And she made him sleep on her knees; and she called for a man, and she caused him to shave off the seven locks of his head; and she began to afflict him, and his strength went from him.
JDG.16.PLAIN: And having lulled him to sleep on her lap, she called a man to shave off the seven braids of his head. In this way she began to subdue him, and his strength left him.

JDG.16.BSB: Then she called out, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” When Samson awoke from his sleep, he thought, “I will escape as I did before and shake myself free.” But he did not know that the LORD had departed from him.
JDG.16.KJV: And she said, The Philistines be on you, Samson. And he awoke out of his sleep, and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he knew not that the LORD was departed from him. ¶
JDG.16.PLAIN: Then she called out, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” When Samson awoke from his sleep, he thought, “I will escape as I did before and shake myself free.” But he did not know that the Lord had departed from him.

JDG.16.BSB: Then the Philistines seized him, gouged out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza, where he was bound with bronze shackles and forced to grind grain in the prison.
JDG.16.KJV: But the Philistines took him, and put out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza, and bound him with fetters of brass; and he did grind in the prison house.
JDG.16.PLAIN: Then the Philistines seized him, gouged out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza, where he was bound with bronze shackles and forced to grind grain in the prison.

JDG.16.BSB: However, the hair of his head began to grow back after it had been shaved.
JDG.16.KJV: However, the hair of his head began to grow again after he was shaven.
JDG.16.PLAIN: However, the hair of his head began to grow back after it had been shaved.

JDG.16.BSB: Now the lords of the Philistines gathered together to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon. They rejoiced and said, “Our god has delivered Samson our enemy into our hands.”
JDG.16.KJV: Then the lords of the Philistines gathered them together for to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god, and to rejoice: for they said, Our god has delivered Samson our enemy into our hand.
JDG.16.PLAIN: Now the lords of the Philistines gathered together to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon. They rejoiced and said, “Our god has delivered Samson our enemy into our hands.”

JDG.16.BSB: And when the people saw him, they praised their god, saying: “Our god has delivered into our hands our enemy who destroyed our land and multiplied our dead.”
JDG.16.KJV: And when the people saw him, they praised their god: for they said, Our god has delivered into our hands our enemy, and the destroyer of our country, which slew many of us.
JDG.16.PLAIN: And when the people saw him, they praised their god, saying: “Our god has delivered into our hands our enemy who destroyed our land and multiplied our dead.”

JDG.16.BSB: And while their hearts were merry, they said, “Call for Samson to entertain us.” So they called Samson out of the prison to entertain them. And they stationed him between the pillars.
JDG.16.KJV: And it came to pass, when their hearts were merry, that they said, Call for Samson, that he may make us sport. And they called for Samson out of the prison house; and he made them sport: and they set him between the pillars.
JDG.16.PLAIN: And while their hearts were merry, they said, “Call for Samson to entertain us.” So they called Samson out of the prison to entertain them. And they stationed him between the pillars.

JDG.16.BSB: Samson said to the servant who held his hand, “Lead me where I can feel the pillars supporting the temple, so I can lean against them.”
JDG.16.KJV: And Samson said to the lad that held him by the hand, Suffer me that I may feel the pillars whereupon the house stands, that I may lean on them.
JDG.16.PLAIN: Samson said to the servant who held his hand, “Lead me where I can feel the pillars supporting the temple, so I can lean against them.”

JDG.16.BSB: Now the temple was full of men and women; all the lords of the Philistines were there, and about three thousand men and women were on the roof watching Samson entertain them.
JDG.16.KJV: Now the house was full of men and women; and all the lords of the Philistines were there; and there were on the roof about three thousand men and women, that beheld while Samson made sport.
JDG.16.PLAIN: Now the temple was full of men and women; all the lords of the Philistines were there, and about three thousand men and women were on the roof watching Samson entertain them.

JDG.16.BSB: Then Samson called out to the LORD: “O Lord GOD, please remember me. Strengthen me, O God, just once more, so that with one vengeful blow I may pay back the Philistines for my two eyes.”
JDG.16.KJV: And Samson called to the LORD, and said, O Lord God, remember me, I pray you, and strengthen me, I pray you, only this once, O God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes.
JDG.16.PLAIN: Then Samson called out to the Lord: “O Lord GOD, please remember me. Strengthen me, O God, just once more, so that with one vengeful blow I may pay back the Philistines for my two eyes.”

JDG.16.BSB: And Samson reached out for the two central pillars supporting the temple. Bracing himself against them with his right hand on one pillar and his left hand on the other,
JDG.16.KJV: And Samson took hold of the two middle pillars on which the house stood, and on which it was borne up, of the one with his right hand, and of the other with his left.
JDG.16.PLAIN: And Samson reached out for the two central pillars supporting the temple. Bracing himself against them with his right hand on one pillar and his left hand on the other,

JDG.16.BSB: Samson said, “Let me die with the Philistines.” Then he pushed with all his might, and the temple fell on the lords and all the people in it. So in his death he killed more than he had killed in his life.
JDG.16.KJV: And Samson said, Let me die with the Philistines. And he bowed himself with all his might; and the house fell on the lords, and on all the people that were therein. So the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life.
JDG.16.PLAIN: Samson said, “Let me die with the Philistines.” Then he pushed with all his might, and the temple fell on the lords and all the people in it. So in his death he killed more than he had killed in his life.

JDG.16.BSB: Then Samson’s brothers and his father’s family came down, carried him back, and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of his father Manoah. And he had judged Israel twenty years.
JDG.16.KJV: Then his brothers and all the house of his father came down, and took him, and brought him up, and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the burial plot of Manoah his father. And he judged Israel twenty years.
JDG.16.PLAIN: Then Samson’s brothers and his father’s family came down, carried him back, and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of his father Manoah. And he had judged Israel twenty years.

JDG.17.BSB: Now a man named Micah from the hill country of Ephraim
JDG.17.KJV: And there was a man of mount Ephraim, whose name was Micah.
JDG.17.PLAIN: Now a man named Micah from the hill country of Ephraim

JDG.17.BSB: said to his mother, “The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from you and about which I heard you utter a curse—I have the silver here with me; I took it.” Then his mother said, “Blessed be my son by the LORD!”
JDG.17.KJV: And he said to his mother, The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from you, about which you cursed, and spoke of also in my ears, behold, the silver is with me; I took it. And his mother said, Blessed be you of the LORD, my son.
JDG.17.PLAIN: said to his mother, “The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from you and about which I heard you utter a curse—I have the silver here with me; I took it.” Then his mother said, “Blessed be my son by the Lord!”

JDG.17.BSB: And when he had returned the eleven hundred shekels of silver to his mother, she said, “I wholly dedicate the silver to the LORD for my son’s benefit, to make a graven image and a molten idol. Therefore I will now return it to you.”
JDG.17.KJV: And when he had restored the eleven hundred shekels of silver to his mother, his mother said, I had wholly dedicated the silver to the LORD from my hand for my son, to make a graven image and a molten image: now therefore I will restore it to you.
JDG.17.PLAIN: And when he had returned the eleven hundred shekels of silver to his mother, she said, “I wholly dedicate the silver to the Lord for my son’s benefit, to make a graven image and a molten idol. Therefore I will now return it to you.”

JDG.17.BSB: So he returned the silver to his mother, and she took two hundred shekels of silver and gave them to a silversmith, who made them into a graven image and a molten idol. And they were placed in the house of Micah.
JDG.17.KJV: Yet he restored the money to his mother; and his mother took two hundred shekels of silver, and gave them to the founder, who made thereof a graven image and a molten image: and they were in the house of Micah.
JDG.17.PLAIN: So he returned the silver to his mother, and she took two hundred shekels of silver and gave them to a silversmith, who made them into a graven image and a molten idol. And they were placed in the house of Micah.

JDG.17.BSB: Now this man Micah had a shrine, and he made an ephod and some household idols, and ordained one of his sons as his priest.
JDG.17.KJV: And the man Micah had an house of gods, and made an ephod, and teraphim, and consecrated one of his sons, who became his priest.
JDG.17.PLAIN: Now this man Micah had a shrine, and he made an ephod and some household idols, and ordained one of his sons as his priest.

JDG.17.BSB: In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
JDG.17.KJV: In those days there was no king in Israel, but every man did that which was right in his own eyes. ¶
JDG.17.PLAIN: In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.

JDG.17.BSB: And there was a young Levite from Bethlehem in Judah who had been residing within the clan of Judah.
JDG.17.KJV: And there was a young man out of Bethlehemjudah of the family of Judah, who was a Levite, and he sojourned there.
JDG.17.PLAIN: And there was a young Levite from Bethlehem in Judah who had been residing within the clan of Judah.

JDG.17.BSB: This man left the city of Bethlehem in Judah to settle where he could find a place. And as he traveled, he came to Micah’s house in the hill country of Ephraim.
JDG.17.KJV: And the man departed out of the city from Bethlehemjudah to sojourn where he could find a place: and he came to mount Ephraim to the house of Micah, as he journeyed.
JDG.17.PLAIN: This man left the city of Bethlehem in Judah to settle where he could find a place. And as he traveled, he came to Micah’s house in the hill country of Ephraim.

JDG.17.BSB: “Where are you from?” Micah asked him. “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” he replied, “and I am on my way to settle wherever I can find a place.”
JDG.17.KJV: And Micah said to him, From where come you? And he said to him, I am a Levite of Bethlehemjudah, and I go to sojourn where I may find a place.
JDG.17.PLAIN: “Where are you from?” Micah asked him. “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” he replied, “and I am on my way to settle wherever I can find a place.”

JDG.17.BSB: “Stay with me,” Micah said to him, “and be my father and priest, and I will give you ten shekels of silver per year, a suit of clothes, and your provisions.” So the Levite went in
JDG.17.KJV: And Micah said to him, Dwell with me, and be to me a father and a priest, and I will give you ten shekels of silver by the year, and a suit of apparel, and your victuals. So the Levite went in.
JDG.17.PLAIN: “Stay with me,” Micah said to him, “and be my father and priest, and I will give you ten shekels of silver per year, a suit of clothes, and your provisions.” So the Levite went in

JDG.17.BSB: and agreed to stay with him, and the young man became like a son to Micah.
JDG.17.KJV: And the Levite was content to dwell with the man; and the young man was to him as one of his sons.
JDG.17.PLAIN: and agreed to stay with him, and the young man became like a son to Micah.

JDG.17.BSB: Micah ordained the Levite, and the young man became his priest and lived in his house.
JDG.17.KJV: And Micah consecrated the Levite; and the young man became his priest, and was in the house of Micah.
JDG.17.PLAIN: Micah ordained the Levite, and the young man became his priest and lived in his house.

JDG.17.BSB: Then Micah said, “Now I know that the LORD will be good to me, because a Levite has become my priest.”
JDG.17.KJV: Then said Micah, Now know I that the LORD will do me good, seeing I have a Levite to my priest.
JDG.17.PLAIN: Then Micah said, “Now I know that the Lord will be good to me, because a Levite has become my priest.”

JDG.18.BSB: In those days there was no king in Israel, and the tribe of the Danites was looking for territory to occupy. For up to that time they had not come into an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
JDG.18.KJV: In those days there was no king in Israel: and in those days the tribe of the Danites sought them an inheritance to dwell in; for to that day all their inheritance had not fallen to them among the tribes of Israel.
JDG.18.PLAIN: In those days there was no king in Israel, and the tribe of the Danites was looking for territory to occupy. For up to that time they had not come into an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.

JDG.18.BSB: So the Danites sent out five men from their clans, men of valor from Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out the land and explore it. “Go and explore the land,” they told them. The men entered the hill country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah, where they spent the night.
JDG.18.KJV: And the children of Dan sent of their family five men from their coasts, men of valor, from Zorah, and from Eshtaol, to spy out the land, and to search it; and they said to them, Go, search the land: who when they came to mount Ephraim, to the house of Micah, they lodged there.
JDG.18.PLAIN: So the Danites sent out five men from their clans, men of valor from Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out the land and explore it. “Go and explore the land,” they told them. The men entered the hill country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah, where they spent the night.

JDG.18.BSB: And while they were near Micah’s house, they recognized the voice of the young Levite; so they went over and asked him, “Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? Why are you here?”
JDG.18.KJV: When they were by the house of Micah, they knew the voice of the young man the Levite: and they turned in thither, and said to him, Who brought you here? and what make you in this place? and what have you here?
JDG.18.PLAIN: And while they were near Micah’s house, they recognized the voice of the young Levite; so they went over and asked him, “Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? Why are you here?”

JDG.18.BSB: “Micah has done this and that for me,” he replied, “and he has hired me to be his priest.”
JDG.18.KJV: And he said to them, Thus and thus deals Micah with me, and has hired me, and I am his priest.
JDG.18.PLAIN: “Micah has done this and that for me,” he replied, “and he has hired me to be his priest.”

JDG.18.BSB: Then they said to him, “Please inquire of God to determine whether we will have a successful journey.”
JDG.18.KJV: And they said to him, Ask counsel, we pray you, of God, that we may know whether our way which we go shall be prosperous.
JDG.18.PLAIN: Then they said to him, “Please inquire of God to determine whether we will have a successful journey.”

JDG.18.BSB: And the priest told them, “Go in peace. The LORD is watching over your journey.”
JDG.18.KJV: And the priest said to them, Go in peace: before the LORD is your way wherein you go. ¶
JDG.18.PLAIN: And the priest told them, “Go in peace. The Lord is watching over your journey.”

JDG.18.BSB: So the five men departed and came to Laish, where they saw that the people were living securely, like the Sidonians, tranquil and unsuspecting. There was nothing lacking in the land and no oppressive ruler. And they were far away from the Sidonians and had no alliance with anyone.
JDG.18.KJV: Then the five men departed, and came to Laish, and saw the people that were therein, how they dwelled careless, after the manner of the Zidonians, quiet and secure; and there was no magistrate in the land, that might put them to shame in any thing; and they were far from the Zidonians, and had no business with any man.
JDG.18.PLAIN: So the five men departed and came to Laish, where they saw that the people were living securely, like the Sidonians, tranquil and unsuspecting. There was nothing lacking in the land and no oppressive ruler. And they were far away from the Sidonians and had no alliance with anyone.

JDG.18.BSB: When the men returned to Zorah and Eshtaol, their brothers asked them, “What did you find?”
JDG.18.KJV: And they came to their brothers to Zorah and Eshtaol: and their brothers said to them, What say you?
JDG.18.PLAIN: When the men returned to Zorah and Eshtaol, their brothers asked them, “What did you find?”

JDG.18.BSB: They answered, “Come on, let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and it is very good. Why would you fail to act? Do not hesitate to go there and take possession of the land!
JDG.18.KJV: And they said, Arise, that we may go up against them: for we have seen the land, and, behold, it is very good: and are you still? be not slothful to go, and to enter to possess the land.
JDG.18.PLAIN: They answered, “Come on, let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and it is very good. Why would you fail to act? Do not hesitate to go there and take possession of the land!

JDG.18.BSB: When you enter, you will come to an unsuspecting people and a spacious land, for God has delivered it into your hand. It is a place where nothing on earth is lacking.”
JDG.18.KJV: When you go, you shall come to a people secure, and to a large land: for God has given it into your hands; a place where there is no want of any thing that is in the earth. ¶
JDG.18.PLAIN: When you enter, you will come to an unsuspecting people and a spacious land, for God has delivered it into your hand. It is a place where nothing on earth is lacking.”

JDG.18.BSB: So six hundred Danites departed from Zorah and Eshtaol, armed with weapons of war.
JDG.18.KJV: And there went from there of the family of the Danites, out of Zorah and out of Eshtaol, six hundred men appointed with weapons of war.
JDG.18.PLAIN: So six hundred Danites departed from Zorah and Eshtaol, armed with weapons of war.

JDG.18.BSB: They went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. That is why the place west of Kiriath-jearim is called Mahaneh-dan to this day.
JDG.18.KJV: And they went up, and pitched in Kirjathjearim, in Judah: why they called that place Mahanehdan to this day: behold, it is behind Kirjathjearim.
JDG.18.PLAIN: They went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. That is why the place west of Kiriath-jearim is called Mahaneh-dan to this day.

JDG.18.BSB: And from there they traveled to the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah’s house.
JDG.18.KJV: And they passed there to mount Ephraim, and came to the house of Micah. ¶
JDG.18.PLAIN: And from there they traveled to the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah’s house.

JDG.18.BSB: Then the five men who had gone to spy out the land of Laish said to their brothers, “Did you know that one of these houses has an ephod, household gods, a graven image, and a molten idol? Now think about what you should do.”
JDG.18.KJV: Then answered the five men that went to spy out the country of Laish, and said to their brothers, Do you know that there is in these houses an ephod, and teraphim, and a graven image, and a molten image? now therefore consider what you have to do.
JDG.18.PLAIN: Then the five men who had gone to spy out the land of Laish said to their brothers, “Did you know that one of these houses has an ephod, household gods, a graven image, and a molten idol? Now think about what you should do.”

JDG.18.BSB: So they turned aside there and went to the home of the young Levite, the house of Micah, and greeted him.
JDG.18.KJV: And they turned thitherward, and came to the house of the young man the Levite, even to the house of Micah, and saluted him.
JDG.18.PLAIN: So they turned aside there and went to the home of the young Levite, the house of Micah, and greeted him.

JDG.18.BSB: The six hundred Danites stood at the entrance of the gate, armed with their weapons of war.
JDG.18.KJV: And the six hundred men appointed with their weapons of war, which were of the children of Dan, stood by the entering of the gate.
JDG.18.PLAIN: The six hundred Danites stood at the entrance of the gate, armed with their weapons of war.

JDG.18.BSB: And the five men who had gone to spy out the land went inside and took the graven image, the ephod, the household idols, and the molten idol, while the priest stood at the entrance of the gate with the six hundred armed men.
JDG.18.KJV: And the five men that went to spy out the land went up, and came in thither, and took the graven image, and the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image: and the priest stood in the entering of the gate with the six hundred men that were appointed with weapons of war.
JDG.18.PLAIN: And the five men who had gone to spy out the land went inside and took the graven image, the ephod, the household idols, and the molten idol, while the priest stood at the entrance of the gate with the six hundred armed men.

JDG.18.BSB: When they entered Micah’s house and took the graven image, the ephod, the household idols, and the molten idol, the priest said to them, “What are you doing?”
JDG.18.KJV: And these went into Micah’s house, and fetched the carved image, the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image. Then said the priest to them, What do you?
JDG.18.PLAIN: When they entered Micah’s house and took the graven image, the ephod, the household idols, and the molten idol, the priest said to them, “What are you doing?”

JDG.18.BSB: “Be quiet,” they told him. “Put your hand over your mouth and come with us and be a father and a priest to us. Is it better for you to be a priest for the house of one person or a priest for a tribe and family in Israel?”
JDG.18.KJV: And they said to him, Hold your peace, lay your hand on your mouth, and go with us, and be to us a father and a priest: is it better for you to be a priest to the house of one man, or that you be a priest to a tribe and a family in Israel?
JDG.18.PLAIN: “Be quiet,” they told him. “Put your hand over your mouth and come with us and be a father and a priest to us. Is it better for you to be a priest for the house of one person or a priest for a tribe and family in Israel?”

JDG.18.BSB: So the priest was glad and took the ephod, the household idols, and the graven image, and went with the people.
JDG.18.KJV: And the priest’s heart was glad, and he took the ephod, and the teraphim, and the graven image, and went in the middle of the people.
JDG.18.PLAIN: So the priest was glad and took the ephod, the household idols, and the graven image, and went with the people.

JDG.18.BSB: Putting their small children, their livestock, and their possessions in front of them, they turned and departed.
JDG.18.KJV: So they turned and departed, and put the little ones and the cattle and the carriage before them. ¶
JDG.18.PLAIN: Putting their small children, their livestock, and their possessions in front of them, they turned and departed.

JDG.18.BSB: After they were some distance from Micah’s house, the men in the houses near Micah’s house mobilized and overtook the Danites.
JDG.18.KJV: And when they were a good way from the house of Micah, the men that were in the houses near to Micah’s house were gathered together, and overtook the children of Dan.
JDG.18.PLAIN: After they were some distance from Micah’s house, the men in the houses near Micah’s house mobilized and overtook the Danites.

JDG.18.BSB: When they called out after them, the Danites turned to face them and said to Micah, “What is the matter with you that you have called out such a company?”
JDG.18.KJV: And they cried to the children of Dan. And they turned their faces, and said to Micah, What ails you, that you come with such a company?
JDG.18.PLAIN: When they called out after them, the Danites turned to face them and said to Micah, “What is the matter with you that you have called out such a company?”

JDG.18.BSB: He replied, “You took the gods I had made, and my priest, and went away. What else do I have? How can you say to me, ‘What is the matter with you?’”
JDG.18.KJV: And he said, You have taken away my gods which I made, and the priest, and you are gone away: and what have I more? and what is this that you say to me, What ails you?
JDG.18.PLAIN: He replied, “You took the gods I had made, and my priest, and went away. What else do I have? How can you say to me, ‘What is the matter with you?’”

JDG.18.BSB: The Danites said to him, “Do not raise your voice against us, or angry men will attack you, and you and your family will lose your lives.”
JDG.18.KJV: And the children of Dan said to him, Let not your voice be heard among us, lest angry fellows run on you, and you lose your life, with the lives of your household.
JDG.18.PLAIN: The Danites said to him, “Do not raise your voice against us, or angry men will attack you, and you and your family will lose your lives.”

JDG.18.BSB: So the Danites went on their way, and Micah turned to go back home, because he saw that they were too strong for him.
JDG.18.KJV: And the children of Dan went their way: and when Micah saw that they were too strong for him, he turned and went back to his house.
JDG.18.PLAIN: So the Danites went on their way, and Micah turned to go back home, because he saw that they were too strong for him.

JDG.18.BSB: After they had taken Micah’s idols and his priest, they went to Laish, to a tranquil and unsuspecting people, and they struck them with their swords and burned down the city.
JDG.18.KJV: And they took the things which Micah had made, and the priest which he had, and came to Laish, to a people that were at quiet and secure: and they smote them with the edge of the sword, and burnt the city with fire.
JDG.18.PLAIN: After they had taken Micah’s idols and his priest, they went to Laish, to a tranquil and unsuspecting people, and they struck them with their swords and burned down the city.

JDG.18.BSB: There was no one to deliver them, because the city was far from Sidon and had no alliance with anyone; it was in a valley near Beth-rehob. And the Danites rebuilt the city and lived there.
JDG.18.KJV: And there was no deliverer, because it was far from Zidon, and they had no business with any man; and it was in the valley that lies by Bethrehob. And they built a city, and dwelled therein.
JDG.18.PLAIN: There was no one to deliver them, because the city was far from Sidon and had no alliance with anyone; it was in a valley near Beth-rehob. And the Danites rebuilt the city and lived there.

JDG.18.BSB: They named it Dan, after their forefather Dan, who was born to Israel—though the city was formerly named Laish.
JDG.18.KJV: And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born to Israel: however, the name of the city was Laish at the first. ¶
JDG.18.PLAIN: They named it Dan, after their forefather Dan, who was born to Israel—though the city was formerly named Laish.

JDG.18.BSB: The Danites set up idols for themselves, and Jonathan son of Gershom, the son of Moses, and his sons were priests for the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.
JDG.18.KJV: And the children of Dan set up the graven image: and Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.
JDG.18.PLAIN: The Danites set up idols for themselves, and Jonathan son of Gershom, the son of Moses, and his sons were priests for the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.

JDG.18.BSB: So they set up for themselves Micah’s graven image, and it was there the whole time the house of God was in Shiloh.
JDG.18.KJV: And they set them up Micah’s graven image, which he made, all the time that the house of God was in Shiloh.
JDG.18.PLAIN: So they set up for themselves Micah’s graven image, and it was there the whole time the house of God was in Shiloh.

JDG.19.BSB: Now in those days, when there was no king in Israel, a Levite who lived in the remote hill country of Ephraim took for himself a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah.
JDG.19.KJV: And it came to pass in those days, when there was no king in Israel, that there was a certain Levite sojourning on the side of mount Ephraim, who took to him a concubine out of Bethlehemjudah.
JDG.19.PLAIN: Now in those days, when there was no king in Israel, a Levite who lived in the remote hill country of Ephraim took for himself a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah.

JDG.19.BSB: But she was unfaithful to him and left him to return to her father’s house in Bethlehem in Judah. After she had been there four months,
JDG.19.KJV: And his concubine played the whore against him, and went away from him to her father’s house to Bethlehemjudah, and was there four whole months.
JDG.19.PLAIN: But she was unfaithful to him and left him to return to her father’s house in Bethlehem in Judah. After she had been there four months,

JDG.19.BSB: her husband got up and went after her to speak kindly to her and bring her back, taking his servant and a pair of donkeys. So the girl brought him into her father’s house, and when her father saw him, he gladly welcomed him.
JDG.19.KJV: And her husband arose, and went after her, to speak friendly to her, and to bring her again, having his servant with him, and a couple of asses: and she brought him into her father’s house: and when the father of the damsel saw him, he rejoiced to meet him.
JDG.19.PLAIN: her husband got up and went after her to speak kindly to her and bring her back, taking his servant and a pair of donkeys. So the girl brought him into her father’s house, and when her father saw him, he gladly welcomed him.

JDG.19.BSB: His father-in-law, the girl’s father, persuaded him to stay, so he remained with him three days, eating, drinking, and lodging there.
JDG.19.KJV: And his father in law, the damsel’s father, retained him; and he stayed with him three days: so they did eat and drink, and lodged there. ¶
JDG.19.PLAIN: His father-in-law, the girl’s father, persuaded him to stay, so he remained with him three days, eating, drinking, and lodging there.

JDG.19.BSB: On the fourth day, they got up early in the morning and prepared to depart, but the girl’s father said to his son-in-law, “Refresh your heart with a morsel of bread, and then you can go.”
JDG.19.KJV: And it came to pass on the fourth day, when they arose early in the morning, that he rose up to depart: and the damsel’s father said to his son in law, Comfort your heart with a morsel of bread, and afterward go your way.
JDG.19.PLAIN: On the fourth day, they got up early in the morning and prepared to depart, but the girl’s father said to his son-in-law, “Refresh your heart with a morsel of bread, and then you can go.”

JDG.19.BSB: So they sat down and the two of them ate and drank together. Then the girl’s father said to the man, “Please agree to stay overnight and let your heart be merry.”

RUT.1.KJV: I went out full and the LORD has brought me home again empty: why then call you me Naomi, seeing the LORD has testified against me, and the Almighty has afflicted me?
RUT.1.PLAIN: I went away full, but the Lord has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi? After all, the Lord has testified against me, and the Almighty has afflicted me.”

RUT.1.BSB: So Naomi returned from the land of Moab with her daughter-in-law Ruth the Moabitess. And they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.
RUT.1.KJV: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter in law, with her, which returned out of the country of Moab: and they came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.
RUT.1.PLAIN: So Naomi returned from the land of Moab with her daughter-in-law Ruth the Moabitess. And they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.

RUT.2.BSB: Now Naomi had a relative on her husband’s side, a prominent man of noble character from the clan of Elimelech, whose name was Boaz.
RUT.2.KJV: And Naomi had a kinsman of her husband’s, a mighty man of wealth, of the family of Elimelech; and his name was Boaz.
RUT.2.PLAIN: Now Naomi had a relative on her husband’s side, a prominent man of noble character from the clan of Elimelech, whose name was Boaz.

RUT.2.BSB: And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, “Please let me go into the fields and glean heads of grain after someone in whose sight I may find favor.” “Go ahead, my daughter,” Naomi replied.
RUT.2.KJV: And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, Let me now go to the field, and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace. And she said to her, Go, my daughter.
RUT.2.PLAIN: And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, “Please let me go into the fields and glean heads of grain after someone in whose sight I may find favor.” “Go ahead, my daughter,” Naomi replied.

RUT.2.BSB: So Ruth departed and went out into the field and gleaned after the harvesters. And she happened to come to the part of the field belonging to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelech.
RUT.2.KJV: And she went, and came, and gleaned in the field after the reapers: and her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging to Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech. ¶
RUT.2.PLAIN: So Ruth departed and went out into the field and gleaned after the harvesters. And she happened to come to the part of the field belonging to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelech.

RUT.2.BSB: Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and said to the harvesters, “The LORD be with you.” “The LORD bless you,” they replied.
RUT.2.KJV: And, behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem, and said to the reapers, The LORD be with you. And they answered him, The LORD bless you.
RUT.2.PLAIN: Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and said to the harvesters, “The Lord be with you.” “The Lord bless you,” they replied.

RUT.2.BSB: And Boaz asked the foreman of his harvesters, “Whose young woman is this?”
RUT.2.KJV: Then said Boaz to his servant that was set over the reapers, Whose damsel is this?
RUT.2.PLAIN: And Boaz asked the foreman of his harvesters, “Whose young woman is this?”

RUT.2.BSB: The foreman answered, “She is the Moabitess who returned with Naomi from the land of Moab.
RUT.2.KJV: And the servant that was set over the reapers answered and said, It is the Moabitish damsel that came back with Naomi out of the country of Moab:
RUT.2.PLAIN: The foreman answered, “She is the Moabitess who returned with Naomi from the land of Moab.

RUT.2.BSB: She has said, ‘Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves after the harvesters.’ So she came out and has continued from morning until now, except that she rested a short time in the shelter.”
RUT.2.KJV: And she said, I pray you, let me glean and gather after the reapers among the sheaves: so she came, and has continued even from the morning until now, that she tarried a little in the house.
RUT.2.PLAIN: She has said, ‘Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves after the harvesters.’ So she came out and has continued from morning until now, except that she rested a short time in the shelter.”

RUT.2.BSB: Then Boaz said to Ruth, “Listen, my daughter. Do not go and glean in another field, and do not go away from this place, but stay here close to my servant girls.
RUT.2.KJV: Then said Boaz to Ruth, Hear you not, my daughter? Go not to glean in another field, neither go from hence, but abide here fast by my maidens:
RUT.2.PLAIN: Then Boaz said to Ruth, “Listen, my daughter. Do not go and glean in another field, and do not go away from this place, but stay here close to my servant girls.

RUT.2.BSB: Let your eyes be on the field they are harvesting, and follow along after these girls. Indeed, I have ordered the young men not to touch you. And when you are thirsty, go and drink from the jars the young men have filled.”
RUT.2.KJV: Let your eyes be on the field that they do reap, and go you after them: have I not charged the young men that they shall not touch you? and when you are thirsty, go to the vessels, and drink of that which the young men have drawn.
RUT.2.PLAIN: Let your eyes be on the field they are harvesting, and follow along after these girls. Indeed, I have ordered the young men not to touch you. And when you are thirsty, go and drink from the jars the young men have filled.”

RUT.2.BSB: At this, she fell on her face, bowing low to the ground, and said to him, “Why have I found such favor in your eyes that you should take notice of me, even though I am a foreigner?”
RUT.2.KJV: Then she fell on her face, and bowed herself to the ground, and said to him, Why have I found grace in your eyes, that you should take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger?
RUT.2.PLAIN: At this, she fell on her face, bowing low to the ground, and said to him, “Why have I found such favor in your eyes that you should take notice of me, even though I am a foreigner?”

RUT.2.BSB: Boaz replied, “I have been made fully aware of all you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband, how you left your father and mother and the land of your birth, and how you came to a people you did not know before.
RUT.2.KJV: And Boaz answered and said to her, It has fully been showed me, all that you have done to your mother in law since the death of your husband: and how you have left your father and your mother, and the land of your nativity, and are come to a people which you knew not heretofore.
RUT.2.PLAIN: Boaz replied, “I have been made fully aware of all you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband, how you left your father and mother and the land of your birth, and how you came to a people you did not know before.

RUT.2.BSB: May the LORD repay your work, and may you receive a rich reward from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have taken refuge.”
RUT.2.KJV: The LORD recompense your work, and a full reward be given you of the LORD God of Israel, under whose wings you are come to trust.
RUT.2.PLAIN: May the Lord repay you for what you have done. May you be richly rewarded by the Lord, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.

RUT.2.BSB: “My lord,” she said, “may I continue to find favor in your eyes, for you have comforted and spoken kindly to your maidservant, though I am not like one of your servant girls.”
RUT.2.KJV: Then she said, Let me find favor in your sight, my lord; for that you have comforted me, and for that you have spoken friendly to your handmaid, though I be not like to one of your handmaidens.
RUT.2.PLAIN: “My lord,” she said, “may I continue to find favor in your eyes, for you have comforted and spoken kindly to your maidservant, though I am not like one of your servant girls.”

RUT.2.BSB: At mealtime Boaz said to her, “Come over here; have some bread and dip it into the vinegar sauce.” So she sat down beside the harvesters, and he offered her roasted grain, and she ate and was satisfied and had some left over.
RUT.2.KJV: And Boaz said to her, At mealtime come you here, and eat of the bread, and dip your morsel in the vinegar. And she sat beside the reapers: and he reached her parched corn, and she did eat, and was sufficed, and left.
RUT.2.PLAIN: At mealtime Boaz said to her, “Come over here; have some bread and dip it into the vinegar sauce.” So she sat down beside the harvesters, and he offered her roasted grain, and she ate and was satisfied and had some left over.

RUT.2.BSB: When Ruth got up to glean, Boaz ordered his young men, “Even if she gathers among the sheaves, do not insult her.
RUT.2.KJV: And when she was risen up to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying, Let her glean even among the sheaves, and reproach her not:
RUT.2.PLAIN: When Ruth got up to glean, Boaz ordered his young men, “Even if she gathers among the sheaves, do not insult her.

RUT.2.BSB: Rather, pull out for her some stalks from the bundles and leave them for her to gather. Do not rebuke her.”
RUT.2.KJV: And let fall also some of the handfuls of purpose for her, and leave them, that she may glean them, and rebuke her not.
RUT.2.PLAIN: Rather, pull out for her some stalks from the bundles and leave them for her to gather. Do not rebuke her.”

RUT.2.BSB: So Ruth gathered grain in the field until evening. And when she beat out what she had gleaned, it was about an ephah of barley.
RUT.2.KJV: So she gleaned in the field until even, and beat out that she had gleaned: and it was about an ephah of barley. ¶
RUT.2.PLAIN: So Ruth gathered grain in the field until evening. And when she beat out what she had gleaned, it was about an ephah of barley.

RUT.2.BSB: She picked up the grain and went into the town, where her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. And she brought out what she had saved from her meal and gave it to Naomi.
RUT.2.KJV: And she took it up, and went into the city: and her mother in law saw what she had gleaned: and she brought forth, and gave to her that she had reserved after she was sufficed.
RUT.2.PLAIN: She picked up the grain and went into the town, where her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. And she brought out what she had saved from her meal and gave it to Naomi.

RUT.2.BSB: Then her mother-in-law asked her, “Where did you glean today, and where did you work? Blessed be the man who noticed you.” So she told her mother-in-law where she had worked. “The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz,” she said.
RUT.2.KJV: And her mother in law said to her, Where have you gleaned to day? and where worked you? blessed be he that did take knowledge of you. And she showed her mother in law with whom she had worked, and said, The man’s name with whom I worked to day is Boaz.
RUT.2.PLAIN: Then her mother-in-law asked her, “Where did you glean today, and where did you work? Blessed be the man who noticed you.” So she told her mother-in-law where she had worked. “The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz,” she said.

RUT.2.BSB: Then Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “May he be blessed by the LORD, who has not withdrawn His kindness from the living or the dead.” Naomi continued, “The man is a close relative. He is one of our kinsman-redeemers.”
RUT.2.KJV: And Naomi said to her daughter in law, Blessed be he of the LORD, who has not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead. And Naomi said to her, The man is near of kin to us, one of our next kinsmen.
RUT.2.PLAIN: Then Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “May he be blessed by the Lord, who has not withdrawn His kindness from the living or the dead.” Naomi continued, “The man is a close relative. He is one of our kinsman-redeemers.”

RUT.2.BSB: Then Ruth the Moabitess said, “He also told me, ‘Stay with my young men until they have finished gathering all my harvest.’”
RUT.2.KJV: And Ruth the Moabitess said, He said to me also, You shall keep fast by my young men, until they have ended all my harvest.
RUT.2.PLAIN: Then Ruth the Moabitess said, “He also told me, ‘Stay with my young men until they have finished gathering all my harvest.’”

RUT.2.BSB: And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law Ruth, “My daughter, it is good for you to work with his young women, so that nothing will happen to you in another field.”
RUT.2.KJV: And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter in law, It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his maidens, that they meet you not in any other field.
RUT.2.PLAIN: And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law Ruth, “My daughter, it is good for you to work with his young women, so that nothing will happen to you in another field.”

RUT.2.BSB: So Ruth stayed close to the servant girls of Boaz to glean grain until the barley and wheat harvests were finished. And she lived with her mother-in-law.
RUT.2.KJV: So she kept fast by the maidens of Boaz to glean to the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest; and dwelled with her mother in law.
RUT.2.PLAIN: So Ruth stayed close to the servant girls of Boaz to glean grain until the barley and wheat harvests were finished. And she lived with her mother-in-law.

RUT.3.BSB: One day Ruth’s mother-in-law Naomi said to her, “My daughter, should I not seek a resting place for you, that it may be well with you?
RUT.3.KJV: Then Naomi her mother in law said to her, My daughter, shall I not seek rest for you, that it may be well with you?
RUT.3.PLAIN: One day Ruth’s mother-in-law Naomi said to her, “My daughter, should I not seek a resting place for you, that it may be well with you?

RUT.3.BSB: Now is not Boaz, with whose servant girls you have been working, a relative of ours? In fact, tonight he is winnowing barley on the threshing floor.
RUT.3.KJV: And now is not Boaz of our kindred, with whose maidens you were? Behold, he winnows barley to night in the threshing floor.
RUT.3.PLAIN: Now is not Boaz, with whose servant girls you have been working, a relative of ours? In fact, tonight he is winnowing barley on the threshing floor.

RUT.3.BSB: Therefore wash yourself, put on perfume, and wear your best clothes. Go down to the threshing floor, but do not let the man know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.
RUT.3.KJV: Wash yourself therefore, and anoint you, and put your raiment on you, and get you down to the floor: but make not yourself known to the man, until he shall have done eating and drinking.
RUT.3.PLAIN: Therefore wash yourself, put on perfume, and wear your best clothes. Go down to the threshing floor, but do not let the man know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.

RUT.3.BSB: When he lies down, note the place where he lies. Then go in and uncover his feet, and lie down, and he will explain to you what you should do.”
RUT.3.KJV: And it shall be, when he lies down, that you shall mark the place where he shall lie, and you shall go in, and uncover his feet, and lay you down; and he will tell you what you shall do.
RUT.3.PLAIN: When he lies down, note the place where he lies. Then go in and uncover his feet, and lie down, and he will explain to you what you should do.”

RUT.3.BSB: “I will do everything you say,” Ruth answered.
RUT.3.KJV: And she said to her, All that you say to me I will do. ¶
RUT.3.PLAIN: “I will do everything you say,” Ruth answered.

RUT.3.BSB: So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had instructed her to do.
RUT.3.KJV: And she went down to the floor, and did according to all that her mother in law bade her.
RUT.3.PLAIN: So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had instructed her to do.

RUT.3.BSB: After Boaz had finished eating and drinking and was in good spirits, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. Then Ruth went in secretly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
RUT.3.KJV: And when Boaz had eaten and drunk, and his heart was merry, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of corn: and she came softly, and uncovered his feet, and laid her down. ¶
RUT.3.PLAIN: After Boaz had finished eating and drinking and was in good spirits, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. Then Ruth went in secretly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.

RUT.3.BSB: At midnight, Boaz was startled, turned over, and there lying at his feet was a woman!
RUT.3.KJV: And it came to pass at midnight, that the man was afraid, and turned himself: and, behold, a woman lay at his feet.
RUT.3.PLAIN: At midnight, Boaz was startled, turned over, and there lying at his feet was a woman!

RUT.3.BSB: “Who are you?” he asked. “I am your servant Ruth,” she replied. “Spread the corner of your garment over me, for you are a kinsman-redeemer.”
RUT.3.KJV: And he said, Who are you? And she answered, I am Ruth your handmaid: spread therefore your skirt over your handmaid; for you are a near kinsman.
RUT.3.PLAIN: “Who are you?” he asked. “I am your servant Ruth,” she replied. “Spread the corner of your garment over me, for you are a kinsman-redeemer.”

RUT.3.BSB: Then Boaz said, “May the LORD bless you, my daughter. You have shown more kindness now than before, because you have not run after the younger men, whether rich or poor.
RUT.3.KJV: And he said, Blessed be you of the LORD, my daughter: for you have showed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, inasmuch as you followed not young men, whether poor or rich.
RUT.3.PLAIN: Then Boaz said, “May the Lord bless you, my daughter. You have shown more kindness now than before, because you have not run after the younger men, whether rich or poor.

RUT.3.BSB: And now do not be afraid, my daughter. I will do for you whatever you request, since all my fellow townspeople know that you are a woman of noble character.
RUT.3.KJV: And now, my daughter, fear not; I will do to you all that you require: for all the city of my people does know that you are a virtuous woman.
RUT.3.PLAIN: And now do not be afraid, my daughter. I will do for you whatever you request, since all my fellow townspeople know that you are a woman of noble character.

RUT.3.BSB: Yes, it is true that I am a kinsman-redeemer, but there is a redeemer nearer than I.
RUT.3.KJV: And now it is true that I am your near kinsman: however, there is a kinsman nearer than I.
RUT.3.PLAIN: Yes, it is true that I am a kinsman-redeemer, but there is a redeemer nearer than I.

RUT.3.BSB: Stay here tonight, and in the morning, if he wants to redeem you, good. Let him redeem you. But if he does not want to redeem you, as surely as the LORD lives, I will. Now lie here until morning.”
RUT.3.KJV: Tarry this night, and it shall be in the morning, that if he will perform to you the part of a kinsman, well; let him do the kinsman’s part: but if he will not do the part of a kinsman to you, then will I do the part of a kinsman to you, as the LORD lives: lie down until the morning. ¶
RUT.3.PLAIN: Stay here tonight, and in the morning, if he wants to redeem you, good. Let him redeem you. But if he does not want to redeem you, as surely as the Lord lives, I will. Now lie here until morning.”

RUT.3.BSB: So she lay down at his feet until morning, but she got up before anyone else could recognize her. Then Boaz said, “Do not let it be known that a woman came to the threshing floor.”
RUT.3.KJV: And she lay at his feet until the morning: and she rose up before one could know another. And he said, Let it not be known that a woman came into the floor.
RUT.3.PLAIN: So she lay down at his feet until morning, but she got up before anyone else could recognize her. Then Boaz said, “Do not let it be known that a woman came to the threshing floor.”

RUT.3.BSB: And he told her, “Bring the shawl you are wearing and hold it out.” When she did so, he shoveled six measures of barley into her shawl. Then he went into the city.
RUT.3.KJV: Also he said, Bring the veil that you have on you, and hold it. And when she held it, he measured six measures of barley, and laid it on her: and she went into the city.
RUT.3.PLAIN: And he told her, “Bring the shawl you are wearing and hold it out.” When she did so, he shoveled six measures of barley into her shawl. Then he went into the city.

RUT.3.BSB: When Ruth returned to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked her, “How did it go, my daughter?” Then Ruth told her all that Boaz had done for her.
RUT.3.KJV: And when she came to her mother in law, she said, Who are you, my daughter? And she told her all that the man had done to her.
RUT.3.PLAIN: When Ruth returned to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked her, “How did it go, my daughter?” Then Ruth told her all that Boaz had done for her.

RUT.3.BSB: And she said, “He gave me these six measures of barley, for he said, ‘Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”
RUT.3.KJV: And she said, These six measures of barley gave he me; for he said to me, Go not empty to your mother in law.
RUT.3.PLAIN: And she said, “He gave me these six measures of barley, for he said, ‘Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”

RUT.3.BSB: “Wait, my daughter,” said Naomi, “until you find out how things go, for he will not rest unless he has resolved the matter today.”
RUT.3.KJV: Then said she, Sit still, my daughter, until you know how the matter will fall: for the man will not be in rest, until he have finished the thing this day.
RUT.3.PLAIN: “Wait, my daughter,” said Naomi, “until you find out how things go, for he will not rest unless he has resolved the matter today.”

RUT.4.BSB: Meanwhile, Boaz went to the gate and sat down there. Soon the kinsman-redeemer of whom he had spoken came along, and Boaz said, “Come over here, my friend, and sit down.” So he went over and sat down.
RUT.4.KJV: Then went Boaz up to the gate, and sat him down there: and, behold, the kinsman of whom Boaz spoke came by; to whom he said, Ho, such a one! turn aside, sit down here. And he turned aside, and sat down.
RUT.4.PLAIN: Meanwhile, Boaz went to the gate and sat down there. Soon the kinsman-redeemer of whom he had spoken came along, and Boaz said, “Come over here, my friend, and sit down.” So he went over and sat down.

RUT.4.BSB: Then Boaz took ten of the elders of the city and said, “Sit here,” and they did so.
RUT.4.KJV: And he took ten men of the elders of the city, and said, Sit you down here. And they sat down.
RUT.4.PLAIN: Then Boaz took ten of the elders of the city and said, “Sit here,” and they did so.

RUT.4.BSB: And he said to the kinsman-redeemer, “Naomi, who has returned from the land of Moab, is selling the piece of land that belonged to our brother Elimelech.
RUT.4.KJV: And he said to the kinsman, Naomi, that is come again out of the country of Moab, sells a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s:
RUT.4.PLAIN: And he said to the kinsman-redeemer, “Naomi, who has returned from the land of Moab, is selling the piece of land that belonged to our brother Elimelech.

RUT.4.BSB: I thought I should inform you that you may buy it back in the presence of those seated here and in the presence of the elders of my people. If you want to redeem it, do so. But if you will not redeem it, tell me so I may know, because there is no one but you to redeem it, and I am next after you.” “I will redeem it,” he replied.
RUT.4.KJV: And I thought to advertise you, saying, Buy it before the inhabitants, and before the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, redeem it: but if you will not redeem it, then tell me, that I may know: for there is none to redeem it beside you; and I am after you. And he said, I will redeem it.
RUT.4.PLAIN: I thought I should inform you that you may buy it back in the presence of those seated here and in the presence of the elders of my people. If you want to redeem it, do so. But if you will not redeem it, tell me so I may know, because there is no one but you to redeem it, and I am next after you.” “I will redeem it,” he replied.

RUT.4.BSB: Then Boaz said, “On the day you buy the land from Naomi and also from Ruth the Moabitess, you must also acquire the widow of the deceased in order to raise up the name of the deceased on his inheritance.”
RUT.4.KJV: Then said Boaz, What day you buy the field of the hand of Naomi, you must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance. ¶
RUT.4.PLAIN: Then Boaz said, “On the day you buy the land from Naomi and also from Ruth the Moabitess, you must also acquire the widow of the deceased in order to raise up the name of the deceased on his inheritance.”

RUT.4.BSB: The kinsman-redeemer replied, “I cannot redeem it myself, or I would jeopardize my own inheritance. Take my right of redemption, because I cannot redeem it.”
RUT.4.KJV: And the kinsman said, I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar my own inheritance: redeem you my right to yourself; for I cannot redeem it.
RUT.4.PLAIN: The kinsman-redeemer replied, “I cannot redeem it myself, or I would jeopardize my own inheritance. Take my right of redemption, because I cannot redeem it.”

RUT.4.BSB: Now in former times in Israel, concerning the redemption or exchange of property, to make any matter legally binding a man would remove his sandal and give it to the other party, and this was a confirmation in Israel.
RUT.4.KJV: Now this was the manner in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning changing, for to confirm all things; a man plucked off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbor: and this was a testimony in Israel.
RUT.4.PLAIN: Now in former times in Israel, concerning the redemption or exchange of property, to make any matter legally binding a man would remove his sandal and give it to the other party, and this was a confirmation in Israel.

RUT.4.BSB: So the kinsman-redeemer removed his sandal and said to Boaz, “Buy it for yourself.”
RUT.4.KJV: Therefore the kinsman said to Boaz, Buy it for you. So he drew off his shoe. ¶
RUT.4.PLAIN: So the kinsman-redeemer removed his sandal and said to Boaz, “Buy it for yourself.”

RUT.4.BSB: At this, Boaz said to the elders and all the people, “You are witnesses today that I am buying from Naomi all that belonged to Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon.
RUT.4.KJV: And Boaz said to the elders, and to all the people, You are witnesses this day, that I have bought all that was Elimelech’s, and all that was Chilion’s and Mahlon’s, of the hand of Naomi.
RUT.4.PLAIN: At this, Boaz said to the elders and all the people, “You are witnesses today that I am buying from Naomi all that belonged to Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon.

RUT.4.BSB: Moreover, I have acquired Ruth the Moabitess, Mahlon’s widow, as my wife, to raise up the name of the deceased through his inheritance, so that his name will not disappear from among his brothers or from the gate of his home. You are witnesses today.”
RUT.4.KJV: Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brothers, and from the gate of his place: you are witnesses this day.
RUT.4.PLAIN: Moreover, I have acquired Ruth the Moabitess, Mahlon’s widow, as my wife, to raise up the name of the deceased through his inheritance, so that his name will not disappear from among his brothers or from the gate of his home. You are witnesses today.”

RUT.4.BSB: “We are witnesses,” said the elders and all the people at the gate. “May the LORD make the woman entering your home like Rachel and Leah, who together built up the house of Israel. May you be prosperous in Ephrathah and famous in Bethlehem.
RUT.4.KJV: And all the people that were in the gate, and the elders, said, We are witnesses. The LORD make the woman that is come into your house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel: and do you worthily in Ephratah, and be famous in Bethlehem:
