1SA.1.BSB: Now there was a man named Elkanah who was from Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim. He was the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.

1SA.8.PLAIN: But when they said, “Give us a king to judge us,” their demand was displeasing in the sight of Samuel; so he prayed to the Lord.

1SA.8.BSB: And the LORD said to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of the people in all that they say to you. For it is not you they have rejected, but they have rejected Me as their king.
1SA.8.KJV: And the LORD said to Samuel, Listen to the voice of the people in all that they say to you: for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.
1SA.8.PLAIN: And the Lord said to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of the people in all that they say to you. For it is not you they have rejected, but they have rejected Me as their king.

1SA.8.BSB: Just as they have done from the day I brought them up out of Egypt until this day, forsaking Me and serving other gods, so they are doing to you.
1SA.8.KJV: According to all the works which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even to this day, with which they have forsaken me, and served other gods, so do they also to you.
1SA.8.PLAIN: Just as they have done from the day I brought them up out of Egypt until this day, forsaking Me and serving other gods, so they are doing to you.

1SA.8.BSB: Now listen to them, but you must solemnly warn them and show them the manner of the king who will reign over them.”
1SA.8.KJV: Now therefore listen to their voice: however, yet protest solemnly to them, and show them the manner of the king that shall reign over them. ¶
1SA.8.PLAIN: Now listen to them, but you must solemnly warn them and show them the manner of the king who will reign over them.”

1SA.8.BSB: So Samuel spoke all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking him for a king.
1SA.8.KJV: And Samuel told all the words of the LORD to the people that asked of him a king.
1SA.8.PLAIN: So Samuel spoke all the words of the Lord to the people who were asking him for a king.

1SA.8.BSB: He said, “This will be the manner of the king who will reign over you: He will take your sons and appoint them to his own chariots and horses, to run in front of his chariots.
1SA.8.KJV: And he said, This will be the manner of the king that shall reign over you: He will take your sons, and appoint them for himself, for his chariots, and to be his horsemen; and some shall run before his chariots.
1SA.8.PLAIN: He said, “This will be the manner of the king who will reign over you: He will take your sons and appoint them to his own chariots and horses, to run in front of his chariots.

1SA.8.BSB: He will appoint some for himself as commanders of thousands and of fifties, and others to plow his ground, to reap his harvest, to make his weapons of war, and to equip his chariots.
1SA.8.KJV: And he will appoint him captains over thousands, and captains over fifties; and will set them to ear his ground, and to reap his harvest, and to make his instruments of war, and instruments of his chariots.
1SA.8.PLAIN: He will appoint some for himself as commanders of thousands and of fifties, and others to plow his ground, to reap his harvest, to make his weapons of war, and to equip his chariots.

1SA.8.BSB: And he will take your daughters to be perfumers, cooks, and bakers.
1SA.8.KJV: And he will take your daughters to be confectionaries, and to be cooks, and to be bakers.
1SA.8.PLAIN: And he will take your daughters to be perfumers, cooks, and bakers.

1SA.8.BSB: He will take the best of your fields and vineyards and olive groves and give them to his servants.
1SA.8.KJV: And he will take your fields, and your vineyards, and your olive groves, even the best of them, and give them to his servants.
1SA.8.PLAIN: He will take the best of your fields and vineyards and olive groves and give them to his servants.

1SA.8.BSB: He will take a tenth of your grain and grape harvest and give it to his officials and servants.
1SA.8.KJV: And he will take the tenth of your seed, and of your vineyards, and give to his officers, and to his servants.
1SA.8.PLAIN: He will take a tenth of your grain and grape harvest and give it to his officials and servants.

1SA.8.BSB: And he will take your menservants and maidservants and your best cattle and donkeys and put them to his own use.
1SA.8.KJV: And he will take your menservants, and your maidservants, and your best young men, and your asses, and put them to his work.
1SA.8.PLAIN: And he will take your menservants and maidservants and your best cattle and donkeys and put them to his own use.

1SA.8.BSB: He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will become his slaves.
1SA.8.KJV: He will take the tenth of your sheep: and you shall be his servants.
1SA.8.PLAIN: He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will become his slaves.

1SA.8.BSB: When that day comes, you will beg for relief from the king you have chosen, but the LORD will not answer you on that day.”
1SA.8.KJV: And you shall cry out in that day because of your king which you shall have chosen you; and the LORD will not hear you in that day. ¶
1SA.8.PLAIN: When that day comes, you will beg for relief from the king you have chosen, but the Lord will not answer you on that day.”

1SA.8.BSB: Nevertheless, the people refused to listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We must have a king over us.
1SA.8.KJV: Nevertheless the people refused to obey the voice of Samuel; and they said, No; but we will have a king over us;
1SA.8.PLAIN: Nevertheless, the people refused to listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We must have a king over us.

1SA.8.BSB: Then we will be like all the other nations, with a king to judge us, to go out before us, and to fight our battles.”
1SA.8.KJV: That we also may be like all the nations; and that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles.
1SA.8.PLAIN: Then we will be like all the other nations, with a king to judge us, to go out before us, and to fight our battles.”

1SA.8.BSB: Samuel listened to all the words of the people and repeated them in the hearing of the LORD.
1SA.8.KJV: And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he rehearsed them in the ears of the LORD.
1SA.8.PLAIN: Samuel listened to all the words of the people and repeated them in the hearing of the Lord.

1SA.8.BSB: “Listen to their voice,” the LORD said to Samuel. “Appoint a king for them.” Then Samuel told the men of Israel, “Everyone must go back to his city.”
1SA.8.KJV: And the LORD said to Samuel, Listen to their voice, and make them a king. And Samuel said to the men of Israel, Go you every man to his city.
1SA.8.PLAIN: “Listen to their voice,” the Lord said to Samuel. “Appoint a king for them.” Then Samuel told the men of Israel, “Everyone must go back to his city.”

1SA.9.BSB: Now there was a Benjamite, a powerful man, whose name was Kish son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah of Benjamin.
1SA.9.KJV: Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Bechorath, the son of Aphiah, a Benjamite, a mighty man of power.
1SA.9.PLAIN: Now there was a Benjamite, a powerful man, whose name was Kish son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah of Benjamin.

1SA.9.BSB: And he had a son named Saul, choice and handsome, without equal among the Israelites—a head taller than any of the people.
1SA.9.KJV: And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a choice young man, and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he: from his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people.
1SA.9.PLAIN: And he had a son named Saul, choice and handsome, without equal among the Israelites—a head taller than any of the people.

1SA.9.BSB: One day the donkeys of Saul’s father Kish wandered off, and Kish said to his son Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
1SA.9.KJV: And the asses of Kish Saul’s father were lost. And Kish said to Saul his son, Take now one of the servants with you, and arise, go seek the asses.
1SA.9.PLAIN: One day the donkeys of Saul’s father Kish wandered off, and Kish said to his son Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”

1SA.9.BSB: So Saul passed through the hill country of Ephraim and then through the land of Shalishah, but did not find the donkeys. He and the servant went through the region of Shaalim, but they were not there. Then they went through the land of Benjamin, and still they did not find them.
1SA.9.KJV: And he passed through mount Ephraim, and passed through the land of Shalisha, but they found them not: then they passed through the land of Shalim, and there they were not: and he passed through the land of the Benjamites, but they found them not.
1SA.9.PLAIN: So Saul passed through the hill country of Ephraim and then through the land of Shalishah, but did not find the donkeys. He and the servant went through the region of Shaalim, but they were not there. Then they went through the land of Benjamin, and still they did not find them.

1SA.9.BSB: When they reached the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant, “Come, let us go back, or my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us.”
1SA.9.KJV: And when they were come to the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant that was with him, Come, and let us return; lest my father leave caring for the asses, and take thought for us.
1SA.9.PLAIN: When they reached the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant, “Come, let us go back, or my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us.”

1SA.9.BSB: “Look,” said the servant, “in this city there is a man of God who is highly respected; everything he says surely comes to pass. Let us go there now. Perhaps he will tell us which way to go.”
1SA.9.KJV: And he said to him, Behold now, there is in this city a man of God, and he is an honorable man; all that he says comes surely to pass: now let us go thither; peradventure he can show us our way that we should go.
1SA.9.PLAIN: “Look,” said the servant, “in this city there is a man of God who is highly respected; everything he says surely comes to pass. Let us go there now. Perhaps he will tell us which way to go.”

1SA.9.BSB: “If we do go,” Saul replied, “what can we give the man? For the bread in our packs is gone, and there is no gift to take to the man of God. What do we have?”
1SA.9.KJV: Then said Saul to his servant, But, behold, if we go, what shall we bring the man? for the bread is spent in our vessels, and there is not a present to bring to the man of God: what have we?
1SA.9.PLAIN: “If we do go,” Saul replied, “what can we give the man? For the bread in our packs is gone, and there is no gift to take to the man of God. What do we have?”

1SA.9.BSB: The servant answered him again. “Look,” he said, “I have here in my hand a quarter shekel of silver. I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way.”
1SA.9.KJV: And the servant answered Saul again, and said, Behold, I have here at hand the fourth part of a shekel of silver: that will I give to the man of God, to tell us our way.
1SA.9.PLAIN: The servant answered him again. “Look,” he said, “I have here in my hand a quarter shekel of silver. I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way.”

1SA.9.BSB: (Formerly in Israel, a man on his way to inquire of God would say, “Come, let us go to the seer.” For the prophet of today was formerly called the seer.)
1SA.9.KJV: (Beforetime in Israel, when a man went to inquire of God, thus he spoke, Come, and let us go to the seer: for he that is now called a Prophet was beforetime called a Seer.)
1SA.9.PLAIN: (Formerly in Israel, a man on his way to inquire of God would say, “Come, let us go to the seer.” For the prophet of today was formerly called the seer.)

1SA.9.BSB: “Good,” said Saul to his servant. “Come, let us go.” So they set out for the city where the man of God was.
1SA.9.KJV: Then said Saul to his servant, Well said; come, let us go. So they went to the city where the man of God was. ¶
1SA.9.PLAIN: “Good,” said Saul to his servant. “Come, let us go.” So they set out for the city where the man of God was.

1SA.9.BSB: And as they were climbing the hill to the city, they met some young women coming out to draw water and asked, “Is the seer here?”
1SA.9.KJV: And as they went up the hill to the city, they found young maidens going out to draw water, and said to them, Is the seer here?
1SA.9.PLAIN: And as they were climbing the hill to the city, they met some young women coming out to draw water and asked, “Is the seer here?”

1SA.9.BSB: “Yes, he is ahead of you,” they answered. “Hurry now, for today he has come to the city because the people have a sacrifice on the high place.
1SA.9.KJV: And they answered them, and said, He is; behold, he is before you: make haste now, for he came to day to the city; for there is a sacrifice of the people to day in the high place:
1SA.9.PLAIN: “Yes, he is ahead of you,” they answered. “Hurry now, for today he has come to the city because the people have a sacrifice on the high place.

1SA.9.BSB: As soon as you enter the city, you will find him before he goes up to the high place to eat. The people will not eat until he comes, because he must bless the sacrifice; after that, the guests will eat. Go up at once; you will find him.”
1SA.9.KJV: As soon as you be come into the city, you shall straightway find him, before he go up to the high place to eat: for the people will not eat until he come, because he does bless the sacrifice; and afterwards they eat that be bidden. Now therefore get you up; for about this time you shall find him.
1SA.9.PLAIN: As soon as you enter the city, you will find him before he goes up to the high place to eat. The people will not eat until he comes, because he must bless the sacrifice; after that, the guests will eat. Go up at once; you will find him.”

1SA.9.BSB: So Saul and his servant went up toward the city, and as they were entering it, there was Samuel coming toward them on his way up to the high place.
1SA.9.KJV: And they went up into the city: and when they were come into the city, behold, Samuel came out against them, for to go up to the high place. ¶
1SA.9.PLAIN: So Saul and his servant went up toward the city, and as they were entering it, there was Samuel coming toward them on his way up to the high place.

1SA.9.BSB: Now on the day before Saul’s arrival, the LORD had revealed to Samuel,
1SA.9.KJV: Now the LORD had told Samuel in his ear a day before Saul came, saying,
1SA.9.PLAIN: Now on the day before Saul’s arrival, the Lord had revealed to Samuel,

1SA.9.BSB: “At this time tomorrow I will send you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you are to anoint him leader over My people Israel; he will save them from the hand of the Philistines. For I have looked upon My people, because their cry has come to Me.”
1SA.9.KJV: To morrow about this time I will send you a man out of the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him to be captain over my people Israel, that he may save my people out of the hand of the Philistines: for I have looked on my people, because their cry is come to me.
1SA.9.PLAIN: “At this time tomorrow I will send you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you are to anoint him leader over My people Israel; he will save them from the hand of the Philistines. For I have looked upon My people, because their cry has come to Me.”

1SA.9.BSB: When Samuel saw Saul, the LORD told him, “Here is the man of whom I spoke; he shall rule over My people.”
1SA.9.KJV: And when Samuel saw Saul, the LORD said to him, Behold the man whom I spoke to you of! this same shall reign over my people.
1SA.9.PLAIN: When Samuel saw Saul, the Lord told him, “Here is the man of whom I spoke; he shall rule over My people.”

1SA.9.BSB: Saul approached Samuel in the gateway and asked, “Would you please tell me where the seer’s house is?”
1SA.9.KJV: Then Saul drew near to Samuel in the gate, and said, Tell me, I pray you, where the seer’s house is.
1SA.9.PLAIN: Saul approached Samuel in the gateway and asked, “Would you please tell me where the seer’s house is?”

1SA.9.BSB: “I am the seer,” Samuel replied. “Go up before me to the high place, for you shall eat with me today. And when I send you off in the morning, I will tell you all that is in your heart.
1SA.9.KJV: And Samuel answered Saul, and said, I am the seer: go up before me to the high place; for you shall eat with me to day, and to morrow I will let you go, and will tell you all that is in your heart.
1SA.9.PLAIN: “I am the seer,” Samuel replied. “Go up before me to the high place, for you shall eat with me today. And when I send you off in the morning, I will tell you all that is in your heart.

1SA.9.BSB: As for the donkeys you lost three days ago, do not worry about them, for they have been found. And upon whom is all the desire of Israel, if not upon you and all your father’s house?”
1SA.9.KJV: And as for your asses that were lost three days ago, set not your mind on them; for they are found. And on whom is all the desire of Israel? Is it not on you, and on all your father’s house?
1SA.9.PLAIN: As for the donkeys you lost three days ago, do not worry about them, for they have been found. And upon whom is all the desire of Israel, if not upon you and all your father’s house?”

1SA.9.BSB: Saul replied, “Am I not a Benjamite from the smallest tribe of Israel, and is not my clan the least of all the clans of Benjamin? So why would you say such a thing to me?”
1SA.9.KJV: And Saul answered and said, Am not I a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel? and my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? why then speak you so to me?
1SA.9.PLAIN: Saul replied, “Am I not a Benjamite from the smallest tribe of Israel, and is not my clan the least of all the clans of Benjamin? So why would you say such a thing to me?”

1SA.9.BSB: Then Samuel took Saul and his servant, brought them into the hall, and seated them in the place of honor among those who were invited—about thirty in all.
1SA.9.KJV: And Samuel took Saul and his servant, and brought them into the parlor, and made them sit in the most chief place among them that were bidden, which were about thirty persons.
1SA.9.PLAIN: Then Samuel took Saul and his servant, brought them into the hall, and seated them in the place of honor among those who were invited—about thirty in all.

1SA.9.BSB: And Samuel said to the cook, “Bring the portion I gave you and told you to set aside.”
1SA.9.KJV: And Samuel said to the cook, Bring the portion which I gave you, of which I said to you, Set it by you.
1SA.9.PLAIN: And Samuel said to the cook, “Bring the portion I gave you and told you to set aside.”

1SA.9.BSB: So the cook picked up the leg and what was attached to it and set it before Saul. Then Samuel said, “Here is what was kept back. It was set apart for you. Eat, for it has been kept for you for this occasion, from the time I said, ‘I have invited the people.’” So Saul dined with Samuel that day.
1SA.9.KJV: And the cook took up the shoulder, and that which was on it, and set it before Saul. And Samuel said, Behold that which is left! set it before you, and eat: for to this time has it been kept for you since I said, I have invited the people. So Saul did eat with Samuel that day. ¶
1SA.9.PLAIN: So the cook picked up the leg and what was attached to it and set it before Saul. Then Samuel said, “Here is what was kept back. It was set apart for you. Eat, for it has been kept for you for this occasion, from the time I said, ‘I have invited the people.’” So Saul dined with Samuel that day.

1SA.9.BSB: And after they had come down from the high place into the city, Samuel spoke with Saul on the roof of his house.
1SA.9.KJV: And when they were come down from the high place into the city, Samuel communed with Saul on the top of the house.
1SA.9.PLAIN: And after they had come down from the high place into the city, Samuel spoke with Saul on the roof of his house.

1SA.9.BSB: They got up early in the morning, and just before dawn Samuel called to Saul on the roof, “Get ready, and I will send you on your way!” So Saul arose, and both he and Samuel went outside together.
1SA.9.KJV: And they arose early: and it came to pass about the spring of the day, that Samuel called Saul to the top of the house, saying, Up, that I may send you away. And Saul arose, and they went out both of them, he and Samuel, abroad.
1SA.9.PLAIN: They got up early in the morning, and just before dawn Samuel called to Saul on the roof, “Get ready, and I will send you on your way!” So Saul arose, and both he and Samuel went outside together.

1SA.9.BSB: As they were going down to the edge of the city, Samuel said to Saul, “Tell the servant to go on ahead of us, but you stay for a while, and I will reveal to you the word of God.” So the servant went on.
1SA.9.KJV: And as they were going down to the end of the city, Samuel said to Saul, Bid the servant pass on before us, (and he passed on), but stand you still a while, that I may show you the word of God.
1SA.9.PLAIN: As they were going down to the edge of the city, Samuel said to Saul, “Tell the servant to go on ahead of us, but you stay for a while, and I will reveal to you the word of God.” So the servant went on.

1SA.10.BSB: Then Samuel took a flask of oil, poured it on Saul’s head, kissed him, and said, “Has not the LORD anointed you ruler over His inheritance?
1SA.10.KJV: Then Samuel took a vial of oil, and poured it on his head, and kissed him, and said, Is it not because the LORD has anointed you to be captain over his inheritance?
1SA.10.PLAIN: Then Samuel took a flask of oil, poured it on Saul’s head, kissed him, and said, “Has not the Lord anointed you ruler over His inheritance?

1SA.10.BSB: When you leave me today, you will find two men at Rachel’s tomb in Zelzah on the border of Benjamin. They will say to you, ‘The donkeys you seek have been found, and now your father has stopped worrying about the donkeys and started worrying about you, asking, “What should I do about my son?”’
1SA.10.KJV: When you are departed from me to day, then you shall find two men by Rachel’s sepulcher in the border of Benjamin at Zelzah; and they will say to you, The asses which you went to seek are found: and, see, your father has left the care of the asses, and sorrows for you, saying, What shall I do for my son?
1SA.10.PLAIN: When you leave me today, you will find two men at Rachel’s tomb in Zelzah on the border of Benjamin. They will say to you, ‘The donkeys you seek have been found, and now your father has stopped worrying about the donkeys and started worrying about you, asking, “What should I do about my son?”’

1SA.10.BSB: Then you will go on from there until you come to the Oak of Tabor. Three men going up to God at Bethel will meet you there, one carrying three young goats, another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a skin of wine.
1SA.10.KJV: Then shall you go on forward from there, and you shall come to the plain of Tabor, and there shall meet you three men going up to God to Bethel, one carrying three kids, and another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a bottle of wine:
1SA.10.PLAIN: Then you will go on from there until you come to the Oak of Tabor. Three men going up to God at Bethel will meet you there, one carrying three young goats, another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a skin of wine.

1SA.10.BSB: They will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you will accept from their hands.
1SA.10.KJV: And they will salute you, and give you two loaves of bread; which you shall receive of their hands.
1SA.10.PLAIN: They will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you will accept from their hands.

1SA.10.BSB: After that you will come to Gibeah of God, where the Philistines have an outpost. As you approach the city, you will meet a group of prophets coming down from the high place, preceded by harps, tambourines, flutes, and lyres, and they will be prophesying.
1SA.10.KJV: After that you shall come to the hill of God, where is the garrison of the Philistines: and it shall come to pass, when you are come thither to the city, that you shall meet a company of prophets coming down from the high place with a psaltery, and a tabret, and a pipe, and a harp, before them; and they shall prophesy:
1SA.10.PLAIN: After that you will come to Gibeah of God, where the Philistines have an outpost. As you approach the city, you will meet a group of prophets coming down from the high place, preceded by harps, tambourines, flutes, and lyres, and they will be prophesying.

1SA.10.BSB: Then the Spirit of the LORD will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them; and you will be transformed into a different person.
1SA.10.KJV: And the Spirit of the LORD will come on you, and you shall prophesy with them, and shall be turned into another man.
1SA.10.PLAIN: Then the Spirit of the Lord will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them; and you will be transformed into a different person.

1SA.10.BSB: When these signs have come, do as the occasion demands, for God is with you.
1SA.10.KJV: And let it be, when these signs are come to you, that you do as occasion serve you; for God is with you.
1SA.10.PLAIN: When these signs have come, do as the occasion demands, for God is with you.

1SA.10.BSB: And you shall go before me to Gilgal, and surely I will come to you to offer burnt offerings and to sacrifice peace offerings. Wait seven days until I come to you and show you what you are to do.”
1SA.10.KJV: And you shall go down before me to Gilgal; and, behold, I will come down to you, to offer burnt offerings, and to sacrifice sacrifices of peace offerings: seven days shall you tarry, till I come to you, and show you what you shall do. ¶
1SA.10.PLAIN: And you shall go before me to Gilgal, and surely I will come to you to offer burnt offerings and to sacrifice peace offerings. Wait seven days until I come to you and show you what you are to do.”

1SA.10.BSB: As Saul turned to leave Samuel, God changed Saul’s heart, and all the signs came to pass that day.
1SA.10.KJV: And it was so, that when he had turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart: and all those signs came to pass that day.
1SA.10.PLAIN: As Saul turned to leave Samuel, God changed Saul’s heart, and all the signs came to pass that day.

1SA.10.BSB: When Saul and his servant arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. Then the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied along with them.
1SA.10.KJV: And when they came thither to the hill, behold, a company of prophets met him; and the Spirit of God came on him, and he prophesied among them.
1SA.10.PLAIN: When Saul and his servant arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. Then the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied along with them.

1SA.10.BSB: All those who had formerly known Saul and saw him prophesying with the prophets asked one another, “What has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?”
1SA.10.KJV: And it came to pass, when all that knew him beforetime saw that, behold, he prophesied among the prophets, then the people said one to another, What is this that is come to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?
1SA.10.PLAIN: All those who had formerly known Saul and saw him prophesying with the prophets asked one another, “What has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?”

1SA.10.BSB: Then a man who lived there replied, “And who is their father?” So the saying became a proverb: “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
1SA.10.KJV: And one of the same place answered and said, But who is their father? Therefore it became a proverb, Is Saul also among the prophets?

1SA.13.BSB: And all Israel heard the news: “Saul has attacked an outpost of the Philistines, and now Israel has become a stench to the Philistines!” Then the people were summoned to join Saul at Gilgal.
1SA.13.KJV: And all Israel heard say that Saul had smitten a garrison of the Philistines, and that Israel also was had in abomination with the Philistines. And the people were called together after Saul to Gilgal. ¶
1SA.13.PLAIN: And all Israel heard the news: “Saul has attacked an outpost of the Philistines, and now Israel has become a stench to the Philistines!” Then the people were summoned to join Saul at Gilgal.

1SA.13.BSB: Now the Philistines assembled to fight against Israel with three thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and troops as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They went up and camped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.
1SA.13.KJV: And the Philistines gathered themselves together to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand which is on the sea shore in multitude: and they came up, and pitched in Michmash, eastward from Bethaven.
1SA.13.PLAIN: Now the Philistines assembled to fight against Israel with three thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and troops as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They went up and camped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.

1SA.13.BSB: Seeing that they were in danger because their troops were hard-pressed, the men of Israel hid in caves and thickets, among the rocks, and in cellars and cisterns.
1SA.13.KJV: When the men of Israel saw that they were in a strait, (for the people were distressed,) then the people did hide themselves in caves, and in thickets, and in rocks, and in high places, and in pits.
1SA.13.PLAIN: Seeing that they were in danger because their troops were hard-pressed, the men of Israel hid in caves and thickets, among the rocks, and in cellars and cisterns.

1SA.13.BSB: Some Hebrews even crossed the Jordan into the land of Gad and Gilead. Saul, however, remained at Gilgal, and all his troops were quaking in fear.
1SA.13.KJV: And some of the Hebrews went over Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. As for Saul, he was yet in Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling. ¶
1SA.13.PLAIN: Some Hebrews even crossed the Jordan into the land of Gad and Gilead. Saul, however, remained at Gilgal, and all his troops were quaking in fear.

1SA.13.BSB: And Saul waited seven days for the time appointed by Samuel, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the troops began to desert Saul.
1SA.13.KJV: And he tarried seven days, according to the set time that Samuel had appointed: but Samuel came not to Gilgal; and the people were scattered from him.
1SA.13.PLAIN: And Saul waited seven days for the time appointed by Samuel, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the troops began to desert Saul.

1SA.13.BSB: So he said, “Bring me the burnt offering and the peace offerings.” And he offered up the burnt offering.
1SA.13.KJV: And Saul said, Bring here a burnt offering to me, and peace offerings. And he offered the burnt offering.
1SA.13.PLAIN: So he said, “Bring me the burnt offering and the peace offerings.” And he offered up the burnt offering.

1SA.13.BSB: Just as he finished offering the burnt offering, Samuel arrived, and Saul went out to greet him.
1SA.13.KJV: And it came to pass, that as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came; and Saul went out to meet him, that he might salute him. ¶
1SA.13.PLAIN: Just as he finished offering the burnt offering, Samuel arrived, and Saul went out to greet him.

1SA.13.BSB: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. And Saul replied, “When I saw that the troops were deserting me, and that you did not come at the appointed time and the Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
1SA.13.KJV: And Samuel said, What have you done? And Saul said, Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that you came not within the days appointed, and that the Philistines gathered themselves together at Michmash;
1SA.13.PLAIN: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. And Saul replied, “When I saw that the troops were deserting me, and that you did not come at the appointed time and the Philistines were gathering at Michmash,

1SA.13.BSB: I thought, ‘Now the Philistines will descend upon me at Gilgal, and I have not sought the favor of the LORD.’ So I felt compelled to offer the burnt offering.”
1SA.13.KJV: Therefore said I, The Philistines will come down now on me to Gilgal, and I have not made supplication to the LORD: I forced myself therefore, and offered a burnt offering.
1SA.13.PLAIN: I thought, ‘Now the Philistines will descend upon me at Gilgal, and I have not sought the favor of the Lord.’ So I felt compelled to offer the burnt offering.”

1SA.13.BSB: “You have acted foolishly,” Samuel declared. “You have not kept the command that the LORD your God gave you; if you had, the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel for all time.
1SA.13.KJV: And Samuel said to Saul, You have done foolishly: you have not kept the commandment of the LORD your God, which he commanded you: for now would the LORD have established your kingdom on Israel for ever.
1SA.13.PLAIN: “You have acted foolishly,” Samuel declared. “You have not kept the command that the Lord your God gave you; if you had, the Lord would have established your kingdom over Israel for all time.

1SA.13.BSB: But now your kingdom will not endure; the LORD has sought a man after His own heart and appointed him ruler over His people, because you have not kept the command of the LORD.”
1SA.13.KJV: But now your kingdom shall not continue: the LORD has sought him a man after his own heart, and the LORD has commanded him to be captain over his people, because you have not kept that which the LORD commanded you.
1SA.13.PLAIN: But now your kingdom will not endure; the Lord has sought a man after His own heart and appointed him ruler over His people, because you have not kept the command of the Lord.”

1SA.13.BSB: Then Samuel set out from Gilgal and went up to Gibeah in Benjamin. And Saul numbered the troops who were with him, about six hundred men.
1SA.13.KJV: And Samuel arose, and got him up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people that were present with him, about six hundred men.
1SA.13.PLAIN: Then Samuel set out from Gilgal and went up to Gibeah in Benjamin. And Saul numbered the troops who were with him, about six hundred men.

1SA.13.BSB: Now Saul and Jonathan his son and the troops with them were staying in Geba of Benjamin, while the Philistines camped at Michmash.
1SA.13.KJV: And Saul, and Jonathan his son, and the people that were present with them, stayed in Gibeah of Benjamin: but the Philistines encamped in Michmash. ¶
1SA.13.PLAIN: Now Saul and Jonathan his son and the troops with them were staying in Geba of Benjamin, while the Philistines camped at Michmash.

1SA.13.BSB: And raiders went out of the Philistine camp in three divisions. One headed toward Ophrah in the land of Shual,
1SA.13.KJV: And the spoilers came out of the camp of the Philistines in three companies: one company turned to the way that leads to Ophrah, to the land of Shual:
1SA.13.PLAIN: And raiders went out of the Philistine camp in three divisions. One headed toward Ophrah in the land of Shual,

1SA.13.BSB: another toward Beth-horon, and the third down the border road overlooking the Valley of Zeboim facing the wilderness.
1SA.13.KJV: And another company turned the way to Bethhoron: and another company turned to the way of the border that looks to the valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness. ¶
1SA.13.PLAIN: another toward Beth-horon, and the third down the border road overlooking the Valley of Zeboim facing the wilderness.

1SA.13.BSB: And no blacksmith could be found in all the land of Israel, because the Philistines had said, “The Hebrews must not be allowed to make swords or spears.”
1SA.13.KJV: Now there was no smith found throughout all the land of Israel: for the Philistines said, Lest the Hebrews make them swords or spears:
1SA.13.PLAIN: And no blacksmith could be found in all the land of Israel, because the Philistines had said, “The Hebrews must not be allowed to make swords or spears.”

1SA.13.BSB: Instead, all the Israelites would go down to the Philistines to sharpen their plowshares, mattocks, axes, and sickles.
1SA.13.KJV: But all the Israelites went down to the Philistines, to sharpen every man his share, and his coulter, and his ax, and his mattock.
1SA.13.PLAIN: Instead, all the Israelites would go down to the Philistines to sharpen their plowshares, mattocks, axes, and sickles.

1SA.13.BSB: The charge was a pim for sharpening a plowshare or mattock, a third of a shekel for sharpening a pitchfork or an axe, and a third of a shekel for repointing an oxgoad.
1SA.13.KJV: Yet they had a file for the mattocks, and for the coulters, and for the forks, and for the axes, and to sharpen the goads.
1SA.13.PLAIN: The charge was a pim for sharpening a plowshare or mattock, a third of a shekel for sharpening a pitchfork or an axe, and a third of a shekel for repointing an oxgoad.

1SA.13.BSB: So on the day of battle not a sword or spear could be found in the hands of the troops with Saul and Jonathan; only Saul and his son Jonathan had weapons.
1SA.13.KJV: So it came to pass in the day of battle, that there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people that were with Saul and Jonathan: but with Saul and with Jonathan his son was there found.
1SA.13.PLAIN: So on the day of battle not a sword or spear could be found in the hands of the troops with Saul and Jonathan; only Saul and his son Jonathan had weapons.

1SA.13.BSB: And a garrison of the Philistines had gone out to the pass at Michmash.
1SA.13.KJV: And the garrison of the Philistines went out to the passage of Michmash.
1SA.13.PLAIN: And a garrison of the Philistines had gone out to the pass at Michmash.

1SA.14.BSB: One day Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man bearing his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the Philistine outpost on the other side.” But Jonathan did not tell his father.
1SA.14.KJV: Now it came to pass on a day, that Jonathan the son of Saul said to the young man that bore his armor, Come, and let us go over to the Philistines’ garrison, that is on the other side. But he told not his father.
1SA.14.PLAIN: One day Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man bearing his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the Philistine outpost on the other side.” But Jonathan did not tell his father.

1SA.14.BSB: Meanwhile, Saul was staying under the pomegranate tree in Migron on the outskirts of Gibeah. And the troops who were with him numbered about six hundred men,
1SA.14.KJV: And Saul tarried in the uttermost part of Gibeah under a pomegranate tree which is in Migron: and the people that were with him were about six hundred men;
1SA.14.PLAIN: Meanwhile, Saul was staying under the pomegranate tree in Migron on the outskirts of Gibeah. And the troops who were with him numbered about six hundred men,

1SA.14.BSB: including Ahijah, who was wearing an ephod. He was the son of Ichabod’s brother Ahitub son of Phinehas, the son of Eli the priest of the LORD in Shiloh. But the troops did not know that Jonathan had left.
1SA.14.KJV: And Ahiah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod’s brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the LORD’s priest in Shiloh, wearing an ephod. And the people knew not that Jonathan was gone. ¶
1SA.14.PLAIN: including Ahijah, who was wearing an ephod. He was the son of Ichabod’s brother Ahitub son of Phinehas, the son of Eli the priest of the Lord in Shiloh. But the troops did not know that Jonathan had left.

1SA.14.BSB: Now there were cliffs on both sides of the pass that Jonathan intended to cross to reach the Philistine outpost. One was named Bozez and the other Seneh.
1SA.14.KJV: And between the passages, by which Jonathan sought to go over to the Philistines’ garrison, there was a sharp rock on the one side, and a sharp rock on the other side: and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.
1SA.14.PLAIN: Now there were cliffs on both sides of the pass that Jonathan intended to cross to reach the Philistine outpost. One was named Bozez and the other Seneh.

1SA.14.BSB: One cliff stood to the north toward Michmash, and the other to the south toward Geba.
1SA.14.KJV: The forefront of the one was situate northward over against Michmash, and the other southward over against Gibeah.
1SA.14.PLAIN: One cliff stood to the north toward Michmash, and the other to the south toward Geba.

1SA.14.BSB: Jonathan said to the young man bearing his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the outpost of these uncircumcised men. Perhaps the LORD will work on our behalf. Nothing can hinder the LORD from saving, whether by many or by few.”
1SA.14.KJV: And Jonathan said to the young man that bore his armor, Come, and let us go over to the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that the LORD will work for us: for there is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few.
1SA.14.PLAIN: Jonathan said to the young man bearing his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the outpost of these uncircumcised men. Perhaps the Lord will work on our behalf. Nothing can hinder the Lord from saving, whether by many or by few.”

1SA.14.BSB: His armor-bearer replied, “Do all that is in your heart. Go ahead; I am with you heart and soul.”
1SA.14.KJV: And his armor bearer said to him, Do all that is in your heart: turn you; behold, I am with you according to your heart.
1SA.14.PLAIN: His armor-bearer replied, “Do all that is in your heart. Go ahead; I am with you heart and soul.”

1SA.14.BSB: “Very well,” said Jonathan, “we will cross over toward these men and show ourselves to them.
1SA.14.KJV: Then said Jonathan, Behold, we will pass over to these men, and we will discover ourselves to them.
1SA.14.PLAIN: “Very well,” said Jonathan, “we will cross over toward these men and show ourselves to them.

1SA.14.BSB: If they say, ‘Wait until we come to you,’ then we will stay where we are and will not go up to them.
1SA.14.KJV: If they say thus to us, Tarry until we come to you; then we will stand still in our place, and will not go up to them.
1SA.14.PLAIN: If they say, ‘Wait until we come to you,’ then we will stay where we are and will not go up to them.

1SA.14.BSB: But if they say, ‘Come on up,’ then we will go up, because this will be our sign that the LORD has delivered them into our hands.”
1SA.14.KJV: But if they say thus, Come up to us; then we will go up: for the LORD has delivered them into our hand: and this shall be a sign to us.
1SA.14.PLAIN: But if they say, ‘Come on up,’ then we will go up, because this will be our sign that the Lord has delivered them into our hands.”

1SA.14.BSB: So the two of them showed themselves to the outpost of the Philistines, who exclaimed, “Look, the Hebrews are coming out of the holes in which they were hiding!”
1SA.14.KJV: And both of them discovered themselves to the garrison of the Philistines: and the Philistines said, Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves.
1SA.14.PLAIN: So the two of them showed themselves to the outpost of the Philistines, who exclaimed, “Look, the Hebrews are coming out of the holes in which they were hiding!”

1SA.14.BSB: So the men of the outpost called out to Jonathan and his armor-bearer, “Come on up, and we will teach you a lesson!” “Follow me,” Jonathan told his armor-bearer, “for the LORD has delivered them into the hand of Israel.”
1SA.14.KJV: And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armor bearer, and said, Come up to us, and we will show you a thing. And Jonathan said to his armor bearer, Come up after me: for the LORD has delivered them into the hand of Israel.
1SA.14.PLAIN: So the men of the outpost called out to Jonathan and his armor-bearer, “Come on up, and we will teach you a lesson!” “Follow me,” Jonathan told his armor-bearer, “for the Lord has delivered them into the hand of Israel.”

1SA.14.BSB: So Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer behind him. And the Philistines fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer followed and finished them off.
1SA.14.KJV: And Jonathan climbed up on his hands and on his feet, and his armor bearer after him: and they fell before Jonathan; and his armor bearer slew after him.
1SA.14.PLAIN: So Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer behind him. And the Philistines fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer followed and finished them off.

1SA.14.BSB: In that first assault, Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down about twenty men over half an acre of land.
1SA.14.KJV: And that first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armor bearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were an half acre of land, which a yoke of oxen might plow.
1SA.14.PLAIN: In that first assault, Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down about twenty men over half an acre of land.

1SA.14.BSB: Then terror struck the Philistines in the camp, in the field, and among all the people. Even those in the outposts and raiding parties trembled. Indeed, the earth quaked and panic spread from God.
1SA.14.KJV: And there was trembling in the host, in the field, and among all the people: the garrison, and the spoilers, they also trembled, and the earth quaked: so it was a very great trembling.
1SA.14.PLAIN: Then terror struck the Philistines in the camp, in the field, and among all the people. Even those in the outposts and raiding parties trembled. Indeed, the earth quaked and panic spread from God.

1SA.14.BSB: Now when Saul’s watchmen at Gibeah in Benjamin looked and saw the troops melting away and scattering in every direction,
1SA.14.KJV: And the watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and, behold, the multitude melted away, and they went on beating down one another.
1SA.14.PLAIN: Now when Saul’s watchmen at Gibeah in Benjamin looked and saw the troops melting away and scattering in every direction,

1SA.14.BSB: Saul said to the troops who were with him, “Call the roll and see who has left us.” And when they had called the roll, they saw that Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.
1SA.14.KJV: Then said Saul to the people that were with him, Number now, and see who is gone from us. And when they had numbered, behold, Jonathan and his armor bearer were not there.
1SA.14.PLAIN: Saul said to the troops who were with him, “Call the roll and see who has left us.” And when they had called the roll, they saw that Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.

1SA.14.BSB: Then Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring the ark of God.” (For at that time it was with the Israelites.)
1SA.14.KJV: And Saul said to Ahiah, Bring here the ark of God. For the ark of God was at that time with the children of Israel. ¶
1SA.14.PLAIN: Then Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring the ark of God.” (For at that time it was with the Israelites.)

1SA.14.BSB: While Saul was talking to the priest, the commotion in the Philistine camp continued to increase. So Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand.”
1SA.14.KJV: And it came to pass, while Saul talked to the priest, that the noise that was in the host of the Philistines went on and increased: and Saul said to the priest, Withdraw your hand.
1SA.14.PLAIN: While Saul was talking to the priest, the commotion in the Philistine camp continued to increase. So Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand.”

1SA.14.BSB: Then Saul and all his troops assembled and marched to the battle, and they found the Philistines in total confusion, with each man wielding the sword against his neighbor.
1SA.14.KJV: And Saul and all the people that were with him assembled themselves, and they came to the battle: and, behold, every man’s sword was against his fellow, and there was a very great discomfiture.
1SA.14.PLAIN: Then Saul and all his troops assembled and marched to the battle, and they found the Philistines in total confusion, with each man wielding the sword against his neighbor.

1SA.14.BSB: And the Hebrews who had previously gone up into the surrounding camps of the Philistines now went over to the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.
1SA.14.KJV: Moreover the Hebrews that were with the Philistines before that time, which went up with them into the camp from the country round about, even they also turned to be with the Israelites that were with Saul and Jonathan.
1SA.14.PLAIN: And the Hebrews who had previously gone up into the surrounding camps of the Philistines now went over to the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.

1SA.14.BSB: When all the Israelites who had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines were fleeing, they also joined Saul and Jonathan in the battle.
1SA.14.KJV: Likewise all the men of Israel which had hid themselves in mount Ephraim, when they heard that the Philistines fled, even they also followed hard after them in the battle.
1SA.14.PLAIN: When all the Israelites who had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines were fleeing, they also joined Saul and Jonathan in the battle.

1SA.14.BSB: So the LORD saved Israel that day, and the battle moved on beyond Beth-aven.
1SA.14.KJV: So the LORD saved Israel that day: and the battle passed over to Bethaven. ¶
1SA.14.PLAIN: So the Lord saved Israel that day, and the battle moved on beyond Beth-aven.

1SA.14.BSB: Now the men of Israel were in distress that day, for Saul had placed the troops under an oath, saying, “Cursed is the man who eats any food before evening, before I have taken vengeance on my enemies.” So none of the troops tasted any food.
1SA.14.KJV: And the men of Israel were distressed that day: for Saul had adjured the people, saying, Cursed be the man that eats any food until evening, that I may be avenged on my enemies. So none of the people tasted any food.
1SA.14.PLAIN: Now the men of Israel were in distress that day, for Saul had placed the troops under an oath, saying, “Cursed is the man who eats any food before evening, before I have taken vengeance on my enemies.” So none of the troops tasted any food.

1SA.14.BSB: Then all the troops entered the forest, and there was honey on the ground.
1SA.14.KJV: And all they of the land came to a wood; and there was honey on the ground.
1SA.14.PLAIN: Then all the troops entered the forest, and there was honey on the ground.

1SA.14.BSB: And when they entered the forest and saw the flowing honey, not one of them put his hand to his mouth, because they feared the oath.
1SA.14.KJV: And when the people were come into the wood, behold, the honey dropped; but no man put his hand to his mouth: for the people feared the oath.
1SA.14.PLAIN: And when they entered the forest and saw the flowing honey, not one of them put his hand to his mouth, because they feared the oath.

1SA.14.BSB: Jonathan, however, had not heard that his father had charged the people with the oath. So he reached out the end of the staff in his hand, dipped it into the honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes brightened.
1SA.14.KJV: But Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath: why he put forth the end of the rod that was in his hand, and dipped it in an honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes were enlightened.
1SA.14.PLAIN: Jonathan, however, had not heard that his father had charged the people with the oath. So he reached out the end of the staff in his hand, dipped it into the honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes brightened.

1SA.14.BSB: Then one of the soldiers told him, “Your father bound the troops with a solemn oath, saying, ‘Cursed is the man who eats food today.’ That is why the people are faint.”
1SA.14.KJV: Then answered one of the people, and said, Your father straightly charged the people with an oath, saying, Cursed be the man that eats any food this day. And the people were faint.
1SA.14.PLAIN: Then one of the soldiers told him, “Your father bound the troops with a solemn oath, saying, ‘Cursed is the man who eats food today.’ That is why the people are faint.”

1SA.14.BSB: “My father has brought trouble to the land,” Jonathan replied. “Just look at how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.
1SA.14.KJV: Then said Jonathan, My father has troubled the land: see, I pray you, how my eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey.
1SA.14.PLAIN: “My father has brought trouble to the land,” Jonathan replied. “Just look at how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.

1SA.14.BSB: How much better it would have been if the troops had eaten freely today from the plunder they took from their enemies! Would not the slaughter of the Philistines have been much greater?”
1SA.14.KJV: How much more, if haply the people had eaten freely to day of the spoil of their enemies which they found? for had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines?
1SA.14.PLAIN: How much better it would have been if the troops had eaten freely today from the plunder they took from their enemies! Would not the slaughter of the Philistines have been much greater?”

1SA.14.BSB: That day, after the Israelites had struck down the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon, the people were very faint.
1SA.14.KJV: And they smote the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon: and the people were very faint.
1SA.14.PLAIN: That day, after the Israelites had struck down the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon, the people were very faint.

1SA.14.BSB: So they rushed greedily to the plunder, taking sheep, cattle, and calves. They slaughtered them on the ground and ate meat with the blood still in it.
1SA.14.KJV: And the people flew on the spoil, and took sheep, and oxen, and calves, and slew them on the ground: and the people did eat them with the blood. ¶
1SA.14.PLAIN: So they rushed greedily to the plunder, taking sheep, cattle, and calves. They slaughtered them on the ground and ate meat with the blood still in it.

1SA.14.BSB: Then someone reported to Saul: “Look, the troops are sinning against the LORD by eating meat with the blood still in it.” “You have broken faith,” said Saul. “Roll a large stone over here at once.”
1SA.14.KJV: Then they told Saul, saying, Behold, the people sin against the LORD, in that they eat with the blood. And he said, You have transgressed: roll a great stone to me this day.
1SA.14.PLAIN: Then someone reported to Saul: “Look, the troops are sinning against the Lord by eating meat with the blood still in it.” “You have broken faith,” said Saul. “Roll a large stone over here at once.”

1SA.14.BSB: Then he said, “Go among the troops and tell them, ‘Each man must bring me his ox or his sheep, slaughter them in this place, and then eat. Do not sin against the LORD by eating meat with the blood still in it.’” So that night everyone brought his ox and slaughtered it there.
1SA.14.KJV: And Saul said, Disperse yourselves among the people, and say to them, Bring me here every man his ox, and every man his sheep, and slay them here, and eat; and sin not against the LORD in eating with the blood. And all the people brought every man his ox with him that night, and slew them there.
1SA.14.PLAIN: Then he said, “Go among the troops and tell them, ‘Each man must bring me his ox or his sheep, slaughter them in this place, and then eat. Do not sin against the Lord by eating meat with the blood still in it.’” So that night everyone brought his ox and slaughtered it there.

1SA.14.BSB: Then Saul built an altar to the LORD; it was the first time he had built an altar to the LORD.
1SA.14.KJV: And Saul built an altar to the LORD: the same was the first altar that he built to the LORD. ¶
1SA.14.PLAIN: Then Saul built an altar to the Lord; it was the first time he had built an altar to the Lord.

1SA.14.BSB: And Saul said, “Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder them until dawn, leaving no man alive!” “Do what seems good to you,” the troops replied. But the priest said, “We must consult God here.”
1SA.14.KJV: And Saul said, Let us go down after the Philistines by night, and spoil them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man of them. And they said, Do whatever seems good to you. Then said the priest, Let us draw near here to God.
