1SA.21.PLAIN: That day David fled from Saul and went to Achish king of Gath.

1SA.21.BSB: But the servants of Achish said to him, “Is this not David, the king of the land? Did they not sing about him in their dances, saying: ‘Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands’?”
1SA.21.KJV: And the servants of Achish said to him, Is not this David the king of the land? did they not sing one to another of him in dances, saying, Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands?
1SA.21.PLAIN: But the servants of Achish said to him, “Is this not David, the king of the land? Did they not sing about him in their dances, saying: ‘Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands’?”

1SA.21.BSB: Now David took these words to heart and was very much afraid of Achish the king of Gath.
1SA.21.KJV: And David laid up these words in his heart, and was sore afraid of Achish the king of Gath.
1SA.21.PLAIN: Now David took these words to heart and was very much afraid of Achish the king of Gath.

1SA.21.BSB: So he changed his behavior before them and feigned madness in their hands; he scratched on the doors of the gate and let his saliva run down his beard.
1SA.21.KJV: And he changed his behavior before them, and feigned himself mad in their hands, and scrabbled on the doors of the gate, and let his spittle fall down on his beard.
1SA.21.PLAIN: So he changed his behavior before them and feigned madness in their hands; he scratched on the doors of the gate and let his saliva run down his beard.

1SA.21.BSB: Then Achish said to his servants, “Look, you can see that the man is insane! Why have you brought him to me?
1SA.21.KJV: Then said Achish to his servants, See, you see the man is mad: why then have you brought him to me?
1SA.21.PLAIN: Then Achish said to his servants, “Look, you can see that the man is insane! Why have you brought him to me?

1SA.21.BSB: Am I in need of madmen, that you have brought this man to rave in my presence? Must this man come into my house?”
1SA.21.KJV: Have I need of mad men, that you have brought this fellow to play the mad man in my presence? shall this fellow come into my house?
1SA.21.PLAIN: Am I in need of madmen, that you have brought this man to rave in my presence? Must this man come into my house?”

1SA.22.BSB: So David left Gath and took refuge in the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and the rest of his father’s household heard about it, they went down to him there.
1SA.22.KJV: David therefore departed there, and escaped to the cave Adullam: and when his brothers and all his father’s house heard it, they went down thither to him.
1SA.22.PLAIN: So David left Gath and took refuge in the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and the rest of his father’s household heard about it, they went down to him there.

1SA.22.BSB: And all who were distressed or indebted or discontented rallied around him, and he became their leader. About four hundred men were with him.
1SA.22.KJV: And every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, gathered themselves to him; and he became a captain over them: and there were with him about four hundred men. ¶
1SA.22.PLAIN: And all who were distressed or indebted or discontented rallied around him, and he became their leader. About four hundred men were with him.

1SA.22.BSB: From there David went to Mizpeh of Moab, where he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and mother stay with you until I learn what God will do for me.”
1SA.22.KJV: And David went there to Mizpeh of Moab: and he said to the king of Moab, Let my father and my mother, I pray you, come forth, and be with you, till I know what God will do for me.
1SA.22.PLAIN: From there David went to Mizpeh of Moab, where he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and mother stay with you until I learn what God will do for me.”

1SA.22.BSB: So he left them in the care of the king of Moab, and they stayed with him the whole time David was in the stronghold.
1SA.22.KJV: And he brought them before the king of Moab: and they dwelled with him all the while that David was in the hold. ¶
1SA.22.PLAIN: So he left them in the care of the king of Moab, and they stayed with him the whole time David was in the stronghold.

1SA.22.BSB: Then the prophet Gad said to David, “Do not stay in the stronghold. Depart and go into the land of Judah.” So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.
1SA.22.KJV: And the prophet Gad said to David, Abide not in the hold; depart, and get you into the land of Judah. Then David departed, and came into the forest of Hareth. ¶
1SA.22.PLAIN: Then the prophet Gad said to David, “Do not stay in the stronghold. Depart and go into the land of Judah.” So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.

1SA.22.BSB: Soon Saul learned that David and his men had been discovered. At that time Saul was in Gibeah, sitting under the tamarisk tree on the hill at Gibeah, with his spear in hand and all his servants standing around him.
1SA.22.KJV: When Saul heard that David was discovered, and the men that were with him, (now Saul stayed in Gibeah under a tree in Ramah, having his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing about him;)
1SA.22.PLAIN: Soon Saul learned that David and his men had been discovered. At that time Saul was in Gibeah, sitting under the tamarisk tree on the hill at Gibeah, with his spear in hand and all his servants standing around him.

1SA.22.BSB: Then Saul said to his servants, “Listen, men of Benjamin! Is the son of Jesse giving all of you fields and vineyards and making you commanders of thousands or hundreds?
1SA.22.KJV: Then Saul said to his servants that stood about him, Hear now, you Benjamites; will the son of Jesse give every one of you fields and vineyards, and make you all captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds;
1SA.22.PLAIN: Then Saul said to his servants, “Listen, men of Benjamin! Is the son of Jesse giving all of you fields and vineyards and making you commanders of thousands or hundreds?

1SA.22.BSB: Is that why all of you have conspired against me? Not one of you told me that my own son had made a covenant with the son of Jesse. Not one of you has shown concern for me or revealed to me that my son has stirred up my own servant to lie in wait against me, as is the case today.”
1SA.22.KJV: That all of you have conspired against me, and there is none that shows me that my son has made a league with the son of Jesse, and there is none of you that is sorry for me, or shows to me that my son has stirred up my servant against me, to lie in wait, as at this day? ¶
1SA.22.PLAIN: Is that why all of you have conspired against me? Not one of you told me that my own son had made a covenant with the son of Jesse. Not one of you has shown concern for me or revealed to me that my son has stirred up my own servant to lie in wait against me, as is the case today.”

1SA.22.BSB: But Doeg the Edomite, who had stationed himself with Saul’s servants, answered: “I saw the son of Jesse come to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob.
1SA.22.KJV: Then answered Doeg the Edomite, which was set over the servants of Saul, and said, I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
1SA.22.PLAIN: But Doeg the Edomite, who had stationed himself with Saul’s servants, answered: “I saw the son of Jesse come to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob.

1SA.22.BSB: Ahimelech inquired of the LORD for him and gave him provisions. He also gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”
1SA.22.KJV: And he inquired of the LORD for him, and gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.
1SA.22.PLAIN: Ahimelech inquired of the Lord for him and gave him provisions. He also gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”

1SA.22.BSB: Then the king sent messengers to summon Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and his father’s whole family, who were priests at Nob. And all of them came to the king.
1SA.22.KJV: Then the king sent to call Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father’s house, the priests that were in Nob: and they came all of them to the king.
1SA.22.PLAIN: Then the king sent messengers to summon Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and his father’s whole family, who were priests at Nob. And all of them came to the king.

1SA.22.BSB: “Listen now, son of Ahitub,” said Saul. “Here I am, my lord,” he replied.
1SA.22.KJV: And Saul said, Hear now, you son of Ahitub. And he answered, Here I am, my lord.
1SA.22.PLAIN: “Listen now, son of Ahitub,” said Saul. “Here I am, my lord,” he replied.

1SA.22.BSB: And Saul asked him, “Why have you and the son of Jesse conspired against me? You gave him bread and a sword and inquired of God for him so that he could rise up against me to lie in wait, as he is doing today.”
1SA.22.KJV: And Saul said to him, Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, in that you have given him bread, and a sword, and have inquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?
1SA.22.PLAIN: And Saul asked him, “Why have you and the son of Jesse conspired against me? You gave him bread and a sword and inquired of God for him so that he could rise up against me to lie in wait, as he is doing today.”

1SA.22.BSB: Ahimelech answered the king, “Who among all your servants is as faithful as David, the king’s son-in-law, the captain of your bodyguard who is honored in your house?
1SA.22.KJV: Then Ahimelech answered the king, and said, And who is so faithful among all your servants as David, which is the king’s son in law, and goes at your bidding, and is honorable in your house?
1SA.22.PLAIN: Ahimelech answered the king, “Who among all your servants is as faithful as David, the king’s son-in-law, the captain of your bodyguard who is honored in your house?

1SA.22.BSB: Was that day the first time I inquired of God for him? Far be it from me! Let not the king accuse your servant or any of my father’s household, for your servant knew nothing of this whole affair—not in part or in whole.”
1SA.22.KJV: Did I then begin to inquire of God for him? be it far from me: let not the king impute any thing to his servant, nor to all the house of my father: for your servant knew nothing of all this, less or more.
1SA.22.PLAIN: Was that day the first time I inquired of God for him? Far be it from me! Let not the king accuse your servant or any of my father’s household, for your servant knew nothing of this whole affair—not in part or in whole.”

1SA.22.BSB: But the king replied, “You will surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s house!”
1SA.22.KJV: And the king said, You shall surely die, Ahimelech, you, and all your father’s house. ¶
1SA.22.PLAIN: But the king replied, “You will surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s house!”

1SA.22.BSB: Then the king ordered the guards at his side, “Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because they too sided with David. For they knew he was fleeing, but they did not tell me.” But the king’s servants would not lift a hand to strike the priests of the LORD.
1SA.22.KJV: And the king said to the footmen that stood about him, Turn, and slay the priests of the LORD: because their hand also is with David, and because they knew when he fled, and did not show it to me. But the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall on the priests of the LORD.
1SA.22.PLAIN: Then the king ordered the guards at his side, “Turn and kill the priests of the Lord, because they too sided with David. For they knew he was fleeing, but they did not tell me.” But the king’s servants would not lift a hand to strike the priests of the Lord.

1SA.22.BSB: So the king ordered Doeg, “You turn and strike down the priests!” And Doeg the Edomite turned and struck down the priests himself. On that day he killed eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.
1SA.22.KJV: And the king said to Doeg, Turn you, and fall on the priests. And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell on the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod.
1SA.22.PLAIN: So the king ordered Doeg, “You turn and strike down the priests!” And Doeg the Edomite turned and struck down the priests himself. On that day he killed eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.

1SA.22.BSB: He also put to the sword Nob, the city of the priests, with its men and women, children and infants, oxen, donkeys, and sheep.
1SA.22.KJV: And Nob, the city of the priests, smote he with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, and oxen, and asses, and sheep, with the edge of the sword. ¶
1SA.22.PLAIN: He also put to the sword Nob, the city of the priests, with its men and women, children and infants, oxen, donkeys, and sheep.

1SA.22.BSB: But one of the sons of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped. His name was Abiathar, and he fled to David.
1SA.22.KJV: And one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David.
1SA.22.PLAIN: But one of the sons of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped. His name was Abiathar, and he fled to David.

1SA.22.BSB: And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.
1SA.22.KJV: And Abiathar showed David that Saul had slain the LORD’s priests.
1SA.22.PLAIN: And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the Lord.

1SA.22.BSB: Then David said to Abiathar, “I knew that Doeg the Edomite was there that day, and that he was sure to tell Saul. I myself am responsible for the lives of everyone in your father’s house.
1SA.22.KJV: And David said to Abiathar, I knew it that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul: I have occasioned the death of all the persons of your father’s house.
1SA.22.PLAIN: Then David said to Abiathar, “I knew that Doeg the Edomite was there that day, and that he was sure to tell Saul. I myself am responsible for the lives of everyone in your father’s house.

1SA.22.BSB: Stay with me; do not be afraid, for he who seeks your life is seeking mine as well. You will be safe with me.”
1SA.22.KJV: Abide you with me, fear not: for he that seeks my life seeks your life: but with me you shall be in safeguard.
1SA.22.PLAIN: Stay with me; do not be afraid, for he who seeks your life is seeking mine as well. You will be safe with me.”

1SA.23.BSB: Now it was reported to David, “Look, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah and looting the threshing floors.”
1SA.23.KJV: Then they told David, saying, Behold, the Philistines fight against Keilah, and they rob the threshing floors.
1SA.23.PLAIN: Now it was reported to David, “Look, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah and looting the threshing floors.”

1SA.23.BSB: So David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go and attack these Philistines?” And the LORD said to David, “Go and attack the Philistines and save Keilah.”
1SA.23.KJV: Therefore David inquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go and smite these Philistines? And the LORD said to David, Go, and smite the Philistines, and save Keilah.
1SA.23.PLAIN: So David inquired of the Lord, “Should I go and attack these Philistines?” And the Lord said to David, “Go and attack the Philistines and save Keilah.”

1SA.23.BSB: But David’s men said to him, “Look, we are afraid here in Judah; how much more if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?”
1SA.23.KJV: And David’s men said to him, Behold, we be afraid here in Judah: how much more then if we come to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?
1SA.23.PLAIN: But David’s men said to him, “Look, we are afraid here in Judah; how much more if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?”

1SA.23.BSB: Once again, David inquired of the LORD, and the LORD answered him: “Go at once to Keilah, for I will deliver the Philistines into your hand.”
1SA.23.KJV: Then David inquired of the LORD yet again. And the LORD answered him and said, Arise, go down to Keilah; for I will deliver the Philistines into your hand.
1SA.23.PLAIN: Once again, David inquired of the Lord, and the Lord answered him: “Go at once to Keilah, for I will deliver the Philistines into your hand.”

1SA.23.BSB: Then David and his men went to Keilah, fought against the Philistines, and carried off their livestock, striking them with a mighty blow. So David saved the people of Keilah.
1SA.23.KJV: So David and his men went to Keilah, and fought with the Philistines, and brought away their cattle, and smote them with a great slaughter. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.
1SA.23.PLAIN: Then David and his men went to Keilah, fought against the Philistines, and carried off their livestock, striking them with a mighty blow. So David saved the people of Keilah.

1SA.23.BSB: (Now Abiathar son of Ahimelech had brought the ephod with him when he fled to David at Keilah.)
1SA.23.KJV: And it came to pass, when Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David to Keilah, that he came down with an ephod in his hand. ¶
1SA.23.PLAIN: (Now Abiathar son of Ahimelech had brought the ephod with him when he fled to David at Keilah.)

1SA.23.BSB: When Saul was told that David had gone to Keilah, he said, “God has delivered him into my hand, for he has trapped himself by entering a town with gates and bars.”
1SA.23.KJV: And it was told Saul that David was come to Keilah. And Saul said, God has delivered him into my hand; for he is shut in, by entering into a town that has gates and bars.
1SA.23.PLAIN: When Saul was told that David had gone to Keilah, he said, “God has delivered him into my hand, for he has trapped himself by entering a town with gates and bars.”

1SA.23.BSB: Then Saul summoned all his troops to go to war at Keilah and besiege David and his men.
1SA.23.KJV: And Saul called all the people together to war, to go down to Keilah, to besiege David and his men. ¶
1SA.23.PLAIN: Then Saul summoned all his troops to go to war at Keilah and besiege David and his men.

1SA.23.BSB: When David learned that Saul was plotting evil against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod.”
1SA.23.KJV: And David knew that Saul secretly practiced mischief against him; and he said to Abiathar the priest, Bring here the ephod.
1SA.23.PLAIN: When David learned that Saul was plotting evil against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod.”

1SA.23.BSB: And David said, “O LORD, God of Israel, Your servant has heard that Saul intends to come to Keilah and destroy the city on my account.
1SA.23.KJV: Then said David, O LORD God of Israel, your servant has certainly heard that Saul seeks to come to Keilah, to destroy the city for my sake.
1SA.23.PLAIN: And David said, “O Lord, God of Israel, Your servant has heard that Saul intends to come to Keilah and destroy the city on my account.

1SA.23.BSB: Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me into his hand? Will Saul come down, as Your servant has heard? O LORD, God of Israel, please tell Your servant.” “He will,” said the LORD.
1SA.23.KJV: Will the men of Keilah deliver me up into his hand? will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? O LORD God of Israel, I beseech you, tell your servant. And the LORD said, He will come down.
1SA.23.PLAIN: Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me into his hand? Will Saul come down, as Your servant has heard? O Lord, God of Israel, please tell Your servant.” “He will,” said the Lord.

1SA.23.BSB: So David asked, “Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me and my men into the hand of Saul?” “They will,” said the LORD.
1SA.23.KJV: Then said David, Will the men of Keilah deliver me and my men into the hand of Saul? And the LORD said, They will deliver you up. ¶
1SA.23.PLAIN: So David asked, “Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me and my men into the hand of Saul?” “They will,” said the Lord.

1SA.23.BSB: Then David and his men, about six hundred strong, set out and departed from Keilah, moving from place to place. When Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah, he declined to go forth.
1SA.23.KJV: Then David and his men, which were about six hundred, arose and departed out of Keilah, and went wherever they could go. And it was told Saul that David was escaped from Keilah; and he declined to go forth.
1SA.23.PLAIN: Then David and his men, about six hundred strong, set out and departed from Keilah, moving from place to place. When Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah, he declined to go forth.

1SA.23.BSB: And David stayed in the wilderness strongholds and in the hill country of the Wilderness of Ziph. Day after day Saul searched for him, but God would not deliver David into his hand.
1SA.23.KJV: And David stayed in the wilderness in strong holds, and remained in a mountain in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him every day, but God delivered him not into his hand.
1SA.23.PLAIN: And David stayed in the wilderness strongholds and in the hill country of the Wilderness of Ziph. Day after day Saul searched for him, but God would not deliver David into his hand.

1SA.23.BSB: While David was in Horesh in the Wilderness of Ziph, he saw that Saul had come out to take his life.
1SA.23.KJV: And David saw that Saul was come out to seek his life: and David was in the wilderness of Ziph in a wood. ¶
1SA.23.PLAIN: While David was in Horesh in the Wilderness of Ziph, he saw that Saul had come out to take his life.

1SA.23.BSB: And Saul’s son Jonathan came to David in Horesh and strengthened his hand in God,
1SA.23.KJV: And Jonathan Saul’s son arose, and went to David into the wood, and strengthened his hand in God.
1SA.23.PLAIN: And Saul’s son Jonathan came to David in Horesh and strengthened his hand in God,

1SA.23.BSB: saying, “Do not be afraid, for my father Saul will never lay a hand on you. And you will be king over Israel, and I will be your second-in-command. Even my father Saul knows this is true.”
1SA.23.KJV: And he said to him, Fear not: for the hand of Saul my father shall not find you; and you shall be king over Israel, and I shall be next to you; and that also Saul my father knows.
1SA.23.PLAIN: saying, “Do not be afraid, for my father Saul will never lay a hand on you. And you will be king over Israel, and I will be your second-in-command. Even my father Saul knows this is true.”

1SA.23.BSB: So the two of them made a covenant before the LORD. And David remained in Horesh, while Jonathan went home.
1SA.23.KJV: And they two made a covenant before the LORD: and David stayed in the wood, and Jonathan went to his house. ¶
1SA.23.PLAIN: So the two of them made a covenant before the Lord. And David remained in Horesh, while Jonathan went home.

1SA.23.BSB: Then the Ziphites came up to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Is not David hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah south of Jeshimon?
1SA.23.KJV: Then came up the Ziphites to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Does not David hide himself with us in strong holds in the wood, in the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south of Jeshimon?
1SA.23.PLAIN: Then the Ziphites came up to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Is not David hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah south of Jeshimon?

1SA.23.BSB: Now, O king, come down whenever your soul desires, and we will be responsible for delivering him into your hand.”
1SA.23.KJV: Now therefore, O king, come down according to all the desire of your soul to come down; and our part shall be to deliver him into the king’s hand.
1SA.23.PLAIN: Now, O king, come down whenever your soul desires, and we will be responsible for delivering him into your hand.”

1SA.23.BSB: “May you be blessed by the LORD,” replied Saul, “for you have had compassion on me.
1SA.23.KJV: And Saul said, Blessed be you of the LORD; for you have compassion on me.
1SA.23.PLAIN: “May you be blessed by the Lord,” replied Saul, “for you have had compassion on me.

1SA.23.BSB: Please go and prepare further. Investigate and watch carefully where he goes and who has seen him there, for I am told that he is extremely cunning.
1SA.23.KJV: Go, I pray you, prepare yet, and know and see his place where his haunt is, and who has seen him there: for it is told me that he deals very subtly.
1SA.23.PLAIN: Please go and prepare further. Investigate and watch carefully where he goes and who has seen him there, for I am told that he is extremely cunning.

1SA.23.BSB: Observe and find out all the places where he hides. Then come back to me with certainty, and I will go with you. If he is in the land, I will search him out among all the clans of Judah.”
1SA.23.KJV: See therefore, and take knowledge of all the lurking places where he hides himself, and come you again to me with the certainty, and I will go with you: and it shall come to pass, if he be in the land, that I will search him out throughout all the thousands of Judah.
1SA.23.PLAIN: Observe and find out all the places where he hides. Then come back to me with certainty, and I will go with you. If he is in the land, I will search him out among all the clans of Judah.”

1SA.23.BSB: So they set out and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. Now David and his men were in the Wilderness of Maon in the Arabah south of Jeshimon,
1SA.23.KJV: And they arose, and went to Ziph before Saul: but David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the plain on the south of Jeshimon.
1SA.23.PLAIN: So they set out and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. Now David and his men were in the Wilderness of Maon in the Arabah south of Jeshimon,

1SA.23.BSB: and Saul and his men went to seek him. When David was told about it, he went down to the rock and stayed in the Wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard of this, he pursued David there.
1SA.23.KJV: Saul also and his men went to seek him. And they told David; why he came down into a rock, and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard that, he pursued after David in the wilderness of Maon.
1SA.23.PLAIN: and Saul and his men went to seek him. When David was told about it, he went down to the rock and stayed in the Wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard of this, he pursued David there.

1SA.23.BSB: Saul was proceeding along one side of the mountain, and David and his men along the other side. Even though David was hurrying to get away, Saul and his men were closing in on David and his men to capture them.
1SA.23.KJV: And Saul went on this side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the mountain: and David made haste to get away for fear of Saul; for Saul and his men compassed David and his men round about to take them. ¶
1SA.23.PLAIN: Saul was proceeding along one side of the mountain, and David and his men along the other side. Even though David was hurrying to get away, Saul and his men were closing in on David and his men to capture them.

1SA.23.BSB: Then a messenger came to Saul, saying, “Come quickly, for the Philistines have raided the land!”
1SA.23.KJV: But there came a messenger to Saul, saying, Haste you, and come; for the Philistines have invaded the land.
1SA.23.PLAIN: Then a messenger came to Saul, saying, “Come quickly, for the Philistines have raided the land!”

1SA.23.BSB: So Saul broke off his pursuit of David and went to meet the Philistines. That is why that place is called Sela-hammahlekoth.
1SA.23.KJV: Why Saul returned from pursuing after David, and went against the Philistines: therefore they called that place Selahammahlekoth. ¶
1SA.23.PLAIN: So Saul broke off his pursuit of David and went to meet the Philistines. That is why that place is called Sela-hammahlekoth.

1SA.23.BSB: And David went up from there and lived in the strongholds of En-gedi.
1SA.23.KJV: And David went up from there, and dwelled in strong holds at Engedi.
1SA.23.PLAIN: And David went up from there and lived in the strongholds of En-gedi.

1SA.24.BSB: After Saul had returned from pursuing the Philistines, he was told, “David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.”

1SA.25.BSB: When Abigail returned to Nabal, there he was in the house, holding a feast fit for a king, in high spirits and very drunk. So she told him nothing until morning light.
1SA.25.KJV: And Abigail came to Nabal; and, behold, he held a feast in his house, like the feast of a king; and Nabal’s heart was merry within him, for he was very drunken: why she told him nothing, less or more, until the morning light.
1SA.25.PLAIN: When Abigail returned to Nabal, there he was in the house, holding a feast fit for a king, in high spirits and very drunk. So she told him nothing until morning light.

1SA.25.BSB: In the morning when Nabal was sober, his wife told him about these events, and his heart failed within him and he became like a stone.
1SA.25.KJV: But it came to pass in the morning, when the wine was gone out of Nabal, and his wife had told him these things, that his heart died within him, and he became as a stone.
1SA.25.PLAIN: In the morning when Nabal was sober, his wife told him about these events, and his heart failed within him and he became like a stone.

1SA.25.BSB: About ten days later, the LORD struck Nabal dead.
1SA.25.KJV: And it came to pass about ten days after, that the LORD smote Nabal, that he died. ¶
1SA.25.PLAIN: About ten days later, the Lord struck Nabal dead.

1SA.25.BSB: On hearing that Nabal was dead, David said, “Blessed be the LORD, who has upheld my cause against the reproach of Nabal and has restrained His servant from evil. For the LORD has brought the wickedness of Nabal down upon his own head.” Then David sent word to Abigail, asking for her in marriage.
1SA.25.KJV: And when David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, Blessed be the LORD, that has pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and has kept his servant from evil: for the LORD has returned the wickedness of Nabal on his own head. And David sent and communed with Abigail, to take her to him to wife.
1SA.25.PLAIN: On hearing that Nabal was dead, David said, “Blessed be the Lord, who has upheld my cause against the reproach of Nabal and has restrained His servant from evil. For the Lord has brought the wickedness of Nabal down upon his own head.” Then David sent word to Abigail, asking for her in marriage.

1SA.25.BSB: When his servants came to Abigail at Carmel, they said, “David has sent us to take you as his wife.”
1SA.25.KJV: And when the servants of David were come to Abigail to Carmel, they spoke to her, saying, David sent us to you, to take you to him to wife.
1SA.25.PLAIN: When his servants came to Abigail at Carmel, they said, “David has sent us to take you as his wife.”

1SA.25.BSB: She arose, then bowed facedown and said, “Here is your maidservant, ready to serve and to wash the feet of my lord’s servants.”
1SA.25.KJV: And she arose, and bowed herself on her face to the earth, and said, Behold, let your handmaid be a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord.
1SA.25.PLAIN: She arose, then bowed facedown and said, “Here is your maidservant, ready to serve and to wash the feet of my lord’s servants.”

1SA.25.BSB: So Abigail hurried and got on a donkey, and attended by five of her maidens, she followed David’s messengers and became his wife.
1SA.25.KJV: And Abigail hurried, and arose and rode on an ass, with five damsels of hers that went after her; and she went after the messengers of David, and became his wife.
1SA.25.PLAIN: So Abigail hurried and got on a donkey, and attended by five of her maidens, she followed David’s messengers and became his wife.

1SA.25.BSB: David had also married Ahinoam of Jezreel. So she and Abigail were both his wives.
1SA.25.KJV: David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel; and they were also both of them his wives. ¶
1SA.25.PLAIN: David had also married Ahinoam of Jezreel. So she and Abigail were both his wives.

1SA.25.BSB: But Saul had given his daughter Michal, David’s wife, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Gallim.
1SA.25.KJV: But Saul had given Michal his daughter, David’s wife, to Phalti the son of Laish, which was of Gallim.
1SA.25.PLAIN: But Saul had given his daughter Michal, David’s wife, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Gallim.

1SA.26.BSB: Then the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Is not David hiding on the hill of Hachilah, opposite Jeshimon?”
1SA.26.KJV: And the Ziphites came to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Does not David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon?
1SA.26.PLAIN: Then the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Is not David hiding on the hill of Hachilah, opposite Jeshimon?”

1SA.26.BSB: So Saul, accompanied by three thousand chosen men of Israel, went down to the Wilderness of Ziph to search for David there.
1SA.26.KJV: Then Saul arose, and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
1SA.26.PLAIN: So Saul, accompanied by three thousand chosen men of Israel, went down to the Wilderness of Ziph to search for David there.

1SA.26.BSB: Saul camped beside the road at the hill of Hachilah opposite Jeshimon, but David was living in the wilderness. When he realized that Saul had followed him there,
1SA.26.KJV: And Saul pitched in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon, by the way. But David stayed in the wilderness, and he saw that Saul came after him into the wilderness.
1SA.26.PLAIN: Saul camped beside the road at the hill of Hachilah opposite Jeshimon, but David was living in the wilderness. When he realized that Saul had followed him there,

1SA.26.BSB: David sent out spies to verify that Saul had arrived.
1SA.26.KJV: David therefore sent out spies, and understood that Saul was come in very deed. ¶
1SA.26.PLAIN: David sent out spies to verify that Saul had arrived.

1SA.26.BSB: Then David set out and went to the place where Saul had camped. He saw the place where Saul and Abner son of Ner, the general of his army, had lain down. Saul was lying inside the inner circle of the camp, with the troops camped around him.
1SA.26.KJV: And David arose, and came to the place where Saul had pitched: and David beheld the place where Saul lay, and Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host: and Saul lay in the trench, and the people pitched round about him.
1SA.26.PLAIN: Then David set out and went to the place where Saul had camped. He saw the place where Saul and Abner son of Ner, the general of his army, had lain down. Saul was lying inside the inner circle of the camp, with the troops camped around him.

1SA.26.BSB: And David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, “Who will go down with me to Saul in the camp?” “I will go with you,” answered Abishai.
1SA.26.KJV: Then answered David and said to Ahimelech the Hittite, and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, brother to Joab, saying, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? And Abishai said, I will go down with you.
1SA.26.PLAIN: And David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, “Who will go down with me to Saul in the camp?” “I will go with you,” answered Abishai.

1SA.26.BSB: That night David and Abishai came to the troops, and Saul was lying there asleep in the inner circle of the camp, with his spear stuck in the ground by his head. And Abner and the troops were lying around him.
1SA.26.KJV: So David and Abishai came to the people by night: and, behold, Saul lay sleeping within the trench, and his spear stuck in the ground at his bolster: but Abner and the people lay round about him.
1SA.26.PLAIN: That night David and Abishai came to the troops, and Saul was lying there asleep in the inner circle of the camp, with his spear stuck in the ground by his head. And Abner and the troops were lying around him.

1SA.26.BSB: Abishai said to David, “Today God has delivered your enemy into your hand. Now, therefore, please let me thrust the spear through him into the ground with one stroke. I will not need to strike him twice!”
1SA.26.KJV: Then said Abishai to David, God has delivered your enemy into your hand this day: now therefore let me smite him, I pray you, with the spear even to the earth at once, and I will not smite him the second time.
1SA.26.PLAIN: Abishai said to David, “Today God has delivered your enemy into your hand. Now, therefore, please let me thrust the spear through him into the ground with one stroke. I will not need to strike him twice!”

1SA.26.BSB: But David said to Abishai, “Do not destroy him, for who can lift a hand against the LORD’s anointed and be guiltless?”
1SA.26.KJV: And David said to Abishai, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the LORD’s anointed, and be guiltless?
1SA.26.PLAIN: But David said to Abishai, “Do not destroy him, for who can lift a hand against the Lord’s anointed and be guiltless?”

1SA.26.BSB: David added, “As surely as the LORD lives, the LORD Himself will strike him down; either his day will come and he will die, or he will go into battle and perish.
1SA.26.KJV: David said furthermore, As the LORD lives, the LORD shall smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall descend into battle, and perish.
1SA.26.PLAIN: David added, “As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord Himself will strike him down; either his day will come and he will die, or he will go into battle and perish.

1SA.26.BSB: But the LORD forbid that I should stretch out my hand against the LORD’s anointed. Instead, take the spear and water jug by his head, and let us go.”
1SA.26.KJV: The LORD forbid that I should stretch forth my hand against the LORD’s anointed: but, I pray you, take you now the spear that is at his bolster, and the cruse of water, and let us go.
1SA.26.PLAIN: But the Lord forbid that I should stretch out my hand against the Lord’s anointed. Instead, take the spear and water jug by his head, and let us go.”

1SA.26.BSB: So David took the spear and water jug by Saul’s head, and they departed. No one saw them or knew about it, nor did anyone wake up; they all remained asleep, because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen on them.
1SA.26.KJV: So David took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul’s bolster; and they got them away, and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither awaked: for they were all asleep; because a deep sleep from the LORD was fallen on them. ¶
1SA.26.PLAIN: So David took the spear and water jug by Saul’s head, and they departed. No one saw them or knew about it, nor did anyone wake up; they all remained asleep, because a deep sleep from the Lord had fallen on them.

1SA.26.BSB: Then David crossed to the other side and stood atop the mountain at a distance; there was a wide gulf between them.
1SA.26.KJV: Then David went over to the other side, and stood on the top of an hill afar off; a great space being between them:
1SA.26.PLAIN: Then David crossed to the other side and stood atop the mountain at a distance; there was a wide gulf between them.

1SA.26.BSB: And David shouted to the troops and to Abner son of Ner, “Will you not answer me, Abner?” “Who calls to the king?” Abner replied.
1SA.26.KJV: And David cried to the people, and to Abner the son of Ner, saying, Answer you not, Abner? Then Abner answered and said, Who are you that cry to the king?
1SA.26.PLAIN: And David shouted to the troops and to Abner son of Ner, “Will you not answer me, Abner?” “Who calls to the king?” Abner replied.

1SA.26.BSB: So David said to Abner, “You are a man, aren’t you? And who in Israel is your equal? Why then did you not protect your lord the king when one of the people came to destroy him?
1SA.26.KJV: And David said to Abner, Are not you a valiant man? and who is like to you in Israel? why then have you not kept your lord the king? for there came one of the people in to destroy the king your lord.
1SA.26.PLAIN: So David said to Abner, “You are a man, aren’t you? And who in Israel is your equal? Why then did you not protect your lord the king when one of the people came to destroy him?

1SA.26.BSB: This thing you have done is not good. As surely as the LORD lives, all of you deserve to die, since you did not protect your lord, the LORD’s anointed. Now look around. Where are the king’s spear and water jug that were by his head?”
1SA.26.KJV: This thing is not good that you have done. As the LORD lives, you are worthy to die, because you have not kept your master, the LORD’s anointed. And now see where the king’s spear is, and the cruse of water that was at his bolster.
1SA.26.PLAIN: This thing you have done is not good. As surely as the Lord lives, all of you deserve to die, since you did not protect your lord, the Lord’s anointed. Now look around. Where are the king’s spear and water jug that were by his head?”

1SA.26.BSB: Then Saul recognized David’s voice and asked, “Is that your voice, David my son?” “It is my voice, my lord and king,” David said.
1SA.26.KJV: And Saul knew David’s voice, and said, Is this your voice, my son David? And David said, It is my voice, my lord, O king.
1SA.26.PLAIN: Then Saul recognized David’s voice and asked, “Is that your voice, David my son?” “It is my voice, my lord and king,” David said.

1SA.26.BSB: And he continued, “Why is my lord pursuing his servant? What have I done? What evil is in my hand?
1SA.26.KJV: And he said, Why does my lord thus pursue after his servant? for what have I done? or what evil is in my hand?
1SA.26.PLAIN: And he continued, “Why is my lord pursuing his servant? What have I done? What evil is in my hand?

1SA.26.BSB: Now please, may my lord the king hear the words of his servant: If the LORD has stirred you up against me, then may He accept an offering. But if men have done it, may they be cursed in the presence of the LORD! For today they have driven me away from sharing in the inheritance of the LORD, saying, ‘Go, serve other gods.’
1SA.26.KJV: Now therefore, I pray you, let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the LORD have stirred you up against me, let him accept an offering: but if they be the children of men, cursed be they before the LORD; for they have driven me out this day from abiding in the inheritance of the LORD, saying, Go, serve other gods.
1SA.26.PLAIN: Now please, may my lord the king hear the words of his servant: If the Lord has stirred you up against me, then may He accept an offering. But if men have done it, may they be cursed in the presence of the Lord! For today they have driven me away from sharing in the inheritance of the Lord, saying, ‘Go, serve other gods.’

1SA.26.BSB: So do not let my blood fall to the ground far from the presence of the LORD. For the king of Israel has come out to look for a flea, like one who hunts a partridge in the mountains.”
1SA.26.KJV: Now therefore, let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the LORD: for the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea, as when one does hunt a partridge in the mountains. ¶
1SA.26.PLAIN: So do not let my blood fall to the ground far from the presence of the Lord. For the king of Israel has come out to look for a flea, like one who hunts a partridge in the mountains.”

1SA.26.BSB: Then Saul replied, “I have sinned. Come back, David my son. I will never harm you again, because today you considered my life precious. I have played the fool and have committed a grave error!”
1SA.26.KJV: Then said Saul, I have sinned: return, my son David: for I will no more do you harm, because my soul was precious in your eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.
1SA.26.PLAIN: Then Saul replied, “I have sinned. Come back, David my son. I will never harm you again, because today you considered my life precious. I have played the fool and have committed a grave error!”

1SA.26.BSB: “Here is the king’s spear,” David answered. “Let one of the young men come over and get it.
1SA.26.KJV: And David answered and said, Behold the king’s spear! and let one of the young men come over and fetch it.
1SA.26.PLAIN: “Here is the king’s spear,” David answered. “Let one of the young men come over and get it.

1SA.26.BSB: May the LORD repay every man for his righteousness and faithfulness. For the LORD delivered you into my hand today, but I would not stretch out my hand against the LORD’s anointed.
1SA.26.KJV: The LORD render to every man his righteousness and his faithfulness; for the LORD delivered you into my hand to day, but I would not stretch forth my hand against the LORD’s anointed.
1SA.26.PLAIN: May the Lord repay every man for his righteousness and faithfulness. For the Lord delivered you into my hand today, but I would not stretch out my hand against the Lord’s anointed.

1SA.26.BSB: As surely as I valued your life today, so may the LORD value my life and rescue me from all trouble.”
1SA.26.KJV: And, behold, as your life was much set by this day in my eyes, so let my life be much set by in the eyes of the LORD, and let him deliver me out of all tribulation.
1SA.26.PLAIN: As surely as I valued your life today, so may the Lord value my life and rescue me from all trouble.”

1SA.26.BSB: Saul said to him, “May you be blessed, David my son. You will accomplish great things and will surely prevail.” So David went on his way, and Saul returned home.
1SA.26.KJV: Then Saul said to David, Blessed be you, my son David: you shall both do great things, and also shall still prevail. So David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.
1SA.26.PLAIN: Saul said to him, “May you be blessed, David my son. You will accomplish great things and will surely prevail.” So David went on his way, and Saul returned home.

1SA.27.BSB: David, however, said to himself, “One of these days now I will be swept away by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than to escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will stop searching for me all over Israel, and I will slip out of his hand.”
1SA.27.KJV: And David said in his heart, I shall now perish one day by the hand of Saul: there is nothing better for me than that I should speedily escape into the land of the Philistines; and Saul shall despair of me, to seek me any more in any coast of Israel: so shall I escape out of his hand.
1SA.27.PLAIN: David, however, said to himself, “One of these days now I will be swept away by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than to escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will stop searching for me all over Israel, and I will slip out of his hand.”

1SA.27.BSB: So David set out with his six hundred men and went to Achish son of Maoch, the king of Gath.
1SA.27.KJV: And David arose, and he passed over with the six hundred men that were with him to Achish, the son of Maoch, king of Gath.
1SA.27.PLAIN: So David set out with his six hundred men and went to Achish son of Maoch, the king of Gath.

1SA.27.BSB: David and his men settled in Gath with Achish. Each man had his family with him, and David had his two wives: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, the widow of Nabal.
1SA.27.KJV: And David dwelled with Achish at Gath, he and his men, every man with his household, even David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal’s wife.
1SA.27.PLAIN: David and his men settled in Gath with Achish. Each man had his family with him, and David had his two wives: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, the widow of Nabal.

1SA.27.BSB: And when Saul learned that David had fled to Gath, he no longer searched for him.
1SA.27.KJV: And it was told Saul that David was fled to Gath: and he sought no more again for him. ¶
1SA.27.PLAIN: And when Saul learned that David had fled to Gath, he no longer searched for him.

1SA.27.BSB: Then David said to Achish, “If I have found favor in your eyes, let me be assigned a place in one of the outlying towns, so I can live there. For why should your servant live in the royal city with you?”
1SA.27.KJV: And David said to Achish, If I have now found grace in your eyes, let them give me a place in some town in the country, that I may dwell there: for why should your servant dwell in the royal city with you?
1SA.27.PLAIN: Then David said to Achish, “If I have found favor in your eyes, let me be assigned a place in one of the outlying towns, so I can live there. For why should your servant live in the royal city with you?”

1SA.27.BSB: That day Achish gave him Ziklag, and to this day it still belongs to the kings of Judah.
1SA.27.KJV: Then Achish gave him Ziklag that day: why Ziklag pertains to the kings of Judah to this day.
1SA.27.PLAIN: That day Achish gave him Ziklag, and to this day it still belongs to the kings of Judah.

1SA.27.BSB: And the time that David lived in Philistine territory amounted to a year and four months.
1SA.27.KJV: And the time that David dwelled in the country of the Philistines was a full year and four months. ¶
1SA.27.PLAIN: And the time that David lived in Philistine territory amounted to a year and four months.

1SA.27.BSB: Now David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites. (From ancient times these people had inhabited the land extending to Shur and Egypt.)
1SA.27.KJV: And David and his men went up, and invaded the Geshurites, and the Gezrites, and the Amalekites: for those nations were of old the inhabitants of the land, as you go to Shur, even to the land of Egypt.
1SA.27.PLAIN: Now David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites. (From ancient times these people had inhabited the land extending to Shur and Egypt.)

1SA.27.BSB: Whenever David attacked a territory, he did not leave a man or woman alive, but he took the flocks and herds, the donkeys, camels, and clothing. Then he would return to Achish,
1SA.27.KJV: And David smote the land, and left neither man nor woman alive, and took away the sheep, and the oxen, and the asses, and the camels, and the apparel, and returned, and came to Achish.
1SA.27.PLAIN: Whenever David attacked a territory, he did not leave a man or woman alive, but he took the flocks and herds, the donkeys, camels, and clothing. Then he would return to Achish,

1SA.27.BSB: who would ask him, “What have you raided today?” And David would reply, “The Negev of Judah,” or “The Negev of Jerahmeel,” or “The Negev of the Kenites.”
1SA.27.KJV: And Achish said, Where have you made a road to day? And David said, Against the south of Judah, and against the south of the Jerahmeelites, and against the south of the Kenites.
1SA.27.PLAIN: who would ask him, “What have you raided today?” And David would reply, “The Negev of Judah,” or “The Negev of Jerahmeel,” or “The Negev of the Kenites.”

1SA.27.BSB: David did not leave a man or woman alive to be brought to Gath, for he said, “Otherwise they will report us, saying, ‘This is what David did.’” And this was David’s custom the whole time he lived in Philistine territory.
1SA.27.KJV: And David saved neither man nor woman alive, to bring tidings to Gath, saying, Lest they should tell on us, saying, So did David, and so will be his manner all the while he dwells in the country of the Philistines.
1SA.27.PLAIN: David did not leave a man or woman alive to be brought to Gath, for he said, “Otherwise they will report us, saying, ‘This is what David did.’” And this was David’s custom the whole time he lived in Philistine territory.

1SA.27.BSB: So Achish trusted David, thinking, “Since he has made himself an utter stench to his people Israel, he will be my servant forever.”
1SA.27.KJV: And Achish believed David, saying, He has made his people Israel utterly to abhor him; therefore he shall be my servant for ever.
1SA.27.PLAIN: So Achish trusted David, thinking, “Since he has made himself an utter stench to his people Israel, he will be my servant forever.”

1SA.28.BSB: Now in those days the Philistines gathered their forces for warfare against Israel. So Achish said to David, “You must understand that you and your men are to go out to battle with me.”
1SA.28.KJV: And it came to pass in those days, that the Philistines gathered their armies together for warfare, to fight with Israel. And Achish said to David, Know you assuredly, that you shall go out with me to battle, you and your men.
1SA.28.PLAIN: Now in those days the Philistines gathered their forces for warfare against Israel. So Achish said to David, “You must understand that you and your men are to go out to battle with me.”

1SA.28.BSB: David replied, “Then you will come to know what your servant can do.” “Very well,” said Achish. “I will make you my bodyguard for life.”
1SA.28.KJV: And David said to Achish, Surely you shall know what your servant can do. And Achish said to David, Therefore will I make you keeper of my head for ever. ¶
1SA.28.PLAIN: David replied, “Then you will come to know what your servant can do.” “Very well,” said Achish. “I will make you my bodyguard for life.”

1SA.28.BSB: Now by this time Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, his own city. And Saul had removed the mediums and spiritists from the land.
1SA.28.KJV: Now Samuel was dead, and all Israel had lamented him, and buried him in Ramah, even in his own city. And Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land.
1SA.28.PLAIN: Now by this time Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, his own city. And Saul had removed the mediums and spiritists from the land.

1SA.28.BSB: The Philistines came together and camped at Shunem, while Saul gathered all Israel and camped at Gilboa.
1SA.28.KJV: And the Philistines gathered themselves together, and came and pitched in Shunem: and Saul gathered all Israel together, and they pitched in Gilboa.
1SA.28.PLAIN: The Philistines came together and camped at Shunem, while Saul gathered all Israel and camped at Gilboa.

1SA.28.BSB: When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was afraid and trembled violently.
1SA.28.KJV: And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.
1SA.28.PLAIN: When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was afraid and trembled violently.

1SA.28.BSB: He inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him by dreams or Urim or prophets.
1SA.28.KJV: And when Saul inquired of the LORD, the LORD answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets. ¶
1SA.28.PLAIN: He inquired of the Lord, but the Lord did not answer him by dreams or Urim or prophets.

1SA.28.BSB: Then Saul said to his servants, “Find me a woman who is a medium, so I can go and consult her.” “There is a medium at Endor,” his servants replied.
1SA.28.KJV: Then said Saul to his servants, Seek me a woman that has a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and inquire of her. And his servants said to him, Behold, there is a woman that has a familiar spirit at Endor.
1SA.28.PLAIN: Then Saul said to his servants, “Find me a woman who is a medium, so I can go and consult her.” “There is a medium at Endor,” his servants replied.

1SA.28.BSB: So Saul disguised himself by putting on different clothes, and he set out with two of his men. They came to the woman at night, and Saul said, “Consult a spirit for me. Bring up for me the one I name.”
1SA.28.KJV: And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and he went, and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night: and he said, I pray you, divine to me by the familiar spirit, and bring me him up, whom I shall name to you.
1SA.28.PLAIN: So Saul disguised himself by putting on different clothes, and he set out with two of his men. They came to the woman at night, and Saul said, “Consult a spirit for me. Bring up for me the one I name.”

1SA.28.BSB: But the woman replied, “Surely you know what Saul has done, how he has killed the mediums and spiritists in the land. Why have you set a trap to get me killed?”
1SA.28.KJV: And the woman said to him, Behold, you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land: why then lay you a snare for my life, to cause me to die?
1SA.28.PLAIN: But the woman replied, “Surely you know what Saul has done, how he has killed the mediums and spiritists in the land. Why have you set a trap to get me killed?”

1SA.28.BSB: Then Saul swore to her by the LORD: “As surely as the LORD lives, no punishment shall come upon you for this.”
1SA.28.KJV: And Saul swore to her by the LORD, saying, As the LORD lives, there shall no punishment happen to you for this thing.
1SA.28.PLAIN: Then Saul swore to her by the Lord: “As surely as the Lord lives, no punishment shall come upon you for this.”

1SA.28.BSB: “Whom shall I bring up for you?” the woman asked. “Bring up Samuel,” he replied.
1SA.28.KJV: Then said the woman, Whom shall I bring up to you? And he said, Bring me up Samuel.
1SA.28.PLAIN: “Whom shall I bring up for you?” the woman asked. “Bring up Samuel,” he replied.

1SA.28.BSB: But when the woman saw Samuel, she cried out in a loud voice and said to Saul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!”
1SA.28.KJV: And when the woman saw Samuel, she cried with a loud voice: and the woman spoke to Saul, saying, Why have you deceived me? for you are Saul.
1SA.28.PLAIN: But when the woman saw Samuel, she cried out in a loud voice and said to Saul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!”

1SA.28.BSB: “Do not be afraid,” the king replied. “What do you see?” “I see a god coming up out of the earth,” the woman answered.
1SA.28.KJV: And the king said to her, Be not afraid: for what saw you? And the woman said to Saul, I saw gods ascending out of the earth.
1SA.28.PLAIN: “Do not be afraid,” the king replied. “What do you see?” “I see a god coming up out of the earth,” the woman answered.

1SA.28.BSB: “What does he look like?” asked Saul. “An old man is coming up,” she replied. “And he is wearing a robe.” So Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed facedown in reverence.
1SA.28.KJV: And he said to her, What form is he of? And she said, An old man comes up; and he is covered with a mantle. And Saul perceived that it was Samuel, and he stooped with his face to the ground, and bowed himself. ¶
1SA.28.PLAIN: “What does he look like?” asked Saul. “An old man is coming up,” she replied. “And he is wearing a robe.” So Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed facedown in reverence.

1SA.28.BSB: Then Samuel said to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” “I am deeply distressed,” replied Saul. “The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned away from me. He no longer answers me, either by prophets or by dreams. So I have called on you to tell me what to do.”
1SA.28.KJV: And Samuel said to Saul, Why have you disquieted me, to bring me up? And Saul answered, I am sore distressed; for the Philistines make war against me, and God is departed from me, and answers me no more, neither by prophets, nor by dreams: therefore I have called you, that you may make known to me what I shall do.
1SA.28.PLAIN: Then Samuel said to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” “I am deeply distressed,” replied Saul. “The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned away from me. He no longer answers me, either by prophets or by dreams. So I have called on you to tell me what to do.”

1SA.28.BSB: “Why do you consult me,” asked Samuel, “since the LORD has turned away from you and become your enemy?
1SA.28.KJV: Then said Samuel, Why then do you ask of me, seeing the LORD is departed from you, and is become your enemy?
1SA.28.PLAIN: “Why do you consult me,” asked Samuel, “since the Lord has turned away from you and become your enemy?

1SA.28.BSB: He has done exactly what He spoke through me: The LORD has torn the kingship out of your hand and given it to your neighbor David.
1SA.28.KJV: And the LORD has done to him, as he spoke by me: for the LORD has rent the kingdom out of your hand, and given it to your neighbor, even to David:
1SA.28.PLAIN: He has done exactly what He spoke through me: The Lord has torn the kingship out of your hand and given it to your neighbor David.

1SA.28.BSB: Because you did not obey the LORD or carry out His burning anger against Amalek, the LORD has done this to you today.
1SA.28.KJV: Because you obeyed not the voice of the LORD, nor executed his fierce wrath on Amalek, therefore has the LORD done this thing to you this day.
1SA.28.PLAIN: Because you did not obey the Lord or carry out His burning anger against Amalek, the Lord has done this to you today.

1SA.28.BSB: Moreover, the LORD will deliver Israel with you into the hand of the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. And the LORD will deliver the army of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.”
1SA.28.KJV: Moreover the LORD will also deliver Israel with you into the hand of the Philistines: and to morrow shall you and your sons be with me: the LORD also shall deliver the host of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.
1SA.28.PLAIN: Moreover, the Lord will deliver Israel with you into the hand of the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. And the Lord will deliver the army of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.”

1SA.28.BSB: Immediately Saul fell flat on the ground, terrified by the words of Samuel. And his strength was gone, because he had not eaten anything all that day and night.
1SA.28.KJV: Then Saul fell straightway all along on the earth, and was sore afraid, because of the words of Samuel: and there was no strength in him; for he had eaten no bread all the day, nor all the night. ¶
1SA.28.PLAIN: Immediately Saul fell flat on the ground, terrified by the words of Samuel. And his strength was gone, because he had not eaten anything all that day and night.

1SA.28.BSB: When the woman came to Saul and saw how distraught he was, she said to him, “Look, your maidservant has obeyed your voice. I took my life in my hands and did as you told me.
1SA.28.KJV: And the woman came to Saul, and saw that he was sore troubled, and said to him, Behold, your handmaid has obeyed your voice, and I have put my life in my hand, and have listened to your words which you spoke to me.
1SA.28.PLAIN: When the woman came to Saul and saw how distraught he was, she said to him, “Look, your maidservant has obeyed your voice. I took my life in my hands and did as you told me.

1SA.28.BSB: Now please listen to your servant and let me set a morsel of bread before you so you may eat and have the strength to go on your way.”
1SA.28.KJV: Now therefore, I pray you, listen you also to the voice of your handmaid, and let me set a morsel of bread before you; and eat, that you may have strength, when you go on your way.
1SA.28.PLAIN: Now please listen to your servant and let me set a morsel of bread before you so you may eat and have the strength to go on your way.”

1SA.28.BSB: Saul refused, saying, “I will not eat.” But his servants joined the woman in urging him, and he heeded their voice. He got up from the ground and sat on the bed.
1SA.28.KJV: But he refused, and said, I will not eat. But his servants, together with the woman, compelled him; and he listened to their voice. So he arose from the earth, and sat on the bed.
1SA.28.PLAIN: Saul refused, saying, “I will not eat.” But his servants joined the woman in urging him, and he heeded their voice. He got up from the ground and sat on the bed.

1SA.28.BSB: The woman had a fattened calf at her house, and she quickly slaughtered it. She also took flour, kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread.
1SA.28.KJV: And the woman had a fat calf in the house; and she hurried, and killed it, and took flour, and kneaded it, and did bake unleavened bread thereof:
1SA.28.PLAIN: The woman had a fattened calf at her house, and she quickly slaughtered it. She also took flour, kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread.

1SA.28.BSB: She served it to Saul and his servants, and they ate. And that night they got up and left.
1SA.28.KJV: And she brought it before Saul, and before his servants; and they did eat. Then they rose up, and went away that night.
1SA.28.PLAIN: She served it to Saul and his servants, and they ate. And that night they got up and left.

1SA.29.BSB: Now the Philistines brought all their forces together at Aphek, while Israel camped by the spring in Jezreel.
1SA.29.KJV: Now the Philistines gathered together all their armies to Aphek: and the Israelites pitched by a fountain which is in Jezreel.
1SA.29.PLAIN: Now the Philistines brought all their forces together at Aphek, while Israel camped by the spring in Jezreel.

1SA.29.BSB: As the Philistine leaders marched out their units of hundreds and thousands, David and his men marched behind them with Achish.
1SA.29.KJV: And the lords of the Philistines passed on by hundreds, and by thousands: but David and his men passed on in the rear guard with Achish.
1SA.29.PLAIN: As the Philistine leaders marched out their units of hundreds and thousands, David and his men marched behind them with Achish.

1SA.29.BSB: Then the commanders of the Philistines asked, “What about these Hebrews?” Achish replied, “Is this not David, the servant of King Saul of Israel? He has been with me all these days, even years, and from the day he defected until today I have found no fault in him.”
1SA.29.KJV: Then said the princes of the Philistines, What do these Hebrews here? And Achish said to the princes of the Philistines, Is not this David, the servant of Saul the king of Israel, which has been with me these days, or these years, and I have found no fault in him since he fell to me to this day?
1SA.29.PLAIN: Then the commanders of the Philistines asked, “What about these Hebrews?” Achish replied, “Is this not David, the servant of King Saul of Israel? He has been with me all these days, even years, and from the day he defected until today I have found no fault in him.”

1SA.29.BSB: But the commanders of the Philistines were angry with Achish and told him, “Send that man back and let him return to the place you assigned him. He must not go down with us into battle only to become our adversary during the war. What better way for him to regain the favor of his master than with the heads of our men?
1SA.29.KJV: And the princes of the Philistines were wroth with him; and the princes of the Philistines said to him, Make this fellow return, that he may go again to his place which you have appointed him, and let him not go down with us to battle, lest in the battle he be an adversary to us: for with which should he reconcile himself to his master? should it not be with the heads of these men?
1SA.29.PLAIN: But the commanders of the Philistines were angry with Achish and told him, “Send that man back and let him return to the place you assigned him. He must not go down with us into battle only to become our adversary during the war. What better way for him to regain the favor of his master than with the heads of our men?

1SA.29.BSB: Is this not the David about whom they sing in their dances: ‘Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands’?”
1SA.29.KJV: Is not this David, of whom they sang one to another in dances, saying, Saul slew his thousands, and David his ten thousands? ¶
1SA.29.PLAIN: Is this not the David about whom they sing in their dances: ‘Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands’?”

1SA.29.BSB: So Achish summoned David and told him, “As surely as the LORD lives, you have been upright in my sight, and it seems right that you should march in and out with me in the army, because I have found no fault in you from the day you came to me until this day. But you have no favor in the sight of the leaders.
1SA.29.KJV: Then Achish called David, and said to him, Surely, as the LORD lives, you have been upright, and your going out and your coming in with me in the host is good in my sight: for I have not found evil in you since the day of your coming to me to this day: nevertheless the lords favor you not.
1SA.29.PLAIN: So Achish summoned David and told him, “As surely as the Lord lives, you have been upright in my sight, and it seems right that you should march in and out with me in the army, because I have found no fault in you from the day you came to me until this day. But you have no favor in the sight of the leaders.

1SA.29.BSB: Therefore turn back now and go in peace, so that you will not do anything to displease the leaders of the Philistines.”
1SA.29.KJV: Why now return, and go in peace, that you displease not the lords of the Philistines. ¶
1SA.29.PLAIN: Therefore turn back now and go in peace, so that you will not do anything to displease the leaders of the Philistines.”

1SA.29.BSB: “But what have I done?” David replied. “What have you found against your servant, from the day I came to you until today, to keep me from going along to fight against the enemies of my lord the king?”
1SA.29.KJV: And David said to Achish, But what have I done? and what have you found in your servant so long as I have been with you to this day, that I may not go fight against the enemies of my lord the king?
1SA.29.PLAIN: “But what have I done?” David replied. “What have you found against your servant, from the day I came to you until today, to keep me from going along to fight against the enemies of my lord the king?”

1SA.29.BSB: Achish replied, “I know that you are as pleasing in my sight as an angel of God. But the commanders of the Philistines have said, ‘He must not go into battle with us.’
1SA.29.KJV: And Achish answered and said to David, I know that you are good in my sight, as an angel of God: notwithstanding the princes of the Philistines have said, He shall not go up with us to the battle.
1SA.29.PLAIN: Achish replied, “I know that you are as pleasing in my sight as an angel of God. But the commanders of the Philistines have said, ‘He must not go into battle with us.’

1SA.29.BSB: Now then, get up early in the morning, along with your master’s servants who came with you, and go as soon as it is light.”
1SA.29.KJV: Why now rise up early in the morning with your master’s servants that are come with you: and as soon as you be up early in the morning, and have light, depart.
1SA.29.PLAIN: Now then, get up early in the morning, along with your master’s servants who came with you, and go as soon as it is light.”

1SA.29.BSB: So David and his men got up early in the morning to return to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
1SA.29.KJV: So David and his men rose up early to depart in the morning, to return into the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
1SA.29.PLAIN: So David and his men got up early in the morning to return to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.

1SA.30.BSB: On the third day David and his men arrived in Ziklag, and the Amalekites had raided the Negev, attacked Ziklag, and burned it down.
1SA.30.KJV: And it came to pass, when David and his men were come to Ziklag on the third day, that the Amalekites had invaded the south, and Ziklag, and smitten Ziklag, and burned it with fire;
1SA.30.PLAIN: On the third day David and his men arrived in Ziklag, and the Amalekites had raided the Negev, attacked Ziklag, and burned it down.

1SA.30.BSB: They had taken captive the women and all who were there, both young and old. They had not killed anyone, but had carried them off as they went on their way.
1SA.30.KJV: And had taken the women captives, that were therein: they slew not any, either great or small, but carried them away, and went on their way. ¶
1SA.30.PLAIN: They had taken captive the women and all who were there, both young and old. They had not killed anyone, but had carried them off as they went on their way.

1SA.30.BSB: When David and his men came to the city, they found it burned down and their wives and sons and daughters taken captive.
1SA.30.KJV: So David and his men came to the city, and, behold, it was burned with fire; and their wives, and their sons, and their daughters, were taken captives.
1SA.30.PLAIN: When David and his men came to the city, they found it burned down and their wives and sons and daughters taken captive.

1SA.30.BSB: So David and the troops with him lifted up their voices and wept until they had no strength left to weep.
1SA.30.KJV: Then David and the people that were with him lifted up their voice and wept, until they had no more power to weep.
1SA.30.PLAIN: So David and the troops with him lifted up their voices and wept until they had no strength left to weep.

1SA.30.BSB: David’s two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel, had been taken captive.
1SA.30.KJV: And David’s two wives were taken captives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
1SA.30.PLAIN: David’s two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel, had been taken captive.

1SA.30.BSB: And David was greatly distressed because the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of every man grieved for his sons and daughters. But David found strength in the LORD his God.
1SA.30.KJV: And David was greatly distressed; for the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters: but David encouraged himself in the LORD his God.
1SA.30.PLAIN: David was greatly distressed, for the people spoke of stoning him; each was bitter in spirit because of their sons and daughters. But David found strength in the Lord his God.

1SA.30.BSB: Then David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, “Bring me the ephod.” So Abiathar brought it to him,
1SA.30.KJV: And David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech’s son, I pray you, bring me here the ephod. And Abiathar brought thither the ephod to David.
1SA.30.PLAIN: Then David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, “Bring me the ephod.” So Abiathar brought it to him,

1SA.30.BSB: and David inquired of the LORD: “Should I pursue these raiders? Will I overtake them?” “Pursue them,” the LORD replied, “for you will surely overtake them and rescue the captives.”
1SA.30.KJV: And David inquired at the LORD, saying, Shall I pursue after this troop? shall I overtake them? And he answered him, Pursue: for you shall surely overtake them, and without fail recover all.
1SA.30.PLAIN: and David inquired of the Lord: “Should I pursue these raiders? Will I overtake them?” “Pursue them,” the Lord replied, “for you will surely overtake them and rescue the captives.”

1SA.30.BSB: So David and his six hundred men went to the Brook of Besor, where some stayed behind
1SA.30.KJV: So David went, he and the six hundred men that were with him, and came to the brook Besor, where those that were left behind stayed.
1SA.30.PLAIN: So David and his six hundred men went to the Brook of Besor, where some stayed behind

1SA.30.BSB: because two hundred men were too exhausted to cross the brook. But David and four hundred men continued in pursuit.
1SA.30.KJV: But David pursued, he and four hundred men: for two hundred stayed behind, which were so faint that they could not go over the brook Besor. ¶
1SA.30.PLAIN: because two hundred men were too exhausted to cross the brook. But David and four hundred men continued in pursuit.

1SA.30.BSB: Now his men found an Egyptian in the field and brought him to David. They gave the man water to drink and food to eat—
1SA.30.KJV: And they found an Egyptian in the field, and brought him to David, and gave him bread, and he did eat; and they made him drink water;
1SA.30.PLAIN: Now his men found an Egyptian in the field and brought him to David. They gave the man water to drink and food to eat—

1SA.30.BSB: a piece of a fig cake and two clusters of raisins. So he ate and was revived, for he had not had any food or water for three days and three nights.
1SA.30.KJV: And they gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins: and when he had eaten, his spirit came again to him: for he had eaten no bread, nor drunk any water, three days and three nights.
1SA.30.PLAIN: a piece of a fig cake and two clusters of raisins. So he ate and was revived, for he had not had any food or water for three days and three nights.

1SA.30.BSB: Then David asked him, “To whom do you belong, and where are you from?” “I am an Egyptian,” he replied, “the slave of an Amalekite. My master abandoned me three days ago when I fell ill.
1SA.30.KJV: And David said to him, To whom belong you? and from where are you? And he said, I am a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite; and my master left me, because three days ago I fell sick.
1SA.30.PLAIN: Then David asked him, “To whom do you belong, and where are you from?” “I am an Egyptian,” he replied, “the slave of an Amalekite. My master abandoned me three days ago when I fell ill.

1SA.30.BSB: We raided the Negev of the Cherethites, the territory of Judah, and the Negev of Caleb, and we burned down Ziklag.”
1SA.30.KJV: We made an invasion on the south of the Cherethites, and on the coast which belongs to Judah, and on the south of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire.
1SA.30.PLAIN: We raided the Negev of the Cherethites, the territory of Judah, and the Negev of Caleb, and we burned down Ziklag.”

1SA.30.BSB: “Will you lead me to these raiders?” David asked. And the man replied, “Swear to me by God that you will not kill me or deliver me into the hand of my master, and I will lead you to them.”
1SA.30.KJV: And David said to him, Can you bring me down to this company? And he said, Swear to me by God, that you will neither kill me, nor deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will bring you down to this company. ¶
1SA.30.PLAIN: “Will you lead me to these raiders?” David asked. And the man replied, “Swear to me by God that you will not kill me or deliver me into the hand of my master, and I will lead you to them.”

1SA.30.BSB: So he led David down, and there were the Amalekites spread out over all the land, eating, drinking, and celebrating the great amount of plunder they had taken from the land of the Philistines and the land of Judah.
1SA.30.KJV: And when he had brought him down, behold, they were spread abroad on all the earth, eating and drinking, and dancing, because of all the great spoil that they had taken out of the land of the Philistines, and out of the land of Judah.
1SA.30.PLAIN: So he led David down, and there were the Amalekites spread out over all the land, eating, drinking, and celebrating the great amount of plunder they had taken from the land of the Philistines and the land of Judah.

1SA.30.BSB: And David struck them down from twilight until the evening of the next day. Not a man escaped, except four hundred young men who fled, riding off on camels.
1SA.30.KJV: And David smote them from the twilight even to the evening of the next day: and there escaped not a man of them, save four hundred young men, which rode on camels, and fled.
1SA.30.PLAIN: And David struck them down from twilight until the evening of the next day. Not a man escaped, except four hundred young men who fled, riding off on camels.

1SA.30.BSB: So David recovered everything the Amalekites had taken, including his two wives.
1SA.30.KJV: And David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away: and David rescued his two wives.
1SA.30.PLAIN: So David recovered everything the Amalekites had taken, including his two wives.

1SA.30.BSB: Nothing was missing, young or old, son or daughter, or any of the plunder the Amalekites had taken. David brought everything back.
1SA.30.KJV: And there was nothing lacking to them, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, neither spoil, nor any thing that they had taken to them: David recovered all.
1SA.30.PLAIN: Nothing was missing, young or old, son or daughter, or any of the plunder the Amalekites had taken. David brought everything back.

1SA.30.BSB: And he recovered all the flocks and herds, which his men drove ahead of the other livestock, calling out, “This is David’s plunder!”
