1SA.30.KJV: And David took all the flocks and the herds, which they drove before those other cattle, and said, This is David’s spoil. ¶
1SA.30.PLAIN: And he recovered all the flocks and herds, which his men drove ahead of the other livestock, calling out, “This is David’s plunder!”

1SA.30.BSB: When David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow him from the Brook of Besor, they came out to meet him and the troops with him. As David approached the men, he greeted them,
1SA.30.KJV: And David came to the two hundred men, which were so faint that they could not follow David, whom they had made also to abide at the brook Besor: and they went forth to meet David, and to meet the people that were with him: and when David came near to the people, he saluted them.
1SA.30.PLAIN: When David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow him from the Brook of Besor, they came out to meet him and the troops with him. As David approached the men, he greeted them,

1SA.30.BSB: but all the wicked and worthless men among those who had gone with David said, “Because they did not go with us, we will not share with them the plunder we recovered, except for each man’s wife and children. They may take them and go.”
1SA.30.KJV: Then answered all the wicked men and men of Belial, of those that went with David, and said, Because they went not with us, we will not give them any of the spoil that we have recovered, save to every man his wife and his children, that they may lead them away, and depart.
1SA.30.PLAIN: but all the wicked and worthless men among those who had gone with David said, “Because they did not go with us, we will not share with them the plunder we recovered, except for each man’s wife and children. They may take them and go.”

1SA.30.BSB: But David said, “My brothers, you must not do this with what the LORD has given us. He has protected us and delivered into our hands the raiders who came against us.
1SA.30.KJV: Then said David, You shall not do so, my brothers, with that which the LORD has given us, who has preserved us, and delivered the company that came against us into our hand.
1SA.30.PLAIN: But David said, “My brothers, you must not do this with what the Lord has given us. He has protected us and delivered into our hands the raiders who came against us.

1SA.30.BSB: Who will listen to your proposal? The share of the one who went to battle will match the share of the one who stayed with the supplies. They will share alike.”
1SA.30.KJV: For who will listen to you in this matter? but as his part is that goes down to the battle, so shall his part be that tarries by the stuff: they shall part alike.
1SA.30.PLAIN: Who will listen to your proposal? The share of the one who went to battle will match the share of the one who stayed with the supplies. They will share alike.”

1SA.30.BSB: And so it has been from that day forward. David established this statute as an ordinance for Israel to this very day.
1SA.30.KJV: And it was so from that day forward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel to this day. ¶
1SA.30.PLAIN: And so it has been from that day forward. David established this statute as an ordinance for Israel to this very day.

1SA.30.BSB: When David arrived in Ziklag, he sent some of the plunder to his friends, the elders of Judah, saying, “Here is a gift for you from the plunder of the LORD’s enemies.”
1SA.30.KJV: And when David came to Ziklag, he sent of the spoil to the elders of Judah, even to his friends, saying, Behold a present for you of the spoil of the enemies of the LORD;
1SA.30.PLAIN: When David arrived in Ziklag, he sent some of the plunder to his friends, the elders of Judah, saying, “Here is a gift for you from the plunder of the Lord’s enemies.”

1SA.30.BSB: He sent gifts to those in Bethel, Ramoth Negev, and Jattir;
1SA.30.KJV: To them which were in Bethel, and to them which were in south Ramoth, and to them which were in Jattir,
1SA.30.PLAIN: He sent gifts to those in Bethel, Ramoth Negev, and Jattir;

1SA.30.BSB: to those in Aroer, Siphmoth, and Eshtemoa;
1SA.30.KJV: And to them which were in Aroer, and to them which were in Siphmoth, and to them which were in Eshtemoa,
1SA.30.PLAIN: to those in Aroer, Siphmoth, and Eshtemoa;

1SA.30.BSB: to those in Racal and in the cities of the Jerahmeelites and Kenites;
1SA.30.KJV: And to them which were in Rachal, and to them which were in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and to them which were in the cities of the Kenites,
1SA.30.PLAIN: to those in Racal and in the cities of the Jerahmeelites and Kenites;

1SA.30.BSB: to those in Hormah, Bor-ashan, and Athach;
1SA.30.KJV: And to them which were in Hormah, and to them which were in Chorashan, and to them which were in Athach,
1SA.30.PLAIN: to those in Hormah, Bor-ashan, and Athach;

1SA.30.BSB: and to those in Hebron and in all the places where David and his men had roamed.
1SA.30.KJV: And to them which were in Hebron, and to all the places where David himself and his men were wont to haunt.
1SA.30.PLAIN: and to those in Hebron and in all the places where David and his men had roamed.

1SA.31.BSB: Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before them, and many fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
1SA.31.KJV: Now the Philistines fought against Israel: and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gilboa.
1SA.31.PLAIN: Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before them, and many fell slain on Mount Gilboa.

1SA.31.BSB: The Philistines followed hard after Saul and his sons, and they killed Saul’s sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
1SA.31.KJV: And the Philistines followed hard on Saul and on his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Melchishua, Saul’s sons.
1SA.31.PLAIN: The Philistines followed hard after Saul and his sons, and they killed Saul’s sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.

1SA.31.BSB: When the battle intensified against Saul, the archers overtook him and wounded him critically.
1SA.31.KJV: And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit him; and he was sore wounded of the archers.
1SA.31.PLAIN: When the battle intensified against Saul, the archers overtook him and wounded him critically.

1SA.31.BSB: Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and run it through me, or these uncircumcised men will come and run me through and torture me!” But his armor-bearer was terrified and refused to do it. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.
1SA.31.KJV: Then said Saul to his armor bearer, Draw your sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me. But his armor bearer would not; for he was sore afraid. Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell on it.
1SA.31.PLAIN: Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and run it through me, or these uncircumcised men will come and run me through and torture me!” But his armor-bearer was terrified and refused to do it. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.

1SA.31.BSB: When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his own sword and died with him.
1SA.31.KJV: And when his armor bearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise on his sword, and died with him.
1SA.31.PLAIN: When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his own sword and died with him.

1SA.31.BSB: So Saul, his three sons, his armor-bearer, and all his men died together that same day.
1SA.31.KJV: So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armor bearer, and all his men, that same day together. ¶
1SA.31.PLAIN: So Saul, his three sons, his armor-bearer, and all his men died together that same day.

1SA.31.BSB: When the Israelites along the valley and those on the other side of the Jordan saw that the army of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons had died, they abandoned their cities and ran away. So the Philistines came and occupied their cities.
1SA.31.KJV: And when the men of Israel that were on the other side of the valley, and they that were on the other side Jordan, saw that the men of Israel fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, they forsook the cities, and fled; and the Philistines came and dwelled in them.
1SA.31.PLAIN: When the Israelites along the valley and those on the other side of the Jordan saw that the army of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons had died, they abandoned their cities and ran away. So the Philistines came and occupied their cities.

1SA.31.BSB: The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the dead, they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
1SA.31.KJV: And it came to pass on the morrow, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his three sons fallen in mount Gilboa.
1SA.31.PLAIN: The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the dead, they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

1SA.31.BSB: They cut off Saul’s head, stripped off his armor, and sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the news in the temples of their idols and among their people.
1SA.31.KJV: And they cut off his head, and stripped off his armor, and sent into the land of the Philistines round about, to publish it in the house of their idols, and among the people.
1SA.31.PLAIN: They cut off Saul’s head, stripped off his armor, and sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the news in the temples of their idols and among their people.

1SA.31.BSB: They put his armor in the temple of the Ashtoreths and hung his body on the wall of Beth-shan.
1SA.31.KJV: And they put his armor in the house of Ashtaroth: and they fastened his body to the wall of Bethshan. ¶
1SA.31.PLAIN: They put his armor in the temple of the Ashtoreths and hung his body on the wall of Beth-shan.

1SA.31.BSB: When the people of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,
1SA.31.KJV: And when the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead heard of that which the Philistines had done to Saul;
1SA.31.PLAIN: When the people of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,

1SA.31.BSB: all their men of valor set out, journeyed all night, and retrieved the bodies of Saul and his sons from the wall of Beth-shan. When they arrived at Jabesh, they burned the bodies there.
1SA.31.KJV: All the valiant men arose, and went all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Bethshan, and came to Jabesh, and burnt them there.
1SA.31.PLAIN: all their men of valor set out, journeyed all night, and retrieved the bodies of Saul and his sons from the wall of Beth-shan. When they arrived at Jabesh, they burned the bodies there.

1SA.31.BSB: Then they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh, and they fasted seven days.
1SA.31.KJV: And they took their bones, and buried them under a tree at Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
1SA.31.PLAIN: Then they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh, and they fasted seven days.

2SA.1.BSB: After the death of Saul, David returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites and stayed in Ziklag two days.
2SA.1.KJV: Now it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had stayed two days in Ziklag;
2SA.1.PLAIN: After the death of Saul, David returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites and stayed in Ziklag two days.

2SA.1.BSB: On the third day a man with torn clothes and dust on his head arrived from Saul’s camp. When he came to David, he fell to the ground to pay him homage.
2SA.1.KJV: It came even to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes rent, and earth on his head: and so it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.
2SA.1.PLAIN: On the third day a man with torn clothes and dust on his head arrived from Saul’s camp. When he came to David, he fell to the ground to pay him homage.

2SA.1.BSB: “Where have you come from?” David asked. “I have escaped from the Israelite camp,” he replied.
2SA.1.KJV: And David said to him, From where come you? And he said to him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.
2SA.1.PLAIN: “Where have you come from?” David asked. “I have escaped from the Israelite camp,” he replied.

2SA.1.BSB: “What was the outcome?” David asked. “Please tell me.” “The troops fled from the battle,” he replied. “Many of them fell and died. And Saul and his son Jonathan are also dead.”
2SA.1.KJV: And David said to him, How went the matter? I pray you, tell me. And he answered, That the people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.
2SA.1.PLAIN: “What was the outcome?” David asked. “Please tell me.” “The troops fled from the battle,” he replied. “Many of them fell and died. And Saul and his son Jonathan are also dead.”

2SA.1.BSB: Then David asked the young man who had brought him the report, “How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?”
2SA.1.KJV: And David said to the young man that told him, How know you that Saul and Jonathan his son be dead?
2SA.1.PLAIN: Then David asked the young man who had brought him the report, “How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?”

2SA.1.BSB: “I happened to be on Mount Gilboa,” he replied, “and there was Saul, leaning on his spear, with the chariots and the cavalry closing in on him.
2SA.1.KJV: And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance on mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned on his spear; and, see, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.
2SA.1.PLAIN: “I happened to be on Mount Gilboa,” he replied, “and there was Saul, leaning on his spear, with the chariots and the cavalry closing in on him.

2SA.1.BSB: When he turned around and saw me, he called out and I answered, ‘Here I am!’
2SA.1.KJV: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called to me. And I answered, Here am I.
2SA.1.PLAIN: When he turned around and saw me, he called out and I answered, ‘Here I am!’

2SA.1.BSB: ‘Who are you?’ he asked. So I told him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’
2SA.1.KJV: And he said to me, Who are you? And I answered him, I am an Amalekite.
2SA.1.PLAIN: ‘Who are you?’ he asked. So I told him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’

2SA.1.BSB: Then he begged me, ‘Stand over me and kill me, for agony has seized me, but my life still lingers.’
2SA.1.KJV: He said to me again, Stand, I pray you, on me, and slay me: for anguish is come on me, because my life is yet whole in me.
2SA.1.PLAIN: Then he begged me, ‘Stand over me and kill me, for agony has seized me, but my life still lingers.’

2SA.1.BSB: So I stood over him and killed him, because I knew that after he had fallen he could not survive. And I took the crown that was on his head and the band that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord.”
2SA.1.KJV: So I stood on him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he was fallen: and I took the crown that was on his head, and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them here to my lord.
2SA.1.PLAIN: So I stood over him and killed him, because I knew that after he had fallen he could not survive. And I took the crown that was on his head and the band that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord.”

2SA.1.BSB: Then David took hold of his own clothes and tore them, and all the men who were with him did the same.
2SA.1.KJV: Then David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the men that were with him:
2SA.1.PLAIN: Then David took hold of his own clothes and tore them, and all the men who were with him did the same.

2SA.1.BSB: They mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and his son Jonathan, and for the people of the LORD and the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
2SA.1.KJV: And they mourned, and wept, and fasted until even, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of the LORD, and for the house of Israel; because they were fallen by the sword. ¶
2SA.1.PLAIN: They mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and his son Jonathan, and for the people of the Lord and the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

2SA.1.BSB: And David inquired of the young man who had brought him the report, “Where are you from?” “I am the son of a foreigner,” he answered. “I am an Amalekite.”
2SA.1.KJV: And David said to the young man that told him, From where are you? And he answered, I am the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.
2SA.1.PLAIN: And David inquired of the young man who had brought him the report, “Where are you from?” “I am the son of a foreigner,” he answered. “I am an Amalekite.”

2SA.1.BSB: So David asked him, “Why were you not afraid to lift your hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed?”
2SA.1.KJV: And David said to him, How were you not afraid to stretch forth your hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed?
2SA.1.PLAIN: So David asked him, “Why were you not afraid to lift your hand to destroy the Lord’s anointed?”

2SA.1.BSB: Then David summoned one of the young men and said, “Go, execute him!” So the young man struck him down, and he died.
2SA.1.KJV: And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, and fall on him. And he smote him that he died.
2SA.1.PLAIN: Then David summoned one of the young men and said, “Go, execute him!” So the young man struck him down, and he died.

2SA.1.BSB: For David had said to the Amalekite, “Your blood be on your own head because your own mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I killed the LORD’s anointed.’”
2SA.1.KJV: And David said to him, Your blood be on your head; for your mouth has testified against you, saying, I have slain the LORD’s anointed. ¶
2SA.1.PLAIN: For David had said to the Amalekite, “Your blood be on your own head because your own mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I killed the Lord’s anointed.’”

2SA.1.BSB: Then David took up this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan,
2SA.1.KJV: And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son:
2SA.1.PLAIN: Then David took up this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan,

2SA.1.BSB: and he ordered that the sons of Judah be taught the Song of the Bow. It is written in the Book of Jashar:
2SA.1.KJV: (Also he bade them teach the children of Judah the use of the bow: behold, it is written in the book of Jasher.)
2SA.1.PLAIN: and he ordered that the sons of Judah be taught the Song of the Bow. It is written in the Book of Jashar:

2SA.1.BSB: “Your glory, O Israel, lies slain on your heights. How the mighty have fallen!
2SA.1.KJV: The beauty of Israel is slain on your high places: how are the mighty fallen!
2SA.1.PLAIN: “Your glory, O Israel, lies slain on your heights. How the mighty have fallen!

2SA.1.BSB: Tell it not in Gath; proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, and the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
2SA.1.KJV: Tell it not in Gath, publish it not in the streets of Askelon; lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.
2SA.1.PLAIN: Tell it not in Gath; proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, and the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.

2SA.1.BSB: O mountains of Gilboa, may you have no dew or rain, no fields yielding offerings of grain. For there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.
2SA.1.KJV: You mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew, neither let there be rain, on you, nor fields of offerings: for there the shield of the mighty is vilely cast away, the shield of Saul, as though he had not been anointed with oil.
2SA.1.PLAIN: O mountains of Gilboa, may you have no dew or rain, no fields yielding offerings of grain. For there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.

2SA.1.BSB: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not retreat, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.
2SA.1.KJV: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan turned not back, and the sword of Saul returned not empty.
2SA.1.PLAIN: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not retreat, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.

2SA.1.BSB: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and delightful in life, were not divided in death. They were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.
2SA.1.KJV: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.
2SA.1.PLAIN: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and delightful in life, were not divided in death. They were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.

2SA.1.BSB: O daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet and luxury, who decked your garments with ornaments of gold.
2SA.1.KJV: You daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet, with other delights, who put on ornaments of gold on your apparel.
2SA.1.PLAIN: O daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet and luxury, who decked your garments with ornaments of gold.

2SA.1.BSB: How the mighty have fallen in the thick of battle! Jonathan lies slain on your heights.
2SA.1.KJV: How are the mighty fallen in the middle of the battle! O Jonathan, you were slain in your high places.
2SA.1.PLAIN: How the mighty have fallen in the thick of battle! Jonathan lies slain on your heights.

2SA.1.BSB: I grieve for you, Jonathan, my brother. You were delightful to me; your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.
2SA.1.KJV: I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant have you been to me: your love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.
2SA.1.PLAIN: I grieve for you, Jonathan, my brother. You were delightful to me; your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.

2SA.1.BSB: How the mighty have fallen and the weapons of war have perished!”
2SA.1.KJV: How are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished!
2SA.1.PLAIN: How the mighty have fallen and the weapons of war have perished!”

2SA.2.BSB: Some time later, David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go up to one of the towns of Judah?” “Go up,” the LORD answered. Then David asked, “Where should I go?” “To Hebron,” replied the LORD.
2SA.2.KJV: And it came to pass after this, that David inquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah? And the LORD said to him, Go up. And David said, Where shall I go up? And he said, To Hebron.
2SA.2.PLAIN: Some time later, David inquired of the Lord, “Should I go up to one of the towns of Judah?” “Go up,” the Lord answered. Then David asked, “Where should I go?” “To Hebron,” replied the Lord.

2SA.2.BSB: So David went there with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel.
2SA.2.KJV: So David went up thither, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail Nabal’s wife the Carmelite.
2SA.2.PLAIN: So David went there with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel.

2SA.2.BSB: David also took the men who were with him, each with his household, and they settled in the towns near Hebron.
2SA.2.KJV: And his men that were with him did David bring up, every man with his household: and they dwelled in the cities of Hebron.
2SA.2.PLAIN: David also took the men who were with him, each with his household, and they settled in the towns near Hebron.

2SA.2.BSB: Then the men of Judah came to Hebron, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, “It was the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul.”
2SA.2.KJV: And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, That the men of Jabeshgilead were they that buried Saul. ¶
2SA.2.PLAIN: Then the men of Judah came to Hebron, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, “It was the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul.”

2SA.2.BSB: So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead to tell them, “The LORD bless you, because you showed this kindness to Saul your lord when you buried him.
2SA.2.KJV: And David sent messengers to the men of Jabeshgilead, and said to them, Blessed be you of the LORD, that you have showed this kindness to your lord, even to Saul, and have buried him.
2SA.2.PLAIN: So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead to tell them, “The Lord bless you, because you showed this kindness to Saul your lord when you buried him.

2SA.2.BSB: Now may the LORD show you loving devotion and faithfulness, and I will also show you the same favor because you have done this.
2SA.2.KJV: And now the LORD show kindness and truth to you: and I also will requite you this kindness, because you have done this thing.
2SA.2.PLAIN: Now may the Lord show you loving devotion and faithfulness, and I will also show you the same favor because you have done this.

2SA.2.BSB: Now then, be strong and courageous, for though Saul your lord is dead, the house of Judah has anointed me as their king.”
2SA.2.KJV: Therefore now let your hands be strengthened, and be you valiant: for your master Saul is dead, and also the house of Judah have anointed me king over them. ¶
2SA.2.PLAIN: Now then, be strong and courageous, for though Saul your lord is dead, the house of Judah has anointed me as their king.”

2SA.2.BSB: Meanwhile, Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul’s army, took Saul’s son Ish-bosheth, moved him to Mahanaim,
2SA.2.KJV: But Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul’s host, took Ishbosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim;
2SA.2.PLAIN: Meanwhile, Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul’s army, took Saul’s son Ish-bosheth, moved him to Mahanaim,

2SA.2.BSB: and made him king over Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin—over all Israel.
2SA.2.KJV: And made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
2SA.2.PLAIN: and made him king over Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin—over all Israel.

2SA.2.BSB: Saul’s son Ish-bosheth was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned for two years. The house of Judah, however, followed David.
2SA.2.KJV: Ishbosheth Saul’s son was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.
2SA.2.PLAIN: Saul’s son Ish-bosheth was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned for two years. The house of Judah, however, followed David.

2SA.2.BSB: And the length of time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
2SA.2.KJV: And the time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months. ¶
2SA.2.PLAIN: And the length of time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

2SA.2.BSB: One day Abner son of Ner and the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul marched out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
2SA.2.KJV: And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ishbosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
2SA.2.PLAIN: One day Abner son of Ner and the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul marched out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

2SA.2.BSB: So Joab son of Zeruiah, along with the servants of David, marched out and met them by the pool of Gibeon. And the two camps took up positions on opposite sides of the pool.
2SA.2.KJV: And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went out, and met together by the pool of Gibeon: and they sat down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.
2SA.2.PLAIN: So Joab son of Zeruiah, along with the servants of David, marched out and met them by the pool of Gibeon. And the two camps took up positions on opposite sides of the pool.

2SA.2.BSB: Then Abner said to Joab, “Let us have the young men get up and compete before us.” “Let them get up,” Joab replied.
2SA.2.KJV: And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men now arise, and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.
2SA.2.PLAIN: Then Abner said to Joab, “Let us have the young men get up and compete before us.” “Let them get up,” Joab replied.

2SA.2.BSB: So they got up and were counted off—twelve for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve for David.
2SA.2.KJV: Then there arose and went over by number twelve of Benjamin, which pertained to Ishbosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.
2SA.2.PLAIN: So they got up and were counted off—twelve for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve for David.

2SA.2.BSB: Then each man grabbed his opponent by the head and thrust his sword into his opponent’s side, and they all fell together. So this place, which is in Gibeon, is called Helkath-hazzurim.
2SA.2.KJV: And they caught every one his fellow by the head, and thrust his sword in his fellow’s side; so they fell down together: why that place was called Helkathhazzurim, which is in Gibeon.
2SA.2.PLAIN: Then each man grabbed his opponent by the head and thrust his sword into his opponent’s side, and they all fell together. So this place, which is in Gibeon, is called Helkath-hazzurim.

2SA.2.BSB: The battle that day was intense, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated by the servants of David.
2SA.2.KJV: And there was a very sore battle that day; and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David. ¶
2SA.2.PLAIN: The battle that day was intense, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated by the servants of David.

2SA.2.BSB: The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Now Asahel was fleet of foot like a wild gazelle,
2SA.2.KJV: And there were three sons of Zeruiah there, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel: and Asahel was as light of foot as a wild roe.
2SA.2.PLAIN: The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Now Asahel was fleet of foot like a wild gazelle,

2SA.2.BSB: and he chased Abner, not turning to the right or to the left in his pursuit.
2SA.2.KJV: And Asahel pursued after Abner; and in going he turned not to the right hand nor to the left from following Abner.
2SA.2.PLAIN: and he chased Abner, not turning to the right or to the left in his pursuit.

2SA.2.BSB: And Abner glanced back and said, “Is that you, Asahel?” “It is,” Asahel replied.
2SA.2.KJV: Then Abner looked behind him, and said, Are you Asahel? And he answered, I am.
2SA.2.PLAIN: And Abner glanced back and said, “Is that you, Asahel?” “It is,” Asahel replied.

2SA.2.BSB: So Abner told him, “Turn to your right or to your left, seize one of the young men, and take his equipment for yourself.” But Asahel would not stop chasing him.
2SA.2.KJV: And Abner said to him, Turn you aside to your right hand or to your left, and lay you hold on one of the young men, and take you his armor. But Asahel would not turn aside from following of him.
2SA.2.PLAIN: So Abner told him, “Turn to your right or to your left, seize one of the young men, and take his equipment for yourself.” But Asahel would not stop chasing him.

2SA.2.BSB: Once again, Abner warned Asahel, “Stop chasing me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How could I show my face to your brother Joab?”
2SA.2.KJV: And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn you aside from following me: why should I smite you to the ground? how then should I hold up my face to Joab your brother?
2SA.2.PLAIN: Once again, Abner warned Asahel, “Stop chasing me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How could I show my face to your brother Joab?”

2SA.2.BSB: But Asahel refused to turn away; so Abner thrust the butt of his spear into his stomach, and it came out his back, and he fell dead on the spot. And every man paused when he came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died.
2SA.2.KJV: However, he refused to turn aside: why Abner with the hinder end of the spear smote him under the fifth rib, that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same place: and it came to pass, that as many as came to the place where Asahel fell down and died stood still.
2SA.2.PLAIN: But Asahel refused to turn away; so Abner thrust the butt of his spear into his stomach, and it came out his back, and he fell dead on the spot. And every man paused when he came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died.

2SA.2.BSB: But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. By sunset, they had gone as far as the hill of Ammah opposite Giah on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.
2SA.2.KJV: Joab also and Abishai pursued after Abner: and the sun went down when they were come to the hill of Ammah, that lies before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon. ¶
2SA.2.PLAIN: But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. By sunset, they had gone as far as the hill of Ammah opposite Giah on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.

2SA.2.BSB: The Benjamites rallied to Abner, formed a single unit, and took their stand atop a hill.
2SA.2.KJV: And the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, and became one troop, and stood on the top of an hill.
2SA.2.PLAIN: The Benjamites rallied to Abner, formed a single unit, and took their stand atop a hill.

2SA.2.BSB: Then Abner called out to Joab: “Must the sword devour forever? Do you not realize that this will only end in bitterness? How long before you tell the troops to stop pursuing their brothers?”
2SA.2.KJV: Then Abner called to Joab, and said, Shall the sword devour for ever? know you not that it will be bitterness in the latter end? how long shall it be then, before you bid the people return from following their brothers?
2SA.2.PLAIN: Then Abner called out to Joab: “Must the sword devour forever? Do you not realize that this will only end in bitterness? How long before you tell the troops to stop pursuing their brothers?”

2SA.2.BSB: “As surely as God lives,” Joab replied, “if you had not spoken up, the troops would have continued pursuing their brothers until morning.”
2SA.2.KJV: And Joab said, As God lives, unless you had spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone up every one from following his brother.
2SA.2.PLAIN: “As surely as God lives,” Joab replied, “if you had not spoken up, the troops would have continued pursuing their brothers until morning.”

2SA.2.BSB: So Joab blew the ram’s horn, and all the troops stopped; they no longer pursued Israel or continued to fight.
2SA.2.KJV: So Joab blew a trumpet, and all the people stood still, and pursued after Israel no more, neither fought they any more.
2SA.2.PLAIN: So Joab blew the ram’s horn, and all the troops stopped; they no longer pursued Israel or continued to fight.

2SA.2.BSB: And all that night Abner and his men marched through the Arabah. They crossed the Jordan, marched all morning, and arrived at Mahanaim.
2SA.2.KJV: And Abner and his men walked all that night through the plain, and passed over Jordan, and went through all Bithron, and they came to Mahanaim.
2SA.2.PLAIN: And all that night Abner and his men marched through the Arabah. They crossed the Jordan, marched all morning, and arrived at Mahanaim.

2SA.2.BSB: When Joab returned from pursuing Abner, he gathered all the troops. In addition to Asahel, nineteen of David’s servants were missing,
2SA.2.KJV: And Joab returned from following Abner: and when he had gathered all the people together, there lacked of David’s servants nineteen men and Asahel.
2SA.2.PLAIN: When Joab returned from pursuing Abner, he gathered all the troops. In addition to Asahel, nineteen of David’s servants were missing,

2SA.2.BSB: but they had struck down 360 Benjamites who were with Abner.
2SA.2.KJV: But the servants of David had smitten of Benjamin, and of Abner’s men, so that three hundred and three score men died. ¶
2SA.2.PLAIN: but they had struck down 360 Benjamites who were with Abner.

2SA.2.BSB: Later, they took Asahel and buried him in his father’s tomb in Bethlehem. Then Joab and his men marched all night and reached Hebron at daybreak.
2SA.2.KJV: And they took up Asahel, and buried him in the sepulcher of his father, which was in Bethlehem. And Joab and his men went all night, and they came to Hebron at break of day.
2SA.2.PLAIN: Later, they took Asahel and buried him in his father’s tomb in Bethlehem. Then Joab and his men marched all night and reached Hebron at daybreak.

2SA.3.BSB: Now the war between the house of Saul and the house of David was protracted. And David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul grew weaker and weaker.
2SA.3.KJV: Now there was long war between the house of Saul and the house of David: but David waxed stronger and stronger, and the house of Saul waxed weaker and weaker. ¶
2SA.3.PLAIN: Now the war between the house of Saul and the house of David was protracted. And David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul grew weaker and weaker.

2SA.3.BSB: And sons were born to David in Hebron: His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel;
2SA.3.KJV: And to David were sons born in Hebron: and his firstborn was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;
2SA.3.PLAIN: And sons were born to David in Hebron: His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel;

2SA.3.BSB: his second was Chileab, by Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel; his third was Absalom, the son of Maacah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur;
2SA.3.KJV: And his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
2SA.3.PLAIN: his second was Chileab, by Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel; his third was Absalom, the son of Maacah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur;

2SA.3.BSB: his fourth was Adonijah, the son of Haggith; his fifth was Shephatiah, the son of Abital;
2SA.3.KJV: And the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;
2SA.3.PLAIN: his fourth was Adonijah, the son of Haggith; his fifth was Shephatiah, the son of Abital;

2SA.3.BSB: and his sixth was Ithream, by David’s wife Eglah. These sons were born to David in Hebron.
2SA.3.KJV: And the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah David’s wife. These were born to David in Hebron. ¶
2SA.3.PLAIN: and his sixth was Ithream, by David’s wife Eglah. These sons were born to David in Hebron.

2SA.3.BSB: During the war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner had continued to strengthen his position in the house of Saul.
2SA.3.KJV: And it came to pass, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner made himself strong for the house of Saul.
2SA.3.PLAIN: During the war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner had continued to strengthen his position in the house of Saul.

2SA.3.BSB: Meanwhile, Saul had a concubine named Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. So Ish-bosheth questioned Abner, “Why did you sleep with my father’s concubine?”
2SA.3.KJV: And Saul had a concubine, whose name was Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah: and Ishbosheth said to Abner, Why have you gone in to my father’s concubine?
2SA.3.PLAIN: Meanwhile, Saul had a concubine named Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. So Ish-bosheth questioned Abner, “Why did you sleep with my father’s concubine?”

2SA.3.BSB: Abner was furious over Ish-bosheth’s accusation. “Am I the head of a dog that belongs to Judah?” he asked. “All this time I have been loyal to the house of your father Saul, to his brothers, and to his friends. I have not delivered you into the hand of David, but now you accuse me of wrongdoing with this woman!
2SA.3.KJV: Then was Abner very wroth for the words of Ishbosheth, and said, Am I a dog’s head, which against Judah do show kindness this day to the house of Saul your father, to his brothers, and to his friends, and have not delivered you into the hand of David, that you charge me to day with a fault concerning this woman?
2SA.3.PLAIN: Abner was furious over Ish-bosheth’s accusation. “Am I the head of a dog that belongs to Judah?” he asked. “All this time I have been loyal to the house of your father Saul, to his brothers, and to his friends. I have not delivered you into the hand of David, but now you accuse me of wrongdoing with this woman!

2SA.3.BSB: May God punish Abner, and ever so severely, if I do not do for David what the LORD has sworn to him:
2SA.3.KJV: So do God to Abner, and more also, except, as the LORD has sworn to David, even so I do to him;
2SA.3.PLAIN: May God punish Abner, and ever so severely, if I do not do for David what the Lord has sworn to him:

2SA.3.BSB: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and to establish the throne of David over Israel and Judah, from Dan to Beersheba.”
2SA.3.KJV: To translate the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beersheba.
2SA.3.PLAIN: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and to establish the throne of David over Israel and Judah, from Dan to Beersheba.”

2SA.3.BSB: And for fear of Abner, Ish-bosheth did not dare to say another word to him.
2SA.3.KJV: And he could not answer Abner a word again, because he feared him. ¶
2SA.3.PLAIN: And for fear of Abner, Ish-bosheth did not dare to say another word to him.

2SA.3.BSB: Then Abner sent messengers in his place to say to David, “To whom does the land belong? Make your covenant with me, and surely my hand will be with you to bring all Israel over to you.”
2SA.3.KJV: And Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, Whose is the land? saying also, Make your league with me, and, behold, my hand shall be with you, to bring about all Israel to you. ¶
2SA.3.PLAIN: Then Abner sent messengers in his place to say to David, “To whom does the land belong? Make your covenant with me, and surely my hand will be with you to bring all Israel over to you.”

2SA.3.BSB: “Good,” replied David, “I will make a covenant with you. But there is one thing I require of you: Do not appear before me unless you bring Saul’s daughter Michal when you come to see me.”
2SA.3.KJV: And he said, Well; I will make a league with you: but one thing I require of you, that is, You shall not see my face, except you first bring Michal Saul’s daughter, when you come to see my face.
2SA.3.PLAIN: “Good,” replied David, “I will make a covenant with you. But there is one thing I require of you: Do not appear before me unless you bring Saul’s daughter Michal when you come to see me.”

2SA.3.BSB: Then David sent messengers to say to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, “Give me back my wife, Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred Philistine foreskins.”
2SA.3.KJV: And David sent messengers to Ishbosheth Saul’s son, saying, Deliver me my wife Michal, which I espoused to me for an hundred foreskins of the Philistines.
2SA.3.PLAIN: Then David sent messengers to say to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, “Give me back my wife, Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred Philistine foreskins.”

2SA.3.BSB: So Ish-bosheth sent and took Michal from her husband Paltiel son of Laish.
2SA.3.KJV: And Ishbosheth sent, and took her from her husband, even from Phaltiel the son of Laish.
2SA.3.PLAIN: So Ish-bosheth sent and took Michal from her husband Paltiel son of Laish.

2SA.3.BSB: Her husband followed her, weeping all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, “Go back.” So he returned home.
2SA.3.KJV: And her husband went with her along weeping behind her to Bahurim. Then said Abner to him, Go, return. And he returned. ¶
2SA.3.PLAIN: Her husband followed her, weeping all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, “Go back.” So he returned home.

2SA.3.BSB: Now Abner conferred with the elders of Israel and said, “In the past you sought David as your king.
2SA.3.KJV: And Abner had communication with the elders of Israel, saying, You sought for David in times past to be king over you:
2SA.3.PLAIN: Now Abner conferred with the elders of Israel and said, “In the past you sought David as your king.

2SA.3.BSB: Now take action, because the LORD has said to David, ‘Through My servant David I will save My people Israel from the hands of the Philistines and of all their enemies.’”
2SA.3.KJV: Now then do it: for the LORD has spoken of David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.
2SA.3.PLAIN: Now take action, because the Lord has said to David, ‘Through My servant David I will save My people Israel from the hands of the Philistines and of all their enemies.’”

2SA.3.BSB: Abner also spoke to the Benjamites and went to Hebron to tell David all that seemed good to Israel and to the whole house of Benjamin.
2SA.3.KJV: And Abner also spoke in the ears of Benjamin: and Abner went also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel, and that seemed good to the whole house of Benjamin.
2SA.3.PLAIN: Abner also spoke to the Benjamites and went to Hebron to tell David all that seemed good to Israel and to the whole house of Benjamin.

2SA.3.BSB: When Abner and twenty of his men came to David at Hebron, David held a feast for them.
2SA.3.KJV: So Abner came to David to Hebron, and twenty men with him. And David made Abner and the men that were with him a feast.
2SA.3.PLAIN: When Abner and twenty of his men came to David at Hebron, David held a feast for them.

2SA.3.BSB: Then Abner said to David, “Let me go at once, and I will gather all Israel to my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with you, and that you may rule over all that your heart desires.” So David dismissed Abner, and he went in peace.
2SA.3.KJV: And Abner said to David, I will arise and go, and will gather all Israel to my lord the king, that they may make a league with you, and that you may reign over all that your heart desires. And David sent Abner away; and he went in peace. ¶
2SA.3.PLAIN: Then Abner said to David, “Let me go at once, and I will gather all Israel to my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with you, and that you may rule over all that your heart desires.” So David dismissed Abner, and he went in peace.

2SA.3.BSB: Just then David’s soldiers and Joab returned from a raid, bringing with them a great plunder. But Abner was not with David in Hebron because David had sent him on his way in peace.
2SA.3.KJV: And, behold, the servants of David and Joab came from pursuing a troop, and brought in a great spoil with them: but Abner was not with David in Hebron; for he had sent him away, and he was gone in peace.
2SA.3.PLAIN: Just then David’s soldiers and Joab returned from a raid, bringing with them a great plunder. But Abner was not with David in Hebron because David had sent him on his way in peace.

2SA.3.BSB: When Joab and all his troops arrived, he was informed, “Abner son of Ner came to see the king, who sent him on his way in peace.”
2SA.3.KJV: When Joab and all the host that was with him were come, they told Joab, saying, Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he has sent him away, and he is gone in peace.
2SA.3.PLAIN: When Joab and all his troops arrived, he was informed, “Abner son of Ner came to see the king, who sent him on his way in peace.”

2SA.3.BSB: So Joab went to the king and said, “What have you done? Look, Abner came to you. Why did you dismiss him? Now he is getting away!
2SA.3.KJV: Then Joab came to the king, and said, What have you done? behold, Abner came to you; why is it that you have sent him away, and he is quite gone?
2SA.3.PLAIN: So Joab went to the king and said, “What have you done? Look, Abner came to you. Why did you dismiss him? Now he is getting away!

2SA.3.BSB: Surely you realize that Abner son of Ner came to deceive you and to track your movements and all that you are doing.”
2SA.3.KJV: You know Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive you, and to know your going out and your coming in, and to know all that you do.
2SA.3.PLAIN: Surely you realize that Abner son of Ner came to deceive you and to track your movements and all that you are doing.”

2SA.3.BSB: As soon as Joab had left David, he sent messengers after Abner, who brought him back from the well of Sirah; but David was unaware of it.
2SA.3.KJV: And when Joab was come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, which brought him again from the well of Sirah: but David knew it not.
2SA.3.PLAIN: As soon as Joab had left David, he sent messengers after Abner, who brought him back from the well of Sirah; but David was unaware of it.

2SA.3.BSB: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pulled him aside into the gateway, as if to speak to him privately, and there Joab stabbed him in the stomach. So Abner died on account of the blood of Joab’s brother Asahel.
2SA.3.KJV: And when Abner was returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside in the gate to speak with him quietly, and smote him there under the fifth rib, that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother. ¶
2SA.3.PLAIN: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pulled him aside into the gateway, as if to speak to him privately, and there Joab stabbed him in the stomach. So Abner died on account of the blood of Joab’s brother Asahel.

2SA.3.BSB: Afterward, David heard about this and said, “I and my kingdom are forever guiltless before the LORD concerning the blood of Abner son of Ner.
2SA.3.KJV: And afterward when David heard it, he said, I and my kingdom are guiltless before the LORD for ever from the blood of Abner the son of Ner:
2SA.3.PLAIN: Afterward, David heard about this and said, “I and my kingdom are forever guiltless before the Lord concerning the blood of Abner son of Ner.

2SA.3.BSB: May it whirl over the heads of Joab and the entire house of his father, and may the house of Joab never be without one having a discharge or skin disease, or one who leans on a staff or falls by the sword or lacks food.”
2SA.3.KJV: Let it rest on the head of Joab, and on all his father’s house; and let there not fail from the house of Joab one that has an issue, or that is a leper, or that leans on a staff, or that falls on the sword, or that lacks bread.
2SA.3.PLAIN: May it whirl over the heads of Joab and the entire house of his father, and may the house of Joab never be without one having a discharge or skin disease, or one who leans on a staff or falls by the sword or lacks food.”

2SA.3.BSB: (Joab and his brother Abishai murdered Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.)
2SA.3.KJV: So Joab, and Abishai his brother slew Abner, because he had slain their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle. ¶
2SA.3.PLAIN: (Joab and his brother Abishai murdered Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.)

2SA.3.BSB: Then David ordered Joab and all the people with him, “Tear your clothes, put on sackcloth, and mourn before Abner.” And King David himself walked behind the funeral bier.
2SA.3.KJV: And David said to Joab, and to all the people that were with him, Rend your clothes, and gird you with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner. And king David himself followed the bier.
2SA.3.PLAIN: Then David ordered Joab and all the people with him, “Tear your clothes, put on sackcloth, and mourn before Abner.” And King David himself walked behind the funeral bier.

2SA.3.BSB: When they buried Abner in Hebron, the king wept aloud at Abner’s tomb, and all the people wept.
2SA.3.KJV: And they buried Abner in Hebron: and the king lifted up his voice, and wept at the grave of Abner; and all the people wept.
2SA.3.PLAIN: When they buried Abner in Hebron, the king wept aloud at Abner’s tomb, and all the people wept.

2SA.3.BSB: And the king sang this lament for Abner: “Should Abner die the death of a fool?
2SA.3.KJV: And the king lamented over Abner, and said, Died Abner as a fool dies?
2SA.3.PLAIN: And the king sang this lament for Abner: “Should Abner die the death of a fool?

2SA.3.BSB: Your hands were not bound, your feet were not fettered. As a man falls before the wicked, so also you fell.” And all the people wept over him even more.
2SA.3.KJV: Your hands were not bound, nor your feet put into fetters: as a man falls before wicked men, so fell you. And all the people wept again over him.
2SA.3.PLAIN: Your hands were not bound, your feet were not fettered. As a man falls before the wicked, so also you fell.” And all the people wept over him even more.

2SA.3.BSB: Then all the people came and urged David to eat something while it was still day, but David took an oath, saying, “May God punish me, and ever so severely, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun sets!”
2SA.3.KJV: And when all the people came to cause David to eat meat while it was yet day, David swore, saying, So do God to me, and more also, if I taste bread, or anything else, till the sun be down.
2SA.3.PLAIN: Then all the people came and urged David to eat something while it was still day, but David took an oath, saying, “May God punish me, and ever so severely, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun sets!”

2SA.3.BSB: All the people took note and were pleased. In fact, everything the king did pleased them.
2SA.3.KJV: And all the people took notice of it, and it pleased them: as whatever the king did pleased all the people.
2SA.3.PLAIN: All the people took note and were pleased. In fact, everything the king did pleased them.

2SA.3.BSB: So on that day all the troops and all Israel were convinced that the king had no part in the murder of Abner son of Ner.
2SA.3.KJV: For all the people and all Israel understood that day that it was not of the king to slay Abner the son of Ner.
2SA.3.PLAIN: So on that day all the troops and all Israel were convinced that the king had no part in the murder of Abner son of Ner.

2SA.3.BSB: Then the king said to his servants, “Do you not realize that a great prince has fallen today in Israel?
2SA.3.KJV: And the king said to his servants, Know you not that there is a prince and a great man fallen this day in Israel?
2SA.3.PLAIN: Then the king said to his servants, “Do you not realize that a great prince has fallen today in Israel?

2SA.3.BSB: And I am weak this day, though anointed as king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too fierce for me. May the LORD repay the evildoer according to his evil!”
2SA.3.KJV: And I am this day weak, though anointed king; and these men the sons of Zeruiah be too hard for me: the LORD shall reward the doer of evil according to his wickedness.
2SA.3.PLAIN: And I am weak this day, though anointed as king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too fierce for me. May the Lord repay the evildoer according to his evil!”

2SA.4.BSB: Now when Ish-bosheth son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, he lost courage, and all Israel was dismayed.
2SA.4.KJV: And when Saul’s son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.
2SA.4.PLAIN: Now when Ish-bosheth son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, he lost courage, and all Israel was dismayed.

2SA.4.BSB: Saul’s son had two men who were leaders of raiding parties. One was named Baanah and the other Rechab; they were sons of Rimmon the Beerothite of the tribe of Benjamin—Beeroth is considered part of Benjamin,
2SA.4.KJV: And Saul’s son had two men that were captains of bands: the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin: (for Beeroth also was reckoned to Benjamin.
2SA.4.PLAIN: Saul’s son had two men who were leaders of raiding parties. One was named Baanah and the other Rechab; they were sons of Rimmon the Beerothite of the tribe of Benjamin—Beeroth is considered part of Benjamin,

2SA.4.BSB: because the Beerothites fled to Gittaim and have lived there as foreigners to this day.
2SA.4.KJV: And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and were sojourners there until this day.)
2SA.4.PLAIN: because the Beerothites fled to Gittaim and have lived there as foreigners to this day.

2SA.4.BSB: And Jonathan son of Saul had a son who was lame in his feet. He was five years old when the report about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and fled, but as she was hurrying to escape, he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.
2SA.4.KJV: And Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son that was lame of his feet. He was five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel, and his nurse took him up, and fled: and it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell, and became lame. And his name was Mephibosheth.
2SA.4.PLAIN: And Jonathan son of Saul had a son who was lame in his feet. He was five years old when the report about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and fled, but as she was hurrying to escape, he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.

2SA.4.BSB: Now Rechab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, set out and arrived at the house of Ish-bosheth in the heat of the day, while the king was taking his midday nap.
2SA.4.KJV: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ishbosheth, who lay on a bed at noon.
2SA.4.PLAIN: Now Rechab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, set out and arrived at the house of Ish-bosheth in the heat of the day, while the king was taking his midday nap.
