2SA.7.BSB: For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought the Israelites up out of Egypt until this day, but I have moved about with a tent as My dwelling.
2SA.7.KJV: Whereas I have not dwelled in any house since the time that I brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt, even to this day, but have walked in a tent and in a tabernacle.
2SA.7.PLAIN: For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought the Israelites up out of Egypt until this day, but I have moved about with a tent as My dwelling.

2SA.7.BSB: In all My journeys with all the Israelites, have I ever asked any of the leaders I appointed to shepherd My people Israel, ‘Why haven’t you built Me a house of cedar?’
2SA.7.KJV: In all the places wherein I have walked with all the children of Israel spoke I a word with any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to feed my people Israel, saying, Why build you not me an house of cedar?
2SA.7.PLAIN: In all My journeys with all the Israelites, have I ever asked any of the leaders I appointed to shepherd My people Israel, ‘Why haven’t you built Me a house of cedar?’

2SA.7.BSB: Now then, you are to tell My servant David that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be the ruler over My people Israel.
2SA.7.KJV: Now therefore so shall you say to my servant David, Thus says the LORD of hosts, I took you from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people, over Israel:
2SA.7.PLAIN: Now then, you are to tell My servant David that this is what the Lord of Hosts says: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be the ruler over My people Israel.

2SA.7.BSB: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you. Now I will make for you a name like the greatest in the land.
2SA.7.KJV: And I was with you wherever you went, and have cut off all your enemies out of your sight, and have made you a great name, like to the name of the great men that are in the earth.
2SA.7.PLAIN: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you. Now I will make for you a name like the greatest in the land.

2SA.7.BSB: And I will provide a place for My people Israel and will plant them so that they may dwell in a place of their own and be disturbed no more. No longer will the sons of wickedness oppress them as they did at the beginning
2SA.7.KJV: Moreover I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in a place of their own, and move no more; neither shall the children of wickedness afflict them any more, as beforetime,
2SA.7.PLAIN: And I will provide a place for My people Israel and will plant them so that they may dwell in a place of their own and be disturbed no more. No longer will the sons of wickedness oppress them as they did at the beginning

2SA.7.BSB: and have done since the day I appointed judges over My people Israel. I will give you rest from all your enemies. The LORD declares to you that He Himself will establish a house for you.
2SA.7.KJV: And as since the time that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel, and have caused you to rest from all your enemies. Also the LORD tells you that he will make you an house. ¶
2SA.7.PLAIN: and have done since the day I appointed judges over My people Israel. I will give you rest from all your enemies. The Lord declares to you that He Himself will establish a house for you.

2SA.7.BSB: And when your days are fulfilled and you rest with your fathers, I will raise up your descendant after you, who will come from your own body, and I will establish his kingdom.
2SA.7.KJV: And when your days be fulfilled, and you shall sleep with your fathers, I will set up your seed after you, which shall proceed out of your bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.
2SA.7.PLAIN: And when your days are fulfilled and you rest with your fathers, I will raise up your descendant after you, who will come from your own body, and I will establish his kingdom.

2SA.7.BSB: He will build a house for My Name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
2SA.7.KJV: He shall build an house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever.
2SA.7.PLAIN: He will build a house for My Name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.

2SA.7.BSB: I will be his Father, and he will be My son. When he does wrong, I will discipline him with the rod of men and with the blows of the sons of men.
2SA.7.KJV: I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men:
2SA.7.PLAIN: I will be his Father, and he will be My son. When he does wrong, I will discipline him with the rod of men and with the blows of the sons of men.

2SA.7.BSB: But My loving devotion will never be removed from him as I removed it from Saul, whom I moved out of your way.
2SA.7.KJV: But my mercy shall not depart away from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away before you.
2SA.7.PLAIN: But My loving devotion will never be removed from him as I removed it from Saul, whom I moved out of your way.

2SA.7.BSB: Your house and kingdom will endure forever before Me, and your throne will be established forever.”
2SA.7.KJV: And your house and your kingdom shall be established for ever before you: your throne shall be established for ever.
2SA.7.PLAIN: Your house and kingdom will endure forever before Me, and your throne will be established forever.”

2SA.7.BSB: So Nathan relayed to David all the words of this entire vision.
2SA.7.KJV: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak to David. ¶
2SA.7.PLAIN: So Nathan relayed to David all the words of this entire vision.

2SA.7.BSB: Then King David went in, sat before the LORD, and said, “Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house, that You have brought me this far?
2SA.7.KJV: Then went king David in, and sat before the LORD, and he said, Who am I, O Lord GOD? and what is my house, that you have brought me till now?
2SA.7.PLAIN: Then King David went in, sat before the Lord, and said, “Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house, that You have brought me this far?

2SA.7.BSB: And as if this was a small thing in Your eyes, O Lord GOD, You have also spoken about the future of the house of Your servant. Is this Your custom with man, O Lord GOD?
2SA.7.KJV: And this was yet a small thing in your sight, O Lord GOD; but you have spoken also of your servant’s house for a great while to come. And is this the manner of man, O Lord GOD?
2SA.7.PLAIN: And as if this was a small thing in Your eyes, O Lord GOD, You have also spoken about the future of the house of Your servant. Is this Your custom with man, O Lord GOD?

2SA.7.BSB: What more can David say to You? For You know Your servant, O Lord GOD.
2SA.7.KJV: And what can David say more to you? for you, Lord GOD, know your servant.
2SA.7.PLAIN: What more can David say to You? For You know Your servant, O Lord GOD.

2SA.7.BSB: For the sake of Your word and according to Your own heart, You have accomplished this great thing and revealed it to Your servant.
2SA.7.KJV: For your word’s sake, and according to your own heart, have you done all these great things, to make your servant know them.
2SA.7.PLAIN: For the sake of Your word and according to Your own heart, You have accomplished this great thing and revealed it to Your servant.

2SA.7.BSB: How great You are, O Lord GOD! For there is none like You, and there is no God but You, according to everything we have heard with our own ears.
2SA.7.KJV: Why you are great, O LORD God: for there is none like you, neither is there any God beside you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
2SA.7.PLAIN: How great you are, Sovereign Lord! There is no one like you, and there is no God but you, as we have heard with our own ears.

2SA.7.BSB: And who is like Your people Israel—the one nation on earth whom God went out to redeem as a people for Himself and to make a name for Himself? You performed great and awesome wonders by driving out nations and their gods from before Your people, whom You redeemed for Yourself from Egypt.
2SA.7.KJV: And what one nation in the earth is like your people, even like Israel, whom God went to redeem for a people to himself, and to make him a name, and to do for you great things and terrible, for your land, before your people, which you redeemed to you from Egypt, from the nations and their gods?
2SA.7.PLAIN: And who is like Your people Israel—the one nation on earth whom God went out to redeem as a people for Himself and to make a name for Himself? You performed great and awesome wonders by driving out nations and their gods from before Your people, whom You redeemed for Yourself from Egypt.

2SA.7.BSB: For You have established Your people Israel as Your very own forever, and You, O LORD, have become their God.
2SA.7.KJV: For you have confirmed to yourself your people Israel to be a people to you for ever: and you, LORD, are become their God.
2SA.7.PLAIN: For You have established Your people Israel as Your very own forever, and You, O Lord, have become their God.

2SA.7.BSB: And now, O LORD God, confirm forever the word You have spoken concerning Your servant and his house. Do as You have promised,
2SA.7.KJV: And now, O LORD God, the word that you have spoken concerning your servant, and concerning his house, establish it for ever, and do as you have said.
2SA.7.PLAIN: And now, O Lord God, confirm forever the word You have spoken concerning Your servant and his house. Do as You have promised,

2SA.7.BSB: so that Your name will be magnified forever when it is said, ‘The LORD of Hosts is God over Israel.’ And the house of Your servant David will be established before You.
2SA.7.KJV: And let your name be magnified for ever, saying, The LORD of hosts is the God over Israel: and let the house of your servant David be established before you.
2SA.7.PLAIN: so that Your name will be magnified forever when it is said, ‘The Lord of Hosts is God over Israel.’ And the house of Your servant David will be established before You.

2SA.7.BSB: For You, O LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, have revealed this to Your servant when You said, ‘I will build a house for you.’ Therefore Your servant has found the courage to offer this prayer to You.
2SA.7.KJV: For you, O LORD of hosts, God of Israel, have revealed to your servant, saying, I will build you an house: therefore has your servant found in his heart to pray this prayer to you.
2SA.7.PLAIN: For You, O Lord of Hosts, the God of Israel, have revealed this to Your servant when You said, ‘I will build a house for you.’ Therefore Your servant has found the courage to offer this prayer to You.

2SA.7.BSB: And now, O Lord GOD, You are God! Your words are true, and You have promised this goodness to Your servant.
2SA.7.KJV: And now, O Lord GOD, you are that God, and your words be true, and you have promised this goodness to your servant:
2SA.7.PLAIN: And now, O Lord GOD, You are God! Your words are true, and You have promised this goodness to Your servant.

2SA.7.BSB: Now therefore, may it please You to bless the house of Your servant, that it may continue forever before You. For You, O Lord GOD, have spoken, and with Your blessing the house of Your servant will be blessed forever.”
2SA.7.KJV: Therefore now let it please you to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue for ever before you: for you, O Lord GOD, have spoken it: and with your blessing let the house of your servant be blessed for ever.
2SA.7.PLAIN: Now therefore, may it please You to bless the house of Your servant, that it may continue forever before You. For You, O Lord GOD, have spoken, and with Your blessing the house of Your servant will be blessed forever.”

2SA.8.BSB: Some time later, David defeated the Philistines, subdued them, and took Metheg-ammah from the hand of the Philistines.
2SA.8.KJV: And after this it came to pass that David smote the Philistines, and subdued them: and David took Methegammah out of the hand of the Philistines.
2SA.8.PLAIN: Some time later, David defeated the Philistines, subdued them, and took Metheg-ammah from the hand of the Philistines.

2SA.8.BSB: David also defeated the Moabites, made them lie down on the ground, and measured them off with a cord. He measured off with two lengths those to be put to death, and with one length those to be spared. So the Moabites became subject to David and brought him tribute.
2SA.8.KJV: And he smote Moab, and measured them with a line, casting them down to the ground; even with two lines measured he to put to death, and with one full line to keep alive. And so the Moabites became David’s servants, and brought gifts. ¶
2SA.8.PLAIN: David also defeated the Moabites, made them lie down on the ground, and measured them off with a cord. He measured off with two lengths those to be put to death, and with one length those to be spared. So the Moabites became subject to David and brought him tribute.

2SA.8.BSB: David also defeated Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, who had marched out to restore his dominion along the Euphrates River.
2SA.8.KJV: David smote also Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his border at the river Euphrates.
2SA.8.PLAIN: David also defeated Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, who had marched out to restore his dominion along the Euphrates River.

2SA.8.BSB: David captured from him a thousand chariots, seven thousand charioteers, and twenty thousand foot soldiers, and he hamstrung all the horses except a hundred he kept for the chariots.
2SA.8.KJV: And David took from him a thousand chariots, and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen: and David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but reserved of them for an hundred chariots.
2SA.8.PLAIN: David captured from him a thousand chariots, seven thousand charioteers, and twenty thousand foot soldiers, and he hamstrung all the horses except a hundred he kept for the chariots.

2SA.8.BSB: When the Arameans of Damascus came to help King Hadadezer of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand men.
2SA.8.KJV: And when the Syrians of Damascus came to succor Hadadezer king of Zobah, David slew of the Syrians two and twenty thousand men.
2SA.8.PLAIN: When the Arameans of Damascus came to help King Hadadezer of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand men.

2SA.8.BSB: Then he placed garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became subject to David and brought him tribute. So the LORD made David victorious wherever he went.
2SA.8.KJV: Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus: and the Syrians became servants to David, and brought gifts. And the LORD preserved David wherever he went.
2SA.8.PLAIN: Then he placed garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became subject to David and brought him tribute. So the Lord made David victorious wherever he went.

2SA.8.BSB: And David took the gold shields that belonged to the officers of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.
2SA.8.KJV: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.
2SA.8.PLAIN: And David took the gold shields that belonged to the officers of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.

2SA.8.BSB: And from Betah and Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took a large amount of bronze.
2SA.8.KJV: And from Betah, and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, king David took exceeding much brass. ¶
2SA.8.PLAIN: And from Betah and Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took a large amount of bronze.

2SA.8.BSB: When King Toi of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer,
2SA.8.KJV: When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer,
2SA.8.PLAIN: When King Toi of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer,

2SA.8.BSB: he sent his son Joram to greet King David and bless him for fighting and defeating Hadadezer, who had been at war with Toi. Joram brought with him articles of silver and gold and bronze,
2SA.8.KJV: Then Toi sent Joram his son to king David, to salute him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer, and smitten him: for Hadadezer had wars with Toi. And Joram brought with him vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass:
2SA.8.PLAIN: he sent his son Joram to greet King David and bless him for fighting and defeating Hadadezer, who had been at war with Toi. Joram brought with him articles of silver and gold and bronze,

2SA.8.BSB: and King David dedicated these to the LORD, along with the silver and gold he had dedicated from all the nations he had subdued—
2SA.8.KJV: Which also king David did dedicate to the LORD, with the silver and gold that he had dedicated of all nations which he subdued;
2SA.8.PLAIN: and King David dedicated these to the Lord, along with the silver and gold he had dedicated from all the nations he had subdued—

2SA.8.BSB: from Edom and Moab, from the Ammonites and Philistines and Amalekites, and from the spoil of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
2SA.8.KJV: Of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
2SA.8.PLAIN: from Edom and Moab, from the Ammonites and Philistines and Amalekites, and from the spoil of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

2SA.8.BSB: And David made a name for himself when he returned from striking down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
2SA.8.KJV: And David got him a name when he returned from smiting of the Syrians in the valley of salt, being eighteen thousand men. ¶
2SA.8.PLAIN: And David made a name for himself when he returned from striking down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

2SA.8.BSB: He placed garrisons throughout Edom, and all the Edomites were subject to David. So the LORD made David victorious wherever he went.
2SA.8.KJV: And he put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom put he garrisons, and all they of Edom became David’s servants. And the LORD preserved David wherever he went.
2SA.8.PLAIN: He placed garrisons throughout Edom, and all the Edomites were subject to David. So the Lord made David victorious wherever he went.

2SA.8.BSB: Thus David reigned over all Israel and administered justice and righteousness for all his people:
2SA.8.KJV: And David reigned over all Israel; and David executed judgment and justice to all his people.
2SA.8.PLAIN: Thus David reigned over all Israel and administered justice and righteousness for all his people:

2SA.8.BSB: Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;
2SA.8.KJV: And Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the host; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;
2SA.8.PLAIN: Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;

2SA.8.BSB: Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Seraiah was the scribe;
2SA.8.KJV: And Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, were the priests; and Seraiah was the scribe;
2SA.8.PLAIN: Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Seraiah was the scribe;

2SA.8.BSB: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites; and David’s sons were priestly leaders.
2SA.8.KJV: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over both the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David’s sons were chief rulers.
2SA.8.PLAIN: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites; and David’s sons were priestly leaders.

2SA.9.BSB: Then David asked, “Is there anyone left from the house of Saul to whom I can show kindness for the sake of Jonathan?”
2SA.9.KJV: And David said, Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?
2SA.9.PLAIN: Then David asked, “Is there anyone left from the house of Saul to whom I can show kindness for the sake of Jonathan?”

2SA.9.BSB: And there was a servant of Saul’s family named Ziba. They summoned him to David, and the king inquired, “Are you Ziba?” “I am your servant,” he replied.
2SA.9.KJV: And there was of the house of Saul a servant whose name was Ziba. And when they had called him to David, the king said to him, Are you Ziba? And he said, Your servant is he.
2SA.9.PLAIN: And there was a servant of Saul’s family named Ziba. They summoned him to David, and the king inquired, “Are you Ziba?” “I am your servant,” he replied.

2SA.9.BSB: So the king asked, “Is there anyone left of Saul’s family to whom I can show the kindness of God?” Ziba answered, “There is still Jonathan’s son, who is lame in both feet.”
2SA.9.KJV: And the king said, Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may show the kindness of God to him? And Ziba said to the king, Jonathan has yet a son, which is lame on his feet.
2SA.9.PLAIN: So the king asked, “Is there anyone left of Saul’s family to whom I can show the kindness of God?” Ziba answered, “There is still Jonathan’s son, who is lame in both feet.”

2SA.9.BSB: “Where is he?” replied the king. And Ziba said, “Indeed, he is in Lo-debar at the house of Machir son of Ammiel.”
2SA.9.KJV: And the king said to him, Where is he? And Ziba said to the king, Behold, he is in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, in Lodebar. ¶
2SA.9.PLAIN: “Where is he?” replied the king. And Ziba said, “Indeed, he is in Lo-debar at the house of Machir son of Ammiel.”

2SA.9.BSB: So King David had him brought from the house of Machir son of Ammiel in Lo-debar.
2SA.9.KJV: Then king David sent, and fetched him out of the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, from Lodebar.
2SA.9.PLAIN: So King David had him brought from the house of Machir son of Ammiel in Lo-debar.

2SA.9.BSB: And when Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he fell facedown in reverence. Then David said, “Mephibosheth!” “I am your servant,” he replied.
2SA.9.KJV: Now when Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, was come to David, he fell on his face, and did reverence. And David said, Mephibosheth. And he answered, Behold your servant! ¶
2SA.9.PLAIN: And when Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he fell facedown in reverence. Then David said, “Mephibosheth!” “I am your servant,” he replied.

2SA.9.BSB: “Do not be afraid,” said David, “for surely I will show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will restore to you all the land of your grandfather Saul, and you will always eat at my table.”
2SA.9.KJV: And David said to him, Fear not: for I will surely show you kindness for Jonathan your father’s sake, and will restore you all the land of Saul your father; and you shall eat bread at my table continually.
2SA.9.PLAIN: “Do not be afraid,” said David, “for surely I will show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will restore to you all the land of your grandfather Saul, and you will always eat at my table.”

2SA.9.BSB: Mephibosheth bowed down and said, “What is your servant, that you should show regard for a dead dog like me?”
2SA.9.KJV: And he bowed himself, and said, What is your servant, that you should look on such a dead dog as I am? ¶
2SA.9.PLAIN: Mephibosheth bowed down and said, “What is your servant, that you should show regard for a dead dog like me?”

2SA.9.BSB: Then the king summoned Saul’s servant Ziba and said to him, “I have given to your master’s grandson all that belonged to Saul and to all his house.
2SA.9.KJV: Then the king called to Ziba, Saul’s servant, and said to him, I have given to your master’s son all that pertained to Saul and to all his house.
2SA.9.PLAIN: Then the king summoned Saul’s servant Ziba and said to him, “I have given to your master’s grandson all that belonged to Saul and to all his house.

2SA.9.BSB: You and your sons and servants are to work the ground for him and bring in the harvest, so that your master’s grandson may have food to eat. But Mephibosheth, your master’s grandson, is always to eat at my table.” Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
2SA.9.KJV: You therefore, and your sons, and your servants, shall till the land for him, and you shall bring in the fruits, that your master’s son may have food to eat: but Mephibosheth your master’s son shall eat bread always at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
2SA.9.PLAIN: You and your sons and servants are to work the ground for him and bring in the harvest, so that your master’s grandson may have food to eat. But Mephibosheth, your master’s grandson, is always to eat at my table.” Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

2SA.9.BSB: And Ziba said to the king, “Your servant will do all that my lord the king has commanded.” So Mephibosheth ate at David’s table like one of the king’s own sons.
2SA.9.KJV: Then said Ziba to the king, According to all that my lord the king has commanded his servant, so shall your servant do. As for Mephibosheth, said the king, he shall eat at my table, as one of the king’s sons.
2SA.9.PLAIN: And Ziba said to the king, “Your servant will do all that my lord the king has commanded.” So Mephibosheth ate at David’s table like one of the king’s own sons.

2SA.9.BSB: And Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica, and all who dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants of Mephibosheth.
2SA.9.KJV: And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Micha. And all that dwelled in the house of Ziba were servants to Mephibosheth.
2SA.9.PLAIN: And Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica, and all who dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants of Mephibosheth.

2SA.9.BSB: So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he always ate at the king’s table, and he was lame in both feet.
2SA.9.KJV: So Mephibosheth dwelled in Jerusalem: for he did eat continually at the king’s table; and was lame on both his feet.
2SA.9.PLAIN: So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he always ate at the king’s table, and he was lame in both feet.

2SA.10.BSB: Some time later, the king of the Ammonites died and was succeeded by his son Hanun.
2SA.10.KJV: And it came to pass after this, that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his stead.
2SA.10.PLAIN: Some time later, the king of the Ammonites died and was succeeded by his son Hanun.

2SA.10.KJV: Then said David, I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father showed kindness to me. And David sent to comfort him by the hand of his servants for his father. And David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.
2SA.10.PLAIN: And David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent some of his servants to console Hanun concerning his father. But when they arrived in the land of the Ammonites,

2SA.10.BSB: the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun their lord, “Just because David has sent you comforters, do you really believe he is showing respect for your father? Has not David instead sent his servants to explore the city, spy it out, and overthrow it?”

2SA.15.BSB: Everyone in the countryside was weeping loudly as all the people passed by. And as the king crossed the Kidron Valley, all the people also passed toward the way of the wilderness.
2SA.15.KJV: And all the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over: the king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over, toward the way of the wilderness. ¶
2SA.15.PLAIN: Everyone in the countryside was weeping loudly as all the people passed by. And as the king crossed the Kidron Valley, all the people also passed toward the way of the wilderness.

2SA.15.BSB: Zadok was also there, and all the Levites with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until the people had passed out of the city.
2SA.15.KJV: And see Zadok also, and all the Levites were with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God: and they set down the ark of God; and Abiathar went up, until all the people had done passing out of the city.
2SA.15.PLAIN: Zadok was also there, and all the Levites with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until the people had passed out of the city.

2SA.15.BSB: Then the king said to Zadok, “Return the ark of God to the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me back and let me see both it and His dwelling place again.
2SA.15.KJV: And the king said to Zadok, Carry back the ark of God into the city: if I shall find favor in the eyes of the LORD, he will bring me again, and show me both it, and his habitation:
2SA.15.PLAIN: Then the king said to Zadok, “Return the ark of God to the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the Lord, He will bring me back and let me see both it and His dwelling place again.

2SA.15.BSB: But if He should say, ‘I do not delight in you,’ then here I am; let Him do to me whatever seems good to Him.”
2SA.15.KJV: But if he thus say, I have no delight in you; behold, here am I, let him do to me as seems good to him.
2SA.15.PLAIN: But if He should say, ‘I do not delight in you,’ then here I am; let Him do to me whatever seems good to Him.”

2SA.15.BSB: The king also said to Zadok the priest, “Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace—you with your son Ahimaaz, and Abiathar with his son Jonathan.
2SA.15.KJV: The king said also to Zadok the priest, Are not you a seer? return into the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz your son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.
2SA.15.PLAIN: The king also said to Zadok the priest, “Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace—you with your son Ahimaaz, and Abiathar with his son Jonathan.

2SA.15.BSB: See, I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”
2SA.15.KJV: See, I will tarry in the plain of the wilderness, until there come word from you to certify me.
2SA.15.PLAIN: See, I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”

2SA.15.BSB: So Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark of God to Jerusalem and stayed there.
2SA.15.KJV: Zadok therefore and Abiathar carried the ark of God again to Jerusalem: and they tarried there. ¶
2SA.15.PLAIN: So Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark of God to Jerusalem and stayed there.

2SA.15.BSB: But David continued up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went up. His head was covered, and he was walking barefoot. And all the people with him covered their heads and went up, weeping as they went.
2SA.15.KJV: And David went up by the ascent of mount Olivet, and wept as he went up, and had his head covered, and he went barefoot: and all the people that was with him covered every man his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up. ¶
2SA.15.PLAIN: But David continued up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went up. His head was covered, and he was walking barefoot. And all the people with him covered their heads and went up, weeping as they went.

2SA.15.BSB: Now someone told David: “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.” So David pleaded, “O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness!”
2SA.15.KJV: And one told David, saying, Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom. And David said, O LORD, I pray you, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness. ¶
2SA.15.PLAIN: Now someone told David: “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.” So David pleaded, “O Lord, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness!”

2SA.15.BSB: When David came to the summit, where he used to worship God, Hushai the Archite was there to meet him with his robe torn and dust on his head.
2SA.15.KJV: And it came to pass, that when David was come to the top of the mount, where he worshipped God, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat rent, and earth on his head:
2SA.15.PLAIN: When David came to the summit, where he used to worship God, Hushai the Archite was there to meet him with his robe torn and dust on his head.

2SA.15.BSB: David said to him, “If you go on with me, you will be a burden to me.
2SA.15.KJV: To whom David said, If you pass on with me, then you shall be a burden to me:
2SA.15.PLAIN: David said to him, “If you go on with me, you will be a burden to me.

2SA.15.BSB: But you can thwart the counsel of Ahithophel for me if you return to the city and say to Absalom: ‘I will be your servant, my king; in the past I was your father’s servant, but now I will be your servant.’
2SA.15.KJV: But if you return to the city, and say to Absalom, I will be your servant, O king; as I have been your father’s servant till now, so will I now also be your servant: then may you for me defeat the counsel of Ahithophel.
2SA.15.PLAIN: But you can thwart the counsel of Ahithophel for me if you return to the city and say to Absalom: ‘I will be your servant, my king; in the past I was your father’s servant, but now I will be your servant.’

2SA.15.BSB: Will not Zadok and Abiathar the priests be there with you? Report to them everything you hear from the king’s palace.
2SA.15.KJV: And have you not there with you Zadok and Abiathar the priests? therefore it shall be, that what thing soever you shall hear out of the king’s house, you shall tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
2SA.15.PLAIN: Will not Zadok and Abiathar the priests be there with you? Report to them everything you hear from the king’s palace.

2SA.15.BSB: Indeed, their two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, are there with them. Send them to me with everything you hear.”
2SA.15.KJV: Behold, they have there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz Zadok’s son, and Jonathan Abiathar’s son; and by them you shall send to me every thing that you can hear.
2SA.15.PLAIN: Indeed, their two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, are there with them. Send them to me with everything you hear.”

2SA.15.BSB: So David’s friend Hushai arrived in Jerusalem just as Absalom was entering the city.
2SA.15.KJV: So Hushai David’s friend came into the city, and Absalom came into Jerusalem.
2SA.15.PLAIN: So David’s friend Hushai arrived in Jerusalem just as Absalom was entering the city.

2SA.16.BSB: When David had gone a little beyond the summit, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth was there to meet him. He had a pair of saddled donkeys loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred clusters of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine.
2SA.16.KJV: And when David was a little past the top of the hill, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, with a couple of asses saddled, and on them two hundred loaves of bread, and an hundred bunches of raisins, and an hundred of summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.
2SA.16.PLAIN: When David had gone a little beyond the summit, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth was there to meet him. He had a pair of saddled donkeys loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred clusters of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine.

2SA.16.BSB: “Why do you have these?” asked the king. Ziba replied, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride, the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness.”
2SA.16.KJV: And the king said to Ziba, What mean you by these? And Ziba said, The asses be for the king’s household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine, that such as be faint in the wilderness may drink.
2SA.16.PLAIN: “Why do you have these?” asked the king. Ziba replied, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride, the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness.”

2SA.16.BSB: “Where is your master’s grandson?” asked the king. And Ziba answered, “Indeed, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he has said, ‘Today, the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my grandfather.’”
2SA.16.KJV: And the king said, And where is your master’s son? And Ziba said to the king, Behold, he stays at Jerusalem: for he said, To day shall the house of Israel restore me the kingdom of my father.
2SA.16.PLAIN: “Where is your master’s grandson?” asked the king. And Ziba answered, “Indeed, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he has said, ‘Today, the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my grandfather.’”

2SA.16.BSB: So the king said to Ziba, “All that belongs to Mephibosheth is now yours!” “I humbly bow before you,” said Ziba. “May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king!”
2SA.16.KJV: Then said the king to Ziba, Behold, your are all that pertained to Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, I humbly beseech you that I may find grace in your sight, my lord, O king. ¶
2SA.16.PLAIN: So the king said to Ziba, “All that belongs to Mephibosheth is now yours!” “I humbly bow before you,” said Ziba. “May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king!”

2SA.16.BSB: As King David approached Bahurim, a man from the family of the house of Saul was just coming out. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and as he approached, he kept yelling out curses.
2SA.16.KJV: And when king David came to Bahurim, behold, there came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed still as he came.
2SA.16.PLAIN: As King David approached Bahurim, a man from the family of the house of Saul was just coming out. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and as he approached, he kept yelling out curses.

2SA.16.BSB: He threw stones at David and at all the servants of the king, though the troops and all the mighty men were on David’s right and left.
2SA.16.KJV: And he cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David: and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.
2SA.16.PLAIN: He threw stones at David and at all the servants of the king, though the troops and all the mighty men were on David’s right and left.

2SA.16.BSB: And as he yelled curses, Shimei said, “Get out, get out, you worthless man of bloodshed!
2SA.16.KJV: And thus said Shimei when he cursed, Come out, come out, you bloody man, and you man of Belial:
2SA.16.PLAIN: And as he yelled curses, Shimei said, “Get out, get out, you worthless man of bloodshed!

2SA.16.BSB: The LORD has paid you back for all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and the LORD has delivered the kingdom into the hand of your son Absalom. See, you have come to ruin because you are a man of bloodshed!”
2SA.16.KJV: The LORD has returned on you all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead you have reigned; and the LORD has delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son: and, behold, you are taken in your mischief, because you are a bloody man. ¶
2SA.16.PLAIN: The Lord has paid you back for all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and the Lord has delivered the kingdom into the hand of your son Absalom. See, you have come to ruin because you are a man of bloodshed!”

2SA.16.BSB: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and cut off his head!”
2SA.16.KJV: Then said Abishai the son of Zeruiah to the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray you, and take off his head.
2SA.16.PLAIN: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and cut off his head!”

2SA.16.BSB: But the king replied, “What have I to do with you, O sons of Zeruiah? If he curses me because the LORD told him, ‘Curse David,’ who can ask, ‘Why did you do this?’”
2SA.16.KJV: And the king said, What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, because the LORD has said to him, Curse David. Who shall then say, Why have you done so?
2SA.16.PLAIN: But the king replied, “What have I to do with you, O sons of Zeruiah? If he curses me because the Lord told him, ‘Curse David,’ who can ask, ‘Why did you do this?’”

2SA.16.BSB: Then David said to Abishai and to all his servants, “Behold, my own son, my own flesh and blood, seeks my life. How much more, then, this Benjamite! Leave him alone and let him curse me, for the LORD has told him so.
2SA.16.KJV: And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, which came forth of my bowels, seeks my life: how much more now may this Benjamite do it? let him alone, and let him curse; for the LORD has bidden him.
2SA.16.PLAIN: Then David said to Abishai and to all his servants, “Look closely — my own son, my own flesh and blood, seeks my life. How much more, then, this Benjamite! Leave him alone and let him curse me, for the Lord has told him so.

2SA.16.BSB: Perhaps the LORD will see my affliction and repay me with good for the cursing I receive today.”
2SA.16.KJV: It may be that the LORD will look on my affliction, and that the LORD will requite me good for his cursing this day.
2SA.16.PLAIN: Perhaps the Lord will see my affliction and repay me with good for the cursing I receive today.”

2SA.16.BSB: So David and his men proceeded along the road as Shimei went along the ridge of the hill opposite him. As Shimei went, he yelled curses, threw stones, and flung dust at David.
2SA.16.KJV: And as David and his men went by the way, Shimei went along on the hill’s side over against him, and cursed as he went, and threw stones at him, and cast dust.
2SA.16.PLAIN: So David and his men proceeded along the road as Shimei went along the ridge of the hill opposite him. As Shimei went, he yelled curses, threw stones, and flung dust at David.

2SA.16.BSB: Finally, the king and all the people with him arrived, exhausted. And there he refreshed himself.
2SA.16.KJV: And the king, and all the people that were with him, came weary, and refreshed themselves there. ¶
2SA.16.PLAIN: Finally, the king and all the people with him arrived, exhausted. And there he refreshed himself.

2SA.16.BSB: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.
2SA.16.KJV: And Absalom, and all the people the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.
2SA.16.PLAIN: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.

2SA.16.BSB: And David’s friend Hushai the Archite went to Absalom and said to him, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
2SA.16.KJV: And it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David’s friend, was come to Absalom, that Hushai said to Absalom, God save the king, God save the king.
2SA.16.PLAIN: And David’s friend Hushai the Archite went to Absalom and said to him, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”

2SA.16.BSB: “Is this the loyalty you show your friend?” Absalom replied. “Why did you not go with your friend?”
2SA.16.KJV: And Absalom said to Hushai, Is this your kindness to your friend? why went you not with your friend?
2SA.16.PLAIN: “Is this the loyalty you show your friend?” Absalom replied. “Why did you not go with your friend?”

2SA.16.BSB: “Not at all,” Hushai answered. “For the one chosen by the LORD, by the people, and by all the men of Israel—his I will be, and with him I will remain.
2SA.16.KJV: And Hushai said to Absalom, No; but whom the LORD, and this people, and all the men of Israel, choose, his will I be, and with him will I abide.
2SA.16.PLAIN: “Not at all,” Hushai answered. “For the one chosen by the Lord, by the people, and by all the men of Israel—his I will be, and with him I will remain.

2SA.16.BSB: Furthermore, whom should I serve if not the son? As I served in your father’s presence, so also I will serve in yours.”
2SA.16.KJV: And again, whom should I serve? should I not serve in the presence of his son? as I have served in your father’s presence, so will I be in your presence. ¶
2SA.16.PLAIN: Furthermore, whom should I serve if not the son? As I served in your father’s presence, so also I will serve in yours.”

2SA.16.BSB: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, “Give me counsel. What should we do?”
2SA.16.KJV: Then said Absalom to Ahithophel, Give counsel among you what we shall do.
2SA.16.PLAIN: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, “Give me counsel. What should we do?”

2SA.16.BSB: Ahithophel replied, “Sleep with your father’s concubines, whom he has left to keep the palace. When all Israel hears that you have become a stench to your father, then the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened.”
2SA.16.KJV: And Ahithophel said to Absalom, Go in to your father’s concubines, which he has left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that you are abhorred of your father: then shall the hands of all that are with you be strong.
2SA.16.PLAIN: Ahithophel replied, “Sleep with your father’s concubines, whom he has left to keep the palace. When all Israel hears that you have become a stench to your father, then the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened.”

2SA.16.BSB: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and he slept with his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
2SA.16.KJV: So they spread Absalom a tent on the top of the house; and Absalom went in to his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
2SA.16.PLAIN: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and he slept with his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.

2SA.16.BSB: Now in those days the advice of Ahithophel was like the consultation of the word of God. Such was the regard that both David and Absalom had for Ahithophel’s advice.
2SA.16.KJV: And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counceled in those days, was as if a man had inquired at the oracle of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.
2SA.16.PLAIN: Now in those days the advice of Ahithophel was like the consultation of the word of God. Such was the regard that both David and Absalom had for Ahithophel’s advice.

2SA.17.BSB: Furthermore, Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Let me choose twelve thousand men and set out tonight in pursuit of David.
2SA.17.KJV: Moreover Ahithophel said to Absalom, Let me now choose out twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David this night:
2SA.17.PLAIN: Furthermore, Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Let me choose twelve thousand men and set out tonight in pursuit of David.

2SA.17.BSB: I will attack him while he is weak and weary; I will throw him into a panic, and all the people with him will flee; I will strike down only the king
2SA.17.KJV: And I will come on him while he is weary and weak handed, and will make him afraid: and all the people that are with him shall flee; and I will smite the king only:
2SA.17.PLAIN: I will attack him while he is weak and weary; I will throw him into a panic, and all the people with him will flee; I will strike down only the king

2SA.17.BSB: and bring all the people back to you as a bride returning to her husband. You seek the life of only one man; then all the people will be at peace.”
2SA.17.KJV: And I will bring back all the people to you: the man whom you seek is as if all returned: so all the people shall be in peace.
2SA.17.PLAIN: and bring all the people back to you as a bride returning to her husband. You seek the life of only one man; then all the people will be at peace.”

2SA.17.BSB: This proposal seemed good to Absalom and all the elders of Israel.
2SA.17.KJV: And the saying pleased Absalom well, and all the elders of Israel.
2SA.17.PLAIN: This proposal seemed good to Absalom and all the elders of Israel.

2SA.17.BSB: Then Absalom said, “Summon Hushai the Archite as well, and let us hear what he too has to say.”
2SA.17.KJV: Then said Absalom, Call now Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likewise what he says.
2SA.17.PLAIN: Then Absalom said, “Summon Hushai the Archite as well, and let us hear what he too has to say.”

2SA.17.BSB: So Hushai came to Absalom, who told him, “Ahithophel has spoken this proposal. Should we carry it out? If not, what do you say?”
2SA.17.KJV: And when Hushai was come to Absalom, Absalom spoke to him, saying, Ahithophel has spoken after this manner: shall we do after his saying? if not; speak you.
2SA.17.PLAIN: So Hushai came to Absalom, who told him, “Ahithophel has spoken this proposal. Should we carry it out? If not, what do you say?”

2SA.17.BSB: Hushai replied, “This time the advice of Ahithophel is not sound.”
2SA.17.KJV: And Hushai said to Absalom, The counsel that Ahithophel has given is not good at this time.
2SA.17.PLAIN: Hushai replied, “This time the advice of Ahithophel is not sound.”

2SA.17.BSB: He continued, “You know your father and his men. They are mighty men, and as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs. Moreover, your father is a man of war who will not spend the night with the troops.
2SA.17.KJV: For, said Hushai, you know your father and his men, that they be mighty men, and they be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field: and your father is a man of war, and will not lodge with the people.
2SA.17.PLAIN: He continued, “You know your father and his men. They are mighty men, and as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs. Moreover, your father is a man of war who will not spend the night with the troops.

2SA.17.BSB: Surely by now he is hiding in a cave or some other location. If some of your troops fall first, whoever hears of it will say, ‘There has been a slaughter among the troops who follow Absalom.’
2SA.17.KJV: Behold, he is hid now in some pit, or in some other place: and it will come to pass, when some of them be overthrown at the first, that whoever hears it will say, There is a slaughter among the people that follow Absalom.
2SA.17.PLAIN: Surely by now he is hiding in a cave or some other location. If some of your troops fall first, whoever hears of it will say, ‘There has been a slaughter among the troops who follow Absalom.’

2SA.17.BSB: Then even the most valiant soldier with the heart of a lion will melt with fear, because all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man who has valiant men with him.
2SA.17.KJV: And he also that is valiant, whose heart is as the heart of a lion, shall utterly melt: for all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man, and they which be with him are valiant men.
2SA.17.PLAIN: Then even the most valiant soldier with the heart of a lion will melt with fear, because all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man who has valiant men with him.

2SA.17.BSB: Instead, I advise that all Israel from Dan to Beersheba—a multitude like the sand on the seashore—be gathered to you, and that you yourself lead them into battle.
2SA.17.KJV: Therefore I counsel that all Israel be generally gathered to you, from Dan even to Beersheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude; and that you go to battle in your own person.
2SA.17.PLAIN: Instead, I advise that all Israel from Dan to Beersheba—a multitude like the sand on the seashore—be gathered to you, and that you yourself lead them into battle.

2SA.17.BSB: Then we will attack David wherever we find him, and we will descend on him like dew on the ground. And of all the men with him, not even one will remain.
2SA.17.KJV: So shall we come on him in some place where he shall be found, and we will light on him as the dew falls on the ground: and of him and of all the men that are with him there shall not be left so much as one.
2SA.17.PLAIN: Then we will attack David wherever we find him, and we will descend on him like dew on the ground. And of all the men with him, not even one will remain.

2SA.17.BSB: If he retreats to a city, all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down to the valley until not even a pebble can be found.”
2SA.17.KJV: Moreover, if he be gotten into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city, and we will draw it into the river, until there be not one small stone found there.
2SA.17.PLAIN: If he retreats to a city, all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down to the valley until not even a pebble can be found.”

2SA.17.BSB: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The advice of Hushai the Archite is better than that of Ahithophel.” For the LORD had purposed to thwart the good counsel of Ahithophel in order to bring disaster on Absalom.
2SA.17.KJV: And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For the LORD had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the LORD might bring evil on Absalom. ¶
2SA.17.PLAIN: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The advice of Hushai the Archite is better than that of Ahithophel.” For the Lord had purposed to thwart the good counsel of Ahithophel in order to bring disaster on Absalom.

2SA.17.BSB: So Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, “This is what Ahithophel has advised Absalom and the elders of Israel, and this is what I have advised.
2SA.17.KJV: Then said Hushai to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus did Ahithophel counsel Absalom and the elders of Israel; and thus and thus have I counceled.
2SA.17.PLAIN: So Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, “This is what Ahithophel has advised Absalom and the elders of Israel, and this is what I have advised.

2SA.17.BSB: Now send quickly and tell David, ‘Do not spend the night at the fords of the wilderness, but be sure to cross over. Otherwise the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up.’”
2SA.17.KJV: Now therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, Lodge not this night in the plains of the wilderness, but speedily pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that are with him.
2SA.17.PLAIN: Now send quickly and tell David, ‘Do not spend the night at the fords of the wilderness, but be sure to cross over. Otherwise the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up.’”

2SA.17.BSB: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel, where a servant girl would come and pass along information to them. They in turn would go and inform King David, for they dared not be seen entering the city.
2SA.17.KJV: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed by Enrogel; for they might not be seen to come into the city: and a wench went and told them; and they went and told king David.
2SA.17.PLAIN: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel, where a servant girl would come and pass along information to them. They in turn would go and inform King David, for they dared not be seen entering the city.

2SA.17.BSB: But a young man did see them and told Absalom. So the two left quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim. He had a well in his courtyard, and they climbed down into it.
2SA.17.KJV: Nevertheless a lad saw them, and told Absalom: but they went both of them away quickly, and came to a man’s house in Bahurim, which had a well in his court; where they went down.
2SA.17.PLAIN: But a young man did see them and told Absalom. So the two left quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim. He had a well in his courtyard, and they climbed down into it.

2SA.17.BSB: Then the man’s wife took a covering and spread it over the mouth of the well, scattering grain over it so nobody would know a thing.
2SA.17.KJV: And the woman took and spread a covering over the well’s mouth, and spread ground corn thereon; and the thing was not known.
2SA.17.PLAIN: Then the man’s wife took a covering and spread it over the mouth of the well, scattering grain over it so nobody would know a thing.

2SA.17.BSB: When Absalom’s servants came to the woman at the house, they asked, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” “They have crossed over the brook,” she replied. The men searched but did not find them, so they returned to Jerusalem.
2SA.17.KJV: And when Absalom’s servants came to the woman to the house, they said, Where is Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said to them, They be gone over the brook of water. And when they had sought and could not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.
2SA.17.PLAIN: When Absalom’s servants came to the woman at the house, they asked, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” “They have crossed over the brook,” she replied. The men searched but did not find them, so they returned to Jerusalem.

2SA.17.BSB: After the men had gone, Ahimaaz and Jonathan climbed up out of the well and went to inform King David, saying, “Get up and cross over the river at once, for Ahithophel has given this advice against you.”
2SA.17.KJV: And it came to pass, after they were departed, that they came up out of the well, and went and told king David, and said to David, Arise, and pass quickly over the water: for thus has Ahithophel counceled against you.
2SA.17.PLAIN: After the men had gone, Ahimaaz and Jonathan climbed up out of the well and went to inform King David, saying, “Get up and cross over the river at once, for Ahithophel has given this advice against you.”

2SA.17.BSB: So David and all the people with him got up and crossed the Jordan. By daybreak, there was no one left who had not crossed the Jordan.
2SA.17.KJV: Then David arose, and all the people that were with him, and they passed over Jordan: by the morning light there lacked not one of them that was not gone over Jordan. ¶
2SA.17.PLAIN: So David and all the people with him got up and crossed the Jordan. By daybreak, there was no one left who had not crossed the Jordan.

2SA.17.BSB: When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and set out for his house in his hometown. He put his affairs in order and hanged himself. So he died and was buried in his father’s tomb.
2SA.17.KJV: And when Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his ass, and arose, and got him home to his house, to his city, and put his household in order, and hanged himself, and died, and was buried in the sepulcher of his father.
2SA.17.PLAIN: When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and set out for his house in his hometown. He put his affairs in order and hanged himself. So he died and was buried in his father’s tomb.

2SA.17.BSB: Then David went to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.
2SA.17.KJV: Then David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom passed over Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him. ¶
2SA.17.PLAIN: Then David went to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.

2SA.17.BSB: Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra, the Ishmaelite who had married Abigail, the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah the mother of Joab.
2SA.17.KJV: And Absalom made Amasa captain of the host instead of Joab: which Amasa was a man’s son, whose name was Ithra an Israelite, that went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah Joab’s mother.
2SA.17.PLAIN: Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra, the Ishmaelite who had married Abigail, the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah the mother of Joab.

2SA.17.BSB: So the Israelites and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.
2SA.17.KJV: So Israel and Absalom pitched in the land of Gilead. ¶
2SA.17.PLAIN: So the Israelites and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.

2SA.17.BSB: When David came to Mahanaim, he was met by Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim.
2SA.17.KJV: And it came to pass, when David was come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lodebar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
2SA.17.PLAIN: When David came to Mahanaim, he was met by Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim.

2SA.17.BSB: They brought beds, basins, and earthen vessels, as well as wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils,
2SA.17.KJV: Brought beds, and basins, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and parched corn, and beans, and lentils, and parched vegetables,
2SA.17.PLAIN: They brought beds, basins, and earthen vessels, as well as wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils,

2SA.17.BSB: honey, curds, sheep, and cheese from the herd for David and his people to eat. For they said, “The people have become hungry, exhausted, and thirsty in the wilderness.”
2SA.17.KJV: And honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of cows, for David, and for the people that were with him, to eat: for they said, The people is hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness.
2SA.17.PLAIN: honey, curds, sheep, and cheese from the herd for David and his people to eat. For they said, “The people have become hungry, exhausted, and thirsty in the wilderness.”

2SA.18.BSB: Then David reviewed his troops and appointed over them commanders of hundreds and of thousands.
2SA.18.KJV: And David numbered the people that were with him, and set captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds over them.
2SA.18.PLAIN: Then David reviewed his troops and appointed over them commanders of hundreds and of thousands.

2SA.18.BSB: He sent out the troops, a third under Joab, a third under Joab’s brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the troops, “I will surely march out with you as well.”
2SA.18.KJV: And David sent forth a third part of the people under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the people, I will surely go forth with you myself also.
2SA.18.PLAIN: He sent out the troops, a third under Joab, a third under Joab’s brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the troops, “I will surely march out with you as well.”

2SA.18.BSB: But the people pleaded, “You must not go out! For if we have to flee, they will pay no attention to us. Even if half of us die, they will not care; but you are worth ten thousand of us. It is better for now if you support us from the city.”
2SA.18.KJV: But the people answered, You shall not go forth: for if we flee away, they will not care for us; neither if half of us die, will they care for us: but now you are worth ten thousand of us: therefore now it is better that you succor us out of the city.
2SA.18.PLAIN: But the people pleaded, “You must not go out! For if we have to flee, they will pay no attention to us. Even if half of us die, they will not care; but you are worth ten thousand of us. It is better for now if you support us from the city.”

2SA.18.BSB: “I will do whatever seems best to you,” the king replied. So he stood beside the gate, while all the troops marched out by hundreds and by thousands.
2SA.18.KJV: And the king said to them, What seems you best I will do. And the king stood by the gate side, and all the people came out by hundreds and by thousands.
2SA.18.PLAIN: “I will do whatever seems best to you,” the king replied. So he stood beside the gate, while all the troops marched out by hundreds and by thousands.

2SA.18.BSB: Now the king had commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, “Treat the young man Absalom gently for my sake.” And all the people heard the king’s orders to each of the commanders regarding Absalom.
2SA.18.KJV: And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Deal gently for my sake with the young man, even with Absalom. And all the people heard when the king gave all the captains charge concerning Absalom. ¶
2SA.18.PLAIN: Now the king had commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, “Treat the young man Absalom gently for my sake.” And all the people heard the king’s orders to each of the commanders regarding Absalom.

2SA.18.BSB: So David’s army marched into the field to engage Israel in the battle, which took place in the forest of Ephraim.
2SA.18.KJV: So the people went out into the field against Israel: and the battle was in the wood of Ephraim;
2SA.18.PLAIN: So David’s army marched into the field to engage Israel in the battle, which took place in the forest of Ephraim.

2SA.18.BSB: There the people of Israel were defeated by David’s servants, and the slaughter was great that day—twenty thousand men.
2SA.18.KJV: Where the people of Israel were slain before the servants of David, and there was there a great slaughter that day of twenty thousand men.
2SA.18.PLAIN: There the people of Israel were defeated by David’s servants, and the slaughter was great that day—twenty thousand men.

2SA.18.BSB: The battle spread over the whole countryside, and that day the forest devoured more people than the sword.
2SA.18.KJV: For the battle was there scattered over the face of all the country: and the wood devoured more people that day than the sword devoured. ¶
2SA.18.PLAIN: The battle spread over the whole countryside, and that day the forest devoured more people than the sword.

2SA.18.BSB: Now Absalom was riding on his mule when he met the servants of David, and as the mule went under the thick branches of a large oak, Absalom’s head was caught fast in the tree. The mule under him kept going, so that he was suspended in midair.
2SA.18.KJV: And Absalom met the servants of David. And Absalom rode on a mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that was under him went away.
2SA.18.PLAIN: Now Absalom was riding on his mule when he met the servants of David, and as the mule went under the thick branches of a large oak, Absalom’s head was caught fast in the tree. The mule under him kept going, so that he was suspended in midair.

2SA.18.BSB: When one of the men saw this, he told Joab, “I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree!”
2SA.18.KJV: And a certain man saw it, and told Joab, and said, Behold, I saw Absalom hanged in an oak.
2SA.18.PLAIN: When one of the men saw this, he told Joab, “I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree!”

2SA.18.BSB: “You just saw him!” Joab exclaimed. “Why did you not strike him to the ground right there? I would have given you ten shekels of silver and a warrior’s belt!”
2SA.18.KJV: And Joab said to the man that told him, And, behold, you saw him, and why did you not smite him there to the ground? and I would have given you ten shekels of silver, and a girdle.
2SA.18.PLAIN: “You just saw him!” Joab exclaimed. “Why did you not strike him to the ground right there? I would have given you ten shekels of silver and a warrior’s belt!”

2SA.18.BSB: The man replied, “Even if a thousand shekels of silver were weighed out into my hands, I would not raise my hand against the son of the king. For we heard the king command you and Abishai and Ittai, ‘Protect the young man Absalom for my sake.’
2SA.18.KJV: And the man said to Joab, Though I should receive a thousand shekels of silver in my hand, yet would I not put forth my hand against the king’s son: for in our hearing the king charged you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Beware that none touch the young man Absalom.
2SA.18.PLAIN: The man replied, “Even if a thousand shekels of silver were weighed out into my hands, I would not raise my hand against the son of the king. For we heard the king command you and Abishai and Ittai, ‘Protect the young man Absalom for my sake.’

2SA.18.BSB: If I had jeopardized my own life—and nothing is hidden from the king—you would have abandoned me.”
2SA.18.KJV: Otherwise I should have worked falsehood against my own life: for there is no matter hid from the king, and you yourself would have set yourself against me.
2SA.18.PLAIN: If I had jeopardized my own life—and nothing is hidden from the king—you would have abandoned me.”

2SA.18.BSB: But Joab declared, “I am not going to wait like this with you!” And he took three spears in his hand and thrust them through the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the oak tree.
2SA.18.KJV: Then said Joab, I may not tarry thus with you. And he took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in the middle of the oak.
2SA.18.PLAIN: But Joab declared, “I am not going to wait like this with you!” And he took three spears in his hand and thrust them through the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the oak tree.

2SA.18.BSB: And ten young men who carried Joab’s armor surrounded Absalom, struck him, and killed him.
2SA.18.KJV: And ten young men that bore Joab’s armor compassed about and smote Absalom, and slew him.
2SA.18.PLAIN: And ten young men who carried Joab’s armor surrounded Absalom, struck him, and killed him.

2SA.18.BSB: Then Joab blew the ram’s horn, and the troops broke off their pursuit of Israel because Joab had restrained them.
2SA.18.KJV: And Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel: for Joab held back the people.
2SA.18.PLAIN: Then Joab blew the ram’s horn, and the troops broke off their pursuit of Israel because Joab had restrained them.

2SA.18.BSB: They took Absalom, cast him into a large pit in the forest, and piled a huge mound of stones over him. Meanwhile, all the Israelites fled, each to his home.
2SA.18.KJV: And they took Absalom, and cast him into a great pit in the wood, and laid a very great heap of stones on him: and all Israel fled every one to his tent. ¶
2SA.18.PLAIN: They took Absalom, cast him into a large pit in the forest, and piled a huge mound of stones over him. Meanwhile, all the Israelites fled, each to his home.

2SA.18.BSB: During his lifetime, Absalom had set up for himself a pillar in the King’s Valley, for he had said, “I have no son to preserve the memory of my name.” So he gave the pillar his name, and to this day it is called Absalom’s Monument.
2SA.18.KJV: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself a pillar, which is in the king’s dale: for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance: and he called the pillar after his own name: and it is called to this day, Absalom’s place. ¶
2SA.18.PLAIN: During his lifetime, Absalom had set up for himself a pillar in the King’s Valley, for he had said, “I have no son to preserve the memory of my name.” So he gave the pillar his name, and to this day it is called Absalom’s Monument.

2SA.18.BSB: Then Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, “Please let me run and tell the king the good news that the LORD has avenged him of his enemies.”
2SA.18.KJV: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, Let me now run, and bear the king tidings, how that the LORD has avenged him of his enemies.
2SA.18.PLAIN: Then Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, “Please let me run and tell the king the good news that the Lord has avenged him of his enemies.”

2SA.18.BSB: But Joab replied, “You are not the man to take good news today. You may do it another day, but you must not do so today, because the king’s son is dead.”
2SA.18.KJV: And Joab said to him, You shall not bear tidings this day, but you shall bear tidings another day: but this day you shall bear no tidings, because the king’s son is dead.
2SA.18.PLAIN: But Joab replied, “You are not the man to take good news today. You may do it another day, but you must not do so today, because the king’s son is dead.”

2SA.18.BSB: So Joab said to a Cushite, “Go, tell the king what you have seen.” The Cushite bowed to Joab and took off running.
2SA.18.KJV: Then said Joab to Cushi, Go tell the king what you have seen. And Cushi bowed himself to Joab, and ran.
2SA.18.PLAIN: So Joab said to a Cushite, “Go, tell the king what you have seen.” The Cushite bowed to Joab and took off running.

2SA.18.BSB: Ahimaaz son of Zadok, however, persisted and said to Joab, “Regardless of whatever may happen, please let me also run behind the Cushite!” “My son,” Joab replied, “why do you want to run, since you will not receive a reward?”
2SA.18.KJV: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok yet again to Joab, But howsoever, let me, I pray you, also run after Cushi. And Joab said, Why will you run, my son, seeing that you have no tidings ready?
2SA.18.PLAIN: Ahimaaz son of Zadok, however, persisted and said to Joab, “Regardless of whatever may happen, please let me also run behind the Cushite!” “My son,” Joab replied, “why do you want to run, since you will not receive a reward?”

2SA.18.BSB: “No matter what, I want to run!” he replied. “Then run!” Joab told him. So Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite.
2SA.18.KJV: But howsoever, said he, let me run. And he said to him, Run. Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain, and overran Cushi.
2SA.18.PLAIN: “No matter what, I want to run!” he replied. “Then run!” Joab told him. So Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite.

2SA.18.BSB: Now David was sitting between the two gates when the watchman went up to the roof of the gateway by the wall, looked out, and saw a man running alone.
2SA.18.KJV: And David sat between the two gates: and the watchman went up to the roof over the gate to the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold a man running alone.
2SA.18.PLAIN: Now David was sitting between the two gates when the watchman went up to the roof of the gateway by the wall, looked out, and saw a man running alone.

2SA.18.BSB: So he called out and told the king. “If he is alone,” the king replied, “he bears good news.” As the first runner drew near,
2SA.18.KJV: And the watchman cried, and told the king. And the king said, If he be alone, there is tidings in his mouth. And he came apace, and drew near.
2SA.18.PLAIN: So he called out and told the king. “If he is alone,” the king replied, “he bears good news.” As the first runner drew near,

2SA.18.BSB: the watchman saw another man running, and he called out to the gatekeeper, “Look! Another man is running alone!” “This one also brings good news,” said the king.
2SA.18.KJV: And the watchman saw another man running: and the watchman called to the porter, and said, Behold another man running alone. And the king said, He also brings tidings.
2SA.18.PLAIN: the watchman saw another man running, and he called out to the gatekeeper, “Look! Another man is running alone!” “This one also brings good news,” said the king.

2SA.18.BSB: The watchman said, “The first man appears to me to be running like Ahimaaz son of Zadok.” “This is a good man,” said the king. “He comes with good news.”
2SA.18.KJV: And the watchman said, Me thinks the running of the foremost is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok. And the king said, He is a good man, and comes with good tidings.
2SA.18.PLAIN: The watchman said, “The first man appears to me to be running like Ahimaaz son of Zadok.” “This is a good man,” said the king. “He comes with good news.”

2SA.18.BSB: Then Ahimaaz called out to the king, “All is well!” And he bowed facedown before the king. He continued, “Blessed be the LORD your God! He has delivered up the men who raised their hands against my lord the king.”
2SA.18.KJV: And Ahimaaz called, and said to the king, All is well. And he fell down to the earth on his face before the king, and said, Blessed be the LORD your God, which has delivered up the men that lifted up their hand against my lord the king.
2SA.18.PLAIN: Then Ahimaaz called out to the king, “All is well!” And he bowed facedown before the king. He continued, “Blessed be the Lord your God! He has delivered up the men who raised their hands against my lord the king.”

2SA.18.BSB: The king asked, “Is the young man Absalom all right?” And Ahimaaz replied, “When Joab sent the king’s servant and your servant, I saw a great tumult, but I do not know what it was.”
2SA.18.KJV: And the king said, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Ahimaaz answered, When Joab sent the king’s servant, and me your servant, I saw a great tumult, but I knew not what it was.
2SA.18.PLAIN: The king asked, “Is the young man Absalom all right?” And Ahimaaz replied, “When Joab sent the king’s servant and your servant, I saw a great tumult, but I do not know what it was.”

2SA.18.BSB: “Move aside,” said the king, “and stand here.” So he stepped aside.
2SA.18.KJV: And the king said to him, Turn aside, and stand here. And he turned aside, and stood still.
2SA.18.PLAIN: “Move aside,” said the king, “and stand here.” So he stepped aside.

2SA.18.BSB: Just then the Cushite came and said, “May my lord the king hear the good news: Today the LORD has avenged you of all who rose up against you!”
2SA.18.KJV: And, behold, Cushi came; and Cushi said, Tidings, my lord the king: for the LORD has avenged you this day of all them that rose up against you.
2SA.18.PLAIN: Just then the Cushite came and said, “May my lord the king hear the good news: Today the Lord has avenged you of all who rose up against you!”

2SA.18.BSB: The king asked the Cushite, “Is the young man Absalom all right?” And the Cushite replied, “May what has become of the young man happen to the enemies of my lord the king and to all who rise up against you to harm you.”
2SA.18.KJV: And the king said to Cushi, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Cushi answered, The enemies of my lord the king, and all that rise against you to do you hurt, be as that young man is. ¶
2SA.18.PLAIN: The king asked the Cushite, “Is the young man Absalom all right?” And the Cushite replied, “May what has become of the young man happen to the enemies of my lord the king and to all who rise up against you to harm you.”

2SA.18.BSB: The king was shaken and went up to the gate chamber and wept. And as he walked, he cried out, “O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you, O Absalom, my son, my son!”
2SA.18.KJV: And the king was much moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept: and as he went, thus he said, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for you, O Absalom, my son, my son!
2SA.18.PLAIN: The king was shaken and went up to the gate chamber and wept. And as he walked, he cried out, “O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you, O Absalom, my son, my son!”

2SA.19.BSB: Then it was reported to Joab, “The king is weeping and mourning over Absalom.”
2SA.19.KJV: And it was told Joab, Behold, the king weeps and mourns for Absalom.
2SA.19.PLAIN: Then it was reported to Joab, “The king is weeping and mourning over Absalom.”

2SA.19.BSB: And that day’s victory was turned into mourning for all the people, because on that day they were told, “The king is grieving over his son.”
2SA.19.KJV: And the victory that day was turned into mourning to all the people: for the people heard say that day how the king was grieved for his son.
2SA.19.PLAIN: And that day’s victory was turned into mourning for all the people, because on that day they were told, “The king is grieving over his son.”

2SA.19.BSB: So they returned to the city quietly that day, as people steal away in humiliation after fleeing a battle.
2SA.19.KJV: And the people got them by stealth that day into the city, as people being ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.
2SA.19.PLAIN: So they returned to the city quietly that day, as people steal away in humiliation after fleeing a battle.

2SA.19.BSB: But the king covered his face and cried out at the top of his voice, “O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!”
2SA.19.KJV: But the king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son!
2SA.19.PLAIN: But the king covered his face and cried out at the top of his voice, “O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!”
