2SA.19.BSB: Then Joab went into the house and said to the king, “Today you have disgraced all your servants who have saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters, of your wives, and of your concubines.
2SA.19.KJV: And Joab came into the house to the king, and said, You have shamed this day the faces of all your servants, which this day have saved your life, and the lives of your sons and of your daughters, and the lives of your wives, and the lives of your concubines;
2SA.19.PLAIN: Then Joab went into the house and said to the king, “Today you have disgraced all your servants who have saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters, of your wives, and of your concubines.

2SA.19.BSB: You love those who hate you and hate those who love you! For you have made it clear today that the commanders and soldiers mean nothing to you. I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead, it would have pleased you!
2SA.19.KJV: In that you love your enemies, and hate your friends. For you have declared this day, that you regard neither princes nor servants: for this day I perceive, that if Absalom had lived, and all we had died this day, then it had pleased you well.
2SA.19.PLAIN: You love those who hate you and hate those who love you! For you have made it clear today that the commanders and soldiers mean nothing to you. I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead, it would have pleased you!

2SA.19.BSB: Now therefore get up! Go out and speak comfort to your servants, for I swear by the LORD that if you do not go out, not a man will remain with you tonight. This will be worse for you than all the adversity that has befallen you from your youth until now!”
2SA.19.KJV: Now therefore arise, go forth, and speak comfortably to your servants: for I swear by the LORD, if you go not forth, there will not tarry one with you this night: and that will be worse to you than all the evil that befell you from your youth until now.
2SA.19.PLAIN: Now therefore get up! Go out and speak comfort to your servants, for I swear by the Lord that if you do not go out, not a man will remain with you tonight. This will be worse for you than all the adversity that has befallen you from your youth until now!”

2SA.19.BSB: So the king got up and sat in the gate, and all the people were told: “Behold, the king is sitting in the gate.” So they all came before the king. Meanwhile, the Israelites had fled, each man to his home.
2SA.19.KJV: Then the king arose, and sat in the gate. And they told to all the people, saying, Behold, the king does sit in the gate. And all the people came before the king: for Israel had fled every man to his tent. ¶
2SA.19.PLAIN: So the king got up and sat in the gate, and all the people were told: “Look closely — the king is sitting in the gate.” So they all came before the king. Meanwhile, the Israelites had fled, each man to his home.

2SA.19.BSB: And all the people throughout the tribes of Israel were arguing, “The king rescued us from the hand of our enemies and delivered us from the hand of the Philistines, but now he has fled the land because of Absalom.
2SA.19.KJV: And all the people were at strife throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, The king saved us out of the hand of our enemies, and he delivered us out of the hand of the Philistines; and now he is fled out of the land for Absalom.
2SA.19.PLAIN: And all the people throughout the tribes of Israel were arguing, “The king rescued us from the hand of our enemies and delivered us from the hand of the Philistines, but now he has fled the land because of Absalom.

2SA.19.BSB: But Absalom, the man we anointed over us, has died in battle. So why do you say nothing about restoring the king?”
2SA.19.KJV: And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now therefore why speak you not a word of bringing the king back? ¶
2SA.19.PLAIN: But Absalom, the man we anointed over us, has died in battle. So why do you say nothing about restoring the king?”

2SA.19.BSB: Then King David sent this message to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests: “Say to the elders of Judah, ‘Why should you be the last to restore the king to his palace, since the talk of all Israel has reached the king at his quarters?
2SA.19.KJV: And king David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, Why are you the last to bring the king back to his house? seeing the speech of all Israel is come to the king, even to his house.
2SA.19.PLAIN: Then King David sent this message to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests: “Say to the elders of Judah, ‘Why should you be the last to restore the king to his palace, since the talk of all Israel has reached the king at his quarters?

2SA.19.BSB: You are my brothers, my own flesh and blood. So why should you be the last to restore the king?’
2SA.19.KJV: You are my brothers, you are my bones and my flesh: why then are you the last to bring back the king?
2SA.19.PLAIN: You are my brothers, my own flesh and blood. So why should you be the last to restore the king?’

2SA.19.BSB: And say to Amasa, ‘Aren’t you my flesh and blood? May God punish me, and ever so severely, if from this time you are not the commander of my army in place of Joab!’”
2SA.19.KJV: And say you to Amasa, Are you not of my bone, and of my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if you be not captain of the host before me continually in the room of Joab.
2SA.19.PLAIN: And say to Amasa, ‘Aren’t you my flesh and blood? May God punish me, and ever so severely, if from this time you are not the commander of my army in place of Joab!’”

2SA.19.BSB: So he swayed the hearts of all the men of Judah as though they were one man, and they sent word to the king: “Return, you and all your servants.”
2SA.19.KJV: And he bowed the heart of all the men of Judah, even as the heart of one man; so that they sent this word to the king, Return you, and all your servants.
2SA.19.PLAIN: So he swayed the hearts of all the men of Judah as though they were one man, and they sent word to the king: “Return, you and all your servants.”

2SA.19.BSB: So the king returned, and when he arrived at the Jordan, the men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet him and escort him across the Jordan.
2SA.19.KJV: So the king returned, and came to Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to conduct the king over Jordan. ¶
2SA.19.PLAIN: So the king returned, and when he arrived at the Jordan, the men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet him and escort him across the Jordan.

2SA.19.BSB: Then Shimei son of Gera, a Benjamite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David,
2SA.19.KJV: And Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite, which was of Bahurim, hurried and came down with the men of Judah to meet king David.
2SA.19.PLAIN: Then Shimei son of Gera, a Benjamite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David,

2SA.19.BSB: along with a thousand men of Benjamin, as well as Ziba the steward of the house of Saul and his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed down to the Jordan before the king
2SA.19.KJV: And there were a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they went over Jordan before the king.
2SA.19.PLAIN: along with a thousand men of Benjamin, as well as Ziba the steward of the house of Saul and his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed down to the Jordan before the king

2SA.19.BSB: and crossed at the ford to carry over the king’s household and to do what was good in his sight. When Shimei son of Gera crossed the Jordan, he fell down before the king
2SA.19.KJV: And there went over a ferry boat to carry over the king’s household, and to do what he thought good. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king, as he was come over Jordan;
2SA.19.PLAIN: and crossed at the ford to carry over the king’s household and to do what was good in his sight. When Shimei son of Gera crossed the Jordan, he fell down before the king

2SA.19.BSB: and said, “My lord, do not hold me guilty, and do not remember your servant’s wrongdoing on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem. May the king not take it to heart.
2SA.19.KJV: And said to the king, Let not my lord impute iniquity to me, neither do you remember that which your servant did perversely the day that my lord the king went out of Jerusalem, that the king should take it to his heart.
2SA.19.PLAIN: and said, “My lord, do not hold me guilty, and do not remember your servant’s wrongdoing on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem. May the king not take it to heart.

2SA.19.BSB: For your servant knows that I have sinned, so here I am today as the first of all the house of Joseph to come down to meet my lord the king.”
2SA.19.KJV: For your servant does know that I have sinned: therefore, behold, I am come the first this day of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.
2SA.19.PLAIN: For your servant knows that I have sinned, so here I am today as the first of all the house of Joseph to come down to meet my lord the king.”

2SA.19.BSB: But Abishai son of Zeruiah said, “Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD’s anointed?”
2SA.19.KJV: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered and said, Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD’s anointed?
2SA.19.PLAIN: But Abishai son of Zeruiah said, “Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the Lord’s anointed?”

2SA.19.BSB: And David replied, “Sons of Zeruiah, what have I to do with you, that you should be my adversaries today? Should any man be put to death in Israel today? Am I not indeed aware that today I am king over Israel?”
2SA.19.KJV: And David said, What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah, that you should this day be adversaries to me? shall there any man be put to death this day in Israel? for do not I know that I am this day king over Israel?
2SA.19.PLAIN: And David replied, “Sons of Zeruiah, what have I to do with you, that you should be my adversaries today? Should any man be put to death in Israel today? Am I not indeed aware that today I am king over Israel?”

2SA.19.BSB: So the king said to Shimei, “You shall not die.” And the king swore an oath to him.
2SA.19.KJV: Therefore the king said to Shimei, You shall not die. And the king swore to him. ¶
2SA.19.PLAIN: So the king said to Shimei, “You shall not die.” And the king swore an oath to him.

2SA.19.BSB: Then Mephibosheth, Saul’s grandson, went down to meet the king. He had not cared for his feet or trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes from the day the king had left until the day he returned safely.
2SA.19.KJV: And Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king, and had neither dressed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came again in peace.
2SA.19.PLAIN: Then Mephibosheth, Saul’s grandson, went down to meet the king. He had not cared for his feet or trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes from the day the king had left until the day he returned safely.

2SA.19.BSB: And he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, who asked him, “Mephibosheth, why did you not go with me?”
2SA.19.KJV: And it came to pass, when he was come to Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said to him, Why went not you with me, Mephibosheth?
2SA.19.PLAIN: And he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, who asked him, “Mephibosheth, why did you not go with me?”

2SA.19.BSB: “My lord the king,” he replied, “because I am lame, I said, ‘I will have my donkey saddled so that I may ride on it and go with the king.’ But my servant Ziba deceived me,
2SA.19.KJV: And he answered, My lord, O king, my servant deceived me: for your servant said, I will saddle me an ass, that I may ride thereon, and go to the king; because your servant is lame.
2SA.19.PLAIN: “My lord the king,” he replied, “because I am lame, I said, ‘I will have my donkey saddled so that I may ride on it and go with the king.’ But my servant Ziba deceived me,

2SA.19.BSB: and he has slandered your servant to my lord the king. Yet my lord the king is like the angel of God, so do what is good in your eyes.
2SA.19.KJV: And he has slandered your servant to my lord the king; but my lord the king is as an angel of God: do therefore what is good in your eyes.
2SA.19.PLAIN: and he has slandered your servant to my lord the king. Yet my lord the king is like the angel of God, so do what is good in your eyes.

2SA.19.BSB: For all the house of my grandfather deserves death from my lord the king, yet you have set your servant among those who eat at your table. What further right, then, do I have to keep appealing to the king?”
2SA.19.KJV: For all of my father’s house were but dead men before my lord the king: yet did you set your servant among them that did eat at your own table. What right therefore have I yet to cry any more to the king?
2SA.19.PLAIN: For all the house of my grandfather deserves death from my lord the king, yet you have set your servant among those who eat at your table. What further right, then, do I have to keep appealing to the king?”

2SA.19.BSB: The king replied, “Why say any more? I hereby declare that you and Ziba are to divide the land.”
2SA.19.KJV: And the king said to him, Why speak you any more of your matters? I have said, You and Ziba divide the land.
2SA.19.PLAIN: The king replied, “Why say any more? I hereby declare that you and Ziba are to divide the land.”

2SA.19.BSB: And Mephibosheth said to the king, “Instead, since my lord the king has safely come to his own house, let Ziba take it all!”
2SA.19.KJV: And Mephibosheth said to the king, Yes, let him take all, for as much as my lord the king is come again in peace to his own house. ¶
2SA.19.PLAIN: And Mephibosheth said to the king, “Instead, since my lord the king has safely come to his own house, let Ziba take it all!”

2SA.19.BSB: Now Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim to cross the Jordan with the king and send him on his way from there.
2SA.19.KJV: And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim, and went over Jordan with the king, to conduct him over Jordan.
2SA.19.PLAIN: Now Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim to cross the Jordan with the king and send him on his way from there.

2SA.19.BSB: Barzillai was quite old, eighty years of age, and since he was a very wealthy man, he had provided for the king while he stayed in Mahanaim.
2SA.19.KJV: Now Barzillai was a very aged man, even fourscore years old: and he had provided the king of sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he was a very great man.
2SA.19.PLAIN: Barzillai was quite old, eighty years of age, and since he was a very wealthy man, he had provided for the king while he stayed in Mahanaim.

2SA.19.BSB: The king said to Barzillai, “Cross over with me, and I will provide for you at my side in Jerusalem.”
2SA.19.KJV: And the king said to Barzillai, Come you over with me, and I will feed you with me in Jerusalem.
2SA.19.PLAIN: The king said to Barzillai, “Cross over with me, and I will provide for you at my side in Jerusalem.”

2SA.19.BSB: But Barzillai replied, “How many years of my life remain, that I should go up to Jerusalem with the king?
2SA.19.KJV: And Barzillai said to the king, How long have I to live, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?
2SA.19.PLAIN: But Barzillai replied, “How many years of my life remain, that I should go up to Jerusalem with the king?

2SA.19.BSB: I am now eighty years old. Can I discern what is good and what is not? Can your servant taste what he eats or drinks? Can I still hear the voice of singing men and women? Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?
2SA.19.KJV: I am this day fourscore years old: and can I discern between good and evil? can your servant taste what I eat or what I drink? can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? why then should your servant be yet a burden to my lord the king?
2SA.19.PLAIN: I am now eighty years old. Can I discern what is good and what is not? Can your servant taste what he eats or drinks? Can I still hear the voice of singing men and women? Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?

2SA.19.BSB: Your servant could go with the king only a short distance past the Jordan; why should the king repay me with such a reward?
2SA.19.KJV: Your servant will go a little way over Jordan with the king: and why should the king recompense it me with such a reward?
2SA.19.PLAIN: Your servant could go with the king only a short distance past the Jordan; why should the king repay me with such a reward?

2SA.19.BSB: Please let your servant return, that I may die in my own city near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Chimham. Let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your sight.”
2SA.19.KJV: Let your servant, I pray you, turn back again, that I may die in my own city, and be buried by the grave of my father and of my mother. But behold your servant Chimham; let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good to you.
2SA.19.PLAIN: Please let your servant return, that I may die in my own city near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Chimham. Let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your sight.”

2SA.19.BSB: The king replied, “Chimham will cross over with me, and I will do for him what seems good in your sight, and I will do for you whatever you desire of me.”
2SA.19.KJV: And the king answered, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good to you: and whatever you shall require of me, that will I do for you.
2SA.19.PLAIN: The king replied, “Chimham will cross over with me, and I will do for him what seems good in your sight, and I will do for you whatever you desire of me.”

2SA.19.BSB: So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and Barzillai returned home.
2SA.19.KJV: And all the people went over Jordan. And when the king was come over, the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned to his own place.
2SA.19.PLAIN: So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and Barzillai returned home.

2SA.19.BSB: Then the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham crossed over with him. All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel escorted the king.
2SA.19.KJV: Then the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him: and all the people of Judah conducted the king, and also half the people of Israel. ¶
2SA.19.PLAIN: Then the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham crossed over with him. All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel escorted the king.

2SA.19.BSB: Soon all the men of Israel came to the king and asked, “Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, take you away secretly and bring the king and his household across the Jordan, together with all of David’s men?”
2SA.19.KJV: And, behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said to the king, Why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen you away, and have brought the king, and his household, and all David’s men with him, over Jordan?
2SA.19.PLAIN: Soon all the men of Israel came to the king and asked, “Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, take you away secretly and bring the king and his household across the Jordan, together with all of David’s men?”

2SA.19.BSB: And all the men of Judah replied to the men of Israel, “We did this because the king is our relative. Why does this anger you? Have we ever eaten at the king’s expense or received anything for ourselves?”
2SA.19.KJV: And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, Because the king is near of kin to us: why then be you angry for this matter? have we eaten at all of the king’s cost? or has he given us any gift?
2SA.19.PLAIN: And all the men of Judah replied to the men of Israel, “We did this because the king is our relative. Why does this anger you? Have we ever eaten at the king’s expense or received anything for ourselves?”

2SA.19.BSB: “We have ten shares in the king,” answered the men of Israel, “so we have more claim to David than you. Why then do you despise us? Were we not the first to speak of restoring our king?” But the men of Judah pressed even harder than the men of Israel.
2SA.19.KJV: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more right in David than you: why then did you despise us, that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king? And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.
2SA.19.PLAIN: “We have ten shares in the king,” answered the men of Israel, “so we have more claim to David than you. Why then do you despise us? Were we not the first to speak of restoring our king?” But the men of Judah pressed even harder than the men of Israel.

2SA.20.BSB: Now a worthless man named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjamite, happened to be there, and he blew the ram’s horn and shouted: “We have no share in David, no inheritance in Jesse’s son. Every man to his tent, O Israel!”
2SA.20.KJV: And there happened to be there a man of Belial, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite: and he blew a trumpet, and said, We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to his tents, O Israel.
2SA.20.PLAIN: Now a worthless man named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjamite, happened to be there, and he blew the ram’s horn and shouted: “We have no share in David, no inheritance in Jesse’s son. Every man to his tent, O Israel!”

2SA.20.BSB: So all the men of Israel deserted David to follow Sheba son of Bichri. But the men of Judah stayed by their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.
2SA.20.KJV: So every man of Israel went up from after David, and followed Sheba the son of Bichri: but the men of Judah joined to their king, from Jordan even to Jerusalem. ¶
2SA.20.PLAIN: So all the men of Israel deserted David to follow Sheba son of Bichri. But the men of Judah stayed by their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

2SA.20.BSB: When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to care for the palace, and he placed them in a house under guard. He provided for them, but he no longer slept with them. They were confined until the day of their death, living as widows.
2SA.20.KJV: And David came to his house at Jerusalem; and the king took the ten women his concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in ward, and fed them, but went not in to them. So they were shut up to the day of their death, living in widowhood. ¶
2SA.20.PLAIN: When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to care for the palace, and he placed them in a house under guard. He provided for them, but he no longer slept with them. They were confined until the day of their death, living as widows.

2SA.20.BSB: Then the king said to Amasa, “Summon the men of Judah to come to me within three days, and be here yourself.”
2SA.20.KJV: Then said the king to Amasa, Assemble me the men of Judah within three days, and be you here present.
2SA.20.PLAIN: Then the king said to Amasa, “Summon the men of Judah to come to me within three days, and be here yourself.”

2SA.20.BSB: So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he took longer than the time allotted him.
2SA.20.KJV: So Amasa went to assemble the men of Judah: but he tarried longer than the set time which he had appointed him.
2SA.20.PLAIN: So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he took longer than the time allotted him.

2SA.20.BSB: And David said to Abishai, “Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. Take your lord’s servants and pursue him, or he will find fortified cities and elude us.”
2SA.20.KJV: And David said to Abishai, Now shall Sheba the son of Bichri do us more harm than did Absalom: take you your lord’s servants, and pursue after him, lest he get him fenced cities, and escape us.
2SA.20.PLAIN: And David said to Abishai, “Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. Take your lord’s servants and pursue him, or he will find fortified cities and elude us.”

2SA.20.BSB: So Joab’s men, along with the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men, marched out of Jerusalem in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.
2SA.20.KJV: And there went out after him Joab’s men, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men: and they went out of Jerusalem, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.
2SA.20.PLAIN: So Joab’s men, along with the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men, marched out of Jerusalem in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.

2SA.20.BSB: And while they were at the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa joined them. Now Joab was dressed in military attire, with a dagger strapped to his belt. And as he stepped forward, he slipped the dagger from its sheath.
2SA.20.KJV: When they were at the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa went before them. And Joab’s garment that he had put on was girded to him, and on it a girdle with a sword fastened on his loins in the sheath thereof; and as he went forth it fell out.
2SA.20.PLAIN: And while they were at the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa joined them. Now Joab was dressed in military attire, with a dagger strapped to his belt. And as he stepped forward, he slipped the dagger from its sheath.

2SA.20.BSB: “Are you well, my brother?” Joab asked Amasa. And with his right hand Joab grabbed Amasa by the beard to kiss him.
2SA.20.KJV: And Joab said to Amasa, Are you in health, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard with the right hand to kiss him.
2SA.20.PLAIN: “Are you well, my brother?” Joab asked Amasa. And with his right hand Joab grabbed Amasa by the beard to kiss him.

2SA.20.BSB: Amasa was not on guard against the dagger in Joab’s hand, and Joab stabbed him in the stomach and spilled out his intestines on the ground. And Joab did not need to strike him again, for Amasa was dead. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bichri.
2SA.20.KJV: But Amasa took no heed to the sword that was in Joab’s hand: so he smote him therewith in the fifth rib, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and struck him not again; and he died. So Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.
2SA.20.PLAIN: Amasa was not on guard against the dagger in Joab’s hand, and Joab stabbed him in the stomach and spilled out his intestines on the ground. And Joab did not need to strike him again, for Amasa was dead. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bichri.

2SA.20.BSB: One of Joab’s young men stood near Amasa and said, “Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David, let him follow Joab!”
2SA.20.KJV: And one of Joab’s men stood by him, and said, He that favors Joab, and he that is for David, let him go after Joab.
2SA.20.PLAIN: One of Joab’s young men stood near Amasa and said, “Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David, let him follow Joab!”

2SA.20.BSB: But Amasa wallowed in his blood in the middle of the road, and when the man saw that all the troops were stopping there, he dragged the body off the road into a field and threw a garment over it.
2SA.20.KJV: And Amasa wallowed in blood in the middle of the highway. And when the man saw that all the people stood still, he removed Amasa out of the highway into the field, and cast a cloth on him, when he saw that every one that came by him stood still.
2SA.20.PLAIN: But Amasa wallowed in his blood in the middle of the road, and when the man saw that all the troops were stopping there, he dragged the body off the road into a field and threw a garment over it.

2SA.20.BSB: As soon as Amasa’s body was removed from the road, all the men went on with Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.
2SA.20.KJV: When he was removed out of the highway, all the people went on after Joab, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri. ¶
2SA.20.PLAIN: As soon as Amasa’s body was removed from the road, all the men went on with Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.

2SA.20.BSB: Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel-beth-maacah and through the entire region of the Berites, who gathered together and followed him.
2SA.20.KJV: And he went through all the tribes of Israel to Abel, and to Bethmaachah, and all the Berites: and they were gathered together, and went also after him.
2SA.20.PLAIN: Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel-beth-maacah and through the entire region of the Berites, who gathered together and followed him.

2SA.20.BSB: And Joab’s troops came and besieged Sheba in Abel-beth-maacah and built a siege ramp against the outer rampart of the city. As all the troops with Joab were battering the wall to topple it,
2SA.20.KJV: And they came and besieged him in Abel of Bethmaachah, and they cast up a bank against the city, and it stood in the trench: and all the people that were with Joab battered the wall, to throw it down. ¶

2SA.22.KJV: For who is God, save the LORD? and who is a rock, save our God?
2SA.22.PLAIN: For who is God besides the Lord? And who is the Rock except our God?

2SA.22.BSB: God is my strong fortress and He makes my way clear.
2SA.22.KJV: God is my strength and power: and he makes my way perfect.
2SA.22.PLAIN: God is my strong fortress and He makes my way clear.

2SA.22.BSB: He makes my feet like those of a deer and stations me upon the heights.
2SA.22.KJV: He makes my feet like hinds’ feet: and sets me on my high places.
2SA.22.PLAIN: He makes my feet like those of a deer and stations me upon the heights.

2SA.22.BSB: He trains my hands for battle; my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
2SA.22.KJV: He teaches my hands to war; so that a bow of steel is broken by my arms.
2SA.22.PLAIN: He trains my hands for battle; my arms can bend a bow of bronze.

2SA.22.BSB: You have given me Your shield of salvation, and Your gentleness exalts me.
2SA.22.KJV: You have also given me the shield of your salvation: and your gentleness has made me great.
2SA.22.PLAIN: You have given me Your shield of salvation, and Your gentleness exalts me.

2SA.22.BSB: You broaden the path beneath me so that my ankles do not give way.
2SA.22.KJV: You have enlarged my steps under me; so that my feet did not slip.
2SA.22.PLAIN: You broaden the path beneath me so that my ankles do not give way.

2SA.22.BSB: I pursued my enemies and destroyed them; I did not turn back until they were consumed.
2SA.22.KJV: I have pursued my enemies, and destroyed them; and turned not again until I had consumed them.
2SA.22.PLAIN: I pursued my enemies and destroyed them; I did not turn back until they were consumed.

2SA.22.BSB: I devoured and crushed them so they could not rise; they have fallen under my feet.
2SA.22.KJV: And I have consumed them, and wounded them, that they could not arise: yes, they are fallen under my feet.
2SA.22.PLAIN: I devoured and crushed them so they could not rise; they have fallen under my feet.

2SA.22.BSB: You have armed me with strength for battle; You have subdued my foes beneath me.
2SA.22.KJV: For you have girded me with strength to battle: them that rose up against me have you subdued under me.
2SA.22.PLAIN: You have armed me with strength for battle; You have subdued my foes beneath me.

2SA.22.BSB: You have made my enemies retreat before me; I put an end to those who hated me.
2SA.22.KJV: You have also given me the necks of my enemies, that I might destroy them that hate me.
2SA.22.PLAIN: You have made my enemies retreat before me; I put an end to those who hated me.

2SA.22.BSB: They looked, but there was no one to save them— to the LORD, but He did not answer.
2SA.22.KJV: They looked, but there was none to save; even to the LORD, but he answered them not.
2SA.22.PLAIN: They looked, but there was no one to save them— to the Lord, but He did not answer.

2SA.22.BSB: I ground them as the dust of the earth; I crushed and trampled them like mud in the streets.
2SA.22.KJV: Then did I beat them as small as the dust of the earth, I did stamp them as the mire of the street, and did spread them abroad.
2SA.22.PLAIN: I ground them as the dust of the earth; I crushed and trampled them like mud in the streets.

2SA.22.BSB: You have delivered me from the strife of my people; You have preserved me as the head of nations; a people I had not known shall serve me.
2SA.22.KJV: You also have delivered me from the strivings of my people, you have kept me to be head of the heathen: a people which I knew not shall serve me.
2SA.22.PLAIN: You have delivered me from the strife of my people; You have preserved me as the head of nations; a people I had not known shall serve me.

2SA.22.BSB: Foreigners cower before me; when they hear me, they obey me.
2SA.22.KJV: Strangers shall submit themselves to me: as soon as they hear, they shall be obedient to me.
2SA.22.PLAIN: Foreigners cower before me; when they hear me, they obey me.

2SA.22.BSB: Foreigners lose heart and come trembling from their strongholds.
2SA.22.KJV: Strangers shall fade away, and they shall be afraid out of their close places.
2SA.22.PLAIN: Foreigners lose heart and come trembling from their strongholds.

2SA.22.BSB: The LORD lives, and blessed be my Rock! And may God, the Rock of my salvation, be exalted—
2SA.22.KJV: The LORD lives; and blessed be my rock; and exalted be the God of the rock of my salvation.
2SA.22.PLAIN: The Lord lives, and blessed be my Rock! And may God, the Rock of my salvation, be exalted—

2SA.22.BSB: the God who avenges me and brings down nations beneath me,
2SA.22.KJV: It is God that avenges me, and that brings down the people under me.
2SA.22.PLAIN: the God who avenges me and brings down nations beneath me,

2SA.22.BSB: who frees me from my enemies. You exalt me above my foes; You rescue me from violent men.
2SA.22.KJV: And that brings me forth from my enemies: you also have lifted me up on high above them that rose up against me: you have delivered me from the violent man.
2SA.22.PLAIN: who frees me from my enemies. You exalt me above my foes; You rescue me from violent men.

2SA.22.BSB: Therefore I will praise You, O LORD, among the nations; I will sing praises to Your name.
2SA.22.KJV: Therefore I will give thanks to you, O LORD, among the heathen, and I will sing praises to your name.
2SA.22.PLAIN: Therefore I will praise You, O Lord, among the nations; I will sing praises to Your name.

2SA.22.BSB: Great salvation He brings to His king. He shows loving devotion to His anointed, to David and his descendants forever.”
2SA.22.KJV: He is the tower of salvation for his king: and shows mercy to his anointed, to David, and to his seed for ever more.
2SA.22.PLAIN: Great salvation He brings to His king. He shows loving devotion to His anointed, to David and his descendants forever.”

2SA.23.BSB: These are the last words of David: “The oracle of David son of Jesse, the oracle of the man raised on high, the one anointed by the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel:
2SA.23.KJV: Now these be the last words of David. David the son of Jesse said, and the man who was raised up on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel, said,
2SA.23.PLAIN: These are the last words of David: “The oracle of David son of Jesse, the oracle of the man raised on high, the one anointed by the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel:

2SA.23.BSB: The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; His word was on my tongue.
2SA.23.KJV: The Spirit of the LORD spoke by me, and his word was in my tongue.
2SA.23.PLAIN: The Spirit of the Lord spoke through me; His word was on my tongue.

2SA.23.BSB: The God of Israel spoke; the Rock of Israel said to me, ‘He who rules the people with justice, who rules in the fear of God,
2SA.23.KJV: The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spoke to me, He that rules over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God.
2SA.23.PLAIN: The God of Israel spoke; the Rock of Israel said to me, ‘He who rules the people with justice, who rules in the fear of God,

2SA.23.BSB: is like the light of the morning at sunrise of a cloudless dawn, the glistening after the rain on the sprouting grass of the earth.’
2SA.23.KJV: And he shall be as the light of the morning, when the sun rises, even a morning without clouds; as the tender grass springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain.
2SA.23.PLAIN: is like the light of the morning at sunrise of a cloudless dawn, the glistening after the rain on the sprouting grass of the earth.’

2SA.23.BSB: Is not my house right with God? For He has established with me an everlasting covenant, ordered and secured in every part. Will He not bring about my full salvation and my every desire?
2SA.23.KJV: Although my house be not so with God; yet he has made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure: for this is all my salvation, and all my desire, although he make it not to grow. ¶
2SA.23.PLAIN: Is not my house right with God? For He has established with me an everlasting covenant, ordered and secured in every part. Will He not bring about my full salvation and my every desire?

2SA.23.BSB: But the worthless are all like thorns raked aside, for they can never be gathered by hand.
2SA.23.KJV: But the sons of Belial shall be all of them as thorns thrust away, because they cannot be taken with hands:
2SA.23.PLAIN: But the worthless are all like thorns raked aside, for they can never be gathered by hand.

2SA.23.BSB: The man who touches them must be armed with iron or with the shaft of a spear. The fire burns them to ashes in the place where they lie.”
2SA.23.KJV: But the man that shall touch them must be fenced with iron and the staff of a spear; and they shall be utterly burned with fire in the same place. ¶
2SA.23.PLAIN: The man who touches them must be armed with iron or with the shaft of a spear. The fire burns them to ashes in the place where they lie.”

2SA.23.BSB: These are the names of David’s mighty men: Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite was chief of the Three. He wielded his spear against eight hundred men, whom he killed at one time.
2SA.23.KJV: These be the names of the mighty men whom David had: The Tachmonite that sat in the seat, chief among the captains; the same was Adino the Eznite: he lift up his spear against eight hundred, whom he slew at one time.
2SA.23.PLAIN: These are the names of David’s mighty men: Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite was chief of the Three. He wielded his spear against eight hundred men, whom he killed at one time.

2SA.23.BSB: Next in command was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite. As one of the three mighty men, he went with David to taunt the Philistines who had gathered for battle at Pas-dammim. The men of Israel retreated,
2SA.23.KJV: And after him was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men with David, when they defied the Philistines that were there gathered together to battle, and the men of Israel were gone away:
2SA.23.PLAIN: Next in command was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite. As one of the three mighty men, he went with David to taunt the Philistines who had gathered for battle at Pas-dammim. The men of Israel retreated,

2SA.23.BSB: but Eleazar stood his ground and struck the Philistines until his hand grew weary and stuck to his sword. The LORD brought about a great victory that day. Then the troops returned to him, but only to plunder the dead.
2SA.23.KJV: He arose, and smote the Philistines until his hand was weary, and his hand stuck to the sword: and the LORD worked a great victory that day; and the people returned after him only to spoil.
2SA.23.PLAIN: but Eleazar stood his ground and struck the Philistines until his hand grew weary and stuck to his sword. The Lord brought about a great victory that day. Then the troops returned to him, but only to plunder the dead.

2SA.23.BSB: And after him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. When the Philistines had banded together near a field full of lentils, Israel’s troops fled from them.
2SA.23.KJV: And after him was Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite. And the Philistines were gathered together into a troop, where was a piece of ground full of lentils: and the people fled from the Philistines.
2SA.23.PLAIN: And after him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. When the Philistines had banded together near a field full of lentils, Israel’s troops fled from them.

2SA.23.BSB: But Shammah took his stand in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines. So the LORD brought about a great victory.
2SA.23.KJV: But he stood in the middle of the ground, and defended it, and slew the Philistines: and the LORD worked a great victory.
2SA.23.PLAIN: But Shammah took his stand in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines. So the Lord brought about a great victory.

2SA.23.BSB: At harvest time, three of the thirty chief men went down to David at the cave of Adullam, while a company of Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.
2SA.23.KJV: And three of the thirty chief went down, and came to David in the harvest time to the cave of Adullam: and the troop of the Philistines pitched in the valley of Rephaim.
2SA.23.PLAIN: At harvest time, three of the thirty chief men went down to David at the cave of Adullam, while a company of Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.

2SA.23.BSB: At that time David was in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was at Bethlehem.
2SA.23.KJV: And David was then in an hold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then in Bethlehem.
2SA.23.PLAIN: At that time David was in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was at Bethlehem.

2SA.23.BSB: David longed for water and said, “Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!”
2SA.23.KJV: And David longed, and said, Oh that one would give me drink of the water of the well of Bethlehem, which is by the gate!
2SA.23.PLAIN: David longed for water and said, “Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!”

2SA.23.BSB: So the three mighty men broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem, and brought it back to David. But he refused to drink it; instead, he poured it out to the LORD,
2SA.23.KJV: And the three mighty men broke through the host of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem, that was by the gate, and took it, and brought it to David: nevertheless he would not drink thereof, but poured it out to the LORD.
2SA.23.PLAIN: So the three mighty men broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem, and brought it back to David. But he refused to drink it; instead, he poured it out to the Lord,

2SA.23.BSB: saying, “Far be it from me, O LORD, to do this! Is this not the blood of the men who risked their lives?” So he refused to drink it. Such were the exploits of the three mighty men.
2SA.23.KJV: And he said, Be it far from me, O LORD, that I should do this: is not this the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives? therefore he would not drink it. These things did these three mighty men.
2SA.23.PLAIN: saying, “Far be it from me, O Lord, to do this! Is this not the blood of the men who risked their lives?” So he refused to drink it. Such were the exploits of the three mighty men.

2SA.23.BSB: Now Abishai, the brother of Joab and son of Zeruiah, was chief of the Three, and he lifted his spear against three hundred men, killed them, and won a name along with the Three.
2SA.23.KJV: And Abishai, the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was chief among three. And he lifted up his spear against three hundred, and slew them, and had the name among three.
2SA.23.PLAIN: Now Abishai, the brother of Joab and son of Zeruiah, was chief of the Three, and he lifted his spear against three hundred men, killed them, and won a name along with the Three.

2SA.23.BSB: Was he not more honored than the Three? And he became their commander, even though he was not included among the Three.
2SA.23.KJV: Was he not most honorable of three? therefore he was their captain: however, he attained not to the first three.
2SA.23.PLAIN: Was he not more honored than the Three? And he became their commander, even though he was not included among the Three.

2SA.23.BSB: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a man of valor from Kabzeel, a man of many exploits. He struck down two champions of Moab, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
2SA.23.KJV: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man, of Kabzeel, who had done many acts, he slew two lion like men of Moab: he went down also and slew a lion in the middle of a pit in time of snow:
2SA.23.PLAIN: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a man of valor from Kabzeel, a man of many exploits. He struck down two champions of Moab, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.

2SA.23.BSB: He also killed an Egyptian, a huge man. Although the Egyptian had a spear in his hand, Benaiah went against him with a club, snatched the spear from his hand, and killed the Egyptian with his own spear.
2SA.23.KJV: And he slew an Egyptian, a goodly man: and the Egyptian had a spear in his hand; but he went down to him with a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and slew him with his own spear.
2SA.23.PLAIN: He also killed an Egyptian, a huge man. Although the Egyptian had a spear in his hand, Benaiah went against him with a club, snatched the spear from his hand, and killed the Egyptian with his own spear.

2SA.23.BSB: These were the exploits of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who won a name alongside the three mighty men.
2SA.23.KJV: These things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and had the name among three mighty men.
2SA.23.PLAIN: These were the exploits of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who won a name alongside the three mighty men.

2SA.23.BSB: He was most honored among the Thirty, but he did not become one of the Three. And David appointed him over his guard.
2SA.23.KJV: He was more honorable than the thirty, but he attained not to the first three. And David set him over his guard.
2SA.23.PLAIN: He was most honored among the Thirty, but he did not become one of the Three. And David appointed him over his guard.

2SA.23.BSB: Now these were members of the Thirty: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
2SA.23.KJV: Asahel the brother of Joab was one of the thirty; Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
2SA.23.PLAIN: Now these were members of the Thirty: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem,

2SA.23.BSB: Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
2SA.23.KJV: Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
2SA.23.PLAIN: Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,

2SA.23.BSB: Helez the Paltite, Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,
2SA.23.KJV: Helez the Paltite, Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,
2SA.23.PLAIN: Helez the Paltite, Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,

2SA.23.BSB: Abiezer the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
2SA.23.KJV: Abiezer the Anethothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
2SA.23.PLAIN: Abiezer the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,

2SA.23.BSB: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
2SA.23.KJV: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
2SA.23.PLAIN: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,

2SA.23.BSB: Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the Benjamites,
2SA.23.KJV: Heleb the son of Baanah, a Netophathite, Ittai the son of Ribai out of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin,
2SA.23.PLAIN: Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the Benjamites,

2SA.23.BSB: Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai from the brooks of Gaash,
2SA.23.KJV: Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash,
2SA.23.PLAIN: Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai from the brooks of Gaash,

2SA.23.BSB: Abi-albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
2SA.23.KJV: Abialbon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
2SA.23.PLAIN: Abi-albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,

2SA.23.BSB: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen,
2SA.23.KJV: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, of the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
2SA.23.PLAIN: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen,

2SA.23.BSB: Jonathan son of Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite,
2SA.23.KJV: Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam the son of Sharar the Hararite,
2SA.23.PLAIN: Jonathan son of Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite,

2SA.23.BSB: Eliphelet son of Ahasbai the Maacathite, Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
2SA.23.KJV: Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maachathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
2SA.23.PLAIN: Eliphelet son of Ahasbai the Maacathite, Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,

2SA.23.BSB: Hezro the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,
2SA.23.KJV: Hezrai the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,
2SA.23.PLAIN: Hezro the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,

2SA.23.BSB: Igal son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
2SA.23.KJV: Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
2SA.23.PLAIN: Igal son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,

2SA.23.BSB: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah,
2SA.23.KJV: Zelek the Ammonite, Nahari the Beerothite, armor bearer to Joab the son of Zeruiah,
2SA.23.PLAIN: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah,

2SA.23.BSB: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
2SA.23.KJV: Ira an Ithrite, Gareb an Ithrite,
2SA.23.PLAIN: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,

2SA.23.BSB: and Uriah the Hittite. There were thirty-seven in all.
2SA.23.KJV: Uriah the Hittite: thirty and seven in all.
2SA.23.PLAIN: and Uriah the Hittite. There were thirty-seven in all.

2SA.24.BSB: Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He stirred up David against them, saying, “Go and take a census of Israel and Judah.”
2SA.24.KJV: And again the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them to say, Go, number Israel and Judah.
2SA.24.PLAIN: Again the anger of the Lord burned against Israel, and He stirred up David against them, saying, “Go and take a census of Israel and Judah.”

2SA.24.BSB: So the king said to Joab the commander of his army, who was with him, “Go now throughout the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beersheba and register the troops, so that I may know their number.”
2SA.24.KJV: For the king said to Joab the captain of the host, which was with him, Go now through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beersheba, and number you the people, that I may know the number of the people.
2SA.24.PLAIN: So the king said to Joab the commander of his army, who was with him, “Go now throughout the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beersheba and register the troops, so that I may know their number.”

2SA.24.BSB: But Joab replied to the king, “May the LORD your God multiply the troops a hundred times over, and may the eyes of my lord the king see it. But why does my lord the king want to do such a thing?”
2SA.24.KJV: And Joab said to the king, Now the LORD your God add to the people, how many soever they be, an hundred times, and that the eyes of my lord the king may see it: but why does my lord the king delight in this thing?
2SA.24.PLAIN: But Joab replied to the king, “May the Lord your God multiply the troops a hundred times over, and may the eyes of my lord the king see it. But why does my lord the king want to do such a thing?”

2SA.24.BSB: Nevertheless, the king’s word prevailed against Joab and against the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army departed from the presence of the king to count the troops of Israel.
2SA.24.KJV: Notwithstanding the king’s word prevailed against Joab, and against the captains of the host. And Joab and the captains of the host went out from the presence of the king, to number the people of Israel. ¶
2SA.24.PLAIN: Nevertheless, the king’s word prevailed against Joab and against the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army departed from the presence of the king to count the troops of Israel.

2SA.24.BSB: They crossed the Jordan and camped near Aroer, south of the town in the middle of the valley, and proceeded toward Gad and Jazer.
2SA.24.KJV: And they passed over Jordan, and pitched in Aroer, on the right side of the city that lies in the middle of the river of Gad, and toward Jazer:
2SA.24.PLAIN: They crossed the Jordan and camped near Aroer, south of the town in the middle of the valley, and proceeded toward Gad and Jazer.

2SA.24.BSB: Then they went to Gilead and the land of Tahtim-hodshi, and on to Dan-jaan and around to Sidon.
2SA.24.KJV: Then they came to Gilead, and to the land of Tahtimhodshi; and they came to Danjaan, and about to Zidon,
2SA.24.PLAIN: Then they went to Gilead and the land of Tahtim-hodshi, and on to Dan-jaan and around to Sidon.

2SA.24.BSB: They went toward the fortress of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites. Finally, they went on to the Negev of Judah, to Beersheba.
2SA.24.KJV: And came to the strong hold of Tyre, and to all the cities of the Hivites, and of the Canaanites: and they went out to the south of Judah, even to Beersheba.
2SA.24.PLAIN: They went toward the fortress of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites. Finally, they went on to the Negev of Judah, to Beersheba.

2SA.24.BSB: At the end of nine months and twenty days, having gone through the whole land, they returned to Jerusalem.
2SA.24.KJV: So when they had gone through all the land, they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
2SA.24.PLAIN: At the end of nine months and twenty days, having gone through the whole land, they returned to Jerusalem.

2SA.24.BSB: And Joab reported to the king the total number of the troops. In Israel there were 800,000 men of valor who drew the sword, and in Judah there were 500,000.
2SA.24.KJV: And Joab gave up the sum of the number of the people to the king: and there were in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men that drew the sword; and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men. ¶
2SA.24.PLAIN: And Joab reported to the king the total number of the troops. In Israel there were 800,000 men of valor who drew the sword, and in Judah there were 500,000.

2SA.24.BSB: After David had numbered the troops, his conscience was stricken and he said to the LORD, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done. Now, O LORD, I beg You to take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.”
2SA.24.KJV: And David’s heart smote him after that he had numbered the people. And David said to the LORD, I have sinned greatly in that I have done: and now, I beseech you, O LORD, take away the iniquity of your servant; for I have done very foolishly.
2SA.24.PLAIN: After David had numbered the troops, his conscience was stricken and he said to the Lord, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done. Now, O Lord, I beg You to take away the brokenness of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.”

2SA.24.BSB: When David got up in the morning, a revelation from the LORD had come to Gad the prophet, David’s seer:
2SA.24.KJV: For when David was up in the morning, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Gad, David’s seer, saying,
2SA.24.PLAIN: When David got up in the morning, a revelation from the Lord had come to Gad the prophet, David’s seer:

2SA.24.BSB: “Go and tell David that this is what the LORD says: ‘I am offering you three options. Choose one of them, and I will carry it out against you.’”
2SA.24.KJV: Go and say to David, Thus says the LORD, I offer you three things; choose you one of them, that I may do it to you.
2SA.24.PLAIN: “Go and tell David that this is what the Lord says: ‘I am offering you three options. Choose one of them, and I will carry it out against you.’”

2SA.24.BSB: So Gad went and said to David, “Do you choose to endure three years of famine in your land, three months of fleeing the pursuit of your enemies, or three days of plague upon your land? Now then, think it over and decide how I should reply to Him who sent me.”
2SA.24.KJV: So Gad came to David, and told him, and said to him, Shall seven years of famine come to you in your land? or will you flee three months before your enemies, while they pursue you? or that there be three days’ pestilence in your land? now advise, and see what answer I shall return to him that sent me.
2SA.24.PLAIN: So Gad went and said to David, “Do you choose to endure three years of famine in your land, three months of fleeing the pursuit of your enemies, or three days of plague upon your land? Now then, think it over and decide how I should reply to Him who sent me.”

2SA.24.BSB: David answered Gad, “I am deeply distressed. Please, let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are great; but do not let me fall into the hands of men.”
2SA.24.KJV: And David said to Gad, I am in a great strait: let us fall now into the hand of the LORD; for his mercies are great: and let me not fall into the hand of man. ¶
2SA.24.PLAIN: David answered Gad, “I am deeply distressed. Please, let us fall into the hand of the Lord, for His mercies are great; but do not let me fall into the hands of men.”

2SA.24.BSB: So the LORD sent a plague upon Israel from that morning until the appointed time, and seventy thousand of the people from Dan to Beersheba died.
2SA.24.KJV: So the LORD sent a pestilence on Israel from the morning even to the time appointed: and there died of the people from Dan even to Beersheba seventy thousand men.
2SA.24.PLAIN: So the Lord sent a plague upon Israel from that morning until the appointed time, and seventy thousand of the people from Dan to Beersheba died.

2SA.24.BSB: But when the angel stretched out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the LORD relented from the calamity and said to the angel who was destroying the people, “Enough! Withdraw your hand now!” At that time the angel of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
2SA.24.KJV: And when the angel stretched out his hand on Jerusalem to destroy it, the LORD repented him of the evil, and said to the angel that destroyed the people, It is enough: stay now your hand. And the angel of the LORD was by the threshing place of Araunah the Jebusite.
2SA.24.PLAIN: But when the angel stretched out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the Lord relented from the calamity and said to the angel who was destroying the people, “Enough! Withdraw your hand now!” At that time the angel of the Lord was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

2SA.24.BSB: When David saw the angel striking down the people, he said to the LORD, “Surely I, the shepherd, have sinned and acted wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done? Please, let Your hand fall upon me and my father’s house.”
2SA.24.KJV: And David spoke to the LORD when he saw the angel that smote the people, and said, See, I have sinned, and I have done wickedly: but these sheep, what have they done? let your hand, I pray you, be against me, and against my father’s house. ¶
2SA.24.PLAIN: When David saw the angel striking down the people, he said to the Lord, “Surely I, the shepherd, have sinned and acted wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done? Please, let Your hand fall upon me and my father’s house.”

2SA.24.BSB: And that day Gad came to David and said to him, “Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”
2SA.24.KJV: And Gad came that day to David, and said to him, Go up, raise an altar to the LORD in the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
2SA.24.PLAIN: And that day Gad came to David and said to him, “Go up and build an altar to the Lord on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”

2SA.24.BSB: So David went up at the word of Gad, just as the LORD had commanded.
2SA.24.KJV: And David, according to the saying of Gad, went up as the LORD commanded.
2SA.24.PLAIN: So David went up at the word of Gad, just as the Lord had commanded.

2SA.24.BSB: When Araunah looked out and saw the king and his servants coming toward him, he went out and bowed facedown before the king.
2SA.24.KJV: And Araunah looked, and saw the king and his servants coming on toward him: and Araunah went out, and bowed himself before the king on his face on the ground.
2SA.24.PLAIN: When Araunah looked out and saw the king and his servants coming toward him, he went out and bowed facedown before the king.

2SA.24.BSB: “Why has my lord the king come to his servant?” Araunah said. “To buy your threshing floor,” David replied, “that I may build an altar to the LORD, so that the plague upon the people may be halted.”
2SA.24.KJV: And Araunah said, Why is my lord the king come to his servant? And David said, To buy the threshing floor of you, to build an altar to the LORD, that the plague may be stayed from the people.
2SA.24.PLAIN: “Why has my lord the king come to his servant?” Araunah said. “To buy your threshing floor,” David replied, “that I may build an altar to the Lord, so that the plague upon the people may be halted.”

2SA.24.BSB: Araunah said to David, “My lord the king may take whatever seems good and offer it up. Here are the oxen for a burnt offering and the threshing sledges and ox yokes for the wood.
2SA.24.KJV: And Araunah said to David, Let my lord the king take and offer up what seems good to him: behold, here be oxen for burnt sacrifice, and threshing instruments and other instruments of the oxen for wood.
2SA.24.PLAIN: Araunah said to David, “My lord the king may take whatever seems good and offer it up. Here are the oxen for a burnt offering and the threshing sledges and ox yokes for the wood.

2SA.24.BSB: O king, Araunah gives all these to the king.” He also said to the king, “May the LORD your God accept you.”
2SA.24.KJV: All these things did Araunah, as a king, give to the king. And Araunah said to the king, The LORD your God accept you.
2SA.24.PLAIN: O king, Araunah gives all these to the king.” He also said to the king, “May the Lord your God accept you.”

2SA.24.BSB: “No,” replied the king, “I insist on paying a price, for I will not offer to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
2SA.24.KJV: And the king said to Araunah, No; but I will surely buy it of you at a price: neither will I offer burnt offerings to the LORD my God of that which does cost me nothing. So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
2SA.24.PLAIN: “No,” replied the king, “I insist on paying a price, for I will not offer to the Lord my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

2SA.24.BSB: And there he built an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then the LORD answered the prayers on behalf of the land, and the plague upon Israel was halted.
2SA.24.KJV: And David built there an altar to the LORD, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. So the LORD was entreated for the land, and the plague was stayed from Israel.
2SA.24.PLAIN: And there he built an altar to the Lord and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then the Lord answered the prayers on behalf of the land, and the plague upon Israel was halted.

1KI.1.BSB: Now King David was old and well along in years, and though they covered him with blankets, he could not keep warm.
1KI.1.KJV: Now king David was old and stricken in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he got no heat.
1KI.1.PLAIN: Now King David was old and well along in years, and though they covered him with blankets, he could not keep warm.

1KI.1.BSB: So his servants said to him, “Let us search for a young virgin for our lord the king, to attend to him and care for him and lie by his side to keep him warm.”
1KI.1.KJV: Why his servants said to him, Let there be sought for my lord the king a young virgin: and let her stand before the king, and let her cherish him, and let her lie in your bosom, that my lord the king may get heat.
1KI.1.PLAIN: So his servants said to him, “Let us search for a young virgin for our lord the king, to attend to him and care for him and lie by his side to keep him warm.”

1KI.1.BSB: Then they searched throughout Israel for a beautiful girl, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.
1KI.1.KJV: So they sought for a fair damsel throughout all the coasts of Israel, and found Abishag a Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
1KI.1.PLAIN: Then they searched throughout Israel for a beautiful girl, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.

1KI.1.BSB: The girl was unsurpassed in beauty; she cared for the king and served him, but he had no relations with her.
1KI.1.KJV: And the damsel was very fair, and cherished the king, and ministered to him: but the king knew her not. ¶
1KI.1.PLAIN: The girl was unsurpassed in beauty; she cared for the king and served him, but he had no relations with her.

1KI.1.BSB: At that time Adonijah, David’s son by Haggith, began to exalt himself, saying, “I will be king!” And he acquired chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run ahead of him.
1KI.1.KJV: Then Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I will be king: and he prepared him chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
1KI.1.PLAIN: At that time Adonijah, David’s son by Haggith, began to exalt himself, saying, “I will be king!” And he acquired chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run ahead of him.

1KI.1.BSB: (His father had never once reprimanded him by saying, “Why do you act this way?” Adonijah was also very handsome, born next after Absalom.)
1KI.1.KJV: And his father had not displeased him at any time in saying, Why have you done so? and he also was a very goodly man; and his mother bore him after Absalom.
1KI.1.PLAIN: (His father had never once reprimanded him by saying, “Why do you act this way?” Adonijah was also very handsome, born next after Absalom.)

1KI.1.BSB: So Adonijah conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, who supported him.
1KI.1.KJV: And he conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah, and with Abiathar the priest: and they following Adonijah helped him.
1KI.1.PLAIN: So Adonijah conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, who supported him.

1KI.1.BSB: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David’s mighty men would not join Adonijah.
1KI.1.KJV: But Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and Nathan the prophet, and Shimei, and Rei, and the mighty men which belonged to David, were not with Adonijah.
1KI.1.PLAIN: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David’s mighty men would not join Adonijah.

1KI.1.BSB: And Adonijah sacrificed sheep, oxen, and fattened calves near the stone of Zoheleth, which is next to En-rogel. He invited all his royal brothers and all the men of Judah who were servants of the king.
1KI.1.KJV: And Adonijah slew sheep and oxen and fat cattle by the stone of Zoheleth, which is by Enrogel, and called all his brothers the king’s sons, and all the men of Judah the king’s servants:
1KI.1.PLAIN: And Adonijah sacrificed sheep, oxen, and fattened calves near the stone of Zoheleth, which is next to En-rogel. He invited all his royal brothers and all the men of Judah who were servants of the king.

1KI.1.BSB: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, or his brother Solomon.
1KI.1.KJV: But Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, and the mighty men, and Solomon his brother, he called not. ¶
1KI.1.PLAIN: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, or his brother Solomon.

1KI.1.BSB: Then Nathan said to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, “Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David does not know it?
1KI.1.KJV: Why Nathan spoke to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, saying, Have you not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith does reign, and David our lord knows it not?
1KI.1.PLAIN: Then Nathan said to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, “Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David does not know it?

1KI.1.BSB: Now please, come and let me advise you. Save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.
1KI.1.KJV: Now therefore come, let me, I pray you, give you counsel, that you may save your own life, and the life of your son Solomon.
1KI.1.PLAIN: Now please, come and let me advise you. Save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.

1KI.1.BSB: Go at once to King David and say, ‘My lord the king, did you not swear to your maidservant, “Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne”? Why then has Adonijah become king?’
1KI.1.KJV: Go and get you in to king David, and say to him, Did not you, my lord, O king, swear to your handmaid, saying, Assuredly Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne? why then does Adonijah reign?
1KI.1.PLAIN: Go at once to King David and say, ‘My lord the king, did you not swear to your maidservant, “Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne”? Why then has Adonijah become king?’

1KI.1.BSB: Then, while you are still there speaking with the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words.”
1KI.1.KJV: Behold, while you yet talk there with the king, I also will come in after you, and confirm your words. ¶
1KI.1.PLAIN: Then, while you are still there speaking with the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words.”

1KI.1.BSB: So Bathsheba went to see the king in his bedroom. Since the king was very old, Abishag the Shunammite was serving him.
1KI.1.KJV: And Bathsheba went in to the king into the chamber: and the king was very old; and Abishag the Shunammite ministered to the king.
1KI.1.PLAIN: So Bathsheba went to see the king in his bedroom. Since the king was very old, Abishag the Shunammite was serving him.

1KI.1.BSB: And Bathsheba bowed down in homage to the king, who asked, “What is your desire?”
1KI.1.KJV: And Bathsheba bowed, and did obeisance to the king. And the king said, What would you?
1KI.1.PLAIN: And Bathsheba bowed down in homage to the king, who asked, “What is your desire?”

1KI.1.BSB: “My lord,” she replied, “you yourself swore to your maidservant by the LORD your God: ‘Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne.’
1KI.1.KJV: And she said to him, My lord, you swore by the LORD your God to your handmaid, saying, Assuredly Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.
1KI.1.PLAIN: “My lord,” she replied, “you yourself swore to your maidservant by the Lord your God: ‘Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne.’

1KI.1.BSB: But now, behold, Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, did not know it.
1KI.1.KJV: And now, behold, Adonijah reigns; and now, my lord the king, you know it not:
1KI.1.PLAIN: But now, look closely — Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, did not know it.

1KI.1.BSB: And he has sacrificed an abundance of oxen, fattened calves, and sheep, and has invited all the other sons of the king, as well as Abiathar the priest and Joab the commander of the army. But he did not invite your servant Solomon.
1KI.1.KJV: And he has slain oxen and fat cattle and sheep in abundance, and has called all the sons of the king, and Abiathar the priest, and Joab the captain of the host: but Solomon your servant has he not called.
1KI.1.PLAIN: And he has sacrificed an abundance of oxen, fattened calves, and sheep, and has invited all the other sons of the king, as well as Abiathar the priest and Joab the commander of the army. But he did not invite your servant Solomon.

1KI.1.BSB: And as for you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are upon you to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
1KI.1.KJV: And you, my lord, O king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, that you should tell them who shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
1KI.1.PLAIN: And as for you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are upon you to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.

1KI.1.BSB: Otherwise, when my lord the king rests with his fathers, I and my son Solomon will be counted as criminals.”
1KI.1.KJV: Otherwise it shall come to pass, when my lord the king shall sleep with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon shall be counted offenders. ¶
1KI.1.PLAIN: Otherwise, when my lord the king rests with his fathers, I and my son Solomon will be counted as criminals.”

1KI.1.BSB: And just then, while Bathsheba was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.
1KI.1.KJV: And, see, while she yet talked with the king, Nathan the prophet also came in.
1KI.1.PLAIN: And just then, while Bathsheba was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.

1KI.1.BSB: So the king was told, “Nathan the prophet is here.” And Nathan went in and bowed facedown before the king.
1KI.1.KJV: And they told the king, saying, Behold Nathan the prophet. And when he was come in before the king, he bowed himself before the king with his face to the ground.
1KI.1.PLAIN: So the king was told, “Nathan the prophet is here.” And Nathan went in and bowed facedown before the king.

1KI.1.BSB: “My lord the king,” said Nathan, “did you say, ‘Adonijah will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne’?
1KI.1.KJV: And Nathan said, My lord, O king, have you said, Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne?
1KI.1.PLAIN: “My lord the king,” said Nathan, “did you say, ‘Adonijah will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne’?

1KI.1.BSB: For today he has gone down and sacrificed an abundance of oxen, fattened calves, and sheep, and has invited all the sons of the king, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest. And behold, they are eating and drinking before him, saying, ‘Long live King Adonijah!’
1KI.1.KJV: For he is gone down this day, and has slain oxen and fat cattle and sheep in abundance, and has called all the king’s sons, and the captains of the host, and Abiathar the priest; and, behold, they eat and drink before him, and say, God save king Adonijah.
1KI.1.PLAIN: For today he has gone down and sacrificed an abundance of oxen, fattened calves, and sheep, and has invited all the sons of the king, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest. And look closely — they are eating and drinking before him, saying, ‘Long live King Adonijah!’

1KI.1.BSB: But me your servant he did not invite, nor Zadok the priest, nor Benaiah son of Jehoiada, nor your servant Solomon.
1KI.1.KJV: But me, even me your servant, and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and your servant Solomon, has he not called.
1KI.1.PLAIN: But me your servant he did not invite, nor Zadok the priest, nor Benaiah son of Jehoiada, nor your servant Solomon.

1KI.1.BSB: Has my lord the king let this happen without informing your servant who should sit on the throne after my lord the king?”
1KI.1.KJV: Is this thing done by my lord the king, and you have not showed it to your servant, who should sit on the throne of my lord the king after him? ¶
1KI.1.PLAIN: Has my lord the king let this happen without informing your servant who should sit on the throne after my lord the king?”

1KI.1.BSB: Then King David said, “Call in Bathsheba for me.” So she came into the king’s presence and stood before him.
1KI.1.KJV: Then king David answered and said, Call me Bathsheba. And she came into the king’s presence, and stood before the king.
1KI.1.PLAIN: Then King David said, “Call in Bathsheba for me.” So she came into the king’s presence and stood before him.

1KI.1.BSB: And the king swore an oath, saying, “As surely as the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from all distress,
1KI.1.KJV: And the king swore, and said, As the LORD lives, that has redeemed my soul out of all distress,
1KI.1.PLAIN: And the king swore an oath, saying, “As surely as the Lord lives, who has redeemed my life from all distress,

1KI.1.BSB: I will carry out this very day exactly what I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel: Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne in my place.”
1KI.1.KJV: Even as I swore to you by the LORD God of Israel, saying, Assuredly Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my stead; even so will I certainly do this day.
1KI.1.PLAIN: I will carry out this very day exactly what I swore to you by the Lord, the God of Israel: Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne in my place.”

1KI.1.BSB: Bathsheba bowed facedown in homage to the king and said, “May my lord King David live forever!”
1KI.1.KJV: Then Bathsheba bowed with her face to the earth, and did reverence to the king, and said, Let my lord king David live for ever. ¶
1KI.1.PLAIN: Bathsheba bowed facedown in homage to the king and said, “May my lord King David live forever!”

1KI.1.BSB: Then King David said, “Call in for me Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada.” So they came before the king.
1KI.1.KJV: And king David said, Call me Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada. And they came before the king.
1KI.1.PLAIN: Then King David said, “Call in for me Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada.” So they came before the king.

1KI.1.BSB: “Take my servants with you,” said the king. “Set my son Solomon on my own mule and take him down to Gihon.
1KI.1.KJV: The king also said to them, Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon:
1KI.1.PLAIN: “Take my servants with you,” said the king. “Set my son Solomon on my own mule and take him down to Gihon.

1KI.1.BSB: There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet are to anoint him king over Israel. You are to blow the ram’s horn and declare, ‘Long live King Solomon!’
1KI.1.KJV: And let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there king over Israel: and blow you with the trumpet, and say, God save king Solomon.
1KI.1.PLAIN: There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet are to anoint him king over Israel. You are to blow the ram’s horn and declare, ‘Long live King Solomon!’

1KI.1.BSB: Then you shall go up with him, and he is to come and sit on my throne and reign in my place. For I have appointed him ruler over Israel and Judah.”
1KI.1.KJV: Then you shall come up after him, that he may come and sit on my throne; for he shall be king in my stead: and I have appointed him to be ruler over Israel and over Judah.
1KI.1.PLAIN: Then you shall go up with him, and he is to come and sit on my throne and reign in my place. For I have appointed him ruler over Israel and Judah.”

1KI.1.BSB: “Amen,” replied Benaiah son of Jehoiada. “May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, so declare it.
1KI.1.KJV: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada answered the king, and said, Amen: the LORD God of my lord the king say so too.
1KI.1.PLAIN: “Amen,” replied Benaiah son of Jehoiada. “May the Lord, the God of my lord the king, so declare it.

1KI.1.BSB: Just as the LORD was with my lord the king, so may He be with Solomon and make his throne even greater than that of my lord King David.”
