1KI.9.BSB: Now at the end of the twenty years during which Solomon built these two houses, the house of the LORD and the royal palace,
1KI.9.KJV: And it came to pass at the end of twenty years, when Solomon had built the two houses, the house of the LORD, and the king’s house,
1KI.9.PLAIN: Now at the end of the twenty years during which Solomon built these two houses, the house of the Lord and the royal palace,

1KI.9.BSB: King Solomon gave twenty towns in the land of Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, who had supplied him with cedar and cypress logs and gold for his every desire.
1KI.9.KJV: (Now Hiram the king of Tyre had furnished Solomon with cedar trees and fir trees, and with gold, according to all his desire,) that then king Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.
1KI.9.PLAIN: King Solomon gave twenty towns in the land of Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, who had supplied him with cedar and cypress logs and gold for his every desire.

1KI.9.BSB: So Hiram went out from Tyre to inspect the towns that Solomon had given him, but he was not pleased with them.
1KI.9.KJV: And Hiram came out from Tyre to see the cities which Solomon had given him; and they pleased him not.
1KI.9.PLAIN: So Hiram went out from Tyre to inspect the towns that Solomon had given him, but he was not pleased with them.

1KI.9.BSB: “What are these towns you have given me, my brother?” asked Hiram, and he called them the Land of Cabul, as they are called to this day.
1KI.9.KJV: And he said, What cities are these which you have given me, my brother? And he called them the land of Cabul to this day.
1KI.9.PLAIN: “What are these towns you have given me, my brother?” asked Hiram, and he called them the Land of Cabul, as they are called to this day.

1KI.9.BSB: And Hiram had sent the king 120 talents of gold.
1KI.9.KJV: And Hiram sent to the king six score talents of gold. ¶
1KI.9.PLAIN: And Hiram had sent the king 120 talents of gold.

1KI.9.BSB: This is the account of the forced labor that King Solomon imposed to build the house of the LORD, his own palace, the supporting terraces, and the wall of Jerusalem, as well as Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
1KI.9.KJV: And this is the reason of the levy which king Solomon raised; for to build the house of the LORD, and his own house, and Millo, and the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor, and Megiddo, and Gezer.
1KI.9.PLAIN: This is the account of the forced labor that King Solomon imposed to build the house of the Lord, his own palace, the supporting terraces, and the wall of Jerusalem, as well as Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.

1KI.9.BSB: Pharaoh king of Egypt had attacked and captured Gezer. He had set it on fire, killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and given it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon’s wife.
1KI.9.KJV: For Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up, and taken Gezer, and burnt it with fire, and slain the Canaanites that dwelled in the city, and given it for a present to his daughter, Solomon’s wife.
1KI.9.PLAIN: Pharaoh king of Egypt had attacked and captured Gezer. He had set it on fire, killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and given it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon’s wife.

1KI.9.BSB: So Solomon rebuilt Gezer, Lower Beth-horon,
1KI.9.KJV: And Solomon built Gezer, and Bethhoron the nether,
1KI.9.PLAIN: So Solomon rebuilt Gezer, Lower Beth-horon,

1KI.9.BSB: Baalath, and Tamar in the Wilderness of Judah,
1KI.9.KJV: And Baalath, and Tadmor in the wilderness, in the land,
1KI.9.PLAIN: Baalath, and Tamar in the Wilderness of Judah,

1KI.9.BSB: as well as all the store cities that Solomon had for his chariots and horses—whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and throughout the land of his dominion.
1KI.9.KJV: And all the cities of store that Solomon had, and cities for his chariots, and cities for his horsemen, and that which Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.
1KI.9.PLAIN: as well as all the store cities that Solomon had for his chariots and horses—whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and throughout the land of his dominion.

1KI.9.BSB: As for all the people who remained of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites (the people who were not Israelites)—
1KI.9.KJV: And all the people that were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, which were not of the children of Israel,
1KI.9.PLAIN: As for all the people who remained of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites (the people who were not Israelites)—

1KI.9.BSB: their descendants who remained in the land, those whom the Israelites were unable to devote to destruction—Solomon conscripted these people to be forced laborers, as they are to this day.
1KI.9.KJV: Their children that were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel also were not able utterly to destroy, on those did Solomon levy a tribute of slavery to this day.
1KI.9.PLAIN: their descendants who remained in the land, those whom the Israelites were unable to devote to destruction—Solomon conscripted these people to be forced laborers, as they are to this day.

1KI.9.BSB: But Solomon did not consign any of the Israelites to slavery, because they were his men of war, his servants, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry.
1KI.9.KJV: But of the children of Israel did Solomon make no slaves: but they were men of war, and his servants, and his princes, and his captains, and rulers of his chariots, and his horsemen.
1KI.9.PLAIN: But Solomon did not consign any of the Israelites to slavery, because they were his men of war, his servants, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry.

1KI.9.BSB: They were also the chief officers over Solomon’s projects: 550 supervisors over the people who did the work.
1KI.9.KJV: These were the chief of the officers that were over Solomon’s work, five hundred and fifty, which bore rule over the people that worked in the work. ¶
1KI.9.PLAIN: They were also the chief officers over Solomon’s projects: 550 supervisors over the people who did the work.

1KI.9.BSB: As soon as Pharaoh’s daughter had come up from the City of David to the palace that Solomon had built for her, he built the supporting terraces.
1KI.9.KJV: But Pharaoh’s daughter came up out of the city of David to her house which Solomon had built for her: then did he build Millo. ¶
1KI.9.PLAIN: As soon as Pharaoh’s daughter had come up from the City of David to the palace that Solomon had built for her, he built the supporting terraces.

1KI.9.BSB: Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he had built for the LORD, burning incense with them before the LORD. So he completed the temple.
1KI.9.KJV: And three times in a year did Solomon offer burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar which he built to the LORD, and he burnt incense on the altar that was before the LORD. So he finished the house. ¶
1KI.9.PLAIN: Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he had built for the Lord, burning incense with them before the Lord. So he completed the temple.

1KI.9.BSB: King Solomon also assembled a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, which is near Eloth in Edom, on the shore of the Red Sea.
1KI.9.KJV: And king Solomon made a navy of ships in Eziongeber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red sea, in the land of Edom.
1KI.9.PLAIN: King Solomon also assembled a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, which is near Eloth in Edom, on the shore of the Red Sea.

1KI.9.BSB: And Hiram sent his servants, men who knew the sea, to serve in the fleet with Solomon’s servants.
1KI.9.KJV: And Hiram sent in the navy his servants, shipmen that had knowledge of the sea, with the servants of Solomon.
1KI.9.PLAIN: And Hiram sent his servants, men who knew the sea, to serve in the fleet with Solomon’s servants.

1KI.9.BSB: They sailed to Ophir and imported gold from there—420 talents—and delivered it to Solomon.
1KI.9.KJV: And they came to Ophir, and fetched from there gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and brought it to king Solomon.
1KI.9.PLAIN: They sailed to Ophir and imported gold from there—420 talents—and delivered it to Solomon.

1KI.10.BSB: Now when the queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to test him with difficult questions.
1KI.10.KJV: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to prove him with hard questions.
1KI.10.PLAIN: Now when the queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the Lord, she came to test him with difficult questions.

1KI.10.BSB: She arrived in Jerusalem with a very large caravan—with camels bearing spices, gold in great abundance, and precious stones. So she came to Solomon and spoke to him all that was on her mind.
1KI.10.KJV: And she came to Jerusalem with a very great train, with camels that bore spices, and very much gold, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart.
1KI.10.PLAIN: She arrived in Jerusalem with a very large caravan—with camels bearing spices, gold in great abundance, and precious stones. So she came to Solomon and spoke to him all that was on her mind.

1KI.10.BSB: And Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too difficult for the king to explain.
1KI.10.KJV: And Solomon told her all her questions: there was not any thing hid from the king, which he told her not.
1KI.10.PLAIN: And Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too difficult for the king to explain.

1KI.10.BSB: When the queen of Sheba saw all the wisdom of Solomon, the palace he had built,
1KI.10.KJV: And when the queen of Sheba had seen all Solomon’s wisdom, and the house that he had built,
1KI.10.PLAIN: When the queen of Sheba saw all the wisdom of Solomon, the palace he had built,

1KI.10.BSB: the food at his table, the seating of his servants, the service and attire of his attendants and cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presented at the house of the LORD, it took her breath away.
1KI.10.KJV: And the meat of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel, and his cupbearers, and his ascent by which he went up to the house of the LORD; there was no more spirit in her.
1KI.10.PLAIN: the food at his table, the seating of his servants, the service and attire of his attendants and cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presented at the house of the Lord, it took her breath away.

1KI.10.BSB: She said to the king, “The report I heard in my own country about your words and wisdom is true.
1KI.10.KJV: And she said to the king, It was a true report that I heard in my own land of your acts and of your wisdom.
1KI.10.PLAIN: She said to the king, “The report I heard in my own country about your words and wisdom is true.

1KI.10.BSB: But I did not believe these things until I came and saw with my own eyes. Indeed, not even half was told to me. Your wisdom and prosperity have far exceeded the report I heard.
1KI.10.KJV: However, I believed not the words, until I came, and my eyes had seen it: and, behold, the half was not told me: your wisdom and prosperity exceeds the fame which I heard.
1KI.10.PLAIN: But I did not believe these things until I came and saw with my own eyes. Indeed, not even half was told to me. Your wisdom and prosperity have far exceeded the report I heard.

1KI.10.BSB: How blessed are your men! How blessed are these servants of yours who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!
1KI.10.KJV: Happy are your men, happy are these your servants, which stand continually before you, and that hear your wisdom.
1KI.10.PLAIN: How blessed are your men! How blessed are these servants of yours who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!

1KI.10.BSB: Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you to set you on the throne of Israel. Because of the LORD’s eternal love for Israel, He has made you king to carry out justice and righteousness.”
1KI.10.KJV: Blessed be the LORD your God, which delighted in you, to set you on the throne of Israel: because the LORD loved Israel for ever, therefore made he you king, to do judgment and justice.
1KI.10.PLAIN: Blessed be the Lord your God, who has delighted in you to set you on the throne of Israel. Because of the Lord’s eternal love for Israel, He has made you king to carry out justice and righteousness.”

1KI.10.BSB: Then she gave the king 120 talents of gold, a great quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again was such an abundance of spices brought in as those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
1KI.10.KJV: And she gave the king an hundred and twenty talents of gold, and of spices very great store, and precious stones: there came no more such abundance of spices as these which the queen of Sheba gave to king Solomon.
1KI.10.PLAIN: Then she gave the king 120 talents of gold, a great quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again was such an abundance of spices brought in as those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.

1KI.10.BSB: (The fleet of Hiram that brought gold from Ophir also brought from Ophir a great cargo of almug wood and precious stones.
1KI.10.KJV: And the navy also of Hiram, that brought gold from Ophir, brought in from Ophir great plenty of almug trees, and precious stones.
1KI.10.PLAIN: (The fleet of Hiram that brought gold from Ophir also brought from Ophir a great cargo of almug wood and precious stones.

1KI.10.BSB: The king made the almug wood into steps for the house of the LORD and for the king’s palace, and into lyres and harps for the singers. Never before had such almug wood been brought in, nor has such been seen to this day.)
1KI.10.KJV: And the king made of the almug trees pillars for the house of the LORD, and for the king’s house, harps also and psalteries for singers: there came no such almug trees, nor were seen to this day.
1KI.10.PLAIN: The king made the almug wood into steps for the house of the Lord and for the king’s palace, and into lyres and harps for the singers. Never before had such almug wood been brought in, nor has such been seen to this day.)

1KI.10.BSB: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all she desired—whatever she asked—besides what he had given her out of his royal bounty. Then she left and returned to her own country, along with her servants.
1KI.10.KJV: And king Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatever she asked, beside that which Solomon gave her of his royal bounty. So she turned and went to her own country, she and her servants. ¶
1KI.10.PLAIN: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all she desired—whatever she asked—besides what he had given her out of his royal bounty. Then she left and returned to her own country, along with her servants.

1KI.10.BSB: The weight of gold that came to Solomon each year was 666 talents,
1KI.10.KJV: Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred three score and six talents of gold,
1KI.10.PLAIN: The weight of gold that came to Solomon each year was 666 talents,

1KI.10.BSB: not including the revenue from the merchants, traders, and all the Arabian kings and governors of the land.
1KI.10.KJV: Beside that he had of the merchants, and of the traffic of the spice merchants, and of all the kings of Arabia, and of the governors of the country. ¶
1KI.10.PLAIN: not including the revenue from the merchants, traders, and all the Arabian kings and governors of the land.

1KI.10.BSB: King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred shekels of gold went into each shield.
1KI.10.KJV: And king Solomon made two hundred targets of beaten gold: six hundred shekels of gold went to one target.
1KI.10.PLAIN: King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred shekels of gold went into each shield.

1KI.10.BSB: He also made three hundred small shields of hammered gold; three minas of gold went into each shield. And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
1KI.10.KJV: And he made three hundred shields of beaten gold; three pound of gold went to one shield: and the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon. ¶
1KI.10.PLAIN: He also made three hundred small shields of hammered gold; three minas of gold went into each shield. And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.

1KI.10.BSB: Additionally, the king made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.
1KI.10.KJV: Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with the best gold.
1KI.10.PLAIN: Additionally, the king made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.

1KI.10.BSB: The throne had six steps, and its back had a rounded top. There were armrests on both sides of the seat, with a lion standing beside each armrest.
1KI.10.KJV: The throne had six steps, and the top of the throne was round behind: and there were stays on either side on the place of the seat, and two lions stood beside the stays.
1KI.10.PLAIN: The throne had six steps, and its back had a rounded top. There were armrests on both sides of the seat, with a lion standing beside each armrest.

1KI.10.BSB: Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at either end of each step. Nothing like this had ever been made for any kingdom.
1KI.10.KJV: And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other on the six steps: there was not the like made in any kingdom. ¶
1KI.10.PLAIN: Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at either end of each step. Nothing like this had ever been made for any kingdom.

1KI.10.BSB: All King Solomon’s drinking cups were gold, and all the utensils of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. There was no silver, because it was accounted as nothing in the days of Solomon.
1KI.10.KJV: And all king Solomon’s drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of pure gold; none were of silver: it was nothing accounted of in the days of Solomon.
1KI.10.PLAIN: All King Solomon’s drinking cups were gold, and all the utensils of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. There was no silver, because it was accounted as nothing in the days of Solomon.

1KI.10.BSB: For the king had the ships of Tarshish at sea with Hiram’s fleet, and once every three years the ships of Tarshish would arrive bearing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
1KI.10.KJV: For the king had at sea a navy of Tharshish with the navy of Hiram: once in three years came the navy of Tharshish, bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.
1KI.10.PLAIN: For the king had the ships of Tarshish at sea with Hiram’s fleet, and once every three years the ships of Tarshish would arrive bearing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

1KI.10.BSB: So King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
1KI.10.KJV: So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and for wisdom. ¶
1KI.10.PLAIN: So King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.

1KI.10.BSB: The whole world sought an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart.
1KI.10.KJV: And all the earth sought to Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
1KI.10.PLAIN: The whole world sought an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart.

1KI.10.BSB: Year after year, each visitor would bring his tribute: articles of silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
1KI.10.KJV: And they brought every man his present, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments, and armor, and spices, horses, and mules, a rate year by year. ¶
1KI.10.PLAIN: Year after year, each visitor would bring his tribute: articles of silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.

1KI.10.BSB: Solomon accumulated 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses, which he stationed in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.
1KI.10.KJV: And Solomon gathered together chariots and horsemen: and he had a thousand and four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he bestowed in the cities for chariots, and with the king at Jerusalem.
1KI.10.PLAIN: Solomon accumulated 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses, which he stationed in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.

1KI.10.BSB: The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore in the foothills.
1KI.10.KJV: And the king made silver to be in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars made he to be as the sycomore trees that are in the vale, for abundance. ¶
1KI.10.PLAIN: The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore in the foothills.

1KI.10.BSB: Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and Kue; the royal merchants purchased them from Kue.
1KI.10.KJV: And Solomon had horses brought out of Egypt, and linen yarn: the king’s merchants received the linen yarn at a price.
1KI.10.PLAIN: Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and Kue; the royal merchants purchased them from Kue.

1KI.10.BSB: A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. Likewise, they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram.
1KI.10.KJV: And a chariot came up and went out of Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and an horse for an hundred and fifty: and so for all the kings of the Hittites, and for the kings of Syria, did they bring them out by their means.
1KI.10.PLAIN: A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. Likewise, they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram.

1KI.11.BSB: King Solomon, however, loved many foreign women along with the daughter of Pharaoh—women of Moab, Ammon, Edom, and Sidon, as well as Hittite women.
1KI.11.KJV: But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites:
1KI.11.PLAIN: King Solomon, however, loved many foreign women along with the daughter of Pharaoh—women of Moab, Ammon, Edom, and Sidon, as well as Hittite women.

1KI.11.BSB: These women were from the nations about which the LORD had told the Israelites, “You must not intermarry with them, for surely they will turn your hearts after their gods.” Yet Solomon clung to these women in love.
1KI.11.KJV: Of the nations concerning which the LORD said to the children of Israel, You shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in to you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods: Solomon joined to these in love.
1KI.11.PLAIN: These women were from the nations about which the Lord had told the Israelites, “You must not intermarry with them, for surely they will turn your hearts after their gods.” Yet Solomon clung to these women in love.

1KI.11.BSB: He had seven hundred wives of royal birth and three hundred concubines—and his wives turned his heart away.
1KI.11.KJV: And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart.
1KI.11.PLAIN: He had seven hundred wives of royal birth and three hundred concubines—and his wives turned his heart away.

1KI.11.BSB: For when Solomon grew old, his wives turned his heart after other gods, and he was not wholeheartedly devoted to the LORD his God, as his father David had been.
1KI.11.KJV: For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father.
1KI.11.PLAIN: For when Solomon grew old, his wives turned his heart after other gods, and he was not wholeheartedly devoted to the Lord his God, as his father David had been.

1KI.11.BSB: Solomon followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
1KI.11.KJV: For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
1KI.11.PLAIN: Solomon followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.

1KI.11.BSB: So Solomon did evil in the sight of the LORD; unlike his father David, he did not follow the LORD completely.
1KI.11.KJV: And Solomon did evil in the sight of the LORD, and went not fully after the LORD, as did David his father.
1KI.11.PLAIN: So Solomon did evil in the sight of the Lord; unlike his father David, he did not follow the Lord completely.

1KI.11.BSB: At that time on a hill east of Jerusalem, Solomon built a high place for Chemosh the abomination of Moab and for Molech the abomination of the Ammonites.
1KI.11.KJV: Then did Solomon build an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, in the hill that is before Jerusalem, and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.
1KI.11.PLAIN: At that time on a hill east of Jerusalem, Solomon built a high place for Chemosh the abomination of Moab and for Molech the abomination of the Ammonites.

1KI.11.BSB: He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods.
1KI.11.KJV: And likewise did he for all his strange wives, which burnt incense and sacrificed to their gods. ¶
1KI.11.PLAIN: He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods.

1KI.11.BSB: Now the LORD grew angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice.
1KI.11.KJV: And the LORD was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the LORD God of Israel, which had appeared to him twice,
1KI.11.PLAIN: Now the Lord grew angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the Lord, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice.

1KI.11.BSB: Although He had warned Solomon explicitly not to follow other gods, Solomon did not keep the LORD’s command.
1KI.11.KJV: And had commanded him concerning this thing, that he should not go after other gods: but he kept not that which the LORD commanded.
1KI.11.PLAIN: Although He had warned Solomon explicitly not to follow other gods, Solomon did not keep the Lord’s command.

1KI.11.BSB: Then the LORD said to Solomon, “Because you have done this and have not kept My covenant and My statutes, which I have commanded you, I will tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.
1KI.11.KJV: Why the LORD said to Solomon, For as much as this is done of you, and you have not kept my covenant and my statutes, which I have commanded you, I will surely rend the kingdom from you, and will give it to your servant.
1KI.11.PLAIN: Then the Lord said to Solomon, “Because you have done this and have not kept My covenant and My statutes, which I have commanded you, I will tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.

1KI.11.BSB: Nevertheless, for the sake of your father David, I will not do it during your lifetime; I will tear it out of the hand of your son.
1KI.11.KJV: Notwithstanding in your days I will not do it for David your father’s sake: but I will rend it out of the hand of your son.
1KI.11.PLAIN: Nevertheless, for the sake of your father David, I will not do it during your lifetime; I will tear it out of the hand of your son.

1KI.11.BSB: Yet I will not tear the whole kingdom away from him. I will give one tribe to your son for the sake of My servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen.”
1KI.11.KJV: However, I will not rend away all the kingdom; but will give one tribe to your son for David my servant’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake which I have chosen. ¶
1KI.11.PLAIN: Yet I will not tear the whole kingdom away from him. I will give one tribe to your son for the sake of My servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen.”

1KI.11.BSB: Then the LORD raised up against Solomon an adversary, Hadad the Edomite, from the royal line of Edom.
1KI.11.KJV: And the LORD stirred up an adversary to Solomon, Hadad the Edomite: he was of the king’s seed in Edom.
1KI.11.PLAIN: Then the Lord raised up against Solomon an adversary, Hadad the Edomite, from the royal line of Edom.

1KI.11.BSB: Earlier, when David was in Edom, Joab the commander of the army had gone to bury the dead and had struck down every male in Edom.
1KI.11.KJV: For it came to pass, when David was in Edom, and Joab the captain of the host was gone up to bury the slain, after he had smitten every male in Edom;
1KI.11.PLAIN: Earlier, when David was in Edom, Joab the commander of the army had gone to bury the dead and had struck down every male in Edom.

1KI.11.BSB: Joab and all Israel had stayed there six months, until he had killed every male in Edom.
1KI.11.KJV: (For six months did Joab remain there with all Israel, until he had cut off every male in Edom:)
1KI.11.PLAIN: Joab and all Israel had stayed there six months, until he had killed every male in Edom.

1KI.11.BSB: But Hadad, still just a young boy, had fled to Egypt, along with some Edomites who were servants of his father.
1KI.11.KJV: That Hadad fled, he and certain Edomites of his father’s servants with him, to go into Egypt; Hadad being yet a little child.
1KI.11.PLAIN: But Hadad, still just a young boy, had fled to Egypt, along with some Edomites who were servants of his father.

1KI.11.BSB: Hadad and his men set out from Midian and went to Paran. They took men from Paran with them and went to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave Hadad a house and land and provided him with food.
1KI.11.KJV: And they arose out of Midian, and came to Paran: and they took men with them out of Paran, and they came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt; which gave him an house, and appointed him victuals, and gave him land.
1KI.11.PLAIN: Hadad and his men set out from Midian and went to Paran. They took men from Paran with them and went to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave Hadad a house and land and provided him with food.

1KI.11.BSB: There Hadad found such great favor in the sight of Pharaoh that he gave to him in marriage the sister of Queen Tahpenes, his own wife.
1KI.11.KJV: And Hadad found great favor in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him to wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
1KI.11.PLAIN: There Hadad found such great favor in the sight of Pharaoh that he gave to him in marriage the sister of Queen Tahpenes, his own wife.

1KI.11.BSB: And the sister of Tahpenes bore Hadad a son named Genubath. Tahpenes herself weaned him in Pharaoh’s palace, and Genubath lived there among the sons of Pharaoh.
1KI.11.KJV: And the sister of Tahpenes bore him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh’s house: and Genubath was in Pharaoh’s household among the sons of Pharaoh.
1KI.11.PLAIN: And the sister of Tahpenes bore Hadad a son named Genubath. Tahpenes herself weaned him in Pharaoh’s palace, and Genubath lived there among the sons of Pharaoh.

1KI.11.BSB: When Hadad heard in Egypt that David had rested with his fathers and that Joab, the commander of the army, was dead, he said to Pharaoh, “Let me go, that I may return to my own country.”
1KI.11.KJV: And when Hadad heard in Egypt that David slept with his fathers, and that Joab the captain of the host was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, Let me depart, that I may go to my own country.
1KI.11.PLAIN: When Hadad heard in Egypt that David had rested with his fathers and that Joab, the commander of the army, was dead, he said to Pharaoh, “Let me go, that I may return to my own country.”

1KI.11.BSB: But Pharaoh asked him, “What have you lacked here with me that you suddenly want to go back to your own country?” “Nothing,” Hadad replied, “but please let me go.”
1KI.11.KJV: Then Pharaoh said to him, But what have you lacked with me, that, behold, you seek to go to your own country? And he answered, Nothing: however, let me go in any wise. ¶
1KI.11.PLAIN: But Pharaoh asked him, “What have you lacked here with me that you suddenly want to go back to your own country?” “Nothing,” Hadad replied, “but please let me go.”

1KI.11.BSB: And God raised up against Solomon another adversary, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from his master, Hadadezer king of Zobah,
1KI.11.KJV: And God stirred him up another adversary, Rezon the son of Eliadah, which fled from his lord Hadadezer king of Zobah:
1KI.11.PLAIN: And God raised up against Solomon another adversary, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from his master, Hadadezer king of Zobah,

1KI.11.BSB: and had gathered men to himself. When David killed the Zobaites, Rezon captained a band of raiders and went to Damascus, where they settled and gained control.
1KI.11.KJV: And he gathered men to him, and became captain over a band, when David slew them of Zobah: and they went to Damascus, and dwelled therein, and reigned in Damascus.
1KI.11.PLAIN: and had gathered men to himself. When David killed the Zobaites, Rezon captained a band of raiders and went to Damascus, where they settled and gained control.

1KI.11.BSB: Rezon was Israel’s enemy throughout the days of Solomon, adding to the trouble caused by Hadad. So Rezon ruled over Aram with hostility toward Israel.
1KI.11.KJV: And he was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, beside the mischief that Hadad did: and he abhorred Israel, and reigned over Syria. ¶
1KI.11.PLAIN: Rezon was Israel’s enemy throughout the days of Solomon, adding to the trouble caused by Hadad. So Rezon ruled over Aram with hostility toward Israel.

1KI.11.BSB: Now Jeroboam son of Nebat was an Ephraimite from Zeredah whose mother was a widow named Zeruah. Jeroboam was a servant of Solomon, but he rebelled against the king,
1KI.11.KJV: And Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephrathite of Zereda, Solomon’s servant, whose mother’s name was Zeruah, a widow woman, even he lifted up his hand against the king.
1KI.11.PLAIN: Now Jeroboam son of Nebat was an Ephraimite from Zeredah whose mother was a widow named Zeruah. Jeroboam was a servant of Solomon, but he rebelled against the king,

1KI.11.BSB: and this is the account of his rebellion against the king. Solomon had built the supporting terraces and repaired the gap in the wall of the city of his father David.
1KI.11.KJV: And this was the cause that he lifted up his hand against the king: Solomon built Millo, and repaired the breaches of the city of David his father.
1KI.11.PLAIN: and this is the account of his rebellion against the king. Solomon had built the supporting terraces and repaired the gap in the wall of the city of his father David.

1KI.11.BSB: Now Jeroboam was a mighty man of valor. So when Solomon noticed that the young man was industrious, he put him in charge of the whole labor force of the house of Joseph.
1KI.11.KJV: And the man Jeroboam was a mighty man of valor: and Solomon seeing the young man that he was industrious, he made him ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph.
1KI.11.PLAIN: Now Jeroboam was a mighty man of valor. So when Solomon noticed that the young man was industrious, he put him in charge of the whole labor force of the house of Joseph.

1KI.11.BSB: During that time, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met Jeroboam on the road as he was going out of Jerusalem. Now Ahijah had wrapped himself in a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the open field.
1KI.11.KJV: And it came to pass at that time when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, that the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him in the way; and he had clad himself with a new garment; and they two were alone in the field:
1KI.11.PLAIN: During that time, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met Jeroboam on the road as he was going out of Jerusalem. Now Ahijah had wrapped himself in a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the open field.

1KI.11.BSB: And Ahijah took hold of the new cloak he was wearing, tore it into twelve pieces,
1KI.11.KJV: And Ahijah caught the new garment that was on him, and rent it in twelve pieces:
1KI.11.PLAIN: And Ahijah took hold of the new cloak he was wearing, tore it into twelve pieces,

1KI.11.BSB: and said to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces for yourself, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Behold, I will tear the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and I will give you ten tribes.
1KI.11.KJV: And he said to Jeroboam, Take you ten pieces: for thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to you:
1KI.11.PLAIN: and said to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces for yourself, for this is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: ‘Look closely — I will tear the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and I will give you ten tribes.

1KI.11.BSB: But one tribe will remain for the sake of My servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.
1KI.11.KJV: (But he shall have one tribe for my servant David’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel:)
1KI.11.PLAIN: But one tribe will remain for the sake of My servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.

1KI.11.BSB: For they have forsaken Me to worship Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites. They have not walked in My ways, nor done what is right in My eyes, nor kept My statutes and judgments, as Solomon’s father David did.
1KI.11.KJV: Because that they have forsaken me, and have worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon, and have not walked in my ways, to do that which is right in my eyes, and to keep my statutes and my judgments, as did David his father.
1KI.11.PLAIN: For they have forsaken Me to worship Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites. They have not walked in My ways, nor done what is right in My eyes, nor kept My statutes and judgments, as Solomon’s father David did.

1KI.11.BSB: Nevertheless, I will not take the whole kingdom out of Solomon’s hand, because I have made him ruler all the days of his life for the sake of David My servant, whom I chose because he kept My commandments and statutes.
1KI.11.KJV: However, I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand: but I will make him prince all the days of his life for David my servant’s sake, whom I chose, because he kept my commandments and my statutes:
1KI.11.PLAIN: Nevertheless, I will not take the whole kingdom out of Solomon’s hand, because I have made him ruler all the days of his life for the sake of David My servant, whom I chose because he kept My commandments and statutes.

1KI.11.BSB: But I will take ten tribes of the kingdom from the hand of his son and give them to you.
1KI.11.KJV: But I will take the kingdom out of his son’s hand, and will give it to you, even ten tribes.
1KI.11.PLAIN: But I will take ten tribes of the kingdom from the hand of his son and give them to you.

1KI.11.BSB: I will give one tribe to his son, so that My servant David will always have a lamp before Me in Jerusalem, the city where I chose to put My Name.
1KI.11.KJV: And to his son will I give one tribe, that David my servant may have a light always before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen me to put my name there.
1KI.11.PLAIN: I will give one tribe to his son, so that My servant David will always have a lamp before Me in Jerusalem, the city where I chose to put My Name.

1KI.11.BSB: But as for you, I will take you, and you shall reign over all that your heart desires, and you will be king over Israel.
1KI.11.KJV: And I will take you, and you shall reign according to all that your soul desires, and shall be king over Israel.
1KI.11.PLAIN: But as for you, I will take you, and you shall reign over all that your heart desires, and you will be king over Israel.

1KI.11.BSB: If you listen to all that I command you, walk in My ways, and do what is right in My sight in order to keep My statutes and commandments as My servant David did, then I will be with you. I will build you a lasting dynasty just as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.
1KI.11.KJV: And it shall be, if you will listen to all that I command you, and will walk in my ways, and do that is right in my sight, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did; that I will be with you, and build you a sure house, as I built for David, and will give Israel to you.
1KI.11.PLAIN: If you listen to all that I command you, walk in My ways, and do what is right in My sight in order to keep My statutes and commandments as My servant David did, then I will be with you. I will build you a lasting dynasty just as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.

1KI.11.BSB: Because of this, I will humble David’s descendants—but not forever.’”
1KI.11.KJV: And I will for this afflict the seed of David, but not for ever.
1KI.11.PLAIN: Because of this, I will humble David’s descendants—but not forever.’”

1KI.11.BSB: Solomon therefore sought to kill Jeroboam. But Jeroboam arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, where he remained until the death of Solomon.
1KI.11.KJV: Solomon sought therefore to kill Jeroboam. And Jeroboam arose, and fled into Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and was in Egypt until the death of Solomon. ¶
1KI.11.PLAIN: Solomon therefore sought to kill Jeroboam. But Jeroboam arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, where he remained until the death of Solomon.

1KI.11.BSB: As for the rest of the acts of Solomon—all that he did, as well as his wisdom—are they not written in the Book of the Acts of Solomon?
1KI.11.KJV: And the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?
1KI.11.PLAIN: As for the rest of the acts of Solomon—all that he did, as well as his wisdom—are they not written in the Book of the Acts of Solomon?

1KI.11.BSB: Thus the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
1KI.11.KJV: And the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
1KI.11.PLAIN: Thus the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.

1KI.11.BSB: And Solomon rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of his father David. And his son Rehoboam reigned in his place.
1KI.11.KJV: And Solomon slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David his father: and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.
1KI.11.PLAIN: And Solomon rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of his father David. And his son Rehoboam reigned in his place.

1KI.12.BSB: Then Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had gone there to make him king.
1KI.12.KJV: And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king.
1KI.12.PLAIN: Then Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had gone there to make him king.

1KI.12.BSB: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about this, he was still in Egypt where he had fled from King Solomon and had been living ever since.
1KI.12.KJV: And it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who was yet in Egypt, heard of it, (for he was fled from the presence of king Solomon, and Jeroboam dwelled in Egypt;)
1KI.12.PLAIN: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about this, he was still in Egypt where he had fled from King Solomon and had been living ever since.

1KI.12.BSB: So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and the whole assembly of Israel came to Rehoboam and said,
1KI.12.KJV: That they sent and called him. And Jeroboam and all the congregation of Israel came, and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
1KI.12.PLAIN: So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and the whole assembly of Israel came to Rehoboam and said,

1KI.12.BSB: “Your father put a heavy yoke on us. But now you should lighten the burden of your father’s service and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.”
1KI.12.KJV: Your father made our yoke grievous: now therefore make you the grievous service of your father, and his heavy yoke which he put on us, lighter, and we will serve you.
1KI.12.PLAIN: “Your father put a heavy yoke on us. But now you should lighten the burden of your father’s service and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.”

1KI.12.BSB: Rehoboam answered, “Go away for three days and then return to me.” So the people departed.
1KI.12.KJV: And he said to them, Depart yet for three days, then come again to me. And the people departed. ¶
1KI.12.PLAIN: Rehoboam answered, “Go away for three days and then return to me.” So the people departed.

1KI.12.BSB: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. “How do you advise me to respond to these people?” he asked.
1KI.12.KJV: And king Rehoboam consulted with the old men, that stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, and said, How do you advise that I may answer this people?
1KI.12.PLAIN: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. “How do you advise me to respond to these people?” he asked.

1KI.12.BSB: They replied, “If you will be a servant to these people and serve them this day, and if you will respond by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.”
1KI.12.KJV: And they spoke to him, saying, If you will be a servant to this people this day, and will serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be your servants for ever.
1KI.12.PLAIN: They replied, “If you will be a servant to these people and serve them this day, and if you will respond by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.”

1KI.12.BSB: But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders; instead, he consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him.
1KI.12.KJV: But he forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him, and which stood before him:
1KI.12.PLAIN: But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders; instead, he consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him.

1KI.12.BSB: He asked them, “What message do you advise that we send back to these people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”
1KI.12.KJV: And he said to them, What counsel give you that we may answer this people, who have spoken to me, saying, Make the yoke which your father did put on us lighter?
1KI.12.PLAIN: He asked them, “What message do you advise that we send back to these people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”

1KI.12.BSB: The young men who had grown up with him replied, “This is how you should answer these people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you should make it lighter.’ This is what you should tell them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!
1KI.12.KJV: And the young men that were grown up with him spoke to him, saying, Thus shall you speak to this people that spoke to you, saying, Your father made our yoke heavy, but make you it lighter to us; thus shall you say to them, My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins.
1KI.12.PLAIN: The young men who had grown up with him replied, “This is how you should answer these people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you should make it lighter.’ This is what you should tell them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!

1KI.12.BSB: Whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.’”
1KI.12.KJV: And now whereas my father did lade you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke: my father has chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions. ¶
1KI.12.PLAIN: Whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.’”

1KI.12.BSB: After three days, Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, since the king had said, “Come back to me on the third day.”
1KI.12.KJV: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam the third day, as the king had appointed, saying, Come to me again the third day.
1KI.12.PLAIN: After three days, Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, since the king had said, “Come back to me on the third day.”

1KI.12.BSB: And the king answered the people harshly. He rejected the advice of the elders
1KI.12.KJV: And the king answered the people roughly, and forsook the old men’s counsel that they gave him;
1KI.12.PLAIN: And the king answered the people harshly. He rejected the advice of the elders

1KI.12.BSB: and spoke to them as the young men had advised, saying, “Whereas my father made your yoke heavy, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.”
1KI.12.KJV: And spoke to them after the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke: my father also chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
1KI.12.PLAIN: and spoke to them as the young men had advised, saying, “Whereas my father made your yoke heavy, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.”

1KI.12.BSB: So the king did not listen to the people, and indeed this turn of events was from the LORD, to fulfill the word He had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah the Shilonite.
1KI.12.KJV: Why the king listened not to the people; for the cause was from the LORD, that he might perform his saying, which the LORD spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat. ¶
1KI.12.PLAIN: So the king did not listen to the people, and indeed this turn of events was from the Lord, to fulfill the word He had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah the Shilonite.

1KI.12.BSB: When all Israel saw that the king had refused to listen to them, they answered the king: “What portion do we have in David, and what inheritance in the son of Jesse? To your tents, O Israel! Look now to your own house, O David!” So the Israelites went home,
1KI.12.KJV: So when all Israel saw that the king listened not to them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to your own house, David. So Israel departed to their tents.
1KI.12.PLAIN: When all Israel saw that the king had refused to listen to them, they answered the king: “What portion do we have in David, and what inheritance in the son of Jesse? To your tents, O Israel! Look now to your own house, O David!” So the Israelites went home,

1KI.12.BSB: but Rehoboam still reigned over the Israelites living in the cities of Judah.
1KI.12.KJV: But as for the children of Israel which dwelled in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.
1KI.12.PLAIN: but Rehoboam still reigned over the Israelites living in the cities of Judah.

1KI.12.BSB: Then King Rehoboam sent out Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. And King Rehoboam mounted his chariot in haste and escaped to Jerusalem.
1KI.12.KJV: Then king Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tribute; and all Israel stoned him with stones, that he died. Therefore king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.
1KI.12.PLAIN: Then King Rehoboam sent out Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. And King Rehoboam mounted his chariot in haste and escaped to Jerusalem.

1KI.12.BSB: So to this day Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David.
1KI.12.KJV: So Israel rebelled against the house of David to this day.
1KI.12.PLAIN: So to this day Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David.

1KI.12.BSB: When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they summoned him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. Only the tribe of Judah followed the house of David.
1KI.12.KJV: And it came to pass, when all Israel heard that Jeroboam was come again, that they sent and called him to the congregation, and made him king over all Israel: there was none that followed the house of David, but the tribe of Judah only. ¶
1KI.12.PLAIN: When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they summoned him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. Only the tribe of Judah followed the house of David.

1KI.12.BSB: And when Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he mobilized the whole house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin—180,000 chosen warriors—to fight against the house of Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
1KI.12.KJV: And when Rehoboam was come to Jerusalem, he assembled all the house of Judah, with the tribe of Benjamin, an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men, which were warriors, to fight against the house of Israel, to bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.
1KI.12.PLAIN: And when Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he mobilized the whole house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin—180,000 chosen warriors—to fight against the house of Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.

1KI.12.BSB: But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God:
1KI.12.KJV: But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
1KI.12.PLAIN: But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God:

1KI.12.BSB: “Tell Rehoboam son of Solomon king of Judah, all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and the rest of the people
1KI.12.KJV: Speak to Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the remnant of the people, saying,
1KI.12.PLAIN: “Tell Rehoboam son of Solomon king of Judah, all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and the rest of the people

1KI.12.BSB: that this is what the LORD says: ‘You are not to go up and fight against your brothers, the Israelites. Each of you must return home, for this word is from Me.’” So they listened to the word of the LORD and turned back according to the word of the LORD.
1KI.12.KJV: Thus says the LORD, You shall not go up, nor fight against your brothers the children of Israel: return every man to his house; for this thing is from me. They listened therefore to the word of the LORD, and returned to depart, according to the word of the LORD. ¶
1KI.12.PLAIN: that this is what the Lord says: ‘You are not to go up and fight against your brothers, the Israelites. Each of you must return home, for this word is from Me.’” So they listened to the word of the Lord and turned back according to the word of the Lord.

1KI.12.BSB: Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. And from there he went out and built Penuel.
1KI.12.KJV: Then Jeroboam built Shechem in mount Ephraim, and dwelled therein; and went out from there, and built Penuel.
1KI.12.PLAIN: Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. And from there he went out and built Penuel.

1KI.12.BSB: Jeroboam said in his heart, “Now the kingdom might revert to the house of David.
1KI.12.KJV: And Jeroboam said in his heart, Now shall the kingdom return to the house of David:
1KI.12.PLAIN: Jeroboam said in his heart, “Now the kingdom might revert to the house of David.

1KI.12.BSB: If these people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of the LORD at Jerusalem, their hearts will return to their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah; then they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.”
1KI.12.KJV: If this people go up to do sacrifice in the house of the LORD at Jerusalem, then shall the heart of this people turn again to their lord, even to Rehoboam king of Judah, and they shall kill me, and go again to Rehoboam king of Judah.
1KI.12.PLAIN: If these people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, their hearts will return to their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah; then they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.”

1KI.12.BSB: After seeking advice, the king made two golden calves and said to the people, “Going up to Jerusalem is too much for you. Here, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.”
1KI.12.KJV: Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said to them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold your gods, O Israel, which brought you up out of the land of Egypt.
