1KI.16.PLAIN: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel, and he reigned in Tirzah two years.

1KI.16.BSB: However, while Elah was in Tirzah getting drunk in the house of Arza the steward of his household there, Elah’s servant Zimri, the commander of half his chariots, conspired against him.
1KI.16.KJV: And his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspired against him, as he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza steward of his house in Tirzah.
1KI.16.PLAIN: However, while Elah was in Tirzah getting drunk in the house of Arza the steward of his household there, Elah’s servant Zimri, the commander of half his chariots, conspired against him.

1KI.16.BSB: So in the twenty-seventh year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Zimri went in, struck Elah down, and killed him. And Zimri reigned in his place.
1KI.16.KJV: And Zimri went in and smote him, and killed him, in the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his stead. ¶
1KI.16.PLAIN: So in the twenty-seventh year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Zimri went in, struck Elah down, and killed him. And Zimri reigned in his place.

1KI.16.BSB: As soon as Zimri began to reign and was seated on the throne, he struck down the entire household of Baasha. He did not leave a single male, whether a kinsman or friend.
1KI.16.KJV: And it came to pass, when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, that he slew all the house of Baasha: he left him not one that urinates against a wall, neither of his kinfolks, nor of his friends.
1KI.16.PLAIN: As soon as Zimri began to reign and was seated on the throne, he struck down the entire household of Baasha. He did not leave a single male, whether a kinsman or friend.

1KI.16.BSB: So Zimri destroyed the entire household of Baasha, according to the word that the LORD had spoken against Baasha through Jehu the prophet.
1KI.16.KJV: Thus did Zimri destroy all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the LORD, which he spoke against Baasha by Jehu the prophet.
1KI.16.PLAIN: So Zimri destroyed the entire household of Baasha, according to the word that the Lord had spoken against Baasha through Jehu the prophet.

1KI.16.BSB: This happened because of all the sins Baasha and his son Elah had committed and had caused Israel to commit, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.
1KI.16.KJV: For all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, by which they sinned, and by which they made Israel to sin, in provoking the LORD God of Israel to anger with their vanities.
1KI.16.PLAIN: This happened because of all the sins Baasha and his son Elah had committed and had caused Israel to commit, provoking the Lord, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.

1KI.16.BSB: As for the rest of the acts of Elah, along with all his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
1KI.16.KJV: Now the rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? ¶
1KI.16.PLAIN: As for the rest of the acts of Elah, along with all his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

1KI.16.BSB: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Zimri reigned in Tirzah for seven days. Now the troops were encamped against Gibbethon of the Philistines,
1KI.16.KJV: In the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah did Zimri reign seven days in Tirzah. And the people were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
1KI.16.PLAIN: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Zimri reigned in Tirzah for seven days. Now the troops were encamped against Gibbethon of the Philistines,

1KI.16.BSB: and the people in the camp heard that Zimri had not only conspired but had also struck down the king. So there in the camp that very day, all Israel proclaimed Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel.
1KI.16.KJV: And the people that were encamped heard say, Zimri has conspired, and has also slain the king: why all Israel made Omri, the captain of the host, king over Israel that day in the camp.
1KI.16.PLAIN: and the people in the camp heard that Zimri had not only conspired but had also struck down the king. So there in the camp that very day, all Israel proclaimed Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel.

1KI.16.BSB: Then Omri and all the Israelites marched up from Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah.
1KI.16.KJV: And Omri went up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they besieged Tirzah.
1KI.16.PLAIN: Then Omri and all the Israelites marched up from Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah.

1KI.16.BSB: When Zimri saw that the city was captured, he entered the citadel of the royal palace and burned it down upon himself. So he died
1KI.16.KJV: And it came to pass, when Zimri saw that the city was taken, that he went into the palace of the king’s house, and burnt the king’s house over him with fire, and died.
1KI.16.PLAIN: When Zimri saw that the city was captured, he entered the citadel of the royal palace and burned it down upon himself. So he died

1KI.16.BSB: because of the sins he had committed, doing evil in the sight of the LORD and following the example of Jeroboam and the sin he had committed and had caused Israel to commit.
1KI.16.KJV: For his sins which he sinned in doing evil in the sight of the LORD, in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin which he did, to make Israel to sin.
1KI.16.PLAIN: because of the sins he had committed, doing evil in the sight of the Lord and following the example of Jeroboam and the sin he had committed and had caused Israel to commit.

1KI.16.BSB: As for the rest of the acts of Zimri and the treason he committed, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
1KI.16.KJV: Now the rest of the acts of Zimri, and his treason that he worked, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? ¶
1KI.16.PLAIN: As for the rest of the acts of Zimri and the treason he committed, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

1KI.16.BSB: At that time the people of Israel were divided: Half of the people supported Tibni son of Ginath as king, and half supported Omri.
1KI.16.KJV: Then were the people of Israel divided into two parts: half of the people followed Tibni the son of Ginath, to make him king; and half followed Omri.
1KI.16.PLAIN: At that time the people of Israel were divided: Half of the people supported Tibni son of Ginath as king, and half supported Omri.

1KI.16.BSB: But the followers of Omri proved stronger than those of Tibni son of Ginath. So Tibni died and Omri became king.
1KI.16.KJV: But the people that followed Omri prevailed against the people that followed Tibni the son of Ginath: so Tibni died, and Omri reigned. ¶
1KI.16.PLAIN: But the followers of Omri proved stronger than those of Tibni son of Ginath. So Tibni died and Omri became king.

1KI.16.BSB: In the thirty-first year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Omri became king of Israel, and he reigned twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.
1KI.16.KJV: In the thirty and first year of Asa king of Judah began Omri to reign over Israel, twelve years: six years reigned he in Tirzah.
1KI.16.PLAIN: In the thirty-first year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Omri became king of Israel, and he reigned twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.

1KI.16.BSB: He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver and built a city there, calling it Samaria after the name of Shemer, who had owned the hill.
1KI.16.KJV: And he bought the hill Samaria of Shemer for two talents of silver, and built on the hill, and called the name of the city which he built, after the name of Shemer, owner of the hill, Samaria. ¶
1KI.16.PLAIN: He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver and built a city there, calling it Samaria after the name of Shemer, who had owned the hill.

1KI.16.BSB: But Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD and acted more wickedly than all who were before him.
1KI.16.KJV: But Omri worked evil in the eyes of the LORD, and did worse than all that were before him.
1KI.16.PLAIN: But Omri did evil in the sight of the Lord and acted more wickedly than all who were before him.

1KI.16.BSB: For he walked in all the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins, which he caused Israel to commit, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.
1KI.16.KJV: For he walked in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and in his sin with which he made Israel to sin, to provoke the LORD God of Israel to anger with their vanities.
1KI.16.PLAIN: For he walked in all the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins, which he caused Israel to commit, provoking the Lord, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.

1KI.16.BSB: As for the rest of the acts of Omri, along with his accomplishments and the might he exercised, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
1KI.16.KJV: Now the rest of the acts of Omri which he did, and his might that he showed, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
1KI.16.PLAIN: As for the rest of the acts of Omri, along with his accomplishments and the might he exercised, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

1KI.16.BSB: And Omri rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab reigned in his place.
1KI.16.KJV: So Omri slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria: and Ahab his son reigned in his stead. ¶
1KI.16.PLAIN: And Omri rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab reigned in his place.

1KI.16.BSB: In the thirty-eighth year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria twenty-two years.
1KI.16.KJV: And in the thirty and eighth year of Asa king of Judah began Ahab the son of Omri to reign over Israel: and Ahab the son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty and two years.
1KI.16.PLAIN: In the thirty-eighth year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria twenty-two years.

1KI.16.BSB: However, Ahab son of Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD, more than all who were before him.
1KI.16.KJV: And Ahab the son of Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD above all that were before him.
1KI.16.PLAIN: However, Ahab son of Omri did evil in the sight of the Lord, more than all who were before him.

1KI.16.BSB: And as if it were not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he even married Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and he then proceeded to serve and worship Baal.
1KI.16.KJV: And it came to pass, as if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, that he took to wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal, and worshipped him.
1KI.16.PLAIN: And as if it were not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he even married Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and he then proceeded to serve and worship Baal.

1KI.16.BSB: First, Ahab set up an altar for Baal in the temple of Baal that he had built in Samaria.
1KI.16.KJV: And he reared up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal, which he had built in Samaria.
1KI.16.PLAIN: First, Ahab set up an altar for Baal in the temple of Baal that he had built in Samaria.

1KI.16.BSB: Then he set up an Asherah pole. Thus Ahab did more to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel before him.
1KI.16.KJV: And Ahab made a grove; and Ahab did more to provoke the LORD God of Israel to anger than all the kings of Israel that were before him. ¶
1KI.16.PLAIN: Then he set up an Asherah pole. Thus Ahab did more to provoke the Lord, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel before him.

1KI.16.BSB: In Ahab’s days, Hiel the Bethelite rebuilt Jericho. At the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and at the cost of Segub his youngest he set up its gates, according to the word that the LORD had spoken through Joshua son of Nun.
1KI.16.KJV: In his days did Hiel the Bethelite build Jericho: he laid the foundation thereof in Abiram his firstborn, and set up the gates thereof in his youngest son Segub, according to the word of the LORD, which he spoke by Joshua the son of Nun.
1KI.16.PLAIN: In Ahab’s days, Hiel the Bethelite rebuilt Jericho. At the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and at the cost of Segub his youngest he set up its gates, according to the word that the Lord had spoken through Joshua son of Nun.

1KI.17.BSB: Now Elijah the Tishbite, who was among the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, “As surely as the LORD lives—the God of Israel before whom I stand—there will be neither dew nor rain in these years except at my word!”
1KI.17.KJV: And Elijah the Tishbite, who was of the inhabitants of Gilead, said to Ahab, As the LORD God of Israel lives, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word.
1KI.17.PLAIN: Now Elijah the Tishbite, who was among the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, “As surely as the Lord lives—the God of Israel before whom I stand—there will be neither dew nor rain in these years except at my word!”

1KI.17.BSB: Then a revelation from the LORD came to Elijah:
1KI.17.KJV: And the word of the LORD came to him, saying,
1KI.17.PLAIN: Then a revelation from the Lord came to Elijah:

1KI.17.BSB: “Leave here, turn eastward, and hide yourself by the Brook of Cherith, east of the Jordan.
1KI.17.KJV: Get you hence, and turn you eastward, and hide yourself by the brook Cherith, that is before Jordan.
1KI.17.PLAIN: “Leave here, turn eastward, and hide yourself by the Brook of Cherith, east of the Jordan.

1KI.17.BSB: And you are to drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.”
1KI.17.KJV: And it shall be, that you shall drink of the brook; and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.
1KI.17.PLAIN: And you are to drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.”

1KI.17.BSB: So Elijah did what the LORD had told him, and he went and lived by the Brook of Cherith, east of the Jordan.
1KI.17.KJV: So he went and did according to the word of the LORD: for he went and dwelled by the brook Cherith, that is before Jordan.
1KI.17.PLAIN: So Elijah did what the Lord had told him, and he went and lived by the Brook of Cherith, east of the Jordan.

1KI.17.BSB: The ravens would bring him bread and meat in the morning and evening, and he would drink from the brook.
1KI.17.KJV: And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the brook.
1KI.17.PLAIN: The ravens would bring him bread and meat in the morning and evening, and he would drink from the brook.

1KI.17.BSB: Some time later, however, the brook dried up because there had been no rain in the land.
1KI.17.KJV: And it came to pass after a while, that the brook dried up, because there had been no rain in the land. ¶
1KI.17.PLAIN: Some time later, however, the brook dried up because there had been no rain in the land.

1KI.17.BSB: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah:
1KI.17.KJV: And the word of the LORD came to him, saying,
1KI.17.PLAIN: Then the word of the Lord came to Elijah:

1KI.17.BSB: “Get up and go to Zarephath of Sidon, and stay there. Behold, I have commanded a widow there to provide for you.”
1KI.17.KJV: Arise, get you to Zarephath, which belongs to Zidon, and dwell there: behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain you.
1KI.17.PLAIN: “Get up and go to Zarephath of Sidon, and stay there. Look closely — I have commanded a widow there to provide for you.”

1KI.17.BSB: So Elijah got up and went to Zarephath. When he arrived at the city gate, there was a widow gathering sticks. Elijah called to her and said, “Please bring me a little water in a cup, so that I may drink.”
1KI.17.KJV: So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman was there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray you, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.
1KI.17.PLAIN: So Elijah got up and went to Zarephath. When he arrived at the city gate, there was a widow gathering sticks. Elijah called to her and said, “Please bring me a little water in a cup, so that I may drink.”

1KI.17.BSB: And as she was going to get it, he called to her and said, “Please bring me a piece of bread.”
1KI.17.KJV: And as she was going to fetch it, he called to her, and said, Bring me, I pray you, a morsel of bread in your hand.
1KI.17.PLAIN: And as she was going to get it, he called to her and said, “Please bring me a piece of bread.”

1KI.17.BSB: But she replied, “As surely as the LORD your God lives, I have no bread—only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. Look, I am gathering a couple of sticks to take home and prepare a meal for myself and my son, so that we may eat it and die.”
1KI.17.KJV: And she said, As the LORD your God lives, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.
1KI.17.PLAIN: But she replied, “As surely as the Lord your God lives, I have no bread—only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. Look, I am gathering a couple of sticks to take home and prepare a meal for myself and my son, so that we may eat it and die.”

1KI.17.BSB: “Do not be afraid,” Elijah said to her. “Go and do as you have said. But first make me a small cake of bread from what you have, and bring it out to me. Afterward, make some for yourself and your son,
1KI.17.KJV: And Elijah said to her, Fear not; go and do as you have said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it to me, and after make for you and for your son.
1KI.17.PLAIN: “Do not be afraid,” Elijah said to her. “Go and do as you have said. But first make me a small cake of bread from what you have, and bring it out to me. Afterward, make some for yourself and your son,

1KI.17.BSB: for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘The jar of flour will not be exhausted and the jug of oil will not run dry until the day the LORD sends rain upon the face of the earth.’”
1KI.17.KJV: For thus says the LORD God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the LORD sends rain on the earth.
1KI.17.PLAIN: for this is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: ‘The jar of flour will not be exhausted and the jug of oil will not run dry until the day the Lord sends rain upon the face of the earth.’”

1KI.17.BSB: So she went and did according to the word of Elijah, and there was food every day for Elijah and the woman and her household.
1KI.17.KJV: And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days.
1KI.17.PLAIN: So she went and did according to the word of Elijah, and there was food every day for Elijah and the woman and her household.

1KI.17.BSB: The jar of flour was not exhausted and the jug of oil did not run dry, according to the word that the LORD had spoken through Elijah.
1KI.17.KJV: And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the LORD, which he spoke by Elijah. ¶
1KI.17.PLAIN: The jar of flour was not exhausted and the jug of oil did not run dry, according to the word that the Lord had spoken through Elijah.

1KI.17.BSB: Later, the son of the woman who owned the house became ill, and his sickness grew worse and worse, until no breath remained in him.
1KI.17.KJV: And it came to pass after these things, that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick; and his sickness was so sore, that there was no breath left in him.
1KI.17.PLAIN: Later, the son of the woman who owned the house became ill, and his sickness grew worse and worse, until no breath remained in him.

1KI.17.BSB: “O man of God,” said the woman to Elijah, “what have you done to me? Have you come to remind me of my iniquity and cause the death of my son?”
1KI.17.KJV: And she said to Elijah, What have I to do with you, O you man of God? are you come to me to call my sin to remembrance, and to slay my son?
1KI.17.PLAIN: “O man of God,” said the woman to Elijah, “what have you done to me? Have you come to remind me of my brokenness and cause the death of my son?”

1KI.17.BSB: But Elijah said to her, “Give me your son.” So he took him from her arms, carried him to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed.
1KI.17.KJV: And he said to her, Give me your son. And he took him out of her bosom, and carried him up into a loft, where he stayed, and laid him on his own bed.
1KI.17.PLAIN: But Elijah said to her, “Give me your son.” So he took him from her arms, carried him to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed.

1KI.17.BSB: Then he cried out to the LORD, “O LORD my God, have You also brought tragedy on this widow who has opened her home to me, by causing her son to die?”
1KI.17.KJV: And he cried to the LORD, and said, O LORD my God, have you also brought evil on the widow with whom I sojourn, by slaying her son?
1KI.17.PLAIN: Then he cried out to the Lord, “O Lord my God, have You also brought tragedy on this widow who has opened her home to me, by causing her son to die?”

1KI.17.BSB: Then he stretched himself out over the child three times and cried out to the LORD, “O LORD my God, please let this boy’s life return to him!”
1KI.17.KJV: And he stretched himself on the child three times, and cried to the LORD, and said, O LORD my God, I pray you, let this child’s soul come into him again.
1KI.17.PLAIN: Then he stretched himself out over the child three times and cried out to the Lord, “O Lord my God, please let this boy’s life return to him!”

1KI.17.BSB: And the LORD listened to the voice of Elijah, and the child’s life returned to him, and he lived.
1KI.17.KJV: And the LORD heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.
1KI.17.PLAIN: And the Lord listened to the voice of Elijah, and the child’s life returned to him, and he lived.

1KI.17.BSB: Then Elijah took the child, brought him down from the upper room into the house, and gave him to his mother. “Look, your son is alive,” Elijah declared.
1KI.17.KJV: And Elijah took the child, and brought him down out of the chamber into the house, and delivered him to his mother: and Elijah said, See, your son lives. ¶
1KI.17.PLAIN: Then Elijah took the child, brought him down from the upper room into the house, and gave him to his mother. “Look, your son is alive,” Elijah declared.

1KI.17.BSB: Then the woman said to Elijah, “Now I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the LORD from your mouth is truth.”
1KI.17.KJV: And the woman said to Elijah, Now by this I know that you are a man of God, and that the word of the LORD in your mouth is truth.
1KI.17.PLAIN: Then the woman said to Elijah, “Now I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the Lord from your mouth is truth.”

1KI.18.BSB: After a long time, in the third year of the drought, the word of the LORD came to Elijah: “Go and present yourself to Ahab, and I will send rain upon the face of the earth.”
1KI.18.KJV: And it came to pass after many days, that the word of the LORD came to Elijah in the third year, saying, Go, show yourself to Ahab; and I will send rain on the earth.
1KI.18.PLAIN: After a long time, in the third year of the drought, the word of the Lord came to Elijah: “Go and present yourself to Ahab, and I will send rain upon the face of the earth.”

1KI.18.BSB: So Elijah went to present himself to Ahab. The famine was severe in Samaria,
1KI.18.KJV: And Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. And there was a sore famine in Samaria.
1KI.18.PLAIN: So Elijah went to present himself to Ahab. The famine was severe in Samaria,

1KI.18.BSB: and Ahab summoned Obadiah, who was in charge of the palace. (Now Obadiah greatly feared the LORD,
1KI.18.KJV: And Ahab called Obadiah, which was the governor of his house. (Now Obadiah feared the LORD greatly:
1KI.18.PLAIN: and Ahab summoned Obadiah, who was in charge of the palace. (Now Obadiah greatly feared the Lord,

1KI.18.BSB: for when Jezebel had slaughtered the prophets of the LORD, Obadiah had taken a hundred prophets and hidden them, fifty men per cave, providing them with food and water.)
1KI.18.KJV: For it was so, when Jezebel cut off the prophets of the LORD, that Obadiah took an hundred prophets, and hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water.)
1KI.18.PLAIN: for when Jezebel had slaughtered the prophets of the Lord, Obadiah had taken a hundred prophets and hidden them, fifty men per cave, providing them with food and water.)

1KI.18.BSB: Then Ahab said to Obadiah, “Go throughout the land to every spring and every valley. Perhaps we will find grass to keep the horses and mules alive so that we will not have to destroy any livestock.”
1KI.18.KJV: And Ahab said to Obadiah, Go into the land, to all fountains of water, and to all brooks: peradventure we may find grass to save the horses and mules alive, that we lose not all the beasts.
1KI.18.PLAIN: Then Ahab said to Obadiah, “Go throughout the land to every spring and every valley. Perhaps we will find grass to keep the horses and mules alive so that we will not have to destroy any livestock.”

1KI.18.BSB: So they divided the land to explore. Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went the other way by himself.
1KI.18.KJV: So they divided the land between them to pass throughout it: Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself. ¶
1KI.18.PLAIN: So they divided the land to explore. Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went the other way by himself.

1KI.18.BSB: Now as Obadiah went on his way, Elijah suddenly met him. When Obadiah recognized him, he fell facedown and said, “Is it you, my lord Elijah?”
1KI.18.KJV: And as Obadiah was in the way, behold, Elijah met him: and he knew him, and fell on his face, and said, Are you that my lord Elijah?
1KI.18.PLAIN: Now as Obadiah went on his way, Elijah suddenly met him. When Obadiah recognized him, he fell facedown and said, “Is it you, my lord Elijah?”

1KI.18.BSB: “It is I,” he answered. “Go tell your master, ‘Elijah is here!’”
1KI.18.KJV: And he answered him, I am: go, tell your lord, Behold, Elijah is here.
1KI.18.PLAIN: “It is I,” he answered. “Go tell your master, ‘Elijah is here!’”

1KI.18.BSB: But Obadiah replied, “How have I sinned, that you are handing your servant over to Ahab to put me to death?

2KI.2.BSB: Then he took the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him and struck the waters. “Where now is the LORD, the God of Elijah?” he asked. And when he had struck the waters, they parted to the right and to the left, and Elisha crossed over.
2KI.2.KJV: And he took the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and smote the waters, and said, Where is the LORD God of Elijah? and when he also had smitten the waters, they parted here and thither: and Elisha went over.
2KI.2.PLAIN: Then he took the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him and struck the waters. “Where now is the Lord, the God of Elijah?” he asked. And when he had struck the waters, they parted to the right and to the left, and Elisha crossed over.

2KI.2.BSB: When the sons of the prophets who were facing him from Jericho saw what had happened, they said, “The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha.” And they went to meet him and bowed down to the ground before him.
2KI.2.KJV: And when the sons of the prophets which were to view at Jericho saw him, they said, The spirit of Elijah does rest on Elisha. And they came to meet him, and bowed themselves to the ground before him. ¶
2KI.2.PLAIN: When the sons of the prophets who were facing him from Jericho saw what had happened, they said, “The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha.” And they went to meet him and bowed down to the ground before him.

2KI.2.BSB: “Look now,” they said to Elisha, “we your servants have fifty valiant men. Please let them go and search for your master. Perhaps the Spirit of the LORD has taken him up and put him on one of the mountains or in one of the valleys.” “Do not send them,” Elisha replied.
2KI.2.KJV: And they said to him, Behold now, there be with your servants fifty strong men; let them go, we pray you, and seek your master: lest peradventure the Spirit of the LORD has taken him up, and cast him on some mountain, or into some valley. And he said, You shall not send.
2KI.2.PLAIN: “Look now,” they said to Elisha, “we your servants have fifty valiant men. Please let them go and search for your master. Perhaps the Spirit of the Lord has taken him up and put him on one of the mountains or in one of the valleys.” “Do not send them,” Elisha replied.

2KI.2.BSB: But when they pressed him to the point of embarrassment, he said, “Send them.” And they sent fifty men, who searched for three days but did not find Elijah.
2KI.2.KJV: And when they urged him till he was ashamed, he said, Send. They sent therefore fifty men; and they sought three days, but found him not.
2KI.2.PLAIN: But when they pressed him to the point of embarrassment, he said, “Send them.” And they sent fifty men, who searched for three days but did not find Elijah.

2KI.2.BSB: When they returned to Elisha, who was staying in Jericho, he said to them, “Didn’t I tell you not to go?”
2KI.2.KJV: And when they came again to him, (for he tarried at Jericho,) he said to them, Did I not say to you, Go not? ¶
2KI.2.PLAIN: When they returned to Elisha, who was staying in Jericho, he said to them, “Didn’t I tell you not to go?”

2KI.2.BSB: Then the men of the city said to Elisha, “Please note, our lord, that the city’s location is good, as you can see. But the water is bad and the land is unfruitful.”
2KI.2.KJV: And the men of the city said to Elisha, Behold, I pray you, the situation of this city is pleasant, as my lord sees: but the water is naught, and the ground barren.
2KI.2.PLAIN: Then the men of the city said to Elisha, “Please note, our lord, that the city’s location is good, as you can see. But the water is bad and the land is unfruitful.”

2KI.2.BSB: “Bring me a new bowl,” he replied, “and put some salt in it.” So they brought it to him,
2KI.2.KJV: And he said, Bring me a new cruse, and put salt therein. And they brought it to him.
2KI.2.PLAIN: “Bring me a new bowl,” he replied, “and put some salt in it.” So they brought it to him,

2KI.2.BSB: and Elisha went out to the spring, cast the salt into it, and said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘I have healed this water. No longer will it cause death or unfruitfulness.’”
2KI.2.KJV: And he went forth to the spring of the waters, and cast the salt in there, and said, Thus says the LORD, I have healed these waters; there shall not be from there any more death or barren land.
2KI.2.PLAIN: and Elisha went out to the spring, cast the salt into it, and said, “This is what the Lord says: ‘I have healed this water. No longer will it cause death or unfruitfulness.’”

2KI.2.BSB: And the waters there have been healthy to this day, according to the word spoken by Elisha.
2KI.2.KJV: So the waters were healed to this day, according to the saying of Elisha which he spoke. ¶
2KI.2.PLAIN: And the waters there have been healthy to this day, according to the word spoken by Elisha.

2KI.2.BSB: From there, Elisha went up to Bethel, and as he was walking up the road, a group of boys came out of the city and jeered at him, chanting, “Go up, you baldhead! Go up, you baldhead!”
2KI.2.KJV: And he went up from there to Bethel: and as he was going up by the way, there came forth little children out of the city, and mocked him, and said to him, Go up, you bald head; go up, you bald head.
2KI.2.PLAIN: From there, Elisha went up to Bethel, and as he was walking up the road, a group of boys came out of the city and jeered at him, chanting, “Go up, you baldhead! Go up, you baldhead!”

2KI.2.BSB: Then he turned around, looked at them, and called down a curse on them in the name of the LORD. Suddenly two female bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of the boys.
2KI.2.KJV: And he turned back, and looked on them, and cursed them in the name of the LORD. And there came forth two she bears out of the wood, and tare forty and two children of them.
2KI.2.PLAIN: Then he turned around, looked at them, and called down a curse on them in the name of the Lord. Suddenly two female bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of the boys.

2KI.2.BSB: And Elisha went on to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
2KI.2.KJV: And he went from there to mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
2KI.2.PLAIN: And Elisha went on to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.

2KI.3.BSB: In the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat’s reign over Judah, Jehoram son of Ahab became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria twelve years.
2KI.3.KJV: Now Jehoram the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and reigned twelve years.
2KI.3.PLAIN: In the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat’s reign over Judah, Jehoram son of Ahab became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria twelve years.

2KI.3.BSB: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, but not as his father and mother had done. He removed the sacred pillar of Baal that his father had made.
2KI.3.KJV: And he worked evil in the sight of the LORD; but not like his father, and like his mother: for he put away the image of Baal that his father had made.
2KI.3.PLAIN: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, but not as his father and mother had done. He removed the sacred pillar of Baal that his father had made.

2KI.3.BSB: Nevertheless, he clung to the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat had caused Israel to commit; he did not turn away from them.
2KI.3.KJV: Nevertheless he joined to the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which made Israel to sin; he departed not therefrom. ¶
2KI.3.PLAIN: Nevertheless, he clung to the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat had caused Israel to commit; he did not turn away from them.

2KI.3.BSB: Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he would render to the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams.
2KI.3.KJV: And Mesha king of Moab was a sheep master, and rendered to the king of Israel an hundred thousand lambs, and an hundred thousand rams, with the wool.
2KI.3.PLAIN: Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he would render to the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams.

2KI.3.BSB: But after the death of Ahab, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
2KI.3.KJV: But it came to pass, when Ahab was dead, that the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel. ¶
2KI.3.PLAIN: But after the death of Ahab, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.

2KI.3.BSB: So at that time King Jehoram set out from Samaria and mobilized all Israel.
2KI.3.KJV: And king Jehoram went out of Samaria the same time, and numbered all Israel.
2KI.3.PLAIN: So at that time King Jehoram set out from Samaria and mobilized all Israel.

2KI.3.BSB: And he sent a message to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: “The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to fight against Moab?” “I will go,” replied Jehoshaphat. “I am like you, my people are your people, and my horses are your horses.”
2KI.3.KJV: And he went and sent to Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, saying, The king of Moab has rebelled against me: will you go with me against Moab to battle? And he said, I will go up: I am as you are, my people as your people, and my horses as your horses.
2KI.3.PLAIN: And he sent a message to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: “The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to fight against Moab?” “I will go,” replied Jehoshaphat. “I am like you, my people are your people, and my horses are your horses.”

2KI.3.BSB: Then he asked, “Which way shall we go up?” “By way of the Desert of Edom,” replied Joram.
2KI.3.KJV: And he said, Which way shall we go up? And he answered, The way through the wilderness of Edom.
2KI.3.PLAIN: Then he asked, “Which way shall we go up?” “By way of the Desert of Edom,” replied Joram.

2KI.3.BSB: So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom set out, and after they had traveled a roundabout route for seven days, they had no water for their army or for their animals.
2KI.3.KJV: So the king of Israel went, and the king of Judah, and the king of Edom: and they fetched a compass of seven days’ journey: and there was no water for the host, and for the cattle that followed them.
2KI.3.PLAIN: So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom set out, and after they had traveled a roundabout route for seven days, they had no water for their army or for their animals.

2KI.3.BSB: “Alas,” said the king of Israel, “for the LORD has summoned these three kings to deliver them into the hand of Moab!”
2KI.3.KJV: And the king of Israel said, Alas! that the LORD has called these three kings together, to deliver them into the hand of Moab!
2KI.3.PLAIN: “Alas,” said the king of Israel, “for the Lord has summoned these three kings to deliver them into the hand of Moab!”

2KI.3.BSB: But Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there no prophet of the LORD here? Let us inquire of the LORD through him.” And one of the servants of the king of Israel answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He used to pour water on the hands of Elijah.”
2KI.3.KJV: But Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the LORD, that we may inquire of the LORD by him? And one of the king of Israel’s servants answered and said, Here is Elisha the son of Shaphat, which poured water on the hands of Elijah.
2KI.3.PLAIN: But Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there no prophet of the Lord here? Let us inquire of the Lord through him.” And one of the servants of the king of Israel answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He used to pour water on the hands of Elijah.”

2KI.3.BSB: Jehoshaphat affirmed, “The word of the LORD is with him.” So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.
2KI.3.KJV: And Jehoshaphat said, The word of the LORD is with him. So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.
2KI.3.PLAIN: Jehoshaphat affirmed, “The word of the Lord is with him.” So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.

2KI.3.BSB: Elisha, however, said to the king of Israel, “What have we to do with each other? Go to the prophets of your father and of your mother!” “No,” replied the king of Israel, “for it is the LORD who has summoned these three kings to deliver them into the hand of Moab.”
2KI.3.KJV: And Elisha said to the king of Israel, What have I to do with you? get you to the prophets of your father, and to the prophets of your mother. And the king of Israel said to him, No: for the LORD has called these three kings together, to deliver them into the hand of Moab.
2KI.3.PLAIN: Elisha, however, said to the king of Israel, “What have we to do with each other? Go to the prophets of your father and of your mother!” “No,” replied the king of Israel, “for it is the Lord who has summoned these three kings to deliver them into the hand of Moab.”

2KI.3.BSB: Then Elisha said, “As surely as the LORD of Hosts lives, before whom I stand, were it not for my regard for the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look at you or acknowledge you.
2KI.3.KJV: And Elisha said, As the LORD of hosts lives, before whom I stand, surely, were it not that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, I would not look toward you, nor see you.
2KI.3.PLAIN: Then Elisha said, “As surely as the Lord of Hosts lives, before whom I stand, were it not for my regard for the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look at you or acknowledge you.

2KI.3.BSB: But now, bring me a harpist.” And while the harpist played, the hand of the LORD came upon Elisha
2KI.3.KJV: But now bring me a minstrel. And it came to pass, when the minstrel played, that the hand of the LORD came on him.
2KI.3.PLAIN: But now, bring me a harpist.” And while the harpist played, the hand of the Lord came upon Elisha

2KI.3.BSB: and he said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Dig this valley full of ditches.’
2KI.3.KJV: And he said, Thus says the LORD, Make this valley full of ditches.
2KI.3.PLAIN: and he said, “This is what the Lord says: ‘Dig this valley full of ditches.’

2KI.3.BSB: For the LORD says, ‘You will not see wind or rain, but the valley will be filled with water, and you will drink—you and your cattle and your animals.’
2KI.3.KJV: For thus says the LORD, You shall not see wind, neither shall you see rain; yet that valley shall be filled with water, that you may drink, both you, and your cattle, and your beasts.
2KI.3.PLAIN: For the Lord says, ‘You will not see wind or rain, but the valley will be filled with water, and you will drink—you and your cattle and your animals.’

2KI.3.BSB: This is a simple matter in the sight of the LORD, and He will also deliver the Moabites into your hand.
2KI.3.KJV: And this is but a light thing in the sight of the LORD: he will deliver the Moabites also into your hand.
2KI.3.PLAIN: This is a simple matter in the sight of the Lord, and He will also deliver the Moabites into your hand.

2KI.3.BSB: And you shall attack every fortified city and every city of importance. You shall cut down every good tree, stop up every spring, and ruin every good field with stones.”
2KI.3.KJV: And you shall smite every fenced city, and every choice city, and shall fell every good tree, and stop all wells of water, and mar every good piece of land with stones.
2KI.3.PLAIN: And you shall attack every fortified city and every city of importance. You shall cut down every good tree, stop up every spring, and ruin every good field with stones.”

2KI.3.BSB: The next morning, at the time of the morning sacrifice, water suddenly flowed from the direction of Edom and filled the land.
2KI.3.KJV: And it came to pass in the morning, when the meat offering was offered, that, behold, there came water by the way of Edom, and the country was filled with water. ¶
2KI.3.PLAIN: The next morning, at the time of the morning sacrifice, water suddenly flowed from the direction of Edom and filled the land.

2KI.3.BSB: Now all the Moabites had heard that the kings had come up to fight against them. So all who could bear arms, young and old, were summoned and stationed at the border.
2KI.3.KJV: And when all the Moabites heard that the kings were come up to fight against them, they gathered all that were able to put on armor, and upward, and stood in the border.
2KI.3.PLAIN: Now all the Moabites had heard that the kings had come up to fight against them. So all who could bear arms, young and old, were summoned and stationed at the border.

2KI.3.BSB: When they got up early in the morning, the sun was shining on the water, and it looked as red as blood to the Moabites across the way.
2KI.3.KJV: And they rose up early in the morning, and the sun shone on the water, and the Moabites saw the water on the other side as red as blood:
2KI.3.PLAIN: When they got up early in the morning, the sun was shining on the water, and it looked as red as blood to the Moabites across the way.

2KI.3.BSB: “This is blood!” they exclaimed. “The kings have clashed swords and slaughtered one another. Now to the plunder, Moab!”
2KI.3.KJV: And they said, This is blood: the kings are surely slain, and they have smitten one another: now therefore, Moab, to the spoil.
2KI.3.PLAIN: “This is blood!” they exclaimed. “The kings have clashed swords and slaughtered one another. Now to the plunder, Moab!”

2KI.3.BSB: But when the Moabites came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and attacked them, and they fled before them. So the Israelites invaded their land and struck down the Moabites.
2KI.3.KJV: And when they came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and smote the Moabites, so that they fled before them: but they went forward smiting the Moabites, even in their country.
2KI.3.PLAIN: But when the Moabites came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and attacked them, and they fled before them. So the Israelites invaded their land and struck down the Moabites.

2KI.3.BSB: They destroyed the cities, and each man threw stones on every good field until it was covered. They stopped up every spring and cut down every good tree. Only Kir-haraseth was left with stones in place, but men with slings surrounded it and attacked it as well.
2KI.3.KJV: And they beat down the cities, and on every good piece of land cast every man his stone, and filled it; and they stopped all the wells of water, and felled all the good trees: only in Kirharaseth left they the stones thereof; however, the slingers went about it, and smote it. ¶
2KI.3.PLAIN: They destroyed the cities, and each man threw stones on every good field until it was covered. They stopped up every spring and cut down every good tree. Only Kir-haraseth was left with stones in place, but men with slings surrounded it and attacked it as well.

2KI.3.BSB: When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too fierce for him, he took with him seven hundred swordsmen to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not prevail.
2KI.3.KJV: And when the king of Moab saw that the battle was too sore for him, he took with him seven hundred men that drew swords, to break through even to the king of Edom: but they could not.
2KI.3.PLAIN: When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too fierce for him, he took with him seven hundred swordsmen to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not prevail.

2KI.3.BSB: So he took his firstborn son, who was to succeed him, and offered him as a burnt offering on the city wall. And there was great fury against the Israelites, so they withdrew and returned to their own land.
2KI.3.KJV: Then he took his oldest son that should have reigned in his stead, and offered him for a burnt offering on the wall. And there was great indignation against Israel: and they departed from him, and returned to their own land.
2KI.3.PLAIN: So he took his firstborn son, who was to succeed him, and offered him as a burnt offering on the city wall. And there was great fury against the Israelites, so they withdrew and returned to their own land.

2KI.4.BSB: Now the wife of one of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, “Your servant, my husband, is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD. And now his creditor is coming to take my two children as his slaves!”
2KI.4.KJV: Now there cried a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets to Elisha, saying, Your servant my husband is dead; and you know that your servant did fear the LORD: and the creditor is come to take to him my two sons to be slaves.
2KI.4.PLAIN: Now the wife of one of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, “Your servant, my husband, is dead, and you know that your servant feared the Lord. And now his creditor is coming to take my two children as his slaves!”

2KI.4.BSB: “How can I help you?” asked Elisha. “Tell me, what do you have in the house?” She answered, “Your servant has nothing in the house but a jar of oil.”
2KI.4.KJV: And Elisha said to her, What shall I do for you? tell me, what have you in the house? And she said, Your handmaid has not any thing in the house, save a pot of oil.
2KI.4.PLAIN: “How can I help you?” asked Elisha. “Tell me, what do you have in the house?” She answered, “Your servant has nothing in the house but a jar of oil.”

2KI.4.BSB: “Go,” said Elisha, “borrow jars, even empty ones, from all your neighbors. Do not gather just a few.
2KI.4.KJV: Then he said, Go, borrow you vessels abroad of all your neighbors, even empty vessels; borrow not a few.
2KI.4.PLAIN: “Go,” said Elisha, “borrow jars, even empty ones, from all your neighbors. Do not gather just a few.

2KI.4.BSB: Then go inside, shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour oil into all these jars, setting the full ones aside.”
2KI.4.KJV: And when you are come in, you shall shut the door on you and on your sons, and shall pour out into all those vessels, and you shall set aside that which is full.
2KI.4.PLAIN: Then go inside, shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour oil into all these jars, setting the full ones aside.”

2KI.4.BSB: So she left him, and after she had shut the door behind her and her sons, they kept bringing jars to her, and she kept pouring.
2KI.4.KJV: So she went from him, and shut the door on her and on her sons, who brought the vessels to her; and she poured out.
2KI.4.PLAIN: So she left him, and after she had shut the door behind her and her sons, they kept bringing jars to her, and she kept pouring.

2KI.4.BSB: When all the jars were full, she said to her son, “Bring me another.” But he replied, “There are no more jars.” Then the oil stopped flowing.
2KI.4.KJV: And it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said to her son, Bring me yet a vessel. And he said to her, There is not a vessel more. And the oil stayed.
2KI.4.PLAIN: When all the jars were full, she said to her son, “Bring me another.” But he replied, “There are no more jars.” Then the oil stopped flowing.

2KI.4.BSB: She went and told the man of God, and he said, “Go, sell the oil, and pay your debt. Then you and your sons can live on the remainder.”
2KI.4.KJV: Then she came and told the man of God. And he said, Go, sell the oil, and pay your debt, and live you and your children of the rest. ¶
2KI.4.PLAIN: She went and told the man of God, and he said, “Go, sell the oil, and pay your debt. Then you and your sons can live on the remainder.”

2KI.4.BSB: One day Elisha went to Shunem, and a prominent woman who lived there persuaded him to have a meal. So whenever he would pass by, he would stop there to eat.
2KI.4.KJV: And it fell on a day, that Elisha passed to Shunem, where was a great woman; and she constrained him to eat bread. And so it was, that as oft as he passed by, he turned in thither to eat bread.
2KI.4.PLAIN: One day Elisha went to Shunem, and a prominent woman who lived there persuaded him to have a meal. So whenever he would pass by, he would stop there to eat.

2KI.4.BSB: Then the woman said to her husband, “Behold, now I know that the one who often comes our way is a holy man of God.
2KI.4.KJV: And she said to her husband, Behold now, I perceive that this is an holy man of God, which passes by us continually.
2KI.4.PLAIN: Then the woman said to her husband, “Look closely — now I know that the one who often comes our way is a holy man of God.

2KI.4.BSB: Please let us make a small room upstairs and put in it a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp for him. Then when he comes to us, he can stay there.”
2KI.4.KJV: Let us make a little chamber, I pray you, on the wall; and let us set for him there a bed, and a table, and a stool, and a candlestick: and it shall be, when he comes to us, that he shall turn in thither.
2KI.4.PLAIN: Please let us make a small room upstairs and put in it a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp for him. Then when he comes to us, he can stay there.”

2KI.4.BSB: One day Elisha came to visit and went to his upper room to lie down.
2KI.4.KJV: And it fell on a day, that he came thither, and he turned into the chamber, and lay there.
2KI.4.PLAIN: One day Elisha came to visit and went to his upper room to lie down.

2KI.4.BSB: And he said to Gehazi his servant, “Call the Shunammite woman.” And when he had called her, she stood before him,
2KI.4.KJV: And he said to Gehazi his servant, Call this Shunammite. And when he had called her, she stood before him.
2KI.4.PLAIN: And he said to Gehazi his servant, “Call the Shunammite woman.” And when he had called her, she stood before him,

2KI.4.BSB: and Elisha said to Gehazi, “Now tell her, ‘Look, you have gone to all this trouble for us. What can we do for you? Can we speak on your behalf to the king or the commander of the army?’” “I have a home among my own people,” she replied.
2KI.4.KJV: And he said to him, Say now to her, Behold, you have been careful for us with all this care; what is to be done for you? would you be spoken for to the king, or to the captain of the host? And she answered, I dwell among my own people.
2KI.4.PLAIN: and Elisha said to Gehazi, “Now tell her, ‘Look, you have gone to all this trouble for us. What can we do for you? Can we speak on your behalf to the king or the commander of the army?’” “I have a home among my own people,” she replied.

2KI.4.BSB: So he asked, “Then what should be done for her?” “Well, she has no son,” Gehazi replied, “and her husband is old.”
2KI.4.KJV: And he said, What then is to be done for her? And Gehazi answered, Truly she has no child, and her husband is old.
2KI.4.PLAIN: So he asked, “Then what should be done for her?” “Well, she has no son,” Gehazi replied, “and her husband is old.”

2KI.4.BSB: “Call her,” said Elisha. So Gehazi called her, and she stood in the doorway.
2KI.4.KJV: And he said, Call her. And when he had called her, she stood in the door.
2KI.4.PLAIN: “Call her,” said Elisha. So Gehazi called her, and she stood in the doorway.

2KI.4.BSB: And Elisha declared, “At this time next year, you will hold a son in your arms.” “No, my lord,” she said. “Do not lie to your maidservant, O man of God.”
2KI.4.KJV: And he said, About this season, according to the time of life, you shall embrace a son. And she said, No, my lord, you man of God, do not lie to your handmaid.
2KI.4.PLAIN: And Elisha declared, “At this time next year, you will hold a son in your arms.” “No, my lord,” she said. “Do not lie to your maidservant, O man of God.”

2KI.13.KJV: In the thirty and seventh year of Joash king of Judah began Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned sixteen years.
2KI.13.PLAIN: In the thirty-seventh year of the reign of Joash over Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king of Israel in Samaria, and he reigned sixteen years.

2KI.13.BSB: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD and did not turn away from all the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat had caused Israel to commit, but he walked in them.
2KI.13.KJV: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD; he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel sin: but he walked therein.
2KI.13.PLAIN: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord and did not turn away from all the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat had caused Israel to commit, but he walked in them.

2KI.13.KJV: And the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, and his might with which he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
2KI.13.PLAIN: As for the rest of the acts of Jehoash, along with all his accomplishments and his might, including his war against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

2KI.13.BSB: And Jehoash rested with his fathers, and Jeroboam succeeded him on the throne. Jehoash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
2KI.13.KJV: And Joash slept with his fathers; and Jeroboam sat on his throne: and Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. ¶
2KI.13.PLAIN: And Jehoash rested with his fathers, and Jeroboam succeeded him on the throne. Jehoash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

2KI.13.BSB: When Elisha had fallen sick with the illness from which he would die, Jehoash king of Israel came down to him and wept over him, saying, “My father, my father, the chariots and horsemen of Israel!”
2KI.13.KJV: Now Elisha was fallen sick of his sickness whereof he died. And Joash the king of Israel came down to him, and wept over his face, and said, O my father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof.
2KI.13.PLAIN: When Elisha had fallen sick with the illness from which he would die, Jehoash king of Israel came down to him and wept over him, saying, “My father, my father, the chariots and horsemen of Israel!”

2KI.13.BSB: Elisha told him, “Take a bow and some arrows.” So Jehoash took a bow and some arrows.
2KI.13.KJV: And Elisha said to him, Take bow and arrows. And he took to him bow and arrows.
2KI.13.PLAIN: Elisha told him, “Take a bow and some arrows.” So Jehoash took a bow and some arrows.

2KI.13.BSB: Then Elisha said to the king of Israel, “Put your hand on the bow.” So the king put his hand on the bow, and Elisha put his hands on the king’s hands.
2KI.13.KJV: And he said to the king of Israel, Put your hand on the bow. And he put his hand on it: and Elisha put his hands on the king’s hands.
2KI.13.PLAIN: Then Elisha said to the king of Israel, “Put your hand on the bow.” So the king put his hand on the bow, and Elisha put his hands on the king’s hands.

2KI.13.BSB: “Open the east window,” said Elisha. So he opened it and Elisha said, “Shoot!” So he shot. And Elisha declared: “This is the LORD’s arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram, for you shall strike the Arameans in Aphek until you have put an end to them.”
2KI.13.KJV: And he said, Open the window eastward. And he opened it. Then Elisha said, Shoot. And he shot. And he said, The arrow of the LORD’s deliverance, and the arrow of deliverance from Syria: for you shall smite the Syrians in Aphek, till you have consumed them.
2KI.13.PLAIN: “Open the east window,” said Elisha. So he opened it and Elisha said, “Shoot!” So he shot. And Elisha declared: “This is the Lord’s arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram, for you shall strike the Arameans in Aphek until you have put an end to them.”

2KI.13.BSB: Then Elisha said, “Take the arrows!” So he took them, and Elisha said to the king of Israel, “Strike the ground!” So he struck the ground three times and stopped.
2KI.13.KJV: And he said, Take the arrows. And he took them. And he said to the king of Israel, Smite on the ground. And he smote thrice, and stayed.
2KI.13.PLAIN: Then Elisha said, “Take the arrows!” So he took them, and Elisha said to the king of Israel, “Strike the ground!” So he struck the ground three times and stopped.

2KI.13.BSB: But the man of God was angry with him and said, “You should have struck the ground five or six times. Then you would have struck down Aram until you had put an end to it. But now you will strike down Aram only three times.”
2KI.13.KJV: And the man of God was wroth with him, and said, You should have smitten five or six times; then had you smitten Syria till you had consumed it: whereas now you shall smite Syria but thrice. ¶
2KI.13.PLAIN: But the man of God was angry with him and said, “You should have struck the ground five or six times. Then you would have struck down Aram until you had put an end to it. But now you will strike down Aram only three times.”

2KI.13.BSB: And Elisha died and was buried. Now the Moabite raiders used to come into the land every spring.
2KI.13.KJV: And Elisha died, and they buried him. And the bands of the Moabites invaded the land at the coming in of the year.
2KI.13.PLAIN: And Elisha died and was buried. Now the Moabite raiders used to come into the land every spring.

2KI.13.BSB: Once, as the Israelites were burying a man, suddenly they saw a band of raiders, so they threw the man’s body into Elisha’s tomb. And as soon as his body touched the bones of Elisha, the man was revived and stood up on his feet.
2KI.13.KJV: And it came to pass, as they were burying a man, that, behold, they spied a band of men; and they cast the man into the sepulcher of Elisha: and when the man was let down, and touched the bones of Elisha, he revived, and stood up on his feet. ¶
2KI.13.PLAIN: Once, as the Israelites were burying a man, suddenly they saw a band of raiders, so they threw the man’s body into Elisha’s tomb. And as soon as his body touched the bones of Elisha, the man was revived and stood up on his feet.

2KI.13.BSB: And Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel throughout the reign of Jehoahaz.
2KI.13.KJV: But Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.
2KI.13.PLAIN: And Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel throughout the reign of Jehoahaz.

2KI.13.BSB: But the LORD was gracious to Israel and had compassion on them, and He turned toward them because of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. And to this day, the LORD has been unwilling to destroy them or cast them from His presence.
2KI.13.KJV: And the LORD was gracious to them, and had compassion on them, and had respect to them, because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and would not destroy them, neither cast he them from his presence as yet.
2KI.13.PLAIN: But the Lord was gracious to Israel and had compassion on them, and He turned toward them because of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. And to this day, the Lord has been unwilling to destroy them or cast them from His presence.

2KI.13.BSB: When Hazael king of Aram died, his son Ben-hadad reigned in his place.
2KI.13.KJV: So Hazael king of Syria died; and Benhadad his son reigned in his stead.
2KI.13.PLAIN: When Hazael king of Aram died, his son Ben-hadad reigned in his place.

2KI.13.BSB: Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took back from Ben-hadad son of Hazael the cities that Hazael had taken in battle from his father Jehoahaz. Jehoash defeated Ben-hadad three times, and so recovered the cities of Israel.
2KI.13.KJV: And Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz took again out of the hand of Benhadad the son of Hazael the cities, which he had taken out of the hand of Jehoahaz his father by war. Three times did Joash beat him, and recovered the cities of Israel.
2KI.13.PLAIN: Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took back from Ben-hadad son of Hazael the cities that Hazael had taken in battle from his father Jehoahaz. Jehoash defeated Ben-hadad three times, and so recovered the cities of Israel.

2KI.14.BSB: In the second year of the reign of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz over Israel, Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah.
2KI.14.KJV: In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel reigned Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah.
2KI.14.PLAIN: In the second year of the reign of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz over Israel, Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah.

2KI.14.BSB: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-nine years. His mother’s name was Jehoaddan; she was from Jerusalem.
2KI.14.KJV: He was twenty and five years old when he began to reign, and reigned twenty and nine years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.
2KI.14.PLAIN: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-nine years. His mother’s name was Jehoaddan; she was from Jerusalem.

2KI.14.BSB: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not as his father David had done. He did everything as his father Joash had done.
2KI.14.KJV: And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, yet not like David his father: he did according to all things as Joash his father did.
2KI.14.PLAIN: And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, but not as his father David had done. He did everything as his father Joash had done.

2KI.14.BSB: Nevertheless, the high places were not taken away, and the people continued sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.
2KI.14.KJV: However, the high places were not taken away: as yet the people did sacrifice and burnt incense on the high places. ¶
2KI.14.PLAIN: Nevertheless, the high places were not taken away, and the people continued sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.

2KI.14.BSB: As soon as the kingdom was firmly in his grasp, Amaziah executed the servants who had murdered his father the king.
2KI.14.KJV: And it came to pass, as soon as the kingdom was confirmed in his hand, that he slew his servants which had slain the king his father.
2KI.14.PLAIN: As soon as the kingdom was firmly in his grasp, Amaziah executed the servants who had murdered his father the king.

2KI.14.BSB: Yet he did not put the sons of the murderers to death, but acted according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, where the LORD commanded: “Fathers must not be put to death for their children, and children must not be put to death for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin.”
2KI.14.KJV: But the children of the murderers he slew not: according to that which is written in the book of the law of Moses, wherein the LORD commanded, saying, The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, nor the children be put to death for the fathers; but every man shall be put to death for his own sin.
2KI.14.PLAIN: Yet he did not put the sons of the murderers to death, but acted according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, where the Lord commanded: “Fathers must not be put to death for their children, and children must not be put to death for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin.”

2KI.14.BSB: Amaziah struck down 10,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. He took Sela in battle and called it Joktheel, which is its name to this very day.
2KI.14.KJV: He slew of Edom in the valley of salt ten thousand, and took Selah by war, and called the name of it Joktheel to this day. ¶
2KI.14.PLAIN: Amaziah struck down 10,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. He took Sela in battle and called it Joktheel, which is its name to this very day.

2KI.14.BSB: Then Amaziah sent messengers to the king of Israel Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu. “Come, let us meet face to face,” he said.
2KI.14.KJV: Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash, the son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, Come, let us look one another in the face.
2KI.14.PLAIN: Then Amaziah sent messengers to the king of Israel Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu. “Come, let us meet face to face,” he said.

2KI.14.BSB: But Jehoash king of Israel replied to Amaziah king of Judah: “A thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son in marriage.’ Then a wild beast in Lebanon came along and trampled the thistle.
2KI.14.KJV: And Jehoash the king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, Give your daughter to my son to wife: and there passed by a wild beast that was in Lebanon, and stepped down the thistle.
2KI.14.PLAIN: But Jehoash king of Israel replied to Amaziah king of Judah: “A thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son in marriage.’ Then a wild beast in Lebanon came along and trampled the thistle.

2KI.14.BSB: You have indeed defeated Edom, and your heart has become proud. Glory in that and stay at home. Why should you stir up trouble so that you fall—you and Judah with you?”
2KI.14.KJV: You have indeed smitten Edom, and your heart has lifted you up: glory of this, and tarry at home: for why should you meddle to your hurt, that you should fall, even you, and Judah with you?
2KI.14.PLAIN: You have indeed defeated Edom, and your heart has become proud. Glory in that and stay at home. Why should you stir up trouble so that you fall—you and Judah with you?”

2KI.14.BSB: But Amaziah would not listen, and Jehoash king of Israel advanced. He and King Amaziah of Judah faced each other at Beth-shemesh in Judah.
2KI.14.KJV: But Amaziah would not hear. Therefore Jehoash king of Israel went up; and he and Amaziah king of Judah looked one another in the face at Bethshemesh, which belongs to Judah.
2KI.14.PLAIN: But Amaziah would not listen, and Jehoash king of Israel advanced. He and King Amaziah of Judah faced each other at Beth-shemesh in Judah.

2KI.14.BSB: And Judah was routed before Israel, and every man fled to his home.
2KI.14.KJV: And Judah was put to the worse before Israel; and they fled every man to their tents.
2KI.14.PLAIN: And Judah was routed before Israel, and every man fled to his home.

2KI.14.BSB: There at Beth-shemesh, Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash, the son of Ahaziah. Then Jehoash went to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate—a section of four hundred cubits.
2KI.14.KJV: And Jehoash king of Israel took Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Jehoash the son of Ahaziah, at Bethshemesh, and came to Jerusalem, and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits.
2KI.14.PLAIN: There at Beth-shemesh, Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash, the son of Ahaziah. Then Jehoash went to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate—a section of four hundred cubits.

2KI.14.BSB: He took all the gold and silver and all the articles found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the royal palace, as well as some hostages. Then he returned to Samaria.
2KI.14.KJV: And he took all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of the LORD, and in the treasures of the king’s house, and hostages, and returned to Samaria. ¶
2KI.14.PLAIN: He took all the gold and silver and all the articles found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the royal palace, as well as some hostages. Then he returned to Samaria.

2KI.14.BSB: As for the rest of the acts of Jehoash, along with his accomplishments, his might, and how he waged war against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
2KI.14.KJV: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoash which he did, and his might, and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
2KI.14.PLAIN: As for the rest of the acts of Jehoash, along with his accomplishments, his might, and how he waged war against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

2KI.14.KJV: And Jehoash slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel; and Jeroboam his son reigned in his stead. ¶
2KI.14.PLAIN: And Jehoash rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. And his son Jeroboam reigned in his place.

2KI.14.BSB: Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived for fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
2KI.14.KJV: And Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah lived after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel fifteen years.
2KI.14.PLAIN: Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived for fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.

2KI.14.BSB: As for the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
2KI.14.KJV: And the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
2KI.14.PLAIN: As for the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

2KI.14.BSB: And conspirators plotted against Amaziah in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But men were sent after him to Lachish, and they killed him there.
2KI.14.KJV: Now they made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem: and he fled to Lachish; but they sent after him to Lachish, and slew him there.
2KI.14.PLAIN: And conspirators plotted against Amaziah in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But men were sent after him to Lachish, and they killed him there.

2KI.14.BSB: They carried him back on horses and buried him in Jerusalem with his fathers in the City of David.
2KI.14.KJV: And they brought him on horses: and he was buried at Jerusalem with his fathers in the city of David. ¶
2KI.14.PLAIN: They carried him back on horses and buried him in Jerusalem with his fathers in the City of David.

2KI.14.BSB: Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
2KI.14.KJV: And all the people of Judah took Azariah, which was sixteen years old, and made him king instead of his father Amaziah.
2KI.14.PLAIN: Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.

2KI.14.BSB: Azariah was the one who rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah after King Amaziah rested with his fathers.
2KI.14.KJV: He built Elath, and restored it to Judah, after that the king slept with his fathers. ¶
2KI.14.PLAIN: Azariah was the one who rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah after King Amaziah rested with his fathers.

2KI.14.BSB: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Amaziah son of Joash over Judah, Jeroboam son of Jehoash became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria forty-one years.
2KI.14.KJV: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel began to reign in Samaria, and reigned forty and one years.
2KI.14.PLAIN: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Amaziah son of Joash over Judah, Jeroboam son of Jehoash became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria forty-one years.

2KI.14.BSB: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD and did not turn away from all the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat had caused Israel to commit.
2KI.14.KJV: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD: he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
2KI.14.PLAIN: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord and did not turn away from all the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat had caused Israel to commit.

2KI.14.BSB: This Jeroboam restored the boundary of Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word that the LORD, the God of Israel, had spoken through His servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath-hepher.
2KI.14.KJV: He restored the coast of Israel from the entering of Hamath to the sea of the plain, according to the word of the LORD God of Israel, which he spoke by the hand of his servant Jonah, the son of Amittai, the prophet, which was of Gathhepher.
2KI.14.PLAIN: This Jeroboam restored the boundary of Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word that the Lord, the God of Israel, had spoken through His servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath-hepher.

2KI.14.BSB: For the LORD saw that the affliction of the Israelites, both slave and free, was very bitter. There was no one to help Israel,
2KI.14.KJV: For the LORD saw the affliction of Israel, that it was very bitter: for there was not any shut up, nor any left, nor any helper for Israel.
2KI.14.PLAIN: For the Lord saw that the affliction of the Israelites, both slave and free, was very bitter. There was no one to help Israel,

2KI.14.BSB: and since the LORD had said that He would not blot out the name of Israel from under heaven, He saved them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Jehoash.
2KI.14.KJV: And the LORD said not that he would blot out the name of Israel from under heaven: but he saved them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash. ¶
2KI.14.PLAIN: and since the Lord had said that He would not blot out the name of Israel from under heaven, He saved them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Jehoash.

2KI.14.BSB: As for the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, along with all his accomplishments and might, and how he waged war and recovered both Damascus and Hamath for Israel from Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
2KI.14.KJV: Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might, how he warred, and how he recovered Damascus, and Hamath, which belonged to Judah, for Israel, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
2KI.14.PLAIN: As for the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, along with all his accomplishments and might, and how he waged war and recovered both Damascus and Hamath for Israel from Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

2KI.14.BSB: And Jeroboam rested with his fathers, the kings of Israel. And his son Zechariah reigned in his place.
2KI.14.KJV: And Jeroboam slept with his fathers, even with the kings of Israel; and Zachariah his son reigned in his stead.
2KI.14.PLAIN: And Jeroboam rested with his fathers, the kings of Israel. And his son Zechariah reigned in his place.

2KI.15.KJV: In the twenty and seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel began Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah to reign.
2KI.15.PLAIN: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam’s reign over Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah became king of Judah.

2KI.15.BSB: He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-two years. His mother’s name was Jecoliah; she was from Jerusalem.
2KI.15.KJV: Sixteen years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned two and fifty years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Jecholiah of Jerusalem.
2KI.15.PLAIN: He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-two years. His mother’s name was Jecoliah; she was from Jerusalem.

2KI.15.BSB: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Amaziah had done.
2KI.15.KJV: And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Amaziah had done;
2KI.15.PLAIN: And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, just as his father Amaziah had done.

2KI.15.BSB: Nevertheless, the high places were not taken away; the people continued sacrificing and burning incense there.
2KI.15.KJV: Save that the high places were not removed: the people sacrificed and burnt incense still on the high places. ¶
2KI.15.PLAIN: Nevertheless, the high places were not taken away; the people continued sacrificing and burning incense there.
