2CH.1.PLAIN: And Solomon and the whole assembly went to the high place at Gibeon because it was the location of God’s Tent of Meeting, which Moses the servant of the Lord had made in the wilderness.

2CH.1.BSB: Now David had brought the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared for it, because he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.
2CH.1.KJV: But the ark of God had David brought up from Kirjathjearim to the place which David had prepared for it: for he had pitched a tent for it at Jerusalem.
2CH.1.PLAIN: Now David had brought the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared for it, because he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.

2CH.1.BSB: But the bronze altar made by Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, was in Gibeon before the tabernacle of the LORD. So Solomon and the assembly inquired of Him there.
2CH.1.KJV: Moreover the brazen altar, that Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, had made, he put before the tabernacle of the LORD: and Solomon and the congregation sought to it.
2CH.1.PLAIN: But the bronze altar made by Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, was in Gibeon before the tabernacle of the Lord. So Solomon and the assembly inquired of Him there.

2CH.1.BSB: Solomon offered sacrifices there before the LORD on the bronze altar in the Tent of Meeting, where he offered a thousand burnt offerings.
2CH.1.KJV: And Solomon went up thither to the brazen altar before the LORD, which was at the tabernacle of the congregation, and offered a thousand burnt offerings on it. ¶
2CH.1.PLAIN: Solomon offered sacrifices there before the Lord on the bronze altar in the Tent of Meeting, where he offered a thousand burnt offerings.

2CH.1.BSB: That night God appeared to Solomon and said, “Ask, and I will give it to you!”
2CH.1.KJV: In that night did God appear to Solomon, and said to him, Ask what I shall give you.
2CH.1.PLAIN: That night God appeared to Solomon and said, “Ask, and I will give it to you!”

2CH.1.BSB: Solomon replied to God: “You have shown much loving devotion to my father David, and You have made me king in his place.
2CH.1.KJV: And Solomon said to God, You have showed great mercy to David my father, and have made me to reign in his stead.
2CH.1.PLAIN: Solomon replied to God: “You have shown much loving devotion to my father David, and You have made me king in his place.

2CH.1.BSB: Now, O LORD God, let Your promise to my father David be fulfilled. For You have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
2CH.1.KJV: Now, O LORD God, let your promise to David my father be established: for you have made me king over a people like the dust of the earth in multitude.
2CH.1.PLAIN: Now, O Lord God, let Your promise to my father David be fulfilled. For You have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.

2CH.1.BSB: Now grant me wisdom and knowledge, so that I may lead this people. For who is able to govern this great people of Yours?”
2CH.1.KJV: Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people: for who can judge this your people, that is so great?
2CH.1.PLAIN: Now grant me wisdom and knowledge, so that I may lead this people. For who is able to govern this great people of Yours?”

2CH.1.BSB: God said to Solomon, “Since this was in your heart instead of requesting riches or wealth or glory for yourself or death for your enemies—and since you have not even requested long life but have asked for wisdom and knowledge to govern My people over whom I have made you king—
2CH.1.KJV: And God said to Solomon, Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked riches, wealth, or honor, nor the life of your enemies, neither yet have asked long life; but have asked wisdom and knowledge for yourself, that you may judge my people, over whom I have made you king:
2CH.1.PLAIN: God said to Solomon, “Since this was in your heart instead of requesting riches or wealth or glory for yourself or death for your enemies—and since you have not even requested long life but have asked for wisdom and knowledge to govern My people over whom I have made you king—

2CH.1.BSB: therefore wisdom and knowledge have been granted to you. And I will also give you riches and wealth and honor unlike anything given to the kings before you or after you.”
2CH.1.KJV: Wisdom and knowledge is granted to you; and I will give you riches, and wealth, and honor, such as none of the kings have had that have been before you, neither shall there any after you have the like. ¶
2CH.1.PLAIN: therefore wisdom and knowledge have been granted to you. And I will also give you riches and wealth and honor unlike anything given to the kings before you or after you.”

2CH.1.BSB: So Solomon went to Jerusalem from the high place in Gibeon before the Tent of Meeting, and he reigned over Israel.
2CH.1.KJV: Then Solomon came from his journey to the high place that was at Gibeon to Jerusalem, from before the tabernacle of the congregation, and reigned over Israel.
2CH.1.PLAIN: So Solomon went to Jerusalem from the high place in Gibeon before the Tent of Meeting, and he reigned over Israel.

2CH.1.BSB: Solomon accumulated 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses, which he stationed in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.
2CH.1.KJV: And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen: and he had a thousand and four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, which he placed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem.
2CH.1.PLAIN: Solomon accumulated 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses, which he stationed in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.

2CH.1.BSB: The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore in the foothills.
2CH.1.KJV: And the king made silver and gold at Jerusalem as plenteous as stones, and cedar trees made he as the sycomore trees that are in the vale for abundance.
2CH.1.PLAIN: The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore in the foothills.

2CH.1.BSB: Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and Kue; the royal merchants purchased them from Kue.
2CH.1.KJV: And Solomon had horses brought out of Egypt, and linen yarn: the king’s merchants received the linen yarn at a price.
2CH.1.PLAIN: Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and Kue; the royal merchants purchased them from Kue.

2CH.1.BSB: A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. Likewise, they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram.
2CH.1.KJV: And they fetched up, and brought forth out of Egypt a chariot for six hundred shekels of silver, and an horse for an hundred and fifty: and so brought they out horses for all the kings of the Hittites, and for the kings of Syria, by their means.
2CH.1.PLAIN: A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. Likewise, they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram.

2CH.2.BSB: Now Solomon purposed to build a house for the Name of the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
2CH.2.KJV: And Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the LORD, and an house for his kingdom.
2CH.2.PLAIN: Now Solomon purposed to build a house for the Name of the Lord and a royal palace for himself.

2CH.2.BSB: So he conscripted 70,000 porters, 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains, and 3,600 supervisors.
2CH.2.KJV: And Solomon told out three score and ten thousand men to bear burdens, and fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred to oversee them. ¶
2CH.2.PLAIN: So he conscripted 70,000 porters, 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains, and 3,600 supervisors.

2CH.2.BSB: Then Solomon sent word to Hiram king of Tyre: “Do for me as you did for my father David when you sent him cedars to build himself a house to live in.
2CH.2.KJV: And Solomon sent to Huram the king of Tyre, saying, As you did deal with David my father, and did send him cedars to build him an house to dwell therein, even so deal with me.
2CH.2.PLAIN: Then Solomon sent word to Hiram king of Tyre: “Do for me as you did for my father David when you sent him cedars to build himself a house to live in.

2CH.2.BSB: Behold, I am about to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God to dedicate to Him for burning fragrant incense before Him, for displaying the showbread continuously, and for making burnt offerings every morning and evening as well as on the Sabbaths, New Moons, and appointed feasts of the LORD our God. This is ordained for Israel forever.
2CH.2.KJV: Behold, I build an house to the name of the LORD my God, to dedicate it to him, and to burn before him sweet incense, and for the continual show bread, and for the burnt offerings morning and evening, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts of the LORD our God. This is an ordinance for ever to Israel.
2CH.2.PLAIN: Look closely — I am about to build a house for the Name of the Lord my God to dedicate to Him for burning fragrant incense before Him, for displaying the showbread continuously, and for making burnt offerings every morning and evening as well as on the Sabbaths, New Moons, and appointed feasts of the Lord our God. This is ordained for Israel forever.

2CH.2.BSB: The house that I am building will be great, for our God is greater than all gods.
2CH.2.KJV: And the house which I build is great: for great is our God above all gods.
2CH.2.PLAIN: The house that I am building will be great, for our God is greater than all gods.

2CH.2.BSB: But who is able to build a house for Him, since the heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain Him? Who then am I, that I should build a house for Him, except as a place to burn sacrifices before Him?
2CH.2.KJV: But who is able to build him an house, seeing the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain him? who am I then, that I should build him an house, save only to burn sacrifice before him?
2CH.2.PLAIN: But who is able to build a house for Him, since the heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain Him? Who then am I, that I should build a house for Him, except as a place to burn sacrifices before Him?

2CH.2.BSB: Send me, therefore, a craftsman skilled in engraving to work with gold and silver, with bronze and iron, and with purple, crimson, and blue yarn. He will work with my craftsmen in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David provided.
2CH.2.KJV: Send me now therefore a man cunning to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass, and in iron, and in purple, and crimson, and blue, and that can skill to grave with the cunning men that are with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom David my father did provide.
2CH.2.PLAIN: Send me, therefore, a craftsman skilled in engraving to work with gold and silver, with bronze and iron, and with purple, crimson, and blue yarn. He will work with my craftsmen in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David provided.

2CH.2.BSB: Send me also cedar, cypress, and algum logs from Lebanon, for I know that your servants have skill to cut timber there. And indeed, my servants will work with yours
2CH.2.KJV: Send me also cedar trees, fir trees, and algum trees, out of Lebanon: for I know that your servants can skill to cut timber in Lebanon; and, behold, my servants shall be with your servants,
2CH.2.PLAIN: Send me also cedar, cypress, and algum logs from Lebanon, for I know that your servants have skill to cut timber there. And indeed, my servants will work with yours

2CH.2.BSB: to prepare for me timber in abundance, because the temple I am building will be great and wonderful.
2CH.2.KJV: Even to prepare me timber in abundance: for the house which I am about to build shall be wonderful great.
2CH.2.PLAIN: to prepare for me timber in abundance, because the temple I am building will be great and wonderful.

2CH.2.BSB: I will pay your servants, the woodcutters, 20,000 cors of ground wheat, 20,000 cors of barley, 20,000 baths of wine, and 20,000 baths of olive oil.”
2CH.2.KJV: And, behold, I will give to your servants, the hewers that cut timber, twenty thousand measures of beaten wheat, and twenty thousand measures of barley, and twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil. ¶
2CH.2.PLAIN: I will pay your servants, the woodcutters, 20,000 cors of ground wheat, 20,000 cors of barley, 20,000 baths of wine, and 20,000 baths of olive oil.”

2CH.2.BSB: Then Hiram king of Tyre wrote a letter in reply to Solomon: “Because the LORD loves His people, He has set you over them as king.”
2CH.2.KJV: Then Huram the king of Tyre answered in writing, which he sent to Solomon, Because the LORD has loved his people, he has made you king over them.
2CH.2.PLAIN: Then Hiram king of Tyre wrote a letter in reply to Solomon: “Because the Lord loves His people, He has set you over them as king.”

2CH.2.BSB: And Hiram added: “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth! He has given King David a wise son with insight and understanding, who will build a temple for the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
2CH.2.KJV: Huram said moreover, Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, that made heaven and earth, who has given to David the king a wise son, endued with prudence and understanding, that might build an house for the LORD, and an house for his kingdom.
2CH.2.PLAIN: And Hiram added: “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth! He has given King David a wise son with insight and understanding, who will build a temple for the Lord and a royal palace for himself.

2CH.2.BSB: So now I am sending you Huram-abi, a skillful man endowed with creativity.
2CH.2.KJV: And now I have sent a cunning man, endued with understanding, of Huram my father’s,
2CH.2.PLAIN: So now I am sending you Huram-abi, a skillful man endowed with creativity.

2CH.2.BSB: He is the son of a woman from the daughters of Dan, and his father is a man of Tyre. He is skilled in work with gold and silver, bronze and iron, stone and wood, purple, blue, and crimson yarn, and fine linen. He is experienced in every kind of engraving and can execute any design that is given him. He will work with your craftsmen and with those of my lord, your father David.
2CH.2.KJV: The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre, skillful to work in gold, and in silver, in brass, in iron, in stone, and in timber, in purple, in blue, and in fine linen, and in crimson; also to grave any manner of engraving, and to find out every device which shall be put to him, with your cunning men, and with the cunning men of my lord David your father.
2CH.2.PLAIN: He is the son of a woman from the daughters of Dan, and his father is a man of Tyre. He is skilled in work with gold and silver, bronze and iron, stone and wood, purple, blue, and crimson yarn, and fine linen. He is experienced in every kind of engraving and can execute any design that is given him. He will work with your craftsmen and with those of my lord, your father David.

2CH.2.BSB: Now let my lord send to his servants the wheat, barley, olive oil, and wine he promised.
2CH.2.KJV: Now therefore the wheat, and the barley, the oil, and the wine, which my lord has spoken of, let him send to his servants:
2CH.2.PLAIN: Now let my lord send to his servants the wheat, barley, olive oil, and wine he promised.

2CH.2.BSB: We will cut logs from Lebanon, as many as you need, and we will float them to you as rafts by sea down to Joppa. Then you can take them up to Jerusalem.”
2CH.2.KJV: And we will cut wood out of Lebanon, as much as you shall need: and we will bring it to you in floats by sea to Joppa; and you shall carry it up to Jerusalem. ¶
2CH.2.PLAIN: We will cut logs from Lebanon, as many as you need, and we will float them to you as rafts by sea down to Joppa. Then you can take them up to Jerusalem.”

2CH.2.BSB: Solomon numbered all the foreign men in the land of Israel following the census his father David had conducted, and there were found to be 153,600 in all.
2CH.2.KJV: And Solomon numbered all the strangers that were in the land of Israel, after the numbering with which David his father had numbered them; and they were found an hundred and fifty thousand and three thousand and six hundred.
2CH.2.PLAIN: Solomon numbered all the foreign men in the land of Israel following the census his father David had conducted, and there were found to be 153,600 in all.

2CH.2.BSB: Solomon made 70,000 of them porters, 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains, and 3,600 supervisors.
2CH.2.KJV: And he set three score and ten thousand of them to be bearers of burdens, and fourscore thousand to be hewers in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred overseers to set the people a work.
2CH.2.PLAIN: Solomon made 70,000 of them porters, 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains, and 3,600 supervisors.

2CH.3.BSB: Then Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to his father David. This was the place that David had prepared on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
2CH.3.KJV: Then Solomon began to build the house of the LORD at Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where the Lord appeared to David his father, in the place that David had prepared in the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
2CH.3.PLAIN: Then Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the Lord had appeared to his father David. This was the place that David had prepared on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

2CH.3.BSB: Solomon began construction on the second day of the second month in the fourth year of his reign.
2CH.3.KJV: And he began to build in the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign. ¶
2CH.3.PLAIN: Solomon began construction on the second day of the second month in the fourth year of his reign.

2CH.3.BSB: The foundation that Solomon laid for the house of God was sixty cubits long and twenty cubits wide, according to the old standard.
2CH.3.KJV: Now these are the things wherein Solomon was instructed for the building of the house of God. The length by cubits after the first measure was three score cubits, and the breadth twenty cubits.
2CH.3.PLAIN: The foundation that Solomon laid for the house of God was sixty cubits long and twenty cubits wide, according to the old standard.

2CH.3.BSB: The portico at the front, extending across the width of the temple, was twenty cubits long and twenty cubits high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold.
2CH.3.KJV: And the porch that was in the front of the house, the length of it was according to the breadth of the house, twenty cubits, and the height was an hundred and twenty: and he overlaid it within with pure gold.
2CH.3.PLAIN: The portico at the front, extending across the width of the temple, was twenty cubits long and twenty cubits high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold.

2CH.3.BSB: He paneled the main room with cypress, which he overlaid with fine gold and decorated with palm trees and chains.
2CH.3.KJV: And the greater house he paneled with fir tree, which he overlaid with fine gold, and set thereon palm trees and chains.
2CH.3.PLAIN: He paneled the main room with cypress, which he overlaid with fine gold and decorated with palm trees and chains.

2CH.3.BSB: He adorned the temple with precious stones for beauty, and its gold was from Parvaim.
2CH.3.KJV: And he garnished the house with precious stones for beauty: and the gold was gold of Parvaim.
2CH.3.PLAIN: He adorned the temple with precious stones for beauty, and its gold was from Parvaim.

2CH.3.BSB: He overlaid its beams, thresholds, walls, and doors with gold, and he carved cherubim on the walls.
2CH.3.KJV: He overlaid also the house, the beams, the posts, and the walls thereof, and the doors thereof, with gold; and graved cherubim on the walls.
2CH.3.PLAIN: He overlaid its beams, thresholds, walls, and doors with gold, and he carved cherubim on the walls.

2CH.3.BSB: Then he made the Most Holy Place; its length corresponded to the width of the temple—twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. And he overlaid the inside with six hundred talents of fine gold.
2CH.3.KJV: And he made the most holy house, the length whereof was according to the breadth of the house, twenty cubits, and the breadth thereof twenty cubits: and he overlaid it with fine gold, amounting to six hundred talents.
2CH.3.PLAIN: Then he made the Most Holy Place; its length corresponded to the width of the temple—twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. And he overlaid the inside with six hundred talents of fine gold.

2CH.3.BSB: The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He also overlaid the upper area with gold.
2CH.3.KJV: And the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. And he overlaid the upper chambers with gold.
2CH.3.PLAIN: The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He also overlaid the upper area with gold.

2CH.3.BSB: In the Most Holy Place he made two cherubim of sculptured work, and he overlaid them with gold.
2CH.3.KJV: And in the most holy house he made two cherubim of image work, and overlaid them with gold. ¶
2CH.3.PLAIN: In the Most Holy Place he made two cherubim of sculptured work, and he overlaid them with gold.

2CH.3.BSB: The total wingspan of the cherubim was twenty cubits. One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long and touched the wall of the temple, and its other wing was five cubits long and touched the wing of the other cherub.
2CH.3.KJV: And the wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits long: one wing of the one cherub was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house: and the other wing was likewise five cubits, reaching to the wing of the other cherub.
2CH.3.PLAIN: The total wingspan of the cherubim was twenty cubits. One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long and touched the wall of the temple, and its other wing was five cubits long and touched the wing of the other cherub.

2CH.3.BSB: The wing of the second cherub also measured five cubits and touched the wall of the temple, while its other wing measured five cubits and touched the wing of the first cherub.
2CH.3.KJV: And one wing of the other cherub was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house: and the other wing was five cubits also, joining to the wing of the other cherub.
2CH.3.PLAIN: The wing of the second cherub also measured five cubits and touched the wall of the temple, while its other wing measured five cubits and touched the wing of the first cherub.

2CH.3.BSB: So the total wingspan of these cherubim was twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, facing the main room.
2CH.3.KJV: The wings of these cherubim spread themselves forth twenty cubits: and they stood on their feet, and their faces were inward. ¶
2CH.3.PLAIN: So the total wingspan of these cherubim was twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, facing the main room.

2CH.3.BSB: He made the veil of blue, purple, and crimson yarn and fine linen, with cherubim woven into it.
2CH.3.KJV: And he made the veil of blue, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen, and worked cherubim thereon.
2CH.3.PLAIN: He made the veil of blue, purple, and crimson yarn and fine linen, with cherubim woven into it.

2CH.3.BSB: In front of the temple he made two pillars, which together were thirty-five cubits high, each with a capital on top measuring five cubits.
2CH.3.KJV: Also he made before the house two pillars of thirty and five cubits high, and the capital that was on the top of each of them was five cubits.
2CH.3.PLAIN: In front of the temple he made two pillars, which together were thirty-five cubits high, each with a capital on top measuring five cubits.

2CH.3.BSB: He made interwoven chains and put them on top of the pillars. He made a hundred pomegranates and fastened them into the chainwork.
2CH.3.KJV: And he made chains, as in the oracle, and put them on the heads of the pillars; and made an hundred pomegranates, and put them on the chains.
2CH.3.PLAIN: He made interwoven chains and put them on top of the pillars. He made a hundred pomegranates and fastened them into the chainwork.

2CH.3.BSB: Then he set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the south and one on the north. The pillar on the south he named Jachin, and the pillar on the north he named Boaz.
2CH.3.KJV: And he reared up the pillars before the temple, one on the right hand, and the other on the left; and called the name of that on the right hand Jachin, and the name of that on the left Boaz.
2CH.3.PLAIN: Then he set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the south and one on the north. The pillar on the south he named Jachin, and the pillar on the north he named Boaz.

2CH.4.BSB: He made a bronze altar twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
2CH.4.KJV: Moreover he made an altar of brass, twenty cubits the length thereof, and twenty cubits the breadth thereof, and ten cubits the height thereof. ¶
2CH.4.PLAIN: He made a bronze altar twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.

2CH.4.BSB: He also made the Sea of cast metal. It was circular in shape, measuring ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits in height, and thirty cubits in circumference.
2CH.4.KJV: Also he made a molten sea of ten cubits from brim to brim, round in compass, and five cubits the height thereof; and a line of thirty cubits did compass it round about.
2CH.4.PLAIN: He also made the Sea of cast metal. It was circular in shape, measuring ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits in height, and thirty cubits in circumference.

2CH.4.BSB: Below the rim, figures of oxen encircled it, ten per cubit all the way around the Sea, cast in two rows as a part of the Sea.
2CH.4.KJV: And under it was the similitude of oxen, which did compass it round about: ten in a cubit, compassing the sea round about. Two rows of oxen were cast, when it was cast.
2CH.4.PLAIN: Below the rim, figures of oxen encircled it, ten per cubit all the way around the Sea, cast in two rows as a part of the Sea.

2CH.4.BSB: The Sea stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The Sea rested on them, with all their hindquarters toward the center.
2CH.4.KJV: It stood on twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east: and the sea was set above on them, and all their hinder parts were inward.
2CH.4.PLAIN: The Sea stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The Sea rested on them, with all their hindquarters toward the center.

2CH.4.BSB: It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was fashioned like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It could hold three thousand baths.
2CH.4.KJV: And the thickness of it was an handbreadth, and the brim of it like the work of the brim of a cup, with flowers of lilies; and it received and held three thousand baths. ¶
2CH.4.PLAIN: It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was fashioned like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It could hold three thousand baths.

2CH.4.BSB: He also made ten basins for washing and placed five on the south side and five on the north. The parts of the burnt offering were rinsed in them, but the priests used the Sea for washing.
2CH.4.KJV: He made also ten lavers, and put five on the right hand, and five on the left, to wash in them: such things as they offered for the burnt offering they washed in them; but the sea was for the priests to wash in.
2CH.4.PLAIN: He also made ten basins for washing and placed five on the south side and five on the north. The parts of the burnt offering were rinsed in them, but the priests used the Sea for washing.

2CH.4.BSB: He made ten gold lampstands according to their specifications and placed them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north.
2CH.4.KJV: And he made ten candlesticks of gold according to their form, and set them in the temple, five on the right hand, and five on the left.
2CH.4.PLAIN: He made ten gold lampstands according to their specifications and placed them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north.

2CH.4.BSB: Additionally, he made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north. He also made a hundred gold bowls.
2CH.4.KJV: He made also ten tables, and placed them in the temple, five on the right side, and five on the left. And he made an hundred basins of gold. ¶

2CH.12.KJV: Then came Shemaiah the prophet to Rehoboam, and to the princes of Judah, that were gathered together to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said to them, Thus says the LORD, You have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak.
2CH.12.PLAIN: Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah who had gathered at Jerusalem because of Shishak, and he said to them, “This is what the Lord says: ‘You have forsaken Me; therefore, I have forsaken you into the hand of Shishak.’”

2CH.12.BSB: So the leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, “The LORD is righteous.”
2CH.12.KJV: Whereupon the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves; and they said, The LORD is righteous.
2CH.12.PLAIN: So the leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, “The Lord is righteous.”

2CH.12.KJV: Nevertheless they shall be his servants; that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.

2CH.12.BSB: So King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem and seized the treasures of the house of the LORD and of the royal palace. He took everything, including the gold shields that Solomon had made.
2CH.12.KJV: So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, and took away the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king’s house; he took all: he carried away also the shields of gold which Solomon had made.
2CH.12.PLAIN: So King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem and seized the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the royal palace. He took everything, including the gold shields that Solomon had made.

2CH.12.BSB: Then King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place and committed them to the care of the captains of the guard on duty at the entrance to the royal palace.

2CH.12.PLAIN: Then King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place and committed them to the care of the captains of the guard on duty at the entrance to the royal palace.

2CH.12.BSB: And whenever the king entered the house of the LORD, the guards would go with him, bearing the shields, and later they would return them to the guardroom.
2CH.12.KJV: And when the king entered into the house of the LORD, the guard came and fetched them, and brought them again into the guard chamber.
2CH.12.PLAIN: And whenever the king entered the house of the Lord, the guards would go with him, bearing the shields, and later they would return them to the guardroom.

2CH.12.BSB: Because Rehoboam humbled himself, the anger of the LORD turned away from him, and He did not destroy him completely. Indeed, conditions were good in Judah.

2CH.12.PLAIN: Because Rehoboam humbled himself, the anger of the Lord turned away from him, and He did not destroy him completely. Indeed, conditions were good in Judah.

2CH.12.BSB: Thus King Rehoboam established himself in Jerusalem. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel in which to put His Name. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonite.
2CH.12.KJV: So king Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem, and reigned: for Rehoboam was one and forty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there. 2CH.12.PLAIN: Thus King Rehoboam established himself in Jerusalem. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the Lord had chosen from all the tribes of Israel in which to put His Name. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonite.

2CH.12.BSB: And Rehoboam did evil because he did not set his heart to seek the LORD.
2CH.12.KJV: And he did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek the LORD.
2CH.12.PLAIN: And Rehoboam did evil because he did not set his heart to seek the Lord.

2CH.12.BSB: Now the acts of Rehoboam, from first to last, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the Prophet and of Iddo the Seer concerning the genealogies? There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout their days.
2CH.12.KJV: Now the acts of Rehoboam, first and last, are they not written in the book of Shemaiah the prophet, and of Iddo the seer concerning genealogies? And there were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
2CH.12.PLAIN: Now the acts of Rehoboam, from first to last, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the Prophet and of Iddo the Seer concerning the genealogies? There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout their days.

2CH.12.BSB: And Rehoboam rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. And his son Abijah reigned in his place.
2CH.12.KJV: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David: and Abijah his son reigned in his stead.
2CH.12.PLAIN: And Rehoboam rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. And his son Abijah reigned in his place.

2CH.13.PLAIN: In the eighteenth year of Jeroboam’s reign, Abijah became king of Judah,

2CH.13.BSB: and he reigned in Jerusalem three years. His mother’s name was Micaiah daughter of Uriel; she was from Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
2CH.13.KJV: He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Michaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
2CH.13.PLAIN: and he reigned in Jerusalem three years. His mother’s name was Micaiah daughter of Uriel; she was from Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

2CH.13.KJV: And Abijah set the battle in array with an army of valiant men of war, even four hundred thousand chosen men: Jeroboam also set the battle in array against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, being mighty men of valor. ¶

2CH.13.BSB: Then Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim in the hill country of Ephraim and said, “Hear me, O Jeroboam and all Israel!
2CH.13.KJV: And Abijah stood up on mount Zemaraim, which is in mount Ephraim, and said, Hear me, you Jeroboam, and all Israel;
2CH.13.PLAIN: Then Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim in the hill country of Ephraim and said, “Hear me, O Jeroboam and all Israel!

2CH.13.BSB: Do you not know that the LORD, the God of Israel, has given the kingship of Israel to David and his descendants forever by a covenant of salt?
2CH.13.KJV: Ought you not to know that the LORD God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
2CH.13.PLAIN: Do you not know that the Lord, the God of Israel, has given the kingship of Israel to David and his descendants forever by a covenant of salt?

2CH.13.BSB: Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master.
2CH.13.KJV: Yet Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon the son of David, is risen up, and has rebelled against his lord.
2CH.13.PLAIN: Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master.

2CH.13.BSB: Then worthless and wicked men gathered around him to resist Rehoboam son of Solomon when he was young, inexperienced, and unable to resist them.
2CH.13.KJV: And there are gathered to him vain men, the children of Belial, and have strengthened themselves against Rehoboam the son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and tenderhearted, and could not withstand them.
2CH.13.PLAIN: Then worthless and wicked men gathered around him to resist Rehoboam son of Solomon when he was young, inexperienced, and unable to resist them.

2CH.13.BSB: And now you think you can resist the kingdom of the LORD, which is in the hands of David’s descendants. You are indeed a vast army, and you have with you the golden calves that Jeroboam made for you as gods.
2CH.13.KJV: And now you think to withstand the kingdom of the LORD in the hand of the sons of David; and you be a great multitude, and there are with your golden calves, which Jeroboam made you for gods.
2CH.13.PLAIN: And now you think you can resist the kingdom of the Lord, which is in the hands of David’s descendants. You are indeed a vast army, and you have with you the golden calves that Jeroboam made for you as gods.

2CH.13.BSB: But did you not drive out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites? And did you not make priests for yourselves as do the peoples of other lands? Now whoever comes to consecrate himself with a young bull and seven rams can become a priest of things that are not gods.
2CH.13.KJV: Have you not cast out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and have made you priests after the manner of the nations of other lands? so that whoever comes to consecrate himself with a young bullock and seven rams, the same may be a priest of them that are no gods.

2CH.13.BSB: But as for us, the LORD is our God. We have not forsaken Him; the priests who minister to the LORD are sons of Aaron, and the Levites attend to their duties.
2CH.13.KJV: But as for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not forsaken him; and the priests, which minister to the LORD, are the sons of Aaron, and the Levites wait on their business:

2CH.13.BSB: Every morning and every evening they present burnt offerings and fragrant incense to the LORD. They set out the rows of showbread on the ceremonially clean table, and every evening they light the lamps of the gold lampstand. We are carrying out the requirements of the LORD our God, while you have forsaken Him.
2CH.13.KJV: And they burn to the LORD every morning and every evening burnt sacrifices and sweet incense: the show bread also set they in order on the pure table; and the candlestick of gold with the lamps thereof, to burn every evening: for we keep the charge of the LORD our God; but you have forsaken him.
2CH.13.PLAIN: Every morning and every evening they present burnt offerings and fragrant incense to the Lord. They set out the rows of showbread on the ceremonially clean table, and every evening they light the lamps of the gold lampstand. We are carrying out the requirements of the Lord our God, while you have forsaken Him.

2CH.13.BSB: Now behold, God Himself is with us as our head, and His priests with their trumpets sound the battle call against you. O children of Israel, do not fight against the LORD, the God of your fathers, for you will not succeed.”
2CH.13.KJV: And, behold, God himself is with us for our captain, and his priests with sounding trumpets to cry alarm against you. O children of Israel, fight you not against the LORD God of your fathers; for you shall not prosper. ¶

2CH.13.BSB: Now Jeroboam had sent troops around to ambush from the rear, so that while he was in front of Judah, the ambush was behind them.

2CH.13.PLAIN: Now Jeroboam had sent troops around to ambush from the rear, so that while he was in front of Judah, the ambush was behind them.

2CH.13.KJV: Then the men of Judah gave a shout: and as the men of Judah shouted, it came to pass, that God smote Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
2CH.13.PLAIN: and the men of Judah raised the battle cry. And when they raised the cry, God routed Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.

2CH.13.PLAIN: So the Israelites fled before Judah, and God delivered them into their hands.

2CH.13.KJV: And Abijah and his people slew them with a great slaughter: so there fell down slain of Israel five hundred thousand chosen men.
2CH.13.PLAIN: Then Abijah and his people struck them with a mighty blow, and 500,000 chosen men of Israel fell slain.

2CH.13.KJV: Thus the children of Israel were brought under at that time, and the children of Judah prevailed, because they relied on the LORD God of their fathers.
2CH.13.PLAIN: Thus the Israelites were subdued at that time, and the men of Judah prevailed because they relied on the Lord, the God of their fathers.

2CH.13.BSB: Abijah pursued Jeroboam and captured some cities from him: Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, along with their villages.
2CH.13.KJV: And Abijah pursued after Jeroboam, and took cities from him, Bethel with the towns thereof, and Jeshanah with the towns thereof, and Ephraim with the towns thereof.
2CH.13.PLAIN: Abijah pursued Jeroboam and captured some cities from him: Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, along with their villages.

2CH.13.PLAIN: Jeroboam did not again recover his power during the days of Abijah, and the Lord struck him down and he died.

2CH.13.KJV: But Abijah waxed mighty, and married fourteen wives, and begat twenty and two sons, and sixteen daughters.

2CH.14.PLAIN: Then Abijah rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. And his son Asa reigned in his place, and in his days the land was at peace for ten years.

2CH.14.KJV: And Asa did that which was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God:
2CH.14.PLAIN: And Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the Lord his God.

2CH.14.KJV: For he took away the altars of the strange gods, and the high places, and broke down the images, and cut down the groves:
2CH.14.PLAIN: He removed the foreign altars and high places, shattered the sacred pillars, and chopped down the Asherah poles.

2CH.14.BSB: He commanded the people of Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, and to observe the law and the commandments.
2CH.14.KJV: And commanded Judah to seek the LORD God of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandment.
2CH.14.PLAIN: He commanded the people of Judah to seek the Lord, the God of their fathers, and to observe the law and the commandments.

2CH.14.BSB: He also removed the high places and incense altars from all the cities of Judah, and under him the kingdom was at peace.
2CH.14.KJV: Also he took away out of all the cities of Judah the high places and the images: and the kingdom was quiet before him. ¶
2CH.14.PLAIN: He also removed the high places and incense altars from all the cities of Judah, and under him the kingdom was at peace.

2CH.14.BSB: So he said to the people of Judah, “Let us build these cities and surround them with walls and towers, with doors and bars. The land is still ours because we have sought the LORD our God. We have sought Him and He has given us rest on every side.” So they built and prospered.
2CH.14.KJV: Therefore he said to Judah, Let us build these cities, and make about them walls, and towers, gates, and bars, while the land is yet before us; because we have sought the LORD our God, we have sought him, and he has given us rest on every side. So they built and prospered.
2CH.14.PLAIN: So he said to the people of Judah, “Let us build these cities and surround them with walls and towers, with doors and bars. The land is still ours because we have sought the Lord our God. We have sought Him and He has given us rest on every side.” So they built and prospered.

2CH.14.BSB: Asa had an army of 300,000 men from Judah bearing large shields and spears, and 280,000 men from Benjamin bearing small shields and drawing the bow. All these were mighty men of valor.
2CH.14.KJV: And Asa had an army of men that bore targets and spears, out of Judah three hundred thousand; and out of Benjamin, that bore shields and drew bows, two hundred and fourscore thousand: all these were mighty men of valor. ¶
2CH.14.PLAIN: Asa had an army of 300,000 men from Judah bearing large shields and spears, and 280,000 men from Benjamin bearing small shields and drawing the bow. All these were mighty men of valor.

2CH.14.KJV: And there came out against them Zerah the Ethiopian with an host of a thousand thousand, and three hundred chariots; and came to Mareshah.
2CH.14.PLAIN: Then Zerah the Cushite came against them with an army of 1,000,000 men and 300 chariots, and they advanced as far as Mareshah.

2CH.14.KJV: Then Asa went out against him, and they set the battle in array in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.
2CH.14.PLAIN: So Asa marched out against him and lined up in battle formation in the Valley of Zephathah near Mareshah.

2CH.14.KJV: And Asa cried to the LORD his God, and said, LORD, it is nothing with you to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O LORD our God; for we rest on you, and in your name we go against this multitude. O LORD, you are our God; let no man prevail against you.
2CH.14.PLAIN: Then Asa cried out to the Lord his God: “O Lord, there is no one besides You to help the powerless against the mighty. 2CH.14.KJV: And Asa and the people that were with him pursued them to Gerar: and the Ethiopians were overthrown, that they could not recover themselves; for they were destroyed before the LORD, and before his host; and they carried away very much spoil.
2CH.14.PLAIN: Then Asa and his army pursued them as far as Gerar. The Cushites fell and could not recover, for they were crushed before the Lord and His army. So the people of Judah carried off a great amount of plunder

2CH.14.BSB: and attacked all the cities around Gerar, because the terror of the LORD had fallen upon them. They plundered all the cities, since there was much plunder there.
2CH.14.KJV: And they smote all the cities round about Gerar; for the fear of the LORD came on them: and they spoiled all the cities; for there was exceeding much spoil in them.
2CH.14.PLAIN: and attacked all the cities around Gerar, because the terror of the Lord had fallen upon them. They plundered all the cities, since there was much plunder there.

2CH.14.BSB: They also attacked the tents of the herdsmen and carried off many sheep and camels. Then they returned to Jerusalem.
2CH.14.KJV: They smote also the tents of cattle, and carried away sheep and camels in abundance, and returned to Jerusalem.
2CH.14.PLAIN: They also attacked the tents of the herdsmen and carried off many sheep and camels. Then they returned to Jerusalem.

2CH.15.BSB: Now the Spirit of God came upon Azariah son of Oded.
2CH.15.KJV: And the Spirit of God came on Azariah the son of Oded:
2CH.15.PLAIN: Now the Spirit of God came upon Azariah son of Oded.

2CH.15.BSB: So he went out to meet Asa and said to him, “Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin. The LORD is with you when you are with Him. If you seek Him, He will be found by you, but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you.
2CH.15.KJV: And he went out to meet Asa, and said to him, Hear you me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin; The LORD is with you, while you be with him; and if you seek him, he will be found of you; but if you forsake him, he will forsake you.
2CH.15.PLAIN: So he went out to meet Asa and said to him, “Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin. The Lord is with you when you are with Him. If you seek Him, He will be found by you, but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you.

2CH.15.BSB: For many years Israel has been without the true God, without a priest to instruct them, and without the law.
2CH.15.KJV: Now for a long season Israel has been without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.
2CH.15.PLAIN: For many years Israel has been without the true God, without a priest to instruct them, and without the law.

2CH.15.BSB: But in their distress they turned to the LORD, the God of Israel, and sought Him, and He was found by them.
2CH.15.KJV: But when they in their trouble did turn to the LORD God of Israel, and sought him, he was found of them.
2CH.15.PLAIN: But in their distress they turned to the Lord, the God of Israel, and sought Him, and He was found by them.

2CH.15.BSB: In those days there was no safety for travelers, because the residents of the lands had many conflicts.
2CH.15.KJV: And in those times there was no peace to him that went out, nor to him that came in, but great vexations were on all the inhabitants of the countries.
2CH.15.PLAIN: In those days there was no safety for travelers, because the residents of the lands had many conflicts.

2CH.15.BSB: Nation was crushed by nation, and city by city, for God afflicted them with all kinds of adversity.
2CH.15.KJV: And nation was destroyed of nation, and city of city: for God did vex them with all adversity.
2CH.15.PLAIN: Nation was crushed by nation, and city by city, for God afflicted them with all kinds of adversity.

2CH.15.BSB: But as for you, be strong; do not be discouraged, for your work will be rewarded.”
2CH.15.KJV: Be you strong therefore, and let not your hands be weak: for your work shall be rewarded.
2CH.15.PLAIN: But as for you, be strong; do not be discouraged, for your work will be rewarded.”

2CH.15.BSB: When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Azariah son of Oded the prophet, he took courage and removed the detestable idols from the whole land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim. He then restored the altar of the LORD that was in front of the portico of the LORD’s temple.
2CH.15.KJV: And when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from mount Ephraim, and renewed the altar of the LORD, that was before the porch of the LORD.
2CH.15.PLAIN: When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Azariah son of Oded the prophet, he took courage and removed the detestable idols from the whole land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim. He then restored the altar of the Lord that was in front of the portico of the Lord’s temple.

2CH.15.BSB: And he assembled all Judah and Benjamin, along with those from the tribes of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who had settled among them, for great numbers had come over to him from Israel when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
2CH.15.KJV: And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
2CH.15.PLAIN: And he assembled all Judah and Benjamin, along with those from the tribes of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who had settled among them, for great numbers had come over to him from Israel when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.

2CH.15.BSB: So they gathered together in Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa’s reign.
2CH.15.KJV: So they gathered themselves together at Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.
2CH.15.PLAIN: So they gathered together in Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa’s reign.

2CH.15.BSB: At that time they sacrificed to the LORD seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep from all the plunder they had brought back.
2CH.15.KJV: And they offered to the LORD the same time, of the spoil which they had brought, seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.
2CH.15.PLAIN: At that time they sacrificed to the Lord seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep from all the plunder they had brought back.

2CH.15.BSB: Then they entered into a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and soul.
2CH.15.KJV: And they entered into a covenant to seek the LORD God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul;
2CH.15.PLAIN: Then they entered into a covenant to seek the Lord, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and soul.

2CH.15.BSB: And whoever would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, would be put to death, whether young or old, man or woman.
2CH.15.KJV: That whoever would not seek the LORD God of Israel should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman.
2CH.15.PLAIN: And whoever would not seek the Lord, the God of Israel, would be put to death, whether young or old, man or woman.

2CH.15.BSB: They took an oath to the LORD with a loud voice, with shouting, trumpets, and rams’ horns.
2CH.15.KJV: And they swore to the LORD with a loud voice, and with shouting, and with trumpets, and with cornets.
2CH.15.PLAIN: They took an oath to the Lord with a loud voice, with shouting, trumpets, and rams’ horns.

2CH.15.BSB: And all Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn it with all their heart. They had sought Him earnestly, and He was found by them. So the LORD gave them rest on every side.
2CH.15.KJV: And all Judah rejoiced at the oath: for they had sworn with all their heart, and sought him with their whole desire; and he was found of them: and the LORD gave them rest round about. ¶
2CH.15.PLAIN: And all Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn it with all their heart. They had sought Him earnestly, and He was found by them. So the Lord gave them rest on every side.

2CH.15.BSB: King Asa also removed his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother because she had made a detestable Asherah pole. Asa chopped down the pole, crushed it, and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
2CH.15.KJV: And also concerning Maachah the mother of Asa the king, he removed her from being queen, because she had made an idol in a grove: and Asa cut down her idol, and stamped it, and burnt it at the brook Kidron.
2CH.15.PLAIN: King Asa also removed his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother because she had made a detestable Asherah pole. Asa chopped down the pole, crushed it, and burned it in the Kidron Valley.

2CH.15.BSB: The high places were not removed from Israel, but Asa’s heart was fully devoted all his days.
2CH.15.KJV: But the high places were not taken away out of Israel: nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect all his days. ¶
2CH.15.PLAIN: The high places were not removed from Israel, but Asa’s heart was fully devoted all his days.

2CH.15.BSB: And he brought into the house of God the silver and gold articles that he and his father had dedicated.
2CH.15.KJV: And he brought into the house of God the things that his father had dedicated, and that he himself had dedicated, silver, and gold, and vessels.
2CH.15.PLAIN: And he brought into the house of God the silver and gold articles that he and his father had dedicated.

2CH.15.BSB: And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.
2CH.15.KJV: And there was no more war to the five and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa.
2CH.15.PLAIN: And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.

2CH.16.BSB: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and fortified Ramah to prevent anyone from leaving or entering the territory of Asa king of Judah.
2CH.16.KJV: In the six and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah, and built Ramah, to the intent that he might let none go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
2CH.16.PLAIN: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and fortified Ramah to prevent anyone from leaving or entering the territory of Asa king of Judah.

2CH.16.BSB: So Asa withdrew the silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the royal palace, and he sent it with this message to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who was ruling in Damascus:
2CH.16.KJV: Then Asa brought out silver and gold out of the treasures of the house of the LORD and of the king’s house, and sent to Benhadad king of Syria, that dwelled at Damascus, saying,
2CH.16.PLAIN: So Asa withdrew the silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the Lord and the royal palace, and he sent it with this message to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who was ruling in Damascus:

2CH.16.BSB: “Let there be a treaty between me and you, between my father and your father. See, I have sent you silver and gold. Now go and break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me.”
2CH.16.KJV: There is a league between me and you, as there was between my father and your father: behold, I have sent you silver and gold; go, break your league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.
2CH.16.PLAIN: “Let there be a treaty between me and you, between my father and your father. See, I have sent you silver and gold. Now go and break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me.”

2CH.16.BSB: And Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, conquering Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.
2CH.16.KJV: And Benhadad listened to king Asa, and sent the captains of his armies against the cities of Israel; and they smote Ijon, and Dan, and Abelmaim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.
2CH.16.PLAIN: And Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, conquering Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.

2CH.16.BSB: When Baasha learned of this, he stopped fortifying Ramah and abandoned his work.
2CH.16.KJV: And it came to pass, when Baasha heard it, that he left off building of Ramah, and let his work cease.
2CH.16.PLAIN: When Baasha learned of this, he stopped fortifying Ramah and abandoned his work.

2CH.16.BSB: Then King Asa brought all the men of Judah, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and the timbers Baasha had used for building. And with these materials he built up Geba and Mizpah.
2CH.16.KJV: Then Asa the king took all Judah; and they carried away the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, with which Baasha was building; and he built therewith Geba and Mizpah. ¶
2CH.16.PLAIN: Then King Asa brought all the men of Judah, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and the timbers Baasha had used for building. And with these materials he built up Geba and Mizpah.

2CH.16.BSB: At that time Hanani the seer came to King Asa of Judah and told him, “Because you have relied on the king of Aram and not on the LORD your God, the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.
2CH.16.KJV: And at that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah, and said to him, Because you have relied on the king of Syria, and not relied on the LORD your God, therefore is the host of the king of Syria escaped out of your hand.
2CH.16.PLAIN: At that time Hanani the seer came to King Asa of Judah and told him, “Because you have relied on the king of Aram and not on the Lord your God, the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.

2CH.16.BSB: Were not the Cushites and Libyans a vast army with many chariots and horsemen? Yet because you relied on the LORD, He delivered them into your hand.
2CH.16.KJV: Were not the Ethiopians and the Lubims a huge host, with very many chariots and horsemen? yet, because you did rely on the LORD, he delivered them into your hand.
2CH.16.PLAIN: Were not the Cushites and Libyans a vast army with many chariots and horsemen? Yet because you relied on the Lord, He delivered them into your hand.

2CH.16.BSB: For the eyes of the LORD roam to and fro over all the earth, to show Himself strong on behalf of those whose hearts are fully devoted to Him. You have acted foolishly in this matter. From now on, therefore, you will be at war.”
2CH.16.KJV: For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to show himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. Herein you have done foolishly: therefore from now on you shall have wars.
2CH.16.PLAIN: For the eyes of the Lord range throughout the earth to strengthen those whose hearts are fully committed to him.

2CH.16.BSB: Asa was angry with the seer and became so enraged over this matter that he put the man in prison. And at the same time Asa oppressed some of the people.
2CH.16.KJV: Then Asa was wroth with the seer, and put him in a prison house; for he was in a rage with him because of this thing. And Asa oppressed some of the people the same time. ¶
2CH.16.PLAIN: Asa was angry with the seer and became so enraged over this matter that he put the man in prison. And at the same time Asa oppressed some of the people.

2CH.16.BSB: Now the rest of the acts of Asa, from beginning to end, are indeed written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
2CH.16.KJV: And, behold, the acts of Asa, first and last, see, they are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
2CH.16.PLAIN: Now the rest of the acts of Asa, from beginning to end, are indeed written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

2CH.16.BSB: In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa became diseased in his feet, and his malady became increasingly severe. Yet even in his illness he did not seek the LORD, but only the physicians.
2CH.16.KJV: And Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to the LORD, but to the physicians. ¶
2CH.16.PLAIN: In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa became diseased in his feet, and his malady became increasingly severe. Yet even in his illness he did not seek the Lord, but only the physicians.

2CH.16.BSB: So in the forty-first year of his reign, Asa died and rested with his fathers.
2CH.16.KJV: And Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the one and fortieth year of his reign.
2CH.16.PLAIN: So in the forty-first year of his reign, Asa died and rested with his fathers.

2CH.16.BSB: And he was buried in the tomb that he had cut out for himself in the City of David. They laid him on a bier that was full of spices and various blended perfumes; then they made a great fire in his honor.
2CH.16.KJV: And they buried him in his own sepulchers, which he had made for himself in the city of David, and laid him in the bed which was filled with sweet odors and divers kinds of spices prepared by the apothecaries’ are: and they made a very great burning for him.
2CH.16.PLAIN: And he was buried in the tomb that he had cut out for himself in the City of David. They laid him on a bier that was full of spices and various blended perfumes; then they made a great fire in his honor.

2CH.17.BSB: Asa’s son Jehoshaphat reigned in his place, and he strengthened himself against Israel.
2CH.17.KJV: And Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead, and strengthened himself against Israel.
2CH.17.PLAIN: Asa’s son Jehoshaphat reigned in his place, and he strengthened himself against Israel.

2CH.17.BSB: He stationed troops in every fortified city of Judah and put garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
2CH.17.KJV: And he placed forces in all the fenced cities of Judah, and set garrisons in the land of Judah, and in the cities of Ephraim, which Asa his father had taken.
2CH.17.PLAIN: He stationed troops in every fortified city of Judah and put garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.

2CH.17.BSB: Now the LORD was with Jehoshaphat because he walked in the earlier ways of his father David. He did not seek out the Baals,
2CH.17.KJV: And the LORD was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the first ways of his father David, and sought not to Baalim;
2CH.17.PLAIN: Now the Lord was with Jehoshaphat because he walked in the earlier ways of his father David. He did not seek out the Baals,

2CH.17.BSB: but he sought the God of his father and walked by His commandments rather than the practices of Israel.
2CH.17.KJV: But sought to the Lord God of his father, and walked in his commandments, and not after the doings of Israel.
2CH.17.PLAIN: but he sought the God of his father and walked by His commandments rather than the practices of Israel.

2CH.17.BSB: So the LORD established the kingdom in his hand, and all Judah brought him tribute, so that he had an abundance of riches and honor.
2CH.17.KJV: Therefore the LORD established the kingdom in his hand; and all Judah brought to Jehoshaphat presents; and he had riches and honor in abundance.
2CH.17.PLAIN: So the Lord established the kingdom in his hand, and all Judah brought him tribute, so that he had an abundance of riches and honor.

2CH.17.BSB: And his heart took delight in the ways of the LORD; furthermore, he removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah.
2CH.17.KJV: And his heart was lifted up in the ways of the LORD: moreover he took away the high places and groves out of Judah. ¶
2CH.17.PLAIN: And his heart took delight in the ways of the Lord; furthermore, he removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah.

2CH.17.BSB: In the third year of his reign, Jehoshaphat sent his officials Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah to teach in the cities of Judah,
2CH.17.KJV: Also in the third year of his reign he sent to his princes, even to Benhail, and to Obadiah, and to Zechariah, and to Nethaneel, and to Michaiah, to teach in the cities of Judah.
2CH.17.PLAIN: In the third year of his reign, Jehoshaphat sent his officials Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah to teach in the cities of Judah,

2CH.17.BSB: accompanied by certain Levites—Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah—along with the priests Elishama and Jehoram.
2CH.17.KJV: And with them he sent Levites, even Shemaiah, and Nethaniah, and Zebadiah, and Asahel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehonathan, and Adonijah, and Tobijah, and Tobadonijah, Levites; and with them Elishama and Jehoram, priests.
2CH.17.PLAIN: accompanied by certain Levites—Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah—along with the priests Elishama and Jehoram.

2CH.17.BSB: They taught throughout Judah, taking with them the Book of the Law of the LORD. They went throughout the towns of Judah and taught the people.
2CH.17.KJV: And they taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of the LORD with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people. ¶
2CH.17.PLAIN: They taught throughout Judah, taking with them the Book of the Law of the Lord. They went throughout the towns of Judah and taught the people.

2CH.17.BSB: And the dread of the LORD fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that surrounded Judah, so that they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.
2CH.17.KJV: And the fear of the LORD fell on all the kingdoms of the lands that were round about Judah, so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat.
2CH.17.PLAIN: And the dread of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that surrounded Judah, so that they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.

2CH.17.BSB: Some Philistines also brought gifts and silver as tribute to Jehoshaphat, and the Arabs brought him 7,700 rams and 7,700 goats from their flocks.
2CH.17.KJV: Also some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat presents, and tribute silver; and the Arabians brought him flocks, seven thousand and seven hundred rams, and seven thousand and seven hundred he goats. ¶
2CH.17.PLAIN: Some Philistines also brought gifts and silver as tribute to Jehoshaphat, and the Arabs brought him 7,700 rams and 7,700 goats from their flocks.

2CH.17.BSB: Jehoshaphat grew stronger and stronger, and he built fortresses and store cities in Judah
2CH.17.KJV: And Jehoshaphat waxed great exceedingly; and he built in Judah castles, and cities of store.
2CH.17.PLAIN: Jehoshaphat grew stronger and stronger, and he built fortresses and store cities in Judah

2CH.17.BSB: and kept vast supplies in the cities of Judah. He also had warriors in Jerusalem who were mighty men of valor.
2CH.17.KJV: And he had much business in the cities of Judah: and the men of war, mighty men of valor, were in Jerusalem.
2CH.17.PLAIN: and kept vast supplies in the cities of Judah. He also had warriors in Jerusalem who were mighty men of valor.

2CH.17.BSB: These are their numbers according to the houses of their fathers: From Judah, the commanders of thousands: Adnah the commander, and with him 300,000 mighty men of valor;
2CH.17.KJV: And these are the numbers of them according to the house of their fathers: Of Judah, the captains of thousands; Adnah the chief, and with him mighty men of valor three hundred thousand.
2CH.17.PLAIN: These are their numbers according to the houses of their fathers: From Judah, the commanders of thousands: Adnah the commander, and with him 300,000 mighty men of valor;

2CH.17.BSB: next to him, Jehohanan the commander, and with him 280,000;
2CH.17.KJV: And next to him was Jehohanan the captain, and with him two hundred and fourscore thousand.
2CH.17.PLAIN: next to him, Jehohanan the commander, and with him 280,000;

2CH.17.BSB: and next to him, Amasiah son of Zichri, the volunteer for the LORD, and with him 200,000 mighty men of valor.
2CH.17.KJV: And next him was Amasiah the son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself to the LORD; and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of valor.
2CH.17.PLAIN: and next to him, Amasiah son of Zichri, the volunteer for the Lord, and with him 200,000 mighty men of valor.

2CH.17.BSB: From Benjamin: Eliada, a mighty man of valor, and with him 200,000 armed with bows and shields;
2CH.17.KJV: And of Benjamin; Eliada a mighty man of valor, and with him armed men with bow and shield two hundred thousand.
2CH.17.PLAIN: From Benjamin: Eliada, a mighty man of valor, and with him 200,000 armed with bows and shields;

2CH.17.BSB: and next to him, Jehozabad, and with him 180,000 armed for battle.
2CH.17.KJV: And next him was Jehozabad, and with him an hundred and fourscore thousand ready prepared for the war.
2CH.17.PLAIN: and next to him, Jehozabad, and with him 180,000 armed for battle.

2CH.17.BSB: These were the men who served the king, besides those he stationed in the fortified cities throughout Judah.
2CH.17.KJV: These waited on the king, beside those whom the king put in the fenced cities throughout all Judah.
2CH.17.PLAIN: These were the men who served the king, besides those he stationed in the fortified cities throughout Judah.

2CH.18.BSB: Now Jehoshaphat had riches and honor in abundance, and he allied himself with Ahab by marriage.
2CH.18.KJV: Now Jehoshaphat had riches and honor in abundance, and joined affinity with Ahab.
2CH.18.PLAIN: Now Jehoshaphat had riches and honor in abundance, and he allied himself with Ahab by marriage.

2CH.18.BSB: And some years later he went down to visit Ahab in Samaria, where Ahab sacrificed many sheep and cattle for him and the people with him, and urged him to march up to Ramoth-gilead.
2CH.18.KJV: And after certain years he went down to Ahab to Samaria. And Ahab killed sheep and oxen for him in abundance, and for the people that he had with him, and persuaded him to go up with him to Ramothgilead.
2CH.18.PLAIN: And some years later he went down to visit Ahab in Samaria, where Ahab sacrificed many sheep and cattle for him and the people with him, and urged him to march up to Ramoth-gilead.

2CH.18.BSB: Ahab king of Israel asked Jehoshaphat king of Judah, “Will you go with me against Ramoth-gilead?” And Jehoshaphat replied, “I am like you, and my people are your people; we will join you in the war.”
2CH.18.KJV: And Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, Will you go with me to Ramothgilead? And he answered him, I am as you are, and my people as your people; and we will be with you in the war. ¶
2CH.18.PLAIN: Ahab king of Israel asked Jehoshaphat king of Judah, “Will you go with me against Ramoth-gilead?” And Jehoshaphat replied, “I am like you, and my people are your people; we will join you in the war.”

2CH.18.BSB: But Jehoshaphat also said to the king of Israel, “Please inquire first for the word of the LORD.”
2CH.18.KJV: And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, Inquire, I pray you, at the word of the LORD to day.
2CH.18.PLAIN: But Jehoshaphat also said to the king of Israel, “Please inquire first for the word of the Lord.”

2CH.18.BSB: So the king of Israel assembled the prophets, four hundred men, and asked them, “Should we go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or should we refrain?” “Go up,” they replied, “and God will deliver it into the hand of the king.”
2CH.18.KJV: Therefore the king of Israel gathered together of prophets four hundred men, and said to them, Shall we go to Ramothgilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And they said, Go up; for God will deliver it into the king’s hand.
2CH.18.PLAIN: So the king of Israel assembled the prophets, four hundred men, and asked them, “Should we go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or should we refrain?” “Go up,” they replied, “and God will deliver it into the hand of the king.”

2CH.18.BSB: But Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there not still a prophet of the LORD here of whom we can inquire?”
2CH.18.KJV: But Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the LORD besides, that we might inquire of him?
2CH.18.PLAIN: But Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there not still a prophet of the Lord here of whom we can inquire?”

2CH.18.BSB: The king of Israel answered, “There is still one man who can ask the LORD, but I hate him because he never prophesies anything good for me, but only bad. He is Micaiah son of Imlah.” “The king should not say that!” Jehoshaphat replied.
2CH.18.KJV: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, There is yet one man, by whom we may inquire of the LORD: but I hate him; for he never prophesied good to me, but always evil: the same is Micaiah the son of Imla. And Jehoshaphat said, Let not the king say so.
2CH.18.PLAIN: The king of Israel answered, “There is still one man who can ask the Lord, but I hate him because he never prophesies anything good for me, but only bad. He is Micaiah son of Imlah.” “The king should not say that!” Jehoshaphat replied.

2CH.18.BSB: So the king of Israel called one of his officials and said, “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah at once.”
2CH.18.KJV: And the king of Israel called for one of his officers, and said, Fetch quickly Micaiah the son of Imla.
