JOB.28.PLAIN: Far from human habitation he cuts a shaft in places forgotten by the foot of man. Far from men he dangles and sways.

JOB.28.BSB: Food may come from the earth, but from below it is transformed as by fire.
JOB.28.KJV: As for the earth, out of it comes bread: and under it is turned up as it were fire.
JOB.28.PLAIN: Food may come from the earth, but from below it is transformed as by fire.

JOB.28.BSB: Its rocks are the source of sapphires, containing flecks of gold.
JOB.28.KJV: The stones of it are the place of sapphires: and it has dust of gold.
JOB.28.PLAIN: Its rocks are the source of sapphires, containing flecks of gold.

JOB.28.BSB: No bird of prey knows that path; no falcon’s eye has seen it.
JOB.28.KJV: There is a path which no fowl knows, and which the vulture’s eye has not seen:
JOB.28.PLAIN: No bird of prey knows that path; no falcon’s eye has seen it.

JOB.28.BSB: Proud beasts have never trodden it; no lion has ever prowled over it.
JOB.28.KJV: The lion’s whelps have not trodden it, nor the fierce lion passed by it.
JOB.28.PLAIN: Proud beasts have never trodden it; no lion has ever prowled over it.

JOB.28.BSB: The miner strikes the flint; he overturns mountains at their base.
JOB.28.KJV: He puts forth his hand on the rock; he overturns the mountains by the roots.
JOB.28.PLAIN: The miner strikes the flint; he overturns mountains at their base.

JOB.28.BSB: He hews out channels in the rocks, and his eyes spot every treasure.
JOB.28.KJV: He cuts out rivers among the rocks; and his eye sees every precious thing.
JOB.28.PLAIN: He hews out channels in the rocks, and his eyes spot every treasure.

JOB.28.BSB: He stops up the sources of the streams to bring what is hidden to light.
JOB.28.KJV: He binds the floods from overflowing; and the thing that is hid brings he forth to light.
JOB.28.PLAIN: He stops up the sources of the streams to bring what is hidden to light.

JOB.28.BSB: But where can wisdom be found, and where does understanding dwell?
JOB.28.KJV: But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding?
JOB.28.PLAIN: But where can wisdom be found, and where does understanding dwell?

JOB.28.BSB: No man can know its value, nor is it found in the land of the living.
JOB.28.KJV: Man knows not the price thereof; neither is it found in the land of the living.
JOB.28.PLAIN: No man can know its value, nor is it found in the land of the living.

JOB.28.BSB: The ocean depths say, ‘It is not in me,’ while the sea declares, ‘It is not with me.’
JOB.28.KJV: The depth says, It is not in me: and the sea said, It is not with me.
JOB.28.PLAIN: The ocean depths say, ‘It is not in me,’ while the sea declares, ‘It is not with me.’

JOB.28.BSB: It cannot be bought with gold, nor can its price be weighed out in silver.
JOB.28.KJV: It cannot be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for the price thereof.
JOB.28.PLAIN: It cannot be bought with gold, nor can its price be weighed out in silver.

JOB.28.BSB: It cannot be valued in the gold of Ophir, in precious onyx or sapphire.
JOB.28.KJV: It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.
JOB.28.PLAIN: It cannot be valued in the gold of Ophir, in precious onyx or sapphire.

JOB.28.BSB: Neither gold nor crystal can compare to it, nor jewels of fine gold be exchanged for it.
JOB.28.KJV: The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it shall not be for jewels of fine gold.
JOB.28.PLAIN: Neither gold nor crystal can compare to it, nor jewels of fine gold be exchanged for it.

JOB.28.BSB: Coral and quartz are unworthy of mention; the price of wisdom is beyond rubies.
JOB.28.KJV: No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom is above rubies.
JOB.28.PLAIN: Coral and quartz are unworthy of mention; the price of wisdom is beyond rubies.

JOB.28.BSB: Topaz from Cush cannot compare to it, nor can it be valued in pure gold.
JOB.28.KJV: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, neither shall it be valued with pure gold.
JOB.28.PLAIN: Topaz from Cush cannot compare to it, nor can it be valued in pure gold.

JOB.28.BSB: From where then does wisdom come, and where does understanding dwell?
JOB.28.KJV: From where then comes wisdom? and where is the place of understanding?
JOB.28.PLAIN: From where then does wisdom come, and where does understanding dwell?

JOB.28.BSB: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing and concealed from the birds of the air.
JOB.28.KJV: Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the fowls of the air.
JOB.28.PLAIN: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing and concealed from the birds of the air.

JOB.28.BSB: Abaddon and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor about it.’
JOB.28.KJV: Destruction and death say, We have heard the fame thereof with our ears.
JOB.28.PLAIN: Abaddon and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor about it.’

JOB.28.BSB: But God understands its way, and He knows its place.
JOB.28.KJV: God understands the way thereof, and he knows the place thereof.
JOB.28.PLAIN: But God understands its way, and He knows its place.

JOB.28.BSB: For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.
JOB.28.KJV: For he looks to the ends of the earth, and sees under the whole heaven;
JOB.28.PLAIN: For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.

JOB.28.BSB: When God fixed the weight of the wind and measured out the waters,
JOB.28.KJV: To make the weight for the winds; and he weighs the waters by measure.
JOB.28.PLAIN: When God fixed the weight of the wind and measured out the waters,

JOB.28.BSB: when He set a limit for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,
JOB.28.KJV: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder:
JOB.28.PLAIN: when He set a limit for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,

JOB.28.BSB: then He looked at wisdom and appraised it; He established it and searched it out.
JOB.28.KJV: Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yes, and searched it out.
JOB.28.PLAIN: then He looked at wisdom and appraised it; He established it and searched it out.

JOB.28.BSB: And He said to man, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.’”
JOB.28.KJV: And to man he said, Behold, the fear of the LORD, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.
JOB.28.PLAIN: And He said to man, ‘Look closely — the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.’”

JOB.29.BSB: And Job continued his discourse:
JOB.29.KJV: Moreover Job continued his parable, and said,
JOB.29.PLAIN: And Job continued his discourse:

JOB.29.BSB: “How I long for the months gone by, for the days when God watched over me,
JOB.29.KJV: Oh that I were as in months past, as in the days when God preserved me;
JOB.29.PLAIN: “How I long for the months gone by, for the days when God watched over me,

JOB.29.BSB: when His lamp shone above my head, and by His light I walked through the darkness,
JOB.29.KJV: When his candle shined on my head, and when by his light I walked through darkness;
JOB.29.PLAIN: when His lamp shone above my head, and by His light I walked through the darkness,

JOB.29.BSB: when I was in my prime, when the friendship of God rested on my tent,
JOB.29.KJV: As I was in the days of my youth, when the secret of God was on my tabernacle;
JOB.29.PLAIN: when I was in my prime, when the friendship of God rested on my tent,

JOB.29.BSB: when the Almighty was still with me and my children were around me,
JOB.29.KJV: When the Almighty was yet with me, when my children were about me;
JOB.29.PLAIN: when the Almighty was still with me and my children were around me,

JOB.29.BSB: when my steps were bathed in cream and the rock poured out for me streams of oil!
JOB.29.KJV: When I washed my steps with butter, and the rock poured me out rivers of oil;
JOB.29.PLAIN: when my steps were bathed in cream and the rock poured out for me streams of oil!

JOB.29.BSB: When I went out to the city gate and took my seat in the public square,
JOB.29.KJV: When I went out to the gate through the city, when I prepared my seat in the street!
JOB.29.PLAIN: When I went out to the city gate and took my seat in the public square,

JOB.29.BSB: the young men saw me and withdrew, and the old men rose to their feet.
JOB.29.KJV: The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose, and stood up.
JOB.29.PLAIN: the young men saw me and withdrew, and the old men rose to their feet.

JOB.29.BSB: The princes refrained from speaking and covered their mouths with their hands.
JOB.29.KJV: The princes refrained talking, and laid their hand on their mouth.
JOB.29.PLAIN: The princes refrained from speaking and covered their mouths with their hands.

JOB.29.BSB: The voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.
JOB.29.KJV: The nobles held their peace, and their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth.
JOB.29.PLAIN: The voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.

JOB.29.BSB: For those who heard me called me blessed, and those who saw me commended me,
JOB.29.KJV: When the ear heard me, then it blessed me; and when the eye saw me, it gave witness to me:
JOB.29.PLAIN: For those who heard me called me blessed, and those who saw me commended me,

JOB.29.BSB: because I rescued the poor who cried out and the fatherless who had no helper.
JOB.29.KJV: Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.
JOB.29.PLAIN: because I rescued the poor who cried out and the fatherless who had no helper.

JOB.29.BSB: The dying man blessed me, and I made the widow’s heart sing for joy.
JOB.29.KJV: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came on me: and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.
JOB.29.PLAIN: The dying man blessed me, and I made the widow’s heart sing for joy.

JOB.29.BSB: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and my turban.
JOB.29.KJV: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment was as a robe and a diadem.
JOB.29.PLAIN: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and my turban.

JOB.29.BSB: I served as eyes to the blind and as feet to the lame.
JOB.29.KJV: I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame.
JOB.29.PLAIN: I served as eyes to the blind and as feet to the lame.

JOB.29.BSB: I was a father to the needy, and I took up the case of the stranger.
JOB.29.KJV: I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.
JOB.29.PLAIN: I was a father to the needy, and I took up the case of the stranger.

JOB.29.BSB: I shattered the fangs of the unjust and snatched the prey from his teeth.
JOB.29.KJV: And I broke the jaws of the wicked, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth.
JOB.29.PLAIN: I shattered the fangs of the unjust and snatched the prey from his teeth.

JOB.29.BSB: So I thought: ‘I will die in my nest and multiply my days as the sand.
JOB.29.KJV: Then I said, I shall die in my nest, and I shall multiply my days as the sand.
JOB.29.PLAIN: So I thought: ‘I will die in my nest and multiply my days as the sand.

JOB.29.BSB: My roots will spread out to the waters, and the dew will rest nightly on my branches.
JOB.29.KJV: My root was spread out by the waters, and the dew lay all night on my branch.
JOB.29.PLAIN: My roots will spread out to the waters, and the dew will rest nightly on my branches.

JOB.29.BSB: My glory is ever new within me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.’
JOB.29.KJV: My glory was fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand.
JOB.29.PLAIN: My glory is ever new within me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.’

JOB.29.BSB: Men listened to me with expectation, waiting silently for my counsel.
JOB.29.KJV: To me men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel.
JOB.29.PLAIN: Men listened to me with expectation, waiting silently for my counsel.

JOB.29.BSB: After my words, they spoke no more; my speech settled on them like dew.
JOB.29.KJV: After my words they spoke not again; and my speech dropped on them.
JOB.29.PLAIN: After my words, they spoke no more; my speech settled on them like dew.

JOB.29.BSB: They waited for me as for rain and drank in my words like spring showers.
JOB.29.KJV: And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain.
JOB.29.PLAIN: They waited for me as for rain and drank in my words like spring showers.

JOB.29.BSB: If I smiled at them, they did not believe it; the light of my countenance was precious.
JOB.29.KJV: If I laughed on them, they believed it not; and the light of my countenance they cast not down.
JOB.29.PLAIN: If I smiled at them, they did not believe it; the light of my countenance was precious.

JOB.29.BSB: I chose their course and presided as chief. So I dwelt as a king among his troops, as a comforter of the mourners.
JOB.29.KJV: I chose out their way, and sat chief, and dwelled as a king in the army, as one that comforts the mourners.
JOB.29.PLAIN: I chose their course and presided as chief. So I dwelt as a king among his troops, as a comforter of the mourners.

JOB.30.BSB: “But now they mock me, men younger than I am, whose fathers I would have refused to entrust with my sheep dogs.
JOB.30.KJV: But now they that are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock.
JOB.30.PLAIN: “But now they mock me, men younger than I am, whose fathers I would have refused to entrust with my sheep dogs.

JOB.30.BSB: What use to me was the strength of their hands, since their vigor had left them?
JOB.30.KJV: Yes, whereto might the strength of their hands profit me, in whom old age was perished?
JOB.30.PLAIN: What use to me was the strength of their hands, since their vigor had left them?

JOB.30.BSB: Gaunt from poverty and hunger, they gnawed the dry land, and the desolate wasteland by night.
JOB.30.KJV: For want and famine they were solitary; fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste.
JOB.30.PLAIN: Gaunt from poverty and hunger, they gnawed the dry land, and the desolate wasteland by night.

JOB.30.BSB: They plucked mallow among the shrubs, and the roots of the broom tree were their food.
JOB.30.KJV: Who cut up mallows by the bushes, and juniper roots for their meat.
JOB.30.PLAIN: They plucked mallow among the shrubs, and the roots of the broom tree were their food.

JOB.30.BSB: They were banished from among men, shouted down like thieves,
JOB.30.KJV: They were driven forth from among men, (they cried after them as after a thief;)
JOB.30.PLAIN: They were banished from among men, shouted down like thieves,

JOB.30.BSB: so that they lived on the slopes of the wadis, among the rocks and in holes in the ground.
JOB.30.KJV: To dwell in the cliffs of the valleys, in caves of the earth, and in the rocks.
JOB.30.PLAIN: so that they lived on the slopes of the wadis, among the rocks and in holes in the ground.

JOB.30.BSB: They cried out among the shrubs and huddled beneath the nettles.
JOB.30.KJV: Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together.
JOB.30.PLAIN: They cried out among the shrubs and huddled beneath the nettles.

JOB.30.BSB: A senseless and nameless brood, they were driven off the land.
JOB.30.KJV: They were children of fools, yes, children of base men: they were viler than the earth.
JOB.30.PLAIN: A senseless and nameless brood, they were driven off the land.

JOB.30.BSB: And now they mock me in song; I have become a byword among them.
JOB.30.KJV: And now am I their song, yes, I am their byword.
JOB.30.PLAIN: And now they mock me in song; I have become a byword among them.

JOB.30.BSB: They abhor me and keep far from me; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.
JOB.30.KJV: They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face.
JOB.30.PLAIN: They abhor me and keep far from me; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.

JOB.30.BSB: Because God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they have cast off restraint in my presence.
JOB.30.KJV: Because he has loosed my cord, and afflicted me, they have also let loose the bridle before me.
JOB.30.PLAIN: Because God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they have cast off restraint in my presence.

JOB.30.BSB: The rabble arises at my right; they lay snares for my feet and build siege ramps against me.
JOB.30.KJV: On my right hand rise the youth; they push away my feet, and they raise up against me the ways of their destruction.
JOB.30.PLAIN: The rabble arises at my right; they lay snares for my feet and build siege ramps against me.

JOB.30.BSB: They tear up my path; they profit from my destruction, with no one to restrain them.
JOB.30.KJV: They mar my path, they set forward my calamity, they have no helper.
JOB.30.PLAIN: They tear up my path; they profit from my destruction, with no one to restrain them.

JOB.30.BSB: They advance as through a wide breach; through the ruins they keep rolling in.
JOB.30.KJV: They came on me as a wide breaking in of waters: in the desolation they rolled themselves on me.
JOB.30.PLAIN: They advance as through a wide breach; through the ruins they keep rolling in.

JOB.30.BSB: Terrors are turned loose against me; they drive away my dignity as by the wind, and my prosperity has passed like a cloud.
JOB.30.KJV: Terrors are turned on me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passes away as a cloud.
JOB.30.PLAIN: Terrors are turned loose against me; they drive away my dignity as by the wind, and my prosperity has passed like a cloud.

JOB.30.BSB: And now my soul is poured out within me; days of affliction grip me.
JOB.30.KJV: And now my soul is poured out on me; the days of affliction have taken hold on me.
JOB.30.PLAIN: And now my soul is poured out within me; days of affliction grip me.

JOB.30.BSB: Night pierces my bones, and my gnawing pains never rest.
JOB.30.KJV: My bones are pierced in me in the night season: and my sinews take no rest.
JOB.30.PLAIN: Night pierces my bones, and my gnawing pains never rest.

JOB.30.BSB: With great force He grasps my garment; He seizes me by the collar of my tunic.
JOB.30.KJV: By the great force of my disease is my garment changed: it binds me about as the collar of my coat.
JOB.30.PLAIN: With great force He grasps my garment; He seizes me by the collar of my tunic.

JOB.30.BSB: He throws me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
JOB.30.KJV: He has cast me into the mire, and I am become like dust and ashes.
JOB.30.PLAIN: He throws me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.

JOB.30.BSB: I cry out to You for help, but You do not answer; when I stand up, You merely look at me.
JOB.30.KJV: I cry to you, and you do not hear me: I stand up, and you regard me not.
JOB.30.PLAIN: I cry out to You for help, but You do not answer; when I stand up, You merely look at me.

JOB.30.BSB: You have ruthlessly turned on me; You oppose me with Your strong hand.
JOB.30.KJV: You are become cruel to me: with your strong hand you oppose yourself against me.
JOB.30.PLAIN: You have ruthlessly turned on me; You oppose me with Your strong hand.

JOB.30.BSB: You snatch me up into the wind and drive me before it; You toss me about in the storm.
JOB.30.KJV: You lift me up to the wind; you cause me to ride on it, and dissolve my substance.
JOB.30.PLAIN: You snatch me up into the wind and drive me before it; You toss me about in the storm.

JOB.30.BSB: Yes, I know that You will bring me down to death, to the place appointed for all the living.
JOB.30.KJV: For I know that you will bring me to death, and to the house appointed for all living.
JOB.30.PLAIN: Yes, I know that You will bring me down to death, to the place appointed for all the living.

JOB.30.BSB: Yet no one stretches out his hand to a ruined man when he cries for help in his distress.
JOB.30.KJV: However, he will not stretch out his hand to the grave, though they cry in his destruction.
JOB.30.PLAIN: Yet no one stretches out his hand to a ruined man when he cries for help in his distress.

JOB.30.BSB: Have I not wept for those in trouble? Has my soul not grieved for the needy?
JOB.30.KJV: Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was not my soul grieved for the poor?
JOB.30.PLAIN: Have I not wept for those in trouble? Has my soul not grieved for the needy?

JOB.30.BSB: But when I hoped for good, evil came; when I looked for light, darkness fell.
JOB.30.KJV: When I looked for good, then evil came to me: and when I waited for light, there came darkness.
JOB.30.PLAIN: But when I hoped for good, evil came; when I looked for light, darkness fell.

JOB.30.BSB: I am churning within and cannot rest; days of affliction confront me.
JOB.30.KJV: My bowels boiled, and rested not: the days of affliction prevented me.
JOB.30.PLAIN: I am churning within and cannot rest; days of affliction confront me.

JOB.30.BSB: I go about blackened, but not by the sun. I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
JOB.30.KJV: I went mourning without the sun: I stood up, and I cried in the congregation.
JOB.30.PLAIN: I go about blackened, but not by the sun. I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.

JOB.30.BSB: I have become a brother of jackals, a companion of ostriches.
JOB.30.KJV: I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls.
JOB.30.PLAIN: I have become a brother of jackals, a companion of ostriches.

JOB.30.BSB: My skin grows black and peels, and my bones burn with fever.
JOB.30.KJV: My skin is black on me, and my bones are burned with heat.
JOB.30.PLAIN: My skin grows black and peels, and my bones burn with fever.

JOB.30.BSB: My harp is tuned to mourning and my flute to the sound of weeping.
JOB.30.KJV: My harp also is turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep.
JOB.30.PLAIN: My harp is tuned to mourning and my flute to the sound of weeping.

JOB.31.BSB: “I have made a covenant with my eyes. How then could I gaze with desire at a virgin?
JOB.31.KJV: I made a covenant with my eyes; why then should I think on a maid?
JOB.31.PLAIN: “I have made a covenant with my eyes. How then could I gaze with desire at a virgin?

JOB.31.BSB: For what is the allotment of God from above, or the heritage from the Almighty on high?
JOB.31.KJV: For what portion of God is there from above? and what inheritance of the Almighty from on high?
JOB.31.PLAIN: For what is the allotment of God from above, or the heritage from the Almighty on high?

JOB.31.BSB: Does not disaster come to the unjust and calamity to the workers of iniquity?
JOB.31.KJV: Is not destruction to the wicked? and a strange punishment to the workers of iniquity?
JOB.31.PLAIN: Does not disaster come to the unjust and calamity to the workers of brokenness?

JOB.31.BSB: Does He not see my ways and count my every step?
JOB.31.KJV: Does not he see my ways, and count all my steps?
JOB.31.PLAIN: Does He not see my ways and count my every step?

JOB.31.BSB: If I have walked in falsehood or my foot has rushed to deceit,
JOB.31.KJV: If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot has hurried to deceit;
JOB.31.PLAIN: If I have walked in falsehood or my foot has rushed to deceit,

JOB.31.BSB: let God weigh me with honest scales, that He may know my integrity.
JOB.31.KJV: Let me be weighed in an even balance that God may know my integrity.
JOB.31.PLAIN: let God weigh me with honest scales, that He may know my integrity.

JOB.31.BSB: If my steps have turned from the path, if my heart has followed my eyes, or if impurity has stuck to my hands,
JOB.31.KJV: If my step has turned out of the way, and my heart walked after my eyes, and if any blot has stuck to my hands;
JOB.31.PLAIN: If my steps have turned from the path, if my heart has followed my eyes, or if impurity has stuck to my hands,

JOB.31.BSB: then may another eat what I have sown, and may my crops be uprooted.
JOB.31.KJV: Then let me sow, and let another eat; yes, let my offspring be rooted out.
JOB.31.PLAIN: then may another eat what I have sown, and may my crops be uprooted.

JOB.31.BSB: If my heart has been enticed by my neighbor’s wife, or I have lurked at his door,
JOB.31.KJV: If my heart have been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at my neighbor’s door;
JOB.31.PLAIN: If my heart has been enticed by my neighbor’s wife, or I have lurked at his door,

JOB.31.BSB: then may my own wife grind grain for another, and may other men sleep with her.
JOB.31.KJV: Then let my wife grind to another, and let others bow down on her.
JOB.31.PLAIN: then may my own wife grind grain for another, and may other men sleep with her.

JOB.31.BSB: For that would be a heinous crime, an iniquity to be judged.
JOB.31.KJV: For this is an heinous crime; yes, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges.
JOB.31.PLAIN: For that would be a heinous crime, an brokenness to be judged.

JOB.31.BSB: For it is a fire that burns down to Abaddon; it would root out my entire harvest.

JOB.34.PLAIN: What man is like Job, who drinks up derision like water?

JOB.34.BSB: He keeps company with evildoers and walks with wicked men.
JOB.34.KJV: Which goes in company with the workers of iniquity, and walks with wicked men.
JOB.34.PLAIN: He keeps company with evildoers and walks with wicked men.

JOB.34.BSB: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight in God.’
JOB.34.KJV: For he has said, It profits a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.
JOB.34.PLAIN: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight in God.’

JOB.34.BSB: Therefore listen to me, O men of understanding. Far be it from God to do wrong, and from the Almighty to act unjustly.
JOB.34.KJV: Therefore listen to me you men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness; and from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.
JOB.34.PLAIN: Therefore listen to me, O men of understanding. Far be it from God to do wrong, and from the Almighty to act unjustly.

JOB.34.BSB: For according to a man’s deeds He repays him; according to a man’s ways He brings consequences.
JOB.34.KJV: For the work of a man shall he render to him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.
JOB.34.PLAIN: For according to a man’s deeds He repays him; according to a man’s ways He brings consequences.

JOB.34.BSB: Indeed, it is true that God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice.
JOB.34.KJV: Yes, surely God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.
JOB.34.PLAIN: Indeed, it is true that God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice.

JOB.34.BSB: Who gave Him charge over the earth? Who appointed Him over the whole world?
JOB.34.KJV: Who has given him a charge over the earth? or who has disposed the whole world?
JOB.34.PLAIN: Who gave Him charge over the earth? Who appointed Him over the whole world?

JOB.34.BSB: If He were to set His heart to it and withdraw His Spirit and breath,
JOB.34.KJV: If he set his heart on man, if he gather to himself his spirit and his breath;
JOB.34.PLAIN: If He were to set His heart to it and withdraw His Spirit and breath,

JOB.34.BSB: all flesh would perish together and mankind would return to the dust.
JOB.34.KJV: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall turn again to dust.
JOB.34.PLAIN: all flesh would perish together and mankind would return to the dust.

JOB.34.BSB: If you have understanding, hear this; listen to my words.
JOB.34.KJV: If now you have understanding, hear this: listen to the voice of my words.
JOB.34.PLAIN: If you have understanding, hear this; listen to my words.

JOB.34.BSB: Could one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the just and mighty One,
JOB.34.KJV: Shall even he that hates right govern? and will you condemn him that is most just?
JOB.34.PLAIN: Could one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the just and mighty One,

JOB.34.BSB: who says to kings, ‘You are worthless!’ and to nobles, ‘You are wicked,’
JOB.34.KJV: Is it fit to say to a king, You are wicked? and to princes, You are ungodly?
JOB.34.PLAIN: who says to kings, ‘You are worthless!’ and to nobles, ‘You are wicked,’

JOB.34.BSB: who is not partial to princes and does not favor rich over poor? For they are all the work of His hands.
JOB.34.KJV: How much less to him that accepts not the persons of princes, nor regards the rich more than the poor? for they all are the work of his hands.
JOB.34.PLAIN: who is not partial to princes and does not favor rich over poor? For they are all the work of His hands.

JOB.34.BSB: They die in an instant, in the middle of the night. The people convulse and pass away; the mighty are removed without human hand.
JOB.34.KJV: In a moment shall they die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and pass away: and the mighty shall be taken away without hand.
JOB.34.PLAIN: They die in an instant, in the middle of the night. The people convulse and pass away; the mighty are removed without human hand.

JOB.34.BSB: For His eyes are on the ways of a man, and He sees his every step.
JOB.34.KJV: For his eyes are on the ways of man, and he sees all his goings.
JOB.34.PLAIN: For His eyes are on the ways of a man, and He sees his every step.

JOB.34.BSB: There is no darkness or deep shadow where the workers of iniquity can hide.
JOB.34.KJV: There is no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
JOB.34.PLAIN: There is no darkness or deep shadow where the workers of brokenness can hide.

JOB.34.BSB: For God need not examine a man further or have him approach for judgment.
JOB.34.KJV: For he will not lay on man more than right; that he should enter into judgment with God.
JOB.34.PLAIN: For God need not examine a man further or have him approach for judgment.

JOB.34.BSB: He shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets up others in their place.
JOB.34.KJV: He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead.
JOB.34.PLAIN: He shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets up others in their place.

JOB.34.BSB: Therefore, He recognizes their deeds; He overthrows them in the night and they are crushed.
JOB.34.KJV: Therefore he knows their works, and he overturns them in the night, so that they are destroyed.
JOB.34.PLAIN: Therefore, He recognizes their deeds; He overthrows them in the night and they are crushed.

JOB.34.BSB: He strikes them for their wickedness in full view,
JOB.34.KJV: He strikes them as wicked men in the open sight of others;
JOB.34.PLAIN: He strikes them for their wickedness in full view,

JOB.34.BSB: because they turned aside from Him and had no regard for any of His ways.
JOB.34.KJV: Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways:
JOB.34.PLAIN: because they turned aside from Him and had no regard for any of His ways.

JOB.34.BSB: They caused the cry of the poor to come before Him, and He heard the outcry of the afflicted.
JOB.34.KJV: So that they cause the cry of the poor to come to him, and he hears the cry of the afflicted.
JOB.34.PLAIN: They caused the cry of the poor to come before Him, and He heard the outcry of the afflicted.

JOB.34.BSB: But when He remains silent, who can condemn Him? When He hides His face, who can see Him? Yet He watches over both man and nation,
JOB.34.KJV: When he gives quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hides his face, who then can behold him? whether it be done against a nation, or against a man only:
JOB.34.PLAIN: But when He remains silent, who can condemn Him? When He hides His face, who can see Him? Yet He watches over both man and nation,

JOB.34.BSB: that godless men should not rule or lay snares for the people.
JOB.34.KJV: That the hypocrite reign not, lest the people be ensnared.
JOB.34.PLAIN: that godless men should not rule or lay snares for the people.

JOB.34.BSB: Suppose someone says to God, ‘I have endured my punishment; I will offend no more.
JOB.34.KJV: Surely it is meet to be said to God, I have borne chastisement, I will not offend any more:
JOB.34.PLAIN: Suppose someone says to God, ‘I have endured my punishment; I will offend no more.

JOB.34.BSB: Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again.’
JOB.34.KJV: That which I see not teach you me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more.
JOB.34.PLAIN: Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again.’

JOB.34.BSB: Should God repay you on your own terms when you have disavowed His? You must choose, not I; so tell me what you know.
JOB.34.KJV: Should it be according to your mind? he will recompense it, whether you refuse, or whether you choose; and not I: therefore speak what you know.
JOB.34.PLAIN: Should God repay you on your own terms when you have disavowed His? You must choose, not I; so tell me what you know.

JOB.34.BSB: Men of understanding will declare to me, and the wise men who hear me will say:
JOB.34.KJV: Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man listen to me.
JOB.34.PLAIN: Men of understanding will declare to me, and the wise men who hear me will say:

JOB.34.BSB: ‘Job speaks without knowledge; his words lack insight.’
JOB.34.KJV: Job has spoken without knowledge, and his words were without wisdom.
JOB.34.PLAIN: ‘Job speaks without knowledge; his words lack insight.’

JOB.34.BSB: If only Job were tried to the utmost for answering like a wicked man.
JOB.34.KJV: My desire is that Job may be tried to the end because of his answers for wicked men.
JOB.34.PLAIN: If only Job were tried to the utmost for answering like a wicked man.

JOB.34.BSB: For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God.”
JOB.34.KJV: For he adds rebellion to his sin, he claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against God.
JOB.34.PLAIN: For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God.”

JOB.35.BSB: And Elihu went on to say:
JOB.35.PLAIN: And Elihu went on to say:

JOB.35.BSB: “Do you think this is just? You say, ‘I am more righteous than God.’
JOB.35.KJV: Think you this to be right, that you said, My righteousness is more than God’s?
JOB.35.PLAIN: “Do you think this is just? You say, ‘I am more righteous than God.’

JOB.35.BSB: For you ask, ‘What does it profit me, and what benefit do I gain apart from sin?’
JOB.35.KJV: For you said, What advantage will it be to you? and, What profit shall I have, if I be cleansed from my sin?
JOB.35.PLAIN: For you ask, ‘What does it profit me, and what benefit do I gain apart from sin?’

JOB.35.BSB: I will reply to you and to your friends as well.
JOB.35.KJV: I will answer you, and your companions with you.
JOB.35.PLAIN: I will reply to you and to your friends as well.

JOB.35.BSB: Look to the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds high above you.
JOB.35.KJV: Look to the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds which are higher than you.
JOB.35.PLAIN: Look to the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds high above you.

JOB.35.BSB: If you sin, what do you accomplish against Him? If you multiply your transgressions, what do you do to Him?
JOB.35.KJV: If you sin, what do you against him? or if your transgressions be multiplied, what do you to him?
JOB.35.PLAIN: If you sin, what do you accomplish against Him? If you multiply your wanderings and failures, what do you do to Him?

JOB.35.BSB: If you are righteous, what do you give Him, or what does He receive from your hand?
JOB.35.KJV: If you be righteous, what give you him? or what receives he of your hand?
JOB.35.PLAIN: If you are righteous, what do you give Him, or what does He receive from your hand?

JOB.35.BSB: Your wickedness affects only a man like yourself, and your righteousness only a son of man.
JOB.35.KJV: Your wickedness may hurt a man as you are; and your righteousness may profit the son of man.
JOB.35.PLAIN: Your wickedness affects only a man like yourself, and your righteousness only a son of man.

JOB.35.BSB: Men cry out under great oppression; they plead for relief from the arm of the mighty.
JOB.35.KJV: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.
JOB.35.PLAIN: Men cry out under great oppression; they plead for relief from the arm of the mighty.

JOB.35.BSB: But no one asks, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives us songs in the night,
JOB.35.KJV: But none says, Where is God my maker, who gives songs in the night;
JOB.35.PLAIN: But no one asks, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives us songs in the night,

JOB.35.BSB: who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the air?’
JOB.35.KJV: Who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth, and makes us wiser than the fowls of heaven?
JOB.35.PLAIN: who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the air?’

JOB.35.BSB: There they cry out, but He does not answer, because of the pride of evil men.
JOB.35.KJV: There they cry, but none gives answer, because of the pride of evil men.
JOB.35.PLAIN: There they cry out, but He does not answer, because of the pride of evil men.

JOB.35.BSB: Surely God does not listen to empty pleas, and the Almighty does not take note of it.
JOB.35.KJV: Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it.
JOB.35.PLAIN: Surely God does not listen to empty pleas, and the Almighty does not take note of it.

JOB.35.BSB: How much less, then, when you say that you do not see Him, that your case is before Him and you must wait for Him,
JOB.35.KJV: Although you say you shall not see him, yet judgment is before him; therefore trust you in him.
JOB.35.PLAIN: How much less, then, when you say that you do not see Him, that your case is before Him and you must wait for Him,

JOB.35.BSB: and further, that in His anger He has not punished or taken much notice of folly!
JOB.35.KJV: But now, because it is not so, he has visited in his anger; yet he knows it not in great extremity:
JOB.35.PLAIN: and further, that in His anger He has not punished or taken much notice of folly!

JOB.35.BSB: So Job opens his mouth in vain and multiplies words without knowledge.”
JOB.35.KJV: Therefore does Job open his mouth in vain; he multiplies words without knowledge.
JOB.35.PLAIN: So Job opens his mouth in vain and multiplies words without knowledge.”

JOB.36.BSB: And Elihu continued:
JOB.36.KJV: Elihu also proceeded, and said,
JOB.36.PLAIN: And Elihu continued:

JOB.36.BSB: “Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you that there is more to be said on God’s behalf.
JOB.36.KJV: Suffer me a little, and I will show you that I have yet to speak on God’s behalf.
JOB.36.PLAIN: “Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you that there is more to be said on God’s behalf.

JOB.36.BSB: I get my knowledge from afar, and I will ascribe justice to my Maker.
JOB.36.KJV: I will fetch my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
JOB.36.PLAIN: I get my knowledge from afar, and I will ascribe justice to my Maker.

JOB.36.BSB: For truly my words are free of falsehood; one perfect in knowledge is with you.
JOB.36.KJV: For truly my words shall not be false: he that is perfect in knowledge is with you.
JOB.36.PLAIN: For truly my words are free of falsehood; one perfect in knowledge is with you.

JOB.36.BSB: Indeed, God is mighty, but He despises no one; He is mighty in strength of understanding.
JOB.36.KJV: Behold, God is mighty, and despises not any: he is mighty in strength and wisdom.
JOB.36.PLAIN: Indeed, God is mighty, but He despises no one; He is mighty in strength of understanding.

JOB.36.BSB: He does not keep the wicked alive, but He grants justice to the afflicted.
JOB.36.KJV: He preserves not the life of the wicked: but gives right to the poor.
JOB.36.PLAIN: He does not keep the wicked alive, but He grants justice to the afflicted.

JOB.36.BSB: He does not take His eyes off the righteous, but He enthrones them with kings and exalts them forever.
JOB.36.KJV: He withdraws not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings are they on the throne; yes, he does establish them for ever, and they are exalted.
JOB.36.PLAIN: He does not take His eyes off the righteous, but He enthrones them with kings and exalts them forever.

JOB.36.BSB: And if men are bound with chains, caught in cords of affliction,
JOB.36.KJV: And if they be bound in fetters, and be held in cords of affliction;
JOB.36.PLAIN: And if men are bound with chains, caught in cords of affliction,

JOB.36.BSB: then He tells them their deeds and how arrogantly they have transgressed.
JOB.36.KJV: Then he shows them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded.
JOB.36.PLAIN: then He tells them their deeds and how arrogantly they have transgressed.

JOB.36.BSB: He opens their ears to correction and commands that they turn from iniquity.
JOB.36.KJV: He opens also their ear to discipline, and commands that they return from iniquity.
JOB.36.PLAIN: He opens their ears to correction and commands that they turn from brokenness.

JOB.36.BSB: If they obey and serve Him, then they end their days in prosperity and their years in happiness.
JOB.36.KJV: If they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.
JOB.36.PLAIN: If they obey and serve Him, then they end their days in prosperity and their years in happiness.

JOB.36.BSB: But if they do not obey, then they perish by the sword and die without knowledge.
JOB.36.KJV: But if they obey not, they shall perish by the sword, and they shall die without knowledge.
JOB.36.PLAIN: But if they do not obey, then they perish by the sword and die without knowledge.

JOB.36.BSB: The godless in heart harbor resentment; even when He binds them, they do not cry for help.
JOB.36.KJV: But the hypocrites in heart heap up wrath: they cry not when he binds them.
JOB.36.PLAIN: The godless in heart harbor resentment; even when He binds them, they do not cry for help.

JOB.36.BSB: They die in their youth, among the male shrine prostitutes.
JOB.36.KJV: They die in youth, and their life is among the unclean.
JOB.36.PLAIN: They die in their youth, among the male shrine prostitutes.

JOB.36.BSB: God rescues the afflicted by their affliction and opens their ears in oppression.
JOB.36.KJV: He delivers the poor in his affliction, and opens their ears in oppression.
JOB.36.PLAIN: God rescues the afflicted by their affliction and opens their ears in oppression.

JOB.36.BSB: Indeed, He drew you from the jaws of distress to a spacious and broad place, to a table full of richness.
JOB.36.KJV: Even so would he have removed you out of the strait into a broad place, where there is no narrow place; and that which should be set on your table should be full of fatness.
JOB.36.PLAIN: Indeed, He drew you from the jaws of distress to a spacious and broad place, to a table full of richness.

JOB.36.BSB: But now you are laden with the judgment due the wicked; judgment and justice have seized you.
JOB.36.KJV: But you have fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold on you.
JOB.36.PLAIN: But now you are laden with the judgment due the wicked; judgment and justice have seized you.

JOB.36.BSB: Be careful that no one lures you with riches; do not let a large bribe lead you astray.
JOB.36.KJV: Because there is wrath, beware lest he take you away with his stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver you.
JOB.36.PLAIN: Be careful that no one lures you with riches; do not let a large bribe lead you astray.

JOB.36.BSB: Can your wealth or all your mighty effort keep you from distress?
JOB.36.KJV: Will he esteem your riches? no, not gold, nor all the forces of strength.
JOB.36.PLAIN: Can your wealth or all your mighty effort keep you from distress?

JOB.36.BSB: Do not long for the night, when people vanish from their homes.
JOB.36.KJV: Desire not the night, when people are cut off in their place.
JOB.36.PLAIN: Do not long for the night, when people vanish from their homes.

JOB.36.BSB: Be careful not to turn to iniquity, for this you have preferred to affliction.
JOB.36.KJV: Take heed, regard not iniquity: for this have you chosen rather than affliction.
JOB.36.PLAIN: Be careful not to turn to brokenness, for this you have preferred to affliction.

JOB.36.BSB: Behold, God is exalted in His power. Who is a teacher like Him?
JOB.36.KJV: Behold, God exalts by his power: who teaches like him?
JOB.36.PLAIN: Look closely — God is exalted in His power. Who is a teacher like Him?

JOB.36.BSB: Who has appointed His way for Him, or told Him, ‘You have done wrong’?
JOB.36.KJV: Who has enjoined him his way? or who can say, You have worked iniquity?
JOB.36.PLAIN: Who has appointed His way for Him, or told Him, ‘You have done wrong’?

JOB.36.BSB: Remember to magnify His work, which men have praised in song.
JOB.36.KJV: Remember that you magnify his work, which men behold.
JOB.36.PLAIN: Remember to magnify His work, which men have praised in song.

JOB.36.BSB: All mankind has seen it; men behold it from afar.
JOB.36.KJV: Every man may see it; man may behold it afar off.
JOB.36.PLAIN: All mankind has seen it; men behold it from afar.

JOB.36.BSB: Indeed, God is great—beyond our knowledge; the number of His years is unsearchable.
JOB.36.KJV: Behold, God is great, and we know him not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.
JOB.36.PLAIN: Indeed, God is great—beyond our knowledge; the number of His years is unsearchable.

JOB.36.BSB: For He draws up drops of water which distill the rain from the mist,
JOB.36.KJV: For he makes small the drops of water: they pour down rain according to the vapor thereof:
JOB.36.PLAIN: For He draws up drops of water which distill the rain from the mist,

JOB.36.BSB: which the clouds pour out and shower abundantly on mankind.
JOB.36.KJV: Which the clouds do drop and distil on man abundantly.
JOB.36.PLAIN: which the clouds pour out and shower abundantly on mankind.

JOB.36.BSB: Furthermore, who can understand how the clouds spread out, how the thunder roars from His pavilion?
JOB.36.KJV: Also can any understand the spreading of the clouds, or the noise of his tabernacle?
JOB.36.PLAIN: Furthermore, who can understand how the clouds spread out, how the thunder roars from His pavilion?

JOB.36.BSB: See how He scatters His lightning around Him and covers the depths of the sea.
JOB.36.KJV: Behold, he spreads his light on it, and covers the bottom of the sea.
JOB.36.PLAIN: See how He scatters His lightning around Him and covers the depths of the sea.

JOB.36.BSB: For by these He judges the nations and provides food in abundance.
JOB.36.KJV: For by them judges he the people; he gives meat in abundance.
JOB.36.PLAIN: For by these He judges the nations and provides food in abundance.

JOB.36.BSB: He fills His hands with lightning and commands it to strike its mark.
JOB.36.KJV: With clouds he covers the light; and commands it not to shine by the cloud that comes between.
JOB.36.PLAIN: He fills His hands with lightning and commands it to strike its mark.

JOB.36.BSB: The thunder declares His presence; even the cattle regard the rising storm.
JOB.36.KJV: The noise thereof shows concerning it, the cattle also concerning the vapor.
JOB.36.PLAIN: The thunder declares His presence; even the cattle regard the rising storm.

JOB.37.BSB: “At this my heart also pounds and leaps from its place.
JOB.37.KJV: At this also my heart trembles, and is moved out of his place.
JOB.37.PLAIN: “At this my heart also pounds and leaps from its place.

JOB.37.BSB: Listen closely to the thunder of His voice and the rumbling that comes from His mouth.
JOB.37.KJV: Hear attentively the noise of his voice, and the sound that goes out of his mouth.
JOB.37.PLAIN: Listen closely to the thunder of His voice and the rumbling that comes from His mouth.

JOB.37.BSB: He unleashes His lightning beneath the whole sky and sends it to the ends of the earth.
JOB.37.KJV: He directs it under the whole heaven, and his lightning to the ends of the earth.
JOB.37.PLAIN: He unleashes His lightning beneath the whole sky and sends it to the ends of the earth.

JOB.37.BSB: Then there comes a roaring sound; He thunders with His majestic voice. He does not restrain the lightning when His voice resounds.
JOB.37.KJV: After it a voice roars: he thunders with the voice of his excellency; and he will not stay them when his voice is heard.
JOB.37.PLAIN: Then there comes a roaring sound; He thunders with His majestic voice. He does not restrain the lightning when His voice resounds.

JOB.37.BSB: God thunders wondrously with His voice; He does great things we cannot comprehend.
JOB.37.KJV: God thunders marvelously with his voice; great things does he, which we cannot comprehend.
JOB.37.PLAIN: God thunders wondrously with His voice; He does great things we cannot comprehend.

JOB.37.BSB: For He says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ and to the gentle rain, ‘Pour out a mighty downpour.’
JOB.37.KJV: For he says to the snow, Be you on the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength.
JOB.37.PLAIN: For He says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ and to the gentle rain, ‘Pour out a mighty downpour.’

JOB.37.BSB: He seals up the hand of every man, so that all men may know His work.
JOB.37.KJV: He seals up the hand of every man; that all men may know his work.
JOB.37.PLAIN: He seals up the hand of every man, so that all men may know His work.

JOB.37.BSB: The wild animals enter their lairs; they settle down in their dens.
JOB.37.KJV: Then the beasts go into dens, and remain in their places.
JOB.37.PLAIN: The wild animals enter their lairs; they settle down in their dens.

JOB.37.BSB: The tempest comes from its chamber, and the cold from the driving north winds.
JOB.37.KJV: Out of the south comes the whirlwind: and cold out of the north.
JOB.37.PLAIN: The tempest comes from its chamber, and the cold from the driving north winds.

JOB.37.BSB: By the breath of God the ice is formed and the watery expanses are frozen.
JOB.37.KJV: By the breath of God frost is given: and the breadth of the waters is straitened.
JOB.37.PLAIN: By the breath of God the ice is formed and the watery expanses are frozen.

JOB.37.BSB: He loads the clouds with moisture; He scatters His lightning through them.
JOB.37.KJV: Also by watering he wearies the thick cloud: he scatters his bright cloud:
JOB.37.PLAIN: He loads the clouds with moisture; He scatters His lightning through them.

JOB.37.BSB: They swirl about, whirling at His direction, accomplishing all that He commands over the face of all the earth.
JOB.37.KJV: And it is turned round about by his counsels: that they may do whatever he commands them on the face of the world in the earth.
JOB.37.PLAIN: They swirl about, whirling at His direction, accomplishing all that He commands over the face of all the earth.

JOB.37.BSB: Whether for punishment or for His land, He accomplishes this in His loving devotion.
JOB.37.KJV: He causes it to come, whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy.
JOB.37.PLAIN: Whether for punishment or for His land, He accomplishes this in His loving devotion.

JOB.37.BSB: Listen to this, O Job; stand still and consider the wonders of God.

PSA.18.PLAIN: The Lord has rewarded me according to my righteousness; He has repaid me according to the cleanness of my hands.

PSA.18.PLAIN: So the Lord has repaid me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands in His sight.

PSA.18.BSB: To the faithful You show Yourself faithful, to the blameless You show Yourself blameless;

PSA.18.KJV: For by you I have run through a troop; and by my God have I leaped over a wall.
PSA.18.PLAIN: For in You I can charge an army, and with my God I can scale a wall.

PSA.18.KJV: It is God that girds me with strength, and makes my way perfect.

PSA.18.KJV: You have also given me the shield of your salvation: and your right hand has held me up, and your gentleness has made me great.
PSA.18.PLAIN: You have given me Your shield of salvation; Your right hand upholds me, and Your gentleness exalts me.

PSA.18.PLAIN: You broaden the path beneath me so that my ankles do not give way.

PSA.18.BSB: I pursued my enemies and overtook them; I did not turn back until they were consumed.
PSA.18.KJV: I have pursued my enemies, and overtaken them: neither did I turn again till they were consumed.
PSA.18.PLAIN: I pursued my enemies and overtook them; I did not turn back until they were consumed.

PSA.18.KJV: I have wounded them that they were not able to rise: they are fallen under my feet.

PSA.19.PLAIN: By them indeed Your servant is warned; in keeping them is great reward.

PSA.22.PLAIN: I cry out by day, O my God, but You do not answer, and by night, but I have no rest.

PSA.22.BSB: Yet You are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel.
PSA.22.KJV: But you are holy, O you that inhabit the praises of Israel.
PSA.22.PLAIN: Yet You are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel.

PSA.22.BSB: In You our fathers trusted; they trusted and You delivered them.
PSA.22.KJV: Our fathers trusted in you: they trusted, and you did deliver them.
PSA.22.PLAIN: In You our fathers trusted; they trusted and You delivered them.

PSA.22.BSB: They cried out to You and were set free; they trusted in You and were not disappointed.
PSA.22.KJV: They cried to you, and were delivered: they trusted in you, and were not confounded.
PSA.22.PLAIN: They cried out to You and were set free; they trusted in You and were not disappointed.

PSA.22.BSB: But I am a worm and not a man, scorned by men and despised by the people.
PSA.22.KJV: But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised of the people.
PSA.22.PLAIN: But I am a worm and not a man, scorned by men and despised by the people.

PSA.22.BSB: All who see me mock me; they sneer and shake their heads:
PSA.22.KJV: All they that see me laugh me to scorn: they shoot out the lip, they shake the head, saying,
PSA.22.PLAIN: All who see me mock me; they sneer and shake their heads:

PSA.22.BSB: “He trusts in the LORD, let the LORD deliver him; let the LORD rescue him, since He delights in him.”
PSA.22.KJV: He trusted on the LORD that he would deliver him: let him deliver him, seeing he delighted in him.
PSA.22.PLAIN: “He trusts in the Lord, let the Lord deliver him; let the Lord rescue him, since He delights in him.”

PSA.22.BSB: Yet You brought me forth from the womb; You made me secure at my mother’s breast.
PSA.22.KJV: But you are he that took me out of the womb: you did make me hope when I was on my mother’s breasts.
PSA.22.PLAIN: Yet You brought me forth from the womb; You made me secure at my mother’s breast.

PSA.22.BSB: From birth I was cast upon You; from my mother’s womb You have been my God.
PSA.22.KJV: I was cast on you from the womb: you are my God from my mother’s belly.
PSA.22.PLAIN: From birth I was cast upon You; from my mother’s womb You have been my God.

PSA.22.BSB: Be not far from me, for trouble is near and there is no one to help.
PSA.22.KJV: Be not far from me; for trouble is near; for there is none to help.
PSA.22.PLAIN: Be not far from me, for trouble is near and there is no one to help.

PSA.22.BSB: Many bulls surround me; strong bulls of Bashan encircle me.
PSA.22.KJV: Many bulls have compassed me: strong bulls of Bashan have beset me round.
PSA.22.PLAIN: Many bulls surround me; strong bulls of Bashan encircle me.

PSA.22.BSB: They open their jaws against me like lions that roar and maul.
PSA.22.KJV: They gaped on me with their mouths, as a ravening and a roaring lion.
PSA.22.PLAIN: They open their jaws against me like lions that roar and maul.

PSA.22.BSB: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are disjointed. My heart is like wax; it melts away within me.
PSA.22.KJV: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint: my heart is like wax; it is melted in the middle of my bowels.
PSA.22.PLAIN: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are disjointed. My heart is like wax; it melts away within me.

PSA.22.BSB: My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth. You lay me in the dust of death.
PSA.22.KJV: My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue sticks to my jaws; and you have brought me into the dust of death.
PSA.22.PLAIN: My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth. You lay me in the dust of death.

PSA.22.BSB: For dogs surround me; a band of evil men encircles me; they have pierced my hands and feet.
PSA.22.KJV: For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have enclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet.
PSA.22.PLAIN: For dogs surround me; a band of evil men encircles me; they have pierced my hands and feet.

PSA.22.BSB: I can count all my bones; they stare and gloat over me.
PSA.22.KJV: I may tell all my bones: they look and stare on me.
PSA.22.PLAIN: I can count all my bones; they stare and gloat over me.

PSA.22.BSB: They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothing.
PSA.22.KJV: They part my garments among them, and cast lots on my clothing.
PSA.22.PLAIN: They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothing.

PSA.22.BSB: But You, O LORD, be not far off; O my Strength, come quickly to help me.
PSA.22.KJV: But be not you far from me, O LORD: O my strength, haste you to help me.
PSA.22.PLAIN: But You, O Lord, be not far off; O my Strength, come quickly to help me.

PSA.22.BSB: Deliver my soul from the sword, my precious life from the power of wild dogs.
PSA.22.KJV: Deliver my soul from the sword; my darling from the power of the dog.
PSA.22.PLAIN: Deliver my soul from the sword, my precious life from the power of wild dogs.

PSA.22.BSB: Save me from the mouth of the lion; at the horns of the wild oxen You have answered me!
PSA.22.KJV: Save me from the lion’s mouth: for you have heard me from the horns of the unicorns.
PSA.22.PLAIN: Save me from the mouth of the lion; at the horns of the wild oxen You have answered me!

PSA.22.BSB: I will proclaim Your name to my brothers; I will praise You in the assembly.
PSA.22.KJV: I will declare your name to my brothers: in the middle of the congregation will I praise you.
PSA.22.PLAIN: I will proclaim Your name to my brothers; I will praise You in the assembly.

PSA.22.BSB: You who fear the LORD, praise Him! All descendants of Jacob, honor Him! All offspring of Israel, revere Him!
PSA.22.KJV: You that fear the LORD, praise him; all you the seed of Jacob, glorify him; and fear him, all you the seed of Israel.
PSA.22.PLAIN: You who fear the Lord, praise Him! All descendants of Jacob, honor Him! All offspring of Israel, revere Him!

PSA.22.BSB: For He has not despised or detested the torment of the afflicted. He has not hidden His face from him, but has attended to his cry for help.
PSA.22.KJV: For he has not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted; neither has he hid his face from him; but when he cried to him, he heard.
PSA.22.PLAIN: For He has not despised or detested the torment of the afflicted. He has not hidden His face from him, but has attended to his cry for help.

PSA.22.BSB: My praise for You resounds in the great assembly; I will fulfill my vows before those who fear You.
PSA.22.KJV: My praise shall be of you in the great congregation: I will pay my vows before them that fear him.
PSA.22.PLAIN: My praise for You resounds in the great assembly; I will fulfill my vows before those who fear You.

PSA.22.BSB: The poor will eat and be satisfied; those who seek the LORD will praise Him. May your hearts live forever!
PSA.22.KJV: The meek shall eat and be satisfied: they shall praise the LORD that seek him: your heart shall live for ever.
PSA.22.PLAIN: The poor will eat and be satisfied; those who seek the Lord will praise Him. May your hearts live forever!

PSA.22.BSB: All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the LORD. All the families of the nations will bow down before Him.
PSA.22.KJV: All the ends of the world shall remember and turn to the LORD: and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before you.
PSA.22.PLAIN: All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the Lord. All the families of the nations will bow down before Him.

PSA.22.BSB: For dominion belongs to the LORD and He rules over the nations.
PSA.22.KJV: For the kingdom is the LORD’s: and he is the governor among the nations.
PSA.22.PLAIN: For dominion belongs to the Lord and He rules over the nations.

PSA.22.BSB: All the rich of the earth will feast and worship; all who go down to the dust will kneel before Him— even those unable to preserve their lives.
PSA.22.KJV: All they that be fat on earth shall eat and worship: all they that go down to the dust shall bow before him: and none can keep alive his own soul.
PSA.22.PLAIN: All the rich of the earth will feast and worship; all who go down to the dust will kneel before Him— even those unable to preserve their lives.

PSA.22.BSB: Posterity will serve Him; they will declare the Lord to a new generation.
PSA.22.KJV: A seed shall serve him; it shall be accounted to the Lord for a generation.
PSA.22.PLAIN: Posterity will serve Him; they will declare the Lord to a new generation.

PSA.22.BSB: They will come and proclaim His righteousness to a people yet unborn— all that He has done.
PSA.22.KJV: They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness to a people that shall be born, that he has done this.
PSA.22.PLAIN: They will come and proclaim His righteousness to a people yet unborn— all that He has done.

PSA.23.BSB: A Psalm of David. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
PSA.23.KJV: ¶ A Psalm of David. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
PSA.23.PLAIN: A Psalm of David. The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.

PSA.23.BSB: He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside quiet waters.
PSA.23.KJV: He makes me to lie down in green pastures: he leads me beside the still waters.
PSA.23.PLAIN: He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside quiet waters.

PSA.23.BSB: He restores my soul; He guides me in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name.
PSA.23.KJV: He restores my soul: he leads me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
PSA.23.PLAIN: He restores my soul; He guides me in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name.

PSA.23.BSB: Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.
PSA.23.KJV: Yes, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for you are with me; your rod and your staff they comfort me.
PSA.23.PLAIN: Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.

PSA.23.BSB: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.
PSA.23.KJV: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies: you anoint my head with oil; my cup runs over.
PSA.23.PLAIN: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.

PSA.23.BSB: Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever.
PSA.23.KJV: Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.
PSA.23.PLAIN: Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the Lord forever.

PSA.24.BSB: A Psalm of David. The earth is the LORD’s, and the fullness thereof, the world and all who dwell therein.
PSA.24.KJV: ¶ A Psalm of David. The earth is the LORD’s, and the fullness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.
PSA.24.PLAIN: A Psalm of David. The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof, the world and all who dwell therein.

PSA.24.BSB: For He has founded it upon the seas and established it upon the waters.
PSA.24.KJV: For he has founded it on the seas, and established it on the floods.
PSA.24.PLAIN: For He has founded it upon the seas and established it upon the waters.

PSA.24.BSB: Who may ascend the hill of the LORD? Who may stand in His holy place?
PSA.24.KJV: Who shall ascend into the hill of the LORD? or who shall stand in his holy place?
PSA.24.PLAIN: Who may ascend the hill of the Lord? Who may stand in His holy place?

PSA.24.BSB: He who has clean hands and a pure heart, who does not lift up his soul to an idol or swear deceitfully.
PSA.24.KJV: He that has clean hands, and a pure heart; who has not lifted up his soul to vanity, nor sworn deceitfully.
PSA.24.PLAIN: He who has clean hands and a pure heart, who does not lift up his soul to an idol or swear deceitfully.

PSA.24.BSB: He will receive blessing from the LORD and vindication from the God of his salvation.
PSA.24.KJV: He shall receive the blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.
PSA.24.PLAIN: He will receive blessing from the Lord and vindication from the God of his salvation.

PSA.24.BSB: Such is the generation of those who seek Him, who seek Your face, O God of Jacob. Selah
PSA.24.KJV: This is the generation of them that seek him, that seek your face, O Jacob. Selah.
PSA.24.PLAIN: Such is the generation of those who seek Him, who seek Your face, O God of Jacob. Selah

PSA.24.BSB: Lift up your heads, O gates! Be lifted up, O ancient doors, that the King of Glory may enter!
PSA.24.KJV: Lift up your heads, O you gates; and be you lift up, you everlasting doors; and the King of glory shall come in.
PSA.24.PLAIN: Lift up your heads, O gates! Be lifted up, O ancient doors, that the King of Glory may enter!

PSA.24.BSB: Who is this King of Glory? The LORD strong and mighty, the LORD mighty in battle.
PSA.24.KJV: Who is this King of glory? The LORD strong and mighty, the LORD mighty in battle.
PSA.24.PLAIN: Who is this King of Glory? The Lord strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle.

PSA.24.BSB: Lift up your heads, O gates! Be lifted up, O ancient doors, that the King of Glory may enter!
PSA.24.KJV: Lift up your heads, O you gates; even lift them up, you everlasting doors; and the King of glory shall come in.
PSA.24.PLAIN: Lift up your heads, O gates! Be lifted up, O ancient doors, that the King of Glory may enter!

PSA.24.BSB: Who is He, this King of Glory? The LORD of Hosts— He is the King of Glory. Selah
PSA.24.KJV: Who is this King of glory? The LORD of hosts, he is the King of glory. Selah.
PSA.24.PLAIN: Who is He, this King of Glory? The Lord of Hosts— He is the King of Glory. Selah

PSA.25.BSB: Of David. To You, O LORD, I lift up my soul;
PSA.25.KJV: ¶ A Psalm of David. To you, O LORD, do I lift up my soul.
PSA.25.PLAIN: Of David. To You, O Lord, I lift up my soul;

PSA.25.BSB: in You, my God, I trust. Do not let me be put to shame; do not let my enemies exult over me.
PSA.25.KJV: O my God, I trust in you: let me not be ashamed, let not my enemies triumph over me.
PSA.25.PLAIN: in You, my God, I trust. Do not let me be put to shame; do not let my enemies exult over me.

PSA.25.BSB: Surely none who wait for You will be put to shame; but those who are faithless without cause will be disgraced.
PSA.25.KJV: Yes, let none that wait on you be ashamed: let them be ashamed which transgress without cause.
PSA.25.PLAIN: Surely none who wait for You will be put to shame; but those who are faithless without cause will be disgraced.

PSA.25.BSB: Show me Your ways, O LORD; teach me Your paths.
PSA.25.KJV: Show me your ways, O LORD; teach me your paths.
PSA.25.PLAIN: Show me Your ways, O Lord; teach me Your paths.

PSA.25.BSB: Guide me in Your truth and teach me, for You are the God of my salvation; all day long I wait for You.
PSA.25.KJV: Lead me in your truth, and teach me: for you are the God of my salvation; on you do I wait all the day.
PSA.25.PLAIN: Guide me in Your truth and teach me, for You are the God of my salvation; all day long I wait for You.

PSA.25.BSB: Remember, O LORD, Your compassion and loving devotion, for they are from age to age.
PSA.25.KJV: Remember, O LORD, your tender mercies and your loving kindnesses; for they have been ever of old.
PSA.25.PLAIN: Remember, O Lord, Your compassion and loving devotion, for they are from age to age.

PSA.25.BSB: Remember not the sins of my youth, nor my rebellious acts; remember me according to Your loving devotion, because of Your goodness, O LORD.
PSA.25.KJV: Remember not the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions: according to your mercy remember you me for your goodness’ sake, O LORD.
PSA.25.PLAIN: Remember not the sins of my youth, nor my rebellious acts; remember me according to Your loving devotion, because of Your goodness, O Lord.

PSA.25.BSB: Good and upright is the LORD; therefore He shows sinners the way.
PSA.25.KJV: Good and upright is the LORD: therefore will he teach sinners in the way.
PSA.25.PLAIN: Good and upright is the Lord; therefore He shows sinners the way.

PSA.25.BSB: He guides the humble in what is right and teaches them His way.
PSA.25.KJV: The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach his way.
PSA.25.PLAIN: He guides the humble in what is right and teaches them His way.

PSA.25.BSB: All the LORD’s ways are loving and faithful to those who keep His covenant and His decrees.
PSA.25.KJV: All the paths of the LORD are mercy and truth to such as keep his covenant and his testimonies.
PSA.25.PLAIN: All the Lord’s ways are loving and faithful to those who keep His covenant and His decrees.

PSA.25.BSB: For the sake of Your name, O LORD, forgive my iniquity, for it is great.
PSA.25.KJV: For your name’s sake, O LORD, pardon my iniquity; for it is great.
PSA.25.PLAIN: For the sake of Your name, O Lord, forgive my brokenness, for it is great.

PSA.25.BSB: Who is the man who fears the LORD? He will instruct him in the path chosen for him.
PSA.25.KJV: What man is he that fears the LORD? him shall he teach in the way that he shall choose.
PSA.25.PLAIN: Who is the man who fears the Lord? He will instruct him in the path chosen for him.

PSA.25.BSB: His soul will dwell in prosperity, and his descendants will inherit the land.
PSA.25.KJV: His soul shall dwell at ease; and his seed shall inherit the earth.
PSA.25.PLAIN: His soul will dwell in prosperity, and his descendants will inherit the land.

PSA.25.BSB: The LORD confides in those who fear Him, and reveals His covenant to them.
PSA.25.KJV: The secret of the LORD is with them that fear him; and he will show them his covenant.
PSA.25.PLAIN: The Lord confides in those who fear Him, and reveals His covenant to them.

PSA.25.BSB: My eyes are always on the LORD, for He will free my feet from the mesh.
PSA.25.KJV: My eyes are ever toward the LORD; for he shall pluck my feet out of the net.
PSA.25.PLAIN: My eyes are always on the Lord, for He will free my feet from the mesh.

PSA.25.BSB: Turn to me and be gracious, for I am lonely and afflicted.
PSA.25.KJV: Turn you to me, and have mercy on me; for I am desolate and afflicted.
PSA.25.PLAIN: Turn to me and be gracious, for I am lonely and afflicted.

PSA.25.BSB: The troubles of my heart increase; free me from my distress.
PSA.25.KJV: The troubles of my heart are enlarged: O bring you me out of my distresses.
PSA.25.PLAIN: The troubles of my heart increase; free me from my distress.

PSA.25.BSB: Consider my affliction and trouble, and take away all my sins.
PSA.25.KJV: Look on my affliction and my pain; and forgive all my sins.
PSA.25.PLAIN: Consider my affliction and trouble, and take away all my sins.

PSA.25.BSB: Consider my enemies, for they are many, and they hate me with vicious hatred.
PSA.25.KJV: Consider my enemies; for they are many; and they hate me with cruel hatred.
PSA.25.PLAIN: Consider my enemies, for they are many, and they hate me with vicious hatred.

PSA.25.BSB: Guard my soul and deliver me; let me not be put to shame, for I take refuge in You.
PSA.25.KJV: O keep my soul, and deliver me: let me not be ashamed; for I put my trust in you.
PSA.25.PLAIN: Guard my soul and deliver me; let me not be put to shame, for I take refuge in You.

PSA.25.BSB: May integrity and uprightness preserve me, because I wait for You.
PSA.25.KJV: Let integrity and uprightness preserve me; for I wait on you.
PSA.25.PLAIN: May integrity and uprightness preserve me, because I wait for You.

PSA.25.BSB: Redeem Israel, O God, from all its distress.
PSA.25.KJV: Redeem Israel, O God, out of all his troubles.
PSA.25.PLAIN: Redeem Israel, O God, from all its distress.

PSA.26.BSB: Of David. Vindicate me, O LORD! For I have walked with integrity; I have trusted in the LORD without wavering.
PSA.26.KJV: ¶ A Psalm of David. Judge me, O LORD; for I have walked in my integrity: I have trusted also in the LORD; therefore I shall not slide.
PSA.26.PLAIN: Of David. Vindicate me, O Lord! For I have walked with integrity; I have trusted in the Lord without wavering.

PSA.26.BSB: Test me, O LORD, and try me; examine my heart and mind.
PSA.26.KJV: Examine me, O LORD, and prove me; try my reins and my heart.
PSA.26.PLAIN: Test me, O Lord, and try me; examine my heart and mind.

PSA.26.BSB: For Your loving devotion is before my eyes, and I have walked in Your truth.
PSA.26.KJV: For your loving kindness is before my eyes: and I have walked in your truth.
PSA.26.PLAIN: For Your loving devotion is before my eyes, and I have walked in Your truth.

PSA.26.BSB: I do not sit with deceitful men, nor keep company with hypocrites.
PSA.26.KJV: I have not sat with vain persons, neither will I go in with dissemblers.
PSA.26.PLAIN: I do not sit with deceitful men, nor keep company with hypocrites.

PSA.26.BSB: I hate the mob of evildoers, and refuse to sit with the wicked.
PSA.26.KJV: I have hated the congregation of evil doers; and will not sit with the wicked.
PSA.26.PLAIN: I hate the mob of evildoers, and refuse to sit with the wicked.

PSA.26.BSB: I wash my hands in innocence that I may go about Your altar, O LORD,
PSA.26.KJV: I will wash my hands in innocence: so will I compass your altar, O LORD:
PSA.26.PLAIN: I wash my hands in innocence that I may go about Your altar, O Lord,

PSA.26.BSB: to raise my voice in thanksgiving and declare all Your wonderful works.
PSA.26.KJV: That I may publish with the voice of thanksgiving, and tell of all your wondrous works.
PSA.26.PLAIN: to raise my voice in thanksgiving and declare all Your wonderful works.

PSA.26.BSB: O LORD, I love the house where You dwell, the place where Your glory resides.
PSA.26.KJV: LORD, I have loved the habitation of your house, and the place where your honor dwells.
PSA.26.PLAIN: O Lord, I love the house where You dwell, the place where Your glory resides.

PSA.26.BSB: Do not take my soul away with sinners, or my life with men of bloodshed,
PSA.26.KJV: Gather not my soul with sinners, nor my life with bloody men:
PSA.26.PLAIN: Do not take my soul away with sinners, or my life with men of bloodshed,

PSA.26.BSB: in whose hands are wicked schemes, whose right hands are full of bribes.
PSA.26.KJV: In whose hands is mischief, and their right hand is full of bribes.
PSA.26.PLAIN: in whose hands are wicked schemes, whose right hands are full of bribes.

PSA.26.BSB: But I will walk with integrity; redeem me and be merciful to me.
PSA.26.KJV: But as for me, I will walk in my integrity: redeem me, and be merciful to me.
PSA.26.PLAIN: But I will walk with integrity; redeem me and be merciful to me.

PSA.26.BSB: My feet stand on level ground; in the congregations I will bless the LORD.
PSA.26.KJV: My foot stands in an even place: in the congregations will I bless the LORD.
PSA.26.PLAIN: My feet stand on level ground; in the congregations I will bless the Lord.

PSA.27.BSB: Of David. The LORD is my light and my salvation— whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life— whom shall I dread?
PSA.27.KJV: ¶ A Psalm of David. The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
PSA.27.PLAIN: Of David. The Lord is my light and my salvation— whom shall I fear? The Lord is the stronghold of my life— whom shall I dread?

PSA.27.BSB: When the wicked came upon me to devour my flesh, my enemies and foes stumbled and fell.
PSA.27.KJV: When the wicked, even my enemies and my foes, came on me to eat up my flesh, they stumbled and fell.
PSA.27.PLAIN: When the wicked came upon me to devour my flesh, my enemies and foes stumbled and fell.

PSA.27.BSB: Though an army encamps around me, my heart will not fear; though a war breaks out against me, I will keep my trust.
PSA.27.KJV: Though an host should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear: though war should rise against me, in this will I be confident.
PSA.27.PLAIN: Though an army encamps around me, my heart will not fear; though a war breaks out against me, I will keep my trust.

PSA.27.BSB: One thing I have asked of the LORD; this is what I desire: to dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to gaze on the beauty of the LORD and seek Him in His temple.
PSA.27.KJV: One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple.
PSA.27.PLAIN: One thing I have asked of the Lord; this is what I desire: to dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to gaze on the beauty of the Lord and seek Him in His temple.

PSA.27.BSB: For in the day of trouble He will hide me in His shelter; He will conceal me under the cover of His tent; He will set me high upon a rock.
PSA.27.KJV: For in the time of trouble he shall hide me in his pavilion: in the secret of his tabernacle shall he hide me; he shall set me up on a rock.
PSA.27.PLAIN: For in the day of trouble He will hide me in His shelter; He will conceal me under the cover of His tent; He will set me high upon a rock.

PSA.27.BSB: Then my head will be held high above my enemies around me. At His tabernacle I will offer sacrifices with shouts of joy; I will sing and make music to the LORD.
PSA.27.KJV: And now shall my head be lifted up above my enemies round about me: therefore will I offer in his tabernacle sacrifices of joy; I will sing, yes, I will sing praises to the LORD.
PSA.27.PLAIN: Then my head will be held high above my enemies around me. At His tabernacle I will offer sacrifices with shouts of joy; I will sing and make music to the Lord.

PSA.27.BSB: Hear, O LORD, my voice when I call; be merciful and answer me.
PSA.27.KJV: Hear, O LORD, when I cry with my voice: have mercy also on me, and answer me.
PSA.27.PLAIN: Hear, O Lord, my voice when I call; be merciful and answer me.

PSA.27.BSB: My heart said, “Seek His face.” Your face, O LORD, I will seek.
PSA.27.KJV: When you said, Seek you my face; my heart said to you, Your face, LORD, will I seek.
PSA.27.PLAIN: My heart said, “Seek His face.” Your face, O Lord, I will seek.

PSA.27.BSB: Hide not Your face from me, nor turn away Your servant in anger. You have been my helper; do not leave me or forsake me, O God of my salvation.
PSA.27.KJV: Hide not your face far from me; put not your servant away in anger: you have been my help; leave me not, neither forsake me, O God of my salvation.
PSA.27.PLAIN: Hide not Your face from me, nor turn away Your servant in anger. You have been my helper; do not leave me or forsake me, O God of my salvation.

PSA.27.BSB: Though my father and mother forsake me, the LORD will receive me.
PSA.27.KJV: When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up.
PSA.27.PLAIN: Though my father and mother forsake me, the Lord will receive me.

PSA.27.BSB: Teach me Your way, O LORD, and lead me on a level path, because of my oppressors.
