PSA.80.BSB: before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Rally Your mighty power and come to save us.
PSA.80.KJV: Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh stir up your strength, and come and save us.
PSA.80.PLAIN: before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Rally Your mighty power and come to save us.

PSA.80.BSB: Restore us, O God, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
PSA.80.KJV: Turn us again, O God, and cause your face to shine; and we shall be saved.
PSA.80.PLAIN: Restore us, O God, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.

PSA.80.BSB: O LORD God of Hosts, how long will Your anger smolder against the prayers of Your people?
PSA.80.KJV: O LORD God of hosts, how long will you be angry against the prayer of your people?
PSA.80.PLAIN: O Lord God of Hosts, how long will Your anger smolder against the prayers of Your people?

PSA.80.BSB: You fed them with the bread of tears and made them drink the full measure of their tears.
PSA.80.KJV: You feed them with the bread of tears; and give them tears to drink in great measure.
PSA.80.PLAIN: You fed them with the bread of tears and made them drink the full measure of their tears.

PSA.80.BSB: You make us contend with our neighbors; our enemies mock us.
PSA.80.KJV: You make us a strife to our neighbors: and our enemies laugh among themselves.
PSA.80.PLAIN: You make us contend with our neighbors; our enemies mock us.

PSA.80.BSB: Restore us, O God of Hosts, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
PSA.80.KJV: Turn us again, O God of hosts, and cause your face to shine; and we shall be saved.
PSA.80.PLAIN: Restore us, O God of Hosts, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.

PSA.80.BSB: You uprooted a vine from Egypt; You drove out the nations and transplanted it.
PSA.80.KJV: You have brought a vine out of Egypt: you have cast out the heathen, and planted it.
PSA.80.PLAIN: You uprooted a vine from Egypt; You drove out the nations and transplanted it.

PSA.80.BSB: You cleared the ground for it, and it took root and filled the land.
PSA.80.KJV: You prepared room before it, and did cause it to take deep root, and it filled the land.
PSA.80.PLAIN: You cleared the ground for it, and it took root and filled the land.

PSA.80.BSB: The mountains were covered by its shade, and the mighty cedars with its branches.
PSA.80.KJV: The hills were covered with the shadow of it, and the boughs thereof were like the goodly cedars.
PSA.80.PLAIN: The mountains were covered by its shade, and the mighty cedars with its branches.

PSA.80.BSB: It sent out its branches to the Sea, and its shoots toward the River.
PSA.80.KJV: She sent out her boughs to the sea, and her branches to the river.
PSA.80.PLAIN: It sent out its branches to the Sea, and its shoots toward the River.

PSA.80.BSB: Why have You broken down its walls, so that all who pass by pick its fruit?
PSA.80.KJV: Why have you then broken down her hedges, so that all they which pass by the way do pluck her?
PSA.80.PLAIN: Why have You broken down its walls, so that all who pass by pick its fruit?

PSA.80.BSB: The boar from the forest ravages it, and the creatures of the field feed upon it.
PSA.80.KJV: The boar out of the wood does waste it, and the wild beast of the field does devour it.
PSA.80.PLAIN: The boar from the forest ravages it, and the creatures of the field feed upon it.

PSA.80.BSB: Return, O God of Hosts, we pray! Look down from heaven and see! Attend to this vine—
PSA.80.KJV: Return, we beseech you, O God of hosts: look down from heaven, and behold, and visit this vine;
PSA.80.PLAIN: Return, O God of Hosts, we pray! Look down from heaven and see! Attend to this vine—

PSA.80.BSB: the root Your right hand has planted, the son You have raised up for Yourself.
PSA.80.KJV: And the vineyard which your right hand has planted, and the branch that you made strong for yourself.
PSA.80.PLAIN: the root Your right hand has planted, the son You have raised up for Yourself.

PSA.80.BSB: Your vine has been cut down and burned; they perish at the rebuke of Your countenance.
PSA.80.KJV: It is burned with fire, it is cut down: they perish at the rebuke of your countenance.
PSA.80.PLAIN: Your vine has been cut down and burned; they perish at the rebuke of Your countenance.

PSA.80.BSB: Let Your hand be upon the man at Your right hand, on the son of man You have raised up for Yourself.
PSA.80.KJV: Let your hand be on the man of your right hand, on the son of man whom you made strong for yourself.
PSA.80.PLAIN: Let Your hand be upon the man at Your right hand, on the son of man You have raised up for Yourself.

PSA.80.BSB: Then we will not turn away from You; revive us, and we will call on Your name.
PSA.80.KJV: So will not we go back from you: quicken us, and we will call on your name.
PSA.80.PLAIN: Then we will not turn away from You; revive us, and we will call on Your name.

PSA.80.BSB: Restore us, O LORD God of Hosts; cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
PSA.80.KJV: Turn us again, O LORD God of hosts, cause your face to shine; and we shall be saved.
PSA.80.PLAIN: Restore us, O Lord God of Hosts; cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.

PSA.81.BSB: For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. Of Asaph. Sing for joy to God our strength; make a joyful noise to the God of Jacob.
PSA.81.KJV: ¶ To the chief Musician upon Gittith. A Psalm of Asaph. Sing aloud to God our strength: make a joyful noise to the God of Jacob.
PSA.81.PLAIN: For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. Of Asaph. Sing for joy to God our strength; make a joyful noise to the God of Jacob.

PSA.81.BSB: Lift up a song, strike the tambourine, play the sweet-sounding harp and lyre.
PSA.81.KJV: Take a psalm, and bring here the tambourine, the pleasant harp with the psaltery.
PSA.81.PLAIN: Lift up a song, strike the tambourine, play the sweet-sounding harp and lyre.

PSA.81.BSB: Sound the ram’s horn at the New Moon, and at the full moon on the day of our Feast.
PSA.81.KJV: Blow up the trumpet in the new moon, in the time appointed, on our solemn feast day.
PSA.81.PLAIN: Sound the ram’s horn at the New Moon, and at the full moon on the day of our Feast.

PSA.81.BSB: For this is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
PSA.81.KJV: For this was a statute for Israel, and a law of the God of Jacob.
PSA.81.PLAIN: For this is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob.

PSA.81.BSB: He ordained it as a testimony for Joseph when he went out over the land of Egypt, where I heard an unfamiliar language:
PSA.81.KJV: This he ordained in Joseph for a testimony, when he went out through the land of Egypt: where I heard a language that I understood not.
PSA.81.PLAIN: He ordained it as a testimony for Joseph when he went out over the land of Egypt, where I heard an unfamiliar language:

PSA.81.BSB: “I relieved his shoulder of the burden; his hands were freed from the basket.
PSA.81.KJV: I removed his shoulder from the burden: his hands were delivered from the pots.
PSA.81.PLAIN: “I relieved his shoulder of the burden; his hands were freed from the basket.

PSA.81.BSB: You called out in distress, and I rescued you; I answered you from the cloud of thunder; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah
PSA.81.KJV: You called in trouble, and I delivered you; I answered you in the secret place of thunder: I proved you at the waters of Meribah. Selah.
PSA.81.PLAIN: You called out in distress, and I rescued you; I answered you from the cloud of thunder; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah

PSA.81.BSB: Hear, O My people, and I will warn you: O Israel, if only you would listen to Me!
PSA.81.KJV: Hear, O my people, and I will testify to you: O Israel, if you will listen to me;
PSA.81.PLAIN: Hear, O My people, and I will warn you: O Israel, if only you would listen to Me!

PSA.81.BSB: There must be no strange god among you, nor shall you bow to a foreign god.
PSA.81.KJV: There shall no strange god be in you; neither shall you worship any strange god.
PSA.81.PLAIN: There must be no strange god among you, nor shall you bow to a foreign god.

PSA.81.BSB: I am the LORD your God, who brought you up out of Egypt. Open wide your mouth, and I will fill it.
PSA.81.KJV: I am the LORD your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt: open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
PSA.81.PLAIN: I am the Lord your God, who brought you up out of Egypt. Open wide your mouth, and I will fill it.

PSA.81.BSB: But My people would not listen to Me, and Israel would not obey Me.
PSA.81.KJV: But my people would not listen to my voice; and Israel would none of me.
PSA.81.PLAIN: But My people would not listen to Me, and Israel would not obey Me.

PSA.81.BSB: So I gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own devices.
PSA.81.KJV: So I gave them up to their own hearts’ lust: and they walked in their own counsels.
PSA.81.PLAIN: So I gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own devices.

PSA.81.BSB: If only My people would listen to Me, if Israel would follow My ways,
PSA.81.KJV: Oh that my people had listened to me, and Israel had walked in my ways!
PSA.81.PLAIN: If only My people would listen to Me, if Israel would follow My ways,

PSA.81.BSB: how soon I would subdue their enemies and turn My hand against their foes!
PSA.81.KJV: I should soon have subdued their enemies, and turned my hand against their adversaries.
PSA.81.PLAIN: how soon I would subdue their enemies and turn My hand against their foes!

PSA.81.BSB: Those who hate the LORD would feign obedience, and their doom would last forever.
PSA.81.KJV: The haters of the LORD should have submitted themselves to him: but their time should have endured for ever.
PSA.81.PLAIN: Those who hate the Lord would feign obedience, and their doom would last forever.

PSA.81.BSB: But I would feed you the finest wheat; with honey from the rock I would satisfy you.”
PSA.81.KJV: He should have fed them also with the finest of the wheat: and with honey out of the rock should I have satisfied you.
PSA.81.PLAIN: But I would feed you the finest wheat; with honey from the rock I would satisfy you.”

PSA.82.BSB: A Psalm of Asaph. God presides in the divine assembly; He renders judgment among the gods:
PSA.82.KJV: ¶ A Psalm of Asaph. God stands in the congregation of the mighty; he judges among the gods.
PSA.82.PLAIN: A Psalm of Asaph. God presides in the divine assembly; He renders judgment among the gods:

PSA.82.BSB: “How long will you judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked? Selah
PSA.82.KJV: How long will you judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked? Selah.
PSA.82.PLAIN: “How long will you judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked? Selah

PSA.82.BSB: Defend the cause of the weak and fatherless; uphold the rights of the afflicted and oppressed.
PSA.82.KJV: Defend the poor and fatherless: do justice to the afflicted and needy.
PSA.82.PLAIN: Defend the cause of the weak and fatherless; uphold the rights of the afflicted and oppressed.

PSA.82.BSB: Rescue the weak and needy; save them from the hand of the wicked.
PSA.82.KJV: Deliver the poor and needy: rid them out of the hand of the wicked.
PSA.82.PLAIN: Rescue the weak and needy; save them from the hand of the wicked.

PSA.82.BSB: They do not know or understand; they wander in the darkness; all the foundations of the earth are shaken.
PSA.82.KJV: They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.
PSA.82.PLAIN: They do not know or understand; they wander in the darkness; all the foundations of the earth are shaken.

PSA.82.BSB: I have said, ‘You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High.’
PSA.82.KJV: I have said, You are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.
PSA.82.PLAIN: I have said, ‘You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High.’

PSA.82.BSB: But like mortals you will die, and like rulers you will fall.”
PSA.82.KJV: But you shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.
PSA.82.PLAIN: But like mortals you will die, and like rulers you will fall.”

PSA.82.BSB: Arise, O God, judge the earth, for all the nations are Your inheritance.
PSA.82.KJV: Arise, O God, judge the earth: for you shall inherit all nations.
PSA.82.PLAIN: Arise, O God, judge the earth, for all the nations are Your inheritance.

PSA.83.BSB: A song. A Psalm of Asaph. O God, be not silent; be not speechless; be not still, O God.
PSA.83.KJV: ¶ A song or Psalm of Asaph. Keep not you silence, O God: hold not your peace, and be not still, O God.
PSA.83.PLAIN: A song. A Psalm of Asaph. O God, be not silent; be not speechless; be not still, O God.

PSA.83.BSB: See how Your enemies rage, how Your foes have reared their heads.
PSA.83.KJV: For, see, your enemies make a tumult: and they that hate you have lifted up the head.
PSA.83.PLAIN: See how Your enemies rage, how Your foes have reared their heads.

PSA.83.BSB: With cunning they scheme against Your people and conspire against those You cherish,
PSA.83.KJV: They have taken crafty counsel against your people, and consulted against your hidden ones.
PSA.83.PLAIN: With cunning they scheme against Your people and conspire against those You cherish,

PSA.83.BSB: saying, “Come, let us erase them as a nation; may the name of Israel be remembered no more.”
PSA.83.KJV: They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.
PSA.83.PLAIN: saying, “Come, let us erase them as a nation; may the name of Israel be remembered no more.”

PSA.83.BSB: For with one mind they plot together, they form an alliance against You—
PSA.83.KJV: For they have consulted together with one consent: they are confederate against you:
PSA.83.PLAIN: For with one mind they plot together, they form an alliance against You—

PSA.83.BSB: the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, of Moab and the Hagrites,
PSA.83.KJV: The tabernacles of Edom, and the Ishmaelites; of Moab, and the Hagarenes;
PSA.83.PLAIN: the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, of Moab and the Hagrites,

PSA.83.BSB: of Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, of Philistia with the people of Tyre.
PSA.83.KJV: Gebal, and Ammon, and Amalek; the Philistines with the inhabitants of Tyre;
PSA.83.PLAIN: of Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, of Philistia with the people of Tyre.

PSA.83.BSB: Even Assyria has joined them, lending strength to the sons of Lot. Selah
PSA.83.KJV: Assur also is joined with them: they have helped the children of Lot. Selah.
PSA.83.PLAIN: Even Assyria has joined them, lending strength to the sons of Lot. Selah

PSA.83.BSB: Do to them as You did to Midian, as to Sisera and Jabin at the River Kishon,
PSA.83.KJV: Do to them as to the Midianites; as to Sisera, as to Jabin, at the brook of Kison:
PSA.83.PLAIN: Do to them as You did to Midian, as to Sisera and Jabin at the River Kishon,

PSA.83.BSB: who perished at Endor and became like dung on the ground.
PSA.83.KJV: Which perished at Endor: they became as dung for the earth.
PSA.83.PLAIN: who perished at Endor and became like dung on the ground.

PSA.83.BSB: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
PSA.83.KJV: Make their nobles like Oreb, and like Zeeb: yes, all their princes as Zebah, and as Zalmunna:
PSA.83.PLAIN: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,

PSA.83.BSB: who said, “Let us possess for ourselves the pastures of God.”
PSA.83.KJV: Who said, Let us take to ourselves the houses of God in possession.
PSA.83.PLAIN: who said, “Let us possess for ourselves the pastures of God.”

PSA.83.BSB: Make them like tumbleweed, O my God, like chaff before the wind.
PSA.83.KJV: O my God, make them like a wheel; as the stubble before the wind.
PSA.83.PLAIN: Make them like tumbleweed, O my God, like chaff before the wind.

PSA.83.BSB: As fire consumes a forest, as a flame sets the mountains ablaze,
PSA.83.KJV: As the fire burns a wood, and as the flame sets the mountains on fire;
PSA.83.PLAIN: As fire consumes a forest, as a flame sets the mountains ablaze,

PSA.83.BSB: so pursue them with Your tempest, and terrify them with Your storm.
PSA.83.KJV: So persecute them with your tempest, and make them afraid with your storm.
PSA.83.PLAIN: so pursue them with Your tempest, and terrify them with Your storm.

PSA.83.BSB: Cover their faces with shame, that they may seek Your name, O LORD.
PSA.83.KJV: Fill their faces with shame; that they may seek your name, O LORD.
PSA.83.PLAIN: Cover their faces with shame, that they may seek Your name, O Lord.

PSA.83.BSB: May they be ever ashamed and terrified; may they perish in disgrace.
PSA.83.KJV: Let them be confounded and troubled for ever; yes, let them be put to shame, and perish:
PSA.83.PLAIN: May they be ever ashamed and terrified; may they perish in disgrace.

PSA.83.BSB: May they know that You alone, whose name is the LORD, are Most High over all the earth.
PSA.83.KJV: That men may know that you, whose name alone is JEHOVAH, are the most high over all the earth.
PSA.83.PLAIN: May they know that You alone, whose name is the Lord, are Most High over all the earth.

PSA.84.BSB: For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. How lovely is Your dwelling place, O LORD of Hosts!
PSA.84.KJV: ¶ To the chief musician upon Gittith, a Psalm for the sons of Korah. How amiable are your tabernacles, O LORD of hosts!
PSA.84.PLAIN: For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. How lovely is Your dwelling place, O Lord of Hosts!

PSA.84.BSB: My soul longs, even faints, for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh cry out for the living God.
PSA.84.KJV: My soul longs, yes, even faints for the courts of the LORD: my heart and my flesh cries out for the living God.
PSA.84.PLAIN: My soul longs, even faints, for the courts of the Lord; my heart and my flesh cry out for the living God.

PSA.84.BSB: Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she places her young near Your altars, O LORD of Hosts, my King and my God.
PSA.84.KJV: Yes, the sparrow has found an house, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, even your altars, O LORD of hosts, my King, and my God.
PSA.84.PLAIN: Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she places her young near Your altars, O Lord of Hosts, my King and my God.

PSA.84.BSB: How blessed are those who dwell in Your house! They are ever praising You. Selah
PSA.84.KJV: Blessed are they that dwell in your house: they will be still praising you. Selah.
PSA.84.PLAIN: How blessed are those who dwell in Your house! They are ever praising You. Selah

PSA.84.BSB: Blessed are those whose strength is in You, whose hearts are set on pilgrimage.
PSA.84.KJV: Blessed is the man whose strength is in you; in whose heart are the ways of them.
PSA.84.PLAIN: Held in quiet grace are those whose strength is in You, whose hearts are set on pilgrimage.

PSA.84.BSB: As they pass through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of springs; even the autumn rain covers it with pools.
PSA.84.KJV: Who passing through the valley of Baca make it a well; the rain also fills the pools.
PSA.84.PLAIN: As they pass through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of springs; even the autumn rain covers it with pools.

PSA.84.BSB: They go from strength to strength, until each appears before God in Zion.
PSA.84.KJV: They go from strength to strength, every one of them in Zion appears before God.
PSA.84.PLAIN: They go from strength to strength, until each appears before God in Zion.

PSA.84.BSB: O LORD God of Hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah
PSA.84.KJV: O LORD God of hosts, hear my prayer: give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah.
PSA.84.PLAIN: O Lord God of Hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah

PSA.84.BSB: Take notice of our shield, O God, and look with favor on the face of Your anointed.
PSA.84.KJV: Behold, O God our shield, and look on the face of your anointed.
PSA.84.PLAIN: Take notice of our shield, O God, and look with favor on the face of Your anointed.

PSA.84.BSB: For better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.
PSA.84.KJV: For a day in your courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
PSA.84.PLAIN: For better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.

PSA.84.BSB: For the LORD God is a sun and a shield; the LORD gives grace and glory; He withholds no good thing from those who walk with integrity.
PSA.84.KJV: For the LORD God is a sun and shield: the LORD will give grace and glory: no good thing will he withhold from them that walk uprightly.
PSA.84.PLAIN: For the Lord God is a sun and a shield; the Lord gives grace and glory; He withholds no good thing from those who walk with integrity.

PSA.84.BSB: O LORD of Hosts, how blessed is the man who trusts in You!
PSA.84.KJV: O LORD of hosts, blessed is the man that trusts in you.
PSA.84.PLAIN: O Lord of Hosts, how blessed is the man who trusts in You!

PSA.85.BSB: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. You showed favor to Your land, O LORD; You restored Jacob from captivity.
PSA.85.KJV: ¶ To the chief musician, a Psalm for the sons of Korah. Lord, you have been favorable to your land: you have brought back the captivity of Jacob.
PSA.85.PLAIN: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. You showed favor to Your land, O Lord; You restored Jacob from captivity.

PSA.85.BSB: You forgave the iniquity of Your people; You covered all their sin. Selah
PSA.85.KJV: You have forgiven the iniquity of your people, you have covered all their sin. Selah.
PSA.85.PLAIN: You forgave the brokenness of Your people; You covered all their sin. Selah

PSA.85.BSB: You withheld all Your fury; You turned from Your burning anger.
PSA.85.KJV: You have taken away all your wrath: you have turned yourself from the fierceness of your anger.
PSA.85.PLAIN: You withheld all Your fury; You turned from Your burning anger.

PSA.85.BSB: Restore us, O God of our salvation, and put away Your displeasure toward us.
PSA.85.KJV: Turn us, O God of our salvation, and cause your anger toward us to cease.
PSA.85.PLAIN: Restore us, O God of our salvation, and put away Your displeasure toward us.

PSA.85.BSB: Will You be angry with us forever? Will You draw out Your anger to all generations?
PSA.85.KJV: Will you be angry with us for ever? will you draw out your anger to all generations?
PSA.85.PLAIN: Will You be angry with us forever? Will You draw out Your anger to all generations?

PSA.85.BSB: Will You not revive us again, that Your people may rejoice in You?
PSA.85.KJV: Will you not revive us again: that your people may rejoice in you?
PSA.85.PLAIN: Will You not revive us again, that Your people may rejoice in You?

PSA.85.BSB: Show us Your loving devotion, O LORD, and grant us Your salvation.
PSA.85.KJV: Show us your mercy, O LORD, and grant us your salvation.
PSA.85.PLAIN: Show us Your loving devotion, O Lord, and grant us Your salvation.

PSA.85.BSB: I will listen to what God the LORD will say; for He will surely speak peace to His people and His saints; He will not let them return to folly.
PSA.85.KJV: I will hear what God the LORD will speak: for he will speak peace to his people, and to his saints: but let them not turn again to folly.
PSA.85.PLAIN: I will listen to what God the Lord will say; for He will surely speak peace to His people and His saints; He will not let them return to folly.

PSA.85.BSB: Surely His salvation is near to those who fear Him, that His glory may dwell in our land.
PSA.85.KJV: Surely his salvation is near them that fear him; that glory may dwell in our land.
PSA.85.PLAIN: Surely His salvation is near to those who fear Him, that His glory may dwell in our land.

PSA.85.BSB: Loving devotion and faithfulness have joined together; righteousness and peace have kissed.
PSA.85.KJV: Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
PSA.85.PLAIN: Loving devotion and faithfulness have joined together; righteousness and peace have kissed.

PSA.85.BSB: Faithfulness sprouts from the earth, and righteousness looks down from heaven.
PSA.85.KJV: Truth shall spring out of the earth; and righteousness shall look down from heaven.
PSA.85.PLAIN: Faithfulness sprouts from the earth, and righteousness looks down from heaven.

PSA.85.BSB: The LORD will indeed provide what is good, and our land will yield its increase.
PSA.85.KJV: Yes, the LORD shall give that which is good; and our land shall yield her increase.

PSA.126.BSB: A song of ascents. When the LORD restored the captives of Zion, we were like dreamers.

PSA.126.KJV: Then was our mouth filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing: then said they among the heathen, The LORD has done great things for them.
PSA.126.PLAIN: Then our mouths were filled with laughter, our tongues with shouts of joy. Then it was said among the nations, “The Lord has done great things for them.”

PSA.126.BSB: The LORD has done great things for us; we are filled with joy.
PSA.126.KJV: The LORD has done great things for us; whereof we are glad.
PSA.126.PLAIN: The Lord has done great things for us; we are filled with joy.

PSA.126.BSB: Restore our captives, O LORD, like streams in the Negev.
PSA.126.KJV: Turn again our captivity, O LORD, as the streams in the south.
PSA.126.PLAIN: Restore our captives, O Lord, like streams in the Negev.

PSA.126.BSB: Those who sow in tears will reap with shouts of joy.
PSA.126.KJV: They that sow in tears shall reap in joy.

PSA.127.BSB: A song of ascents. Of Solomon. Unless the LORD builds the house, its builders labor in vain; unless the LORD protects the city, its watchmen stand guard in vain.
PSA.127.KJV: ¶ A song of degrees. Except the LORD build the house, they labor in vain that build it: except the LORD keep the city, the watchman wakes but in vain.

PSA.127.BSB: In vain you rise early and stay up late, toiling for bread to eat— for He gives sleep to His beloved.
PSA.127.KJV: It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he gives his beloved sleep.
PSA.127.PLAIN: In vain you rise early and stay up late, toiling for bread to eat— for He gives sleep to His beloved.

PSA.127.BSB: Children are indeed a heritage from the LORD, and the fruit of the womb is His reward.
PSA.127.KJV: See, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.
PSA.127.PLAIN: Children are indeed a heritage from the Lord, and the fruit of the womb is His reward.

PSA.127.BSB: Like arrows in the hand of a warrior, so are children born in one’s youth.
PSA.127.KJV: As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth.
PSA.127.PLAIN: Like arrows in the hand of a warrior, so are children born in one’s youth.

PSA.127.BSB: Blessed is the man whose quiver is full of them. He will not be put to shame when he confronts the enemies at the gate.
PSA.127.KJV: Happy is the man that has his quiver full of them: they shall not be ashamed, but they shall speak with the enemies in the gate.
PSA.127.PLAIN: Blessed is the man whose quiver is full of them. He will not be put to shame when he confronts the enemies at the gate.

PSA.128.BSB: A song of ascents. Blessed are all who fear the LORD, who walk in His ways!
PSA.128.KJV: ¶ A song of degrees. Blessed is every one that fears the LORD; that walks in his ways.
PSA.128.PLAIN: A song of ascents. Held in quiet grace are all who fear the Lord, who walk in His ways!

PSA.128.BSB: For when you eat the fruit of your labor, blessings and prosperity will be yours.
PSA.128.KJV: For you shall eat the labor of your hands: happy shall you be, and it shall be well with you.
PSA.128.PLAIN: For when you eat the fruit of your labor, blessings and prosperity will be yours.

PSA.128.BSB: Your wife will be like a fruitful vine flourishing within your house, your sons like olive shoots sitting around your table.
PSA.128.KJV: Your wife shall be as a fruitful vine by the sides of your house: your children like olive plants round about your table.
PSA.128.PLAIN: Your wife will be like a fruitful vine flourishing within your house, your sons like olive shoots sitting around your table.

PSA.128.BSB: In this way indeed shall blessing come to the man who fears the LORD.
PSA.128.KJV: Behold, that thus shall the man be blessed that fears the LORD.
PSA.128.PLAIN: In this way indeed shall blessing come to the man who fears the Lord.

PSA.128.BSB: May the LORD bless you from Zion, that you may see the prosperity of Jerusalem all the days of your life,
PSA.128.KJV: The LORD shall bless you out of Zion: and you shall see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life.
PSA.128.PLAIN: May the Lord bless you from Zion, that you may see the prosperity of Jerusalem all the days of your life,

PSA.129.BSB: The LORD is righteous; He has cut me from the cords of the wicked.
PSA.129.KJV: The LORD is righteous: he has cut asunder the cords of the wicked.

PSA.129.KJV: Let them all be confounded and turned back that hate Zion.

PSA.129.KJV: Let them be as the grass on the housetops, which wither before it grows up:

PSA.129.PLAIN: unable to fill the hands of the reaper, or the arms of the binder of sheaves.

PSA.130.KJV: Let Israel hope in the LORD: for with the LORD there is mercy, and with him is plenteous redemption.
PSA.130.PLAIN: O Israel, put your hope in the Lord, for with the Lord is loving devotion, and with Him is redemption in abundance.

PSA.130.BSB: And He will redeem Israel from all iniquity.
PSA.130.KJV: And he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities.
PSA.130.PLAIN: And He will redeem Israel from all brokenness.

PSA.136.BSB: He made the great lights— His loving devotion endures forever.
PSA.136.KJV: To him that made great lights: for his mercy endures for ever:

PSA.136.BSB: the sun to rule the day, His loving devotion endures forever.

PSA.136.KJV: To him that smote Egypt in their firstborn: for his mercy endures for ever:

PSA.136.KJV: But overthrew Pharaoh and his host in the Red sea: for his mercy endures for ever.

PSA.136.KJV: To him which led his people through the wilderness: for his mercy endures for ever.
PSA.136.PLAIN: He led His people through the wilderness. His loving devotion endures forever.

PSA.136.BSB: He struck down great kings His loving devotion endures forever.
PSA.136.KJV: To him which smote great kings: for his mercy endures for ever:
PSA.136.PLAIN: He struck down great kings His loving devotion endures forever.

PSA.136.BSB: and slaughtered mighty kings— His loving devotion endures forever.
PSA.136.KJV: And slew famous kings: for his mercy endures for ever:
PSA.136.PLAIN: and slaughtered mighty kings— His loving devotion endures forever.

PSA.136.BSB: Sihon king of the Amorites His loving devotion endures forever.
PSA.136.KJV: Sihon king of the Amorites: for his mercy endures for ever:
PSA.136.PLAIN: Sihon king of the Amorites His loving devotion endures forever.

PSA.136.BSB: and Og king of Bashan— His loving devotion endures forever.
PSA.136.KJV: And Og the king of Bashan: for his mercy endures for ever:
PSA.136.PLAIN: and Og king of Bashan— His loving devotion endures forever.

PSA.136.BSB: and He gave their land as an inheritance, His loving devotion endures forever.
PSA.136.KJV: And gave their land for an heritage: for his mercy endures for ever:
PSA.136.PLAIN: and He gave their land as an inheritance, His loving devotion endures forever.

PSA.136.BSB: a heritage to His servant Israel. His loving devotion endures forever.
PSA.136.KJV: Even an heritage to Israel his servant: for his mercy endures for ever.
PSA.136.PLAIN: a heritage to His servant Israel. His loving devotion endures forever.

PSA.136.BSB: He remembered us in our low estate His loving devotion endures forever.
PSA.136.KJV: Who remembered us in our low estate: for his mercy endures for ever:
PSA.136.PLAIN: He remembered us in our low estate His loving devotion endures forever.

PSA.136.BSB: and freed us from our enemies. His loving devotion endures forever.
PSA.136.KJV: And has redeemed us from our enemies: for his mercy endures for ever.
PSA.136.PLAIN: and freed us from our enemies. His loving devotion endures forever.

PSA.136.BSB: He gives food to every creature. His loving devotion endures forever.
PSA.136.KJV: Who gives food to all flesh: for his mercy endures for ever.
PSA.136.PLAIN: He gives food to every creature. His loving devotion endures forever.

PSA.136.BSB: Give thanks to the God of heaven! His loving devotion endures forever.
PSA.136.KJV: O give thanks to the God of heaven: for his mercy endures for ever.
PSA.136.PLAIN: Give thanks to the God of heaven! His loving devotion endures forever.

PSA.137.BSB: By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept when we remembered Zion.
PSA.137.KJV: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yes, we wept, when we remembered Zion.
PSA.137.PLAIN: By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept when we remembered Zion.

PSA.137.BSB: There on the willows we hung our harps,
PSA.137.KJV: We hanged our harps on the willows in the middle thereof.
PSA.137.PLAIN: There on the willows we hung our harps,

PSA.137.BSB: for there our captors requested a song; our tormentors demanded songs of joy: “Sing us a song of Zion.”
PSA.137.KJV: For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion.
PSA.137.PLAIN: for there our captors requested a song; our tormentors demanded songs of joy: “Sing us a song of Zion.”

PSA.137.BSB: How can we sing a song of the LORD in a foreign land?
PSA.137.KJV: How shall we sing the LORD’s song in a strange land?
PSA.137.PLAIN: How can we sing a song of the Lord in a foreign land?

PSA.137.BSB: If I forget you, O Jerusalem, may my right hand cease to function.
PSA.137.KJV: If I forget you, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget her cunning.
PSA.137.PLAIN: If I forget you, O Jerusalem, may my right hand cease to function.

PSA.137.BSB: May my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not exalt Jerusalem as my greatest joy!
PSA.137.KJV: If I do not remember you, let my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth; if I prefer not Jerusalem above my chief joy.
PSA.137.PLAIN: May my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not exalt Jerusalem as my greatest joy!

PSA.137.BSB: Remember, O LORD, the sons of Edom on the day Jerusalem fell: “Destroy it,” they said, “tear it down to its foundations!”
PSA.137.KJV: Remember, O LORD, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Raze it, raze it, even to the foundation thereof.
PSA.137.PLAIN: Remember, O Lord, the sons of Edom on the day Jerusalem fell: “Destroy it,” they said, “tear it down to its foundations!”

PSA.137.BSB: O Daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction, blessed is he who repays you as you have done to us.
PSA.137.KJV: O daughter of Babylon, who are to be destroyed; happy shall he be, that rewards you as you have served us.
PSA.137.PLAIN: O Daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction, blessed is he who repays you as you have done to us.

PSA.137.BSB: Blessed is he who seizes your infants and dashes them against the rocks.
PSA.137.KJV: Happy shall he be, that takes and dashes your little ones against the stones.
PSA.137.PLAIN: Blessed is he who seizes your infants and dashes them against the rocks.

PSA.138.BSB: Of David. I give You thanks with all my heart; before the gods I sing Your praises.
PSA.138.KJV: ¶ A Psalm of David. I will praise you with my whole heart: before the gods will I sing praise to you.
PSA.138.PLAIN: Of David. I give You thanks with all my heart; before the gods I sing Your praises.

PSA.138.BSB: I bow down toward Your holy temple and give thanks to Your name for Your loving devotion and Your faithfulness; You have exalted Your name and Your word above all else.
PSA.138.KJV: I will worship toward your holy temple, and praise your name for your loving kindness and for your truth: for you have magnified your word above all your name.
PSA.138.PLAIN: I bow down toward Your holy temple and give thanks to Your name for Your loving devotion and Your faithfulness; You have exalted Your name and Your word above all else.

PSA.138.BSB: On the day I called, You answered me; You emboldened me and strengthened my soul.
PSA.138.KJV: In the day when I cried you answered me, and strengthened me with strength in my soul.
PSA.138.PLAIN: On the day I called, You answered me; You emboldened me and strengthened my soul.

PSA.138.BSB: All the kings of the earth will give You thanks, O LORD, when they hear the words of Your mouth.
PSA.138.KJV: All the kings of the earth shall praise you, O LORD, when they hear the words of your mouth.
PSA.138.PLAIN: All the kings of the earth will give You thanks, O Lord, when they hear the words of Your mouth.

PSA.138.BSB: They will sing of the ways of the LORD, for the glory of the LORD is great.
PSA.138.KJV: Yes, they shall sing in the ways of the LORD: for great is the glory of the LORD.
PSA.138.PLAIN: They will sing of the ways of the Lord, for the glory of the Lord is great.

PSA.138.BSB: Though the LORD is on high, He attends to the lowly; but the proud He knows from afar.
PSA.138.KJV: Though the LORD be high, yet has he respect to the lowly: but the proud he knows afar off.
PSA.138.PLAIN: Though the Lord is on high, He attends to the lowly; but the proud He knows from afar.

PSA.138.BSB: If I walk in the midst of trouble, You preserve me from the anger of my foes; You extend Your hand, and Your right hand saves me.
PSA.138.KJV: Though I walk in the middle of trouble, you will revive me: you shall stretch forth your hand against the wrath of my enemies, and your right hand shall save me.
PSA.138.PLAIN: If I walk in the midst of trouble, You preserve me from the anger of my foes; You extend Your hand, and Your right hand saves me.

PSA.138.BSB: The LORD will fulfill His purpose for me. O LORD, Your loving devotion endures forever— do not abandon the works of Your hands.
PSA.138.KJV: The LORD will perfect that which concerns me: your mercy, O LORD, endures for ever: forsake not the works of your own hands.
PSA.138.PLAIN: The Lord will fulfill His purpose for me. O Lord, Your loving devotion endures forever— do not abandon the works of Your hands.

PSA.139.BSB: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. O LORD, You have searched me and known me.
PSA.139.KJV: ¶ To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. O lord, you have searched me, and known me.
PSA.139.PLAIN: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. O Lord, You have searched me and known me.

PSA.139.BSB: You know when I sit and when I rise; You understand my thoughts from afar.
PSA.139.KJV: You know my sitting down and my rising up, you understand my thought afar off.
PSA.139.PLAIN: You know when I sit and when I rise; You understand my thoughts from afar.

PSA.139.BSB: You search out my path and my lying down; You are aware of all my ways.
PSA.139.KJV: You compass my path and my lying down, and are acquainted with all my ways.
PSA.139.PLAIN: You search out my path and my lying down; You are aware of all my ways.

PSA.139.BSB: Even before a word is on my tongue, You know all about it, O LORD.
PSA.139.KJV: For there is not a word in my tongue, but, see, O LORD, you know it altogether.
PSA.139.PLAIN: Even before a word is on my tongue, You know all about it, O Lord.

PSA.139.BSB: You hem me in behind and before; You have laid Your hand upon me.
PSA.139.KJV: You have beset me behind and before, and laid your hand on me.
PSA.139.PLAIN: You hem me in behind and before; You have laid Your hand upon me.

PSA.139.BSB: Such knowledge is too wonderful for me, too lofty for me to attain.
PSA.139.KJV: Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot attain to it.
PSA.139.PLAIN: Such knowledge is too wonderful for me, too lofty for me to attain.

PSA.139.BSB: Where can I go to escape Your Spirit? Where can I flee from Your presence?
PSA.139.KJV: Where shall I go from your spirit? or where shall I flee from your presence?
PSA.139.PLAIN: Where can I go to escape Your Spirit? Where can I flee from Your presence?

PSA.139.BSB: If I ascend to the heavens, You are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, You are there.
PSA.139.KJV: If I ascend up into heaven, you are there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, you are there.
PSA.139.PLAIN: If I ascend to the heavens, You are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, You are there.

PSA.139.BSB: If I rise on the wings of the dawn, if I settle by the farthest sea,
PSA.139.KJV: If I take the wings of the morning, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea;
PSA.139.PLAIN: If I rise on the wings of the dawn, if I settle by the farthest sea,

PSA.139.BSB: even there Your hand will guide me; Your right hand will hold me fast.
PSA.139.KJV: Even there shall your hand lead me, and your right hand shall hold me.
PSA.139.PLAIN: even there Your hand will guide me; Your right hand will hold me fast.

PSA.139.BSB: If I say, “Surely the darkness will hide me, and the light become night around me”—
PSA.139.KJV: If I say, Surely the darkness shall cover me; even the night shall be light about me.
PSA.139.PLAIN: If I say, “Surely the darkness will hide me, and the light become night around me”—

PSA.139.BSB: even the darkness is not dark to You, but the night shines like the day, for darkness is as light to You.
PSA.139.KJV: Yes, the darkness hides not from you; but the night shines as the day: the darkness and the light are both alike to you.
PSA.139.PLAIN: even the darkness is not dark to You, but the night shines like the day, for darkness is as light to You.

PSA.139.BSB: For You formed my inmost being; You knit me together in my mother’s womb.
PSA.139.KJV: For you have possessed my reins: you have covered me in my mother’s womb.
PSA.139.PLAIN: For You formed my inmost being; You knit me together in my mother’s womb.

PSA.139.BSB: I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Marvelous are Your works, and I know this very well.
PSA.139.KJV: I will praise you; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvelous are your works; and that my soul knows right well.
PSA.139.PLAIN: I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Marvelous are Your works, and I know this very well.

PSA.139.BSB: My frame was not hidden from You when I was made in secret, when I was woven together in the depths of the earth.
PSA.139.KJV: My substance was not hid from you, when I was made in secret, and curiously worked in the lowest parts of the earth.
PSA.139.PLAIN: My frame was not hidden from You when I was made in secret, when I was woven together in the depths of the earth.

PSA.139.BSB: Your eyes saw my unformed body; all my days were written in Your book and ordained for me before one of them came to be.
PSA.139.KJV: Your eyes did see my substance, yet being imperfect; and in your book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.
PSA.139.PLAIN: Your eyes saw my unformed body; all my days were written in Your book and ordained for me before one of them came to be.

PSA.139.BSB: How precious to me are Your thoughts, O God, how vast is their sum!
PSA.139.KJV: How precious also are your thoughts to me, O God! how great is the sum of them!
PSA.139.PLAIN: How precious to me are Your thoughts, O God, how vast is their sum!

PSA.139.BSB: If I were to count them, they would outnumber the grains of sand; and when I awake, I am still with You.
PSA.139.KJV: If I should count them, they are more in number than the sand: when I awake, I am still with you.
PSA.139.PLAIN: If I were to count them, they would outnumber the grains of sand; and when I awake, I am still with You.

PSA.139.BSB: O God, that You would slay the wicked— away from me, you bloodthirsty men—
PSA.139.KJV: Surely you will slay the wicked, O God: depart from me therefore, you bloody men.
PSA.139.PLAIN: O God, that You would slay the wicked— away from me, you bloodthirsty men—

PSA.139.BSB: who speak of You deceitfully; Your enemies take Your name in vain.
PSA.139.KJV: For they speak against you wickedly, and your enemies take your name in vain.
PSA.139.PLAIN: who speak of You deceitfully; Your enemies take Your name in vain.

PSA.139.BSB: Do I not hate those who hate You, O LORD, and detest those who rise against You?
PSA.139.KJV: Do not I hate them, O LORD, that hate you? and am not I grieved with those that rise up against you?
PSA.139.PLAIN: Do I not hate those who hate You, O Lord, and detest those who rise against You?

PSA.139.BSB: I hate them with perfect hatred; I count them as my enemies.
PSA.139.KJV: I hate them with perfect hatred: I count them my enemies.
PSA.139.PLAIN: I hate them with perfect hatred; I count them as my enemies.

PSA.139.BSB: Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my concerns.
PSA.139.KJV: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts:
PSA.139.PLAIN: Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my concerns.

PSA.139.BSB: See if there is any offensive way in me; lead me in the way everlasting.
PSA.139.KJV: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.
PSA.139.PLAIN: See if there is any offensive way in me; lead me in the way everlasting.

PSA.140.BSB: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. Rescue me, O LORD, from evil men. Protect me from men of violence,
PSA.140.KJV: ¶ To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. Deliver me, O LORD, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man;
PSA.140.PLAIN: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. Rescue me, O Lord, from evil men. Protect me from men of violence,

PSA.140.BSB: who devise evil in their hearts and stir up war all day long.
PSA.140.KJV: Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.
PSA.140.PLAIN: who devise evil in their hearts and stir up war all day long.

PSA.140.BSB: They sharpen their tongues like snakes; the venom of vipers is on their lips. Selah
PSA.140.KJV: They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders’ poison is under their lips. Selah.
PSA.140.PLAIN: They sharpen their tongues like snakes; the venom of vipers is on their lips. Selah

PSA.140.BSB: Guard me, O LORD, from the hands of the wicked. Keep me safe from men of violence who scheme to make me stumble.
PSA.140.KJV: Keep me, O LORD, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.
PSA.140.PLAIN: Guard me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked. Keep me safe from men of violence who scheme to make me stumble.

PSA.140.BSB: The proud hide a snare for me; the cords of their net are spread along the path, and lures are set out for me. Selah
PSA.140.KJV: The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net by the wayside; they have set gins for me. Selah.
PSA.140.PLAIN: The proud hide a snare for me; the cords of their net are spread along the path, and lures are set out for me. Selah

PSA.140.BSB: I say to the LORD, “You are my God.” Hear, O LORD, my cry for help.
PSA.140.KJV: I said to the LORD, You are my God: hear the voice of my supplications, O LORD.
PSA.140.PLAIN: I say to the Lord, “You are my God.” Hear, O Lord, my cry for help.

PSA.140.BSB: O GOD the Lord, the strength of my salvation, You shield my head in the day of battle.
PSA.140.KJV: O GOD the Lord, the strength of my salvation, you have covered my head in the day of battle.
PSA.140.PLAIN: O GOD the Lord, the strength of my salvation, You shield my head in the day of battle.

PSA.140.BSB: Grant not, O LORD, the desires of the wicked; do not promote their evil plans, lest they be exalted. Selah
PSA.140.KJV: Grant not, O LORD, the desires of the wicked: further not his wicked device; lest they exalt themselves. Selah.
PSA.140.PLAIN: Grant not, O Lord, the desires of the wicked; do not promote their evil plans, lest they be exalted. Selah

PSA.140.BSB: May the heads of those who surround me be covered in the trouble their lips have caused.
PSA.140.KJV: As for the head of those that compass me about, let the mischief of their own lips cover them.
PSA.140.PLAIN: May the heads of those who surround me be covered in the trouble their lips have caused.

PSA.140.BSB: May burning coals fall on them; may they be thrown into the fire, into the miry pits, never to rise again.
PSA.140.KJV: Let burning coals fall on them: let them be cast into the fire; into deep pits, that they rise not up again.
PSA.140.PLAIN: May burning coals fall on them; may they be thrown into the fire, into the miry pits, never to rise again.

PSA.140.BSB: May no slanderer be established in the land; may calamity hunt down the man of violence.
PSA.140.KJV: Let not an evil speaker be established in the earth: evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him.
PSA.140.PLAIN: May no slanderer be established in the land; may calamity hunt down the man of violence.

PSA.140.BSB: I know that the LORD upholds justice for the poor and defends the cause of the needy.
PSA.140.KJV: I know that the LORD will maintain the cause of the afflicted, and the right of the poor.
PSA.140.PLAIN: I know that the Lord upholds justice for the poor and defends the cause of the needy.

PSA.140.BSB: Surely the righteous will praise Your name; the upright will dwell in Your presence.
PSA.140.KJV: Surely the righteous shall give thanks to your name: the upright shall dwell in your presence.
PSA.140.PLAIN: Surely the righteous will praise Your name; the upright will dwell in Your presence.

PSA.141.BSB: A Psalm of David. I call upon You, O LORD; come quickly to me. Hear my voice when I call to You.
PSA.141.KJV: ¶ A Psalm of David. Lord, I cry to you: make haste to me; give ear to my voice, when I cry to you.
PSA.141.PLAIN: A Psalm of David. I call upon You, O Lord; come quickly to me. Hear my voice when I call to You.

PSA.141.BSB: May my prayer be set before You like incense, my uplifted hands like the evening offering.
PSA.141.KJV: Let my prayer be set forth before you as incense; and the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice.
PSA.141.PLAIN: May my prayer be set before You like incense, my uplifted hands like the evening offering.

PSA.141.BSB: Set a guard, O LORD, over my mouth; keep watch at the door of my lips.
PSA.141.KJV: Set a watch, O LORD, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips.
PSA.141.PLAIN: Set a guard, O Lord, over my mouth; keep watch at the door of my lips.

PSA.141.BSB: Do not let my heart be drawn to any evil thing or take part in works of wickedness with men who do iniquity; let me not feast on their delicacies.
PSA.141.KJV: Incline not my heart to any evil thing, to practice wicked works with men that work iniquity: and let me not eat of their dainties.
PSA.141.PLAIN: Do not let my heart be drawn to any evil thing or take part in works of wickedness with men who do brokenness; let me not feast on their delicacies.

PSA.141.BSB: Let the righteous man strike me; let his rebuke be an act of loving devotion. It is oil for my head; let me not refuse it. For my prayer is ever against the deeds of the wicked.
PSA.141.KJV: Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness: and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil, which shall not break my head: for yet my prayer also shall be in their calamities.
PSA.141.PLAIN: Let the righteous man strike me; let his rebuke be an act of loving devotion. It is oil for my head; let me not refuse it. For my prayer is ever against the deeds of the wicked.

PSA.141.BSB: When their rulers are thrown down from the cliffs, the people will listen to my words, for they are pleasant.
PSA.141.KJV: When their judges are overthrown in stony places, they shall hear my words; for they are sweet.
PSA.141.PLAIN: When their rulers are thrown down from the cliffs, the people will listen to my words, for they are pleasant.

PSA.141.BSB: As when one plows and breaks up the soil, so our bones have been scattered at the mouth of Sheol.
PSA.141.KJV: Our bones are scattered at the grave’s mouth, as when one cuts and splits wood on the earth.
PSA.141.PLAIN: As when one plows and breaks up the soil, so our bones have been scattered at the mouth of Sheol.

PSA.141.BSB: But my eyes are fixed on You, O GOD the Lord. In You I seek refuge; do not leave my soul defenseless.
PSA.141.KJV: But my eyes are to you, O GOD the Lord: in you is my trust; leave not my soul destitute.
PSA.141.PLAIN: But my eyes are fixed on You, O GOD the Lord. In You I seek refuge; do not leave my soul defenseless.

PSA.141.BSB: Keep me from the snares they have laid for me, and from the lures of evildoers.
PSA.141.KJV: Keep me from the snares which they have laid for me, and the gins of the workers of iniquity.
PSA.141.PLAIN: Keep me from the snares they have laid for me, and from the lures of evildoers.

PSA.141.BSB: Let the wicked fall into their own nets, while I pass by in safety.
PSA.141.KJV: Let the wicked fall into their own nets, whilst that I with escape.
PSA.141.PLAIN: Let the wicked fall into their own nets, while I pass by in safety.

PSA.142.BSB: A Maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer. I cry aloud to the LORD; I lift my voice to the LORD for mercy.
PSA.142.KJV: ¶ Maschil of David; A prayer when he was in the cave. I cried to the LORD with my voice; with my voice to the LORD did I make my supplication.
PSA.142.PLAIN: A Maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer. I cry aloud to the Lord; I lift my voice to the Lord for mercy.

PSA.142.BSB: I pour out my complaint before Him; I reveal my trouble to Him.

ECC.1.BSB: These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:
ECC.1.KJV: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
ECC.1.PLAIN: These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:

ECC.1.BSB: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher, “futility of futilities! Everything is futile!”
ECC.1.KJV: Vanity of vanities, says the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.
ECC.1.PLAIN: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher, “futility of futilities! Everything is futile!”

ECC.1.BSB: What does a man gain from all his labor, at which he toils under the sun?
ECC.1.KJV: What profit has a man of all his labor which he takes under the sun?
ECC.1.PLAIN: What does a man gain from all his labor, at which he toils under the sun?

ECC.1.BSB: Generations come and generations go, but the earth remains forever.
ECC.1.KJV: One generation passes away, and another generation comes: but the earth stays for ever.
ECC.1.PLAIN: Generations come and generations go, but the earth remains forever.

ECC.1.BSB: The sun rises and the sun sets; it hurries back to where it rises.
ECC.1.KJV: The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, and hastens to his place where he arose.
ECC.1.PLAIN: The sun rises and the sun sets; it hurries back to where it rises.

ECC.1.BSB: The wind blows southward, then turns northward; round and round it swirls, ever returning on its course.
ECC.1.KJV: The wind goes toward the south, and turns about to the north; it whirls about continually, and the wind returns again according to his circuits.
ECC.1.PLAIN: The wind blows southward, then turns northward; round and round it swirls, ever returning on its course.

ECC.1.BSB: All the rivers flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full; to the place from which the streams come, there again they flow.
ECC.1.KJV: All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea is not full; to the place from where the rivers come, thither they return again.
ECC.1.PLAIN: All the rivers flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full; to the place from which the streams come, there again they flow.

ECC.1.BSB: All things are wearisome, more than one can describe; the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear content with hearing.
ECC.1.KJV: All things are full of labor; man cannot utter it: the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
ECC.1.PLAIN: All things are wearisome, more than one can describe; the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear content with hearing.

ECC.1.BSB: What has been will be again, and what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.
ECC.1.KJV: The thing that has been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.
ECC.1.PLAIN: What has been will be again, and what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.

ECC.1.BSB: Is there a case where one can say, “Look, this is new”? It has already existed in the ages before us.
ECC.1.KJV: Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? it has been already of old time, which was before us.
ECC.1.PLAIN: Is there a case where one can say, “Look, this is new”? It has already existed in the ages before us.

ECC.1.BSB: There is no remembrance of those who came before, and those yet to come will not be remembered by those who follow after.
ECC.1.KJV: There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after. ¶
ECC.1.PLAIN: There is no remembrance of those who came before, and those yet to come will not be remembered by those who follow after.

ECC.1.BSB: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
ECC.1.KJV: I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
ECC.1.PLAIN: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

ECC.1.BSB: And I set my mind to seek and explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven. What a heavy burden God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them!
ECC.1.KJV: And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all things that are done under heaven: this sore travail has God given to the sons of man to be exercised therewith.
ECC.1.PLAIN: And I set my mind to seek and explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven. What a heavy burden God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them!

ECC.1.BSB: I have seen all the things that are done under the sun, and have found them all to be futile, a pursuit of the wind.
ECC.1.KJV: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all is vanity and vexation of spirit.
ECC.1.PLAIN: I have seen all the things that are done under the sun, and have found them all to be futile, a pursuit of the wind.

ECC.1.BSB: What is crooked cannot be straightened, and what is lacking cannot be counted.
ECC.1.KJV: That which is crooked cannot be made straight: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.
ECC.1.PLAIN: What is crooked cannot be straightened, and what is lacking cannot be counted.

ECC.1.BSB: I said to myself, “Behold, I have grown and increased in wisdom beyond all those before me who were over Jerusalem, and my mind has observed a wealth of wisdom and knowledge.”
ECC.1.KJV: I communed with my own heart, saying, See, I am come to great estate, and have gotten more wisdom than all they that have been before me in Jerusalem: yes, my heart had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.
ECC.1.PLAIN: I said to myself, “Look closely — I have grown and increased in wisdom beyond all those before me who were over Jerusalem, and my mind has observed a wealth of wisdom and knowledge.”

ECC.1.BSB: So I set my mind to know wisdom and madness and folly; I learned that this, too, is a pursuit of the wind.
ECC.1.KJV: And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.
ECC.1.PLAIN: So I set my mind to know wisdom and madness and folly; I learned that this, too, is a pursuit of the wind.

ECC.1.BSB: For with much wisdom comes much sorrow, and as knowledge grows, grief increases.
ECC.1.KJV: For in much wisdom is much grief: and he that increases knowledge increases sorrow.
ECC.1.PLAIN: For with much wisdom comes much sorrow, and as knowledge grows, grief increases.

ECC.2.BSB: I said to myself, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure; enjoy what is good!” But it proved to be futile.
ECC.2.KJV: I said in my heart, Go to now, I will prove you with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also is vanity.
ECC.2.PLAIN: I said to myself, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure; enjoy what is good!” But it proved to be futile.

ECC.2.BSB: I said of laughter, “It is folly,” and of pleasure, “What does it accomplish?”
ECC.2.KJV: I said of laughter, It is mad: and of mirth, What does it?
ECC.2.PLAIN: I said of laughter, “It is folly,” and of pleasure, “What does it accomplish?”

ECC.2.BSB: I sought to cheer my body with wine and to embrace folly—my mind still guiding me with wisdom—until I could see what was worthwhile for men to do under heaven during the few days of their lives.
ECC.2.KJV: I sought in my heart to give myself to wine, yet acquainting my heart with wisdom; and to lay hold on folly, till I might see what was that good for the sons of men, which they should do under the heaven all the days of their life.
ECC.2.PLAIN: I sought to cheer my body with wine and to embrace folly—my mind still guiding me with wisdom—until I could see what was worthwhile for men to do under heaven during the few days of their lives.

ECC.2.BSB: I expanded my pursuits. I built houses and planted vineyards for myself.
ECC.2.KJV: I made me great works; I built me houses; I planted me vineyards:
ECC.2.PLAIN: I expanded my pursuits. I built houses and planted vineyards for myself.

ECC.2.BSB: I made gardens and parks for myself, where I planted all kinds of fruit trees.
ECC.2.KJV: I made me gardens and orchards, and I planted trees in them of all kind of fruits:
ECC.2.PLAIN: I made gardens and parks for myself, where I planted all kinds of fruit trees.

ECC.2.BSB: I built reservoirs to water my groves of flourishing trees.
ECC.2.KJV: I made me pools of water, to water therewith the wood that brings forth trees:
ECC.2.PLAIN: I built reservoirs to water my groves of flourishing trees.

ECC.2.BSB: I acquired menservants and maidservants, and servants were born in my house. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me,
ECC.2.KJV: I got me servants and maidens, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of great and small cattle above all that were in Jerusalem before me:
ECC.2.PLAIN: I acquired menservants and maidservants, and servants were born in my house. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me,

ECC.2.BSB: and I accumulated for myself silver and gold and the treasure of kings and provinces. I gathered to myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men—many concubines.
ECC.2.KJV: I gathered me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings and of the provinces: I got me men singers and women singers, and the delights of the sons of men, as musical instruments, and that of all sorts.
ECC.2.PLAIN: and I accumulated for myself silver and gold and the treasure of kings and provinces. I gathered to myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men—many concubines.

ECC.2.BSB: So I became great and surpassed all in Jerusalem who had preceded me; and my wisdom remained with me.
ECC.2.KJV: So I was great, and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained with me.
ECC.2.PLAIN: So I became great and surpassed all in Jerusalem who had preceded me; and my wisdom remained with me.

ECC.2.BSB: Anything my eyes desired, I did not deny myself. I refused my heart no pleasure. For my heart took delight in all my work, and this was the reward for all my labor.
ECC.2.KJV: And whatever my eyes desired I kept not from them, I withheld not my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced in all my labor: and this was my portion of all my labor.
ECC.2.PLAIN: Anything my eyes desired, I did not deny myself. I refused my heart no pleasure. For my heart took delight in all my work, and this was the reward for all my labor.

ECC.2.BSB: Yet when I considered all the works that my hands had accomplished and what I had toiled to achieve, I found everything to be futile, a pursuit of the wind; there was nothing to be gained under the sun.
ECC.2.KJV: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had worked, and on the labor that I had labored to do: and, behold, all was vanity and vexation of spirit, and there was no profit under the sun. ¶
ECC.2.PLAIN: Yet when I considered all the works that my hands had accomplished and what I had toiled to achieve, I found everything to be futile, a pursuit of the wind; there was nothing to be gained under the sun.

ECC.2.BSB: Then I turned to consider wisdom and madness and folly; for what more can the king’s successor do than what has already been accomplished?
ECC.2.KJV: And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what can the man do that comes after the king? even that which has been already done.
ECC.2.PLAIN: Then I turned to consider wisdom and madness and folly; for what more can the king’s successor do than what has already been accomplished?

ECC.2.BSB: And I saw that wisdom exceeds folly, just as light exceeds darkness:
ECC.2.KJV: Then I saw that wisdom excels folly, as far as light excels darkness.
ECC.2.PLAIN: And I saw that wisdom exceeds folly, just as light exceeds darkness:

ECC.2.BSB: The wise man has eyes in his head, but the fool walks in darkness. Yet I also came to realize that one fate overcomes them both.
ECC.2.KJV: The wise man’s eyes are in his head; but the fool walks in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happens to them all.
ECC.2.PLAIN: The wise man has eyes in his head, but the fool walks in darkness. Yet I also came to realize that one fate overcomes them both.

ECC.2.BSB: So I said to myself, “The fate of the fool will also befall me. What then have I gained by being wise?” And I said to myself that this too is futile.
ECC.2.KJV: Then said I in my heart, As it happens to the fool, so it happens even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then I said in my heart, that this also is vanity.
ECC.2.PLAIN: So I said to myself, “The fate of the fool will also befall me. What then have I gained by being wise?” And I said to myself that this too is futile.

ECC.2.BSB: For there is no lasting remembrance of the wise, just as with the fool, seeing that both will be forgotten in the days to come. Alas, the wise man will die just like the fool!
ECC.2.KJV: For there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dies the wise man? as the fool.
ECC.2.PLAIN: For there is no lasting remembrance of the wise, just as with the fool, seeing that both will be forgotten in the days to come. Alas, the wise man will die just like the fool!

ECC.2.BSB: So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. For everything is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
ECC.2.KJV: Therefore I hated life; because the work that is worked under the sun is grievous to me: for all is vanity and vexation of spirit. ¶
ECC.2.PLAIN: So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. For everything is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

ECC.2.BSB: I hated all for which I had toiled under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.
ECC.2.KJV: Yes, I hated all my labor which I had taken under the sun: because I should leave it to the man that shall be after me.
ECC.2.PLAIN: I hated all for which I had toiled under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.

ECC.2.BSB: And who knows whether that man will be wise or foolish? Yet he will take over all the labor at which I have worked skillfully under the sun. This too is futile.
ECC.2.KJV: And who knows whether he shall be a wise man or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labor wherein I have labored, and wherein I have showed myself wise under the sun. This is also vanity.
ECC.2.PLAIN: And who knows whether that man will be wise or foolish? Yet he will take over all the labor at which I have worked skillfully under the sun. This too is futile.

ECC.2.BSB: So my heart began to despair over all the labor that I had done under the sun.
ECC.2.KJV: Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labor which I took under the sun.
ECC.2.PLAIN: So my heart began to despair over all the labor that I had done under the sun.

ECC.2.BSB: When there is a man who has labored with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, and he must give his portion to a man who has not worked for it, this too is futile and a great evil.
ECC.2.KJV: For there is a man whose labor is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that has not labored therein shall he leave it for his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil.
ECC.2.PLAIN: When there is a man who has labored with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, and he must give his portion to a man who has not worked for it, this too is futile and a great evil.

ECC.2.BSB: For what does a man get for all the toil and striving with which he labors under the sun?
ECC.2.KJV: For what has man of all his labor, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he has labored under the sun?
ECC.2.PLAIN: For what does a man get for all the toil and striving with which he labors under the sun?

ECC.2.BSB: Indeed, all his days are filled with grief, and his task is sorrowful; even at night, his mind does not rest. This too is futile.
ECC.2.KJV: For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yes, his heart takes not rest in the night. This is also vanity. ¶
ECC.2.PLAIN: Indeed, all his days are filled with grief, and his task is sorrowful; even at night, his mind does not rest. This too is futile.

ECC.2.BSB: Nothing is better for a man than to eat and drink and enjoy his work. I have also seen that this is from the hand of God.
ECC.2.KJV: There is nothing better for a man, than that he should eat and drink, and that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labor. This also I saw, that it was from the hand of God.
ECC.2.PLAIN: Nothing is better for a man than to eat and drink and enjoy his work. I have also seen that this is from the hand of God.

ECC.2.BSB: For apart from Him, who can eat and who can find enjoyment?
ECC.2.KJV: For who can eat, or who else can hasten hereunto, more than I?
ECC.2.PLAIN: For apart from Him, who can eat and who can find enjoyment?

ECC.2.BSB: To the man who is pleasing in His sight, He gives wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner He assigns the task of gathering and accumulating that which he will hand over to one who pleases God. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
ECC.2.KJV: For God gives to a man that is good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he gives travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him that is good before God. This also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
ECC.2.PLAIN: To the man who is pleasing in His sight, He gives wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner He assigns the task of gathering and accumulating that which he will hand over to one who pleases God. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

ECC.3.BSB: To everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:
ECC.3.KJV: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
ECC.3.PLAIN: There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens.

ECC.3.BSB: a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot,
ECC.3.KJV: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;
ECC.3.PLAIN: a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot,

ECC.3.BSB: a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to break down and a time to build,
ECC.3.KJV: A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
ECC.3.PLAIN: a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to break down and a time to build,

ECC.3.BSB: a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance,
ECC.3.KJV: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
ECC.3.PLAIN: a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance,

ECC.3.BSB: a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together, a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing,
ECC.3.KJV: A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
ECC.3.PLAIN: a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together, a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing,

ECC.3.BSB: a time to search and a time to count as lost, a time to keep and a time to discard,
ECC.3.KJV: A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;
ECC.3.PLAIN: a time to search and a time to count as lost, a time to keep and a time to discard,

ECC.3.BSB: a time to tear and a time to mend, a time to be silent and a time to speak,
ECC.3.KJV: A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
ECC.3.PLAIN: a time to tear and a time to mend, a time to be silent and a time to speak,

ECC.3.BSB: a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.
ECC.3.KJV: A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.
ECC.3.PLAIN: a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.

ECC.3.BSB: What does the worker gain from his toil?
ECC.3.KJV: What profit has he that works in that wherein he labors?
ECC.3.PLAIN: What does the worker gain from his toil?

ECC.3.BSB: I have seen the burden that God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them.
ECC.3.KJV: I have seen the travail, which God has given to the sons of men to be exercised in it.
ECC.3.PLAIN: I have seen the burden that God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them.

ECC.3.BSB: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the hearts of men, yet they cannot fathom the work that God has done from beginning to end.
ECC.3.KJV: He has made every thing beautiful in his time: also he has set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God makes from the beginning to the end.
ECC.3.PLAIN: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the human heart, yet no one can fathom what God has done from beginning to end.

ECC.3.BSB: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and do good while they live,
ECC.3.KJV: I know that there is no good in them, but for a man to rejoice, and to do good in his life.
ECC.3.PLAIN: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and do good while they live,

ECC.3.BSB: and also that every man should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all his labor—this is the gift of God.
ECC.3.KJV: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labor, it is the gift of God.
ECC.3.PLAIN: and also that every man should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all his labor—this is the gift of God.

ECC.3.BSB: I know that everything God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it or taken from it. God does it so that they should fear Him.
ECC.3.KJV: I know that, whatever God does, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God does it, that men should fear before him.
ECC.3.PLAIN: I know that everything God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it or taken from it. God does it so that they should fear Him.

ECC.3.BSB: What exists has already been, and what will be has already been, for God will call to account what has passed.
ECC.3.KJV: That which has been is now; and that which is to be has already been; and God requires that which is past. ¶
ECC.3.PLAIN: What exists has already been, and what will be has already been, for God will call to account what has passed.

ECC.3.BSB: Furthermore, I saw under the sun that in the place of judgment there is wickedness, and in the place of righteousness there is wickedness.
ECC.3.KJV: And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment, that wickedness was there; and the place of righteousness, that iniquity was there.
ECC.3.PLAIN: Furthermore, I saw under the sun that in the place of judgment there is wickedness, and in the place of righteousness there is wickedness.

ECC.3.BSB: I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked, since there is a time for every activity and every deed.”
ECC.3.KJV: I said in my heart, God shall judge the righteous and the wicked: for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.
ECC.3.PLAIN: I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked, since there is a time for every activity and every deed.”

ECC.3.BSB: I said to myself, “As for the sons of men, God tests them so that they may see for themselves that they are but beasts.”
ECC.3.KJV: I said in my heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.
ECC.3.PLAIN: I said to myself, “As for the sons of men, God tests them so that they may see for themselves that they are but beasts.”

ECC.3.BSB: For the fates of both men and beasts are the same: As one dies, so dies the other—they all have the same breath. Man has no advantage over the animals, since everything is futile.
ECC.3.KJV: For that which befalls the sons of men befalls beasts; even one thing befalls them: as the one dies, so dies the other; yes, they have all one breath; so that a man has no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.
ECC.3.PLAIN: For the fates of both men and beasts are the same: As one dies, so dies the other—they all have the same breath. Man has no advantage over the animals, since everything is futile.

ECC.3.BSB: All go to one place; all come from dust, and all return to dust.
ECC.3.KJV: All go to one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.
ECC.3.PLAIN: All go to one place; all come from dust, and all return to dust.

ECC.3.BSB: Who knows if the spirit of man rises upward and the spirit of the animal descends into the earth?
ECC.3.KJV: Who knows the spirit of man that goes upward, and the spirit of the beast that goes downward to the earth?
ECC.3.PLAIN: Who knows if the spirit of man rises upward and the spirit of the animal descends into the earth?

ECC.3.BSB: I have seen that there is nothing better for a man than to enjoy his work, because that is his lot. For who can bring him to see what will come after him?
ECC.3.KJV: Why I perceive that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that is his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?
ECC.3.PLAIN: I have seen that there is nothing better for a man than to enjoy his work, because that is his lot. For who can bring him to see what will come after him?

ECC.4.BSB: Again I looked, and I considered all the oppression taking place under the sun. I saw the tears of the oppressed, and they had no comforter; the power lay in the hands of their oppressors, and there was no comforter.
ECC.4.KJV: So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.
