ECC.4.PLAIN: Again I looked, and I considered all the oppression taking place under the sun. I saw the tears of the oppressed, and they had no comforter; the power lay in the hands of their oppressors, and there was no comforter.

ECC.4.BSB: So I admired the dead, who had already died, above the living, who are still alive.
ECC.4.KJV: Why I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.
ECC.4.PLAIN: So I admired the dead, who had already died, above the living, who are still alive.

ECC.4.BSB: But better than both is he who has not yet existed, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.
ECC.4.KJV: Yes, better is he than both they, which has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun. ¶
ECC.4.PLAIN: But better than both is he who has not yet existed, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.

ECC.4.BSB: I saw that all labor and success spring from a man’s envy of his neighbor. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
ECC.4.KJV: Again, I considered all travail, and every right work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbor. This is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
ECC.4.PLAIN: I saw that all labor and success spring from a man’s envy of his neighbor. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

ECC.4.BSB: The fool folds his hands and consumes his own flesh.
ECC.4.KJV: The fool folds his hands together, and eats his own flesh.
ECC.4.PLAIN: The fool folds his hands and consumes his own flesh.

ECC.4.BSB: Better one handful with tranquility than two handfuls with toil and pursuit of the wind.
ECC.4.KJV: Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit. ¶
ECC.4.PLAIN: Better one handful with tranquility than two handfuls with toil and pursuit of the wind.

ECC.4.BSB: Again, I saw futility under the sun.
ECC.4.KJV: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.
ECC.4.PLAIN: Again, I saw futility under the sun.

ECC.4.BSB: There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile—a miserable task.
ECC.4.KJV: There is one alone, and there is not a second; yes, he has neither child nor brother: yet is there no end of all his labor; neither is his eye satisfied with riches; neither says he, For whom do I labor, and bereave my soul of good? This is also vanity, yes, it is a sore travail. ¶
ECC.4.PLAIN: There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile—a miserable task.

ECC.4.BSB: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor.
ECC.4.KJV: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labor.
ECC.4.PLAIN: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor.

ECC.4.BSB: For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!
ECC.4.KJV: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falls; for he has not another to help him up.
ECC.4.PLAIN: For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!

ECC.4.BSB: Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; but how can one keep warm alone?
ECC.4.KJV: Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone?
ECC.4.PLAIN: Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; but how can one keep warm alone?

ECC.4.BSB: And though one may be overpowered, two can resist. Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.
ECC.4.KJV: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken. ¶
ECC.4.PLAIN: And though one may be overpowered, two can resist. Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.

ECC.4.BSB: Better is a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to take a warning.
ECC.4.KJV: Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.
ECC.4.PLAIN: Better is a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to take a warning.

ECC.4.BSB: For the youth has come from the prison to the kingship, though he was born poor in his own kingdom.
ECC.4.KJV: For out of prison he comes to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becomes poor.
ECC.4.PLAIN: For the youth has come from the prison to the kingship, though he was born poor in his own kingdom.

ECC.4.BSB: I saw that all who lived and walked under the sun followed this second one, the youth who succeeded the king.
ECC.4.KJV: I considered all the living which walk under the sun, with the second child that shall stand up in his stead.
ECC.4.PLAIN: I saw that all who lived and walked under the sun followed this second one, the youth who succeeded the king.

ECC.4.BSB: There is no limit to all the people who were before them. Yet the successor will not be celebrated by those who come even later. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
ECC.4.KJV: There is no end of all the people, even of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
ECC.4.PLAIN: There is no limit to all the people who were before them. Yet the successor will not be celebrated by those who come even later. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

ECC.5.BSB: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Draw near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not know that they do wrong.
ECC.5.KJV: Keep your foot when you go to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.
ECC.5.PLAIN: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Draw near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not know that they do wrong.

ECC.5.BSB: Do not be quick to speak, and do not be hasty in your heart to utter a word before God. After all, God is in heaven and you are on earth. So let your words be few.
ECC.5.KJV: Be not rash with your mouth, and let not your heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and you on earth: therefore let your words be few.
ECC.5.PLAIN: Do not be quick to speak, and do not be hasty in your heart to utter a word before God. After all, God is in heaven and you are on earth. So let your words be few.

ECC.5.BSB: As a dream comes through many cares, so the speech of a fool comes with many words.
ECC.5.KJV: For a dream comes through the multitude of business; and a fool’s voice is known by multitude of words.
ECC.5.PLAIN: As a dream comes through many cares, so the speech of a fool comes with many words.

ECC.5.BSB: When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it, because He takes no pleasure in fools. Fulfill your vow.
ECC.5.KJV: When you vow a vow to God, defer not to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools: pay that which you have vowed.
ECC.5.PLAIN: When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it, because He takes no pleasure in fools. Fulfill your vow.

ECC.5.BSB: It is better not to vow than to make a vow and not fulfill it.
ECC.5.KJV: Better is it that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay.
ECC.5.PLAIN: It is better not to vow than to make a vow and not fulfill it.

ECC.5.BSB: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not tell the messenger that your vow was a mistake. Why should God be angry with your words and destroy the work of your hands?
ECC.5.KJV: Suffer not your mouth to cause your flesh to sin; neither say you before the angel, that it was an error: why should God be angry at your voice, and destroy the work of your hands?
ECC.5.PLAIN: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not tell the messenger that your vow was a mistake. Why should God be angry with your words and destroy the work of your hands?

ECC.5.BSB: For as many dreams bring futility, so do many words. Therefore, fear God.
ECC.5.KJV: For in the multitude of dreams and many words there are also divers vanities: but fear you God. ¶
ECC.5.PLAIN: For as many dreams bring futility, so do many words. Therefore, fear God.

ECC.5.BSB: If you see the oppression of the poor and the denial of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be astonished at the matter; for one official is watched by a superior, and others higher still are over them.
ECC.5.KJV: If you see the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regards; and there be higher than they. ¶
ECC.5.PLAIN: If you see the oppression of the poor and the denial of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be astonished at the matter; for one official is watched by a superior, and others higher still are over them.

ECC.5.BSB: The produce of the earth is taken by all; the king himself profits from the fields.
ECC.5.KJV: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king himself is served by the field.
ECC.5.PLAIN: The produce of the earth is taken by all; the king himself profits from the fields.

ECC.5.BSB: He who loves money is never satisfied by money, and he who loves wealth is never satisfied by income. This too is futile.
ECC.5.KJV: He that loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loves abundance with increase: this is also vanity.
ECC.5.PLAIN: He who loves money is never satisfied by money, and he who loves wealth is never satisfied by income. This too is futile.

ECC.5.BSB: When good things increase, so do those who consume them; what then is the profit to the owner, except to behold them with his eyes?
ECC.5.KJV: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good is there to the owners thereof, saving the beholding of them with their eyes?
ECC.5.PLAIN: When good things increase, so do those who consume them; what then is the profit to the owner, except to behold them with his eyes?

ECC.5.BSB: The sleep of the worker is sweet, whether he eats little or much, but the abundance of the rich man permits him no sleep.
ECC.5.KJV: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.
ECC.5.PLAIN: The sleep of the worker is sweet, whether he eats little or much, but the abundance of the rich man permits him no sleep.

ECC.5.BSB: There is a grievous evil I have seen under the sun: wealth hoarded to the harm of its owner,
ECC.5.KJV: There is a sore evil which I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt.
ECC.5.PLAIN: There is a grievous evil I have seen under the sun: wealth hoarded to the harm of its owner,

ECC.5.BSB: or wealth lost in a failed venture, so when that man has a son there is nothing to pass on.
ECC.5.KJV: But those riches perish by evil travail: and he begets a son, and there is nothing in his hand.
ECC.5.PLAIN: or wealth lost in a failed venture, so when that man has a son there is nothing to pass on.

ECC.5.BSB: As a man came from his mother’s womb, so he will depart again, naked as he arrived. He takes nothing for his labor to carry in his hands.
ECC.5.KJV: As he came forth of his mother’s womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labor, which he may carry away in his hand.
ECC.5.PLAIN: As a man came from his mother’s womb, so he will depart again, naked as he arrived. He takes nothing for his labor to carry in his hands.

ECC.5.BSB: This too is a grievous evil: Exactly as a man is born, so he will depart. What does he gain as he toils for the wind?
ECC.5.KJV: And this also is a sore evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit has he that has labored for the wind?
ECC.5.PLAIN: This too is a grievous evil: Exactly as a man is born, so he will depart. What does he gain as he toils for the wind?

ECC.5.BSB: Moreover, all his days he eats in darkness, with much sorrow, sickness, and anger.
ECC.5.KJV: All his days also he eats in darkness, and he has much sorrow and wrath with his sickness. ¶
ECC.5.PLAIN: Moreover, all his days he eats in darkness, with much sorrow, sickness, and anger.

ECC.5.BSB: Here is what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat and drink, and to find satisfaction in all the labor one does under the sun during the few days of life that God has given him—for this is his lot.
ECC.5.KJV: Behold that which I have seen: it is good and comely for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labor that he takes under the sun all the days of his life, which God gives him: for it is his portion.
ECC.5.PLAIN: Here is what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat and drink, and to find satisfaction in all the labor one does under the sun during the few days of life that God has given him—for this is his lot.

ECC.5.BSB: Furthermore, God has given riches and wealth to every man, and He has enabled him to enjoy them, to accept his lot, and to rejoice in his labor. This is a gift from God.
ECC.5.KJV: Every man also to whom God has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor; this is the gift of God.
ECC.5.PLAIN: Furthermore, God has given riches and wealth to every man, and He has enabled him to enjoy them, to accept his lot, and to rejoice in his labor. This is a gift from God.

ECC.5.BSB: For a man seldom considers the days of his life, because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart.
ECC.5.KJV: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God answers him in the joy of his heart.
ECC.5.PLAIN: For a man seldom considers the days of his life, because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart.

ECC.6.BSB: There is another evil I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily upon mankind:
ECC.6.KJV: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men:
ECC.6.PLAIN: There is another evil I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily upon mankind:

ECC.6.BSB: God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing his heart desires; but God does not allow him to enjoy them. Instead, a stranger will enjoy them. This is futile and a grievous affliction.
ECC.6.KJV: A man to whom God has given riches, wealth, and honor, so that he wants nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet God gives him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eats it: this is vanity, and it is an evil disease. ¶
ECC.6.PLAIN: God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing his heart desires; but God does not allow him to enjoy them. Instead, a stranger will enjoy them. This is futile and a grievous affliction.

ECC.6.BSB: A man may father a hundred children and live for many years; yet no matter how long he lives, if he is unsatisfied with his prosperity and does not even receive a proper burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.
ECC.6.KJV: If a man beget an hundred children, and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled with good, and also that he have no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he.
ECC.6.PLAIN: A man may father a hundred children and live for many years; yet no matter how long he lives, if he is unsatisfied with his prosperity and does not even receive a proper burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.

ECC.6.BSB: For a stillborn child enters in futility and departs in darkness, and his name is shrouded in obscurity.
ECC.6.KJV: For he comes in with vanity, and departs in darkness, and his name shall be covered with darkness.
ECC.6.PLAIN: For a stillborn child enters in futility and departs in darkness, and his name is shrouded in obscurity.

ECC.6.BSB: The child, though neither seeing the sun nor knowing anything, has more rest than that man,
ECC.6.KJV: Moreover he has not seen the sun, nor known any thing: this has more rest than the other. ¶
ECC.6.PLAIN: The child, though neither seeing the sun nor knowing anything, has more rest than that man,

ECC.6.BSB: even if he lives a thousand years twice over but fails to enjoy his prosperity. Do not all go to the same place?
ECC.6.KJV: Yes, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet has he seen no good: do not all go to one place?
ECC.6.PLAIN: even if he lives a thousand years twice over but fails to enjoy his prosperity. Do not all go to the same place?

ECC.6.BSB: All a man’s labor is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied.
ECC.6.KJV: All the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
ECC.6.PLAIN: All a man’s labor is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied.

ECC.6.BSB: What advantage, then, has the wise man over the fool? What gain comes to the poor man who knows how to conduct himself before others?
ECC.6.KJV: For what has the wise more than the fool? what has the poor, that knows to walk before the living? ¶
ECC.6.PLAIN: What advantage, then, has the wise man over the fool? What gain comes to the poor man who knows how to conduct himself before others?

ECC.6.BSB: Better what the eye can see than the wandering of desire. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
ECC.6.KJV: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
ECC.6.PLAIN: Better what the eye can see than the wandering of desire. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

ECC.6.BSB: Whatever exists was named long ago, and what happens to a man is foreknown; but he cannot contend with one stronger than he.
ECC.6.KJV: That which has been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he. ¶
ECC.6.PLAIN: Whatever exists was named long ago, and what happens to a man is foreknown; but he cannot contend with one stronger than he.

ECC.6.BSB: For the more words, the more futility—and how does that profit anyone?
ECC.6.KJV: Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?
ECC.6.PLAIN: For the more words, the more futility—and how does that profit anyone?

ECC.6.BSB: For who knows what is good for a man during the few days in which he passes through his fleeting life like a shadow? Who can tell a man what will come after him under the sun?
ECC.6.KJV: For who knows what is good for man in this life, all the days of his vain life which he spends as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?
ECC.6.PLAIN: For who knows what is good for a man during the few days in which he passes through his fleeting life like a shadow? Who can tell a man what will come after him under the sun?

ECC.7.BSB: A good name is better than fine perfume, and one’s day of death is better than his day of birth.
ECC.7.KJV: A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one’s birth. ¶
ECC.7.PLAIN: A good name is better than fine perfume, and one’s day of death is better than his day of birth.

ECC.7.BSB: It is better to enter a house of mourning than a house of feasting, since death is the end of every man, and the living should take this to heart.
ECC.7.KJV: It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart.
ECC.7.PLAIN: It is better to enter a house of mourning than a house of feasting, since death is the end of every man, and the living should take this to heart.

ECC.7.BSB: Sorrow is better than laughter, for a sad countenance is good for the heart.
ECC.7.KJV: Sorrow is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.
ECC.7.PLAIN: Sorrow is better than laughter, for a sad countenance is good for the heart.

ECC.7.BSB: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.
ECC.7.KJV: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
ECC.7.PLAIN: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.

ECC.7.BSB: It is better to heed a wise man’s rebuke than to listen to the song of fools.
ECC.7.KJV: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
ECC.7.PLAIN: It is better to heed a wise man’s rebuke than to listen to the song of fools.

ECC.7.BSB: For like the crackling of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This too is futile.
ECC.7.KJV: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool: this also is vanity. ¶
ECC.7.PLAIN: For like the crackling of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This too is futile.

ECC.7.BSB: Surely extortion turns a wise man into a fool, and a bribe corrupts the heart.
ECC.7.KJV: Surely oppression makes a wise man mad; and a gift destroys the heart.
ECC.7.PLAIN: Surely extortion turns a wise man into a fool, and a bribe corrupts the heart.

ECC.7.BSB: The end of a matter is better than the beginning, and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.
ECC.7.KJV: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
ECC.7.PLAIN: The end of a matter is better than the beginning, and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.

ECC.7.BSB: Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger settles in the lap of a fool.
ECC.7.KJV: Be not hasty in your spirit to be angry: for anger rests in the bosom of fools.
ECC.7.PLAIN: Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger settles in the lap of a fool.

ECC.7.BSB: Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?” For it is unwise of you to ask about this.
ECC.7.KJV: Say not you, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? for you do not inquire wisely concerning this. ¶
ECC.7.PLAIN: Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?” For it is unwise of you to ask about this.

ECC.7.BSB: Wisdom, like an inheritance, is good, and it benefits those who see the sun.
ECC.7.KJV: Wisdom is good with an inheritance: and by it there is profit to them that see the sun.
ECC.7.PLAIN: Wisdom, like an inheritance, is good, and it benefits those who see the sun.

ECC.7.BSB: For wisdom, like money, is a shelter, and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its owner.
ECC.7.KJV: For wisdom is a defense, and money is a defense: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom gives life to them that have it.
ECC.7.PLAIN: For wisdom, like money, is a shelter, and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its owner.

ECC.7.BSB: Consider the work of God: Who can straighten what He has bent?
ECC.7.KJV: Consider the work of God: for who can make that straight, which he has made crooked?
ECC.7.PLAIN: Consider the work of God: Who can straighten what He has bent?

ECC.7.BSB: In the day of prosperity, be joyful, but in the day of adversity, consider this: God has made one of these along with the other, so that a man cannot discover anything that will come after him.
ECC.7.KJV: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also has set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.
ECC.7.PLAIN: In the day of prosperity, be joyful, but in the day of adversity, consider this: God has made one of these along with the other, so that a man cannot discover anything that will come after him.

ECC.7.BSB: In my futile life I have seen both of these: A righteous man perishing in his righteousness, and a wicked man living long in his wickedness.
ECC.7.KJV: All things have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just man that perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man that prolongs his life in his wickedness.
ECC.7.PLAIN: In my futile life I have seen both of these: A righteous man perishing in his righteousness, and a wicked man living long in his wickedness.

ECC.7.BSB: Do not be overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
ECC.7.KJV: Be not righteous over much; neither make yourself over wise: why should you destroy yourself?
ECC.7.PLAIN: Do not be overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you destroy yourself?

ECC.7.BSB: Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?
ECC.7.KJV: Be not over much wicked, neither be you foolish: why should you die before your time?
ECC.7.PLAIN: Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?

ECC.7.BSB: It is good to grasp the one and not let the other slip from your hand. For he who fears God will follow both warnings.
ECC.7.KJV: It is good that you should take hold of this; yes, also from this withdraw not your hand: for he that fears God shall come forth of them all.
ECC.7.PLAIN: It is good to grasp the one and not let the other slip from your hand. For he who fears God will follow both warnings.

ECC.7.BSB: Wisdom makes the wise man stronger than ten rulers in a city.
ECC.7.KJV: Wisdom strengthens the wise more than ten mighty men which are in the city.
ECC.7.PLAIN: Wisdom makes the wise man stronger than ten rulers in a city.

ECC.7.BSB: Surely there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.
ECC.7.KJV: For there is not a just man on earth, that does good, and sins not.
ECC.7.PLAIN: Surely there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.

ECC.7.BSB: Do not pay attention to every word that is spoken, or you may hear your servant cursing you.
ECC.7.KJV: Also take no heed to all words that are spoken; lest you hear your servant curse you:
ECC.7.PLAIN: Do not pay attention to every word that is spoken, or you may hear your servant cursing you.

ECC.7.BSB: For you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others.
ECC.7.KJV: For oftentimes also your own heart knows that you yourself likewise have cursed others. ¶
ECC.7.PLAIN: For you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others.

ECC.7.BSB: All this I tested by wisdom, saying, “I resolve to be wise.” But it was beyond me.
ECC.7.KJV: All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.
ECC.7.PLAIN: All this I tested by wisdom, saying, “I resolve to be wise.” But it was beyond me.

ECC.7.BSB: What exists is out of reach and very deep. Who can fathom it?
ECC.7.KJV: That which is far off, and exceeding deep, who can find it out?
ECC.7.PLAIN: What exists is out of reach and very deep. Who can fathom it?

ECC.7.BSB: I directed my mind to understand, to explore, to search out wisdom and explanations, and to understand the stupidity of wickedness and the folly of madness.
ECC.7.KJV: I applied my heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason of things, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness and madness:
ECC.7.PLAIN: I directed my mind to understand, to explore, to search out wisdom and explanations, and to understand the stupidity of wickedness and the folly of madness.

ECC.7.BSB: And I find more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a net, and whose hands are chains. The man who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is ensnared.
ECC.7.KJV: And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoever pleases God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.
ECC.7.PLAIN: And I find more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a net, and whose hands are chains. The man who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is ensnared.

ECC.7.BSB: “Behold,” says the Teacher, “I have discovered this by adding one thing to another to find an explanation.
ECC.7.KJV: Behold, this have I found, says the preacher, counting one by one, to find out the account:
ECC.7.PLAIN: “Look closely — ” says the Teacher, “I have discovered this by adding one thing to another to find an explanation.

ECC.7.BSB: While my soul was still searching but not finding, among a thousand I have found one upright man, but among all these I have not found one such woman.
ECC.7.KJV: Which yet my soul seeks, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.
ECC.7.PLAIN: While my soul was still searching but not finding, among a thousand I have found one upright man, but among all these I have not found one such woman.

ECC.7.BSB: Only this have I found: I have discovered that God made men upright, but they have sought out many schemes.”
ECC.7.KJV: See, this only have I found, that God has made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.
ECC.7.PLAIN: Only this have I found: I have discovered that God made men upright, but they have sought out many schemes.”

ECC.8.BSB: Who is like the wise man? Who knows the interpretation of a matter? A man’s wisdom brightens his face, and the sternness of his face is changed.
ECC.8.KJV: Who is as the wise man? and who knows the interpretation of a thing? a man’s wisdom makes his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.
ECC.8.PLAIN: Who is like the wise man? Who knows the interpretation of a matter? A man’s wisdom brightens his face, and the sternness of his face is changed.

ECC.8.BSB: Keep the king’s command, I say, because of your oath before God.
ECC.8.KJV: I counsel you to keep the king’s commandment, and that in regard of the oath of God.
ECC.8.PLAIN: Keep the king’s command, I say, because of your oath before God.

ECC.8.BSB: Do not hasten to leave his presence, and do not persist in a bad cause, for he will do whatever he pleases.
ECC.8.KJV: Be not hasty to go out of his sight: stand not in an evil thing; for he does whatever pleases him.
ECC.8.PLAIN: Do not hasten to leave his presence, and do not persist in a bad cause, for he will do whatever he pleases.

ECC.8.BSB: For the king’s word is supreme, and who can say to him, “What are you doing?”
ECC.8.KJV: Where the word of a king is, there is power: and who may say to him, What do you?
ECC.8.PLAIN: For the king’s word is supreme, and who can say to him, “What are you doing?”

ECC.8.BSB: Whoever keeps his command will come to no harm, and a wise heart knows the right time and procedure.
ECC.8.KJV: Whoever keeps the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man’s heart discerns both time and judgment. ¶
ECC.8.PLAIN: Whoever keeps his command will come to no harm, and a wise heart knows the right time and procedure.

ECC.8.BSB: For there is a right time and procedure to every purpose, though a man’s misery weighs heavily upon him.
ECC.8.KJV: Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man is great on him.
ECC.8.PLAIN: For there is a right time and procedure to every purpose, though a man’s misery weighs heavily upon him.

ECC.8.BSB: Since no one knows what will happen, who can tell him what is to come?
ECC.8.KJV: For he knows not that which shall be: for who can tell him when it shall be?
ECC.8.PLAIN: Since no one knows what will happen, who can tell him what is to come?

ECC.8.BSB: As no man has power over the wind to contain it, so no one has authority over his day of death. As no one can be discharged in wartime, so wickedness will not release those who practice it.
ECC.8.KJV: There is no man that has power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither has he power in the day of death: and there is no discharge in that war; neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it.
ECC.8.PLAIN: As no man has power over the wind to contain it, so no one has authority over his day of death. As no one can be discharged in wartime, so wickedness will not release those who practice it.

ECC.8.BSB: All this I have seen, applying my mind to every deed that is done under the sun; there is a time when one man lords it over another to his own detriment.
ECC.8.KJV: All this have I seen, and applied my heart to every work that is done under the sun: there is a time wherein one man rules over another to his own hurt.
ECC.8.PLAIN: All this I have seen, applying my mind to every deed that is done under the sun; there is a time when one man lords it over another to his own detriment.

ECC.8.BSB: Then too, I saw the burial of the wicked who used to go in and out of the holy place, and they were praised in the city where they had done so. This too is futile.
ECC.8.KJV: And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so done: this is also vanity.
ECC.8.PLAIN: Then too, I saw the burial of the wicked who used to go in and out of the holy place, and they were praised in the city where they had done so. This too is futile.

ECC.8.BSB: When the sentence for a crime is not speedily executed, the hearts of men become fully set on doing evil.
ECC.8.KJV: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil. ¶
ECC.8.PLAIN: When the sentence for a crime is not speedily executed, the hearts of men become fully set on doing evil.

ECC.8.BSB: Although a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives long, yet I also know that it will go well with those who fear God, who are reverent in His presence.
ECC.8.KJV: Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his days be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, which fear before him:
ECC.8.PLAIN: Although a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives long, yet I also know that it will go well with those who fear God, who are reverent in His presence.

ECC.8.BSB: Yet because the wicked do not fear God, it will not go well with them, and their days will not lengthen like a shadow.
ECC.8.KJV: But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong his days, which are as a shadow; because he fears not before God.
ECC.8.PLAIN: Yet because the wicked do not fear God, it will not go well with them, and their days will not lengthen like a shadow.

ECC.8.BSB: There is a futility that is done on the earth: There are righteous men who get what the actions of the wicked deserve, and there are wicked men who get what the actions of the righteous deserve. I say that this too is futile.
ECC.8.KJV: There is a vanity which is done on the earth; that there be just men, to whom it happens according to the work of the wicked; again, there be wicked men, to whom it happens according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also is vanity.
ECC.8.PLAIN: There is a futility that is done on the earth: There are righteous men who get what the actions of the wicked deserve, and there are wicked men who get what the actions of the righteous deserve. I say that this too is futile.

ECC.8.BSB: So I commended the enjoyment of life, because there is nothing better for a man under the sun than to eat and drink and be merry. For this joy will accompany him in his labor during the days of his life that God gives him under the sun.
ECC.8.KJV: Then I commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide with him of his labor the days of his life, which God gives him under the sun. ¶
ECC.8.PLAIN: So I commended the enjoyment of life, because there is nothing better for a man under the sun than to eat and drink and be merry. For this joy will accompany him in his labor during the days of his life that God gives him under the sun.

ECC.8.BSB: When I applied my mind to know wisdom and to observe the task that one performs on the earth—though his eyes do not see sleep in the day or even in the night—
ECC.8.KJV: When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done on the earth: (for also there is that neither day nor night sees sleep with his eyes:)
ECC.8.PLAIN: When I applied my mind to know wisdom and to observe the task that one performs on the earth—though his eyes do not see sleep in the day or even in the night—

ECC.8.BSB: I saw every work of God, and that a man is unable to comprehend the work that is done under the sun. Despite his efforts to search it out, he cannot find its meaning; even if the wise man claims to know, he is unable to comprehend.
ECC.8.KJV: Then I beheld all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labor to seek it out, yet he shall not find it; yes farther; though a wise man think to know it, yet shall he not be able to find it.
ECC.8.PLAIN: I saw every work of God, and that a man is unable to comprehend the work that is done under the sun. Despite his efforts to search it out, he cannot find its meaning; even if the wise man claims to know, he is unable to comprehend.

ECC.9.BSB: So I took all this to heart and concluded that the righteous and the wise, as well as their deeds, are in God’s hands. Man does not know what lies ahead, whether love or hate.
ECC.9.KJV: For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God: no man knows either love or hatred by all that is before them.
ECC.9.PLAIN: So I took all this to heart and concluded that the righteous and the wise, as well as their deeds, are in God’s hands. Man does not know what lies ahead, whether love or hate.

ECC.9.BSB: It is the same for all: There is a common fate for the righteous and the wicked, for the good and the bad, for the clean and the unclean, for the one who sacrifices and the one who does not. As it is for the good, so it is for the sinner; as it is for the one who makes a vow, so it is for the one who refuses to take a vow.
ECC.9.KJV: All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrifices, and to him that sacrifices not: as is the good, so is the sinner; and he that swears, as he that fears an oath.
ECC.9.PLAIN: It is the same for all: There is a common fate for the righteous and the wicked, for the good and the bad, for the clean and the unclean, for the one who sacrifices and the one who does not. As it is for the good, so it is for the sinner; as it is for the one who makes a vow, so it is for the one who refuses to take a vow.

ECC.9.BSB: This is an evil in everything that is done under the sun: There is one fate for everyone. Furthermore, the hearts of men are full of evil and madness while they are alive, and afterward they join the dead.
ECC.9.KJV: This is an evil among all things that are done under the sun, that there is one event to all: yes, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead. ¶
ECC.9.PLAIN: This is an evil in everything that is done under the sun: There is one fate for everyone. Furthermore, the hearts of men are full of evil and madness while they are alive, and afterward they join the dead.

ECC.9.BSB: There is hope, however, for anyone who is among the living; for even a live dog is better than a dead lion.
ECC.9.KJV: For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
ECC.9.PLAIN: There is hope, however, for anyone who is among the living; for even a live dog is better than a dead lion.

ECC.9.BSB: For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
ECC.9.KJV: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.
ECC.9.PLAIN: For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.

ECC.9.BSB: Their love, their hate, and their envy have already vanished, and they will never again have a share in all that is done under the sun.
ECC.9.KJV: Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any thing that is done under the sun. ¶
ECC.9.PLAIN: Their love, their hate, and their envy have already vanished, and they will never again have a share in all that is done under the sun.

ECC.9.BSB: Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, for God has already approved your works:
ECC.9.KJV: Go your way, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart; for God now accepts your works.
ECC.9.PLAIN: Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, for God has already approved your works:

ECC.9.BSB: Let your garments always be white, and never spare the oil for your head.
ECC.9.KJV: Let your garments be always white; and let your head lack no ointment.
ECC.9.PLAIN: Let your garments always be white, and never spare the oil for your head.

ECC.9.BSB: Enjoy life with your beloved wife all the days of the fleeting life that God has given you under the sun—all your fleeting days. For this is your portion in life and in your labor under the sun.
ECC.9.KJV: Live joyfully with the wife whom you love all the days of the life of your vanity, which he has given you under the sun, all the days of your vanity: for that is your portion in this life, and in your labor which you take under the sun.
ECC.9.PLAIN: Enjoy life with your beloved wife all the days of the fleeting life that God has given you under the sun—all your fleeting days. For this is your portion in life and in your labor under the sun.

ECC.9.BSB: Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.
ECC.9.KJV: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, where you go. ¶
ECC.9.PLAIN: Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.

ECC.9.BSB: I saw something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; neither is the bread to the wise, nor the wealth to the intelligent, nor the favor to the skillful. For time and chance happen to all.
ECC.9.KJV: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happens to them all.
ECC.9.PLAIN: I saw something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; neither is the bread to the wise, nor the wealth to the intelligent, nor the favor to the skillful. For time and chance happen to all.

ECC.9.BSB: For surely no man knows his time: Like fish caught in a cruel net or birds trapped in a snare, so men are ensnared in an evil time that suddenly falls upon them.
ECC.9.KJV: For man also knows not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falls suddenly on them. ¶
ECC.9.PLAIN: For surely no man knows his time: Like fish caught in a cruel net or birds trapped in a snare, so men are ensnared in an evil time that suddenly falls upon them.

ECC.9.BSB: I have also seen this wisdom under the sun, and it was great to me:
ECC.9.KJV: This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it seemed great to me:
ECC.9.PLAIN: I have also seen this wisdom under the sun, and it was great to me:

ECC.9.BSB: There was a small city with few men. A mighty king came against it, surrounded it, and built large siege ramps against it.
ECC.9.KJV: There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it:
ECC.9.PLAIN: There was a small city with few men. A mighty king came against it, surrounded it, and built large siege ramps against it.

ECC.9.BSB: Now a poor wise man was found in the city, and he saved the city by his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man.
ECC.9.KJV: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.
ECC.9.PLAIN: Now a poor wise man was found in the city, and he saved the city by his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man.

ECC.9.BSB: And I said, “Wisdom is better than strength, but the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are not heeded.”
ECC.9.KJV: Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
ECC.9.PLAIN: And I said, “Wisdom is better than strength, but the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are not heeded.”

ECC.9.BSB: The calm words of the wise are heeded over the shouts of a ruler among fools.
ECC.9.KJV: The words of wise men are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that rules among fools.
ECC.9.PLAIN: The calm words of the wise are heeded over the shouts of a ruler among fools.

ECC.9.BSB: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.
ECC.9.KJV: Wisdom is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroys much good.
ECC.9.PLAIN: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.

ECC.10.BSB: As dead flies bring a stench to the perfumer’s oil, so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.
ECC.10.KJV: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking smell: so does a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honor.
ECC.10.PLAIN: As dead flies bring a stench to the perfumer’s oil, so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.

ECC.10.BSB: A wise man’s heart inclines to the right, but the heart of a fool to the left.
ECC.10.KJV: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand; but a fool’s heart at his left.
ECC.10.PLAIN: A wise man’s heart inclines to the right, but the heart of a fool to the left.

ECC.10.BSB: Even as the fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking, and he shows everyone that he is a fool.
ECC.10.KJV: Yes also, when he that is a fool walks by the way, his wisdom fails him, and he says to every one that he is a fool.
ECC.10.PLAIN: Even as the fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking, and he shows everyone that he is a fool.

ECC.10.BSB: If the ruler’s temper flares against you, do not abandon your post, for calmness lays great offenses to rest.
ECC.10.KJV: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against you, leave not your place; for yielding pacifies great offenses.
ECC.10.PLAIN: If the ruler’s temper flares against you, do not abandon your post, for calmness lays great offenses to rest.

ECC.10.BSB: There is an evil I have seen under the sun— an error that proceeds from the ruler:
ECC.10.KJV: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, as an error which proceeds from the ruler:
ECC.10.PLAIN: There is an evil I have seen under the sun— an error that proceeds from the ruler:

ECC.10.BSB: Folly is appointed to great heights, but the rich sit in lowly positions.
ECC.10.KJV: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.
ECC.10.PLAIN: Folly is appointed to great heights, but the rich sit in lowly positions.

ECC.10.BSB: I have seen slaves on horseback, while princes go on foot like slaves.
ECC.10.KJV: I have seen servants on horses, and princes walking as servants on the earth.
ECC.10.PLAIN: I have seen slaves on horseback, while princes go on foot like slaves.

ECC.10.BSB: He who digs a pit may fall into it, and he who breaches a wall may be bitten by a snake.
ECC.10.KJV: He that digs a pit shall fall into it; and whoever breaks an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
ECC.10.PLAIN: He who digs a pit may fall into it, and he who breaches a wall may be bitten by a snake.

ECC.10.BSB: The one who quarries stones may be injured by them, and he who splits logs endangers himself.
ECC.10.KJV: Whoever removes stones shall be hurt therewith; and he that splits wood shall be endangered thereby.
ECC.10.PLAIN: The one who quarries stones may be injured by them, and he who splits logs endangers himself.

ECC.10.BSB: If the axe is dull and the blade unsharpened, more strength must be exerted, but skill produces success.
ECC.10.KJV: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.
ECC.10.PLAIN: If the axe is dull and the blade unsharpened, more strength must be exerted, but skill produces success.

ECC.10.BSB: If the snake bites before it is charmed, there is no profit for the charmer.
ECC.10.KJV: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better.
ECC.10.PLAIN: If the snake bites before it is charmed, there is no profit for the charmer.

ECC.10.BSB: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious, but the lips of a fool consume him.
ECC.10.KJV: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
ECC.10.PLAIN: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious, but the lips of a fool consume him.

ECC.10.BSB: The beginning of his talk is folly, and the end of his speech is evil madness.
ECC.10.KJV: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness: and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
ECC.10.PLAIN: The beginning of his talk is folly, and the end of his speech is evil madness.

ECC.10.BSB: Yet the fool multiplies words. No one knows what is coming, and who can tell him what will come after him?
ECC.10.KJV: A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?
ECC.10.PLAIN: Yet the fool multiplies words. No one knows what is coming, and who can tell him what will come after him?

ECC.10.BSB: The toil of a fool wearies him, for he does not know the way to the city.
ECC.10.KJV: The labor of the foolish wearies every one of them, because he knows not how to go to the city. ¶
ECC.10.PLAIN: The toil of a fool wearies him, for he does not know the way to the city.

ECC.10.BSB: Woe to you, O land whose king is a youth, and whose princes feast in the morning.
ECC.10.KJV: Woe to you, O land, when your king is a child, and your princes eat in the morning!
ECC.10.PLAIN: Woe to you, O land whose king is a youth, and whose princes feast in the morning.

ECC.10.BSB: Blessed are you, O land whose king is a son of nobles, and whose princes feast at the proper time— for strength and not for drunkenness.
ECC.10.KJV: Blessed are you, O land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness! ¶
ECC.10.PLAIN: Held in quiet grace are you, O land whose king is a son of nobles, and whose princes feast at the proper time— for strength and not for drunkenness.

ECC.10.BSB: Through laziness the roof caves in, and in the hands of the idle, the house leaks.
ECC.10.KJV: By much slothfulness the building decays; and through idleness of the hands the house drops through. ¶
ECC.10.PLAIN: Through laziness the roof caves in, and in the hands of the idle, the house leaks.

ECC.10.BSB: A feast is prepared for laughter, and wine makes life merry, but money is the answer for everything.
ECC.10.KJV: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes merry: but money answers all things. ¶
ECC.10.PLAIN: A feast is prepared for laughter, and wine makes life merry, but money is the answer for everything.

ECC.10.BSB: Do not curse the king even in your thoughts, or curse the rich even in your bedroom, for a bird of the air may carry your words, and a winged creature may report your speech.
ECC.10.KJV: Curse not the king, no not in your thought; and curse not the rich in your bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which has wings shall tell the matter.
ECC.10.PLAIN: Do not curse the king even in your thoughts, or curse the rich even in your bedroom, for a bird of the air may carry your words, and a winged creature may report your speech.

ECC.11.BSB: Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.
ECC.11.KJV: Cast your bread on the waters: for you shall find it after many days.
ECC.11.PLAIN: Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.

ECC.11.BSB: Divide your portion among seven, or even eight, for you do not know what disaster may befall the land.
ECC.11.KJV: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for you know not what evil shall be on the earth.
ECC.11.PLAIN: Divide your portion among seven, or even eight, for you do not know what disaster may befall the land.

ECC.11.BSB: If the clouds are full, they will pour out rain upon the earth; whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where it falls, there it will lie.
ECC.11.KJV: If the clouds be full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth: and if the tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it shall be.
ECC.11.PLAIN: If the clouds are full, they will pour out rain upon the earth; whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where it falls, there it will lie.

ECC.11.BSB: He who watches the wind will fail to sow, and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap.
ECC.11.KJV: He that observes the wind shall not sow; and he that regards the clouds shall not reap.
ECC.11.PLAIN: He who watches the wind will fail to sow, and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap.

ECC.11.BSB: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.
ECC.11.KJV: As you know not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so you know not the works of God who makes all.
ECC.11.PLAIN: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.

ECC.11.BSB: Sow your seed in the morning, and do not rest your hands in the evening, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper.
ECC.11.KJV: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening withhold not your hand: for you know not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good. ¶
ECC.11.PLAIN: Sow your seed in the morning, and do not rest your hands in the evening, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper.

ECC.11.BSB: Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.
ECC.11.KJV: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun:
ECC.11.PLAIN: Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.

ECC.11.BSB: So if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all. But let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. Everything to come is futile.
ECC.11.KJV: But if a man live many years, and rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that comes is vanity. ¶
ECC.11.PLAIN: So if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all. But let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. Everything to come is futile.

ECC.11.BSB: Rejoice, O young man, while you are young, and let your heart be glad in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes, but know that for all these things God will bring you to judgment.
ECC.11.KJV: Rejoice, O young man, in your youth; and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth, and walk in the ways of your heart, and in the sight of your eyes: but know you, that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
ECC.11.PLAIN: Rejoice, O young man, while you are young, and let your heart be glad in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes, but know that for all these things God will bring you to judgment.

ECC.11.BSB: So banish sorrow from your heart, and cast off pain from your body, for youth and vigor are fleeting.
ECC.11.KJV: Therefore remove sorrow from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh: for childhood and youth are vanity.
ECC.11.PLAIN: So banish sorrow from your heart, and cast off pain from your body, for youth and vigor are fleeting.

ECC.12.BSB: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of adversity come and the years approach of which you will say, “I find no pleasure in them,”
ECC.12.KJV: Remember now your Creator in the days of your youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw near, when you shall say, I have no pleasure in them;
ECC.12.PLAIN: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of adversity come and the years approach of which you will say, “I find no pleasure in them,”

ECC.12.BSB: before the light of the sun, moon, and stars is darkened, and the clouds return after the rain,
ECC.12.KJV: While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain:
ECC.12.PLAIN: before the light of the sun, moon, and stars is darkened, and the clouds return after the rain,

ECC.12.BSB: on the day the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men stoop, when those grinding cease because they are few and those watching through windows see dimly,
ECC.12.KJV: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened,
ECC.12.PLAIN: on the day the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men stoop, when those grinding cease because they are few and those watching through windows see dimly,

ECC.12.BSB: when the doors to the street are shut and the sound of the mill fades away, when one rises at the sound of a bird and all the daughters of song grow faint,
ECC.12.KJV: And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of music shall be brought low;
ECC.12.PLAIN: when the doors to the street are shut and the sound of the mill fades away, when one rises at the sound of a bird and all the daughters of song grow faint,

ECC.12.BSB: when men fear the heights and dangers of the road, when the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper loses its spring, and the caper berry shrivels— for then man goes to his eternal home and mourners walk the streets.
ECC.12.KJV: Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goes to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:
ECC.12.PLAIN: when men fear the heights and dangers of the road, when the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper loses its spring, and the caper berry shrivels— for then man goes to his eternal home and mourners walk the streets.

ECC.12.BSB: Remember Him before the silver cord is snapped and the golden bowl is crushed, before the pitcher is shattered at the spring and the wheel is broken at the well,
ECC.12.KJV: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.
ECC.12.PLAIN: Remember Him before the silver cord is snapped and the golden bowl is crushed, before the pitcher is shattered at the spring and the wheel is broken at the well,

ECC.12.BSB: before the dust returns to the ground from which it came and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
ECC.12.KJV: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return to God who gave it. ¶
ECC.12.PLAIN: before the dust returns to the ground from which it came and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

ECC.12.BSB: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher. “Everything is futile!”
ECC.12.KJV: Vanity of vanities, says the preacher; all is vanity.
ECC.12.PLAIN: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher. “Everything is futile!”

ECC.12.BSB: Not only was the Teacher wise, but he also taught the people knowledge; he pondered, searched out, and arranged many proverbs.
ECC.12.KJV: And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yes, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
ECC.12.PLAIN: Not only was the Teacher wise, but he also taught the people knowledge; he pondered, searched out, and arranged many proverbs.

ECC.12.BSB: The Teacher searched to find delightful sayings and to record accurate words of truth.
ECC.12.KJV: The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright, even words of truth.
ECC.12.PLAIN: The Teacher searched to find delightful sayings and to record accurate words of truth.

ECC.12.BSB: The words of the wise are like goads, and the anthologies of the masters are like firmly embedded nails driven by a single Shepherd.
ECC.12.KJV: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
ECC.12.PLAIN: The words of the wise are like goads, and the anthologies of the masters are like firmly embedded nails driven by a single Shepherd.

ECC.12.BSB: And by these, my son, be further warned: There is no end to the making of many books, and much study wearies the body.
ECC.12.KJV: And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh. ¶
ECC.12.PLAIN: And by these, my son, be further warned: There is no end to the making of many books, and much study wearies the body.

ECC.12.BSB: When all has been heard, the conclusion of the matter is this: Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the whole duty of man.
ECC.12.KJV: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
ECC.12.PLAIN: Here is the conclusion of the matter: Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole duty of humankind.

ECC.12.BSB: For God will bring every deed into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.
ECC.12.KJV: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.
ECC.12.PLAIN: For God will bring every deed into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.

SNG.1.BSB: This is Solomon’s Song of Songs.
SNG.1.KJV: The song of songs, which is Solomon’s.
SNG.1.PLAIN: This is Solomon’s Song of Songs.

SNG.1.BSB: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! For your love is more delightful than wine.
SNG.1.KJV: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for your love is better than wine.
SNG.1.PLAIN: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! For your love is more delightful than wine.

SNG.1.BSB: The fragrance of your perfume is pleasing; your name is like perfume poured out. No wonder the maidens adore you.
SNG.1.KJV: Because of the smell of your good ointments your name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love you.
SNG.1.PLAIN: The fragrance of your perfume is pleasing; your name is like perfume poured out. No wonder the maidens adore you.

SNG.1.BSB: Take me away with you—let us hurry! May the king bring me to his chambers. We will rejoice and delight in you; we will praise your love more than wine. It is only right that they adore you.
SNG.1.KJV: Draw me, we will run after you: the king has brought me into his chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in you, we will remember your love more than wine: the upright love you.
SNG.1.PLAIN: Take me away with you—let us hurry! May the king bring me to his chambers. We will rejoice and delight in you; we will praise your love more than wine. It is only right that they adore you.

SNG.1.BSB: I am dark, yet lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.
SNG.1.KJV: I am black, but comely, O you daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.
SNG.1.PLAIN: I am dark, yet lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.

SNG.1.BSB: Do not stare because I am dark, for the sun has gazed upon me. My mother’s sons were angry with me; they made me a keeper of the vineyards, but my own vineyard I have neglected.
SNG.1.KJV: Look not on me, because I am black, because the sun has looked on me: my mother’s children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; but my own vineyard have I not kept.
SNG.1.PLAIN: Do not stare because I am dark, for the sun has gazed upon me. My mother’s sons were angry with me; they made me a keeper of the vineyards, but my own vineyard I have neglected.

SNG.1.BSB: Tell me, O one I love, where do you pasture your sheep? Where do you rest them at midday? Why should I be like a veiled woman beside the flocks of your companions?
SNG.1.KJV: Tell me, O you whom my soul loves, where you feed, where you make your flock to rest at noon: for why should I be as one that turns aside by the flocks of your companions? ¶
SNG.1.PLAIN: Tell me, O one I love, where do you pasture your sheep? Where do you rest them at midday? Why should I be like a veiled woman beside the flocks of your companions?

SNG.1.BSB: If you do not know, O fairest of women, follow the tracks of the flock, and graze your young goats near the tents of the shepherds.
SNG.1.KJV: If you know not, O you fairest among women, go your way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed your kids beside the shepherds’ tents.
SNG.1.PLAIN: If you do not know, O fairest of women, follow the tracks of the flock, and graze your young goats near the tents of the shepherds.

SNG.1.BSB: I compare you, my darling, to a mare among Pharaoh’s chariots.
SNG.1.KJV: I have compared you, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh’s chariots.
SNG.1.PLAIN: I compare you, my darling, to a mare among Pharaoh’s chariots.

SNG.1.BSB: Your cheeks are beautiful with ornaments, your neck with strings of jewels.
SNG.1.KJV: Your cheeks are comely with rows of jewels, your neck with chains of gold.
SNG.1.PLAIN: Your cheeks are beautiful with ornaments, your neck with strings of jewels.

SNG.1.BSB: We will make you ornaments of gold, studded with beads of silver.
SNG.1.KJV: We will make you borders of gold with studs of silver. ¶
SNG.1.PLAIN: We will make you ornaments of gold, studded with beads of silver.

SNG.1.BSB: While the king was at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.
SNG.1.KJV: While the king sits at his table, my spikenard sends forth the smell thereof.
SNG.1.PLAIN: While the king was at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.

SNG.1.BSB: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh resting between my breasts.
SNG.1.KJV: A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved to me; he shall lie all night between my breasts.
SNG.1.PLAIN: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh resting between my breasts.

SNG.1.BSB: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En-gedi.
SNG.1.KJV: My beloved is to me as a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of Engedi.
SNG.1.PLAIN: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En-gedi.

SNG.1.BSB: How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves.
SNG.1.KJV: Behold, you are fair, my love; behold, you are fair; you have doves’ eyes.
SNG.1.PLAIN: How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves.

SNG.1.BSB: How handsome you are, my beloved! Oh, how delightful! The soft grass is our bed.
SNG.1.KJV: Behold, you are fair, my beloved, yes, pleasant: also our bed is green.
SNG.1.PLAIN: How handsome you are, my beloved! Oh, how delightful! The soft grass is our bed.

SNG.1.BSB: The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are fragrant firs.
SNG.1.KJV: The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir.
SNG.1.PLAIN: The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are fragrant firs.

SNG.2.BSB: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valley.
SNG.2.KJV: I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys.
SNG.2.PLAIN: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valley.

SNG.2.BSB: Like a lily among the thorns is my darling among the maidens.
SNG.2.KJV: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
SNG.2.PLAIN: Like a lily among the thorns is my darling among the maidens.

SNG.2.BSB: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest is my beloved among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.
SNG.2.KJV: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
SNG.2.PLAIN: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest is my beloved among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.

SNG.2.BSB: He has brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me is love.
SNG.2.KJV: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.
SNG.2.PLAIN: He has taken me to the banquet hall, and his banner over me is love.

SNG.2.BSB: Sustain me with raisins; refresh me with apples, for I am faint with love.
SNG.2.KJV: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I am sick of love.
SNG.2.PLAIN: Sustain me with raisins; refresh me with apples, for I am faint with love.

SNG.2.BSB: His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.
SNG.2.KJV: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand does embrace me.
SNG.2.PLAIN: His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.

SNG.2.BSB: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.
SNG.2.KJV: I charge you, O you daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that you stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please. ¶
SNG.2.PLAIN: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.

SNG.2.BSB: Listen! My beloved approaches. Look! Here he comes, leaping across the mountains, bounding over the hills.
SNG.2.KJV: The voice of my beloved! behold, he comes leaping on the mountains, skipping on the hills.
SNG.2.PLAIN: Listen! My beloved approaches. Look! Here he comes, leaping across the mountains, bounding over the hills.

SNG.2.BSB: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look, he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice.
SNG.2.KJV: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: behold, he stands behind our wall, he looks forth at the windows, showing himself through the lattice.
SNG.2.PLAIN: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look, he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice.

SNG.2.BSB: My beloved calls to me, “Arise, my darling. Come away with me, my beautiful one.
SNG.2.KJV: My beloved spoke, and said to me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
SNG.2.PLAIN: My beloved calls to me, “Arise, my darling. Come away with me, my beautiful one.

SNG.2.BSB: For now the winter is past; the rain is over and gone.
SNG.2.KJV: For, see, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone;
SNG.2.PLAIN: For now the winter is past; the rain is over and gone.

SNG.2.BSB: The flowers have appeared in the countryside; the season of singing has come, and the cooing of turtledoves is heard in our land.
SNG.2.KJV: The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;
SNG.2.PLAIN: The flowers have appeared in the countryside; the season of singing has come, and the cooing of turtledoves is heard in our land.

SNG.2.BSB: The fig tree ripens its figs; the blossoming vines spread their fragrance. Arise, come away, my darling; come away with me, my beautiful one.”
SNG.2.KJV: The fig tree puts forth her green figs, and the vines with the tender grape give a good smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away. ¶
SNG.2.PLAIN: The fig tree ripens its figs; the blossoming vines spread their fragrance. Arise, come away, my darling; come away with me, my beautiful one.”

SNG.2.BSB: O my dove in the clefts of the rock, in the crevices of the cliff, let me see your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your countenance is lovely.
SNG.2.KJV: O my dove, that are in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the stairs, let me see your countenance, let me hear your voice; for sweet is your voice, and your countenance is comely.
SNG.2.PLAIN: O my dove in the clefts of the rock, in the crevices of the cliff, let me see your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your countenance is lovely.

SNG.2.BSB: Catch for us the foxes— the little foxes that ruin the vineyards— for our vineyards are in bloom.
SNG.2.KJV: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes. ¶
SNG.2.PLAIN: Catch for us the foxes— the little foxes that ruin the vineyards— for our vineyards are in bloom.

SNG.2.BSB: My beloved is mine and I am his; he pastures his flock among the lilies.
SNG.2.KJV: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feeds among the lilies.
SNG.2.PLAIN: My beloved is mine and I am his; he pastures his flock among the lilies.

SNG.2.BSB: Before the day breaks and shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of Bether.
SNG.2.KJV: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be you like a roe or a young hart on the mountains of Bether.
SNG.2.PLAIN: Before the day breaks and shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of Bether.

SNG.3.BSB: On my bed at night I sought the one I love; I sought him, but did not find him.
SNG.3.KJV: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but I found him not.
SNG.3.PLAIN: On my bed at night I sought the one I love; I sought him, but did not find him.

SNG.3.BSB: I will arise now and go about the city, through the streets and squares. I will seek the one I love. So I sought him but did not find him.
SNG.3.KJV: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but I found him not.
SNG.3.PLAIN: I will arise now and go about the city, through the streets and squares. I will seek the one I love. So I sought him but did not find him.

SNG.3.BSB: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city: “Have you seen the one I love?”
SNG.3.KJV: The watchmen that go about the city found me: to whom I said, Saw you him whom my soul loves?
SNG.3.PLAIN: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city: “Have you seen the one I love?”

SNG.3.BSB: I had just passed them when I found the one I love. I held him and would not let go until I had brought him to my mother’s house, to the chamber of the one who conceived me.
SNG.3.KJV: It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loves: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.
SNG.3.PLAIN: I had just passed them when I found the one I love. I held him and would not let go until I had brought him to my mother’s house, to the chamber of the one who conceived me.

SNG.3.BSB: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.
SNG.3.KJV: I charge you, O you daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that you stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please. ¶
SNG.3.PLAIN: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.

SNG.3.BSB: Who is this coming up from the wilderness like a column of smoke, scented with myrrh and frankincense from all the spices of the merchant?
SNG.3.KJV: Who is this that comes out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?
SNG.3.PLAIN: Who is this coming up from the wilderness like a column of smoke, scented with myrrh and frankincense from all the spices of the merchant?

SNG.3.BSB: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage, escorted by sixty of the mightiest men of Israel.
SNG.3.KJV: Behold his bed, which is Solomon’s; three score valiant men are about it, of the valiant of Israel.
SNG.3.PLAIN: Look closely — it is Solomon’s carriage, escorted by sixty of the mightiest men of Israel.

SNG.3.BSB: All are skilled with the sword, experienced in warfare. Each has his sword at his side prepared for the terror of the night.
SNG.3.KJV: They all hold swords, being expert in war: every man has his sword on his thigh because of fear in the night.
SNG.3.PLAIN: All are skilled with the sword, experienced in warfare. Each has his sword at his side prepared for the terror of the night.

SNG.3.BSB: King Solomon has made his carriage out of the timber of Lebanon.
SNG.3.KJV: King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.
SNG.3.PLAIN: King Solomon has made his carriage out of the timber of Lebanon.

SNG.3.BSB: He has made its posts of silver, its base of gold, its seat of purple fabric. Its interior is inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.
SNG.3.KJV: He made the pillars thereof of silver, the bottom thereof of gold, the covering of it of purple, the middle thereof being paved with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.
SNG.3.PLAIN: He has made its posts of silver, its base of gold, its seat of purple fabric. Its interior is inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.

SNG.3.BSB: Come out, O daughters of Zion, and gaze at King Solomon, wearing the crown his mother bestowed on the day of his wedding— the day of his heart’s rejoicing.
SNG.3.KJV: Go forth, O you daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown with which his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.
SNG.3.PLAIN: Come out, O daughters of Zion, and gaze at King Solomon, wearing the crown his mother bestowed on the day of his wedding— the day of his heart’s rejoicing.

SNG.4.BSB: How beautiful you are, my darling— how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down Mount Gilead.
SNG.4.KJV: Behold, you are fair, my love; behold, you are fair; you have doves’ eyes within your locks: your hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.
SNG.4.PLAIN: How beautiful you are, my darling— how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down Mount Gilead.

SNG.4.BSB: Your teeth are like a flock of newly shorn sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.
SNG.4.KJV: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep that are even shorn, which came up from the washing; whereof every one bear twins, and none is barren among them.
SNG.4.PLAIN: Your teeth are like a flock of newly shorn sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.

SNG.4.BSB: Your lips are like a scarlet ribbon, and your mouth is lovely. Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.
