SNG.4.KJV: Your lips are like a thread of scarlet, and your speech is comely: your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate within your locks.
SNG.4.PLAIN: Your lips are like a scarlet ribbon, and your mouth is lovely. Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.

SNG.4.BSB: Your neck is like the tower of David, built with rows of stones; on it hang a thousand shields, all of them shields of warriors.
SNG.4.KJV: Your neck is like the tower of David built for an armory, where on there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.
SNG.4.PLAIN: Your neck is like the tower of David, built with rows of stones; on it hang a thousand shields, all of them shields of warriors.

SNG.4.BSB: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle grazing among the lilies.
SNG.4.KJV: Your two breasts are like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.
SNG.4.PLAIN: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle grazing among the lilies.

SNG.4.BSB: Before the day breaks and the shadows flee, I will make my way to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.
SNG.4.KJV: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.
SNG.4.PLAIN: Before the day breaks and the shadows flee, I will make my way to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.

SNG.4.BSB: You are altogether beautiful, my darling; in you there is no flaw.
SNG.4.KJV: You are all fair, my love; there is no spot in you. ¶
SNG.4.PLAIN: You are altogether beautiful, my darling; in you there is no flaw.

SNG.4.BSB: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon! Descend from the peak of Amana, from the summits of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards.
SNG.4.KJV: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
SNG.4.PLAIN: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon! Descend from the peak of Amana, from the summits of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards.

SNG.4.BSB: You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride; you have stolen my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your neck.
SNG.4.KJV: You have ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; you have ravished my heart with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck.
SNG.4.PLAIN: You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride; you have stolen my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your neck.

SNG.4.BSB: How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! Your love is much better than wine, and the fragrance of your perfume than all spices.
SNG.4.KJV: How fair is your love, my sister, my spouse! how much better is your love than wine! and the smell of your ointments than all spices!
SNG.4.PLAIN: How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! Your love is much better than wine, and the fragrance of your perfume than all spices.

SNG.4.BSB: Your lips, my bride, drip sweetness like the honeycomb; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the aroma of Lebanon.
SNG.4.KJV: Your lips, O my spouse, drop as the honeycomb: honey and milk are under your tongue; and the smell of your garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
SNG.4.PLAIN: Your lips, my bride, drip sweetness like the honeycomb; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the aroma of Lebanon.

SNG.4.BSB: My sister, my bride, you are a garden locked up, a spring enclosed, a fountain sealed.
SNG.4.KJV: A garden enclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.
SNG.4.PLAIN: My sister, my bride, you are a garden locked up, a spring enclosed, a fountain sealed.

SNG.4.BSB: Your branches are an orchard of pomegranates with the choicest of fruits, with henna and nard,
SNG.4.KJV: Your plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,
SNG.4.PLAIN: Your branches are an orchard of pomegranates with the choicest of fruits, with henna and nard,

SNG.4.BSB: with nard and saffron, with calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of frankincense tree, with myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices.
SNG.4.KJV: Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:
SNG.4.PLAIN: with nard and saffron, with calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of frankincense tree, with myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices.

SNG.4.BSB: You are a garden spring, a well of fresh water flowing down from Lebanon.
SNG.4.KJV: A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon. ¶
SNG.4.PLAIN: You are a garden spring, a well of fresh water flowing down from Lebanon.

SNG.4.BSB: Awake, O north wind, and come, O south wind. Breathe on my garden and spread the fragrance of its spices. Let my beloved come into his garden and taste its choicest fruits.
SNG.4.KJV: Awake, O north wind; and come, you south; blow on my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.
SNG.4.PLAIN: Awake, O north wind, and come, O south wind. Breathe on my garden and spread the fragrance of its spices. Let my beloved come into his garden and taste its choicest fruits.

SNG.5.BSB: I have come to my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends, and drink; drink freely, O beloved.
SNG.5.KJV: I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yes, drink abundantly, O beloved. ¶
SNG.5.PLAIN: I have come to my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends, and drink; drink freely, O beloved.

SNG.5.BSB: I sleep, but my heart is awake. A sound! My beloved is knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one. My head is drenched with dew, my hair with the dampness of the night.”
SNG.5.KJV: I sleep, but my heart wakes: it is the voice of my beloved that knocks, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.
SNG.5.PLAIN: I sleep, but my heart is awake. A sound! My beloved is knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one. My head is drenched with dew, my hair with the dampness of the night.”

SNG.5.BSB: I have taken off my robe— must I put it back on? I have washed my feet— must I soil them again?
SNG.5.KJV: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?
SNG.5.PLAIN: I have taken off my robe— must I put it back on? I have washed my feet— must I soil them again?

SNG.5.BSB: My beloved put his hand to the latch; my heart pounded for him.
SNG.5.KJV: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, and my bowels were moved for him.
SNG.5.PLAIN: My beloved put his hand to the latch; my heart pounded for him.

SNG.5.BSB: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh on the handles of the bolt.
SNG.5.KJV: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers with sweet smelling myrrh, on the handles of the lock.
SNG.5.PLAIN: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh on the handles of the bolt.

SNG.5.BSB: I opened for my beloved, but he had turned and gone. My heart sank at his departure. I sought him, but did not find him. I called, but he did not answer.
SNG.5.KJV: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: my soul failed when he spoke: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
SNG.5.PLAIN: I opened for my beloved, but he had turned and gone. My heart sank at his departure. I sought him, but did not find him. I called, but he did not answer.

SNG.5.BSB: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city. They beat me and bruised me; they took away my cloak, those guardians of the walls.
SNG.5.KJV: The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
SNG.5.PLAIN: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city. They beat me and bruised me; they took away my cloak, those guardians of the walls.

SNG.5.BSB: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you, if you find my beloved, tell him I am sick with love.
SNG.5.KJV: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, that you tell him, that I am sick of love. ¶
SNG.5.PLAIN: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you, if you find my beloved, tell him I am sick with love.

SNG.5.BSB: How is your beloved better than others, O most beautiful among women? How is your beloved better than another, that you charge us so?
SNG.5.KJV: What is your beloved more than another beloved, O you fairest among women? what is your beloved more than another beloved, that you do so charge us?
SNG.5.PLAIN: How is your beloved better than others, O most beautiful among women? How is your beloved better than another, that you charge us so?

SNG.5.BSB: My beloved is dazzling and ruddy, outstanding among ten thousand.
SNG.5.KJV: My beloved is white and ruddy, the most chief among ten thousand.
SNG.5.PLAIN: My beloved is dazzling and ruddy, outstanding among ten thousand.

SNG.5.BSB: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy and black as a raven.
SNG.5.KJV: His head is as the most fine gold, his locks are bushy, and black as a raven.
SNG.5.PLAIN: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy and black as a raven.

SNG.5.BSB: His eyes are like doves beside the streams of water, bathed in milk and mounted like jewels.
SNG.5.KJV: His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk, and fitly set.
SNG.5.PLAIN: His eyes are like doves beside the streams of water, bathed in milk and mounted like jewels.

SNG.5.BSB: His cheeks are like beds of spice, towers of perfume. His lips are like lilies, dripping with flowing myrrh.
SNG.5.KJV: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers: his lips like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.
SNG.5.PLAIN: His cheeks are like beds of spice, towers of perfume. His lips are like lilies, dripping with flowing myrrh.

SNG.5.BSB: His arms are rods of gold set with beryl. His body is an ivory panel bedecked with sapphires.
SNG.5.KJV: His hands are as gold rings set with the beryl: his belly is as bright ivory overlaid with sapphires.
SNG.5.PLAIN: His arms are rods of gold set with beryl. His body is an ivory panel bedecked with sapphires.

SNG.5.BSB: His legs are pillars of marble set on bases of pure gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, as majestic as the cedars.
SNG.5.KJV: His legs are as pillars of marble, set on sockets of fine gold: his countenance is as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
SNG.5.PLAIN: His legs are pillars of marble set on bases of pure gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, as majestic as the cedars.

SNG.5.BSB: His mouth is most sweet; he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
SNG.5.KJV: His mouth is most sweet: yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
SNG.5.PLAIN: His mouth is most sweet; he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

SNG.6.BSB: Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful among women? Which way has he turned? We will seek him with you.
SNG.6.KJV: Where is your beloved gone, O you fairest among women? where is your beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with you.
SNG.6.PLAIN: Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful among women? Which way has he turned? We will seek him with you.

SNG.6.BSB: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens and to gather lilies.
SNG.6.KJV: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
SNG.6.PLAIN: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens and to gather lilies.

SNG.6.BSB: I belong to my beloved and he belongs to me; he pastures his flock among the lilies.
SNG.6.KJV: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine: he feeds among the lilies. ¶
SNG.6.PLAIN: I belong to my beloved and he belongs to me; he pastures his flock among the lilies.

SNG.6.BSB: You are as beautiful, my darling, as Tirzah, as lovely as Jerusalem, as majestic as troops with banners.
SNG.6.KJV: You are beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army with banners.
SNG.6.PLAIN: You are as beautiful, my darling, as Tirzah, as lovely as Jerusalem, as majestic as troops with banners.

SNG.6.BSB: Turn your eyes away from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down from Gilead.
SNG.6.KJV: Turn away your eyes from me, for they have overcome me: your hair is as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.
SNG.6.PLAIN: Turn your eyes away from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down from Gilead.

SNG.6.BSB: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.
SNG.6.KJV: Your teeth are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, whereof every one bears twins, and there is not one barren among them.
SNG.6.PLAIN: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.

SNG.6.BSB: Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.
SNG.6.KJV: As a piece of a pomegranate are your temples within your locks.
SNG.6.PLAIN: Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.

SNG.6.BSB: There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and maidens without number,
SNG.6.KJV: There are three score queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number.
SNG.6.PLAIN: There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and maidens without number,

SNG.6.BSB: but my dove, my perfect one, is unique, the favorite of the mother who bore her. The maidens see her and call her blessed; the queens and concubines sing her praises.
SNG.6.KJV: My dove, my undefiled is but one; she is the only one of her mother, she is the choice one of her that bore her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her; yes, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her. ¶
SNG.6.PLAIN: but my dove, my perfect one, is unique, the favorite of the mother who bore her. The maidens see her and call her blessed; the queens and concubines sing her praises.

SNG.6.BSB: Who is this who shines like the dawn, as fair as the moon, as bright as the sun, as majestic as the stars in procession?
SNG.6.KJV: Who is she that looks forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?
SNG.6.PLAIN: Who is this who shines like the dawn, as fair as the moon, as bright as the sun, as majestic as the stars in procession?

SNG.6.BSB: I went down to the walnut grove to see the blossoms of the valley, to see if the vines were budding or the pomegranates were in bloom.
SNG.6.KJV: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, and to see whether the vine flourished and the pomegranates budded.
SNG.6.PLAIN: I went down to the walnut grove to see the blossoms of the valley, to see if the vines were budding or the pomegranates were in bloom.

SNG.6.BSB: Before I realized it, my desire had set me among the royal chariots of my people.
SNG.6.KJV: Or ever I was aware, my soul made me like the chariots of Amminadib.
SNG.6.PLAIN: Before I realized it, my desire had set me among the royal chariots of my people.

SNG.6.BSB: Come back, come back, O Shulammite! Come back, come back, that we may gaze upon you. Why do you look at the Shulammite, as on the dance of Mahanaim?
SNG.6.KJV: Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look on you. What will you see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.
SNG.6.PLAIN: Come back, come back, O Shulammite! Come back, come back, that we may gaze upon you. Why do you look at the Shulammite, as on the dance of Mahanaim?

SNG.7.BSB: How beautiful are your sandaled feet, O daughter of the prince! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the handiwork of a master.
SNG.7.KJV: How beautiful are your feet with shoes, O prince’s daughter! the joints of your thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.
SNG.7.PLAIN: How beautiful are your sandaled feet, O daughter of the prince! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the handiwork of a master.

SNG.7.BSB: Your navel is a rounded goblet; it never lacks blended wine. Your waist is a mound of wheat encircled by the lilies.
SNG.7.KJV: Your navel is like a round goblet, which wants not liquor: your belly is like an heap of wheat set about with lilies.
SNG.7.PLAIN: Your navel is a rounded goblet; it never lacks blended wine. Your waist is a mound of wheat encircled by the lilies.

SNG.7.BSB: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
SNG.7.KJV: Your two breasts are like two young roes that are twins.
SNG.7.PLAIN: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.

SNG.7.BSB: Your neck is like a tower made of ivory; your eyes are like the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bath-rabbim; your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, facing toward Damascus.
SNG.7.KJV: Your neck is as a tower of ivory; your eyes like the fish pools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bathrabbim: your nose is as the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.
SNG.7.PLAIN: Your neck is like a tower made of ivory; your eyes are like the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bath-rabbim; your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, facing toward Damascus.

SNG.7.BSB: Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel, the hair of your head like purple threads; the king is captured in your tresses.
SNG.7.KJV: Your head on you is like Carmel, and the hair of your head like purple; the king is held in the galleries.
SNG.7.PLAIN: Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel, the hair of your head like purple threads; the king is captured in your tresses.

SNG.7.BSB: How fair and pleasant you are, O love, with your delights!
SNG.7.KJV: How fair and how pleasant are you, O love, for delights!
SNG.7.PLAIN: How fair and pleasant you are, O love, with your delights!

SNG.7.BSB: Your stature is like a palm tree; your breasts are clusters of fruit.
SNG.7.KJV: This your stature is like to a palm tree, and your breasts to clusters of grapes.
SNG.7.PLAIN: Your stature is like a palm tree; your breasts are clusters of fruit.

SNG.7.BSB: I said, “I will climb the palm tree; I will take hold of its fruit.” May your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the fragrance of your breath like apples,
SNG.7.KJV: I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof: now also your breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the smell of your nose like apples;
SNG.7.PLAIN: I said, “I will climb the palm tree; I will take hold of its fruit.” May your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the fragrance of your breath like apples,

SNG.7.BSB: and your mouth like the finest wine. May it flow smoothly to my beloved, gliding gently over lips and teeth.
SNG.7.KJV: And the roof of your mouth like the best wine for my beloved, that goes down sweetly, causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak. ¶
SNG.7.PLAIN: and your mouth like the finest wine. May it flow smoothly to my beloved, gliding gently over lips and teeth.

SNG.7.BSB: I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me.
SNG.7.KJV: I am my beloved’s, and his desire is toward me.
SNG.7.PLAIN: I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me.

SNG.7.BSB: Come, my beloved, let us go to the countryside; let us spend the night among the wildflowers.
SNG.7.KJV: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages.
SNG.7.PLAIN: Come, my beloved, let us go to the countryside; let us spend the night among the wildflowers.

SNG.7.BSB: Let us go early to the vineyards to see if the vine has budded, if the blossom has opened, if the pomegranates are in bloom— there I will give you my love.
SNG.7.KJV: Let us get up early to the vineyards; let us see if the vine flourish, whether the tender grape appear, and the pomegranates bud forth: there will I give you my loves.
SNG.7.PLAIN: Let us go early to the vineyards to see if the vine has budded, if the blossom has opened, if the pomegranates are in bloom— there I will give you my love.

SNG.7.BSB: The mandrakes send forth a fragrance, and at our door is every delicacy, new as well as old, that I have treasured up for you, my beloved.
SNG.7.KJV: The mandrakes give a smell, and at our gates are all manner of pleasant fruits, new and old, which I have laid up for you, O my beloved.
SNG.7.PLAIN: The mandrakes send forth a fragrance, and at our door is every delicacy, new as well as old, that I have treasured up for you, my beloved.

SNG.8.BSB: O that you were to me like a brother who nursed at my mother’s breasts! If I found you outdoors, I would kiss you, and no one would despise me.
SNG.8.KJV: O that you were as my brother, that sucked the breasts of my mother! when I should find you without, I would kiss you; yes, I should not be despised.
SNG.8.PLAIN: O that you were to me like a brother who nursed at my mother’s breasts! If I found you outdoors, I would kiss you, and no one would despise me.

SNG.8.BSB: I would lead you and bring you to the house of my mother who taught me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the nectar of my pomegranates.
SNG.8.KJV: I would lead you, and bring you into my mother’s house, who would instruct me: I would cause you to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate.
SNG.8.PLAIN: I would lead you and bring you to the house of my mother who taught me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the nectar of my pomegranates.

SNG.8.BSB: His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.
SNG.8.KJV: His left hand should be under my head, and his right hand should embrace me.
SNG.8.PLAIN: His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.

SNG.8.BSB: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.
SNG.8.KJV: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that you stir not up, nor awake my love, until he please.
SNG.8.PLAIN: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.

SNG.8.BSB: Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? I roused you under the apple tree; there your mother conceived you; there she travailed and brought you forth.
SNG.8.KJV: Who is this that comes up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? I raised you up under the apple tree: there your mother brought you forth: there she brought you forth that bore you. ¶
SNG.8.PLAIN: Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? I roused you under the apple tree; there your mother conceived you; there she travailed and brought you forth.

SNG.8.BSB: Set me as a seal over your heart, as a seal upon your arm. For love is as strong as death, its jealousy as unrelenting as Sheol. Its sparks are fiery flames, the fiercest blaze of all.
SNG.8.KJV: Set me as a seal on your heart, as a seal on your arm: for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave: the coals thereof are coals of fire, which has a most vehement flame.
SNG.8.PLAIN: Set me as a seal over your heart, as a seal upon your arm. For love is as strong as death, its jealousy as unrelenting as Sheol. Its sparks are fiery flames, the fiercest blaze of all.

SNG.8.BSB: Mighty waters cannot quench love; rivers cannot sweep it away. If a man were to give all the wealth of his house for love, his offer would be utterly scorned.
SNG.8.KJV: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be scorned. ¶
SNG.8.PLAIN: Many waters cannot quench love; rivers cannot sweep it away. If one were to give all the wealth of their house for love, it would be utterly scorned.

SNG.8.BSB: We have a little sister, and her breasts are not yet grown. What shall we do for our sister on the day she is spoken for?
SNG.8.KJV: We have a little sister, and she has no breasts: what shall we do for our sister in the day when she shall be spoken for?
SNG.8.PLAIN: We have a little sister, and her breasts are not yet grown. What shall we do for our sister on the day she is spoken for?

SNG.8.BSB: If she is a wall, we will build a tower of silver upon her. If she is a door, we will enclose her with panels of cedar.
SNG.8.KJV: If she be a wall, we will build on her a palace of silver: and if she be a door, we will enclose her with boards of cedar.
SNG.8.PLAIN: If she is a wall, we will build a tower of silver upon her. If she is a door, we will enclose her with panels of cedar.

SNG.8.BSB: I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. So I have become in his eyes like one who brings peace.
SNG.8.KJV: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers: then was I in his eyes as one that found favor.
SNG.8.PLAIN: I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. So I have become in his eyes like one who brings peace.

SNG.8.BSB: Solomon had a vineyard in Baal-hamon. He leased it to the tenants. For its fruit, each was to bring a thousand shekels of silver.
SNG.8.KJV: Solomon had a vineyard at Baalhamon; he let out the vineyard to keepers; every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand pieces of silver.
SNG.8.PLAIN: Solomon had a vineyard in Baal-hamon. He leased it to the tenants. For its fruit, each was to bring a thousand shekels of silver.

SNG.8.BSB: But my own vineyard is mine to give; the thousand shekels are for you, O Solomon, and two hundred are for those who tend its fruit.
SNG.8.KJV: My vineyard, which is mine, is before me: you, O Solomon, must have a thousand, and those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred.
SNG.8.PLAIN: But my own vineyard is mine to give; the thousand shekels are for you, O Solomon, and two hundred are for those who tend its fruit.

SNG.8.BSB: You who dwell in the gardens, my companions are listening for your voice. Let me hear it!
SNG.8.KJV: You that dwell in the gardens, the companions listen to your voice: cause me to hear it. ¶
SNG.8.PLAIN: You who dwell in the gardens, my companions are listening for your voice. Let me hear it!

SNG.8.BSB: Come away, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices.
SNG.8.KJV: Make haste, my beloved, and be you like to a roe or to a young hart on the mountains of spices.
SNG.8.PLAIN: Come away, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices.

ISA.1.BSB: This is the vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem that Isaiah son of Amoz saw during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
ISA.1.KJV: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
ISA.1.PLAIN: This is the vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem that Isaiah son of Amoz saw during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

ISA.1.BSB: Listen, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, for the LORD has spoken: “I have raised children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against Me.
ISA.1.KJV: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth: for the LORD has spoken, I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me.
ISA.1.PLAIN: Listen, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord has spoken: “I have raised children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against Me.

ISA.1.BSB: The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master’s manger, but Israel does not know; My people do not understand.”
ISA.1.KJV: The ox knows his owner, and the ass his master’s crib: but Israel does not know, my people does not consider.
ISA.1.PLAIN: The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master’s manger, but Israel does not know; My people do not understand.”

ISA.1.BSB: Alas, O sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a brood of evildoers, children of depravity! They have forsaken the LORD; they have despised the Holy One of Israel and turned their backs on Him.
ISA.1.KJV: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the LORD, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger, they are gone away backward. ¶
ISA.1.PLAIN: Alas, O sinful nation, a people laden with brokenness, a brood of evildoers, children of depravity! They have forsaken the Lord; they have despised the Holy One of Israel and turned their backs on Him.

ISA.1.BSB: Why do you want more beatings? Why do you keep rebelling? Your head has a massive wound, and your whole heart is afflicted.
ISA.1.KJV: Why should you be stricken any more? you will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.
ISA.1.PLAIN: Why do you want more beatings? Why do you keep rebelling? Your head has a massive wound, and your whole heart is afflicted.

ISA.1.BSB: From the sole of your foot to the top of your head, there is no soundness— only wounds and welts and festering sores neither cleansed nor bandaged nor soothed with oil.
ISA.1.KJV: From the sole of the foot even to the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrefying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.
ISA.1.PLAIN: From the sole of your foot to the top of your head, there is no soundness— only wounds and welts and festering sores neither cleansed nor bandaged nor soothed with oil.

ISA.1.BSB: Your land is desolate; your cities are burned with fire. Foreigners devour your fields before you— a desolation demolished by strangers.
ISA.1.KJV: Your country is desolate, your cities are burned with fire: your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.
ISA.1.PLAIN: Your land is desolate; your cities are burned with fire. Foreigners devour your fields before you— a desolation demolished by strangers.

ISA.1.BSB: And the Daughter of Zion is abandoned like a shelter in a vineyard, like a shack in a cucumber field, like a city besieged.
ISA.1.KJV: And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city.
ISA.1.PLAIN: And the Daughter of Zion is abandoned like a shelter in a vineyard, like a shack in a cucumber field, like a city besieged.

ISA.1.BSB: Unless the LORD of Hosts had left us a few survivors, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.
ISA.1.KJV: Except the LORD of hosts had left to us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like to Gomorrah. ¶
ISA.1.PLAIN: Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us a few survivors, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.

ISA.1.BSB: Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom; listen to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!
ISA.1.KJV: Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom; give ear to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah.
ISA.1.PLAIN: Hear the word of the Lord, you rulers of Sodom; listen to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!

ISA.1.BSB: “What good to Me is your multitude of sacrifices?” says the LORD. “I am full from the burnt offerings of rams and the fat of well-fed cattle; I take no delight in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats.
ISA.1.KJV: To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices to me? says the LORD: I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.
ISA.1.PLAIN: “What good to Me is your multitude of sacrifices?” says the Lord. “I am full from the burnt offerings of rams and the fat of well-fed cattle; I take no delight in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats.

ISA.1.BSB: When you come to appear before Me, who has required this of you— this trampling of My courts?
ISA.1.KJV: When you come to appear before me, who has required this at your hand, to tread my courts?
ISA.1.PLAIN: When you come to appear before Me, who has required this of you— this trampling of My courts?

ISA.1.BSB: Bring your worthless offerings no more; your incense is detestable to Me— your New Moons, Sabbaths, and convocations. I cannot endure iniquity in a solemn assembly.
ISA.1.KJV: Bring no more vain oblations; incense is an abomination to me; the new moons and sabbaths, the calling of assemblies, I cannot away with; it is iniquity, even the solemn meeting.
ISA.1.PLAIN: Bring your worthless offerings no more; your incense is detestable to Me— your New Moons, Sabbaths, and convocations. I cannot endure brokenness in a solemn assembly.

ISA.1.BSB: I hate your New Moons and your appointed feasts. They have become a burden to Me; I am weary of bearing them.
ISA.1.KJV: Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hates: they are a trouble to me; I am weary to bear them.

ISA.1.BSB: When you spread out your hands in prayer, I will hide My eyes from you; even though you multiply your prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are covered with blood.
ISA.1.KJV: And when you spread forth your hands, I will hide my eyes from you: yes, when you make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood. ¶
ISA.1.PLAIN: When you spread out your hands in prayer, I will hide My eyes from you; even though you multiply your prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are covered with blood.

ISA.1.BSB: Wash and cleanse yourselves. Remove your evil deeds from My sight. Stop doing evil!
ISA.1.KJV: Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes; cease to do evil;
ISA.1.PLAIN: Wash and cleanse yourselves. Remove your evil deeds from My sight. Stop doing evil!

ISA.1.BSB: Learn to do right; seek justice and correct the oppressor. Defend the fatherless and plead the case of the widow.”
ISA.1.KJV: Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.

ISA.1.BSB: “Come now, let us reason together,” says the LORD. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow; though they are as red as crimson, they will become like wool.
ISA.1.KJV: Come now, and let us reason together, says the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

ISA.1.BSB: If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the best of the land.
ISA.1.KJV: If you be willing and obedient, you shall eat the good of the land:
ISA.1.PLAIN: If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the best of the land.

ISA.1.BSB: But if you resist and rebel, you will be devoured by the sword.” For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
ISA.1.KJV: But if you refuse and rebel, you shall be devoured with the sword: for the mouth of the LORD has spoken it. ¶
ISA.1.PLAIN: But if you resist and rebel, you will be devoured by the sword.” For the mouth of the Lord has spoken.

ISA.1.BSB: See how the faithful city has become a harlot! She once was full of justice; righteousness resided within her, but now only murderers!
ISA.1.KJV: How is the faithful city become an harlot! it was full of judgment; righteousness lodged in it; but now murderers.
ISA.1.PLAIN: See how the faithful city has become a harlot! She once was full of justice; righteousness resided within her, but now only murderers!

ISA.1.BSB: Your silver has become dross; your fine wine is diluted with water.
ISA.1.KJV: Your silver is become dross, your wine mixed with water:
ISA.1.PLAIN: Your silver has become dross; your fine wine is diluted with water.

ISA.1.BSB: Your rulers are rebels, friends of thieves. They all love bribes and chasing after rewards. They do not defend the fatherless, and the plea of the widow never comes before them.
ISA.1.KJV: Your princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves: every one loves gifts, and follows after rewards: they judge not the fatherless, neither does the cause of the widow come to them.
ISA.1.PLAIN: Your rulers are rebels, friends of thieves. They all love bribes and chasing after rewards. They do not defend the fatherless, and the plea of the widow never comes before them.

ISA.1.KJV: Therefore says the LORD, the LORD of hosts, the mighty One of Israel, Ah, I will ease me of my adversaries, and avenge me of my enemies: ¶
ISA.1.PLAIN: Therefore the Lord GOD of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, declares: “Ah, I will be relieved of My foes and avenge Myself on My enemies.

ISA.1.BSB: I will turn My hand against you; I will thoroughly purge your dross; I will remove all your impurities.
ISA.1.KJV: And I will turn my hand on you, and purely purge away your dross, and take away all your tin:
ISA.1.PLAIN: I will turn My hand against you; I will thoroughly purge your dross; I will remove all your impurities.

ISA.1.BSB: I will restore your judges as at first, and your counselors as at the beginning. After that you will be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful City.”
ISA.1.KJV: And I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counsellors as at the beginning: afterward you shall be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city.
ISA.1.PLAIN: I will restore your judges as at first, and your counselors as at the beginning. After that you will be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful City.”

ISA.1.BSB: Zion will be redeemed with justice, her repentant ones with righteousness.
ISA.1.KJV: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness. ¶
ISA.1.PLAIN: Zion will be redeemed with justice, her repentant ones with righteousness.

ISA.1.BSB: But rebels and sinners will together be shattered, and those who forsake the LORD will perish.
ISA.1.KJV: And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together, and they that forsake the LORD shall be consumed.
ISA.1.PLAIN: But rebels and sinners will together be shattered, and those who forsake the Lord will perish.

ISA.1.KJV: For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which you have desired, and you shall be confounded for the gardens that you have chosen.
ISA.1.PLAIN: Surely you will be ashamed of the sacred oaks in which you have delighted; you will be embarrassed by the gardens that you have chosen.

ISA.1.BSB: For you will become like an oak whose leaves are withered, like a garden without water.
ISA.1.KJV: For you shall be as an oak whose leaf fades, and as a garden that has no water.
ISA.1.PLAIN: For you will become like an oak whose leaves are withered, like a garden without water.

ISA.1.KJV: And the strong shall be as wick, and the maker of it as a spark, and they shall both burn together, and none shall quench them.

ISA.2.KJV: And many people shall go and say, Come you, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

ISA.2.KJV: And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

ISA.4.PLAIN: On that day the Branch of the Lord will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the pride and glory of Israel’s survivors.

ISA.4.BSB: Whoever remains in Zion and whoever is left in Jerusalem will be called holy— all in Jerusalem who are recorded among the living—
ISA.4.KJV: And it shall come to pass, that he that is left in Zion, and he that remains in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, even every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem:
ISA.4.PLAIN: Whoever remains in Zion and whoever is left in Jerusalem will be called holy— all in Jerusalem who are recorded among the living—

ISA.4.BSB: when the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and cleansed the bloodstains from the heart of Jerusalem by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of fire.
ISA.4.KJV: When the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and shall have purged the blood of Jerusalem from the middle thereof by the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning.
ISA.4.PLAIN: when the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and cleansed the bloodstains from the heart of Jerusalem by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of fire.

ISA.4.BSB: Then the LORD will create over all of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud of smoke by day and a glowing flame of fire by night. For over all the glory there will be a canopy,
ISA.4.KJV: And the LORD will create on every dwelling place of mount Zion, and on her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night: for on all the glory shall be a defense.
ISA.4.PLAIN: Then the Lord will create over all of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud of smoke by day and a glowing flame of fire by night. For over all the glory there will be a canopy,

ISA.4.BSB: a shelter to give shade from the heat by day, and a refuge and hiding place from the storm and the rain.
ISA.4.KJV: And there shall be a tabernacle for a shadow in the day time from the heat, and for a place of refuge, and for a covert from storm and from rain.
ISA.4.PLAIN: a shelter to give shade from the heat by day, and a refuge and hiding place from the storm and the rain.

ISA.5.BSB: I will sing for my beloved a song of his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a very fertile hill.
ISA.5.KJV: Now will I sing to my well beloved a song of my beloved touching his vineyard. My well beloved has a vineyard in a very fruitful hill:
ISA.5.PLAIN: I will sing for my beloved a song of his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a very fertile hill.

ISA.5.BSB: He dug it up and cleared the stones and planted the finest vines. He built a watchtower in the middle and dug out a winepress as well. He waited for the vineyard to yield good grapes, but the fruit it produced was sour!
ISA.5.KJV: And he fenced it, and gathered out the stones thereof, and planted it with the choicest vine, and built a tower in the middle of it, and also made a wine press therein: and he looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes.
ISA.5.PLAIN: He dug it up and cleared the stones and planted the finest vines. He built a watchtower in the middle and dug out a winepress as well. He waited for the vineyard to yield good grapes, but the fruit it produced was sour!

ISA.5.BSB: “And now, O dwellers of Jerusalem and men of Judah, I exhort you to judge between Me and My vineyard.
ISA.5.KJV: And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem, and men of Judah, judge, I pray you, between me and my vineyard.
ISA.5.PLAIN: “And now, O dwellers of Jerusalem and men of Judah, I exhort you to judge between Me and My vineyard.

ISA.5.BSB: What more could I have done for My vineyard than I already did for it? Why, when I expected sweet grapes, did it bring forth sour fruit?
ISA.5.KJV: What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it? why, when I looked that it should bring forth grapes, brought it forth wild grapes?
ISA.5.PLAIN: What more could I have done for My vineyard than I already did for it? Why, when I expected sweet grapes, did it bring forth sour fruit?

ISA.5.BSB: Now I will tell you what I am about to do to My vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it will be consumed; I will tear down its wall, and it will be trampled.
ISA.5.KJV: And now go to; I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; and break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down:
ISA.5.PLAIN: Now I will tell you what I am about to do to My vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it will be consumed; I will tear down its wall, and it will be trampled.

ISA.5.BSB: I will make it a wasteland, neither pruned nor cultivated, and thorns and briers will grow up. I will command the clouds that rain shall not fall on it.”
ISA.5.KJV: And I will lay it waste: it shall not be pruned, nor dig; but there shall come up briers and thorns: I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain on it.
ISA.5.PLAIN: I will make it a wasteland, neither pruned nor cultivated, and thorns and briers will grow up. I will command the clouds that rain shall not fall on it.”

ISA.5.BSB: For the vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are the plant of His delight. He looked for justice, but saw bloodshed; for righteousness, but heard a cry of distress.
ISA.5.KJV: For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant: and he looked for judgment, but behold oppression; for righteousness, but behold a cry. ¶
ISA.5.PLAIN: For the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are the plant of His delight. He looked for justice, but saw bloodshed; for righteousness, but heard a cry of distress.

ISA.5.BSB: Woe to you who add house to house and join field to field until no place is left and you live alone in the land.
ISA.5.KJV: Woe to them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the middle of the earth!
ISA.5.PLAIN: Woe to you who add house to house and join field to field until no place is left and you live alone in the land.

ISA.5.BSB: I heard the LORD of Hosts declare: “Surely many houses will become desolate, great mansions left unoccupied.
ISA.5.KJV: In my ears said the LORD of hosts, Of a truth many houses shall be desolate, even great and fair, without inhabitant.
ISA.5.PLAIN: I heard the Lord of Hosts declare: “Surely many houses will become desolate, great mansions left unoccupied.

ISA.5.BSB: For ten acres of vineyard will yield but a bath of wine, and a homer of seed only an ephah of grain.”
ISA.5.KJV: Yes, ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and the seed of an homer shall yield an ephah. ¶
ISA.5.PLAIN: For ten acres of vineyard will yield but a bath of wine, and a homer of seed only an ephah of grain.”

ISA.5.BSB: Woe to those who rise early in the morning in pursuit of strong drink, who linger into the evening, to be inflamed by wine.
ISA.5.KJV: Woe to them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink; that continue until night, till wine inflame them!
ISA.5.PLAIN: Woe to those who rise early in the morning in pursuit of strong drink, who linger into the evening, to be inflamed by wine.

ISA.5.BSB: At their feasts are the lyre and harp, tambourines and flutes and wine. They disregard the actions of the LORD and fail to see the work of His hands.
ISA.5.KJV: And the harp, and the viol, the tabret, and pipe, and wine, are in their feasts: but they regard not the work of the LORD, neither consider the operation of his hands. ¶
ISA.5.PLAIN: At their feasts are the lyre and harp, tambourines and flutes and wine. They disregard the actions of the Lord and fail to see the work of His hands.

ISA.5.BSB: Therefore My people will go into exile for their lack of understanding; their dignitaries are starving and their masses are parched with thirst.
ISA.5.KJV: Therefore my people are gone into captivity, because they have no knowledge: and their honorable men are famished, and their multitude dried up with thirst.
ISA.5.PLAIN: Therefore My people will go into exile for their lack of understanding; their dignitaries are starving and their masses are parched with thirst.

ISA.5.BSB: Therefore Sheol enlarges its throat and opens wide its enormous jaws, and down go Zion’s nobles and masses, her revelers and carousers!
ISA.5.KJV: Therefore hell has enlarged herself, and opened her mouth without measure: and their glory, and their multitude, and their pomp, and he that rejoices, shall descend into it.
ISA.5.PLAIN: Therefore Sheol enlarges its throat and opens wide its enormous jaws, and down go Zion’s nobles and masses, her revelers and carousers!

ISA.5.BSB: So mankind will be brought low, and each man humbled; the arrogant will lower their eyes.
ISA.5.KJV: And the mean man shall be brought down, and the mighty man shall be humbled, and the eyes of the lofty shall be humbled:
ISA.5.PLAIN: So mankind will be brought low, and each man humbled; the arrogant will lower their eyes.

ISA.5.BSB: But the LORD of Hosts will be exalted by His justice, and the holy God will show Himself holy in righteousness.
ISA.5.KJV: But the LORD of hosts shall be exalted in judgment, and God that is holy shall be sanctified in righteousness.
ISA.5.PLAIN: But the Lord of Hosts will be exalted by His justice, and the holy God will show Himself holy in righteousness.

ISA.5.BSB: Lambs will graze as in their own pastures, and strangers will feed in the ruins of the wealthy.
ISA.5.KJV: Then shall the lambs feed after their manner, and the waste places of the fat ones shall strangers eat.
ISA.5.PLAIN: Lambs will graze as in their own pastures, and strangers will feed in the ruins of the wealthy.

ISA.5.BSB: Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of deceit and pull sin along with cart ropes,
ISA.5.KJV: Woe to them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as it were with a cart rope:
ISA.5.PLAIN: Woe to those who draw brokenness with cords of deceit and pull sin along with cart ropes,

ISA.5.BSB: to those who say, “Let Him hurry and hasten His work so that we may see it! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come so that we may know it!”
ISA.5.KJV: That say, Let him make speed, and hasten his work, that we may see it: and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, that we may know it! ¶
ISA.5.PLAIN: to those who say, “Let Him hurry and hasten His work so that we may see it! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come so that we may know it!”

ISA.5.BSB: Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who turn darkness to light and light to darkness, who replace bitter with sweet and sweet with bitter.
ISA.5.KJV: Woe to them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!
ISA.5.PLAIN: Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who turn darkness to light and light to darkness, who replace bitter with sweet and sweet with bitter.

ISA.5.BSB: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight.
ISA.5.KJV: Woe to them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!
ISA.5.PLAIN: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight.

ISA.5.BSB: Woe to those who are heroes in drinking wine and champions in mixing strong drink,
ISA.5.KJV: Woe to them that are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink:
ISA.5.PLAIN: Woe to those who are heroes in drinking wine and champions in mixing strong drink,

ISA.5.BSB: who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the innocent of justice.
ISA.5.KJV: Which justify the wicked for reward, and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him!
ISA.5.PLAIN: who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the innocent of justice.

ISA.5.BSB: Therefore, as a tongue of fire consumes the straw, and as dry grass shrivels in the flame, so their roots will decay and their blossoms will blow away like dust; for they have rejected the instruction of the LORD of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.
ISA.5.KJV: Therefore as the fire devours the stubble, and the flame consumes the chaff, so their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall go up as dust: because they have cast away the law of the LORD of hosts, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.
ISA.5.PLAIN: Therefore, as a tongue of fire consumes the straw, and as dry grass shrivels in the flame, so their roots will decay and their blossoms will blow away like dust; for they have rejected the instruction of the Lord of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

ISA.5.BSB: Therefore the anger of the LORD burns against His people; His hand is raised against them to strike them down. The mountains quake, and the corpses lay like refuse in the streets. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
ISA.5.KJV: Therefore is the anger of the LORD kindled against his people, and he has stretched forth his hand against them, and has smitten them: and the hills did tremble, and their carcasses were torn in the middle of the streets. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still. ¶
ISA.5.PLAIN: Therefore the anger of the Lord burns against His people; His hand is raised against them to strike them down. The mountains quake, and the corpses lay like refuse in the streets. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.

ISA.5.BSB: He lifts a banner for the distant nations and whistles for those at the ends of the earth. Behold—how speedily and swiftly they come!
ISA.5.KJV: And he will lift up an ensign to the nations from far, and will hiss to them from the end of the earth: and, behold, they shall come with speed swiftly:
ISA.5.PLAIN: He lifts a banner for the distant nations and whistles for those at the ends of the earth. Behold—how speedily and swiftly they come!

ISA.5.BSB: None of them grows weary or stumbles; no one slumbers or sleeps. No belt is loose and no sandal strap is broken.
ISA.5.KJV: None shall be weary nor stumble among them; none shall slumber nor sleep; neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the lace of their shoes be broken:
ISA.5.PLAIN: None of them grows weary or stumbles; no one slumbers or sleeps. No belt is loose and no sandal strap is broken.

ISA.5.BSB: Their arrows are sharpened, and all their bows are strung. The hooves of their horses are like flint; their chariot wheels are like a whirlwind.
ISA.5.KJV: Whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent, their horses’ hoofs shall be counted like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind:
ISA.5.PLAIN: Their arrows are sharpened, and all their bows are strung. The hooves of their horses are like flint; their chariot wheels are like a whirlwind.

ISA.5.BSB: Their roaring is like that of a lion; they roar like young lions. They growl and seize their prey; they carry it away from deliverance.
ISA.5.KJV: Their roaring shall be like a lion, they shall roar like young lions: yes, they shall roar, and lay hold of the prey, and shall carry it away safe, and none shall deliver it.
ISA.5.PLAIN: Their roaring is like that of a lion; they roar like young lions. They growl and seize their prey; they carry it away from deliverance.

ISA.5.BSB: In that day they will roar over it, like the roaring of the sea. If one looks over the land, he will see darkness and distress; even the light will be obscured by clouds.
ISA.5.KJV: And in that day they shall roar against them like the roaring of the sea: and if one look to the land, behold darkness and sorrow, and the light is darkened in the heavens thereof.
ISA.5.PLAIN: In that day they will roar over it, like the roaring of the sea. If one looks over the land, he will see darkness and distress; even the light will be obscured by clouds.

ISA.6.BSB: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted; and the train of His robe filled the temple.
ISA.6.KJV: In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the LORD sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.
ISA.6.PLAIN: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted; and the train of His robe filled the temple.

ISA.6.BSB: Above Him stood seraphim, each having six wings: With two wings they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they were flying.
ISA.6.KJV: Above it stood the seraphim: each one had six wings; with two he covered his face, and with two he covered his feet, and with two he did fly.
ISA.6.PLAIN: Above Him stood seraphim, each having six wings: With two wings they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they were flying.

ISA.6.BSB: And they were calling out to one another: “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory.”
ISA.6.KJV: And one cried to another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.
ISA.6.PLAIN: And they were calling out to one another: “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory.”

ISA.6.BSB: At the sound of their voices the doorposts and thresholds shook, and the temple was filled with smoke.
ISA.6.KJV: And the posts of the door moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke. ¶
ISA.6.PLAIN: At the sound of their voices the doorposts and thresholds shook, and the temple was filled with smoke.

ISA.6.BSB: Then I said: “Woe is me, for I am ruined, because I am a man of unclean lips dwelling among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Hosts.”
ISA.6.KJV: Then said I, Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the middle of a people of unclean lips: for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts.
ISA.6.PLAIN: Then I said: “Woe is me, for I am ruined, because I am a man of unclean lips dwelling among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the Lord of Hosts.”

ISA.6.BSB: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.
ISA.6.KJV: Then flew one of the seraphim to me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar:
ISA.6.PLAIN: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.

ISA.6.BSB: And with it he touched my mouth and said: “Now that this has touched your lips, your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned for.”
ISA.6.KJV: And he laid it on my mouth, and said, See, this has touched your lips; and your iniquity is taken away, and your sin purged.
ISA.6.PLAIN: And with it he touched my mouth and said: “Now that this has touched your lips, your brokenness is removed and your sin is atoned for.”

ISA.6.BSB: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying: “Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?” And I said: “Here am I. Send me!”
ISA.6.KJV: Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me. ¶
ISA.6.PLAIN: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, 'Whom shall I send? And who will go for us?' And I said, 'Here am I. Send me!'

ISA.6.BSB: And He replied: “Go and tell this people, ‘Be ever hearing, but never understanding; be ever seeing, but never perceiving.’
ISA.6.KJV: And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear you indeed, but understand not; and see you indeed, but perceive not.
ISA.6.PLAIN: And He replied: “Go and tell this people, ‘Be ever hearing, but never understanding; be ever seeing, but never perceiving.’

ISA.6.BSB: Make the hearts of this people calloused; deafen their ears and close their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed.”
ISA.6.KJV: Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.
ISA.6.PLAIN: Make the hearts of this people calloused; deafen their ears and close their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed.”

ISA.6.BSB: Then I asked: “How long, O Lord?” And He replied: “Until the cities lie ruined and without inhabitant, until the houses are left unoccupied and the land is desolate and ravaged,
ISA.6.KJV: Then said I, Lord, how long? And he answered, Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate,
ISA.6.PLAIN: Then I asked: “How long, O Lord?” And He replied: “Until the cities lie ruined and without inhabitant, until the houses are left unoccupied and the land is desolate and ravaged,

ISA.6.BSB: until the LORD has driven men far away and the land is utterly forsaken.
ISA.6.KJV: And the LORD have removed men far away, and there be a great forsaking in the middle of the land. ¶
ISA.6.PLAIN: until the Lord has driven men far away and the land is utterly forsaken.

ISA.6.BSB: And though a tenth remains in the land, it will be burned again. As the terebinth and oak leave stumps when felled, so the holy seed will be a stump in the land.”
ISA.6.KJV: But yet in it shall be a tenth, and it shall return, and shall be eaten: as a teil tree, and as an oak, whose substance is in them, when they cast their leaves: so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.
ISA.6.PLAIN: And though a tenth remains in the land, it will be burned again. As the terebinth and oak leave stumps when felled, so the holy seed will be a stump in the land.”

ISA.7.BSB: Now in the days that Ahaz son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, was king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram marched up to wage war against Jerusalem. He was accompanied by Pekah son of Remaliah the king of Israel, but he could not overpower the city.
ISA.7.KJV: And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up toward Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.
ISA.7.PLAIN: Now in the days that Ahaz son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, was king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram marched up to wage war against Jerusalem. He was accompanied by Pekah son of Remaliah the king of Israel, but he could not overpower the city.

ISA.7.BSB: When it was reported to the house of David that Aram was in league with Ephraim, the hearts of Ahaz and his people trembled like trees in the forest shaken by the wind.
ISA.7.KJV: And it was told the house of David, saying, Syria is confederate with Ephraim. And his heart was moved, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the wood are moved with the wind.
ISA.7.PLAIN: When it was reported to the house of David that Aram was in league with Ephraim, the hearts of Ahaz and his people trembled like trees in the forest shaken by the wind.

ISA.7.BSB: Then the LORD said to Isaiah, “Go out with your son Shear-jashub to meet Ahaz at the end of the aqueduct that feeds the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field,
ISA.7.KJV: Then said the LORD to Isaiah, Go forth now to meet Ahaz, you, and Shearjashub your son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller’s field;
ISA.7.PLAIN: Then the Lord said to Isaiah, “Go out with your son Shear-jashub to meet Ahaz at the end of the aqueduct that feeds the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field,

ISA.7.BSB: and say to him: Calm down and be quiet. Do not be afraid or disheartened over these two smoldering stubs of firewood—over the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram and of the son of Remaliah.
ISA.7.KJV: And say to him, Take heed, and be quiet; fear not, neither be fainthearted for the two tails of these smoking firebrands, for the fierce anger of Rezin with Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.
ISA.7.PLAIN: and say to him: Calm down and be quiet. Do not be afraid or disheartened over these two smoldering stubs of firewood—over the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram and of the son of Remaliah.

ISA.7.BSB: For Aram, along with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has plotted your ruin, saying:
ISA.7.KJV: Because Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, have taken evil counsel against you, saying,
ISA.7.PLAIN: For Aram, along with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has plotted your ruin, saying:

ISA.7.BSB: ‘Let us invade Judah, terrorize it, and divide it among ourselves. Then we can install the son of Tabeal over it as king.’
ISA.7.KJV: Let us go up against Judah, and vex it, and let us make a breach therein for us, and set a king in the middle of it, even the son of Tabeal:
ISA.7.PLAIN: ‘Let us invade Judah, terrorize it, and divide it among ourselves. Then we can install the son of Tabeal over it as king.’

ISA.7.BSB: But this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘It will not arise; it will not happen.
ISA.7.KJV: Thus says the Lord GOD, It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass.
ISA.7.PLAIN: But this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘It will not arise; it will not happen.

ISA.7.BSB: For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered as a people.
ISA.7.KJV: For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within three score and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.
ISA.7.PLAIN: For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered as a people.

ISA.7.BSB: The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not stand firm in your faith, then you will not stand at all.’”
ISA.7.KJV: And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If you will not believe, surely you shall not be established. ¶
ISA.7.PLAIN: The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not stand firm in your faith, then you will not stand at all.’”

ISA.7.BSB: Again the LORD spoke to Ahaz, saying,
ISA.7.KJV: Moreover the LORD spoke again to Ahaz, saying,
ISA.7.PLAIN: Again the Lord spoke to Ahaz, saying,

ISA.7.BSB: “Ask for a sign from the LORD your God, whether from the depths of Sheol or the heights of heaven.”
ISA.7.KJV: Ask you a sign of the LORD your God; ask it either in the depth, or in the height above.
ISA.7.PLAIN: “Ask for a sign from the Lord your God, whether from the depths of Sheol or the heights of heaven.”

ISA.7.BSB: But Ahaz replied, “I will not ask; I will not test the LORD.”
ISA.7.KJV: But Ahaz said, I will not ask, neither will I tempt the LORD.
ISA.7.PLAIN: But Ahaz replied, “I will not ask; I will not test the Lord.”

ISA.7.BSB: Then Isaiah said, “Hear now, O house of David! Is it not enough to try the patience of men? Will you try the patience of my God as well?
ISA.7.KJV: And he said, Hear you now, O house of David; Is it a small thing for you to weary men, but will you weary my God also?
ISA.7.PLAIN: Then Isaiah said, “Hear now, O house of David! Is it not enough to try the patience of men? Will you try the patience of my God as well?

ISA.7.BSB: Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son, and will call Him Immanuel.
ISA.7.KJV: Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
ISA.7.PLAIN: Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: Look closely — the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son, and will call Him Immanuel.

ISA.7.BSB: By the time He knows enough to reject evil and choose good, He will be eating curds and honey.
ISA.7.KJV: Butter and honey shall he eat, that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good.
ISA.7.PLAIN: By the time He knows enough to reject evil and choose good, He will be eating curds and honey.

ISA.7.BSB: For before the boy knows enough to reject evil and choose good, the land of the two kings you dread will be laid waste.

ISA.17.KJV: In that day shall his strong cities be as a forsaken bough, and an uppermost branch, which they left because of the children of Israel: and there shall be desolation.
ISA.17.PLAIN: In that day their strong cities will be like forsaken thickets and summits, abandoned to the Israelites and to utter desolation.

ISA.17.BSB: For you have forgotten the God of your salvation and failed to remember the Rock of your refuge. Therefore, though you cultivate delightful plots and set out cuttings from exotic vines—
ISA.17.KJV: Because you have forgotten the God of your salvation, and have not been mindful of the rock of your strength, therefore shall you plant pleasant plants, and shall set it with strange slips:
ISA.17.PLAIN: For you have forgotten the God of your salvation and failed to remember the Rock of your refuge. Therefore, though you cultivate delightful plots and set out cuttings from exotic vines—

ISA.17.BSB: though on the day you plant you make them grow, and on that morning you help your seed sprout— yet the harvest will vanish on the day of disease and incurable pain.
ISA.17.KJV: In the day shall you make your plant to grow, and in the morning shall you make your seed to flourish: but the harvest shall be a heap in the day of grief and of desperate sorrow. ¶
ISA.17.PLAIN: though on the day you plant you make them grow, and on that morning you help your seed sprout— yet the harvest will vanish on the day of disease and incurable pain.

ISA.17.BSB: Alas, the tumult of many peoples; they rage like the roaring seas and clamoring nations; they rumble like the crashing of mighty waters.
ISA.17.KJV: Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!
ISA.17.PLAIN: Alas, the tumult of many peoples; they rage like the roaring seas and clamoring nations; they rumble like the crashing of mighty waters.

ISA.17.BSB: The nations rage like the rush of many waters. He rebukes them, and they flee far away, driven before the wind like chaff on the hills, like tumbleweeds before a gale.
ISA.17.KJV: The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters: but God shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far off, and shall be chased as the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like a rolling thing before the whirlwind.
ISA.17.PLAIN: The nations rage like the rush of many waters. He rebukes them, and they flee far away, driven before the wind like chaff on the hills, like tumbleweeds before a gale.

ISA.17.BSB: In the evening, there is sudden terror! Before morning, they are no more! This is the portion of those who loot us and the lot of those who plunder us.
ISA.17.KJV: And behold at evening trouble; and before the morning he is not. This is the portion of them that spoil us, and the lot of them that rob us.
ISA.17.PLAIN: In the evening, there is sudden terror! Before morning, they are no more! This is the portion of those who loot us and the lot of those who plunder us.

ISA.18.BSB: Woe to the land of whirring wings, along the rivers of Cush,
ISA.18.KJV: Woe to the land shadowing with wings, which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia:
ISA.18.PLAIN: Woe to the land of whirring wings, along the rivers of Cush,

ISA.18.BSB: which sends couriers by sea, in papyrus vessels on the waters. Go, swift messengers, to a people tall and smooth-skinned, to a people widely feared, to a powerful nation of strange speech, whose land is divided by rivers.
ISA.18.KJV: That sends ambassadors by the sea, even in vessels of bulrushes on the waters, saying, Go, you swift messengers, to a nation scattered and peeled, to a people terrible from their beginning till now; a nation meted out and trodden down, whose land the rivers have spoiled!
ISA.18.PLAIN: which sends couriers by sea, in papyrus vessels on the waters. Go, swift messengers, to a people tall and smooth-skinned, to a people widely feared, to a powerful nation of strange speech, whose land is divided by rivers.

ISA.18.BSB: All you people of the world and dwellers of the earth, when a banner is raised on the mountains, you will see it; when a ram’s horn sounds, you will hear it.
ISA.18.KJV: All you inhabitants of the world, and dwellers on the earth, see you, when he lifts up an ensign on the mountains; and when he blows a trumpet, hear you.
ISA.18.PLAIN: All you people of the world and dwellers of the earth, when a banner is raised on the mountains, you will see it; when a ram’s horn sounds, you will hear it.

ISA.18.BSB: For this is what the LORD has told me: “I will quietly look on from My dwelling place, like shimmering heat in the sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.”
ISA.18.KJV: For so the LORD said to me, I will take my rest, and I will consider in my dwelling place like a clear heat on herbs, and like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.
ISA.18.PLAIN: For this is what the Lord has told me: “I will quietly look on from My dwelling place, like shimmering heat in the sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.”

ISA.18.BSB: For before the harvest, when the blossom is gone and the flower becomes a ripening grape, He will cut off the shoots with a pruning knife and remove and discard the branches.
ISA.18.KJV: For before the harvest, when the bud is perfect, and the sour grape is ripening in the flower, he shall both cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks, and take away and cut down the branches.
ISA.18.PLAIN: For before the harvest, when the blossom is gone and the flower becomes a ripening grape, He will cut off the shoots with a pruning knife and remove and discard the branches.

ISA.18.BSB: They will all be left to the mountain birds of prey, and to the beasts of the land. The birds will feed on them in summer, and all the wild animals in winter.
ISA.18.KJV: They shall be left together to the fowls of the mountains, and to the beasts of the earth: and the fowls shall summer on them, and all the beasts of the earth shall winter on them. ¶
ISA.18.PLAIN: They will all be left to the mountain birds of prey, and to the beasts of the land. The birds will feed on them in summer, and all the wild animals in winter.

ISA.18.BSB: At that time gifts will be brought to the LORD of Hosts— from a people tall and smooth-skinned, from a people widely feared, from a powerful nation of strange speech, whose land is divided by rivers— to Mount Zion, the place of the Name of the LORD of Hosts.
ISA.18.KJV: In that time shall the present be brought to the LORD of hosts of a people scattered and peeled, and from a people terrible from their beginning till now; a nation meted out and trodden under foot, whose land the rivers have spoiled, to the place of the name of the LORD of hosts, the mount Zion.
ISA.18.PLAIN: At that time gifts will be brought to the Lord of Hosts— from a people tall and smooth-skinned, from a people widely feared, from a powerful nation of strange speech, whose land is divided by rivers— to Mount Zion, the place of the Name of the Lord of Hosts.

ISA.19.BSB: This is the burden against Egypt: Behold, the LORD rides on a swift cloud; He is coming to Egypt. The idols of Egypt will tremble before Him, and the hearts of the Egyptians will melt within them.
ISA.19.KJV: The burden of Egypt. Behold, the LORD rides on a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and the heart of Egypt shall melt in the middle of it.
ISA.19.PLAIN: This is the burden against Egypt: Look closely — the Lord rides on a swift cloud; He is coming to Egypt. The idols of Egypt will tremble before Him, and the hearts of the Egyptians will melt within them.

ISA.19.BSB: “So I will incite Egyptian against Egyptian; brother will fight against brother, neighbor against neighbor, city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.
ISA.19.KJV: And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbor; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.
ISA.19.PLAIN: “So I will incite Egyptian against Egyptian; brother will fight against brother, neighbor against neighbor, city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.

ISA.19.BSB: Then the spirit of the Egyptians will be emptied out from among them, and I will frustrate their plans, so that they will resort to idols and spirits of the dead, to mediums and spiritists.
ISA.19.KJV: And the spirit of Egypt shall fail in the middle thereof; and I will destroy the counsel thereof: and they shall seek to the idols, and to the charmers, and to them that have familiar spirits, and to the wizards.
ISA.19.PLAIN: Then the spirit of the Egyptians will be emptied out from among them, and I will frustrate their plans, so that they will resort to idols and spirits of the dead, to mediums and spiritists.

ISA.19.BSB: I will deliver the Egyptians into the hands of harsh masters, and a fierce king will rule over them,” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts.
ISA.19.KJV: And the Egyptians will I give over into the hand of a cruel lord; and a fierce king shall rule over them, says the Lord, the LORD of hosts.
ISA.19.PLAIN: I will deliver the Egyptians into the hands of harsh masters, and a fierce king will rule over them,” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts.

ISA.19.BSB: The waters of the Nile will dry up, and the riverbed will be parched and empty.
ISA.19.KJV: And the waters shall fail from the sea, and the river shall be wasted and dried up.
ISA.19.PLAIN: The waters of the Nile will dry up, and the riverbed will be parched and empty.

ISA.19.BSB: The canals will stink; the streams of Egypt will trickle and dry up; the reeds and rushes will wither.
ISA.19.KJV: And they shall turn the rivers far away; and the brooks of defense shall be emptied and dried up: the reeds and flags shall wither.
ISA.19.PLAIN: The canals will stink; the streams of Egypt will trickle and dry up; the reeds and rushes will wither.

ISA.19.BSB: The bulrushes by the Nile, by the mouth of the river, and all the fields sown along the Nile, will wither, blow away, and be no more.
ISA.19.KJV: The paper reeds by the brooks, by the mouth of the brooks, and every thing sown by the brooks, shall wither, be driven away, and be no more.
ISA.19.PLAIN: The bulrushes by the Nile, by the mouth of the river, and all the fields sown along the Nile, will wither, blow away, and be no more.

ISA.19.BSB: Then the fishermen will mourn, all who cast a hook into the Nile will lament, and those who spread nets on the waters will pine away.
ISA.19.KJV: The fishers also shall mourn, and all they that cast angle into the brooks shall lament, and they that spread nets on the waters shall languish.
ISA.19.PLAIN: Then the fishermen will mourn, all who cast a hook into the Nile will lament, and those who spread nets on the waters will pine away.

ISA.19.BSB: The workers in flax will be dismayed, and the weavers of fine linen will turn pale.
ISA.19.KJV: Moreover they that work in fine flax, and they that weave networks, shall be confounded.
ISA.19.PLAIN: The workers in flax will be dismayed, and the weavers of fine linen will turn pale.

ISA.19.BSB: The workers in cloth will be dejected, and all the hired workers will be sick at heart.
ISA.19.KJV: And they shall be broken in the purposes thereof, all that make sluices and ponds for fish. ¶
ISA.19.PLAIN: The workers in cloth will be dejected, and all the hired workers will be sick at heart.

ISA.19.BSB: The princes of Zoan are mere fools; Pharaoh’s wise counselors give senseless advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, “I am one of the wise, a son of eastern kings”?
