JER.44.BSB: This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: As for you and your wives, you have spoken with your mouths and fulfilled with your hands your words: ‘We will surely perform our vows that we have made to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her.’ Go ahead, then, do what you have promised! Keep your vows!
JER.44.KJV: Thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, saying; You and your wives have both spoken with your mouths, and fulfilled with your hand, saying, We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings to her: you will surely accomplish your vows, and surely perform your vows.
JER.44.PLAIN: This is what the Lord of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: As for you and your wives, you have spoken with your mouths and fulfilled with your hands your words: ‘We will surely perform our vows that we have made to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her.’ Go ahead, then, do what you have promised! Keep your vows!

JER.44.BSB: Nevertheless, hear the word of the LORD, all you people of Judah living in Egypt: Behold, I have sworn by My great name, says the LORD, that never again will any man of Judah living in the land of Egypt invoke My name or say, ‘As surely as the Lord GOD lives.’
JER.44.KJV: Therefore hear you the word of the LORD, all Judah that dwell in the land of Egypt; Behold, I have sworn by my great name, says the LORD, that my name shall no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, The Lord GOD lives.
JER.44.PLAIN: Nevertheless, hear the word of the Lord, all you people of Judah living in Egypt: Look closely — I have sworn by My great name, says the Lord, that never again will any man of Judah living in the land of Egypt invoke My name or say, ‘As surely as the Lord GOD lives.’

JER.44.BSB: I am watching over them for harm and not for good, and every man of Judah who is in the land of Egypt will meet his end by sword or famine, until they are finished off.
JER.44.KJV: Behold, I will watch over them for evil, and not for good: and all the men of Judah that are in the land of Egypt shall be consumed by the sword and by the famine, until there be an end of them.
JER.44.PLAIN: I am watching over them for harm and not for good, and every man of Judah who is in the land of Egypt will meet his end by sword or famine, until they are finished off.

JER.44.BSB: Those who escape the sword will return from Egypt to Judah, few in number, and the whole remnant of Judah who went to dwell in the land of Egypt will know whose word will stand, Mine or theirs!
JER.44.KJV: Yet a small number that escape the sword shall return out of the land of Egypt into the land of Judah, and all the remnant of Judah, that are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall know whose words shall stand, mine, or theirs. ¶
JER.44.PLAIN: Those who escape the sword will return from Egypt to Judah, few in number, and the whole remnant of Judah who went to dwell in the land of Egypt will know whose word will stand, Mine or theirs!

JER.44.BSB: This will be a sign to you that I will punish you in this place, declares the LORD, so that you may know that My threats of harm against you will surely stand.
JER.44.KJV: And this shall be a sign to you, says the LORD, that I will punish you in this place, that you may know that my words shall surely stand against you for evil:
JER.44.PLAIN: This will be a sign to you that I will punish you in this place, declares the Lord, so that you may know that My threats of harm against you will surely stand.

JER.44.BSB: This is what the LORD says: Behold, I will deliver Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hands of his enemies who seek his life, just as I delivered Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the enemy who was seeking his life.”
JER.44.KJV: Thus says the LORD; Behold, I will give pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of them that seek his life; as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, and that sought his life.
JER.44.PLAIN: This is what the Lord says: Look closely — I will deliver Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hands of his enemies who seek his life, just as I delivered Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the enemy who was seeking his life.”

JER.45.BSB: This is the word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah when he wrote these words on a scroll at the dictation of Jeremiah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
JER.45.KJV: The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch the son of Neriah, when he had written these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, saying,
JER.45.PLAIN: This is the word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah when he wrote these words on a scroll at the dictation of Jeremiah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:

JER.45.BSB: “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says to you, Baruch:
JER.45.KJV: Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, to you, O Baruch:
JER.45.PLAIN: “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says to you, Baruch:

JER.45.BSB: You have said, ‘Woe is me because the LORD has added sorrow to my pain! I am worn out with groaning and have found no rest.’”
JER.45.KJV: You did say, Woe is me now! for the LORD has added grief to my sorrow; I fainted in my sighing, and I find no rest. ¶
JER.45.PLAIN: You have said, ‘Woe is me because the Lord has added sorrow to my pain! I am worn out with groaning and have found no rest.’”

JER.45.BSB: Thus Jeremiah was to say to Baruch: “This is what the LORD says: Throughout the land I will demolish what I have built and uproot what I have planted.
JER.45.KJV: Thus shall you say to him, The LORD says thus; Behold, that which I have built will I break down, and that which I have planted I will pluck up, even this whole land.
JER.45.PLAIN: Thus Jeremiah was to say to Baruch: “This is what the Lord says: Throughout the land I will demolish what I have built and uproot what I have planted.

JER.45.BSB: But as for you, do you seek great things for yourself? Stop seeking! For I will bring disaster on every living creature, declares the LORD, but wherever you go, I will grant your life as a spoil of war.”
JER.45.KJV: And seek you great things for yourself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil on all flesh, says the LORD: but your life will I give to you for a prey in all places where you go.
JER.45.PLAIN: But as for you, do you seek great things for yourself? Stop seeking! For I will bring disaster on every living creature, declares the Lord, but wherever you go, I will grant your life as a spoil of war.”

JER.46.BSB: This is the word of the LORD about the nations—the word that came to Jeremiah the prophet
JER.46.KJV: The word of the LORD which came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Gentiles;
JER.46.PLAIN: This is the word of the Lord about the nations—the word that came to Jeremiah the prophet

JER.46.BSB: concerning Egypt and the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, which was defeated at Carchemish on the Euphrates River by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah:
JER.46.KJV: Against Egypt, against the army of Pharaohnecho king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah.
JER.46.PLAIN: concerning Egypt and the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, which was defeated at Carchemish on the Euphrates River by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah:

JER.46.BSB: “Deploy your shields, small and large; advance for battle!
JER.46.KJV: Order you the buckler and shield, and draw near to battle.
JER.46.PLAIN: “Deploy your shields, small and large; advance for battle!

JER.46.BSB: Harness the horses; mount the steeds; take your positions with helmets on! Polish your spears; put on armor!
JER.46.KJV: Harness the horses; and get up, you horsemen, and stand forth with your helmets; furbish the spears, and put on the brigandines.
JER.46.PLAIN: Harness the horses; mount the steeds; take your positions with helmets on! Polish your spears; put on armor!

JER.46.BSB: Why am I seeing this? They are terrified, they are retreating; their warriors are defeated, they flee in haste without looking back; terror is on every side!” declares the LORD.
JER.46.KJV: Why have I seen them dismayed and turned away back? and their mighty ones are beaten down, and are fled apace, and look not back: for fear was round about, says the LORD.
JER.46.PLAIN: Why am I seeing this? They are terrified, they are retreating; their warriors are defeated, they flee in haste without looking back; terror is on every side!” declares the Lord.

JER.46.BSB: “The swift cannot flee, and the warrior cannot escape! In the north by the River Euphrates they stumble and fall.
JER.46.KJV: Let not the swift flee away, nor the mighty man escape; they shall stumble, and fall toward the north by the river Euphrates.
JER.46.PLAIN: “The swift cannot flee, and the warrior cannot escape! In the north by the River Euphrates they stumble and fall.

JER.46.BSB: Who is this, rising like the Nile, like rivers whose waters churn?
JER.46.KJV: Who is this that comes up as a flood, whose waters are moved as the rivers?
JER.46.PLAIN: Who is this, rising like the Nile, like rivers whose waters churn?

JER.46.BSB: Egypt rises like the Nile, and its waters churn like rivers, boasting, ‘I will rise and cover the earth; I will destroy the cities and their people.’
JER.46.KJV: Egypt rises up like a flood, and his waters are moved like the rivers; and he says, I will go up, and will cover the earth; I will destroy the city and the inhabitants thereof.
JER.46.PLAIN: Egypt rises like the Nile, and its waters churn like rivers, boasting, ‘I will rise and cover the earth; I will destroy the cities and their people.’

JER.46.BSB: Advance, O horses! Race furiously, O chariots! Let the warriors come forth— Cush and Put carrying their shields, men of Lydia drawing the bow.
JER.46.KJV: Come up, you horses; and rage, you chariots; and let the mighty men come forth; the Ethiopians and the Libyans, that handle the shield; and the Lydians, that handle and bend the bow.
JER.46.PLAIN: Advance, O horses! Race furiously, O chariots! Let the warriors come forth— Cush and Put carrying their shields, men of Lydia drawing the bow.

JER.46.BSB: For that day belongs to the Lord GOD of Hosts, a day of vengeance against His foes. The sword will devour until it is satisfied, until it is quenched with their blood. For the Lord GOD of Hosts will hold a sacrifice in the land of the north by the River Euphrates.
JER.46.KJV: For this is the day of the Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge him of his adversaries: and the sword shall devour, and it shall be satiate and made drunk with their blood: for the Lord GOD of hosts has a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates.
JER.46.PLAIN: For that day belongs to the Lord GOD of Hosts, a day of vengeance against His foes. The sword will devour until it is satisfied, until it is quenched with their blood. For the Lord GOD of Hosts will hold a sacrifice in the land of the north by the River Euphrates.

JER.46.BSB: Go up to Gilead for balm, O Virgin Daughter of Egypt! In vain you try many remedies, but for you there is no healing.
JER.46.KJV: Go up into Gilead, and take balm, O virgin, the daughter of Egypt: in vain shall you use many medicines; for you shall not be cured.
JER.46.PLAIN: Go up to Gilead for balm, O Virgin Daughter of Egypt! In vain you try many remedies, but for you there is no healing.

JER.46.BSB: The nations have heard of your shame, and your outcry fills the earth, because warrior stumbles over warrior and both of them have fallen together.”
JER.46.KJV: The nations have heard of your shame, and your cry has filled the land: for the mighty man has stumbled against the mighty, and they are fallen both together. ¶
JER.46.PLAIN: The nations have heard of your shame, and your outcry fills the earth, because warrior stumbles over warrior and both of them have fallen together.”

JER.46.BSB: This is the word that the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt:
JER.46.KJV: The word that the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet, how Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon should come and smite the land of Egypt.
JER.46.PLAIN: This is the word that the Lord spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt:

JER.46.BSB: “Announce it in Egypt, and proclaim it in Migdol; proclaim it in Memphis and Tahpanhes: ‘Take your positions and prepare yourself, for the sword devours those around you.’
JER.46.KJV: Declare you in Egypt, and publish in Migdol, and publish in Noph and in Tahpanhes: say you, Stand fast, and prepare you; for the sword shall devour round about you.
JER.46.PLAIN: “Announce it in Egypt, and proclaim it in Migdol; proclaim it in Memphis and Tahpanhes: ‘Take your positions and prepare yourself, for the sword devours those around you.’

JER.46.BSB: Why have your warriors been laid low? They cannot stand, for the LORD has thrust them down.
JER.46.KJV: Why are your valiant men swept away? they stood not, because the LORD did drive them.
JER.46.PLAIN: Why have your warriors been laid low? They cannot stand, for the Lord has thrust them down.

JER.46.BSB: They continue to stumble; indeed, they have fallen over one another. They say, ‘Get up! Let us return to our people and to the land of our birth, away from the sword of the oppressor.’
JER.46.KJV: He made many to fall, yes, one fell on another: and they said, Arise, and let us go again to our own people, and to the land of our nativity, from the oppressing sword.
JER.46.PLAIN: They continue to stumble; indeed, they have fallen over one another. They say, ‘Get up! Let us return to our people and to the land of our birth, away from the sword of the oppressor.’

JER.46.BSB: There they will cry out: ‘Pharaoh king of Egypt was all noise; he has let the appointed time pass him by.’
JER.46.KJV: They did cry there, Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he has passed the time appointed.
JER.46.PLAIN: There they will cry out: ‘Pharaoh king of Egypt was all noise; he has let the appointed time pass him by.’

JER.46.BSB: As surely as I live, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts, there will come one who is like Tabor among the mountains and like Carmel by the sea.
JER.46.KJV: As I live, says the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts, Surely as Tabor is among the mountains, and as Carmel by the sea, so shall he come.
JER.46.PLAIN: As surely as I live, declares the King, whose name is the Lord of Hosts, there will come one who is like Tabor among the mountains and like Carmel by the sea.

JER.46.BSB: Pack your bags for exile, O daughter dwelling in Egypt! For Memphis will be laid waste, destroyed and uninhabited.
JER.46.KJV: O you daughter dwelling in Egypt, furnish yourself to go into captivity: for Noph shall be waste and desolate without an inhabitant.
JER.46.PLAIN: Pack your bags for exile, O daughter dwelling in Egypt! For Memphis will be laid waste, destroyed and uninhabited.

JER.46.BSB: Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a gadfly from the north is coming against her.
JER.46.KJV: Egypt is like a very fair heifer, but destruction comes; it comes out of the north.
JER.46.PLAIN: Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a gadfly from the north is coming against her.

JER.46.BSB: Even the mercenaries among her are like fattened calves. They too will turn back; together they will flee, they will not stand their ground, for the day of calamity is coming upon them— the time of their punishment.
JER.46.KJV: Also her hired men are in the middle of her like fatted bullocks; for they also are turned back, and are fled away together: they did not stand, because the day of their calamity was come on them, and the time of their visitation.
JER.46.PLAIN: Even the mercenaries among her are like fattened calves. They too will turn back; together they will flee, they will not stand their ground, for the day of calamity is coming upon them— the time of their punishment.

JER.46.BSB: Egypt will hiss like a fleeing serpent, for the enemy will advance in force; with axes they will come against her like woodsmen cutting down trees.
JER.46.KJV: The voice thereof shall go like a serpent; for they shall march with an army, and come against her with axes, as hewers of wood.
JER.46.PLAIN: Egypt will hiss like a fleeing serpent, for the enemy will advance in force; with axes they will come against her like woodsmen cutting down trees.

JER.46.BSB: They will chop down her forest, declares the LORD, dense though it may be, for they are more numerous than locusts; they cannot be counted.
JER.46.KJV: They shall cut down her forest, says the LORD, though it cannot be searched; because they are more than the grasshoppers, and are innumerable.
JER.46.PLAIN: They will chop down her forest, declares the Lord, dense though it may be, for they are more numerous than locusts; they cannot be counted.

JER.46.BSB: The Daughter of Egypt will be put to shame; she will be delivered into the hands of the people of the north.”
JER.46.KJV: The daughter of Egypt shall be confounded; she shall be delivered into the hand of the people of the north.
JER.46.PLAIN: The Daughter of Egypt will be put to shame; she will be delivered into the hands of the people of the north.”

JER.46.BSB: The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Behold, I am about to punish Amon god of Thebes, along with Pharaoh, Egypt with her gods and kings, and those who trust in Pharaoh.
JER.46.KJV: The LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says; Behold, I will punish the multitude of No, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, with their gods, and their kings; even Pharaoh, and all them that trust in him:
JER.46.PLAIN: The Lord of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Look closely — I am about to punish Amon god of Thebes, along with Pharaoh, Egypt with her gods and kings, and those who trust in Pharaoh.

JER.46.BSB: I will deliver them into the hands of those who seek their lives—of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his officers. But after this, Egypt will be inhabited as in days of old, declares the LORD.
JER.46.KJV: And I will deliver them into the hand of those that seek their lives, and into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of his servants: and afterward it shall be inhabited, as in the days of old, says the LORD. ¶
JER.46.PLAIN: I will deliver them into the hands of those who seek their lives—of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his officers. But after this, Egypt will be inhabited as in days of old, declares the Lord.

JER.46.BSB: But you, O Jacob My servant, do not be afraid, and do not be dismayed, O Israel. For I will surely save you out of a distant place, your descendants from the land of their captivity! Jacob will return to quiet and ease, with no one to make him afraid.
JER.46.KJV: But fear not you, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel: for, behold, I will save you from afar off, and your seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and be in rest and at ease, and none shall make him afraid.
JER.46.PLAIN: But you, O Jacob My servant, do not be afraid, and do not be dismayed, O Israel. For I will surely save you out of a distant place, your descendants from the land of their captivity! Jacob will return to quiet and ease, with no one to make him afraid.

JER.46.BSB: And you, My servant Jacob, do not be afraid, declares the LORD, for I am with you. Though I will completely destroy all the nations to which I have banished you, I will not completely destroy you. Yet I will discipline you justly, and will by no means leave you unpunished.”
JER.46.KJV: Fear you not, O Jacob my servant, says the LORD: for I am with you; for I will make a full end of all the nations where I have driven you: but I will not make a full end of you, but correct you in measure; yet will I not leave you wholly unpunished.
JER.46.PLAIN: And you, My servant Jacob, do not be afraid, declares the Lord, for I am with you. Though I will completely destroy all the nations to which I have banished you, I will not completely destroy you. Yet I will discipline you justly, and will by no means leave you unpunished.”

JER.47.BSB: This is the word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet about the Philistines before Pharaoh struck down Gaza.
JER.47.KJV: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Philistines, before that Pharaoh smote Gaza.
JER.47.PLAIN: This is the word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet about the Philistines before Pharaoh struck down Gaza.

JER.47.BSB: This is what the LORD says: “See how the waters are rising from the north and becoming an overflowing torrent. They will overflow the land and its fullness, the cities and their inhabitants. The people will cry out, and all who dwell in the land will wail
JER.47.KJV: Thus says the LORD; Behold, waters rise up out of the north, and shall be an overflowing flood, and shall overflow the land, and all that is therein; the city, and them that dwell therein: then the men shall cry, and all the inhabitants of the land shall howl.
JER.47.PLAIN: This is what the Lord says: “See how the waters are rising from the north and becoming an overflowing torrent. They will overflow the land and its fullness, the cities and their inhabitants. The people will cry out, and all who dwell in the land will wail

JER.47.BSB: at the sound of the galloping hooves of stallions, the rumbling of chariots, and the clatter of their wheels. The fathers will not turn back for their sons; their hands will hang limp.
JER.47.KJV: At the noise of the stamping of the hoofs of his strong horses, at the rushing of his chariots, and at the rumbling of his wheels, the fathers shall not look back to their children for feebleness of hands;
JER.47.PLAIN: at the sound of the galloping hooves of stallions, the rumbling of chariots, and the clatter of their wheels. The fathers will not turn back for their sons; their hands will hang limp.

JER.47.BSB: For the day has come to destroy all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every remaining ally. Indeed, the LORD is about to destroy the Philistines, the remnant from the coasts of Caphtor.
JER.47.KJV: Because of the day that comes to spoil all the Philistines, and to cut off from Tyrus and Zidon every helper that remains: for the LORD will spoil the Philistines, the remnant of the country of Caphtor.
JER.47.PLAIN: For the day has come to destroy all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every remaining ally. Indeed, the Lord is about to destroy the Philistines, the remnant from the coasts of Caphtor.

JER.47.BSB: The people of Gaza will shave their heads in mourning; Ashkelon will be silenced. O remnant of their valley, how long will you gash yourself?
JER.47.KJV: Baldness is come on Gaza; Ashkelon is cut off with the remnant of their valley: how long will you cut yourself?
JER.47.PLAIN: The people of Gaza will shave their heads in mourning; Ashkelon will be silenced. O remnant of their valley, how long will you gash yourself?

JER.47.BSB: ‘Alas, O sword of the LORD, how long until you rest? Return to your sheath; cease and be still!’
JER.47.KJV: O you sword of the LORD, how long will it be before you be quiet? put up yourself into your scabbard, rest, and be still.
JER.47.PLAIN: ‘Alas, O sword of the Lord, how long until you rest? Return to your sheath; cease and be still!’

JER.47.BSB: How can it rest when the LORD has commanded it? He has appointed it against Ashkelon and the shore of its coastland.”
JER.47.KJV: How can it be quiet, seeing the LORD has given it a charge against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore? there has he appointed it.
JER.47.PLAIN: How can it rest when the Lord has commanded it? He has appointed it against Ashkelon and the shore of its coastland.”

JER.48.BSB: Concerning Moab, this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Woe to Nebo, for it will be devastated. Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced; the fortress will be shattered and dismantled.
JER.48.KJV: Against Moab thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Woe to Nebo! for it is spoiled: Kiriathaim is confounded and taken: Misgab is confounded and dismayed.
JER.48.PLAIN: Concerning Moab, this is what the Lord of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Woe to Nebo, for it will be devastated. Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced; the fortress will be shattered and dismantled.

JER.48.BSB: There is no longer praise for Moab; in Heshbon they devise evil against her: ‘Come, let us cut her off from nationhood.’ You too, O people of Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will pursue you.
JER.48.KJV: There shall be no more praise of Moab: in Heshbon they have devised evil against it; come, and let us cut it off from being a nation. Also you shall be cut down, O Madmen; the sword shall pursue you.
JER.48.PLAIN: There is no longer praise for Moab; in Heshbon they devise evil against her: ‘Come, let us cut her off from nationhood.’ You too, O people of Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will pursue you.

JER.48.BSB: A voice cries out from Horonaim: ‘Devastation and great destruction!’
JER.48.KJV: A voice of crying shall be from Horonaim, spoiling and great destruction.
JER.48.PLAIN: A voice cries out from Horonaim: ‘Devastation and great destruction!’

JER.48.BSB: Moab will be shattered; her little ones will cry out.
JER.48.KJV: Moab is destroyed; her little ones have caused a cry to be heard.
JER.48.PLAIN: Moab will be shattered; her little ones will cry out.

JER.48.BSB: For on the ascent to Luhith they weep bitterly as they go, and on the descent to Horonaim cries of distress resound over the destruction:
JER.48.KJV: For in the going up of Luhith continual weeping shall go up; for in the going down of Horonaim the enemies have heard a cry of destruction.
JER.48.PLAIN: For on the ascent to Luhith they weep bitterly as they go, and on the descent to Horonaim cries of distress resound over the destruction:

JER.48.BSB: ‘Flee! Run for your lives! Become like a juniper in the desert.’
JER.48.KJV: Flee, save your lives, and be like the heath in the wilderness. ¶
JER.48.PLAIN: ‘Flee! Run for your lives! Become like a juniper in the desert.’

JER.48.BSB: Because you trust in your works and treasures, you too will be captured, and Chemosh will go into exile with his priests and officials.
JER.48.KJV: For because you have trusted in your works and in your treasures, you shall also be taken: and Chemosh shall go forth into captivity with his priests and his princes together.
JER.48.PLAIN: Because you trust in your works and treasures, you too will be captured, and Chemosh will go into exile with his priests and officials.

JER.48.BSB: The destroyer will move against every city, and not one town will escape. The valley will also be ruined, and the high plain will be destroyed, as the LORD has said.
JER.48.KJV: And the spoiler shall come on every city, and no city shall escape: the valley also shall perish, and the plain shall be destroyed, as the LORD has spoken.
JER.48.PLAIN: The destroyer will move against every city, and not one town will escape. The valley will also be ruined, and the high plain will be destroyed, as the Lord has said.

JER.48.BSB: Put salt on Moab, for she will be laid waste; her cities will become desolate, with no one to dwell in them.
JER.48.KJV: Give wings to Moab, that it may flee and get away: for the cities thereof shall be desolate, without any to dwell therein.
JER.48.PLAIN: Put salt on Moab, for she will be laid waste; her cities will become desolate, with no one to dwell in them.

JER.48.BSB: Cursed is the one who is remiss in doing the work of the LORD, and cursed is he who withholds his sword from bloodshed.
JER.48.KJV: Cursed be he that does the work of the LORD deceitfully, and cursed be he that keeps back his sword from blood. ¶
JER.48.PLAIN: Cursed is the one who is remiss in doing the work of the Lord, and cursed is he who withholds his sword from bloodshed.

JER.48.BSB: Moab has been at ease from youth, settled like wine on its dregs; he has not been poured from vessel to vessel or gone into exile. So his flavor has remained the same, and his aroma is unchanged.
JER.48.KJV: Moab has been at ease from his youth, and he has settled on his lees, and has not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither has he gone into captivity: therefore his taste remained in him, and his scent is not changed.
JER.48.PLAIN: Moab has been at ease from youth, settled like wine on its dregs; he has not been poured from vessel to vessel or gone into exile. So his flavor has remained the same, and his aroma is unchanged.

JER.48.BSB: Therefore behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will send to him wanderers, who will pour him out. They will empty his vessels and shatter his jars.
JER.48.KJV: Therefore, behold, the days come, says the LORD, that I will send to him wanderers, that shall cause him to wander, and shall empty his vessels, and break their bottles.
JER.48.PLAIN: Therefore look closely — the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will send to him wanderers, who will pour him out. They will empty his vessels and shatter his jars.

JER.48.BSB: Then Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, just as the house of Israel was ashamed when they trusted in Bethel.
JER.48.KJV: And Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel their confidence. ¶
JER.48.PLAIN: Then Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, just as the house of Israel was ashamed when they trusted in Bethel.

JER.48.BSB: How can you say, ‘We are warriors, mighty men ready for battle’?
JER.48.KJV: How say you, We are mighty and strong men for the war?
JER.48.PLAIN: How can you say, ‘We are warriors, mighty men ready for battle’?

JER.48.BSB: Moab has been destroyed and its towns have been invaded; the best of its young men have gone down in the slaughter, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.
JER.48.KJV: Moab is spoiled, and gone up out of her cities, and his chosen young men are gone down to the slaughter, says the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts.
JER.48.PLAIN: Moab has been destroyed and its towns have been invaded; the best of its young men have gone down in the slaughter, declares the King, whose name is the Lord of Hosts.

JER.48.BSB: Moab’s calamity is at hand, and his affliction is rushing swiftly.
JER.48.KJV: The calamity of Moab is near to come, and his affliction hastens fast.
JER.48.PLAIN: Moab’s calamity is at hand, and his affliction is rushing swiftly.

JER.48.BSB: Mourn for him, all you who surround him, everyone who knows his name; tell how the mighty scepter is shattered— the glorious staff!
JER.48.KJV: All you that are about him, bemoan him; and all you that know his name, say, How is the strong staff broken, and the beautiful rod!
JER.48.PLAIN: Mourn for him, all you who surround him, everyone who knows his name; tell how the mighty scepter is shattered— the glorious staff!

JER.48.BSB: Come down from your glory; sit on parched ground, O daughter dwelling in Dibon, for the destroyer of Moab has come against you; he has destroyed your fortresses.
JER.48.KJV: You daughter that do inhabit Dibon, come down from your glory, and sit in thirst; for the spoiler of Moab shall come on you, and he shall destroy your strong holds.
JER.48.PLAIN: Come down from your glory; sit on parched ground, O daughter dwelling in Dibon, for the destroyer of Moab has come against you; he has destroyed your fortresses.

JER.48.BSB: Stand by the road and watch, O dweller of Aroer! Ask the man fleeing or the woman escaping, ‘What has happened?’
JER.48.KJV: O inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the way, and espy; ask him that flees, and her that escapes, and say, What is done?
JER.48.PLAIN: Stand by the road and watch, O dweller of Aroer! Ask the man fleeing or the woman escaping, ‘What has happened?’

JER.48.BSB: Moab is put to shame, for it has been shattered. Wail and cry out! Declare by the Arnon that Moab is destroyed.
JER.48.KJV: Moab is confounded; for it is broken down: howl and cry; tell you it in Arnon, that Moab is spoiled,
JER.48.PLAIN: Moab is put to shame, for it has been shattered. Wail and cry out! Declare by the Arnon that Moab is destroyed.

JER.48.BSB: Judgment has come upon the high plain— upon Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath,
JER.48.KJV: And judgment is come on the plain country; on Holon, and on Jahazah, and on Mephaath,
JER.48.PLAIN: Judgment has come upon the high plain— upon Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath,

JER.48.BSB: upon Dibon, Nebo, and Beth-diblathaim,
JER.48.KJV: And on Dibon, and on Nebo, and on Bethdiblathaim,
JER.48.PLAIN: upon Dibon, Nebo, and Beth-diblathaim,

JER.48.BSB: upon Kiriathaim, Beth-gamul, and Beth-meon,
JER.48.KJV: And on Kiriathaim, and on Bethgamul, and on Bethmeon,
JER.48.PLAIN: upon Kiriathaim, Beth-gamul, and Beth-meon,

JER.48.BSB: upon Kerioth, Bozrah, and all the towns of Moab, those far and near.
JER.48.KJV: And on Kerioth, and on Bozrah, and on all the cities of the land of Moab, far or near.
JER.48.PLAIN: upon Kerioth, Bozrah, and all the towns of Moab, those far and near.

JER.48.BSB: The horn of Moab has been cut off, and his arm is broken,” declares the LORD.
JER.48.KJV: The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken, says the LORD. ¶
JER.48.PLAIN: The horn of Moab has been cut off, and his arm is broken,” declares the Lord.

JER.48.BSB: “Make him drunk, because he has magnified himself against the LORD; so Moab will wallow in his own vomit, and he will also become a laughingstock.
JER.48.KJV: Make you him drunken: for he magnified himself against the LORD: Moab also shall wallow in his vomit, and he also shall be in derision.
JER.48.PLAIN: “Make him drunk, because he has magnified himself against the Lord; so Moab will wallow in his own vomit, and he will also become a laughingstock.

JER.48.BSB: Was not Israel your object of ridicule? Was he ever found among thieves? For whenever you speak of him you shake your head.
JER.48.KJV: For was not Israel a derision to you? was he found among thieves? for since you spoke of him, you skipped for joy.
JER.48.PLAIN: Was not Israel your object of ridicule? Was he ever found among thieves? For whenever you speak of him you shake your head.

JER.48.BSB: Abandon the towns and settle among the rocks, O dwellers of Moab! Be like a dove that nests at the mouth of a cave.
JER.48.KJV: O you that dwell in Moab, leave the cities, and dwell in the rock, and be like the dove that makes her nest in the sides of the hole’s mouth.
JER.48.PLAIN: Abandon the towns and settle among the rocks, O dwellers of Moab! Be like a dove that nests at the mouth of a cave.

JER.48.BSB: We have heard of Moab’s pomposity, his exceeding pride and conceit, his proud arrogance and haughtiness of heart.
JER.48.KJV: We have heard the pride of Moab, (he is exceeding proud) his loftiness, and his arrogance, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart.
JER.48.PLAIN: We have heard of Moab’s pomposity, his exceeding pride and conceit, his proud arrogance and haughtiness of heart.

JER.48.BSB: I know his insolence,” declares the LORD, “but it is futile. His boasting is as empty as his deeds.
JER.48.KJV: I know his wrath, says the LORD; but it shall not be so; his lies shall not so effect it.
JER.48.PLAIN: I know his insolence,” declares the Lord, “but it is futile. His boasting is as empty as his deeds.

JER.48.BSB: Therefore I will wail for Moab; I will cry out for all of Moab; I will moan for the men of Kir-heres.
JER.48.KJV: Therefore will I howl for Moab, and I will cry out for all Moab; my heart shall mourn for the men of Kirheres.
JER.48.PLAIN: Therefore I will wail for Moab; I will cry out for all of Moab; I will moan for the men of Kir-heres.

JER.48.BSB: I will weep for you, O vine of Sibmah, more than I weep for Jazer. Your tendrils have extended to the sea; they reach even to Jazer. The destroyer has descended on your summer fruit and grape harvest.
JER.48.KJV: O vine of Sibmah, I will weep for you with the weeping of Jazer: your plants are gone over the sea, they reach even to the sea of Jazer: the spoiler is fallen on your summer fruits and on your vintage.
JER.48.PLAIN: I will weep for you, O vine of Sibmah, more than I weep for Jazer. Your tendrils have extended to the sea; they reach even to Jazer. The destroyer has descended on your summer fruit and grape harvest.

JER.48.BSB: Joy and gladness are removed from the orchard and from the fields of Moab. I have stopped the flow of wine from the presses; no one treads them with shouts of joy; their shouts are not for joy.
JER.48.KJV: And joy and gladness is taken from the plentiful field, and from the land of Moab, and I have caused wine to fail from the winepresses: none shall tread with shouting; their shouting shall be no shouting.
JER.48.PLAIN: Joy and gladness are removed from the orchard and from the fields of Moab. I have stopped the flow of wine from the presses; no one treads them with shouts of joy; their shouts are not for joy.

JER.48.BSB: There is a cry from Heshbon to Elealeh; they raise their voices to Jahaz, from Zoar to Horonaim and Eglath-shelishiyah; for even the waters of Nimrim have dried up.
JER.48.KJV: From the cry of Heshbon even to Elealeh, and even to Jahaz, have they uttered their voice, from Zoar even to Horonaim, as an heifer of three years old: for the waters also of Nimrim shall be desolate.
JER.48.PLAIN: There is a cry from Heshbon to Elealeh; they raise their voices to Jahaz, from Zoar to Horonaim and Eglath-shelishiyah; for even the waters of Nimrim have dried up.

JER.48.BSB: In Moab, declares the LORD, I will bring an end to those who make offerings on the high places and burn incense to their gods.
JER.48.KJV: Moreover I will cause to cease in Moab, says the LORD, him that offers in the high places, and him that burns incense to his gods.
JER.48.PLAIN: In Moab, declares the Lord, I will bring an end to those who make offerings on the high places and burn incense to their gods.

JER.48.BSB: Therefore My heart laments like a flute for Moab; it laments like a flute for the men of Kir-heres, because the wealth they acquired has perished.
JER.48.KJV: Therefore my heart shall sound for Moab like pipes, and my heart shall sound like pipes for the men of Kirheres: because the riches that he has gotten are perished.
JER.48.PLAIN: Therefore My heart laments like a flute for Moab; it laments like a flute for the men of Kir-heres, because the wealth they acquired has perished.

JER.48.BSB: For every head is shaved and every beard is clipped; on every hand is a gash, and around every waist is sackcloth.
JER.48.KJV: For every head shall be bald, and every beard clipped: on all the hands shall be cuttings, and on the loins sackcloth.
JER.48.PLAIN: For every head is shaved and every beard is clipped; on every hand is a gash, and around every waist is sackcloth.

JER.48.BSB: On all the rooftops of Moab and in the public squares, everyone is mourning; for I have shattered Moab like an unwanted jar,” declares the LORD.
JER.48.KJV: There shall be lamentation generally on all the housetops of Moab, and in the streets thereof: for I have broken Moab like a vessel wherein is no pleasure, says the LORD.
JER.48.PLAIN: On all the rooftops of Moab and in the public squares, everyone is mourning; for I have shattered Moab like an unwanted jar,” declares the Lord.

JER.48.BSB: “How shattered it is! How they wail! How Moab has turned his back in shame! Moab has become an object of ridicule and horror to all those around him.”
JER.48.KJV: They shall howl, saying, How is it broken down! how has Moab turned the back with shame! so shall Moab be a derision and a dismaying to all them about him.
JER.48.PLAIN: “How shattered it is! How they wail! How Moab has turned his back in shame! Moab has become an object of ridicule and horror to all those around him.”

JER.48.BSB: For this is what the LORD says: “Behold, an eagle swoops down and spreads his wings against Moab.
JER.48.KJV: For thus says the LORD; Behold, he shall fly as an eagle, and shall spread his wings over Moab.
JER.48.PLAIN: For this is what the Lord says: “Look closely — an eagle swoops down and spreads his wings against Moab.

JER.48.BSB: Kirioth has been taken, and the strongholds seized. In that day the heart of Moab’s warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
JER.48.KJV: Kerioth is taken, and the strong holds are surprised, and the mighty men’s hearts in Moab at that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.
JER.48.PLAIN: Kirioth has been taken, and the strongholds seized. In that day the heart of Moab’s warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.

JER.48.BSB: Moab will be destroyed as a nation because he vaunted himself against the LORD.
JER.48.KJV: And Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he has magnified himself against the LORD.
JER.48.PLAIN: Moab will be destroyed as a nation because he vaunted himself against the Lord.

JER.48.BSB: Terror and pit and snare await you, O dweller of Moab,” declares the LORD.
JER.48.KJV: Fear, and the pit, and the snare, shall be on you, O inhabitant of Moab, says the LORD.
JER.48.PLAIN: Terror and pit and snare await you, O dweller of Moab,” declares the Lord.

JER.48.BSB: “Whoever flees the panic will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs from the pit will be caught in the snare. For I will bring upon Moab the year of their punishment,” declares the LORD.
JER.48.KJV: He that flees from the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that gets up out of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for I will bring on it, even on Moab, the year of their visitation, says the LORD.
JER.48.PLAIN: “Whoever flees the panic will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs from the pit will be caught in the snare. For I will bring upon Moab the year of their punishment,” declares the Lord.

JER.48.BSB: “Those who flee will stand helpless in Heshbon’s shadow, because fire has gone forth from Heshbon and a flame from within Sihon. It devours the foreheads of Moab and the skulls of the sons of tumult.
JER.48.KJV: They that fled stood under the shadow of Heshbon because of the force: but a fire shall come forth out of Heshbon, and a flame from the middle of Sihon, and shall devour the corner of Moab, and the crown of the head of the tumultuous ones.
JER.48.PLAIN: “Those who flee will stand helpless in Heshbon’s shadow, because fire has gone forth from Heshbon and a flame from within Sihon. It devours the foreheads of Moab and the skulls of the sons of tumult.

JER.48.BSB: Woe to you, O Moab! The people of Chemosh have perished; for your sons have been taken into exile and your daughters have gone into captivity.
JER.48.KJV: Woe be to you, O Moab! the people of Chemosh perishes: for your sons are taken captives, and your daughters captives. ¶
JER.48.PLAIN: Woe to you, O Moab! The people of Chemosh have perished; for your sons have been taken into exile and your daughters have gone into captivity.

JER.48.BSB: Yet in the latter days I will restore Moab from captivity,” declares the LORD. Here ends the judgment on Moab.
JER.48.KJV: Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days, says the LORD. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.
JER.48.PLAIN: Yet in the latter days I will restore Moab from captivity,” declares the Lord. Here ends the judgment on Moab.

JER.49.BSB: Concerning the Ammonites, this is what the LORD says: “Has Israel no sons? Is he without heir? Why then has Milcom taken possession of Gad? Why have his people settled in their cities?
JER.49.KJV: Concerning the Ammonites, thus says the LORD; Has Israel no sons? has he no heir? why then does their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?
JER.49.PLAIN: Concerning the Ammonites, this is what the Lord says: “Has Israel no sons? Is he without heir? Why then has Milcom taken possession of Gad? Why have his people settled in their cities?

JER.49.BSB: Therefore, behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will sound the battle cry against Rabbah of the Ammonites. It will become a heap of ruins, and its villages will be burned. Then Israel will drive out their dispossessors, says the LORD.
JER.49.KJV: Therefore, behold, the days come, says the LORD, that I will cause an alarm of war to be heard in Rabbah of the Ammonites; and it shall be a desolate heap, and her daughters shall be burned with fire: then shall Israel be heir to them that were his heirs, said the LORD.
JER.49.PLAIN: Therefore, look closely — the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will sound the battle cry against Rabbah of the Ammonites. It will become a heap of ruins, and its villages will be burned. Then Israel will drive out their dispossessors, says the Lord.

JER.49.BSB: Wail, O Heshbon, for Ai has been destroyed; cry out, O daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth and mourn; run back and forth within your walls, for Milcom will go into exile together with his priests and officials.
JER.49.KJV: Howl, O Heshbon, for Ai is spoiled: cry, you daughters of Rabbah, gird you with sackcloth; lament, and run to and fro by the hedges; for their king shall go into captivity, and his priests and his princes together.
JER.49.PLAIN: Wail, O Heshbon, for Ai has been destroyed; cry out, O daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth and mourn; run back and forth within your walls, for Milcom will go into exile together with his priests and officials.

JER.49.BSB: Why do you boast of your valleys— your valleys so fruitful, O faithless daughter? You trust in your riches and say, ‘Who can come against me?’
JER.49.KJV: Why glory you in the valleys, your flowing valley, O backsliding daughter? that trusted in her treasures, saying, Who shall come to me?
JER.49.PLAIN: Why do you boast of your valleys— your valleys so fruitful, O faithless daughter? You trust in your riches and say, ‘Who can come against me?’

JER.49.BSB: Behold, I am about to bring terror upon you, declares the Lord GOD of Hosts, from all those around you. You will each be driven headlong, with no one to regather the fugitives.
JER.49.KJV: Behold, I will bring a fear on you, says the Lord GOD of hosts, from all those that be about you; and you shall be driven out every man right forth; and none shall gather up him that wanders.
JER.49.PLAIN: Look closely — I am about to bring terror upon you, declares the Lord GOD of Hosts, from all those around you. You will each be driven headlong, with no one to regather the fugitives.

JER.49.BSB: Yet afterward I will restore the Ammonites from captivity,” declares the LORD.
JER.49.KJV: And afterward I will bring again the captivity of the children of Ammon, says the LORD. ¶
JER.49.PLAIN: Yet afterward I will restore the Ammonites from captivity,” declares the Lord.

JER.49.BSB: Concerning Edom, this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Is there no longer wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom decayed?
JER.49.KJV: Concerning Edom, thus says the LORD of hosts; Is wisdom no more in Teman? is counsel perished from the prudent? is their wisdom vanished?
JER.49.PLAIN: Concerning Edom, this is what the Lord of Hosts says: “Is there no longer wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom decayed?

JER.49.BSB: Turn and run! Lie low, O dwellers of Dedan, for I will bring disaster on Esau at the time I punish him.
JER.49.KJV: Flee you, turn back, dwell deep, O inhabitants of Dedan; for I will bring the calamity of Esau on him, the time that I will visit him.
JER.49.PLAIN: Turn and run! Lie low, O dwellers of Dedan, for I will bring disaster on Esau at the time I punish him.

JER.49.BSB: If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleanings? Were thieves to come in the night, would they not steal only what they wanted?
JER.49.KJV: If grape gatherers come to you, would they not leave some gleaning grapes? if thieves by night, they will destroy till they have enough.
JER.49.PLAIN: If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleanings? Were thieves to come in the night, would they not steal only what they wanted?

JER.49.BSB: But I will strip Esau bare; I will uncover his hiding places, and he will be unable to conceal himself. His descendants will be destroyed along with his relatives and neighbors, and he will be no more.
JER.49.KJV: But I have made Esau bore, I have uncovered his secret places, and he shall not be able to hide himself: his seed is spoiled, and his brothers, and his neighbors, and he is not.
JER.49.PLAIN: But I will strip Esau bare; I will uncover his hiding places, and he will be unable to conceal himself. His descendants will be destroyed along with his relatives and neighbors, and he will be no more.

JER.49.BSB: Abandon your orphans; I will preserve their lives. Let your widows trust in Me.”
JER.49.KJV: Leave your fatherless children, I will preserve them alive; and let your widows trust in me.
JER.49.PLAIN: Abandon your orphans; I will preserve their lives. Let your widows trust in Me.”

JER.49.BSB: For this is what the LORD says: “If those who do not deserve to drink the cup must drink it, can you possibly remain unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for you must drink it too.
JER.49.KJV: For thus says the LORD; Behold, they whose judgment was not to drink of the cup have assuredly drunken; and are you he that shall altogether go unpunished? you shall not go unpunished, but you shall surely drink of it.
JER.49.PLAIN: For this is what the Lord says: “If those who do not deserve to drink the cup must drink it, can you possibly remain unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for you must drink it too.

JER.49.BSB: For by Myself I have sworn, declares the LORD, that Bozrah will become a desolation, a disgrace, a ruin, and a curse, and all her cities will be in ruins forever.”
JER.49.KJV: For I have sworn by myself, says the LORD, that Bozrah shall become a desolation, a reproach, a waste, and a curse; and all the cities thereof shall be perpetual wastes.
JER.49.PLAIN: For by Myself I have sworn, declares the Lord, that Bozrah will become a desolation, a disgrace, a ruin, and a curse, and all her cities will be in ruins forever.”

JER.49.BSB: I have heard a message from the LORD; an envoy has been sent to the nations: “Assemble yourselves to march against her! Rise up for battle!”
JER.49.KJV: I have heard a rumor from the LORD, and an ambassador is sent to the heathen, saying, Gather you together, and come against her, and rise up to the battle.
JER.49.PLAIN: I have heard a message from the Lord; an envoy has been sent to the nations: “Assemble yourselves to march against her! Rise up for battle!”

JER.49.BSB: “For behold, I will make you small among nations, despised among men.
JER.49.KJV: For, see, I will make you small among the heathen, and despised among men.
JER.49.PLAIN: “For look closely — I will make you small among nations, despised among men.

JER.49.BSB: The terror you cause and the pride of your heart have deceived you, O dwellers in the clefts of the rocks, O occupiers of the mountain summit. Though you elevate your nest like the eagle, even from there I will bring you down,” declares the LORD.
JER.49.KJV: Your terribleness has deceived you, and the pride of your heart, O you that dwell in the clefts of the rock, that hold the height of the hill: though you should make your nest as high as the eagle, I will bring you down from there, says the LORD.
JER.49.PLAIN: The terror you cause and the pride of your heart have deceived you, O dwellers in the clefts of the rocks, O occupiers of the mountain summit. Though you elevate your nest like the eagle, even from there I will bring you down,” declares the Lord.

JER.49.BSB: “Edom will become an object of horror. All who pass by will be appalled and will scoff at all her wounds.
JER.49.KJV: Also Edom shall be a desolation: every one that goes by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss at all the plagues thereof.
JER.49.PLAIN: “Edom will become an object of horror. All who pass by will be appalled and will scoff at all her wounds.

JER.49.BSB: As Sodom and Gomorrah were overthrown along with their neighbors,” says the LORD, “no one will dwell there; no man will abide there.
JER.49.KJV: As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbor cities thereof, says the LORD, no man shall abide there, neither shall a son of man dwell in it.
JER.49.PLAIN: As Sodom and Gomorrah were overthrown along with their neighbors,” says the Lord, “no one will dwell there; no man will abide there.

JER.49.BSB: Behold, one will come up like a lion from the thickets of the Jordan to the watered pasture. For in an instant I will chase Edom from her land. Who is the chosen one I will appoint for this? For who is like Me, and who can challenge Me? What shepherd can stand against Me?”
JER.49.KJV: Behold, he shall come up like a lion from the swelling of Jordan against the habitation of the strong: but I will suddenly make him run away from her: and who is a chosen man, that I may appoint over her? for who is like me? and who will appoint me the time? and who is that shepherd that will stand before me?
JER.49.PLAIN: Look closely — one will come up like a lion from the thickets of the Jordan to the watered pasture. For in an instant I will chase Edom from her land. Who is the chosen one I will appoint for this? For who is like Me, and who can challenge Me? What shepherd can stand against Me?”

JER.49.BSB: Therefore hear the plans that the LORD has drawn up against Edom and the strategies He has devised against the people of Teman: Surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; certainly their pasture will be made desolate because of them.
JER.49.KJV: Therefore hear the counsel of the LORD, that he has taken against Edom; and his purposes, that he has purposed against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out: surely he shall make their habitations desolate with them.
JER.49.PLAIN: Therefore hear the plans that the Lord has drawn up against Edom and the strategies He has devised against the people of Teman: Surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; certainly their pasture will be made desolate because of them.

JER.49.BSB: At the sound of their fall the earth will quake; their cry will resound to the Red Sea.
JER.49.KJV: The earth is moved at the noise of their fall, at the cry the noise thereof was heard in the Red sea.
JER.49.PLAIN: At the sound of their fall the earth will quake; their cry will resound to the Red Sea.

JER.49.BSB: Look! An eagle will soar and swoop down, spreading its wings over Bozrah. In that day the hearts of Edom’s mighty men will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
JER.49.KJV: Behold, he shall come up and fly as the eagle, and spread his wings over Bozrah: and at that day shall the heart of the mighty men of Edom be as the heart of a woman in her pangs. ¶

JER.51.PLAIN: For the Lord will destroy Babylon; He will silence her mighty voice. The waves will roar like great waters; the tumult of their voices will resound.

JER.51.BSB: For a destroyer is coming against her— against Babylon. Her warriors will be captured, and their bows will be broken, for the LORD is a God of retribution; He will repay in full.
JER.51.KJV: Because the spoiler is come on her, even on Babylon, and her mighty men are taken, every one of their bows is broken: for the LORD God of recompenses shall surely requite.
JER.51.PLAIN: For a destroyer is coming against her— against Babylon. Her warriors will be captured, and their bows will be broken, for the Lord is a God of retribution; He will repay in full.

JER.51.BSB: I will make her princes and wise men drunk, along with her governors, officials, and warriors. Then they will fall asleep forever and not wake up,” declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.
JER.51.KJV: And I will make drunk her princes, and her wise men, her captains, and her rulers, and her mighty men: and they shall sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake, says the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts.
JER.51.PLAIN: I will make her princes and wise men drunk, along with her governors, officials, and warriors. Then they will fall asleep forever and not wake up,” declares the King, whose name is the Lord of Hosts.

JER.51.BSB: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Babylon’s thick walls will be leveled, and her high gates consumed by fire. So the labor of the people will be for nothing; the nations will exhaust themselves to fuel the flames.”
JER.51.KJV: Thus says the LORD of hosts; The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly broken, and her high gates shall be burned with fire; and the people shall labor in vain, and the folk in the fire, and they shall be weary. ¶
JER.51.PLAIN: This is what the Lord of Hosts says: “Babylon’s thick walls will be leveled, and her high gates consumed by fire. So the labor of the people will be for nothing; the nations will exhaust themselves to fuel the flames.”

JER.51.BSB: This is the message that Jeremiah the prophet gave to the quartermaster Seraiah son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, when he went to Babylon with King Zedekiah of Judah in the fourth year of Zedekiah’s reign.
JER.51.KJV: The word which Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah, when he went with Zedekiah the king of Judah into Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. And this Seraiah was a quiet prince.
JER.51.PLAIN: This is the message that Jeremiah the prophet gave to the quartermaster Seraiah son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, when he went to Babylon with King Zedekiah of Judah in the fourth year of Zedekiah’s reign.

JER.51.BSB: Jeremiah had written on a single scroll about all the disaster that would come upon Babylon—all these words that had been written concerning Babylon.
JER.51.KJV: So Jeremiah wrote in a book all the evil that should come on Babylon, even all these words that are written against Babylon.
JER.51.PLAIN: Jeremiah had written on a single scroll about all the disaster that would come upon Babylon—all these words that had been written concerning Babylon.

JER.51.BSB: And Jeremiah said to Seraiah, “When you get to Babylon, see that you read all these words aloud,
JER.51.KJV: And Jeremiah said to Seraiah, When you come to Babylon, and shall see, and shall read all these words;
JER.51.PLAIN: And Jeremiah said to Seraiah, “When you get to Babylon, see that you read all these words aloud,

JER.51.BSB: and say, ‘O LORD, You have promised to cut off this place so that no one will remain—neither man nor beast. Indeed, it will be desolate forever.’
JER.51.KJV: Then shall you say, O LORD, you have spoken against this place, to cut it off, that none shall remain in it, neither man nor beast, but that it shall be desolate for ever.
JER.51.PLAIN: and say, ‘O Lord, You have promised to cut off this place so that no one will remain—neither man nor beast. Indeed, it will be desolate forever.’

JER.51.BSB: When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and cast it into the Euphrates.
JER.51.KJV: And it shall be, when you have made an end of reading this book, that you shall bind a stone to it, and cast it into the middle of Euphrates:
JER.51.PLAIN: When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and cast it into the Euphrates.

JER.51.BSB: Then you are to say, ‘In the same way Babylon will sink and never rise again, because of the disaster I will bring upon her. And her people will grow weary.’” Here end the words of Jeremiah.
JER.51.KJV: And you shall say, Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise from the evil that I will bring on her: and they shall be weary. Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.
JER.51.PLAIN: Then you are to say, ‘In the same way Babylon will sink and never rise again, because of the disaster I will bring upon her. And her people will grow weary.’” Here end the words of Jeremiah.

JER.52.BSB: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah; she was from Libnah.
JER.52.KJV: Zedekiah was one and twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
JER.52.PLAIN: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah; she was from Libnah.

JER.52.BSB: And Zedekiah did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done.
JER.52.KJV: And he did that which was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
JER.52.PLAIN: And Zedekiah did evil in the sight of the Lord, just as Jehoiakim had done.

JER.52.BSB: For because of the anger of the LORD, all this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until He finally banished them from His presence. And Zedekiah also rebelled against the king of Babylon.
JER.52.KJV: For through the anger of the LORD it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, till he had cast them out from his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon. ¶
JER.52.PLAIN: For because of the anger of the Lord, all this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until He finally banished them from His presence. And Zedekiah also rebelled against the king of Babylon.

JER.52.BSB: So in the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against Jerusalem with his entire army. They encamped outside the city and built a siege wall all around it.
JER.52.KJV: And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and pitched against it, and built forts against it round about.
JER.52.PLAIN: So in the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against Jerusalem with his entire army. They encamped outside the city and built a siege wall all around it.

JER.52.BSB: And the city was kept under siege until King Zedekiah’s eleventh year.
JER.52.KJV: So the city was besieged to the eleventh year of king Zedekiah.
JER.52.PLAIN: And the city was kept under siege until King Zedekiah’s eleventh year.

JER.52.BSB: By the ninth day of the fourth month, the famine in the city was so severe that the people of the land had no food.
JER.52.KJV: And in the fourth month, in the ninth day of the month, the famine was sore in the city, so that there was no bread for the people of the land.
JER.52.PLAIN: By the ninth day of the fourth month, the famine in the city was so severe that the people of the land had no food.

JER.52.BSB: Then the city was breached; and though the Chaldeans had surrounded the city, all the men of war fled the city by night by way of the gate between the two walls near the king’s garden. They headed toward the Arabah,
JER.52.KJV: Then the city was broken up, and all the men of war fled, and went forth out of the city by night by the way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king’s garden; (now the Chaldeans were by the city round about:) and they went by the way of the plain. ¶
JER.52.PLAIN: Then the city was breached; and though the Chaldeans had surrounded the city, all the men of war fled the city by night by way of the gate between the two walls near the king’s garden. They headed toward the Arabah,

JER.52.BSB: but the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was separated from him.
JER.52.KJV: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.
JER.52.PLAIN: but the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was separated from him.

JER.52.BSB: The Chaldeans seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced judgment on Zedekiah.
JER.52.KJV: Then they took the king, and carried him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath; where he gave judgment on him.
JER.52.PLAIN: The Chaldeans seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced judgment on Zedekiah.

JER.52.BSB: There at Riblah the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and he also killed all the officials of Judah.
JER.52.KJV: And the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes: he slew also all the princes of Judah in Riblah.
JER.52.PLAIN: There at Riblah the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and he also killed all the officials of Judah.

JER.52.BSB: Then he put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon, where he kept him in custody until his dying day.
JER.52.KJV: Then he put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in chains, and carried him to Babylon, and put him in prison till the day of his death. ¶
JER.52.PLAIN: Then he put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon, where he kept him in custody until his dying day.

JER.52.BSB: On the tenth day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign over Babylon, Nebuzaradan captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, entered Jerusalem.
JER.52.KJV: Now in the fifth month, in the tenth day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, came Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, which served the king of Babylon, into Jerusalem,
JER.52.PLAIN: On the tenth day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign over Babylon, Nebuzaradan captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, entered Jerusalem.

JER.52.BSB: He burned down the house of the LORD, the royal palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem—every significant building.
JER.52.KJV: And burned the house of the LORD, and the king’s house; and all the houses of Jerusalem, and all the houses of the great men, burned he with fire:
JER.52.PLAIN: He burned down the house of the Lord, the royal palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem—every significant building.

JER.52.BSB: And the whole army of the Chaldeans under the captain of the guard broke down all the walls around Jerusalem.
JER.52.KJV: And all the army of the Chaldeans, that were with the captain of the guard, broke down all the walls of Jerusalem round about.
JER.52.PLAIN: And the whole army of the Chaldeans under the captain of the guard broke down all the walls around Jerusalem.

JER.52.BSB: Then Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried into exile some of the poorest people and those who remained in the city, along with the deserters who had defected to the king of Babylon and the rest of the craftsmen.
JER.52.KJV: Then Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive certain of the poor of the people, and the residue of the people that remained in the city, and those that fell away, that fell to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude.
JER.52.PLAIN: Then Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried into exile some of the poorest people and those who remained in the city, along with the deserters who had defected to the king of Babylon and the rest of the craftsmen.

JER.52.BSB: But Nebuzaradan captain of the guard left behind some of the poorest of the land to tend the vineyards and fields.
JER.52.KJV: But Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left certain of the poor of the land for vinedressers and for farmers.
JER.52.PLAIN: But Nebuzaradan captain of the guard left behind some of the poorest of the land to tend the vineyards and fields.

JER.52.BSB: Moreover, the Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars and stands and the bronze Sea in the house of the LORD, and they carried all the bronze to Babylon.
JER.52.KJV: Also the pillars of brass that were in the house of the LORD, and the bases, and the brazen sea that was in the house of the LORD, the Chaldeans broke, and carried all the brass of them to Babylon.
JER.52.PLAIN: Moreover, the Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars and stands and the bronze Sea in the house of the Lord, and they carried all the bronze to Babylon.

JER.52.BSB: They also took away the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes, and all the articles of bronze used in the temple service.
JER.52.KJV: The caldrons also, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the bowls, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass with which they ministered, took they away.
JER.52.PLAIN: They also took away the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes, and all the articles of bronze used in the temple service.

JER.52.BSB: The captain of the guard also took away the basins, censers, sprinkling bowls, pots, lampstands, pans, and drink offering bowls—anything made of pure gold or fine silver.
JER.52.KJV: And the basins, and the fire pans, and the bowls, and the caldrons, and the candlesticks, and the spoons, and the cups; that which was of gold in gold, and that which was of silver in silver, took the captain of the guard away.
JER.52.PLAIN: The captain of the guard also took away the basins, censers, sprinkling bowls, pots, lampstands, pans, and drink offering bowls—anything made of pure gold or fine silver.

JER.52.BSB: As for the two pillars, the Sea, the twelve bronze bulls under it, and the movable stands that King Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, the weight of the bronze from all these articles was beyond measure.
JER.52.KJV: The two pillars, one sea, and twelve brazen bulls that were under the bases, which king Solomon had made in the house of the LORD: the brass of all these vessels was without weight.
JER.52.PLAIN: As for the two pillars, the Sea, the twelve bronze bulls under it, and the movable stands that King Solomon had made for the house of the Lord, the weight of the bronze from all these articles was beyond measure.

JER.52.BSB: Each pillar was eighteen cubits tall and twelve cubits in circumference; each was hollow, four fingers thick.
JER.52.KJV: And concerning the pillars, the height of one pillar was eighteen cubits; and a fillet of twelve cubits did compass it; and the thickness thereof was four fingers: it was hollow.
JER.52.PLAIN: Each pillar was eighteen cubits tall and twelve cubits in circumference; each was hollow, four fingers thick.

JER.52.BSB: The bronze capital atop one pillar was five cubits high, with a network of bronze pomegranates all around. The second pillar, with its pomegranates, was similar.
JER.52.KJV: And a capital of brass was on it; and the height of one capital was five cubits, with network and pomegranates on the capitals round about, all of brass. The second pillar also and the pomegranates were like to these.
JER.52.PLAIN: The bronze capital atop one pillar was five cubits high, with a network of bronze pomegranates all around. The second pillar, with its pomegranates, was similar.

JER.52.BSB: Each capital had ninety-six pomegranates on the sides, and a total of a hundred pomegranates were above the surrounding network.
JER.52.KJV: And there were ninety and six pomegranates on a side; and all the pomegranates on the network were an hundred round about. ¶
JER.52.PLAIN: Each capital had ninety-six pomegranates on the sides, and a total of a hundred pomegranates were above the surrounding network.

JER.52.BSB: The captain of the guard also took away Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest of second rank, and the three doorkeepers.
JER.52.KJV: And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door:
JER.52.PLAIN: The captain of the guard also took away Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest of second rank, and the three doorkeepers.

JER.52.BSB: Of those still in the city, he took a court official who had been appointed over the men of war, as well as seven trusted royal advisers. He also took the scribe of the captain of the army, who had enlisted the people of the land, and sixty men who were found in the city.
JER.52.KJV: He took also out of the city an eunuch, which had the charge of the men of war; and seven men of them that were near the king’s person, which were found in the city; and the principal scribe of the host, who mustered the people of the land; and three score men of the people of the land, that were found in the middle of the city.
JER.52.PLAIN: Of those still in the city, he took a court official who had been appointed over the men of war, as well as seven trusted royal advisers. He also took the scribe of the captain of the army, who had enlisted the people of the land, and sixty men who were found in the city.

JER.52.BSB: Nebuzaradan captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
JER.52.KJV: So Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah.
JER.52.PLAIN: Nebuzaradan captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

JER.52.BSB: There at Riblah in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death. So Judah was taken into exile, away from its own land.
JER.52.KJV: And the king of Babylon smote them, and put them to death in Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was carried away captive out of his own land.
JER.52.PLAIN: There at Riblah in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death. So Judah was taken into exile, away from its own land.

JER.52.BSB: These are the people Nebuchadnezzar carried away: in the seventh year, 3,023 Jews;
JER.52.KJV: This is the people whom Nebuchadrezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year three thousand Jews and three and twenty:
JER.52.PLAIN: These are the people Nebuchadnezzar carried away: in the seventh year, 3,023 Jews;

JER.52.BSB: in Nebuchadnezzar’s eighteenth year, 832 people from Jerusalem;
JER.52.KJV: In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar he carried away captive from Jerusalem eight hundred thirty and two persons:
JER.52.PLAIN: in Nebuchadnezzar’s eighteenth year, 832 people from Jerusalem;

JER.52.BSB: in Nebuchadnezzar’s twenty-third year, Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried away 745 Jews. So in all, 4,600 people were taken away.
JER.52.KJV: In the three and twentieth year of Nebuchadrezzar Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive of the Jews seven hundred forty and five persons: all the persons were four thousand and six hundred. ¶
JER.52.PLAIN: in Nebuchadnezzar’s twenty-third year, Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried away 745 Jews. So in all, 4,600 people were taken away.

JER.52.BSB: On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month of the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the first year of the reign of Evil-merodach king of Babylon, he pardoned Jehoiachin king of Judah and released him from prison.
JER.52.KJV: And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, in the five and twentieth day of the month, that Evilmerodach king of Babylon in the first year of his reign lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and brought him forth out of prison.
JER.52.PLAIN: On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month of the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the first year of the reign of Evil-merodach king of Babylon, he pardoned Jehoiachin king of Judah and released him from prison.

JER.52.BSB: And he spoke kindly to Jehoiachin and set his throne above the thrones of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
JER.52.KJV: And spoke kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon,
JER.52.PLAIN: And he spoke kindly to Jehoiachin and set his throne above the thrones of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.

JER.52.BSB: So Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes, and he dined regularly at the king’s table for the rest of his life.
JER.52.KJV: And changed his prison garments: and he did continually eat bread before him all the days of his life.
JER.52.PLAIN: So Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes, and he dined regularly at the king’s table for the rest of his life.

JER.52.BSB: And the king of Babylon provided Jehoiachin a daily portion for the rest of his life, until the day of his death.
JER.52.KJV: And for his diet, there was a continual diet given him of the king of Babylon, every day a portion until the day of his death, all the days of his life.
JER.52.PLAIN: And the king of Babylon provided Jehoiachin a daily portion for the rest of his life, until the day of his death.

LAM.1.BSB: How lonely lies the city, once so full of people! She who was great among the nations has become a widow. The princess of the provinces has become a slave.
LAM.1.KJV: How does the city sit solitary, that was full of people! how is she become as a widow! she that was great among the nations, and princess among the provinces, how is she become tributary!
LAM.1.PLAIN: How lonely lies the city, once so full of people! She who was great among the nations has become a widow. The princess of the provinces has become a slave.

LAM.1.BSB: She weeps aloud in the night, with tears upon her cheeks. Among all her lovers there is no one to comfort her. All her friends have betrayed her; they have become her enemies.
LAM.1.KJV: She weeps sore in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks: among all her lovers she has none to comfort her: all her friends have dealt treacherously with her, they are become her enemies.
LAM.1.PLAIN: She weeps aloud in the night, with tears upon her cheeks. Among all her lovers there is no one to comfort her. All her friends have betrayed her; they have become her enemies.

LAM.1.BSB: Judah has gone into exile under affliction and harsh slavery; she dwells among the nations but finds no place to rest. All her pursuers have overtaken her in the midst of her distress.
LAM.1.KJV: Judah is gone into captivity because of affliction, and because of great servitude: she dwells among the heathen, she finds no rest: all her persecutors overtook her between the straits.
LAM.1.PLAIN: Judah has gone into exile under affliction and harsh slavery; she dwells among the nations but finds no place to rest. All her pursuers have overtaken her in the midst of her distress.

LAM.1.BSB: The roads to Zion mourn, because no one comes to her appointed feasts. All her gates are deserted; her priests groan, her maidens grieve, and she herself is bitter with anguish.
LAM.1.KJV: The ways of Zion do mourn, because none come to the solemn feasts: all her gates are desolate: her priests sigh, her virgins are afflicted, and she is in bitterness.
LAM.1.PLAIN: The roads to Zion mourn, because no one comes to her appointed feasts. All her gates are deserted; her priests groan, her maidens grieve, and she herself is bitter with anguish.
