EZK.3.BSB: If I say to the wicked man, ‘You will surely die,’ but you do not warn him or speak out to warn him from his wicked way to save his life, that wicked man will die in his iniquity, and I will hold you responsible for his blood.
EZK.3.KJV: When I say to the wicked, You shall surely die; and you give him not warning, nor speak to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life; the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at your hand.
EZK.3.PLAIN: If I say to the wicked man, ‘You will surely die,’ but you do not warn him or speak out to warn him from his wicked way to save his life, that wicked man will die in his brokenness, and I will hold you responsible for his blood.

EZK.3.BSB: But if you warn a wicked man and he does not turn from his wickedness and his wicked way, he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved yourself.
EZK.3.KJV: Yet if you warn the wicked, and he turn not from his wickedness, nor from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquity; but you have delivered your soul.
EZK.3.PLAIN: But if you warn a wicked man and he does not turn from his wickedness and his wicked way, he will die in his brokenness, but you will have saved yourself.

EZK.3.BSB: Now if a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and I put a stumbling block before him, he will die. If you did not warn him, he will die in his sin, and the righteous acts he did will not be remembered. And I will hold you responsible for his blood.
EZK.3.KJV: Again, When a righteous man does turn from his righteousness, and commit iniquity, and I lay a stumbling-block before him, he shall die: because you have not given him warning, he shall die in his sin, and his righteousness which he has done shall not be remembered; but his blood will I require at your hand.
EZK.3.PLAIN: Now if a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits brokenness, and I put a stumbling block before him, he will die. If you did not warn him, he will die in his sin, and the righteous acts he did will not be remembered. And I will hold you responsible for his blood.

EZK.3.BSB: But if you warn the righteous man not to sin, and he does not sin, he will indeed live because he heeded your warning, and you will have saved yourself.”
EZK.3.KJV: Nevertheless if you warn the righteous man, that the righteous sin not, and he does not sin, he shall surely live, because he is warned; also you have delivered your soul. ¶
EZK.3.PLAIN: But if you warn the righteous man not to sin, and he does not sin, he will indeed live because he heeded your warning, and you will have saved yourself.”

EZK.3.BSB: And there the hand of the LORD was upon me, and He said to me, “Get up, go out to the plain, and there I will speak with you.”
EZK.3.KJV: And the hand of the LORD was there on me; and he said to me, Arise, go forth into the plain, and I will there talk with you.
EZK.3.PLAIN: And there the hand of the Lord was upon me, and He said to me, “Get up, go out to the plain, and there I will speak with you.”

EZK.3.BSB: So I got up and went out to the plain, and behold, the glory of the LORD was present there, like the glory I had seen by the River Kebar, and I fell facedown.
EZK.3.KJV: Then I arose, and went forth into the plain: and, behold, the glory of the LORD stood there, as the glory which I saw by the river of Chebar: and I fell on my face.
EZK.3.PLAIN: So I got up and went out to the plain, and look closely — the glory of the Lord was present there, like the glory I had seen by the River Kebar, and I fell facedown.

EZK.3.BSB: Then the Spirit entered me and set me on my feet. He spoke with me and said, “Go, shut yourself inside your house.
EZK.3.KJV: Then the spirit entered into me, and set me on my feet, and spoke with me, and said to me, Go, shut yourself within your house.
EZK.3.PLAIN: Then the Spirit entered me and set me on my feet. He spoke with me and said, “Go, shut yourself inside your house.

EZK.3.BSB: And you, son of man, they will tie with ropes, and you will be bound so that you cannot go out among the people.
EZK.3.KJV: But you, O son of man, behold, they shall put bands on you, and shall bind you with them, and you shall not go out among them:
EZK.3.PLAIN: And you, son of man, they will tie with ropes, and you will be bound so that you cannot go out among the people.

EZK.3.BSB: I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, and you will be silent and unable to rebuke them, though they are a rebellious house.
EZK.3.KJV: And I will make your tongue sticks to the roof of your mouth, that you shall be dumb, and shall not be to them a reprover: for they are a rebellious house.
EZK.3.PLAIN: I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, and you will be silent and unable to rebuke them, though they are a rebellious house.

EZK.3.BSB: But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you are to tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says.’ Whoever listens, let him listen; and whoever refuses, let him refuse, for they are a rebellious house.
EZK.3.KJV: But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you shall say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD; He that hears, let him hear; and he that declines, let him forbear: for they are a rebellious house.
EZK.3.PLAIN: But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you are to tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says.’ Whoever listens, let him listen; and whoever refuses, let him refuse, for they are a rebellious house.

EZK.4.BSB: “Now you, son of man, take a brick, place it before you, and draw on it the city of Jerusalem.
EZK.4.KJV: You also, son of man, take you a tile, and lay it before you, and portray on it the city, even Jerusalem:
EZK.4.PLAIN: “Now you, son of man, take a brick, place it before you, and draw on it the city of Jerusalem.

EZK.4.BSB: Then lay siege against it: Construct a siege wall, build a ramp to it, set up camps against it, and place battering rams around it on all sides.
EZK.4.KJV: And lay siege against it, and build a fort against it, and cast a mount against it; set the camp also against it, and set battering rams against it round about.
EZK.4.PLAIN: Then lay siege against it: Construct a siege wall, build a ramp to it, set up camps against it, and place battering rams around it on all sides.

EZK.4.BSB: Then take an iron plate and set it up as an iron wall between yourself and the city. Turn your face toward it so that it is under siege, and besiege it. This will be a sign to the house of Israel.
EZK.4.KJV: Moreover take you to you an iron pan, and set it for a wall of iron between you and the city: and set your face against it, and it shall be besieged, and you shall lay siege against it. This shall be a sign to the house of Israel.
EZK.4.PLAIN: Then take an iron plate and set it up as an iron wall between yourself and the city. Turn your face toward it so that it is under siege, and besiege it. This will be a sign to the house of Israel.

EZK.7.KJV: The time is come, the day draws near: let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn: for wrath is on all the multitude thereof.
EZK.7.PLAIN: The time has come; the day has arrived. Let the buyer not rejoice and the seller not mourn, for wrath is upon the whole multitude.

EZK.7.BSB: The seller will surely not recover what he sold while both remain alive. For the vision concerning the whole multitude will not be revoked, and because of their iniquity, not one of them will preserve his life.
EZK.7.KJV: For the seller shall not return to that which is sold, although they were yet alive: for the vision is touching the whole multitude thereof, which shall not return; neither shall any strengthen himself in the iniquity of his life.
EZK.7.PLAIN: The seller will surely not recover what he sold while both remain alive. For the vision concerning the whole multitude will not be revoked, and because of their brokenness, not one of them will preserve his life.

EZK.7.BSB: They have blown the trumpet and made everything ready, but no one goes to war, for My wrath is upon the whole multitude.
EZK.7.KJV: They have blown the trumpet, even to make all ready; but none goes to the battle: for my wrath is on all the multitude thereof.
EZK.7.PLAIN: They have blown the trumpet and made everything ready, but no one goes to war, for My wrath is upon the whole multitude.

EZK.7.BSB: The sword is outside; plague and famine are within. Those in the country will die by the sword, and those in the city will be devoured by famine and plague.
EZK.7.KJV: The sword is without, and the pestilence and the famine within: he that is in the field shall die with the sword; and he that is in the city, famine and pestilence shall devour him. ¶
EZK.7.PLAIN: The sword is outside; plague and famine are within. Those in the country will die by the sword, and those in the city will be devoured by famine and plague.

EZK.7.BSB: The survivors will escape and live in the mountains, moaning like doves of the valley, each for his own iniquity.
EZK.7.KJV: But they that escape of them shall escape, and shall be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them mourning, every one for his iniquity.
EZK.7.PLAIN: The survivors will escape and live in the mountains, moaning like doves of the valley, each for his own brokenness.

EZK.7.BSB: Every hand will go limp, and every knee will turn to water.
EZK.7.KJV: All hands shall be feeble, and all knees shall be weak as water.
EZK.7.PLAIN: Every hand will go limp, and every knee will turn to water.

EZK.7.BSB: They will put on sackcloth, and terror will overwhelm them. Shame will cover all their faces, and all their heads will be shaved.
EZK.7.KJV: They shall also gird themselves with sackcloth, and horror shall cover them; and shame shall be on all faces, and baldness on all their heads.
EZK.7.PLAIN: They will put on sackcloth, and terror will overwhelm them. Shame will cover all their faces, and all their heads will be shaved.

EZK.7.BSB: They will throw their silver into the streets, and their gold will seem unclean. Their silver and gold cannot save them in the day of the wrath of the LORD. They cannot satisfy their appetites or fill their stomachs with wealth, for it became the stumbling block that brought their iniquity.
EZK.7.KJV: They shall cast their silver in the streets, and their gold shall be removed: their silver and their gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the LORD: they shall not satisfy their souls, neither fill their bowels: because it is the stumbling block of their iniquity. ¶
EZK.7.PLAIN: They will throw their silver into the streets, and their gold will seem unclean. Their silver and gold cannot save them in the day of the wrath of the Lord. They cannot satisfy their appetites or fill their stomachs with wealth, for it became the stumbling block that brought their brokenness.

EZK.7.BSB: His beautiful ornaments they transformed into pride and used them to fashion their vile images and detestable idols. Therefore I will make these into something unclean for them.
EZK.7.KJV: As for the beauty of his ornament, he set it in majesty: but they made the images of their abominations and of their detestable things therein: therefore have I set it far from them.
EZK.7.PLAIN: His beautiful ornaments they transformed into pride and used them to fashion their vile images and detestable idols. Therefore I will make these into something unclean for them.

EZK.7.BSB: And I will hand these things over as plunder to foreigners and loot to the wicked of the earth, who will defile them.
EZK.7.KJV: And I will give it into the hands of the strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth for a spoil; and they shall pollute it.
EZK.7.PLAIN: And I will hand these things over as plunder to foreigners and loot to the wicked of the earth, who will defile them.

EZK.7.BSB: I will turn My face away from them, and they will defile My treasured place. Violent men will enter it, and they will defile it.
EZK.7.KJV: My face will I turn also from them, and they shall pollute my secret place: for the robbers shall enter into it, and defile it. ¶
EZK.7.PLAIN: I will turn My face away from them, and they will defile My treasured place. Violent men will enter it, and they will defile it.

EZK.7.BSB: Forge the chain, for the land is full of crimes of bloodshed, and the city is full of violence.
EZK.7.KJV: Make a chain: for the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence.
EZK.7.PLAIN: Forge the chain, for the land is full of crimes of bloodshed, and the city is full of violence.

EZK.7.BSB: So I will bring the most wicked of nations to take possession of their houses. I will end the pride of the mighty, and their holy places will be profaned.
EZK.7.KJV: Why I will bring the worst of the heathen, and they shall possess their houses: I will also make the pomp of the strong to cease; and their holy places shall be defiled.
EZK.7.PLAIN: So I will bring the most wicked of nations to take possession of their houses. I will end the pride of the mighty, and their holy places will be profaned.

EZK.7.BSB: Anguish is coming! They will seek peace, but find none.
EZK.7.KJV: Destruction comes; and they shall seek peace, and there shall be none.
EZK.7.PLAIN: Anguish is coming! They will seek peace, but find none.

EZK.7.BSB: Disaster upon disaster will come, and rumor after rumor. Then they will seek a vision from a prophet, but instruction from the priests will perish, as will counsel from the elders.
EZK.7.KJV: Mischief shall come on mischief, and rumor shall be on rumor; then shall they seek a vision of the prophet; but the law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the ancients.
EZK.7.PLAIN: Disaster upon disaster will come, and rumor after rumor. Then they will seek a vision from a prophet, but instruction from the priests will perish, as will counsel from the elders.

EZK.7.BSB: The king will mourn, the prince will be clothed with despair, and the hands of the people of the land will tremble. I will deal with them according to their conduct, and I will judge them by their own standards. Then they will know that I am the LORD.’”
EZK.7.KJV: The king shall mourn, and the prince shall be clothed with desolation, and the hands of the people of the land shall be troubled: I will do to them after their way, and according to their deserts will I judge them; and they shall know that I am the LORD.
EZK.7.PLAIN: The king will mourn, the prince will be clothed with despair, and the hands of the people of the land will tremble. I will deal with them according to their conduct, and I will judge them by their own standards. Then they will know that I am the Lord.’”

EZK.8.BSB: In the sixth year, on the fifth day of the sixth month, I was sitting in my house, and the elders of Judah were sitting before me; and there the hand of the Lord GOD fell upon me.
EZK.8.KJV: And it came to pass in the sixth year, in the sixth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I sat in my house, and the elders of Judah sat before me, that the hand of the Lord GOD fell there on me.
EZK.8.PLAIN: In the sixth year, on the fifth day of the sixth month, I was sitting in my house, and the elders of Judah were sitting before me; and there the hand of the Lord GOD fell upon me.

EZK.8.BSB: Then I looked and saw a figure like that of a man. From His waist down His appearance was like fire, and from His waist up He was as bright as the gleam of amber.
EZK.8.KJV: Then I beheld, and see a likeness as the appearance of fire: from the appearance of his loins even downward, fire; and from his loins even upward, as the appearance of brightness, as the color of amber.
EZK.8.PLAIN: Then I looked and saw a figure like that of a man. From His waist down His appearance was like fire, and from His waist up He was as bright as the gleam of amber.

EZK.8.BSB: He stretched out what looked like a hand and took me by the hair of my head. Then the Spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven and carried me in visions of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the north gate of the inner court, where the idol that provokes jealousy was seated.
EZK.8.KJV: And he put forth the form of an hand, and took me by a lock of my head; and the spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heaven, and brought me in the visions of God to Jerusalem, to the door of the inner gate that looks toward the north; where was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provokes to jealousy.
EZK.8.PLAIN: He stretched out what looked like a hand and took me by the hair of my head. Then the Spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven and carried me in visions of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the north gate of the inner court, where the idol that provokes jealousy was seated.

EZK.8.BSB: And there I saw the glory of the God of Israel, like the vision I had seen in the plain.
EZK.8.KJV: And, behold, the glory of the God of Israel was there, according to the vision that I saw in the plain. ¶
EZK.8.PLAIN: And there I saw the glory of the God of Israel, like the vision I had seen in the plain.

EZK.8.BSB: “Son of man,” He said to me, “now lift up your eyes to the north.” So I lifted up my eyes to the north, and in the entrance north of the Altar Gate I saw this idol of jealousy.
EZK.8.KJV: Then said he to me, Son of man, lift up your eyes now the way toward the north. So I lifted up my eyes the way toward the north, and behold northward at the gate of the altar this image of jealousy in the entry.
EZK.8.PLAIN: “Son of man,” He said to me, “now lift up your eyes to the north.” So I lifted up my eyes to the north, and in the entrance north of the Altar Gate I saw this idol of jealousy.

EZK.8.BSB: “Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see what they are doing—the great abominations that the house of Israel is committing—to drive Me far from My sanctuary? Yet you will see even greater abominations.”
EZK.8.KJV: He said furthermore to me, Son of man, see you what they do? even the great abominations that the house of Israel commits here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary? but turn you yet again, and you shall see greater abominations. ¶
EZK.8.PLAIN: “Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see what they are doing—the great abominations that the house of Israel is committing—to drive Me far from My sanctuary? Yet you will see even greater abominations.”

EZK.8.BSB: Then He brought me to the entrance to the court, and I looked and saw a hole in the wall.
EZK.8.KJV: And he brought me to the door of the court; and when I looked, behold a hole in the wall.
EZK.8.PLAIN: Then He brought me to the entrance to the court, and I looked and saw a hole in the wall.

EZK.8.BSB: “Son of man,” He told me, “dig through the wall.” So I dug through the wall and discovered a doorway.
EZK.8.KJV: Then said he to me, Son of man, dig now in the wall: and when I had dig in the wall, behold a door.
EZK.8.PLAIN: “Son of man,” He told me, “dig through the wall.” So I dug through the wall and discovered a doorway.

EZK.8.BSB: Then He said to me, “Go in and see the wicked abominations they are committing here.”
EZK.8.KJV: And he said to me, Go in, and behold the wicked abominations that they do here.
EZK.8.PLAIN: Then He said to me, “Go in and see the wicked abominations they are committing here.”

EZK.8.BSB: So I went in and looked, and engraved all around the wall was every kind of crawling creature and detestable beast, along with all the idols of the house of Israel.
EZK.8.KJV: So I went in and saw; and behold every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, portrayed on the wall round about.
EZK.8.PLAIN: So I went in and looked, and engraved all around the wall was every kind of crawling creature and detestable beast, along with all the idols of the house of Israel.

EZK.8.BSB: Before them stood seventy elders of the house of Israel, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them. Each had a censer in his hand, and a fragrant cloud of incense was rising.
EZK.8.KJV: And there stood before them seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel, and in the middle of them stood Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan, with every man his censer in his hand; and a thick cloud of incense went up.
EZK.8.PLAIN: Before them stood seventy elders of the house of Israel, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them. Each had a censer in his hand, and a fragrant cloud of incense was rising.

EZK.8.BSB: “Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the darkness, each at the shrine of his own idol? For they are saying, ‘The LORD does not see us; the LORD has forsaken the land.’”
EZK.8.KJV: Then said he to me, Son of man, have you seen what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, the LORD sees us not; the LORD has forsaken the earth. ¶
EZK.8.PLAIN: “Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the darkness, each at the shrine of his own idol? For they are saying, ‘The Lord does not see us; the Lord has forsaken the land.’”

EZK.8.BSB: Again, He told me, “You will see them committing even greater abominations.”
EZK.8.KJV: He said also to me, Turn you yet again, and you shall see greater abominations that they do.
EZK.8.PLAIN: Again, He told me, “You will see them committing even greater abominations.”

EZK.8.BSB: Then He brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the LORD, and I saw women sitting there, weeping for Tammuz.
EZK.8.KJV: Then he brought me to the door of the gate of the LORD’s house which was toward the north; and, behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz. ¶
EZK.8.PLAIN: Then He brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the Lord, and I saw women sitting there, weeping for Tammuz.

EZK.8.BSB: “Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see this? Yet you will see even greater abominations than these.”
EZK.8.KJV: Then said he to me, Have you seen this, O son of man? turn you yet again, and you shall see greater abominations than these.
EZK.8.PLAIN: “Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see this? Yet you will see even greater abominations than these.”

EZK.8.BSB: So He brought me to the inner court of the house of the LORD, and there at the entrance to the temple of the LORD, between the portico and the altar, were about twenty-five men with their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces toward the east; and they were bowing to the east in worship of the sun.
EZK.8.KJV: And he brought me into the inner court of the LORD’s house, and, behold, at the door of the temple of the LORD, between the porch and the altar, were about five and twenty men, with their backs toward the temple of the LORD, and their faces toward the east; and they worshipped the sun toward the east. ¶
EZK.8.PLAIN: So He brought me to the inner court of the house of the Lord, and there at the entrance to the temple of the Lord, between the portico and the altar, were about twenty-five men with their backs to the temple of the Lord and their faces toward the east; and they were bowing to the east in worship of the sun.

EZK.8.BSB: “Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see this? Is it not enough for the house of Judah to commit the abominations they are practicing here, that they must also fill the land with violence and continually provoke Me to anger? Look, they are even putting the branch to their nose!
EZK.8.KJV: Then he said to me, Have you seen this, O son of man? Is it a light thing to the house of Judah that they commit the abominations which they commit here? for they have filled the land with violence, and have returned to provoke me to anger: and, see, they put the branch to their nose.
EZK.8.PLAIN: “Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see this? Is it not enough for the house of Judah to commit the abominations they are practicing here, that they must also fill the land with violence and continually provoke Me to anger? Look, they are even putting the branch to their nose!

EZK.8.BSB: Therefore I will respond with wrath. I will not look on them with pity, nor will I spare them. Although they shout loudly in My ears, I will not listen to them.”
EZK.8.KJV: Therefore will I also deal in fury: my eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity: and though they cry in my ears with a loud voice, yet will I not hear them.
EZK.8.PLAIN: Therefore I will respond with wrath. I will not look on them with pity, nor will I spare them. Although they shout loudly in My ears, I will not listen to them.”

EZK.9.BSB: Then I heard Him call out in a loud voice, saying, “Draw near, O executioners of the city, each with a weapon of destruction in hand.”
EZK.9.KJV: He cried also in my ears with a loud voice, saying, Cause them that have charge over the city to draw near, even every man with his destroying weapon in his hand.
EZK.9.PLAIN: Then I heard Him call out in a loud voice, saying, “Draw near, O executioners of the city, each with a weapon of destruction in hand.”

EZK.9.BSB: And I saw six men coming from the direction of the Upper Gate, which faces north, each with a weapon of slaughter in his hand. With them was another man clothed in linen who had a writing kit at his side. And they came in and stood beside the bronze altar.
EZK.9.KJV: And, behold, six men came from the way of the higher gate, which lies toward the north, and every man a slaughter weapon in his hand; and one man among them was clothed with linen, with a writer’s inkhorn by his side: and they went in, and stood beside the brazen altar.
EZK.9.PLAIN: And I saw six men coming from the direction of the Upper Gate, which faces north, each with a weapon of slaughter in his hand. With them was another man clothed in linen who had a writing kit at his side. And they came in and stood beside the bronze altar.

EZK.9.BSB: Then the glory of the God of Israel rose from above the cherubim, where it had been, and moved to the threshold of the temple. And He called to the man clothed in linen who had the writing kit at his side.
EZK.9.KJV: And the glory of the God of Israel was gone up from the cherub, whereupon he was, to the threshold of the house. And he called to the man clothed with linen, which had the writer’s inkhorn by his side;
EZK.9.PLAIN: Then the glory of the God of Israel rose from above the cherubim, where it had been, and moved to the threshold of the temple. And He called to the man clothed in linen who had the writing kit at his side.

EZK.9.BSB: “Go throughout the city of Jerusalem,” said the LORD, “and put a mark on the foreheads of the men sighing and groaning over all the abominations committed there.”
EZK.9.KJV: And the LORD said to him, Go through the middle of the city, through the middle of Jerusalem, and set a mark on the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the middle thereof. ¶
EZK.9.PLAIN: “Go throughout the city of Jerusalem,” said the Lord, “and put a mark on the foreheads of the men sighing and groaning over all the abominations committed there.”

EZK.9.BSB: And as I listened, He said to the others, “Follow him through the city and start killing; do not show pity or spare anyone!
EZK.9.KJV: And to the others he said in my hearing, Go you after him through the city, and smite: let not your eye spare, neither have you pity:
EZK.9.PLAIN: And as I listened, He said to the others, “Follow him through the city and start killing; do not show pity or spare anyone!

EZK.9.BSB: Slaughter the old men, the young men and maidens, the women and children; but do not go near anyone who has the mark. Now begin at My sanctuary.” So they began with the elders who were before the temple.
EZK.9.KJV: Slay utterly old and young, both maids, and little children, and women: but come not near any man on whom is the mark; and begin at my sanctuary. Then they began at the ancient men which were before the house.
EZK.9.PLAIN: Slaughter the old men, the young men and maidens, the women and children; but do not go near anyone who has the mark. Now begin at My sanctuary.” So they began with the elders who were before the temple.

EZK.9.BSB: Then He told them, “Defile the temple and fill the courts with the slain. Go forth!” So they went out and began killing throughout the city.
EZK.9.KJV: And he said to them, Defile the house, and fill the courts with the slain: go you forth. And they went forth, and slew in the city. ¶
EZK.9.PLAIN: Then He told them, “Defile the temple and fill the courts with the slain. Go forth!” So they went out and began killing throughout the city.

EZK.9.BSB: While they were killing, I was left alone. And I fell facedown and cried out, “Oh, Lord GOD, when You pour out Your wrath on Jerusalem, will You destroy the entire remnant of Israel?”
EZK.9.KJV: And it came to pass, while they were slaying them, and I was left, that I fell on my face, and cried, and said, Ah Lord GOD! will you destroy all the residue of Israel in your pouring out of your fury on Jerusalem?
EZK.9.PLAIN: While they were killing, I was left alone. And I fell facedown and cried out, “Oh, Lord GOD, when You pour out Your wrath on Jerusalem, will You destroy the entire remnant of Israel?”

EZK.9.BSB: He replied, “The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great. The land is full of bloodshed, and the city is full of perversity. For they say, ‘The LORD has forsaken the land; the LORD does not see.’
EZK.9.KJV: Then said he to me, The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceeding great, and the land is full of blood, and the city full of perverseness: for they say, The LORD has forsaken the earth, and the LORD sees not.
EZK.9.PLAIN: He replied, “The brokenness of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great. The land is full of bloodshed, and the city is full of perversity. For they say, ‘The Lord has forsaken the land; the Lord does not see.’

EZK.9.BSB: But as for Me, I will not look on them with pity, nor will I spare them. I will bring their deeds down upon their own heads.”
EZK.9.KJV: And as for me also, my eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity, but I will recompense their way on their head.
EZK.9.PLAIN: But as for Me, I will not look on them with pity, nor will I spare them. I will bring their deeds down upon their own heads.”

EZK.9.BSB: Then the man clothed in linen with the writing kit at his side reported back, “I have done as You commanded.”
EZK.9.KJV: And, behold, the man clothed with linen, which had the inkhorn by his side, reported the matter, saying, I have done as you have commanded me.
EZK.9.PLAIN: Then the man clothed in linen with the writing kit at his side reported back, “I have done as You commanded.”

EZK.10.BSB: And I looked and saw above the expanse, above the heads of the cherubim, the likeness of a throne of sapphire.

EZK.10.PLAIN: And I looked and saw above the expanse, above the heads of the cherubim, the likeness of a throne of sapphire.

EZK.10.PLAIN: And the Lord said to the man clothed in linen, “Go inside the wheelwork beneath the cherubim. Fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim and scatter them over the city.” And as I watched, he went in.

EZK.10.PLAIN: Then the glory of the Lord rose from above the cherubim and stood over the threshold of the temple. The temple was filled with the cloud, and the court was filled with the brightness of the glory of the Lord.

EZK.16.PLAIN: For this is what the Lord GOD says: I will deal with you according to your deeds, since you have despised the oath by breaking the covenant.

EZK.16.BSB: But I will remember the covenant I made with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish an everlasting covenant with you.
EZK.16.KJV: Nevertheless I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish to you an everlasting covenant.
EZK.16.PLAIN: But I will remember the covenant I made with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish an everlasting covenant with you.

EZK.16.BSB: Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you receive your older and younger sisters. I will give them to you as daughters, but not because of My covenant with you.
EZK.16.KJV: Then you shall remember your ways, and be ashamed, when you shall receive your sisters, your elder and your younger: and I will give them to you for daughters, but not by your covenant.
EZK.16.PLAIN: Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you receive your older and younger sisters. I will give them to you as daughters, but not because of My covenant with you.

EZK.16.BSB: So I will establish My covenant with you, and you will know that I am the LORD,
EZK.16.KJV: And I will establish my covenant with you; and you shall know that I am the LORD:
EZK.16.PLAIN: So I will establish My covenant with you, and you will know that I am the Lord,

EZK.16.BSB: so that when I make atonement for all you have done, you will remember and be ashamed and never again open your mouth because of your disgrace, declares the Lord GOD.”
EZK.16.KJV: That you may remember, and be confounded, and never open your mouth any more because of your shame, when I am pacified toward you for all that you have done, says the Lord GOD.
EZK.16.PLAIN: so that when I make atonement for all you have done, you will remember and be ashamed and never again open your mouth because of your disgrace, declares the Lord GOD.”

EZK.17.BSB: Now the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
EZK.17.KJV: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
EZK.17.PLAIN: Now the word of the Lord came to me, saying,

EZK.17.BSB: “Son of man, pose a riddle; speak a parable to the house of Israel
EZK.17.KJV: Son of man, put forth a riddle, and speak a parable to the house of Israel;
EZK.17.PLAIN: “Son of man, pose a riddle; speak a parable to the house of Israel

EZK.17.BSB: and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘A great eagle with great wings and long pinions, full of feathers of many colors, came to Lebanon and took away the top of the cedar.
EZK.17.KJV: And say, Thus says the Lord GOD; A great eagle with great wings, long winged, full of feathers, which had divers colors, came to Lebanon, and took the highest branch of the cedar:
EZK.17.PLAIN: and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘A great eagle with great wings and long pinions, full of feathers of many colors, came to Lebanon and took away the top of the cedar.

EZK.17.BSB: He plucked off its topmost shoot, carried it to the land of merchants, and planted it in a city of traders.
EZK.17.KJV: He cropped off the top of his young twigs, and carried it into a land of traffic; he set it in a city of merchants.
EZK.17.PLAIN: He plucked off its topmost shoot, carried it to the land of merchants, and planted it in a city of traders.

EZK.17.BSB: He took some of the seed of the land and planted it in fertile soil; he placed it by abundant waters and set it out like a willow.
EZK.17.KJV: He took also of the seed of the land, and planted it in a fruitful field; he placed it by great waters, and set it as a willow tree.
EZK.17.PLAIN: He took some of the seed of the land and planted it in fertile soil; he placed it by abundant waters and set it out like a willow.

EZK.17.BSB: It sprouted and became a spreading vine, low in height, with branches turned toward him; yet its roots remained where it stood. So it became a vine and yielded branches and sent out shoots.
EZK.17.KJV: And it grew, and became a spreading vine of low stature, whose branches turned toward him, and the roots thereof were under him: so it became a vine, and brought forth branches, and shot forth sprigs.
EZK.17.PLAIN: It sprouted and became a spreading vine, low in height, with branches turned toward him; yet its roots remained where it stood. So it became a vine and yielded branches and sent out shoots.

EZK.17.BSB: But there was another great eagle with great wings and many feathers. And behold, this vine bent its roots toward him. It stretched out its branches to him from its planting bed, so that he might water it.
EZK.17.KJV: There was also another great eagle with great wings and many feathers: and, behold, this vine did bend her roots toward him, and shot forth her branches toward him, that he might water it by the furrows of her plantation.
EZK.17.PLAIN: But there was another great eagle with great wings and many feathers. And look closely — this vine bent its roots toward him. It stretched out its branches to him from its planting bed, so that he might water it.

EZK.17.BSB: It had been planted in good soil by abundant waters in order to yield branches and bear fruit and become a splendid vine.’
EZK.17.KJV: It was planted in a good soil by great waters, that it might bring forth branches, and that it might bear fruit, that it might be a goodly vine.
EZK.17.PLAIN: It had been planted in good soil by abundant waters in order to yield branches and bear fruit and become a splendid vine.’

EZK.17.BSB: So you are to tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Will it flourish? Will it not be uprooted and stripped of its fruit so that it shrivels? All its foliage will wither! It will not take a strong arm or many people to pull it up by its roots.
EZK.17.KJV: Say you, Thus says the Lord GOD; Shall it prosper? shall he not pull up the roots thereof, and cut off the fruit thereof, that it wither? it shall wither in all the leaves of her spring, even without great power or many people to pluck it up by the roots thereof.
EZK.17.PLAIN: So you are to tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Will it flourish? Will it not be uprooted and stripped of its fruit so that it shrivels? All its foliage will wither! It will not take a strong arm or many people to pull it up by its roots.

EZK.17.BSB: Even if it is transplanted, will it flourish? Will it not completely wither when the east wind strikes? It will wither on the bed where it sprouted.’”
EZK.17.KJV: Yes, behold, being planted, shall it prosper? shall it not utterly wither, when the east wind touches it? it shall wither in the furrows where it grew. ¶
EZK.17.PLAIN: Even if it is transplanted, will it flourish? Will it not completely wither when the east wind strikes? It will wither on the bed where it sprouted.’”

EZK.17.BSB: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
EZK.17.KJV: Moreover the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
EZK.17.PLAIN: Then the word of the Lord came to me, saying,

EZK.17.BSB: “Now say to this rebellious house: ‘Do you not know what these things mean?’ Tell them, ‘Behold, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, carried off its king and officials, and brought them back with him to Babylon.
EZK.17.KJV: Say now to the rebellious house, Know you not what these things mean? tell them, Behold, the king of Babylon is come to Jerusalem, and has taken the king thereof, and the princes thereof, and led them with him to Babylon;
EZK.17.PLAIN: “Now say to this rebellious house: ‘Do you not know what these things mean?’ Tell them, ‘Look closely — the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, carried off its king and officials, and brought them back with him to Babylon.

EZK.17.BSB: He took a member of the royal family and made a covenant with him, putting him under oath. Then he carried away the leading men of the land,
EZK.17.KJV: And has taken of the king’s seed, and made a covenant with him, and has taken an oath of him: he has also taken the mighty of the land:
EZK.17.PLAIN: He took a member of the royal family and made a covenant with him, putting him under oath. Then he carried away the leading men of the land,

EZK.17.BSB: so that the kingdom would be brought low, unable to lift itself up, surviving only by keeping his covenant.
EZK.17.KJV: That the kingdom might be base, that it might not lift itself up, but that by keeping of his covenant it might stand.
EZK.17.PLAIN: so that the kingdom would be brought low, unable to lift itself up, surviving only by keeping his covenant.

EZK.17.BSB: But this king rebelled against Babylon by sending his envoys to Egypt to ask for horses and a large army. Will he flourish? Will the one who does such things escape? Can he break a covenant and yet escape?’
EZK.17.KJV: But he rebelled against him in sending his ambassadors into Egypt, that they might give him horses and much people. Shall he prosper? shall he escape that does such things? or shall he break the covenant, and be delivered?
EZK.17.PLAIN: But this king rebelled against Babylon by sending his envoys to Egypt to ask for horses and a large army. Will he flourish? Will the one who does such things escape? Can he break a covenant and yet escape?’

EZK.17.BSB: ‘As surely as I live,’ declares the Lord GOD, ‘he will die in Babylon, in the land of the king who enthroned him, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke.
EZK.17.KJV: As I live, says the Lord GOD, surely in the place where the king dwells that made him king, whose oath he despised, and whose covenant he broke, even with him in the middle of Babylon he shall die.
EZK.17.PLAIN: ‘As surely as I live,’ declares the Lord GOD, ‘he will die in Babylon, in the land of the king who enthroned him, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke.

EZK.17.BSB: Pharaoh with his mighty army and vast horde will not help him in battle, when ramps are built and siege walls constructed to destroy many lives.
EZK.17.KJV: Neither shall Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company make for him in the war, by casting up mounts, and building forts, to cut off many persons:
EZK.17.PLAIN: Pharaoh with his mighty army and vast horde will not help him in battle, when ramps are built and siege walls constructed to destroy many lives.

EZK.17.BSB: He despised the oath by breaking the covenant. Seeing that he gave his hand in pledge yet did all these things, he will not escape!’
EZK.17.KJV: Seeing he despised the oath by breaking the covenant, when, see, he had given his hand, and has done all these things, he shall not escape.
EZK.17.PLAIN: He despised the oath by breaking the covenant. Seeing that he gave his hand in pledge yet did all these things, he will not escape!’

EZK.17.BSB: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘As surely as I live, I will bring down upon his head My oath that he despised and My covenant that he broke.
EZK.17.KJV: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD; As I live, surely my oath that he has despised, and my covenant that he has broken, even it will I recompense on his own head.
EZK.17.PLAIN: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘As surely as I live, I will bring down upon his head My oath that he despised and My covenant that he broke.

EZK.17.BSB: I will spread My net over him and catch him in My snare. I will bring him to Babylon and execute judgment upon him there for the treason he committed against Me.
EZK.17.KJV: And I will spread my net on him, and he shall be taken in my snare, and I will bring him to Babylon, and will plead with him there for his trespass that he has trespassed against me.
EZK.17.PLAIN: I will spread My net over him and catch him in My snare. I will bring him to Babylon and execute judgment upon him there for the treason he committed against Me.

EZK.17.BSB: All his choice troops will fall by the sword, and those who survive will be scattered to every wind. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.’
EZK.17.KJV: And all his fugitives with all his bands shall fall by the sword, and they that remain shall be scattered toward all winds: and you shall know that I the LORD have spoken it. ¶
EZK.17.PLAIN: All his choice troops will fall by the sword, and those who survive will be scattered to every wind. Then you will know that I, the Lord, have spoken.’

EZK.17.BSB: This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will take a shoot from the lofty top of the cedar, and I will set it out. I will pluck a tender sprig from its topmost shoots, and I will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.
EZK.17.KJV: Thus says the Lord GOD; I will also take of the highest branch of the high cedar, and will set it; I will crop off from the top of his young twigs a tender one, and will plant it on an high mountain and eminent:
EZK.17.PLAIN: This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will take a shoot from the lofty top of the cedar, and I will set it out. I will pluck a tender sprig from its topmost shoots, and I will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.

EZK.17.BSB: I will plant it on the mountain heights of Israel so that it will bear branches; it will yield fruit and become a majestic cedar. Birds of every kind will nest under it, taking shelter in the shade of its branches.
EZK.17.KJV: In the mountain of the height of Israel will I plant it: and it shall bring forth boughs, and bear fruit, and be a goodly cedar: and under it shall dwell all fowl of every wing; in the shadow of the branches thereof shall they dwell.
EZK.17.PLAIN: I will plant it on the mountain heights of Israel so that it will bear branches; it will yield fruit and become a majestic cedar. Birds of every kind will nest under it, taking shelter in the shade of its branches.

EZK.17.BSB: Then all the trees of the field will know that I am the LORD. I bring the tall tree down and make the low tree tall. I dry up the green tree and make the withered tree flourish. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I have done it.’”
EZK.17.KJV: And all the trees of the field shall know that I the LORD have brought down the high tree, have exalted the low tree, have dried up the green tree, and have made the dry tree to flourish: I the LORD have spoken and have done it.
EZK.17.PLAIN: Then all the trees of the field will know that I am the Lord. I bring the tall tree down and make the low tree tall. I dry up the green tree and make the withered tree flourish. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I have done it.’”

EZK.18.BSB: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
EZK.18.KJV: The word of the LORD came to me again, saying,
EZK.18.PLAIN: Then the word of the Lord came to me, saying,

EZK.18.BSB: “What do you people mean by quoting this proverb about the land of Israel: ‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are set on edge’?
EZK.18.KJV: What mean you, that you use this proverb concerning the land of Israel, saying, The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge?
EZK.18.PLAIN: “What do you people mean by quoting this proverb about the land of Israel: ‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are set on edge’?

EZK.18.BSB: As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, you will no longer quote this proverb in Israel.
EZK.18.KJV: As I live, says the Lord GOD, you shall not have occasion any more to use this proverb in Israel.
EZK.18.PLAIN: As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, you will no longer quote this proverb in Israel.

EZK.18.BSB: Behold, every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.
EZK.18.KJV: Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sins, it shall die. ¶
EZK.18.PLAIN: Look closely — every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.

EZK.18.BSB: Now suppose a man is righteous and does what is just and right:
EZK.18.KJV: But if a man be just, and do that which is lawful and right,
EZK.18.PLAIN: Now suppose a man is righteous and does what is just and right:

EZK.18.BSB: He does not eat at the mountain or look to the idols of the house of Israel. He does not defile his neighbor’s wife or approach a woman during her period.
EZK.18.KJV: And has not eaten on the mountains, neither has lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, neither has defiled his neighbor’s wife, neither has come near to a menstruous woman,
EZK.18.PLAIN: He does not eat at the mountain or look to the idols of the house of Israel. He does not defile his neighbor’s wife or approach a woman during her period.

EZK.18.BSB: He does not oppress another, but restores the pledge to the debtor. He does not commit robbery, but gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.
EZK.18.KJV: And has not oppressed any, but has restored to the debtor his pledge, has spoiled none by violence, has given his bread to the hungry, and has covered the naked with a garment;
EZK.18.PLAIN: He does not oppress another, but restores the pledge to the debtor. He does not commit robbery, but gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.

EZK.18.BSB: He does not engage in usury or take excess interest, but he withholds his hand from iniquity and executes true justice between men.
EZK.18.KJV: He that has not given forth on usury, neither has taken any increase, that has withdrawn his hand from iniquity, has executed true judgment between man and man,
EZK.18.PLAIN: He does not engage in usury or take excess interest, but he withholds his hand from brokenness and executes true justice between men.

EZK.18.BSB: He follows My statutes and faithfully keeps My ordinances. That man is righteous; surely he will live, declares the Lord GOD.
EZK.18.KJV: Has walked in my statutes, and has kept my judgments, to deal truly; he is just, he shall surely live, says the Lord GOD. ¶
EZK.18.PLAIN: He follows My statutes and faithfully keeps My ordinances. That man is righteous; surely he will live, declares the Lord GOD.

EZK.18.BSB: Now suppose that man has a violent son, who sheds blood or does any of these things,
EZK.18.KJV: If he beget a son that is a robber, a shedder of blood, and that does the like to any one of these things,
EZK.18.PLAIN: Now suppose that man has a violent son, who sheds blood or does any of these things,

EZK.18.BSB: though the father has done none of them: Indeed, the son eats at the mountain and defiles his neighbor’s wife.
EZK.18.KJV: And that does not any of those duties, but even has eaten on the mountains, and defiled his neighbor’s wife,
EZK.18.PLAIN: though the father has done none of them: Indeed, the son eats at the mountain and defiles his neighbor’s wife.

EZK.18.BSB: He oppresses the poor and needy; he commits robbery and does not restore a pledge. He lifts his eyes to idols; he commits abominations.
EZK.18.KJV: Has oppressed the poor and needy, has spoiled by violence, has not restored the pledge, and has lifted up his eyes to the idols, has committed abomination,
EZK.18.PLAIN: He oppresses the poor and needy; he commits robbery and does not restore a pledge. He lifts his eyes to idols; he commits abominations.

EZK.18.BSB: He engages in usury and takes excess interest. Will this son live? He will not! Since he has committed all these abominations, he will surely die; his blood will be on his own head.
EZK.18.KJV: Has given forth on usury, and has taken increase: shall he then live? he shall not live: he has done all these abominations; he shall surely die; his blood shall be on him. ¶
EZK.18.PLAIN: He engages in usury and takes excess interest. Will this son live? He will not! Since he has committed all these abominations, he will surely die; his blood will be on his own head.

EZK.18.BSB: Now suppose this son has a son who sees all the sins his father has committed, considers them, and does not do likewise:
EZK.18.KJV: Now, see, if he beget a son, that sees all his father’s sins which he has done, and considers, and does not such like,
EZK.18.PLAIN: Now suppose this son has a son who sees all the sins his father has committed, considers them, and does not do likewise:

EZK.18.BSB: He does not eat at the mountain or look to the idols of the house of Israel. He does not defile his neighbor’s wife.
EZK.18.KJV: That has not eaten on the mountains, neither has lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, has not defiled his neighbor’s wife,
EZK.18.PLAIN: He does not eat at the mountain or look to the idols of the house of Israel. He does not defile his neighbor’s wife.

EZK.18.BSB: He does not oppress another, or retain a pledge, or commit robbery. He gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.
EZK.18.KJV: Neither has oppressed any, has not withheld the pledge, neither has spoiled by violence, but has given his bread to the hungry, and has covered the naked with a garment,
EZK.18.PLAIN: He does not oppress another, or retain a pledge, or commit robbery. He gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.

EZK.18.BSB: He withholds his hand from harming the poor and takes no interest or usury. He keeps My ordinances and follows My statutes. Such a man will not die for his father’s iniquity. He will surely live.
EZK.18.KJV: That has taken off his hand from the poor, that has not received usury nor increase, has executed my judgments, has walked in my statutes; he shall not die for the iniquity of his father, he shall surely live.
EZK.18.PLAIN: He withholds his hand from harming the poor and takes no interest or usury. He keeps My ordinances and follows My statutes. Such a man will not die for his father’s brokenness. He will surely live.

EZK.18.BSB: As for his father, he will die for his own iniquity, because he practiced extortion, robbed his brother, and did what was wrong among his people.
EZK.18.KJV: As for his father, because he cruelly oppressed, spoiled his brother by violence, and did that which is not good among his people, see, even he shall die in his iniquity. ¶
EZK.18.PLAIN: As for his father, he will die for his own brokenness, because he practiced extortion, robbed his brother, and did what was wrong among his people.

EZK.18.BSB: Yet you may ask, ‘Why shouldn’t the son bear the iniquity of his father?’ Since the son has done what is just and right, carefully observing all My statutes, he will surely live.
EZK.18.KJV: Yet say you, Why? does not the son bear the iniquity of the father? When the son has done that which is lawful and right, and has kept all my statutes, and has done them, he shall surely live.
EZK.18.PLAIN: Yet you may ask, ‘Why shouldn’t the son bear the brokenness of his father?’ Since the son has done what is just and right, carefully observing all My statutes, he will surely live.

EZK.18.BSB: The soul who sins is the one who will die. A son will not bear the iniquity of his father, and a father will not bear the iniquity of his son. The righteousness of the righteous man will fall upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked man will fall upon him.
EZK.18.KJV: The soul that sins, it shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son: the righteousness of the righteous shall be on him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be on him.
EZK.18.PLAIN: The soul who sins is the one who will die. A son will not bear the brokenness of his father, and a father will not bear the brokenness of his son. The righteousness of the righteous man will fall upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked man will fall upon him.

EZK.18.BSB: But if the wicked man turns from all the sins he has committed, keeps all My statutes, and does what is just and right, he will surely live; he will not die.
EZK.18.KJV: But if the wicked will turn from all his sins that he has committed, and keep all my statutes, and do that which is lawful and right, he shall surely live, he shall not die.
EZK.18.PLAIN: But if the wicked man turns from all the sins he has committed, keeps all My statutes, and does what is just and right, he will surely live; he will not die.

EZK.18.BSB: None of the transgressions he has committed will be held against him. Because of the righteousness he has practiced, he will live.
EZK.18.KJV: All his transgressions that he has committed, they shall not be mentioned to him: in his righteousness that he has done he shall live.
EZK.18.PLAIN: None of the wanderings and failures he has committed will be held against him. Because of the righteousness he has practiced, he will live.

EZK.18.BSB: Do I take any pleasure in the death of the wicked? declares the Lord GOD. Wouldn’t I prefer that he turn from his ways and live?
EZK.18.KJV: Have I any pleasure at all that the wicked should die? says the Lord GOD: and not that he should return from his ways, and live? ¶
EZK.18.PLAIN: Do I take any pleasure in the death of the wicked? declares the Lord GOD. Wouldn’t I prefer that he turn from his ways and live?

EZK.18.BSB: But if a righteous man turns from his righteousness and practices iniquity, committing the same abominations as the wicked, will he live? None of the righteous acts he did will be remembered. Because of the unfaithfulness and sin he has committed, he will die.
EZK.18.KJV: But when the righteous turns away from his righteousness, and commits iniquity, and does according to all the abominations that the wicked man does, shall he live? All his righteousness that he has done shall not be mentioned: in his trespass that he has trespassed, and in his sin that he has sinned, in them shall he die. ¶
EZK.18.PLAIN: But if a righteous man turns from his righteousness and practices brokenness, committing the same abominations as the wicked, will he live? None of the righteous acts he did will be remembered. Because of the unfaithfulness and sin he has committed, he will die.

EZK.18.BSB: Yet you say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ Hear now, O house of Israel: Is it My way that is unjust? Is it not your ways that are unjust?
EZK.18.KJV: Yet you say, The way of the LORD is not equal. Hear now, O house of Israel; Is not my way equal? are not your ways unequal?
EZK.18.PLAIN: Yet you say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ Hear now, O house of Israel: Is it My way that is unjust? Is it not your ways that are unjust?

EZK.18.BSB: If a righteous man turns from his righteousness and practices iniquity, he will die for this. He will die because of the iniquity he has committed.
EZK.18.KJV: When a righteous man turns away from his righteousness, and commits iniquity, and dies in them; for his iniquity that he has done shall he die.
EZK.18.PLAIN: If a righteous man turns from his righteousness and practices brokenness, he will die for this. He will die because of the brokenness he has committed.

EZK.18.BSB: But if a wicked man turns from the wickedness he has committed and does what is just and right, he will save his life.
EZK.18.KJV: Again, when the wicked man turns away from his wickedness that he has committed, and does that which is lawful and right, he shall save his soul alive.
EZK.18.PLAIN: But if a wicked man turns from the wickedness he has committed and does what is just and right, he will save his life.

EZK.18.BSB: Because he considered and turned from all the transgressions he had committed, he will surely live; he will not die.
EZK.18.KJV: Because he considers, and turns away from all his transgressions that he has committed, he shall surely live, he shall not die.
EZK.18.PLAIN: Because he considered and turned from all the wanderings and failures he had committed, he will surely live; he will not die.

EZK.18.BSB: Yet the house of Israel says, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ Are My ways unjust, O house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are unjust?
EZK.18.KJV: Yet says the house of Israel, The way of the LORD is not equal. O house of Israel, are not my ways equal? are not your ways unequal?
EZK.18.PLAIN: Yet the house of Israel says, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ Are My ways unjust, O house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are unjust?

EZK.18.BSB: Therefore, O house of Israel, I will judge you, each according to his ways, declares the Lord GOD. Repent and turn from all your transgressions, so that your iniquity will not become your downfall.
EZK.18.KJV: Therefore I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ways, says the Lord GOD. Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions; so iniquity shall not be your ruin. ¶
EZK.18.PLAIN: Therefore, O house of Israel, I will judge you, each according to his ways, declares the Lord GOD. Repent and turn from all your wanderings and failures, so that your brokenness will not become your downfall.

EZK.18.BSB: Cast away from yourselves all the transgressions you have committed, and fashion for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why should you die, O house of Israel?
EZK.18.KJV: Cast away from you all your transgressions, whereby you have transgressed; and make you a new heart and a new spirit: for why will you die, O house of Israel?
EZK.18.PLAIN: Cast away from yourselves all the wanderings and failures you have committed, and fashion for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why should you die, O house of Israel?

EZK.18.BSB: For I take no pleasure in anyone’s death, declares the Lord GOD. So repent and live!
EZK.18.KJV: For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dies, says the Lord GOD: why turn yourselves, and live you.
EZK.18.PLAIN: For I take no pleasure in anyone’s death, declares the Lord GOD. So repent and live!

EZK.19.BSB: “As for you, take up a lament for the princes of Israel
EZK.19.KJV: Moreover take you up a lamentation for the princes of Israel,
EZK.19.PLAIN: “As for you, take up a lament for the princes of Israel

EZK.19.BSB: and say: ‘What was your mother? A lioness among the lions! She lay down among the young lions; she reared her cubs.
EZK.19.KJV: And say, What is your mother? A lioness: she lay down among lions, she nourished her whelps among young lions.
EZK.19.PLAIN: and say: ‘What was your mother? A lioness among the lions! She lay down among the young lions; she reared her cubs.

EZK.19.KJV: And she brought up one of her whelps: it became a young lion, and it learned to catch the prey; it devoured men.
EZK.19.PLAIN: She brought up one of her cubs, and he became a young lion. After learning to tear his prey, he devoured men.

EZK.19.BSB: When the nations heard of him, he was trapped in their pit. With hooks they led him away to the land of Egypt.
EZK.19.KJV: The nations also heard of him; he was taken in their pit, and they brought him with chains to the land of Egypt.
EZK.19.PLAIN: When the nations heard of him, he was trapped in their pit. With hooks they led him away to the land of Egypt.

EZK.19.BSB: When she saw that she had waited in vain, that her hope was lost, she took another of her cubs and made him a young lion.
EZK.19.KJV: Now when she saw that she had waited, and her hope was lost, then she took another of her whelps, and made him a young lion.
EZK.19.PLAIN: When she saw that she had waited in vain, that her hope was lost, she took another of her cubs and made him a young lion.

EZK.19.BSB: He prowled among the lions, and became a young lion. After learning to tear his prey, he devoured men.
EZK.19.KJV: And he went up and down among the lions, he became a young lion, and learned to catch the prey, and devoured men.
EZK.19.PLAIN: He prowled among the lions, and became a young lion. After learning to tear his prey, he devoured men.

EZK.19.BSB: He broke down their strongholds and devastated their cities. The land and everything in it shuddered at the sound of his roaring.
EZK.19.KJV: And he knew their desolate palaces, and he laid waste their cities; and the land was desolate, and the fullness thereof, by the noise of his roaring.
EZK.19.PLAIN: He broke down their strongholds and devastated their cities. The land and everything in it shuddered at the sound of his roaring.

EZK.19.BSB: Then the nations set out against him from the provinces on every side. They spread their net over him; he was trapped in their pit.
EZK.19.KJV: Then the nations set against him on every side from the provinces, and spread their net over him: he was taken in their pit.
EZK.19.PLAIN: Then the nations set out against him from the provinces on every side. They spread their net over him; he was trapped in their pit.

EZK.19.BSB: With hooks they caged him and brought him to the king of Babylon. They brought him into captivity so that his roar was heard no longer on the mountains of Israel.
EZK.19.KJV: And they put him in ward in chains, and brought him to the king of Babylon: they brought him into holds, that his voice should no more be heard on the mountains of Israel. ¶
EZK.19.PLAIN: With hooks they caged him and brought him to the king of Babylon. They brought him into captivity so that his roar was heard no longer on the mountains of Israel.

EZK.19.BSB: Your mother was like a vine in your vineyard, planted by the water; it was fruitful and full of branches because of the abundant waters.
EZK.19.KJV: Your mother is like a vine in your blood, planted by the waters: she was fruitful and full of branches by reason of many waters.
EZK.19.PLAIN: Your mother was like a vine in your vineyard, planted by the water; it was fruitful and full of branches because of the abundant waters.

EZK.19.BSB: It had strong branches, fit for a ruler’s scepter. It towered high above the thick branches, conspicuous for its height and for its dense foliage.
EZK.19.KJV: And she had strong rods for the scepters of them that bore rule, and her stature was exalted among the thick branches, and she appeared in her height with the multitude of her branches.
EZK.19.PLAIN: It had strong branches, fit for a ruler’s scepter. It towered high above the thick branches, conspicuous for its height and for its dense foliage.

EZK.19.BSB: But it was uprooted in fury, cast down to the ground, and the east wind dried up its fruit. Its strong branches were stripped off and they withered; the fire consumed them.
EZK.19.KJV: But she was plucked up in fury, she was cast down to the ground, and the east wind dried up her fruit: her strong rods were broken and withered; the fire consumed them.
EZK.19.PLAIN: But it was uprooted in fury, cast down to the ground, and the east wind dried up its fruit. Its strong branches were stripped off and they withered; the fire consumed them.

EZK.19.BSB: Now it is planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land.
EZK.19.KJV: And now she is planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty ground.
EZK.19.PLAIN: Now it is planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land.

EZK.19.BSB: Fire has gone out from its main branch and devoured its fruit; on it no strong branch remains fit for a ruler’s scepter.’ This is a lament and shall be used as a lament.”
EZK.19.KJV: And fire is gone out of a rod of her branches, which has devoured her fruit, so that she has no strong rod to be a scepter to rule. This is a lamentation, and shall be for a lamentation.
EZK.19.PLAIN: Fire has gone out from its main branch and devoured its fruit; on it no strong branch remains fit for a ruler’s scepter.’ This is a lament and shall be used as a lament.”

EZK.20.BSB: In the seventh year, on the tenth day of the fifth month, some of the elders of Israel came to inquire of the LORD, and they sat down before me.
EZK.20.KJV: And it came to pass in the seventh year, in the fifth month, the tenth day of the month, that certain of the elders of Israel came to inquire of the LORD, and sat before me.
EZK.20.PLAIN: In the seventh year, on the tenth day of the fifth month, some of the elders of Israel came to inquire of the Lord, and they sat down before me.

EZK.20.BSB: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
EZK.20.KJV: Then came the word of the LORD to me, saying,
EZK.20.PLAIN: Then the word of the Lord came to me, saying,

EZK.20.BSB: “Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: Have you come to inquire of Me? As surely as I live, I will not be consulted by you, declares the Lord GOD.
EZK.20.KJV: Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel, and say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD; Are you come to inquire of me? As I live, said the Lord GOD, I will not be inquired of by you.
EZK.20.PLAIN: “Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: Have you come to inquire of Me? As surely as I live, I will not be consulted by you, declares the Lord GOD.

EZK.20.BSB: Will you judge them, will you judge them, son of man? Confront them with the abominations of their fathers
EZK.20.KJV: Will you judge them, son of man, will you judge them? cause them to know the abominations of their fathers: ¶
EZK.20.PLAIN: Will you judge them, will you judge them, son of man? Confront them with the abominations of their fathers

EZK.20.BSB: and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: On the day I chose Israel, I swore an oath to the descendants of the house of Jacob and made Myself known to them in the land of Egypt. With an uplifted hand I said to them, ‘I am the LORD your God.’
EZK.20.KJV: And say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD; In the day when I chose Israel, and lifted up my hand to the seed of the house of Jacob, and made myself known to them in the land of Egypt, when I lifted up my hand to them, saying, I am the LORD your God;
EZK.20.PLAIN: and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: On the day I chose Israel, I swore an oath to the descendants of the house of Jacob and made Myself known to them in the land of Egypt. With an uplifted hand I said to them, ‘I am the Lord your God.’

EZK.20.BSB: On that day I swore to bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land that I had searched out for them, a land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands.
EZK.20.KJV: In the day that I lifted up my hand to them, to bring them forth of the land of Egypt into a land that I had espied for them, flowing with milk and honey, which is the glory of all lands:
EZK.20.PLAIN: On that day I swore to bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land that I had searched out for them, a land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands.

EZK.20.BSB: And I said to them: ‘Each of you must throw away the abominations before his eyes, and you must not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.’
EZK.20.KJV: Then said I to them, Cast you away every man the abominations of his eyes, and defile not yourselves with the idols of Egypt: I am the LORD your God.
EZK.20.PLAIN: And I said to them: ‘Each of you must throw away the abominations before his eyes, and you must not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.’

EZK.20.BSB: But they rebelled against Me and refused to listen. None of them cast away the abominations before their eyes, and they did not forsake the idols of Egypt. So I resolved to pour out My wrath upon them and vent My anger against them in the land of Egypt.
EZK.20.KJV: But they rebelled against me, and would not listen to me: they did not every man cast away the abominations of their eyes, neither did they forsake the idols of Egypt: then I said, I will pour out my fury on them, to accomplish my anger against them in the middle of the land of Egypt.
EZK.20.PLAIN: But they rebelled against Me and refused to listen. None of them cast away the abominations before their eyes, and they did not forsake the idols of Egypt. So I resolved to pour out My wrath upon them and vent My anger against them in the land of Egypt.

EZK.20.BSB: But I acted for the sake of My name, that it should not be profaned in the eyes of the nations among whom they were living, in whose sight I had revealed Myself to Israel by bringing them out of the land of Egypt.
EZK.20.KJV: But I worked for my name’s sake, that it should not be polluted before the heathen, among whom they were, in whose sight I made myself known to them, in bringing them forth out of the land of Egypt. ¶
EZK.20.PLAIN: But I acted for the sake of My name, that it should not be profaned in the eyes of the nations among whom they were living, in whose sight I had revealed Myself to Israel by bringing them out of the land of Egypt.

EZK.20.BSB: So I brought them out of the land of Egypt and led them into the wilderness.
EZK.20.KJV: Why I caused them to go forth out of the land of Egypt, and brought them into the wilderness.
EZK.20.PLAIN: So I brought them out of the land of Egypt and led them into the wilderness.

EZK.20.BSB: And I gave them My statutes and made known to them My ordinances—for the man who does these things will live by them.
EZK.20.KJV: And I gave them my statutes, and showed them my judgments, which if a man do, he shall even live in them.
EZK.20.PLAIN: And I gave them My statutes and made known to them My ordinances—for the man who does these things will live by them.

EZK.20.BSB: I also gave them My Sabbaths as a sign between us, so that they would know that I am the LORD who sanctifies them.
EZK.20.KJV: Moreover also I gave them my sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am the LORD that sanctify them.
EZK.20.PLAIN: I also gave them My Sabbaths as a sign between us, so that they would know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them.

EZK.20.BSB: Yet the house of Israel rebelled against Me in the wilderness. Then I resolved to pour out My wrath upon them and put an end to them in the wilderness.
EZK.20.KJV: But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness: they walked not in my statutes, and they despised my judgments, which if a man do, he shall even live in them; and my sabbaths they greatly polluted: then I said, I would pour out my fury on them in the wilderness, to consume them.
EZK.20.PLAIN: Yet the house of Israel rebelled against Me in the wilderness. They did not follow My statutes and they rejected My ordinances—though the man who does these things will live by them—and they utterly profaned My Sabbaths. EZK.20.BSB: But I acted for the sake of My name, so that it would not be profaned in the eyes of the nations in whose sight I had brought them out.
EZK.20.KJV: But I worked for my name’s sake, that it should not be polluted before the heathen, in whose sight I brought them out.
EZK.20.PLAIN: But I acted for the sake of My name, so that it would not be profaned in the eyes of the nations in whose sight I had brought them out.

EZK.20.BSB: Moreover, with an uplifted hand I swore to them in the wilderness that I would not bring them into the land that I had given them—a land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands—
EZK.20.KJV: Yet also I lifted up my hand to them in the wilderness, that I would not bring them into the land which I had given them, flowing with milk and honey, which is the glory of all lands;
EZK.20.PLAIN: Moreover, with an uplifted hand I swore to them in the wilderness that I would not bring them into the land that I had given them—a land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands—

EZK.20.BSB: because they kept rejecting My ordinances, refusing to walk in My statutes, and profaning My Sabbaths; for their hearts continually went after their idols.
EZK.20.KJV: Because they despised my judgments, and walked not in my statutes, but polluted my sabbaths: for their heart went after their idols.
EZK.20.PLAIN: because they kept rejecting My ordinances, refusing to walk in My statutes, and profaning My Sabbaths; for their hearts continually went after their idols.

EZK.20.BSB: Yet I looked on them with pity and did not destroy them or bring them to an end in the wilderness.
EZK.20.KJV: Nevertheless my eye spared them from destroying them, neither did I make an end of them in the wilderness.
EZK.20.PLAIN: Yet I looked on them with pity and did not destroy them or bring them to an end in the wilderness.

EZK.20.BSB: In the wilderness I said to their children: ‘Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers or keep their ordinances or defile yourselves with their idols.
EZK.20.KJV: But I said to their children in the wilderness, Walk you not in the statutes of your fathers, neither observe their judgments, nor defile yourselves with their idols:
EZK.20.PLAIN: In the wilderness I said to their children: ‘Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers or keep their ordinances or defile yourselves with their idols.

EZK.20.BSB: I am the LORD your God; walk in My statutes, keep My ordinances, and practice them.
EZK.20.KJV: I am the LORD your God; walk in my statutes, and keep my judgments, and do them;
EZK.20.PLAIN: I am the Lord your God; walk in My statutes, keep My ordinances, and practice them.

EZK.20.BSB: Keep My Sabbaths holy, that they may be a sign between us, so that you may know that I am the LORD your God.’
EZK.20.KJV: And hallow my sabbaths; and they shall be a sign between me and you, that you may know that I am the LORD your God.
EZK.20.PLAIN: Keep My Sabbaths holy, that they may be a sign between us, so that you may know that I am the Lord your God.’

EZK.20.BSB: But the children rebelled against Me. They did not walk in My statutes or carefully observe My ordinances—though the man who does these things will live by them—and they profaned My Sabbaths. So I resolved to pour out My wrath upon them and vent My anger against them in the wilderness.
EZK.20.KJV: Notwithstanding the children rebelled against me: they walked not in my statutes, neither kept my judgments to do them, which if a man do, he shall even live in them; they polluted my sabbaths: then I said, I would pour out my fury on them, to accomplish my anger against them in the wilderness.
EZK.20.PLAIN: But the children rebelled against Me. So I resolved to pour out My wrath upon them and vent My anger against them in the wilderness.

EZK.20.BSB: But I withheld My hand and acted for the sake of My name, so that it would not be profaned in the eyes of the nations in whose sight I had brought them out.
EZK.20.KJV: Nevertheless I withdrew my hand, and worked for my name’s sake, that it should not be polluted in the sight of the heathen, in whose sight I brought them forth.
EZK.20.PLAIN: But I withheld My hand and acted for the sake of My name, so that it would not be profaned in the eyes of the nations in whose sight I had brought them out.

EZK.20.BSB: However, with an uplifted hand I swore to them in the wilderness that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands.
EZK.20.KJV: I lifted up my hand to them also in the wilderness, that I would scatter them among the heathen, and disperse them through the countries;
EZK.20.PLAIN: However, with an uplifted hand I swore to them in the wilderness that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands.

EZK.20.BSB: For they did not practice My ordinances, but they rejected My statutes and profaned My Sabbaths, fixing their eyes on the idols of their fathers.
EZK.20.KJV: Because they had not executed my judgments, but had despised my statutes, and had polluted my sabbaths, and their eyes were after their fathers’ idols.
EZK.20.PLAIN: For they did not practice My ordinances, but they rejected My statutes and profaned My Sabbaths, fixing their eyes on the idols of their fathers.

EZK.20.BSB: I also gave them over to statutes that were not good and ordinances by which they could not live.
EZK.20.KJV: Why I gave them also statutes that were not good, and judgments whereby they should not live;
EZK.20.PLAIN: I also gave them over to statutes that were not good and ordinances by which they could not live.

EZK.20.BSB: And I pronounced them unclean through their gifts—the sacrifice of every firstborn in the fire—so that I might devastate them, in order that they would know that I am the LORD.
EZK.20.KJV: And I polluted them in their own gifts, in that they caused to pass through the fire all that opens the womb, that I might make them desolate, to the end that they might know that I am the LORD. ¶
