JOL.1.BSB: It has laid waste My grapevine and splintered My fig tree. It has stripped off the bark and thrown it away; the branches have turned white.
JOL.1.KJV: He has laid my vine waste, and barked my fig tree: he has made it clean bore, and cast it away; the branches thereof are made white. ¶
JOL.1.PLAIN: It has laid waste My grapevine and splintered My fig tree. It has stripped off the bark and thrown it away; the branches have turned white.

JOL.1.BSB: Wail like a virgin dressed in sackcloth, grieving for the husband of her youth.
JOL.1.KJV: Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth.
JOL.1.PLAIN: Wail like a virgin dressed in sackcloth, grieving for the husband of her youth.

JOL.1.BSB: Grain and drink offerings have been cut off from the house of the LORD; the priests are in mourning, those who minister before the LORD.
JOL.1.KJV: The meat offering and the drink offering is cut off from the house of the LORD; the priests, the LORD’s ministers, mourn.
JOL.1.PLAIN: Grain and drink offerings have been cut off from the house of the Lord; the priests are in mourning, those who minister before the Lord.

JOL.1.BSB: The field is ruined; the land mourns. For the grain is destroyed, the new wine is dried up, and the oil fails.
JOL.1.KJV: The field is wasted, the land mourns; for the corn is wasted: the new wine is dried up, the oil languishes.
JOL.1.PLAIN: The field is ruined; the land mourns. For the grain is destroyed, the new wine is dried up, and the oil fails.

JOL.1.BSB: Be dismayed, O farmers, wail, O vinedressers, over the wheat and barley, because the harvest of the field has perished.
JOL.1.KJV: Be you ashamed, O you farmers; howl, O you vinedressers, for the wheat and for the barley; because the harvest of the field is perished.
JOL.1.PLAIN: Be dismayed, O farmers, wail, O vinedressers, over the wheat and barley, because the harvest of the field has perished.

JOL.1.BSB: The grapevine is dried up, and the fig tree is withered; the pomegranate, palm, and apple— all the trees of the orchard—are withered. Surely the joy of mankind has dried up.
JOL.1.KJV: The vine is dried up, and the fig tree languishes; the pomegranate tree, the palm tree also, and the apple tree, even all the trees of the field, are withered: because joy is withered away from the sons of men.
JOL.1.PLAIN: The grapevine is dried up, and the fig tree is withered; the pomegranate, palm, and apple— all the trees of the orchard—are withered. Surely the joy of mankind has dried up.

JOL.1.BSB: Put on sackcloth and lament, O priests; wail, O ministers of the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, O ministers of my God, because the grain and drink offerings are withheld from the house of your God.
JOL.1.KJV: Gird yourselves, and lament, you priests: howl, you ministers of the altar: come, lie all night in sackcloth, you ministers of my God: for the meat offering and the drink offering is withheld from the house of your God. ¶
JOL.1.PLAIN: Put on sackcloth and lament, O priests; wail, O ministers of the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, O ministers of my God, because the grain and drink offerings are withheld from the house of your God.

JOL.1.BSB: Consecrate a fast; proclaim a solemn assembly! Gather the elders and all the residents of the land to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.
JOL.1.KJV: Sanctify you a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land into the house of the LORD your God, and cry to the LORD,
JOL.1.PLAIN: Consecrate a fast; proclaim a solemn assembly! Gather the elders and all the residents of the land to the house of the Lord your God, and cry out to the Lord.

JOL.1.BSB: Alas for the day! For the Day of the LORD is near, and it will come as destruction from the Almighty.
JOL.1.KJV: Alas for the day! for the day of the LORD is at hand, and as a destruction from the Almighty shall it come.
JOL.1.PLAIN: Alas for the day! For the Day of the Lord is near, and it will come as destruction from the Almighty.

JOL.1.BSB: Has not the food been cut off before our very eyes— joy and gladness from the house of our God?
JOL.1.KJV: Is not the meat cut off before our eyes, yes, joy and gladness from the house of our God?
JOL.1.PLAIN: Has not the food been cut off before our very eyes— joy and gladness from the house of our God?

JOL.1.BSB: The seeds lie shriveled beneath the clods; the storehouses are in ruins; the granaries are broken down, for the grain has withered away.
JOL.1.KJV: The seed is rotten under their clods, the garners are laid desolate, the barns are broken down; for the corn is withered.
JOL.1.PLAIN: The seeds lie shriveled beneath the clods; the storehouses are in ruins; the granaries are broken down, for the grain has withered away.

JOL.1.BSB: How the cattle groan! The herds wander in confusion because they have no pasture. Even the flocks of sheep are suffering.
JOL.1.KJV: How do the beasts groan! the herds of cattle are perplexed, because they have no pasture; yes, the flocks of sheep are made desolate.
JOL.1.PLAIN: How the cattle groan! The herds wander in confusion because they have no pasture. Even the flocks of sheep are suffering.

JOL.1.BSB: To You, O LORD, I call, for fire has consumed the open pastures and flames have scorched all the trees of the field.
JOL.1.KJV: O LORD, to you will I cry: for the fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and the flame has burned all the trees of the field.
JOL.1.PLAIN: To You, O Lord, I call, for fire has consumed the open pastures and flames have scorched all the trees of the field.

JOL.1.BSB: Even the beasts of the field pant for You, for the streams of water have dried up, and fire has consumed the open pastures.
JOL.1.KJV: The beasts of the field cry also to you: for the rivers of waters are dried up, and the fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness.
JOL.1.PLAIN: Even the beasts of the field pant for You, for the streams of water have dried up, and fire has consumed the open pastures.

JOL.2.BSB: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion; sound the alarm on My holy mountain! Let all who dwell in the land tremble, for the Day of the LORD is coming; indeed, it is near—
JOL.2.KJV: Blow you the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain: let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: for the day of the LORD comes, for it is near at hand;
JOL.2.PLAIN: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion; sound the alarm on My holy mountain! Let all who dwell in the land tremble, for the Day of the Lord is coming; indeed, it is near—

JOL.2.BSB: a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness. Like the dawn overspreading the mountains a great and strong army appears, such as never was of old, nor will ever be in ages to come.
JOL.2.KJV: A day of darkness and of gloominess, a day of clouds and of thick darkness, as the morning spread on the mountains: a great people and a strong; there has not been ever the like, neither shall be any more after it, even to the years of many generations.
JOL.2.PLAIN: a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness. Like the dawn overspreading the mountains a great and strong army appears, such as never was of old, nor will ever be in ages to come.

JOL.2.BSB: Before them a fire devours, and behind them a flame scorches. The land before them is like the Garden of Eden, but behind them, it is like a desert wasteland— surely nothing will escape them.
JOL.2.KJV: A fire devours before them; and behind them a flame burns: the land is as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them a desolate wilderness; yes, and nothing shall escape them.
JOL.2.PLAIN: Before them a fire devours, and behind them a flame scorches. The land before them is like the Garden of Eden, but behind them, it is like a desert wasteland— surely nothing will escape them.

JOL.2.BSB: Their appearance is like that of horses, and they gallop like swift steeds.
JOL.2.KJV: The appearance of them is as the appearance of horses; and as horsemen, so shall they run.
JOL.2.PLAIN: Their appearance is like that of horses, and they gallop like swift steeds.

JOL.2.BSB: With a sound like that of chariots they bound over the mountaintops, like the crackling of fire consuming stubble, like a mighty army deployed for battle.
JOL.2.KJV: Like the noise of chariots on the tops of mountains shall they leap, like the noise of a flame of fire that devours the stubble, as a strong people set in battle array.
JOL.2.PLAIN: With a sound like that of chariots they bound over the mountaintops, like the crackling of fire consuming stubble, like a mighty army deployed for battle.

JOL.2.BSB: Nations writhe in horror before them; every face turns pale.
JOL.2.KJV: Before their face the people shall be much pained: all faces shall gather blackness.
JOL.2.PLAIN: Nations writhe in horror before them; every face turns pale.

JOL.2.BSB: They charge like mighty men; they scale the walls like men of war. Each one marches in formation, not swerving from the course.
JOL.2.KJV: They shall run like mighty men; they shall climb the wall like men of war; and they shall march every one on his ways, and they shall not break their ranks:
JOL.2.PLAIN: They charge like mighty men; they scale the walls like men of war. Each one marches in formation, not swerving from the course.

JOL.2.BSB: They do not jostle one another; each proceeds in his path. They burst through the defenses, never breaking ranks.
JOL.2.KJV: Neither shall one thrust another; they shall walk every one in his path: and when they fall on the sword, they shall not be wounded.
JOL.2.PLAIN: They do not jostle one another; each proceeds in his path. They burst through the defenses, never breaking ranks.

JOL.2.BSB: They storm the city; they run along the wall; they climb into houses, entering through windows like thieves.
JOL.2.KJV: They shall run to and fro in the city; they shall run on the wall, they shall climb up on the houses; they shall enter in at the windows like a thief.
JOL.2.PLAIN: They storm the city; they run along the wall; they climb into houses, entering through windows like thieves.

JOL.2.BSB: Before them the earth quakes; the heavens tremble. The sun and moon grow dark, and the stars lose their brightness.
JOL.2.KJV: The earth shall quake before them; the heavens shall tremble: the sun and the moon shall be dark, and the stars shall withdraw their shining:
JOL.2.PLAIN: Before them the earth quakes; the heavens tremble. The sun and moon grow dark, and the stars lose their brightness.

JOL.2.BSB: The LORD raises His voice in the presence of His army. Indeed, His camp is very large, for mighty are those who obey His command. For the Day of the LORD is great and very dreadful. Who can endure it?

JOL.2.PLAIN: The Lord raises His voice in the presence of His army. Indeed, His camp is very large, for mighty are those who obey His command. For the Day of the Lord is great and very dreadful. Who can endure it?

JOL.2.BSB: “Yet even now,” declares the LORD, “return to Me with all your heart, with fasting, weeping, and mourning.”
JOL.2.KJV: Therefore also now, says the LORD, turn you even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning:
JOL.2.PLAIN: “Yet even now,” declares the Lord, “return to Me with all your heart, with fasting, weeping, and mourning.”

JOL.2.BSB: So rend your hearts and not your garments, and return to the LORD your God. For He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion. And He relents from sending disaster.
JOL.2.KJV: And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn to the LORD your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repents him of the evil.
JOL.2.PLAIN: Rend your heart and not your garments. Return to the Lord your God, for he is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in love, and he relents from sending calamity.

JOL.2.BSB: Who knows? He may turn and relent and leave a blessing behind Him— grain and drink offerings for the LORD your God.
JOL.2.KJV: Who knows if he will return and repent, and leave a blessing behind him; even a meat offering and a drink offering to the LORD your God? ¶
JOL.2.PLAIN: Who knows? He may turn and relent and leave a blessing behind Him— grain and drink offerings for the Lord your God.

JOL.2.BSB: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion, consecrate a fast, proclaim a sacred assembly.
JOL.2.KJV: Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly:
JOL.2.PLAIN: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion, consecrate a fast, proclaim a sacred assembly.

JOL.2.BSB: Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the aged, gather the children, even those nursing at the breast. Let the bridegroom leave his room, and the bride her chamber.
JOL.2.KJV: Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children, and those that suck the breasts: let the bridegroom go forth of his chamber, and the bride out of her closet.
JOL.2.PLAIN: Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the aged, gather the children, even those nursing at the breast. Let the bridegroom leave his room, and the bride her chamber.

JOL.2.BSB: Let the priests who minister before the LORD weep between the portico and the altar, saying, “Spare Your people, O LORD, and do not make Your heritage a reproach, an object of scorn among the nations. Why should they say among the peoples, ‘Where is their God?’”
JOL.2.KJV: Let the priests, the ministers of the LORD, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare your people, O LORD, and give not your heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: why should they say among the people, Where is their God? ¶
JOL.2.PLAIN: Let the priests who minister before the Lord weep between the portico and the altar, saying, “Spare Your people, O Lord, and do not make Your heritage a reproach, an object of scorn among the nations. Why should they say among the peoples, ‘Where is their God?’”

JOL.2.BSB: Then the LORD became jealous for His land, and He spared His people.
JOL.2.KJV: Then will the LORD be jealous for his land, and pity his people.
JOL.2.PLAIN: Then the Lord became jealous for His land, and He spared His people.

JOL.2.BSB: And the LORD answered His people: “Behold, I will send you grain, new wine, and oil, and by them you will be satisfied. I will never again make you a reproach among the nations.
JOL.2.KJV: Yes, the LORD will answer and say to his people, Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil, and you shall be satisfied therewith: and I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen:
JOL.2.PLAIN: And the Lord answered His people: “Look closely — I will send you grain, new wine, and oil, and by them you will be satisfied. I will never again make you a reproach among the nations.

JOL.2.BSB: The northern army I will drive away from you, banishing it to a barren and desolate land, its front ranks into the Eastern Sea, and its rear guard into the Western Sea. And its stench will rise; its foul odor will ascend. For He has done great things.
JOL.2.KJV: But I will remove far off from you the northern army, and will drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea, and his stink shall come up, and his ill smell shall come up, because he has done great things. ¶
JOL.2.PLAIN: The northern army I will drive away from you, banishing it to a barren and desolate land, its front ranks into the Eastern Sea, and its rear guard into the Western Sea. And its stench will rise; its foul odor will ascend. For He has done great things.

JOL.2.BSB: Do not be afraid, O land; rejoice and be glad, for the LORD has done great things.
JOL.2.KJV: Fear not, O land; be glad and rejoice: for the LORD will do great things.
JOL.2.PLAIN: Do not be afraid, O land; rejoice and be glad, for the Lord has done great things.

JOL.2.BSB: Do not be afraid, O beasts of the field, for the open pastures have turned green, the trees bear their fruit, and the fig tree and vine yield their best.
JOL.2.KJV: Be not afraid, you beasts of the field: for the pastures of the wilderness do spring, for the tree bears her fruit, the fig tree and the vine do yield their strength.
JOL.2.PLAIN: Do not be afraid, O beasts of the field, for the open pastures have turned green, the trees bear their fruit, and the fig tree and vine yield their best.

JOL.2.BSB: Be glad, O children of Zion, and rejoice in the LORD your God, for He has given you the autumn rains for your vindication. He sends you showers, both autumn and spring rains, as before.
JOL.2.KJV: Be glad then, you children of Zion, and rejoice in the LORD your God: for he has given you the former rain moderately, and he will cause to come down for you the rain, the former rain, and the latter rain in the first month.
JOL.2.PLAIN: Be glad, O children of Zion, and rejoice in the Lord your God, for He has given you the autumn rains for your vindication. He sends you showers, both autumn and spring rains, as before.

JOL.2.BSB: The threshing floors will be full of grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.
JOL.2.KJV: And the floors shall be full of wheat, and the vats shall overflow with wine and oil.
JOL.2.PLAIN: The threshing floors will be full of grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.

JOL.2.BSB: I will repay you for the years eaten by locusts— the swarming locust, the young locust, the destroying locust, and the devouring locust— My great army that I sent against you.
JOL.2.KJV: And I will restore to you the years that the locust has eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpillar, and the palmerworm, my great army which I sent among you.
JOL.2.PLAIN: I will restore to you the years the locusts have eaten — the great army I sent among you.

JOL.2.BSB: You will have plenty to eat, until you are satisfied. You will praise the name of the LORD your God, who has worked wonders for you. My people will never again be put to shame.
JOL.2.KJV: And you shall eat in plenty, and be satisfied, and praise the name of the LORD your God, that has dealt wondrously with you: and my people shall never be ashamed.
JOL.2.PLAIN: You will have plenty to eat, until you are satisfied. You will praise the name of the Lord your God, who has worked wonders for you. My people will never again be put to shame.

JOL.2.BSB: Then you will know that I am present in Israel and that I am the LORD your God, and there is no other. My people will never again be put to shame.
JOL.2.KJV: And you shall know that I am in the middle of Israel, and that I am the LORD your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed. ¶
JOL.2.PLAIN: Then you will know that I am present in Israel and that I am the Lord your God, and there is no other. My people will never again be put to shame.

JOL.2.BSB: And afterward, I will pour out My Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions.
JOL.2.KJV: And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions:
JOL.2.PLAIN: And afterward, I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions.

JOL.2.BSB: Even on My menservants and maidservants, I will pour out My Spirit in those days.
JOL.2.KJV: And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days will I pour out my spirit.
JOL.2.PLAIN: Even on My menservants and maidservants, I will pour out My Spirit in those days.

JOL.2.BSB: I will show wonders in the heavens and on the earth, blood and fire and columns of smoke.
JOL.2.KJV: And I will show wonders in the heavens and in the earth, blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke.
JOL.2.PLAIN: I will show wonders in the heavens and on the earth, blood and fire and columns of smoke.

JOL.2.BSB: The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the LORD.
JOL.2.KJV: The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of the LORD come.
JOL.2.PLAIN: The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the Lord.

JOL.2.BSB: And everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as the LORD has promised, among the remnant called by the LORD.
JOL.2.KJV: And it shall come to pass, that whoever shall call on the name of the LORD shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the LORD has said, and in the remnant whom the LORD shall call.
JOL.2.PLAIN: And everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as the Lord has promised, among the remnant called by the Lord.

JOL.3.BSB: “Yes, in those days and at that time, when I restore Judah and Jerusalem from captivity,
JOL.3.KJV: For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,
JOL.3.PLAIN: “Yes, in those days and at that time, when I restore Judah and Jerusalem from captivity,

JOL.3.BSB: I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment against them concerning My people, My inheritance, Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations as they divided up My land.

JOL.3.BSB: They cast lots for My people; they bartered a boy for a prostitute and sold a girl for wine to drink.
JOL.3.KJV: And they have cast lots for my people; and have given a boy for an harlot, and sold a girl for wine, that they might drink.
JOL.3.PLAIN: They cast lots for My people; they bartered a boy for a prostitute and sold a girl for wine to drink.

JOL.3.BSB: Now what do you have against Me, O Tyre, Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia? Are you rendering against Me a recompense? If you retaliate against Me, I will swiftly and speedily return your recompense upon your heads.
JOL.3.KJV: Yes, and what have you to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine? will you render me a recompense? and if you recompense me, swiftly and speedily will I return your recompense on your own head;
JOL.3.PLAIN: Now what do you have against Me, O Tyre, Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia? Are you rendering against Me a recompense? If you retaliate against Me, I will swiftly and speedily return your recompense upon your heads.

JOL.3.BSB: For you took My silver and gold and carried off My finest treasures to your temples.
JOL.3.KJV: Because you have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried into your temples my goodly pleasant things:
JOL.3.PLAIN: For you took My silver and gold and carried off My finest treasures to your temples.

JOL.3.BSB: You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, to send them far from their homeland.
JOL.3.KJV: The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have you sold to the Grecians, that you might remove them far from their border.
JOL.3.PLAIN: You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, to send them far from their homeland.

JOL.3.BSB: Behold, I will rouse them from the places to which you sold them; I will return your recompense upon your heads.
JOL.3.KJV: Behold, I will raise them out of the place where you have sold them, and will return your recompense on your own head:
JOL.3.PLAIN: Look closely — I will rouse them from the places to which you sold them; I will return your recompense upon your heads.

JOL.3.BSB: I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans—to a distant nation.” Indeed, the LORD has spoken.
JOL.3.KJV: And I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah, and they shall sell them to the Sabeans, to a people far off: for the LORD has spoken it. ¶
JOL.3.PLAIN: I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans—to a distant nation.” Indeed, the Lord has spoken.

JOL.3.BSB: Proclaim this among the nations: “Prepare for war; rouse the mighty men; let all the men of war advance and attack!
JOL.3.KJV: Proclaim you this among the Gentiles; Prepare war, wake up the mighty men, let all the men of war draw near; let them come up:
JOL.3.PLAIN: Proclaim this among the nations: “Prepare for war; rouse the mighty men; let all the men of war advance and attack!

JOL.3.BSB: Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears. Let the weak say, ‘I am strong!’
JOL.3.KJV: Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears: let the weak say, I am strong.
JOL.3.PLAIN: Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears. Let the weak say, ‘I am strong!’

JOL.3.BSB: Come quickly, all you surrounding nations, and gather yourselves. Bring down Your mighty ones, O LORD.
JOL.3.KJV: Assemble yourselves, and come, all you heathen, and gather yourselves together round about: thither cause your mighty ones to come down, O LORD.
JOL.3.PLAIN: Come quickly, all you surrounding nations, and gather yourselves. Bring down Your mighty ones, O Lord.

JOL.3.BSB: Let the nations be roused and advance to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit down to judge all the nations on every side.
JOL.3.KJV: Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about.
JOL.3.PLAIN: Let the nations be roused and advance to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit down to judge all the nations on every side.

JOL.3.BSB: Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come, trample the grapes, for the winepress is full; the wine vats overflow because their wickedness is great.
JOL.3.KJV: Put you in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe: come, get you down; for the press is full, the fats overflow; for their wickedness is great.
JOL.3.PLAIN: Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come, trample the grapes, for the winepress is full; the wine vats overflow because their wickedness is great.

JOL.3.BSB: Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision! For the Day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision.
JOL.3.KJV: Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision: for the day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision.
JOL.3.PLAIN: Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision! For the Day of the Lord is near in the valley of decision.

JOL.3.BSB: The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will no longer shine.
JOL.3.KJV: The sun and the moon shall be darkened, and the stars shall withdraw their shining.
JOL.3.PLAIN: The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will no longer shine.

JOL.3.BSB: The LORD will roar from Zion and raise His voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth will tremble. But the LORD will be a refuge for His people, a stronghold for the people of Israel.
JOL.3.KJV: The LORD also shall roar out of Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth shall shake: but the LORD will be the hope of his people, and the strength of the children of Israel.
JOL.3.PLAIN: The Lord will roar from Zion and raise His voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth will tremble. But the Lord will be a refuge for His people, a stronghold for the people of Israel.

JOL.3.BSB: Then you will know that I am the LORD your God, who dwells in Zion, My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy, never again to be overrun by foreigners.
JOL.3.KJV: So shall you know that I am the LORD your God dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain: then shall Jerusalem be holy, and there shall no strangers pass through her any more. ¶
JOL.3.PLAIN: Then you will know that I am the Lord your God, who dwells in Zion, My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy, never again to be overrun by foreigners.

JOL.3.BSB: And in that day the mountains will drip with sweet wine, and the hills will flow with milk. All the streams of Judah will run with water, and a spring will flow from the house of the LORD to water the Valley of Acacias.
JOL.3.KJV: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the mountains shall drop down new wine, and the hills shall flow with milk, and all the rivers of Judah shall flow with waters, and a fountain shall come forth out of the house of the LORD, and shall water the valley of Shittim.
JOL.3.PLAIN: And in that day the mountains will drip with sweet wine, and the hills will flow with milk. All the streams of Judah will run with water, and a spring will flow from the house of the Lord to water the Valley of Acacias.

JOL.3.BSB: Egypt will become desolate, and Edom a desert wasteland, because of the violence done to the people of Judah, in whose land they shed innocent blood.
JOL.3.KJV: Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom shall be a desolate wilderness, for the violence against the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land.
JOL.3.PLAIN: Egypt will become desolate, and Edom a desert wasteland, because of the violence done to the people of Judah, in whose land they shed innocent blood.

JOL.3.BSB: But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
JOL.3.KJV: But Judah shall dwell for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
JOL.3.PLAIN: But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.

JOL.3.BSB: For I will avenge their blood, which I have not yet avenged.” For the LORD dwells in Zion.
JOL.3.KJV: For I will cleanse their blood that I have not cleansed: for the LORD dwells in Zion.
JOL.3.PLAIN: For I will avenge their blood, which I have not yet avenged.” For the Lord dwells in Zion.

AMO.9.BSB: “In that day I will restore the fallen tent of David. I will repair its gaps, restore its ruins, and rebuild it as in the days of old,

AMO.9.BSB: that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations that bear My name,” declares the LORD, who will do this.

AMO.9.KJV: And I will bring again the captivity of my people of Israel, and they shall build the waste cities, and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, and drink the wine thereof; they shall also make gardens, and eat the fruit of them.

OBA.1.BSB: This is the vision of Obadiah: This is what the Lord GOD says about Edom— We have heard a message from the LORD; an envoy has been sent among the nations to say, “Rise up, and let us go to battle against her!”—
OBA.1.KJV: The vision of Obadiah. Thus says the Lord GOD concerning Edom; We have heard a rumor from the LORD, and an ambassador is sent among the heathen, Arise you, and let us rise up against her in battle.
OBA.1.PLAIN: This is the vision of Obadiah: This is what the Lord GOD says about Edom— We have heard a message from the Lord; an envoy has been sent among the nations to say, “Rise up, and let us go to battle against her!”—

OBA.1.BSB: “Behold, I will make you small among the nations; you will be deeply despised.
OBA.1.KJV: Behold, I have made you small among the heathen: you are greatly despised. ¶
OBA.1.PLAIN: “Look closely — I will make you small among the nations; you will be deeply despised.

OBA.1.BSB: The pride of your heart has deceived you, O dwellers in the clefts of the rocks whose habitation is the heights, who say in your heart, ‘Who can bring me down to the ground?’
OBA.1.KJV: The pride of your heart has deceived you, you that dwell in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that says in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?
OBA.1.PLAIN: The pride of your heart has deceived you, O dwellers in the clefts of the rocks whose habitation is the heights, who say in your heart, ‘Who can bring me down to the ground?’

OBA.1.BSB: Though you soar like the eagle and make your nest among the stars, even from there I will bring you down,” declares the LORD.
OBA.1.KJV: Though you exalt yourself as the eagle, and though you set your nest among the stars, there will I bring you down, says the LORD.
OBA.1.PLAIN: Though you soar like the eagle and make your nest among the stars, even from there I will bring you down,” declares the Lord.

OBA.1.BSB: “If thieves came to you, if robbers by night— oh, how you will be ruined— would they not steal only what they wanted? If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleanings?
OBA.1.KJV: If thieves came to you, if robbers by night, (how are you cut off!) would they not have stolen till they had enough? if the grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some grapes?
OBA.1.PLAIN: “If thieves came to you, if robbers by night— oh, how you will be ruined— would they not steal only what they wanted? If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleanings?

OBA.1.BSB: But how Esau will be pillaged, his hidden treasures sought out!
OBA.1.KJV: How are the things of Esau searched out! how are his hidden things sought up!
OBA.1.PLAIN: But how Esau will be pillaged, his hidden treasures sought out!

OBA.1.BSB: All the men allied with you will drive you to the border; the men at peace with you will deceive and overpower you. Those who eat your bread will set a trap for you without your awareness of it.
OBA.1.KJV: All the men of your confederacy have brought you even to the border: the men that were at peace with you have deceived you, and prevailed against you; they that eat your bread have laid a wound under you: there is none understanding in him.
OBA.1.PLAIN: All the men allied with you will drive you to the border; the men at peace with you will deceive and overpower you. Those who eat your bread will set a trap for you without your awareness of it.

OBA.1.BSB: In that day, declares the LORD, will I not destroy the wise men of Edom and the men of understanding in the mountains of Esau?
OBA.1.KJV: Shall I not in that day, says the LORD, even destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mount of Esau?
OBA.1.PLAIN: In that day, declares the Lord, will I not destroy the wise men of Edom and the men of understanding in the mountains of Esau?

OBA.1.BSB: Then your mighty men, O Teman, will be terrified, so that everyone in the mountains of Esau will be cut down in the slaughter.
OBA.1.KJV: And your mighty men, O Teman, shall be dismayed, to the end that every one of the mount of Esau may be cut off by slaughter. ¶
OBA.1.PLAIN: Then your mighty men, O Teman, will be terrified, so that everyone in the mountains of Esau will be cut down in the slaughter.

OBA.1.BSB: Because of the violence against your brother Jacob, you will be covered with shame and cut off forever.
OBA.1.KJV: For your violence against your brother Jacob shame shall cover you, and you shall be cut off for ever.
OBA.1.PLAIN: Because of the violence against your brother Jacob, you will be covered with shame and cut off forever.

OBA.1.BSB: On the day you stood aloof while strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gate and cast lots for Jerusalem, you were just like one of them.
OBA.1.KJV: In the day that you stood on the other side, in the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots on Jerusalem, even you were as one of them.
OBA.1.PLAIN: On the day you stood aloof while strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gate and cast lots for Jerusalem, you were just like one of them.

OBA.1.BSB: But you should not gloat in that day, your brother’s day of misfortune, nor rejoice over the people of Judah in the day of their destruction, nor boast proudly in the day of their distress.
OBA.1.KJV: But you should not have looked on the day of your brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither should you have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction; neither should you have spoken proudly in the day of distress.
OBA.1.PLAIN: But you should not gloat in that day, your brother’s day of misfortune, nor rejoice over the people of Judah in the day of their destruction, nor boast proudly in the day of their distress.

OBA.1.BSB: You should not enter the gate of My people in the day of their disaster, nor gloat over their affliction in the day of their disaster, nor loot their wealth in the day of their disaster.
OBA.1.KJV: You should not have entered into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity; yes, you should not have looked on their affliction in the day of their calamity, nor have laid hands on their substance in the day of their calamity;
OBA.1.PLAIN: You should not enter the gate of My people in the day of their disaster, nor gloat over their affliction in the day of their disaster, nor loot their wealth in the day of their disaster.

OBA.1.BSB: Nor should you stand at the crossroads to cut off their fugitives, nor deliver up their survivors in the day of their distress.
OBA.1.KJV: Neither should you have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape; neither should you have delivered up those of his that did remain in the day of distress.
OBA.1.PLAIN: Nor should you stand at the crossroads to cut off their fugitives, nor deliver up their survivors in the day of their distress.

OBA.1.BSB: For the Day of the LORD is near for all the nations. As you have done, it will be done to you; your recompense will return upon your own head.
OBA.1.KJV: For the day of the LORD is near on all the heathen: as you have done, it shall be done to you: your reward shall return on your own head.
OBA.1.PLAIN: The day of the Lord is near for all nations. As you have done, it will be done to you; your deeds will return upon your own head.

OBA.1.BSB: For as you drank on My holy mountain, so all the nations will drink continually. They will drink and gulp it down; they will be as if they had never existed.
OBA.1.KJV: For as you have drunk on my holy mountain, so shall all the heathen drink continually, yes, they shall drink, and they shall swallow down, and they shall be as though they had not been. ¶
OBA.1.PLAIN: For as you drank on My holy mountain, so all the nations will drink continually. They will drink and gulp it down; they will be as if they had never existed.

OBA.1.BSB: But on Mount Zion there will be deliverance, and it will be holy, and the house of Jacob will reclaim their possession.
OBA.1.KJV: But on mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions.
OBA.1.PLAIN: But on Mount Zion there will be deliverance, and it will be holy, and the house of Jacob will reclaim their possession.

OBA.1.BSB: Then the house of Jacob will be a blazing fire, and the house of Joseph a burning flame; but the house of Esau will be stubble— Jacob will set it ablaze and consume it. Therefore no survivor will remain from the house of Esau.” For the LORD has spoken.
OBA.1.KJV: And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the LORD has spoken it.
OBA.1.PLAIN: Then the house of Jacob will be a blazing fire, and the house of Joseph a burning flame; but the house of Esau will be stubble— Jacob will set it ablaze and consume it. Therefore no survivor will remain from the house of Esau.” For the Lord has spoken.

OBA.1.BSB: Those from the Negev will possess the mountains of Esau; those from the foothills will possess the land of the Philistines. They will occupy the fields of Ephraim and Samaria, and Benjamin will possess Gilead.
OBA.1.KJV: And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau; and they of the plain the Philistines: and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria: and Benjamin shall possess Gilead.
OBA.1.PLAIN: Those from the Negev will possess the mountains of Esau; those from the foothills will possess the land of the Philistines. They will occupy the fields of Ephraim and Samaria, and Benjamin will possess Gilead.

OBA.1.KJV: And the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites, even to Zarephath; and the captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Sepharad, shall possess the cities of the south.
OBA.1.PLAIN: And the exiles of this host of the Israelites will possess the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath; and the exiles from Jerusalem who are in Sepharad will possess the cities of the Negev.

OBA.1.KJV: And saviors shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the LORD’s.
OBA.1.PLAIN: The deliverers will ascend Mount Zion to rule over the mountains of Esau. And the kingdom will belong to the Lord.

JON.1.BSB: Now the word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai, saying,
JON.1.KJV: Now the word of the LORD came to Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,
JON.1.PLAIN: Now the word of the Lord came to Jonah son of Amittai, saying,

JON.1.BSB: “Get up! Go to the great city of Nineveh and preach against it, because its wickedness has come up before Me.”
JON.1.KJV: Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me.
JON.1.PLAIN: “Get up! Go to the great city of Nineveh and preach against it, because its wickedness has come up before Me.”

JON.1.BSB: Jonah, however, got up to flee to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa and found a ship bound for Tarshish. So he paid the fare and went aboard to sail for Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.
JON.1.KJV: But Jonah rose up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the LORD, and went down to Joppa; and he found a ship going to Tarshish: so he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish from the presence of the LORD. ¶
JON.1.PLAIN: Jonah, however, got up to flee to Tarshish, away from the presence of the Lord. He went down to Joppa and found a ship bound for Tarshish. So he paid the fare and went aboard to sail for Tarshish, away from the presence of the Lord.

JON.1.BSB: Then the LORD hurled a great wind upon the sea, and such a violent storm arose that the ship was in danger of breaking apart.
JON.1.KJV: But the LORD sent out a great wind into the sea, and there was a mighty tempest in the sea, so that the ship was like to be broken.
JON.1.PLAIN: Then the Lord hurled a great wind upon the sea, and such a violent storm arose that the ship was in danger of breaking apart.

JON.1.BSB: The sailors were afraid, and each cried out to his own god. And they threw the ship’s cargo into the sea to lighten the load. But Jonah had gone down to the lowest part of the vessel, where he lay down and fell into a deep sleep.
JON.1.KJV: Then the mariners were afraid, and cried every man to his god, and cast forth the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten it of them. But Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.
JON.1.PLAIN: The sailors were afraid, and each cried out to his own god. And they threw the ship’s cargo into the sea to lighten the load. But Jonah had gone down to the lowest part of the vessel, where he lay down and fell into a deep sleep.

JON.1.BSB: The captain approached him and said, “How can you sleep? Get up and call upon your God. Perhaps this God will consider us, so that we may not perish.”
JON.1.KJV: So the shipmaster came to him, and said to him, What mean you, O sleeper? arise, call on your God, if so be that God will think on us, that we perish not.
JON.1.PLAIN: The captain approached him and said, “How can you sleep? Get up and call upon your God. Perhaps this God will consider us, so that we may not perish.”

JON.1.BSB: “Come!” said the sailors to one another. “Let us cast lots to find out who is responsible for this calamity that is upon us.” So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
JON.1.KJV: And they said every one to his fellow, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is on us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
JON.1.PLAIN: “Come!” said the sailors to one another. “Let us cast lots to find out who is responsible for this calamity that is upon us.” So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.

JON.1.BSB: “Tell us now,” they demanded, “who is to blame for this calamity that is upon us? What is your occupation, and where have you come from? What is your country, and who are your people?”
JON.1.KJV: Then said they to him, Tell us, we pray you, for whose cause this evil is on us; What is your occupation? and from where come you? what is your country? and of what people are you?
JON.1.PLAIN: “Tell us now,” they demanded, “who is to blame for this calamity that is upon us? What is your occupation, and where have you come from? What is your country, and who are your people?”

JON.1.BSB: “I am a Hebrew,” replied Jonah. “I worship the LORD, the God of the heavens, who made the sea and the dry land.”
JON.1.KJV: And he said to them, I am an Hebrew; and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, which has made the sea and the dry land.
JON.1.PLAIN: “I am a Hebrew,” replied Jonah. “I worship the Lord, the God of the heavens, who made the sea and the dry land.”

JON.1.BSB: Then the men were even more afraid and said to him, “What have you done?” The men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the LORD, because he had told them.

JON.1.PLAIN: Then the men were even more afraid and said to him, “What have you done?” The men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the Lord, because he had told them.

JON.1.BSB: Now the sea was growing worse and worse, so they said to Jonah, “What must we do to you to calm this sea for us?”
JON.1.KJV: Then said they to him, What shall we do to you, that the sea may be calm to us? for the sea worked, and was tempestuous.
JON.1.PLAIN: Now the sea was growing worse and worse, so they said to Jonah, “What must we do to you to calm this sea for us?”

JON.1.BSB: “Pick me up,” he answered, “and cast me into the sea, so it may quiet down for you. For I know that I am to blame for this violent storm that has come upon you.”
JON.1.KJV: And he said to them, Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm to you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is on you.
JON.1.PLAIN: “Pick me up,” he answered, “and cast me into the sea, so it may quiet down for you. For I know that I am to blame for this violent storm that has come upon you.”

JON.1.BSB: Nevertheless, the men rowed hard to get back to dry land, but they could not, for the sea was raging against them more and more.
JON.1.KJV: Nevertheless the men rowed hard to bring it to the land; but they could not: for the sea worked, and was tempestuous against them.
JON.1.PLAIN: Nevertheless, the men rowed hard to get back to dry land, but they could not, for the sea was raging against them more and more.

JON.1.BSB: So they cried out to the LORD: “Please, O LORD, do not let us perish on account of this man’s life! Do not charge us with innocent blood! For You, O LORD, have done as You pleased.”
JON.1.KJV: Why they cried to the LORD, and said, We beseech you, O LORD, we beseech you, let us not perish for this man’s life, and lay not on us innocent blood: for you, O LORD, have done as it pleased you.
JON.1.PLAIN: So they cried out to the Lord: “Please, O Lord, do not let us perish on account of this man’s life! Do not charge us with innocent blood! For You, O Lord, have done as You pleased.”

JON.1.BSB: At this, they picked up Jonah and cast him into the sea, and the raging sea grew calm.
JON.1.KJV: So they look up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea: and the sea ceased from her raging.
JON.1.PLAIN: At this, they picked up Jonah and cast him into the sea, and the raging sea grew calm.

JON.1.BSB: Then the men feared the LORD greatly, and they offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows to Him.
JON.1.KJV: Then the men feared the LORD exceedingly, and offered a sacrifice to the LORD, and made vows. ¶
JON.1.PLAIN: Then the men feared the Lord greatly, and they offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made vows to Him.

JON.1.BSB: Now the LORD had appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah spent three days and three nights in the belly of the fish.
JON.1.KJV: Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

JON.2.BSB: From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the LORD his God,

JON.2.PLAIN: From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the Lord his God,

JON.2.BSB: saying: “In my distress I called to the LORD, and He answered me. From the belly of Sheol I called for help, and You heard my voice.

JON.2.PLAIN: saying: “In my distress I called to the Lord, and He answered me. From the belly of Sheol I called for help, and You heard my voice.

JON.2.KJV: For you had cast me into the deep, in the middle of the seas; and the floods compassed me about: all your billows and your waves passed over me.
JON.2.PLAIN: For You cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the current swirled about me; all Your breakers and waves swept over me.

JON.2.BSB: At this, I said, ‘I have been banished from Your sight; yet I will look once more toward Your holy temple.’
JON.2.KJV: Then I said, I am cast out of your sight; yet I will look again toward your holy temple.
JON.2.PLAIN: At this, I said, ‘I have been banished from Your sight; yet I will look once more toward Your holy temple.’

JON.2.PLAIN: To the roots of the mountains I descended; the earth beneath me barred me in forever! But You raised my life from the pit, O Lord my God!

JON.2.KJV: When my soul fainted within me I remembered the LORD: and my prayer came in to you, into your holy temple.
JON.2.PLAIN: As my life was fading away, I remembered the Lord. My prayer went up to You, to Your holy temple.

JON.2.PLAIN: Those who cling to worthless idols forsake His loving devotion.

JON.2.BSB: But I, with the voice of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to You. I will fulfill what I have vowed. Salvation is from the LORD!”
JON.2.KJV: But I will sacrifice to you with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD. ¶
JON.2.PLAIN: But I, with shouts of grateful praise, will sacrifice to you. What I have vowed I will make good. Salvation comes from the Lord.

JON.2.KJV: And the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited out Jonah on the dry land.
JON.2.PLAIN: And the Lord commanded the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land.

JON.3.BSB: Then the word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time:
JON.3.KJV: And the word of the LORD came to Jonah the second time, saying,

JON.3.BSB: “Get up! Go to the great city of Nineveh and proclaim to it the message that I give you.”
JON.3.KJV: Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and preach to it the preaching that I bid you.

JON.3.BSB: On the first day of his journey, Jonah set out into the city and proclaimed, “Forty more days and Nineveh will be overturned!”
JON.3.KJV: And Jonah began to enter into the city a day’s journey, and he cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown. ¶
