MAT.16.PLAIN: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?”

MAT.16.BSB: Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
MAT.16.KJV: And Simon Peter answered and said, You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
MAT.16.PLAIN: Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

MAT.16.BSB: Jesus replied, “Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah! For this was not revealed to you by flesh and blood, but by My Father in heaven.
MAT.16.KJV: And Jesus answered and said to him, Blessed are you, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood has not revealed it to you, but my Father which is in heaven.
MAT.16.PLAIN: Jesus replied, “Held in quiet grace are you, Simon son of Jonah! For this was not revealed to you by flesh and blood, but by My Father in heaven.

MAT.16.BSB: And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
MAT.16.KJV: And I say also to you, That you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.
MAT.16.PLAIN: And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.

MAT.16.BSB: I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.”
MAT.16.KJV: And I will give to you the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatever you shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatever you shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
MAT.16.PLAIN: I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.”

MAT.16.BSB: Then He admonished the disciples not to tell anyone that He was the Christ.
MAT.16.KJV: Then charged he his disciples that they should tell no man that he was Jesus the Christ. ¶
MAT.16.PLAIN: Then He admonished the disciples not to tell anyone that He was the Christ.

MAT.16.BSB: From that time on Jesus began to show His disciples that He must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things at the hands of the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and that He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.
MAT.16.KJV: From that time forth began Jesus to show to his disciples, how that he must go to Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.
MAT.16.PLAIN: From that time on Jesus began to show His disciples that He must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things at the hands of the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and that He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.

MAT.16.BSB: Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him. “Far be it from You, Lord!” he said. “This shall never happen to You!”
MAT.16.KJV: Then Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from you, Lord: this shall not be to you.
MAT.16.PLAIN: Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him. “Far be it from You, Lord!” he said. “This shall never happen to You!”

MAT.16.BSB: But Jesus turned and said to Peter, “Get behind Me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to Me. For you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.”
MAT.16.KJV: But he turned, and said to Peter, Get you behind me, Satan: you are an offense to me: for you mind not the things that be of God, but those that be of men. ¶
MAT.16.PLAIN: But Jesus turned and said to Peter, “Get behind Me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to Me. For you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.”

MAT.16.BSB: Then Jesus told His disciples, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.
MAT.16.KJV: Then said Jesus to his disciples, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
MAT.16.PLAIN: If anyone wants to follow me, they need to let go of themselves, take up their cross, and come after me.

MAT.16.BSB: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will find it.
MAT.16.KJV: For whoever will save his life shall lose it: and whoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it.
MAT.16.PLAIN: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will find it.

MAT.16.BSB: What will it profit a man if he gains the whole world, yet forfeits his soul? Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?
MAT.16.KJV: For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?
MAT.16.PLAIN: What will it profit a man if he gains the whole world, yet forfeits his soul? Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?

MAT.16.BSB: For the Son of Man will come in His Father’s glory with His angels, and then He will repay each one according to what he has done.
MAT.16.KJV: For the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.
MAT.16.PLAIN: For the Son of Man will come in His Father’s glory with His angels, and then He will repay each one according to what he has done.

MAT.16.BSB: Truly I tell you, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom.”
MAT.16.KJV: Truly I say to you, There be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.
MAT.16.PLAIN: Truly I tell you, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom.”

MAT.17.BSB: After six days Jesus took with Him Peter, James, and John the brother of James, and led them up a high mountain by themselves.
MAT.17.KJV: And after six days Jesus takes Peter, James, and John his brother, and brings them up into an high mountain apart,
MAT.17.PLAIN: After six days Jesus took with Him Peter, James, and John the brother of James, and led them up a high mountain by themselves.

MAT.17.BSB: There He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and His clothes became as white as the light.
MAT.17.KJV: And was transfigured before them: and his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light.
MAT.17.PLAIN: There He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and His clothes became as white as the light.

MAT.17.BSB: Suddenly Moses and Elijah appeared before them, talking with Jesus.
MAT.17.KJV: And, behold, there appeared to them Moses and Elias talking with him.
MAT.17.PLAIN: Suddenly Moses and Elijah appeared before them, talking with Jesus.

MAT.17.BSB: Peter said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If You wish, I will put up three shelters—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
MAT.17.KJV: Then answered Peter, and said to Jesus, Lord, it is good for us to be here: if you will, let us make here three tabernacles; one for you, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.
MAT.17.PLAIN: Peter said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If You wish, I will put up three shelters—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

MAT.17.BSB: While Peter was still speaking, a bright cloud enveloped them, and a voice from the cloud said, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to Him!”
MAT.17.KJV: While he yet spoke, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear you him.
MAT.17.PLAIN: While Peter was still speaking, a bright cloud enveloped them, and a voice from the cloud said, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to Him!”

MAT.17.BSB: When the disciples heard this, they fell facedown in terror.
MAT.17.KJV: And when the disciples heard it, they fell on their face, and were sore afraid.
MAT.17.PLAIN: When the disciples heard this, they fell facedown in terror.

MAT.17.BSB: Then Jesus came over and touched them. “Get up,” He said. “Do not be afraid.”
MAT.17.KJV: And Jesus came and touched them, and said, Arise, and be not afraid.
MAT.17.PLAIN: Then Jesus came over and touched them. “Get up,” He said. “Do not be afraid.”

MAT.17.BSB: And when they looked up, they saw no one except Jesus.
MAT.17.KJV: And when they had lifted up their eyes, they saw no man, save Jesus only.
MAT.17.PLAIN: And when they looked up, they saw no one except Jesus.

MAT.17.BSB: As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus commanded them, “Do not tell anyone about this vision until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead.”
MAT.17.KJV: And as they came down from the mountain, Jesus charged them, saying, Tell the vision to no man, until the Son of man be risen again from the dead.
MAT.17.PLAIN: As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus commanded them, “Do not tell anyone about this vision until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead.”

MAT.17.BSB: The disciples asked Him, “Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
MAT.17.KJV: And his disciples asked him, saying, Why then say the scribes that Elias must first come?
MAT.17.PLAIN: The disciples asked Him, “Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

MAT.17.BSB: Jesus replied, “Elijah does indeed come, and he will restore all things.
MAT.17.KJV: And Jesus answered and said to them, Elias truly shall first come, and restore all things.
MAT.17.PLAIN: Jesus replied, “Elijah does indeed come, and he will restore all things.

MAT.17.BSB: But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but have done to him whatever they wished. In the same way, the Son of Man will suffer at their hands.”
MAT.17.KJV: But I say to you, That Elias is come already, and they knew him not, but have done to him whatever they listed. Likewise shall also the Son of man suffer of them.
MAT.17.PLAIN: But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but have done to him whatever they wished. In the same way, the Son of Man will suffer at their hands.”

MAT.17.BSB: Then the disciples understood that He was speaking to them about John the Baptist.
MAT.17.KJV: Then the disciples understood that he spoke to them of John the Baptist. ¶
MAT.17.PLAIN: Then the disciples understood that He was speaking to them about John the Baptist.

MAT.17.BSB: When they came to the crowd, a man came up to Jesus and knelt before Him.
MAT.17.KJV: And when they were come to the multitude, there came to him a certain man, kneeling down to him, and saying,
MAT.17.PLAIN: When they came to the crowd, a man came up to Jesus and knelt before Him.

MAT.17.BSB: “Lord, have mercy on my son,” he said. “He has seizures and is suffering terribly. He often falls into the fire or into the water.
MAT.17.KJV: Lord, have mercy on my son: for he is lunatic, and sore vexed: for often he falls into the fire, and oft into the water.
MAT.17.PLAIN: “Lord, have mercy on my son,” he said. “He has seizures and is suffering terribly. He often falls into the fire or into the water.

MAT.17.BSB: I brought him to Your disciples, but they could not heal him.”
MAT.17.KJV: And I brought him to your disciples, and they could not cure him.
MAT.17.PLAIN: I brought him to Your disciples, but they could not heal him.”

MAT.17.BSB: “O unbelieving and perverse generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy here to Me.”
MAT.17.KJV: Then Jesus answered and said, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him here to me.
MAT.17.PLAIN: “O unbelieving and perverse generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy here to Me.”

MAT.17.BSB: Then Jesus rebuked the demon, and it came out of the boy, and he was healed from that moment.
MAT.17.KJV: And Jesus rebuked the devil; and he departed out of him: and the child was cured from that very hour.
MAT.17.PLAIN: Then Jesus rebuked the demon, and it came out of the boy, and he was healed from that moment.

MAT.17.BSB: Afterward the disciples came to Jesus privately and asked, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”
MAT.17.KJV: Then came the disciples to Jesus apart, and said, Why could not we cast him out?
MAT.17.PLAIN: Afterward the disciples came to Jesus privately and asked, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”

MAT.17.BSB: “Because you have so little faith,” He answered. “For truly I tell you, if you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you.”
MAT.17.KJV: And Jesus said to them, Because of your unbelief: for truly I say to you, If you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you shall say to this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible to you.
MAT.17.PLAIN: If you had faith even the size of a mustard seed, you could tell a mountain to move, and it would — nothing would be impossible for you.

MAT.17.KJV: However, this kind goes not out but by prayer and fasting. ¶

MAT.17.BSB: When they gathered together in Galilee, Jesus told them, “The Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men.
MAT.17.KJV: And while they stayed in Galilee, Jesus said to them, The Son of man shall be betrayed into the hands of men:
MAT.17.PLAIN: When they gathered together in Galilee, Jesus told them, “The Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men.

MAT.17.BSB: They will kill Him, and on the third day He will be raised to life.” And the disciples were deeply grieved.
MAT.17.KJV: And they shall kill him, and the third day he shall be raised again. And they were exceeding sorry. ¶
MAT.17.PLAIN: They will kill Him, and on the third day He will be raised to life.” And the disciples were deeply grieved.

MAT.17.BSB: After they had arrived in Capernaum, the collectors of the two-drachma tax came to Peter and asked, “Does your Teacher pay the two drachmas?”
MAT.17.KJV: And when they were come to Capernaum, they that received tribute money came to Peter, and said, Does not your master pay tribute?
MAT.17.PLAIN: After they had arrived in Capernaum, the collectors of the two-drachma tax came to Peter and asked, “Does your Teacher pay the two drachmas?”

MAT.17.BSB: “Yes,” he answered. When Peter entered the house, Jesus preempted him. “What do you think, Simon?” He asked. “From whom do the kings of the earth collect customs and taxes: from their own sons, or from others?”
MAT.17.KJV: He says, Yes. And when he was come into the house, Jesus prevented him, saying, What think you, Simon? of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? of their own children, or of strangers?
MAT.17.PLAIN: “Yes,” he answered. When Peter entered the house, Jesus preempted him. “What do you think, Simon?” He asked. “From whom do the kings of the earth collect customs and taxes: from their own sons, or from others?”

MAT.17.BSB: “From others,” Peter answered. “Then the sons are exempt,” Jesus declared.
MAT.17.KJV: Peter says to him, Of strangers. Jesus says to him, Then are the children free.
MAT.17.PLAIN: “From others,” Peter answered. “Then the sons are exempt,” Jesus declared.

MAT.17.BSB: “But so that we may not offend them, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish you catch. When you open its mouth, you will find a four-drachma coin. Take it and give it to them for My tax and yours.”
MAT.17.KJV: Notwithstanding, lest we should offend them, go you to the sea, and cast an hook, and take up the fish that first comes up; and when you have opened his mouth, you shall find a piece of money: that take, and give to them for me and you.
MAT.17.PLAIN: “But so that we may not offend them, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish you catch. When you open its mouth, you will find a four-drachma coin. Take it and give it to them for My tax and yours.”

MAT.18.BSB: At that time the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”
MAT.18.KJV: At the same time came the disciples to Jesus, saying, Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?
MAT.18.PLAIN: At that time the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”

MAT.18.BSB: Jesus invited a little child to stand among them.
MAT.18.KJV: And Jesus called a little child to him, and set him in the middle of them,
MAT.18.PLAIN: Jesus invited a little child to stand among them.

MAT.18.BSB: “Truly I tell you,” He said, “unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
MAT.18.KJV: And said, Truly I say to you, Except you be converted, and become as little children, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.
MAT.18.PLAIN: “Truly I tell you,” He said, “unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.

MAT.18.BSB: Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
MAT.18.KJV: Whoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
MAT.18.PLAIN: Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.

MAT.18.BSB: And whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me.
MAT.18.KJV: And whoever shall receive one such little child in my name receives me.
MAT.18.PLAIN: And whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me.

MAT.18.BSB: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea.
MAT.18.KJV: But whoever shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea. ¶
MAT.18.PLAIN: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea.

MAT.18.BSB: Woe to the world for the causes of sin. These stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the man through whom they come!
MAT.18.KJV: Woe to the world because of offenses! for it must needs be that offenses come; but woe to that man by whom the offense comes!
MAT.18.PLAIN: Woe to the world for the causes of sin. These stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the man through whom they come!

MAT.18.BSB: If your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.
MAT.18.KJV: Why if your hand or your foot offend you, cut them off, and cast them from you: it is better for you to enter into life halt or maimed, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into everlasting fire.
MAT.18.PLAIN: If your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.

MAT.18.BSB: And if your eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.
MAT.18.KJV: And if your eye offend you, pluck it out, and cast it from you: it is better for you to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire.
MAT.18.PLAIN: And if your eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.

MAT.18.BSB: See that you do not look down on any of these little ones. For I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of My Father in heaven.
MAT.18.KJV: Take heed that you despise not one of these little ones; for I say to you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven.
MAT.18.PLAIN: See that you do not look down on any of these little ones. For I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of My Father in heaven.

MAT.18.KJV: For the Son of man is come to save that which was lost.

MAT.18.BSB: What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost?
MAT.18.KJV: How think you? if a man have an hundred sheep, and one of them be gone astray, does he not leave the ninety and nine, and goes into the mountains, and seeks that which is gone astray?
MAT.18.PLAIN: What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost?

MAT.18.BSB: And if he finds it, truly I tell you, he rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.
MAT.18.KJV: And if so be that he find it, truly I say to you, he rejoices more of that sheep, than of the ninety and nine which went not astray.
MAT.18.PLAIN: And if he finds it, truly I tell you, he rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.

MAT.18.BSB: In the same way, your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish.
MAT.18.KJV: Even so it is not the will of your Father which is in heaven, that one of these little ones should perish. ¶
MAT.18.PLAIN: In the same way, your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish.

MAT.18.BSB: If your brother sins against you, go and confront him privately. If he listens to you, you have won your brother over.
MAT.18.KJV: Moreover if your brother shall trespass against you, go and tell him his fault between you and him alone: if he shall hear you, you have gained your brother.
MAT.18.PLAIN: If your brother sins against you, go and confront him privately. If he listens to you, you have won your brother over.

MAT.18.BSB: But if he will not listen, take one or two others along, so that ‘every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.’
MAT.18.KJV: But if he will not hear you, then take with you one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.
MAT.18.PLAIN: But if he will not listen, take one or two others along, so that ‘every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.’

MAT.18.BSB: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church. And if he refuses to listen even to the church, regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector.
MAT.18.KJV: And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it to the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be to you as an heathen man and a publican.
MAT.18.PLAIN: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church. And if he refuses to listen even to the church, regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector.

MAT.18.BSB: Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.
MAT.18.KJV: Truly I say to you, Whatever you shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatever you shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
MAT.18.PLAIN: Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.

MAT.18.BSB: Again, I tell you truly that if two of you on the earth agree about anything you ask for, it will be done for you by My Father in heaven.
MAT.18.KJV: Again I say to you, That if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven.
MAT.18.PLAIN: Again, I tell you truly that if two of you on the earth agree about anything you ask for, it will be done for you by My Father in heaven.

MAT.18.BSB: For where two or three gather together in My name, there am I with them.”
MAT.18.KJV: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the middle of them. ¶
MAT.18.PLAIN: Wherever two or three of you come together in my name, I'm right there among you.

MAT.18.BSB: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother who sins against me? Up to seven times?”
MAT.18.KJV: Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?
MAT.18.PLAIN: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother who sins against me? Up to seven times?”

MAT.18.BSB: Jesus answered, “I tell you, not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!
MAT.18.KJV: Jesus says to him, I say not to you, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven. ¶
MAT.18.PLAIN: Jesus answered, “I tell you, not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!

MAT.18.BSB: Because of this, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
MAT.18.KJV: Therefore is the kingdom of heaven likened to a certain king, which would take account of his servants.
MAT.18.PLAIN: Because of this, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.

MAT.18.BSB: As he began the settlements, a debtor was brought to him owing ten thousand talents.
MAT.18.KJV: And when he had begun to reckon, one was brought to him, which owed him ten thousand talents.
MAT.18.PLAIN: As he began the settlements, a debtor was brought to him owing ten thousand talents.

MAT.18.BSB: Since the man was unable to pay, the master ordered that he be sold to pay his debt, along with his wife and children and everything he owned.
MAT.18.KJV: But for as much as he had not to pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.
MAT.18.PLAIN: Since the man was unable to pay, the master ordered that he be sold to pay his debt, along with his wife and children and everything he owned.

MAT.18.BSB: Then the servant fell on his knees before him. ‘Have patience with me,’ he begged, ‘and I will pay back everything.’
MAT.18.KJV: The servant therefore fell down, and worshipped him, saying, Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay you all.
MAT.18.PLAIN: Then the servant fell on his knees before him. ‘Have patience with me,’ he begged, ‘and I will pay back everything.’

MAT.18.BSB: His master had compassion on him, forgave his debt, and released him.
MAT.18.KJV: Then the lord of that servant was moved with compassion, and loosed him, and forgave him the debt.
MAT.18.PLAIN: His master had compassion on him, forgave his debt, and released him.

MAT.18.BSB: But when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii. He grabbed him and began to choke him, saying, ‘Pay back what you owe me!’
MAT.18.KJV: But the same servant went out, and found one of his fellow servants, which owed him an hundred pence: and he laid hands on him, and took him by the throat, saying, Pay me that you owe.
MAT.18.PLAIN: But when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii. He grabbed him and began to choke him, saying, ‘Pay back what you owe me!’

MAT.18.BSB: So his fellow servant fell down and begged him, ‘Have patience with me, and I will pay you back.’
MAT.18.KJV: And his fellow servant fell down at his feet, and sought him, saying, Have patience with me, and I will pay you all.
MAT.18.PLAIN: So his fellow servant fell down and begged him, ‘Have patience with me, and I will pay you back.’

MAT.18.BSB: But he refused. Instead, he went and had the man thrown into prison until he could pay his debt.
MAT.18.KJV: And he would not: but went and cast him into prison, till he should pay the debt.
MAT.18.PLAIN: But he refused. Instead, he went and had the man thrown into prison until he could pay his debt.

MAT.18.BSB: When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly distressed, and they went and recounted all of this to their master.
MAT.18.KJV: So when his fellow servants saw what was done, they were very sorry, and came and told to their lord all that was done.
MAT.18.PLAIN: When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly distressed, and they went and recounted all of this to their master.

MAT.18.BSB: Then the master summoned him and declared, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave all your debt because you begged me.
