LUK.15.PLAIN: The younger son said to him, ‘Father, give me my share of the estate.’ So he divided his property between them.

LUK.15.BSB: After a few days, the younger son got everything together and journeyed to a distant country, where he squandered his wealth in wild living.
LUK.15.KJV: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.
LUK.15.PLAIN: After a few days, the younger son got everything together and journeyed to a distant country, where he squandered his wealth in wild living.

LUK.15.BSB: After he had spent all he had, a severe famine swept through that country, and he began to be in need.
LUK.15.KJV: And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want.
LUK.15.PLAIN: After he had spent all he had, a severe famine swept through that country, and he began to be in need.

LUK.15.BSB: So he went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed the pigs.
LUK.15.KJV: And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
LUK.15.PLAIN: So he went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed the pigs.

LUK.15.BSB: He longed to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating, but no one would give him a thing.
LUK.15.KJV: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave to him.
LUK.15.PLAIN: He longed to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating, but no one would give him a thing.

LUK.15.BSB: Finally he came to his senses and said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have plenty of food? But here I am, starving to death!
LUK.15.KJV: And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!
LUK.15.PLAIN: Finally he came to his senses and said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have plenty of food? But here I am, starving to death!

LUK.15.BSB: I will get up and go back to my father and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.
LUK.15.KJV: I will arise and go to my father, and will say to him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before you,
LUK.15.PLAIN: I will get up and go back to my father and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.

LUK.15.BSB: I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants.”’
LUK.15.KJV: And am no more worthy to be called your son: make me as one of your hired servants.
LUK.15.PLAIN: I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants.”’

LUK.15.BSB: So he got up and went to his father. But while he was still in the distance, his father saw him and was filled with compassion. He ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him.
LUK.15.KJV: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
LUK.15.PLAIN: So he got up and went to his father. While he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion — he ran to his son, threw his arms around him, and kissed him.

LUK.15.BSB: The son declared, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
LUK.15.KJV: And the son said to him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight, and am no more worthy to be called your son.
LUK.15.PLAIN: The son declared, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’

LUK.15.BSB: But the father said to his servants, ‘Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.
LUK.15.KJV: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:
LUK.15.PLAIN: But the father said to his servants, ‘Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.

LUK.15.BSB: Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let us feast and celebrate.
LUK.15.KJV: And bring here the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:
LUK.15.PLAIN: Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let us feast and celebrate.

LUK.15.BSB: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again! He was lost and is found!’ So they began to celebrate.
LUK.15.KJV: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
LUK.15.PLAIN: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again! He was lost and is found!’ So they began to celebrate.

LUK.15.BSB: Meanwhile the older son was in the field, and as he approached the house, he heard music and dancing.
LUK.15.KJV: Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing.
LUK.15.PLAIN: Meanwhile the older son was in the field, and as he approached the house, he heard music and dancing.

LUK.15.BSB: So he called one of the servants and asked what was going on.
LUK.15.KJV: And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.
LUK.15.PLAIN: So he called one of the servants and asked what was going on.

LUK.15.BSB: ‘Your brother has returned,’ he said, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has him back safe and sound.’
LUK.15.KJV: And he said to him, Your brother is come; and your father has killed the fatted calf, because he has received him safe and sound.
LUK.15.PLAIN: ‘Your brother has returned,’ he said, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has him back safe and sound.’

LUK.15.BSB: The older son became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.
LUK.15.KJV: And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and entreated him.
LUK.15.PLAIN: The older son became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.

LUK.15.BSB: But he answered his father, ‘Look, all these years I have served you and never disobeyed a commandment of yours. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.
LUK.15.KJV: And he answering said to his father, See, these many years do I serve you, neither transgressed I at any time your commandment: and yet you never gave me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:
LUK.15.PLAIN: But he answered his father, ‘Look, all these years I have served you and never disobeyed a commandment of yours. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.

LUK.15.BSB: But when this son of yours returns from squandering your wealth with prostitutes, you kill the fattened calf for him!’
LUK.15.KJV: But as soon as this your son was come, which has devoured your living with harlots, you have killed for him the fatted calf.
LUK.15.PLAIN: But when this son of yours returns from squandering your wealth with prostitutes, you kill the fattened calf for him!’

LUK.15.BSB: ‘Son, you are always with me,’ the father said, ‘and all that is mine is yours.
LUK.15.KJV: And he said to him, Son, you are ever with me, and all that I have is yours.
LUK.15.PLAIN: ‘Son, you are always with me,’ the father said, ‘and all that is mine is yours.

LUK.15.BSB: But it was fitting to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’”
LUK.15.KJV: It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this your brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.
LUK.15.PLAIN: But it was fitting to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’”

LUK.16.BSB: Jesus also said to His disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.
LUK.16.KJV: And he said also to his disciples, There was a certain rich man, which had a steward; and the same was accused to him that he had wasted his goods.
LUK.16.PLAIN: Jesus also said to His disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.

LUK.16.BSB: So he called him in to ask, ‘What is this I hear about you? Turn in an account of your management, for you cannot be manager any longer.’
LUK.16.KJV: And he called him, and said to him, How is it that I hear this of you? give an account of your stewardship; for you may be no longer steward.
LUK.16.PLAIN: So he called him in to ask, ‘What is this I hear about you? Turn in an account of your management, for you cannot be manager any longer.’

LUK.16.BSB: The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position? I am too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg.
LUK.16.KJV: Then the steward said within himself, What shall I do? for my lord takes away from me the stewardship: I cannot dig; to beg I am ashamed.
LUK.16.PLAIN: The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position? I am too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg.

LUK.16.BSB: I know what I will do, so that after my removal from management, people will welcome me into their homes.’
LUK.16.KJV: I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.
LUK.16.PLAIN: I know what I will do, so that after my removal from management, people will welcome me into their homes.’

LUK.16.BSB: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors. ‘How much do you owe my master?’ he asked the first.
LUK.16.KJV: So he called every one of his lord’s debtors to him, and said to the first, How much owe you to my lord?
LUK.16.PLAIN: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors. ‘How much do you owe my master?’ he asked the first.

LUK.16.BSB: ‘A hundred measures of olive oil,’ he answered. ‘Take your bill,’ said the manager. ‘Sit down quickly, and write fifty.’
LUK.16.KJV: And he said, An hundred measures of oil. And he said to him, Take your bill, and sit down quickly, and write fifty.
LUK.16.PLAIN: ‘A hundred measures of olive oil,’ he answered. ‘Take your bill,’ said the manager. ‘Sit down quickly, and write fifty.’

LUK.16.BSB: Then he asked another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ ‘A hundred measures of wheat,’ he replied. ‘Take your bill and write eighty,’ he told him.
LUK.16.KJV: Then said he to another, And how much owe you? And he said, An hundred measures of wheat. And he said to him, Take your bill, and write fourscore.
LUK.16.PLAIN: Then he asked another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ ‘A hundred measures of wheat,’ he replied. ‘Take your bill and write eighty,’ he told him.

LUK.16.BSB: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.
LUK.16.KJV: And the lord commended the unjust steward, because he had done wisely: for the children of this world are in their generation wiser than the children of light.
LUK.16.PLAIN: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.

LUK.16.BSB: I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves, so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.
LUK.16.KJV: And I say to you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when you fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.
LUK.16.PLAIN: I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves, so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.

LUK.16.BSB: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
LUK.16.KJV: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.
LUK.16.PLAIN: Whoever is faithful with a little will be faithful with a lot; whoever is dishonest with a little will be dishonest with a lot too.

LUK.16.BSB: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?
LUK.16.KJV: If therefore you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?
LUK.16.PLAIN: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?

LUK.16.BSB: And if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your own?
LUK.16.KJV: And if you have not been faithful in that which is another man’s, who shall give you that which is your own? ¶
LUK.16.PLAIN: And if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your own?

LUK.16.BSB: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.”
LUK.16.KJV: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.
LUK.16.PLAIN: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.”

LUK.16.BSB: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all of this and were scoffing at Jesus.
LUK.16.KJV: And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him.
LUK.16.PLAIN: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all of this and were scoffing at Jesus.

LUK.16.BSB: So He said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For what is prized among men is detestable before God.
LUK.16.KJV: And he said to them, You are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knows your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.
LUK.16.PLAIN: So He said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For what is prized among men is detestable before God.

LUK.16.BSB: The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John. Since that time, the gospel of the kingdom of God is being preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
LUK.16.KJV: The law and the prophets were until John: since that time the kingdom of God is preached, and every man presses into it.
LUK.16.PLAIN: The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John. Since that time, the gospel of the kingdom of God is being preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.

LUK.16.BSB: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law.
LUK.16.KJV: And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one pronunciation mark of the law to fail.
LUK.16.PLAIN: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law.

LUK.16.BSB: Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery, and he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
LUK.16.KJV: Whoever puts away his wife, and marries another, commits adultery: and whoever marries her that is put away from her husband commits adultery. ¶
LUK.16.PLAIN: Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery, and he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

LUK.16.BSB: Now there was a rich man dressed in purple and fine linen, who lived each day in joyous splendor.
LUK.16.KJV: There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day:
LUK.16.PLAIN: Now there was a rich man dressed in purple and fine linen, who lived each day in joyous splendor.

LUK.16.BSB: And a beggar named Lazarus lay at his gate, covered with sores
LUK.16.KJV: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores,
LUK.16.PLAIN: And a beggar named Lazarus lay at his gate, covered with sores

LUK.16.BSB: and longing to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
LUK.16.KJV: And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.
LUK.16.PLAIN: and longing to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.

LUK.16.BSB: One day the beggar died and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s side. And the rich man also died and was buried.
LUK.16.KJV: And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;
LUK.16.PLAIN: One day the beggar died and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s side. And the rich man also died and was buried.

LUK.16.BSB: In Hades, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham from afar, with Lazarus by his side.
LUK.16.KJV: And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and sees Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.
LUK.16.PLAIN: In Hades, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham from afar, with Lazarus by his side.

LUK.16.BSB: So he cried out, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue. For I am in agony in this fire.’
LUK.16.KJV: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.
LUK.16.PLAIN: So he cried out, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue. For I am in agony in this fire.’

LUK.16.BSB: But Abraham answered, ‘Child, remember that during your lifetime you received your good things, while Lazarus received bad things. But now he is comforted here, while you are in agony.
LUK.16.KJV: But Abraham said, Son, remember that you in your lifetime received your good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and you are tormented.
LUK.16.PLAIN: But Abraham answered, ‘Child, remember that during your lifetime you received your good things, while Lazarus received bad things. But now he is comforted here, while you are in agony.

LUK.16.BSB: And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that even those who wish cannot cross from here to you, nor can anyone cross from there to us.’
LUK.16.KJV: And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from there.
LUK.16.PLAIN: And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that even those who wish cannot cross from here to you, nor can anyone cross from there to us.’

LUK.16.BSB: ‘Then I beg you, father,’ he said, ‘send Lazarus to my father’s house,
LUK.16.KJV: Then he said, I pray you therefore, father, that you would send him to my father’s house:
LUK.16.PLAIN: ‘Then I beg you, father,’ he said, ‘send Lazarus to my father’s house,

LUK.16.BSB: for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also end up in this place of torment.’
LUK.16.KJV: For I have five brothers; that he may testify to them, lest they also come into this place of torment.
LUK.16.PLAIN: for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also end up in this place of torment.’

LUK.16.BSB: But Abraham replied, ‘They have Moses and the prophets; let your brothers listen to them.’
LUK.16.KJV: Abraham says to him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.
LUK.16.PLAIN: But Abraham replied, ‘They have Moses and the prophets; let your brothers listen to them.’

LUK.16.BSB: ‘No, father Abraham,’ he said, ‘but if someone is sent to them from the dead, they will repent.’
LUK.16.KJV: And he said, No, father Abraham: but if one went to them from the dead, they will repent.
LUK.16.PLAIN: ‘No, father Abraham,’ he said, ‘but if someone is sent to them from the dead, they will repent.’

LUK.16.BSB: Then Abraham said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.’”
LUK.16.KJV: And he said to him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.
LUK.16.PLAIN: Then Abraham said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.’”

LUK.17.BSB: Jesus said to His disciples, “It is inevitable that stumbling blocks will come, but woe to the one through whom they come!
LUK.17.KJV: Then said he to the disciples, It is impossible but that offenses will come: but woe to him, through whom they come!
LUK.17.PLAIN: Jesus said to His disciples, “It is inevitable that stumbling blocks will come, but woe to the one through whom they come!

LUK.17.BSB: It would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.
LUK.17.KJV: It were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea, than that he should offend one of these little ones. ¶
LUK.17.PLAIN: It would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.

LUK.17.BSB: Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
LUK.17.KJV: Take heed to yourselves: If your brother trespass against you, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.
LUK.17.PLAIN: Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.

LUK.17.BSB: Even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times returns to say, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”
LUK.17.KJV: And if he trespass against you seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to you, saying, I repent; you shall forgive him.
LUK.17.PLAIN: Even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times returns to say, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”

LUK.17.BSB: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith!”
LUK.17.KJV: And the apostles said to the Lord, Increase our faith.
LUK.17.PLAIN: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith!”

LUK.17.BSB: And the Lord answered, “If you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it will obey you.
LUK.17.KJV: And the Lord said, If you had faith as a grain of mustard seed, you might say to this sycamine tree, Be you plucked up by the root, and be you planted in the sea; and it should obey you.
LUK.17.PLAIN: And the Lord answered, “If you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it will obey you.

LUK.17.BSB: Which of you whose servant comes in from plowing or shepherding in the field will say to him, ‘Come at once and sit down to eat’?
LUK.17.KJV: But which of you, having a servant plowing or feeding cattle, will say to him by and by, when he is come from the field, Go and sit down to meat?
LUK.17.PLAIN: Which of you whose servant comes in from plowing or shepherding in the field will say to him, ‘Come at once and sit down to eat’?

LUK.17.BSB: Instead, won’t he tell him, ‘Prepare my meal and dress yourself to serve me while I eat and drink; and afterward you may eat and drink’?
LUK.17.KJV: And will not rather say to him, Make ready with which I may sup, and gird yourself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunken; and afterward you shall eat and drink?
LUK.17.PLAIN: Instead, won’t he tell him, ‘Prepare my meal and dress yourself to serve me while I eat and drink; and afterward you may eat and drink’?

LUK.17.BSB: Does he thank the servant because he did what he was told?
LUK.17.KJV: Does he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him? I trow not.
LUK.17.PLAIN: Does he thank the servant because he did what he was told?

LUK.17.BSB: So you also, when you have done everything commanded of you, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.’”
LUK.17.KJV: So likewise you, when you shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do. ¶
LUK.17.PLAIN: So you also, when you have done everything commanded of you, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.’”

LUK.17.BSB: While Jesus was on His way to Jerusalem, He was passing between Samaria and Galilee.
LUK.17.KJV: And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the middle of Samaria and Galilee.
LUK.17.PLAIN: While Jesus was on His way to Jerusalem, He was passing between Samaria and Galilee.

LUK.17.BSB: As He entered one of the villages, He was met by ten lepers. They stood at a distance
LUK.17.KJV: And as he entered into a certain village, there met him ten men that were lepers, which stood afar off:
LUK.17.PLAIN: As He entered one of the villages, He was met by ten lepers. They stood at a distance

LUK.17.BSB: and raised their voices, shouting, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
LUK.17.KJV: And they lifted up their voices, and said, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.
LUK.17.PLAIN: and raised their voices, shouting, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”

LUK.17.BSB: When Jesus saw them, He said, “Go, show yourselves to the priests.” And as they were on their way, they were cleansed.
LUK.17.KJV: And when he saw them, he said to them, Go show yourselves to the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed.
LUK.17.PLAIN: When Jesus saw them, He said, “Go, show yourselves to the priests.” And as they were on their way, they were cleansed.

LUK.17.BSB: When one of them saw that he was healed, he came back, praising God in a loud voice.
LUK.17.KJV: And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God,
LUK.17.PLAIN: When one of them saw that he was healed, he came back, praising God in a loud voice.

LUK.17.BSB: He fell facedown at Jesus’ feet in thanksgiving to Him—and he was a Samaritan.
LUK.17.KJV: And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan.
LUK.17.PLAIN: He fell facedown at Jesus’ feet in thanksgiving to Him—and he was a Samaritan.

LUK.17.BSB: “Were not all ten cleansed?” Jesus asked. “Where then are the other nine?
LUK.17.KJV: And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?
LUK.17.PLAIN: “Were not all ten cleansed?” Jesus asked. “Where then are the other nine?

LUK.17.BSB: Was no one found except this foreigner to return and give glory to God?”
LUK.17.KJV: There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger.
LUK.17.PLAIN: Was no one found except this foreigner to return and give glory to God?”

LUK.17.BSB: Then Jesus said to him, “Rise and go; your faith has made you well!”
LUK.17.KJV: And he said to him, Arise, go your way: your faith has made you whole. ¶

JHN.1.PLAIN: “Then who are you?” they inquired. “Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the Prophet?” He answered, “No.”

JHN.1.BSB: So they said to him, “Who are you? We need an answer for those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”
JHN.1.KJV: Then said they to him, Who are you? that we may give an answer to them that sent us. What say you of yourself?
JHN.1.PLAIN: So they said to him, “Who are you? We need an answer for those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”

JHN.1.BSB: John replied in the words of Isaiah the prophet: “I am a voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way for the Lord.’”
JHN.1.KJV: He said, I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Isaiah.
JHN.1.PLAIN: John replied in the words of Isaiah the prophet: “I am a voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way for the Lord.’”

JHN.1.BSB: Then the Pharisees who had been sent
JHN.1.KJV: And they which were sent were of the Pharisees.
JHN.1.PLAIN: Then the Pharisees who had been sent

JHN.1.BSB: asked him, “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?”
JHN.1.KJV: And they asked him, and said to him, Why baptize you then, if you be not that Christ, nor Elias, neither that prophet?
JHN.1.PLAIN: asked him, “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?”

JHN.1.BSB: “I baptize with water,” John replied, “but among you stands One you do not know.
JHN.1.KJV: John answered them, saying, I baptize with water: but there stands one among you, whom you know not;
JHN.1.PLAIN: “I baptize with water,” John replied, “but among you stands One you do not know.

JHN.1.BSB: He is the One who comes after me, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.”
JHN.1.KJV: He it is, who coming after me is preferred before me, whose shoe’s lace I am not worthy to unloose.
JHN.1.PLAIN: He is the One who comes after me, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.”

JHN.1.BSB: All this happened at Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
JHN.1.KJV: These things were done in Bethabara beyond Jordan, where John was baptizing. ¶
JHN.1.PLAIN: All this happened at Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.

JHN.1.BSB: The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
JHN.1.KJV: The next day John sees Jesus coming to him, and says, Behold the Lamb of God, which takes away the sin of the world.
JHN.1.PLAIN: The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!

JHN.1.BSB: This is He of whom I said, ‘A man who comes after me has surpassed me because He was before me.’
JHN.1.KJV: This is he of whom I said, After me comes a man which is preferred before me: for he was before me.
JHN.1.PLAIN: This is He of whom I said, ‘A man who comes after me has surpassed me because He was before me.’

JHN.1.BSB: I myself did not know Him, but the reason I came baptizing with water was that He might be revealed to Israel.”
JHN.1.KJV: And I knew him not: but that he should be made manifest to Israel, therefore am I come baptizing with water.
JHN.1.PLAIN: I myself did not know Him, but the reason I came baptizing with water was that He might be revealed to Israel.”

JHN.1.BSB: Then John testified, “I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove and resting on Him.
JHN.1.KJV: And John bore record, saying, I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it stayed on him.
JHN.1.PLAIN: Then John testified, “I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove and resting on Him.

JHN.1.BSB: I myself did not know Him, but the One who sent me to baptize with water told me, ‘The man on whom you see the Spirit descend and rest is He who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.’
JHN.1.KJV: And I knew him not: but he that sent me to baptize with water, the same said to me, On whom you shall see the Spirit descending, and remaining on him, the same is he which baptizes with the Holy Ghost.
JHN.1.PLAIN: I myself did not know Him, but the One who sent me to baptize with water told me, ‘The man on whom you see the Spirit descend and rest is He who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.’

JHN.1.BSB: I have seen and testified that this is the Son of God.”
JHN.1.KJV: And I saw, and bore record that this is the Son of God. ¶
JHN.1.PLAIN: I have seen and testified that this is the Son of God.”

JHN.1.BSB: The next day John was there again with two of his disciples.
JHN.1.KJV: Again the next day after John stood, and two of his disciples;
JHN.1.PLAIN: The next day John was there again with two of his disciples.

JHN.1.BSB: When he saw Jesus walking by, he said, “Look, the Lamb of God!”
JHN.1.KJV: And looking on Jesus as he walked, he says, Behold the Lamb of God!
JHN.1.PLAIN: When he saw Jesus walking by, he said, “Look, the Lamb of God!”

JHN.1.BSB: And when the two disciples heard him say this, they followed Jesus.
JHN.1.KJV: And the two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.
JHN.1.PLAIN: And when the two disciples heard him say this, they followed Jesus.

JHN.1.BSB: Jesus turned and saw them following. “What do you want?” He asked. They said to Him, “Rabbi” (which means Teacher), “where are You staying?”
JHN.1.KJV: Then Jesus turned, and saw them following, and says to them, What seek you? They said to him, Rabbi, (which is to say, being interpreted, Master,) where dwell you?
JHN.1.PLAIN: Jesus turned and saw them following. “What do you want?” He asked. They said to Him, “Rabbi” (which means Teacher), “where are You staying?”

JHN.1.BSB: “Come and see,” He replied. So they went and saw where He was staying, and spent that day with Him. It was about the tenth hour.
JHN.1.KJV: He says to them, Come and see. They came and saw where he dwelled, and stayed with him that day: for it was about the tenth hour.
JHN.1.PLAIN: “Come and see,” He replied. So they went and saw where He was staying, and spent that day with Him. It was about the tenth hour.

JHN.1.BSB: Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, was one of the two who heard John’s testimony and followed Jesus.
JHN.1.KJV: One of the two which heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.
JHN.1.PLAIN: Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, was one of the two who heard John’s testimony and followed Jesus.

JHN.1.BSB: He first found his brother Simon and told him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated as Christ).
JHN.1.KJV: He first finds his own brother Simon, and says to him, We have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ.
JHN.1.PLAIN: He first found his brother Simon and told him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated as Christ).

JHN.1.BSB: Andrew brought him to Jesus, who looked at him and said, “You are Simon son of John. You will be called Cephas” (which is translated as Peter).
JHN.1.KJV: And he brought him to Jesus. And when Jesus beheld him, he said, You are Simon the son of Jona: you shall be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone. ¶
JHN.1.PLAIN: Andrew brought him to Jesus, who looked at him and said, “You are Simon son of John. You will be called Cephas” (which is translated as Peter).

JHN.1.BSB: The next day Jesus decided to set out for Galilee. Finding Philip, He told him, “Follow Me.”
JHN.1.KJV: The day following Jesus would go forth into Galilee, and finds Philip, and says to him, Follow me.
JHN.1.PLAIN: The next day Jesus decided to set out for Galilee. Finding Philip, He told him, “Follow Me.”

JHN.1.BSB: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter.
JHN.1.KJV: Now Philip was of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.
JHN.1.PLAIN: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter.

JHN.1.BSB: Philip found Nathanael and told him, “We have found the One Moses wrote about in the Law, the One the prophets foretold—Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”
JHN.1.KJV: Philip finds Nathanael, and says to him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.
JHN.1.PLAIN: Philip found Nathanael and told him, “We have found the One Moses wrote about in the Law, the One the prophets foretold—Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”

JHN.1.BSB: “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Nathanael asked. “Come and see,” said Philip.
JHN.1.KJV: And Nathanael says to him, Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip said to him, Come and see.
JHN.1.PLAIN: “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Nathanael asked. “Come and see,” said Philip.

JHN.1.BSB: When Jesus saw Nathanael approaching, He said of him, “Here is a true Israelite, in whom there is no deceit.”
JHN.1.KJV: Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and says of him, Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!
JHN.1.PLAIN: When Jesus saw Nathanael approaching, He said of him, “Here is a true Israelite, in whom there is no deceit.”

JHN.1.BSB: “How do You know me?” Nathanael asked. Jesus replied, “Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree.”
JHN.1.KJV: Nathanael says to him, From where know you me? Jesus answered and said to him, Before that Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.
JHN.1.PLAIN: “How do You know me?” Nathanael asked. Jesus replied, “Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree.”

JHN.1.BSB: “Rabbi,” Nathanael answered, “You are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!”
JHN.1.KJV: Nathanael answered and says to him, Rabbi, you are the Son of God; you are the King of Israel.
JHN.1.PLAIN: “Rabbi,” Nathanael answered, “You are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!”

JHN.1.BSB: Jesus said to him, “Do you believe just because I told you I saw you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than these.”
JHN.1.KJV: Jesus answered and said to him, Because I said to you, I saw you under the fig tree, believe you? you shall see greater things than these.
JHN.1.PLAIN: Jesus said to him, “Do you believe just because I told you I saw you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than these.”

JHN.1.BSB: Then He declared, “Truly, truly, I tell you, you will all see heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”
JHN.1.KJV: And he says to him, Truly, truly, I say to you, Hereafter you shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of man.
JHN.1.PLAIN: Then He declared, “Hear this steady truth, you will all see heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”

JHN.2.BSB: On the third day a wedding took place at Cana in Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there,
JHN.2.KJV: And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there:
JHN.2.PLAIN: On the third day a wedding took place at Cana in Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there,

JHN.2.BSB: and Jesus and His disciples had also been invited to the wedding.
JHN.2.KJV: And both Jesus was called, and his disciples, to the marriage.
JHN.2.PLAIN: and Jesus and His disciples had also been invited to the wedding.

JHN.2.BSB: When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to Him, “They have no more wine.”
JHN.2.KJV: And when they wanted wine, the mother of Jesus says to him, They have no wine.
JHN.2.PLAIN: When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to Him, “They have no more wine.”

JHN.2.BSB: “Woman, why does this concern us?” Jesus replied. “My hour has not yet come.”
JHN.2.KJV: Jesus says to her, Woman, what have I to do with you? my hour is not yet come.
JHN.2.PLAIN: “Woman, why does this concern us?” Jesus replied. “My hour has not yet come.”

JHN.2.BSB: His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever He tells you.”
JHN.2.KJV: His mother says to the servants, Whatever he said to you, do it.
JHN.2.PLAIN: His mother told the servants, 'Whatever he tells you, do it.'

JHN.2.BSB: Now six stone water jars had been set there for the Jewish rites of purification. Each could hold from twenty to thirty gallons.
JHN.2.KJV: And there were set there six water pots of stone, after the manner of the purifying of the Jews, containing two or three firkins apiece.
JHN.2.PLAIN: Now six stone water jars had been set there for the Jewish rites of purification. Each could hold from twenty to thirty gallons.

JHN.2.BSB: Jesus told the servants, “Fill the jars with water.” So they filled them to the brim.
JHN.2.KJV: Jesus says to them, Fill the water pots with water. And they filled them up to the brim.
JHN.2.PLAIN: Jesus told the servants, “Fill the jars with water.” So they filled them to the brim.

JHN.2.BSB: “Now draw some out,” He said, “and take it to the master of the banquet.” They did so,
JHN.2.KJV: And he says to them, Draw out now, and bear to the governor of the feast. And they bore it.
JHN.2.PLAIN: “Now draw some out,” He said, “and take it to the master of the banquet.” They did so,

JHN.2.BSB: and the master of the banquet tasted the water that had been turned into wine. He did not know where it was from, but the servants who had drawn the water knew. Then he called the bridegroom aside
JHN.2.KJV: When the ruler of the feast had tasted the water that was made wine, and knew not from where it was: (but the servants which drew the water knew;) the governor of the feast called the bridegroom,
JHN.2.PLAIN: and the master of the banquet tasted the water that had been turned into wine. He did not know where it was from, but the servants who had drawn the water knew. Then he called the bridegroom aside

JHN.2.BSB: and said, “Everyone serves the fine wine first, and then the cheap wine after the guests are drunk. But you have saved the fine wine until now!”
JHN.2.KJV: And says to him, Every man at the beginning does set forth good wine; and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse: but you have kept the good wine until now.
JHN.2.PLAIN: and said, “Everyone serves the fine wine first, and then the cheap wine after the guests are drunk. But you have saved the fine wine until now!”

JHN.2.BSB: Jesus performed this, the first of His signs, at Cana in Galilee. He thus revealed His glory, and His disciples believed in Him.
JHN.2.KJV: This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; and his disciples believed on him. ¶
JHN.2.PLAIN: Jesus performed this, the first of His signs, at Cana in Galilee. He thus revealed His glory, and His disciples believed in Him.

JHN.2.BSB: After this, He went down to Capernaum with His mother and brothers and His disciples, and they stayed there a few days.
JHN.2.KJV: After this he went down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, and his brothers, and his disciples: and they continued there not many days. ¶
JHN.2.PLAIN: After this, He went down to Capernaum with His mother and brothers and His disciples, and they stayed there a few days.

JHN.2.BSB: When the Jewish Passover was near, Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
JHN.2.KJV: And the Jews’ passover was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
JHN.2.PLAIN: When the Jewish Passover was near, Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

JHN.2.BSB: In the temple courts He found men selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and money changers seated at their tables.
JHN.2.KJV: And found in the temple those that sold oxen and sheep and doves, and the changers of money sitting:
JHN.2.PLAIN: In the temple courts He found men selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and money changers seated at their tables.

JHN.2.BSB: So He made a whip out of cords and drove all from the temple courts, both sheep and cattle. He poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables.
JHN.2.KJV: And when he had made a whip of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep, and the oxen; and poured out the changers’ money, and overthrew the tables;
JHN.2.PLAIN: So He made a whip out of cords and drove all from the temple courts, both sheep and cattle. He poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables.

JHN.2.BSB: To those selling doves He said, “Get these out of here! How dare you turn My Father’s house into a marketplace!”
JHN.2.KJV: And said to them that sold doves, Take these things hence; make not my Father’s house an house of merchandise.
JHN.2.PLAIN: To those selling doves He said, “Get these out of here! How dare you turn My Father’s house into a marketplace!”

JHN.2.BSB: His disciples remembered that it is written: “Zeal for Your house will consume Me.”
JHN.2.KJV: And his disciples remembered that it was written, The zeal of your house has eaten me up. ¶
JHN.2.PLAIN: His disciples remembered that it is written: “Zeal for Your house will consume Me.”

JHN.2.BSB: On account of this, the Jews demanded, “What sign can You show us to prove Your authority to do these things?”
JHN.2.KJV: Then answered the Jews and said to him, What sign show you to us, seeing that you do these things?
JHN.2.PLAIN: On account of this, the Jews demanded, “What sign can You show us to prove Your authority to do these things?”

JHN.2.BSB: Jesus answered, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up again.”
JHN.2.KJV: Jesus answered and said to them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.
JHN.2.PLAIN: Jesus answered, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up again.”

JHN.2.BSB: “This temple took forty-six years to build,” the Jews replied, “and You are going to raise it up in three days?”
JHN.2.KJV: Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and will you raise it up in three days?
JHN.2.PLAIN: “This temple took forty-six years to build,” the Jews replied, “and You are going to raise it up in three days?”

JHN.2.BSB: But Jesus was speaking about the temple of His body.
JHN.2.KJV: But he spoke of the temple of his body.
JHN.2.PLAIN: But Jesus was speaking about the temple of His body.

JHN.2.BSB: After He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this. Then they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.
JHN.2.KJV: When therefore he was risen from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this to them; and they believed the scripture, and the word which Jesus had said. ¶
JHN.2.PLAIN: After He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this. Then they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.

JHN.2.BSB: While He was in Jerusalem at the Passover Feast, many people saw the signs He was doing and believed in His name.
JHN.2.KJV: Now when he was in Jerusalem at the passover, in the feast day, many believed in his name, when they saw the miracles which he did.
JHN.2.PLAIN: While He was in Jerusalem at the Passover Feast, many people saw the signs He was doing and believed in His name.

JHN.2.BSB: But Jesus did not entrust Himself to them, for He knew them all.
JHN.2.KJV: But Jesus did not commit himself to them, because he knew all men,
JHN.2.PLAIN: But Jesus did not entrust Himself to them, for He knew them all.

JHN.2.BSB: He did not need any testimony about man, for He knew what was in a man.
JHN.2.KJV: And needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man.
JHN.2.PLAIN: He did not need any testimony about man, for He knew what was in a man.

JHN.3.BSB: Now there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a leader of the Jews.
JHN.3.KJV: There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews:
JHN.3.PLAIN: Now there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a leader of the Jews.

JHN.3.BSB: He came to Jesus at night and said, “Rabbi, we know that You are a teacher who has come from God. For no one could perform the signs You are doing if God were not with him.”
JHN.3.KJV: The same came to Jesus by night, and said to him, Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher come from God: for no man can do these miracles that you do, except God be with him.
JHN.3.PLAIN: He came to Jesus at night and said, “Rabbi, we know that You are a teacher who has come from God. For no one could perform the signs You are doing if God were not with him.”

JHN.3.BSB: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again.”
JHN.3.KJV: Jesus answered and said to him, Truly, truly, I say to you, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
JHN.3.PLAIN: Jesus replied, “Hear this steady truth, no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again.”

JHN.3.BSB: “How can a man be born when he is old?” Nicodemus asked. “Can he enter his mother’s womb a second time to be born?”
JHN.3.KJV: Nicodemus says to him, How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter the second time into his mother’s womb, and be born?
JHN.3.PLAIN: “How can a man be born when he is old?” Nicodemus asked. “Can he enter his mother’s womb a second time to be born?”

JHN.3.BSB: Jesus answered, “Truly, truly, I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God unless he is born of water and the Spirit.
JHN.3.KJV: Jesus answered, Truly, truly, I say to you, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
JHN.3.PLAIN: Jesus answered, “Hear this steady truth, no one can enter the kingdom of God unless he is born of water and the Spirit.

JHN.3.BSB: Flesh is born of flesh, but spirit is born of the Spirit.
JHN.3.KJV: That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.
JHN.3.PLAIN: Flesh is born of flesh, but spirit is born of the Spirit.

JHN.3.BSB: Do not be amazed that I said, ‘You must be born again.’
JHN.3.KJV: Marvel not that I said to you, You must be born again.
JHN.3.PLAIN: Do not be amazed that I said, ‘You must be born again.’

JHN.3.BSB: The wind blows where it wishes. You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.”
JHN.3.KJV: The wind blows where it wants, and you hear the sound thereof, but can not tell from where it comes, and where it goes: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.
JHN.3.PLAIN: The wind blows where it wishes. You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.”

JHN.3.BSB: “How can this be?” Nicodemus asked.
JHN.3.KJV: Nicodemus answered and said to him, How can these things be?
JHN.3.PLAIN: “How can this be?” Nicodemus asked.

JHN.3.BSB: “You are Israel’s teacher,” said Jesus, “and you do not understand these things?
JHN.3.KJV: Jesus answered and said to him, Are you a master of Israel, and know not these things?
JHN.3.PLAIN: “You are Israel’s teacher,” said Jesus, “and you do not understand these things?

JHN.3.BSB: Truly, truly, I tell you, we speak of what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, and yet you people do not accept our testimony.
JHN.3.KJV: Truly, truly, I say to you, We speak that we do know, and testify that we have seen; and you receive not our witness.
JHN.3.PLAIN: Hear this steady truth, we speak of what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, and yet you people do not accept our testimony.

JHN.3.BSB: If I have told you about earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you about heavenly things?
JHN.3.KJV: If I have told you earthly things, and you believe not, how shall you believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?
JHN.3.PLAIN: If I have told you about earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you about heavenly things?

JHN.3.BSB: No one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven—the Son of Man.
JHN.3.KJV: And no man has ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven. ¶
JHN.3.PLAIN: No one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven—the Son of Man.

JHN.3.BSB: Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up,
JHN.3.KJV: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up:
JHN.3.PLAIN: Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up,

JHN.3.BSB: that everyone who believes in Him may have eternal life.
JHN.3.KJV: That whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life. ¶
JHN.3.PLAIN: that everyone who believes in Him may have eternal life.

JHN.3.BSB: For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son, that everyone who believes in Him shall not perish but have eternal life.
JHN.3.KJV: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
JHN.3.PLAIN: God loved the world so much that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him won't perish but will have eternal life.

JHN.3.BSB: For God did not send His Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through Him.
JHN.3.KJV: For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. ¶
JHN.3.PLAIN: For God did not send His Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through Him.

JHN.3.BSB: Whoever believes in Him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe has already been condemned, because he has not believed in the name of God’s one and only Son.
JHN.3.KJV: He that believes on him is not condemned: but he that believes not is condemned already, because he has not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.
JHN.3.PLAIN: Whoever believes in Him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe has already been condemned, because he has not believed in the name of God’s one and only Son.

JHN.3.BSB: And this is the verdict: The Light has come into the world, but men loved the darkness rather than the Light because their deeds were evil.
JHN.3.KJV: And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.
JHN.3.PLAIN: And this is the verdict: The Light has come into the world, but men loved the darkness rather than the Light because their deeds were evil.

JHN.3.BSB: Everyone who does evil hates the Light, and does not come into the Light for fear that his deeds will be exposed.
JHN.3.KJV: For every one that does evil hates the light, neither comes to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.
JHN.3.PLAIN: Everyone who does evil hates the Light, and does not come into the Light for fear that his deeds will be exposed.

JHN.3.BSB: But whoever practices the truth comes into the Light, so that it may be seen clearly that what he has done has been accomplished in God.”
JHN.3.KJV: But he that does truth comes to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are worked in God. ¶
JHN.3.PLAIN: But whoever practices the truth comes into the Light, so that it may be seen clearly that what he has done has been accomplished in God.”

JHN.3.BSB: After this, Jesus and His disciples went into the Judean countryside, where He spent some time with them and baptized.
JHN.3.KJV: After these things came Jesus and his disciples into the land of Judaea; and there he tarried with them, and baptized. ¶
JHN.3.PLAIN: After this, Jesus and His disciples went into the Judean countryside, where He spent some time with them and baptized.

JHN.3.BSB: Now John was also baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because the water was plentiful there, and people kept coming to be baptized.
JHN.3.KJV: And John also was baptizing in Aenon near to Salim, because there was much water there: and they came, and were baptized.
JHN.3.PLAIN: Now John was also baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because the water was plentiful there, and people kept coming to be baptized.

JHN.3.BSB: (For John had not yet been thrown into prison.)
JHN.3.KJV: For John was not yet cast into prison. ¶
JHN.3.PLAIN: (For John had not yet been thrown into prison.)

JHN.3.BSB: Then a dispute arose between John’s disciples and a certain Jew over the issue of ceremonial washing.
JHN.3.KJV: Then there arose a question between some of John’s disciples and the Jews about purifying.
JHN.3.PLAIN: Then a dispute arose between John’s disciples and a certain Jew over the issue of ceremonial washing.

JHN.3.BSB: So John’s disciples came to him and said, “Look, Rabbi, the One who was with you beyond the Jordan, the One you testified about—He is baptizing, and everyone is going to Him.”
JHN.3.KJV: And they came to John, and said to him, Rabbi, he that was with you beyond Jordan, to whom you bore witness, behold, the same baptizes, and all men come to him.
JHN.3.PLAIN: So John’s disciples came to him and said, “Look, Rabbi, the One who was with you beyond the Jordan, the One you testified about—He is baptizing, and everyone is going to Him.”

JHN.3.BSB: John replied, “A man can receive only what is given him from heaven.
JHN.3.KJV: John answered and said, A man can receive nothing, except it be given him from heaven.
JHN.3.PLAIN: John replied, “A man can receive only what is given him from heaven.

JHN.3.BSB: You yourselves can testify that I said, ‘I am not the Christ, but am sent ahead of Him.’
JHN.3.KJV: You yourselves bear me witness, that I said, I am not the Christ, but that I am sent before him.
JHN.3.PLAIN: You yourselves can testify that I said, ‘I am not the Christ, but am sent ahead of Him.’

JHN.3.BSB: The bride belongs to the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom stands and listens for him, and is overjoyed to hear the bridegroom’s voice. That joy is mine, and it is now complete.
JHN.3.KJV: He that has the bride is the bridegroom: but the friend of the bridegroom, which stands and hears him, rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice: this my joy therefore is fulfilled.
JHN.3.PLAIN: The bride belongs to the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom stands and listens for him, and is overjoyed to hear the bridegroom’s voice. That joy is mine, and it is now complete.

JHN.3.BSB: He must increase; I must decrease.
JHN.3.KJV: He must increase, but I must decrease.
JHN.3.PLAIN: He must increase; I must decrease.

JHN.3.BSB: The One who comes from above is above all. The one who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks as one from the earth. The One who comes from heaven is above all.
JHN.3.KJV: He that comes from above is above all: he that is of the earth is earthly, and speaks of the earth: he that comes from heaven is above all.
JHN.3.PLAIN: The One who comes from above is above all. The one who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks as one from the earth. The One who comes from heaven is above all.

JHN.3.BSB: He testifies to what He has seen and heard, yet no one accepts His testimony.
JHN.3.KJV: And what he has seen and heard, that he testifies; and no man receives his testimony.
JHN.3.PLAIN: He testifies to what He has seen and heard, yet no one accepts His testimony.

JHN.3.BSB: Whoever accepts His testimony has certified that God is truthful.
JHN.3.KJV: He that has received his testimony has set to his seal that God is true.
JHN.3.PLAIN: Whoever accepts His testimony has certified that God is truthful.

JHN.3.BSB: For the One whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for God gives the Spirit without limit.
JHN.3.KJV: For he whom God has sent speaks the words of God: for God gives not the Spirit by measure to him.
JHN.3.PLAIN: For the One whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for God gives the Spirit without limit.

JHN.3.BSB: The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in His hands.
JHN.3.KJV: The Father loves the Son, and has given all things into his hand.
JHN.3.PLAIN: The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in His hands.

JHN.3.BSB: Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life. Whoever rejects the Son will not see life. Instead, the wrath of God remains on him.”
JHN.3.KJV: He that believes on the Son has everlasting life: and he that believes not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God stays on him.
JHN.3.PLAIN: Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life. Whoever rejects the Son will not see life. Instead, the wrath of God remains on him.”

JHN.4.BSB: When Jesus realized that the Pharisees were aware He was gaining and baptizing more disciples than John
JHN.4.KJV: When therefore the LORD knew how the Pharisees had heard that Jesus made and baptized more disciples than John,
JHN.4.PLAIN: When Jesus realized that the Pharisees were aware He was gaining and baptizing more disciples than John

JHN.4.BSB: (although it was not Jesus who baptized, but His disciples),
JHN.4.KJV: (Though Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples,)
JHN.4.PLAIN: (although it was not Jesus who baptized, but His disciples),

JHN.4.BSB: He left Judea and returned to Galilee.
JHN.4.KJV: He left Judaea, and departed again into Galilee.
JHN.4.PLAIN: He left Judea and returned to Galilee.

JHN.4.BSB: Now He had to pass through Samaria.
JHN.4.KJV: And he must needs go through Samaria.
JHN.4.PLAIN: Now He had to pass through Samaria.

JHN.4.BSB: So He came to a town of Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of ground that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
JHN.4.KJV: Then comes he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
JHN.4.PLAIN: So He came to a town of Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of ground that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.

JHN.4.BSB: Since Jacob’s well was there, Jesus, weary from His journey, sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour.
JHN.4.KJV: Now Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus on the well: and it was about the sixth hour.
JHN.4.PLAIN: Since Jacob’s well was there, Jesus, weary from His journey, sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour.

JHN.4.BSB: When a Samaritan woman came to draw water, Jesus said to her, “Give Me a drink.”
JHN.4.KJV: There comes a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus says to her, Give me to drink.
JHN.4.PLAIN: When a Samaritan woman came to draw water, Jesus said to her, “Give Me a drink.”

JHN.4.BSB: (His disciples had gone into the town to buy food.)
JHN.4.KJV: (For his disciples were gone away to the city to buy meat.)
JHN.4.PLAIN: (His disciples had gone into the town to buy food.)

JHN.4.BSB: “You are a Jew,” said the woman. “How can You ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.)
JHN.4.KJV: Then says the woman of Samaria to him, How is it that you, being a Jew, ask drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.
JHN.4.PLAIN: “You are a Jew,” said the woman. “How can You ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.)

JHN.4.BSB: Jesus answered, “If you knew the gift of God and who is asking you for a drink, you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water.”
JHN.4.KJV: Jesus answered and said to her, If you knew the gift of God, and who it is that says to you, Give me to drink; you would have asked of him, and he would have given you living water.
JHN.4.PLAIN: Jesus answered, “If you knew the gift of God and who is asking you for a drink, you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water.”

JHN.4.BSB: “Sir,” the woman replied, “You have nothing to draw with and the well is deep. Where then will You get this living water?
JHN.4.KJV: The woman says to him, Sir, you have nothing to draw with, and the well is deep: from where then have you that living water?
JHN.4.PLAIN: “Sir,” the woman replied, “You have nothing to draw with and the well is deep. Where then will You get this living water?

JHN.4.BSB: Are You greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well and drank from it himself, as did his sons and his livestock?”
JHN.4.KJV: Are you greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well, and drank thereof himself, and his children, and his cattle?
JHN.4.PLAIN: Are You greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well and drank from it himself, as did his sons and his livestock?”

JHN.4.BSB: Jesus said to her, “Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again.
JHN.4.KJV: Jesus answered and said to her, Whoever drinks of this water shall thirst again:
JHN.4.PLAIN: Jesus said to her, “Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again.

JHN.4.BSB: But whoever drinks the water I give him will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give him will become in him a fount of water springing up to eternal life.”
JHN.4.KJV: But whoever drinks of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
JHN.4.PLAIN: Whoever drinks the water I give will never be thirsty again — it becomes a spring inside them, welling up to eternal life.

JHN.4.BSB: The woman said to Him, “Sir, give me this water so that I will not get thirsty and have to keep coming here to draw water.”
JHN.4.KJV: The woman says to him, Sir, give me this water, that I thirst not, neither come here to draw.
JHN.4.PLAIN: The woman said to Him, “Sir, give me this water so that I will not get thirsty and have to keep coming here to draw water.”

JHN.4.BSB: Jesus told her, “Go, call your husband and come back.”
JHN.4.KJV: Jesus says to her, Go, call your husband, and come here.
JHN.4.PLAIN: Jesus told her, “Go, call your husband and come back.”

JHN.4.BSB: “I have no husband,” the woman replied. Jesus said to her, “You are correct to say that you have no husband.
JHN.4.KJV: The woman answered and said, I have no husband. Jesus said to her, You have well said, I have no husband:
JHN.4.PLAIN: “I have no husband,” the woman replied. Jesus said to her, “You are correct to say that you have no husband.

JHN.4.BSB: In fact, you have had five husbands, and the man you now have is not your husband. You have spoken truthfully.”
JHN.4.KJV: For you have had five husbands; and he whom you now have is not your husband: in that said you truly.
JHN.4.PLAIN: In fact, you have had five husbands, and the man you now have is not your husband. You have spoken truthfully.”

JHN.4.BSB: “Sir,” the woman said, “I see that You are a prophet.
JHN.4.KJV: The woman says to him, Sir, I perceive that you are a prophet.
JHN.4.PLAIN: “Sir,” the woman said, “I see that You are a prophet.

JHN.4.BSB: Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews say that the place where one must worship is in Jerusalem.”
JHN.4.KJV: Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and you say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.
JHN.4.PLAIN: Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews say that the place where one must worship is in Jerusalem.”

JHN.4.BSB: “Believe Me, woman,” Jesus replied, “a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
JHN.4.KJV: Jesus says to her, Woman, believe me, the hour comes, when you shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.
JHN.4.PLAIN: “Believe Me, woman,” Jesus replied, “a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.

JHN.4.BSB: You worship what you do not know; we worship what we do know, for salvation is from the Jews.
JHN.4.KJV: You worship you know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.
JHN.4.PLAIN: You worship what you do not know; we worship what we do know, for salvation is from the Jews.

JHN.4.BSB: But a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him.
JHN.4.KJV: But the hour comes, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeks such to worship him.
JHN.4.PLAIN: But a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him.

JHN.4.BSB: God is Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.”
JHN.4.KJV: God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.
JHN.4.PLAIN: God is Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.”

JHN.4.BSB: The woman said, “I know that Messiah” (called Christ) “is coming. When He comes, He will explain everything to us.”
JHN.4.KJV: The woman says to him, I know that Messias comes, which is called Christ: when he is come, he will tell us all things.
JHN.4.PLAIN: The woman said, “I know that Messiah” (called Christ) “is coming. When He comes, He will explain everything to us.”

JHN.4.BSB: Jesus answered, “I who speak to you am He.”
JHN.4.KJV: Jesus says to her, I that speak to you am he. ¶
JHN.4.PLAIN: Jesus answered, “I who speak to you am He.”

JHN.4.BSB: Just then His disciples returned and were surprised that He was speaking with a woman. But no one asked Him, “What do You want from her?” or “Why are You talking with her?”
JHN.4.KJV: And on this came his disciples, and marveled that he talked with the woman: yet no man said, What seek you? or, Why talk you with her?
JHN.4.PLAIN: Just then His disciples returned and were surprised that He was speaking with a woman. But no one asked Him, “What do You want from her?” or “Why are You talking with her?”

JHN.4.BSB: Then the woman left her water jar, went back into the town, and said to the people,
JHN.4.KJV: The woman then left her water pot, and went her way into the city, and says to the men,
JHN.4.PLAIN: Then the woman left her water jar, went back into the town, and said to the people,

JHN.4.BSB: “Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did. Could this be the Christ?”
JHN.4.KJV: Come, see a man, which told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ?
JHN.4.PLAIN: “Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did. Could this be the Christ?”

JHN.4.BSB: So they left the town and made their way toward Jesus.
JHN.4.KJV: Then they went out of the city, and came to him. ¶
JHN.4.PLAIN: So they left the town and made their way toward Jesus.

JHN.4.BSB: Meanwhile the disciples urged Him, “Rabbi, eat something.”
JHN.4.KJV: In the mean while his disciples prayed him, saying, Master, eat.
JHN.4.PLAIN: Meanwhile the disciples urged Him, “Rabbi, eat something.”

JHN.4.BSB: But He told them, “I have food to eat that you know nothing about.”
JHN.4.KJV: But he said to them, I have meat to eat that you know not of.
JHN.4.PLAIN: But He told them, “I have food to eat that you know nothing about.”

JHN.4.BSB: So the disciples asked one another, “Could someone have brought Him food?”
JHN.4.KJV: Therefore says the disciples one to another, Has any man brought him something to eat?
JHN.4.PLAIN: So the disciples asked one another, “Could someone have brought Him food?”

JHN.4.BSB: Jesus explained, “My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me and to finish His work.
JHN.4.KJV: Jesus said to them, My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.
JHN.4.PLAIN: Jesus explained, “My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me and to finish His work.

JHN.4.BSB: Do you not say, ‘There are still four months until the harvest’? I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are ripe for harvest.
JHN.4.KJV: Say not you, There are yet four months, and then comes harvest? behold, I say to you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest.
JHN.4.PLAIN: Do you not say, ‘There are still four months until the harvest’? I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are ripe for harvest.

JHN.4.BSB: Already the reaper draws his wages and gathers a crop for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.
JHN.4.KJV: And he that reaps receives wages, and gathers fruit to life eternal: that both he that sows and he that reaps may rejoice together.
JHN.4.PLAIN: Already the reaper draws his wages and gathers a crop for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.

JHN.4.BSB: For in this case the saying ‘One sows and another reaps’ is true.
JHN.4.KJV: And herein is that saying true, One sows, and another reaps.
JHN.4.PLAIN: For in this case the saying ‘One sows and another reaps’ is true.

JHN.4.BSB: I sent you to reap what you have not worked for; others have done the hard work, and now you have taken up their labor.”
JHN.4.KJV: I sent you to reap that where on you bestowed no labor: other men labored, and you are entered into their labors. ¶
JHN.4.PLAIN: I sent you to reap what you have not worked for; others have done the hard work, and now you have taken up their labor.”

JHN.4.BSB: Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in Jesus because of the woman’s testimony, “He told me everything I ever did.”
JHN.4.KJV: And many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him for the saying of the woman, which testified, He told me all that ever I did.
JHN.4.PLAIN: Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in Jesus because of the woman’s testimony, “He told me everything I ever did.”

JHN.4.BSB: So when the Samaritans came to Him, they asked Him to stay with them, and He stayed two days.
JHN.4.KJV: So when the Samaritans were come to him, they sought him that he would tarry with them: and he stayed there two days.
JHN.4.PLAIN: So when the Samaritans came to Him, they asked Him to stay with them, and He stayed two days.

JHN.4.BSB: And many more believed because of His message.
JHN.4.KJV: And many more believed because of his own word;
JHN.4.PLAIN: And many more believed because of His message.

JHN.4.BSB: They said to the woman, “We now believe not only because of your words; we have heard for ourselves, and we know that this man truly is the Savior of the world.”
JHN.4.KJV: And said to the woman, Now we believe, not because of your saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world. ¶
JHN.4.PLAIN: They said to the woman, “We now believe not only because of your words; we have heard for ourselves, and we know that this man truly is the Savior of the world.”

JHN.4.BSB: After two days, Jesus left for Galilee.
JHN.4.KJV: Now after two days he departed there, and went into Galilee.
JHN.4.PLAIN: After two days, Jesus left for Galilee.

JHN.4.BSB: Now He Himself had testified that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown.
JHN.4.KJV: For Jesus himself testified, that a prophet has no honor in his own country.
JHN.4.PLAIN: Now He Himself had testified that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown.

JHN.4.BSB: Yet when He arrived, the Galileans welcomed Him. They had seen all the great things He had done in Jerusalem at the feast, for they had gone there as well.
JHN.4.KJV: Then when he was come into Galilee, the Galilaeans received him, having seen all the things that he did at Jerusalem at the feast: for they also went to the feast.
JHN.4.PLAIN: Yet when He arrived, the Galileans welcomed Him. They had seen all the great things He had done in Jerusalem at the feast, for they had gone there as well.

JHN.4.BSB: So once again He came to Cana in Galilee, where He had turned the water into wine. And there was a royal official whose son lay sick at Capernaum.
JHN.4.KJV: So Jesus came again into Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. And there was a certain nobleman, whose son was sick at Capernaum.
JHN.4.PLAIN: So once again He came to Cana in Galilee, where He had turned the water into wine. And there was a royal official whose son lay sick at Capernaum.

JHN.4.BSB: When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went and begged Him to come down and heal his son, who was about to die.
JHN.4.KJV: When he heard that Jesus was come out of Judaea into Galilee, he went to him, and sought him that he would come down, and heal his son: for he was at the point of death.
JHN.4.PLAIN: When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went and begged Him to come down and heal his son, who was about to die.

JHN.4.BSB: Jesus said to him, “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will never believe.”
JHN.4.KJV: Then said Jesus to him, Except you see signs and wonders, you will not believe.
JHN.4.PLAIN: Jesus said to him, “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will never believe.”

JHN.4.BSB: “Sir,” the official said, “come down before my child dies.”
JHN.4.KJV: The nobleman says to him, Sir, come down before my child dies.
JHN.4.PLAIN: “Sir,” the official said, “come down before my child dies.”

JHN.4.BSB: “Go,” said Jesus. “Your son will live.” The man took Jesus at His word and departed.
JHN.4.KJV: Jesus says to him, Go your way; your son lives. And the man believed the word that Jesus had spoken to him, and he went his way.
JHN.4.PLAIN: “Go,” said Jesus. “Your son will live.” The man took Jesus at His word and departed.

JHN.4.BSB: And while he was still on the way, his servants met him with the news that his boy was alive.
JHN.4.KJV: And as he was now going down, his servants met him, and told him, saying, Your son lives.
JHN.4.PLAIN: And while he was still on the way, his servants met him with the news that his boy was alive.

JHN.4.BSB: So he inquired as to the hour when his son had recovered, and they told him, “The fever left him yesterday at the seventh hour.”
JHN.4.KJV: Then inquired he of them the hour when he began to amend. And they said to him, Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.
JHN.4.PLAIN: So he inquired as to the hour when his son had recovered, and they told him, “The fever left him yesterday at the seventh hour.”

JHN.4.BSB: Then the father realized that this was the very hour in which Jesus had told him, “Your son will live.” And he and all his household believed.
JHN.4.KJV: So the father knew that it was at the same hour, in the which Jesus said to him, Your son lives: and himself believed, and his whole house.
JHN.4.PLAIN: Then the father realized that this was the very hour in which Jesus had told him, “Your son will live.” And he and all his household believed.

JHN.4.BSB: This was now the second sign that Jesus performed after coming from Judea into Galilee.
JHN.4.KJV: This is again the second miracle that Jesus did, when he was come out of Judaea into Galilee.
JHN.4.PLAIN: This was now the second sign that Jesus performed after coming from Judea into Galilee.

JHN.5.BSB: Some time later there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
JHN.5.KJV: After this there was a feast of the Jews; and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
JHN.5.PLAIN: Some time later there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

JHN.5.BSB: Now there is in Jerusalem near the Sheep Gate a pool with five covered colonnades, which in Hebrew is called Bethesda.
JHN.5.KJV: Now there is at Jerusalem by the sheep market a pool, which is called in the Hebrew tongue Bethesda, having five porches.
JHN.5.PLAIN: Now there is in Jerusalem near the Sheep Gate a pool with five covered colonnades, which in Hebrew is called Bethesda.

JHN.5.BSB: On these walkways lay a great number of the sick, the blind, the lame, and the paralyzed.
JHN.5.KJV: In these lay a great multitude of weak folk, of blind, halt, withered, waiting for the moving of the water.
JHN.5.PLAIN: On these walkways lay a great number of the sick, the blind, the lame, and the paralyzed.

JHN.5.KJV: For an angel went down at a certain season into the pool, and troubled the water: whoever then first after the troubling of the water stepped in was made whole of whatever disease he had.

JHN.5.BSB: One man there had been an invalid for thirty-eight years.
JHN.5.KJV: And a certain man was there, which had an infirmity thirty and eight years.
JHN.5.PLAIN: One man there had been an invalid for thirty-eight years.

JHN.5.BSB: When Jesus saw him lying there and realized that he had spent a long time in this condition, He asked him, “Do you want to get well?”
JHN.5.KJV: When Jesus saw him lie, and knew that he had been now a long time in that case, he says to him, Will you be made whole?
JHN.5.PLAIN: When Jesus saw him lying there and realized that he had spent a long time in this condition, He asked him, “Do you want to get well?”

JHN.5.BSB: “Sir,” the invalid replied, “I have no one to help me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am on my way, someone else goes in before me.”
JHN.5.KJV: The weak man answered him, Sir, I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into the pool: but while I am coming, another steps down before me.
JHN.5.PLAIN: “Sir,” the invalid replied, “I have no one to help me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am on my way, someone else goes in before me.”
