ACT.15.PLAIN: For Moses has been proclaimed in every city from ancient times and is read in the synagogues on every Sabbath.”

ACT.15.BSB: Then the apostles and elders, with the whole church, decided to select men from among them to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, two leaders among the brothers,
ACT.15.KJV: Then pleased it the apostles and elders with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas; namely, Judas surnamed Barsabas and Silas, chief men among the brothers:
ACT.15.PLAIN: Then the apostles and elders, with the whole church, decided to select men from among them to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, two leaders among the brothers,

ACT.15.BSB: and sent them with this letter: The apostles and the elders, your brothers, To the brothers among the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Greetings.
ACT.15.KJV: And they wrote letters by them after this manner; The apostles and elders and brothers send greeting to the brothers which are of the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia.
ACT.15.PLAIN: and sent them with this letter: The apostles and the elders, your brothers, To the brothers among the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Greetings.

ACT.15.BSB: It has come to our attention that some went out from us without our authorization and unsettled you, troubling your minds by what they said.
ACT.15.KJV: For as much as we have heard, that certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, You must be circumcised, and keep the law: to whom we gave no such commandment:
ACT.15.PLAIN: It has come to our attention that some went out from us without our authorization and unsettled you, troubling your minds by what they said.

ACT.15.BSB: So we all agreed to choose men to send to you along with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
ACT.15.KJV: It seemed good to us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
ACT.15.PLAIN: So we all agreed to choose men to send to you along with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,

ACT.15.BSB: men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
ACT.15.KJV: Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
ACT.15.PLAIN: men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

ACT.15.BSB: Therefore we are sending Judas and Silas to tell you in person the same things we are writing.
ACT.15.KJV: We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, who shall also tell you the same things by mouth.
ACT.15.PLAIN: Therefore we are sending Judas and Silas to tell you in person the same things we are writing.

ACT.15.BSB: It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to burden you with anything beyond these essential requirements:
ACT.15.KJV: For it seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us, to lay on you no greater burden than these necessary things;
ACT.15.PLAIN: It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to burden you with anything beyond these essential requirements:

ACT.15.BSB: You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. You will do well to avoid these things. Farewell.
ACT.15.KJV: That you abstain from meats offered to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from fornication: from which if you keep yourselves, you shall do well. Fare you well.
ACT.15.PLAIN: You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. You will do well to avoid these things. Farewell.

ACT.15.BSB: So the men were sent off and went down to Antioch, where they assembled the congregation and delivered the letter.
ACT.15.KJV: So when they were dismissed, they came to Antioch: and when they had gathered the multitude together, they delivered the letter:
ACT.15.PLAIN: So the men were sent off and went down to Antioch, where they assembled the congregation and delivered the letter.

ACT.15.BSB: When the people read it, they rejoiced at its encouraging message.
ACT.15.KJV: Which when they had read, they rejoiced for the consolation.
ACT.15.PLAIN: When the people read it, they rejoiced at its encouraging message.

ACT.15.BSB: Judas and Silas, who themselves were prophets, said much to encourage and strengthen the brothers.
ACT.15.KJV: And Judas and Silas, being prophets also themselves, exhorted the brothers with many words, and confirmed them.
ACT.15.PLAIN: Judas and Silas, who themselves were prophets, said much to encourage and strengthen the brothers.

ACT.15.BSB: After spending some time there, they were sent off by the brothers in peace to return to those who had sent them.
ACT.15.KJV: And after they had tarried there a space, they were let go in peace from the brothers to the apostles.
ACT.15.PLAIN: After spending some time there, they were sent off by the brothers in peace to return to those who had sent them.

ACT.15.KJV: Notwithstanding it pleased Silas to abide there still.

ACT.15.BSB: But Paul and Barnabas remained at Antioch, along with many others, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord.
ACT.15.KJV: Paul also and Barnabas continued in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, with many others also. ¶
ACT.15.PLAIN: But Paul and Barnabas remained at Antioch, along with many others, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord.

ACT.15.BSB: Some time later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let us go back and visit the brothers in every town where we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.”
ACT.15.KJV: And some days after Paul said to Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brothers in every city where we have preached the word of the LORD, and see how they do.
ACT.15.PLAIN: Some time later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let us go back and visit the brothers in every town where we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.”

ACT.15.BSB: Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark.
ACT.15.KJV: And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark.
ACT.15.PLAIN: Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark.

ACT.15.BSB: But Paul thought it best not to take him, because he had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not accompanied them in the work.
ACT.15.KJV: But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work.
ACT.15.PLAIN: But Paul thought it best not to take him, because he had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not accompanied them in the work.

ACT.15.BSB: Their disagreement was so sharp that they parted company. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus,
ACT.15.KJV: And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed to Cyprus;
ACT.15.PLAIN: Their disagreement was so sharp that they parted company. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus,

ACT.15.BSB: but Paul chose Silas and left, commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.
ACT.15.KJV: And Paul chose Silas, and departed, being recommended by the brothers to the grace of God.
ACT.15.PLAIN: but Paul chose Silas and left, commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.

ACT.15.BSB: And he traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
ACT.15.KJV: And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches.
ACT.15.PLAIN: And he traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.

ACT.16.BSB: Paul came to Derbe and then to Lystra, where he found a disciple named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father.
ACT.16.KJV: Then came he to Derbe and Lystra: and, behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timotheus, the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek:
ACT.16.PLAIN: Paul came to Derbe and then to Lystra, where he found a disciple named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father.

ACT.16.BSB: The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.
ACT.16.KJV: Which was well reported of by the brothers that were at Lystra and Iconium.
ACT.16.PLAIN: The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.

ACT.16.BSB: Paul wanted Timothy to accompany him, so he took him and circumcised him on account of the Jews in that area, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
ACT.16.KJV: Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters: for they knew all that his father was a Greek.
ACT.16.PLAIN: Paul wanted Timothy to accompany him, so he took him and circumcised him on account of the Jews in that area, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.

ACT.16.BSB: As they went from town to town, they delivered the decisions handed down by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem for the people to obey.
ACT.16.KJV: And as they went through the cities, they delivered them the decrees for to keep, that were ordained of the apostles and elders which were at Jerusalem.
ACT.16.PLAIN: As they went from town to town, they delivered the decisions handed down by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem for the people to obey.

ACT.16.BSB: So the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew daily in numbers.
ACT.16.KJV: And so were the churches established in the faith, and increased in number daily.
ACT.16.PLAIN: So the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew daily in numbers.

ACT.16.BSB: After the Holy Spirit had prevented them from speaking the word in the province of Asia, they traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia.
ACT.16.KJV: Now when they had gone throughout Phrygia and the region of Galatia, and were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia,
ACT.16.PLAIN: After the Holy Spirit had prevented them from speaking the word in the province of Asia, they traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia.

ACT.16.BSB: And when they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them.
ACT.16.KJV: After they were come to Mysia, they assayed to go into Bithynia: but the Spirit suffered them not.
ACT.16.PLAIN: And when they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them.

ACT.16.BSB: So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.
ACT.16.KJV: And they passing by Mysia came down to Troas.
ACT.16.PLAIN: So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.

ACT.16.BSB: During the night, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
ACT.16.KJV: And a vision appeared to Paul in the night; There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us.
ACT.16.PLAIN: During the night Paul had a vision: a man of Macedonia stood and begged him, 'Come over to Macedonia and help us.'

ACT.16.BSB: As soon as Paul had seen the vision, we got ready to leave for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.
ACT.16.KJV: And after he had seen the vision, immediately we endeavored to go into Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the Lord had called us for to preach the gospel to them.
ACT.16.PLAIN: As soon as Paul had seen the vision, we got ready to leave for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.

ACT.16.BSB: We sailed from Troas straight to Samothrace, and the following day on to Neapolis.
ACT.16.KJV: Therefore loosing from Troas, we came with a straight course to Samothracia, and the next day to Neapolis;
ACT.16.PLAIN: We sailed from Troas straight to Samothrace, and the following day on to Neapolis.

ACT.16.BSB: From there we went to the Roman colony of Philippi, the leading city of that district of Macedonia. And we stayed there several days.
ACT.16.KJV: And from there to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia, and a colony: and we were in that city abiding certain days.
ACT.16.PLAIN: From there we went to the Roman colony of Philippi, the leading city of that district of Macedonia. And we stayed there several days.

ACT.16.BSB: On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate along the river, where it was customary to find a place of prayer. After sitting down, we spoke to the women who had gathered there.
ACT.16.KJV: And on the sabbath we went out of the city by a river side, where prayer was wont to be made; and we sat down, and spoke to the women which resorted thither. ¶
ACT.16.PLAIN: On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate along the river, where it was customary to find a place of prayer. After sitting down, we spoke to the women who had gathered there.

ACT.16.BSB: Among those listening was a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who was a worshiper of God. The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message.
ACT.16.KJV: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended to the things which were spoken of Paul.
ACT.16.PLAIN: A woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth who worshiped God, was listening. The Lord opened her heart to respond to what Paul was saying.

ACT.16.BSB: And when she and her household had been baptized, she urged us, “If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.” And she persuaded us.
ACT.16.KJV: And when she was baptized, and her household, she sought us, saying, If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there. And she constrained us. ¶
ACT.16.PLAIN: And when she and her household had been baptized, she urged us, “If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.” And she persuaded us.

ACT.16.BSB: One day as we were going to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl with a spirit of divination, who earned a large income for her masters by fortune-telling.
ACT.16.KJV: And it came to pass, as we went to prayer, a certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination met us, which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying:
ACT.16.PLAIN: One day as we were going to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl with a spirit of divination, who earned a large income for her masters by fortune-telling.

ACT.16.BSB: This girl followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation!”
ACT.16.KJV: The same followed Paul and us, and cried, saying, These men are the servants of the most high God, which show to us the way of salvation.
ACT.16.PLAIN: This girl followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation!”

ACT.16.BSB: She continued this for many days. Eventually Paul grew so aggravated that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!” And the spirit left her at that very moment.
ACT.16.KJV: And this did she many days. But Paul, being grieved, turned and said to the spirit, I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her. And he came out the same hour. ¶
ACT.16.PLAIN: She continued this for many days. Eventually Paul grew so aggravated that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!” And the spirit left her at that very moment.

ACT.16.BSB: When the girl’s owners saw that their hope of making money was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities in the marketplace.
ACT.16.KJV: And when her masters saw that the hope of their gains was gone, they caught Paul and Silas, and drew them into the marketplace to the rulers,
ACT.16.PLAIN: When the girl’s owners saw that their hope of making money was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities in the marketplace.

ACT.16.BSB: They brought them to the magistrates and said, “These men are Jews and are throwing our city into turmoil
ACT.16.KJV: And brought them to the magistrates, saying, These men, being Jews, do exceedingly trouble our city,
ACT.16.PLAIN: They brought them to the magistrates and said, “These men are Jews and are throwing our city into turmoil

ACT.16.BSB: by promoting customs that are unlawful for us Romans to adopt or practice.”
ACT.16.KJV: And teach customs, which are not lawful for us to receive, neither to observe, being Romans.
ACT.16.PLAIN: by promoting customs that are unlawful for us Romans to adopt or practice.”

ACT.16.BSB: The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates ordered that they be stripped and beaten with rods.
ACT.16.KJV: And the multitude rose up together against them: and the magistrates rent off their clothes, and commanded to beat them.
ACT.16.PLAIN: The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates ordered that they be stripped and beaten with rods.

ACT.16.BSB: And after striking them with many blows, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them securely.
ACT.16.KJV: And when they had laid many stripes on them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely:
ACT.16.PLAIN: And after striking them with many blows, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them securely.

ACT.16.BSB: On receiving this order, he placed them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.
ACT.16.KJV: Who, having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks. ¶
ACT.16.PLAIN: On receiving this order, he placed them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.

ACT.16.BSB: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.
ACT.16.KJV: And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises to God: and the prisoners heard them.
ACT.16.PLAIN: Around midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening.

ACT.16.BSB: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the foundations of the prison. At once all the doors flew open and everyone’s chains came loose.
ACT.16.KJV: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one’s bands were loosed.
ACT.16.PLAIN: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the foundations of the prison. At once all the doors flew open and everyone’s chains came loose.

ACT.16.BSB: When the jailer woke up and saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, presuming that the prisoners had escaped.
ACT.16.KJV: And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled.
ACT.16.PLAIN: When the jailer woke up and saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, presuming that the prisoners had escaped.

ACT.16.BSB: But Paul called out in a loud voice, “Do not harm yourself! We are all here!”
ACT.16.KJV: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do yourself no harm: for we are all here.
ACT.16.PLAIN: But Paul called out in a loud voice, “Do not harm yourself! We are all here!”

ACT.16.BSB: Calling for lights, the jailer rushed in and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.
ACT.16.KJV: Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas,
ACT.16.PLAIN: Calling for lights, the jailer rushed in and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.

ACT.16.BSB: Then he brought them out and asked, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”
ACT.16.KJV: And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?
ACT.16.PLAIN: Then he brought them out and asked, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”

ACT.16.BSB: They replied, “Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your household.”
ACT.16.KJV: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and you shall be saved, and your house.
ACT.16.PLAIN: They said, 'Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved — you and your household.'

ACT.16.BSB: Then Paul and Silas spoke the word of the Lord to him and to everyone in his house.
ACT.16.KJV: And they spoke to him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house.
ACT.16.PLAIN: Then Paul and Silas spoke the word of the Lord to him and to everyone in his house.

ACT.16.BSB: At that hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds. And without delay, he and all his household were baptized.
ACT.16.KJV: And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway.
ACT.16.PLAIN: At that hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds. And without delay, he and all his household were baptized.

ACT.16.BSB: Then he brought them into his home and set a meal before them. So he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God.
ACT.16.KJV: And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.
ACT.16.PLAIN: Then he brought them into his home and set a meal before them. So he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God.

ACT.16.BSB: When daylight came, the magistrates sent their officers with the order: “Release those men.”
ACT.16.KJV: And when it was day, the magistrates sent the sergeants, saying, Let those men go.
ACT.16.PLAIN: When daylight came, the magistrates sent their officers with the order: “Release those men.”

ACT.16.BSB: The jailer informed Paul: “The magistrates have sent orders to release you. Now you may go on your way in peace.”
ACT.16.KJV: And the keeper of the prison told this saying to Paul, The magistrates have sent to let you go: now therefore depart, and go in peace.
ACT.16.PLAIN: The jailer informed Paul: “The magistrates have sent orders to release you. Now you may go on your way in peace.”

ACT.16.BSB: But Paul said to the officers, “They beat us publicly without a trial and threw us into prison, even though we are Roman citizens. And now do they want to send us away secretly? Absolutely not! Let them come themselves and escort us out!”
ACT.16.KJV: But Paul said to them, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privately? no truly; but let them come themselves and fetch us out.
ACT.16.PLAIN: But Paul said to the officers, “They beat us publicly without a trial and threw us into prison, even though we are Roman citizens. And now do they want to send us away secretly? Absolutely not! Let them come themselves and escort us out!”

ACT.16.BSB: So the officers relayed this message to the magistrates, who were alarmed to hear that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens.
ACT.16.KJV: And the sergeants told these words to the magistrates: and they feared, when they heard that they were Romans.
ACT.16.PLAIN: So the officers relayed this message to the magistrates, who were alarmed to hear that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens.

ACT.16.BSB: They came to appease them and led them out, requesting that they leave the city.
ACT.16.KJV: And they came and sought them, and brought them out, and desired them to depart out of the city.
ACT.16.PLAIN: They came to appease them and led them out, requesting that they leave the city.

ACT.16.BSB: After Paul and Silas came out of the prison, they went to Lydia’s house to see the brothers and encourage them. Then they left the city.
ACT.16.KJV: And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brothers, they comforted them, and departed.
ACT.16.PLAIN: After Paul and Silas came out of the prison, they went to Lydia’s house to see the brothers and encourage them. Then they left the city.

ACT.17.BSB: When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
ACT.17.KJV: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews:
ACT.17.PLAIN: When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

ACT.17.BSB: As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue, and on three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
ACT.17.KJV: And Paul, as his manner was, went in to them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,
ACT.17.PLAIN: As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue, and on three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,

ACT.17.BSB: explaining and proving that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. “This Jesus I am proclaiming to you is the Christ,” he declared.
ACT.17.KJV: Opening and alleging, that Christ must needs have suffered, and risen again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom I preach to you, is Christ.
ACT.17.PLAIN: explaining and proving that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. “This Jesus I am proclaiming to you is the Christ,” he declared.

ACT.17.BSB: Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women.
ACT.17.KJV: And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few. ¶
ACT.17.PLAIN: Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women.

ACT.17.BSB: The Jews, however, became jealous. So they brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar. They raided Jason’s house in search of Paul and Silas, hoping to bring them out to the people.
ACT.17.KJV: But the Jews which believed not, moved with envy, took to them certain lewd fellows of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the city on an uproar, and assaulted the house of Jason, and sought to bring them out to the people.
ACT.17.PLAIN: The Jews, however, became jealous. So they brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar. They raided Jason’s house in search of Paul and Silas, hoping to bring them out to the people.

ACT.17.BSB: But when they could not find them, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city officials, shouting, “These men who have turned the world upside down have now come here,
ACT.17.KJV: And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brothers to the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come here also;
ACT.17.PLAIN: But when they could not find them, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city officials, shouting, “These men who have turned the world upside down have now come here,

ACT.17.BSB: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. They are all defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!”
ACT.17.KJV: Whom Jason has received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, one Jesus.
ACT.17.PLAIN: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. They are all defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!”

ACT.17.BSB: On hearing this, the crowd and city officials were greatly disturbed.
ACT.17.KJV: And they troubled the people and the rulers of the city, when they heard these things.
ACT.17.PLAIN: On hearing this, the crowd and city officials were greatly disturbed.

ACT.17.BSB: And they collected bond from Jason and the others, and then released them.
ACT.17.KJV: And when they had taken security of Jason, and of the other, they let them go. ¶
ACT.17.PLAIN: And they collected bond from Jason and the others, and then released them.

ACT.17.BSB: As soon as night had fallen, the brothers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. On arriving there, they went into the Jewish synagogue.
ACT.17.KJV: And the brothers immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night to Berea: who coming thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.
ACT.17.PLAIN: As soon as night had fallen, the brothers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. On arriving there, they went into the Jewish synagogue.

ACT.17.BSB: Now the Bereans were more noble-minded than the Thessalonians, for they received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true.
ACT.17.KJV: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.
ACT.17.PLAIN: These people were more open-minded than those in Thessalonica; they received the message eagerly and examined the scriptures every day to see if it was true.

ACT.17.BSB: As a result, many of them believed, along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men.
ACT.17.KJV: Therefore many of them believed; also of honorable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.
ACT.17.PLAIN: As a result, many of them believed, along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men.

ACT.17.BSB: But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that Paul was also proclaiming the word of God in Berea, they went there themselves to incite and agitate the crowds.
ACT.17.KJV: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached of Paul at Berea, they came thither also, and stirred up the people.
ACT.17.PLAIN: But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that Paul was also proclaiming the word of God in Berea, they went there themselves to incite and agitate the crowds.

ACT.17.BSB: The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast, but Silas and Timothy remained in Berea.
ACT.17.KJV: And then immediately the brothers sent away Paul to go as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timotheus stayed there still.
ACT.17.PLAIN: The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast, but Silas and Timothy remained in Berea.

ACT.17.BSB: Those who escorted Paul brought him to Athens and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible.
ACT.17.KJV: And they that conducted Paul brought him to Athens: and receiving a commandment to Silas and Timotheus for to come to him with all speed, they departed. ¶
ACT.17.PLAIN: Those who escorted Paul brought him to Athens and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible.

ACT.17.BSB: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply disturbed in his spirit to see that the city was full of idols.
ACT.17.KJV: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry.
ACT.17.PLAIN: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply disturbed in his spirit to see that the city was full of idols.

ACT.17.BSB: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and God-fearing Gentiles, and in the marketplace with those he met each day.
ACT.17.KJV: Therefore disputed he in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the devout persons, and in the market daily with them that met with him.
ACT.17.PLAIN: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and God-fearing Gentiles, and in the marketplace with those he met each day.

ACT.17.BSB: Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also began to debate with him. Some of them asked, “What is this babbler trying to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign gods.” They said this because Paul was proclaiming the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.
ACT.17.KJV: Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seems to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached to them Jesus, and the resurrection.
ACT.17.PLAIN: Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also began to debate with him. Some of them asked, “What is this babbler trying to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign gods.” They said this because Paul was proclaiming the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.

ACT.17.BSB: So they took Paul and brought him to the Areopagus, where they asked him, “May we know what this new teaching is that you are presenting?
ACT.17.KJV: And they took him, and brought him to Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof you speak, is?
ACT.17.PLAIN: So they took Paul and brought him to the Areopagus, where they asked him, “May we know what this new teaching is that you are presenting?

ACT.17.BSB: For you are bringing some strange notions to our ears, and we want to know what they mean.”
ACT.17.KJV: For you bring certain strange things to our ears: we would know therefore what these things mean.
ACT.17.PLAIN: For you are bringing some strange notions to our ears, and we want to know what they mean.”

ACT.17.BSB: Now all the Athenians and foreigners who lived there spent their time doing nothing more than hearing and articulating new ideas.
ACT.17.KJV: (For all the Athenians and strangers which were there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.) ¶
ACT.17.PLAIN: Now all the Athenians and foreigners who lived there spent their time doing nothing more than hearing and articulating new ideas.

ACT.17.BSB: Then Paul stood up in the meeting of the Areopagus and said, “Men of Athens, I see that in every way you are very religious.
ACT.17.KJV: Then Paul stood in the middle of Mars’ hill, and said, You men of Athens, I perceive that in all things you are too superstitious.
ACT.17.PLAIN: Then Paul stood up in the meeting of the Areopagus and said, “Men of Athens, I see that in every way you are very religious.

ACT.17.BSB: For as I walked around and examined your objects of worship, I even found an altar with this inscription: TO AN UNKNOWN GOD. Therefore what you worship as something unknown, I now proclaim to you.
ACT.17.KJV: For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore you ignorantly worship, him declare I to you.
ACT.17.PLAIN: For as I walked around and examined your objects of worship, I even found an altar with this inscription: TO AN UNKNOWN GOD. Therefore what you worship as something unknown, I now proclaim to you.

ACT.17.BSB: The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth and does not live in temples made by human hands.
ACT.17.KJV: God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwells not in temples made with hands;
ACT.17.PLAIN: The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth, and he doesn't live in temples built by human hands.

ACT.17.BSB: Nor is He served by human hands, as if He needed anything, because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else.
ACT.17.KJV: Neither is worshipped with men’s hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he gives to all life, and breath, and all things;
ACT.17.PLAIN: Nor is He served by human hands, as if He needed anything, because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else.

ACT.17.BSB: From one man He made every nation of men, that they should inhabit the whole earth; and He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.
ACT.17.KJV: And has made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and has determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;
ACT.17.PLAIN: From one man He made every nation of men, that they should inhabit the whole earth; and He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.

ACT.17.BSB: God intended that they would seek Him and perhaps reach out for Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.
ACT.17.KJV: That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us:
ACT.17.PLAIN: God did this so people would seek him and perhaps reach out and find him — though he is not far from any one of us.

ACT.17.BSB: ‘For in Him we live and move and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘We are His offspring.’
ACT.17.KJV: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
ACT.17.PLAIN: For in him we live and move and have our being. As some of your own poets have said, 'We are his offspring.'

ACT.17.BSB: Therefore, being offspring of God, we should not think that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by man’s skill and imagination.
ACT.17.KJV: For as much then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like to gold, or silver, or stone, graven by are and man’s device.
ACT.17.PLAIN: Therefore, being offspring of God, we should not think that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by man’s skill and imagination.

ACT.17.BSB: Although God overlooked the ignorance of earlier times, He now commands all people everywhere to repent.
ACT.17.KJV: And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commands all men every where to repent:
ACT.17.PLAIN: Although God overlooked the ignorance of earlier times, He now commands all people everywhere to repent.

ACT.17.BSB: For He has set a day when He will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead.”
ACT.17.KJV: Because he has appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he has ordained; whereof he has given assurance to all men, in that he has raised him from the dead. ¶
ACT.17.PLAIN: For He has set a day when He will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead.”

ACT.17.BSB: When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some began to mock him, but others said, “We want to hear you again on this topic.”
ACT.17.KJV: And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked: and others said, We will hear you again of this matter.
ACT.17.PLAIN: When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some began to mock him, but others said, “We want to hear you again on this topic.”

ACT.17.BSB: At that, Paul left the Areopagus.
ACT.17.KJV: So Paul departed from among them.
ACT.17.PLAIN: At that, Paul left the Areopagus.

ACT.17.BSB: But some joined him and believed, including Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others who were with them.
ACT.17.KJV: However, certain men joined to him, and believed: among the which was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
ACT.17.PLAIN: But some joined him and believed, including Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others who were with them.

ACT.18.BSB: After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.
ACT.18.KJV: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;
ACT.18.PLAIN: After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.

ACT.18.BSB: There he found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to visit them,
ACT.18.KJV: And found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:) and came to them.
ACT.18.PLAIN: There he found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to visit them,

ACT.18.BSB: and he stayed and worked with them because they were tentmakers by trade, just as he was.
ACT.18.KJV: And because he was of the same craft, he stayed with them, and worked: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.
ACT.18.PLAIN: and he stayed and worked with them because they were tentmakers by trade, just as he was.

ACT.18.BSB: Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue, trying to persuade Jews and Greeks alike.
ACT.18.KJV: And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks.
ACT.18.PLAIN: Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue, trying to persuade Jews and Greeks alike.

ACT.18.BSB: And when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself fully to the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
ACT.18.KJV: And when Silas and Timotheus were come from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in the spirit, and testified to the Jews that Jesus was Christ.
ACT.18.PLAIN: And when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself fully to the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.

ACT.18.BSB: But when they opposed and insulted him, he shook out his garments and told them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent of it. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”
ACT.18.KJV: And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook his raiment, and said to them, Your blood be on your own heads; I am clean; from now on I will go to the Gentiles. ¶
ACT.18.PLAIN: But when they opposed and insulted him, he shook out his garments and told them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent of it. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”

ACT.18.BSB: So Paul left the synagogue and went next door to the house of Titus Justus, a worshiper of God.
ACT.18.KJV: And he departed there, and entered into a certain man’s house, named Justus, one that worshipped God, whose house joined hard to the synagogue.
ACT.18.PLAIN: So Paul left the synagogue and went next door to the house of Titus Justus, a worshiper of God.

ACT.18.BSB: Crispus, the synagogue leader, and his whole household believed in the Lord. And many of the Corinthians who heard the message believed and were baptized.
ACT.18.KJV: And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.
ACT.18.PLAIN: Crispus, the synagogue leader, and his whole household believed in the Lord. And many of the Corinthians who heard the message believed and were baptized.

ACT.18.BSB: One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: “Do not be afraid; keep on speaking; do not be silent.
ACT.18.KJV: Then spoke the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not your peace:
ACT.18.PLAIN: One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: 'Don't be afraid; keep speaking, and don't be silent.'

ACT.18.BSB: For I am with you and no one will lay a hand on you, because I have many people in this city.”
ACT.18.KJV: For I am with you, and no man shall set on you to hurt you: for I have much people in this city.
ACT.18.PLAIN: For I am with you, and no one will attack or harm you, because I have many people in this city.

ACT.18.BSB: So Paul stayed for a year and a half, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians.
ACT.18.KJV: And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them. ¶
ACT.18.PLAIN: So Paul stayed for a year and a half, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians.

ACT.18.BSB: While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews coordinated an attack on Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.
ACT.18.KJV: And when Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord against Paul, and brought him to the judgment seat,
ACT.18.PLAIN: While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews coordinated an attack on Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.

ACT.18.BSB: “This man is persuading the people to worship God in ways contrary to the law,” they said.
ACT.18.KJV: Saying, This fellow persuades men to worship God contrary to the law.
ACT.18.PLAIN: “This man is persuading the people to worship God in ways contrary to the law,” they said.

ACT.18.BSB: But just as Paul was about to speak, Gallio told the Jews, “If this matter involved a wrongdoing or vicious crime, O Jews, it would be reasonable for me to hear your complaint.
ACT.18.KJV: And when Paul was now about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, If it were a matter of wrong or wicked lewdness, O you Jews, reason would that I should bear with you:
ACT.18.PLAIN: But just as Paul was about to speak, Gallio told the Jews, “If this matter involved a wrongdoing or vicious crime, O Jews, it would be reasonable for me to hear your complaint.

ACT.18.BSB: But since it is a dispute about words and names and your own law, settle it yourselves. I refuse to be a judge of such things.”
ACT.18.KJV: But if it be a question of words and names, and of your law, look you to it; for I will be no judge of such matters.
ACT.18.PLAIN: But since it is a dispute about words and names and your own law, settle it yourselves. I refuse to be a judge of such things.”

ACT.18.BSB: And he drove them away from the judgment seat.
ACT.18.KJV: And he drove them from the judgment seat.
ACT.18.PLAIN: And he drove them away from the judgment seat.

ACT.18.BSB: At this, the crowd seized Sosthenes the synagogue leader and beat him in front of the judgment seat. But none of this was of concern to Gallio.
ACT.18.KJV: Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things. ¶
ACT.18.PLAIN: At this, the crowd seized Sosthenes the synagogue leader and beat him in front of the judgment seat. But none of this was of concern to Gallio.

ACT.18.BSB: Paul remained in Corinth for quite some time before saying goodbye to the brothers. He had his head shaved in Cenchrea to keep a vow he had made, and then he sailed for Syria, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila.
ACT.18.KJV: And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brothers, and sailed there into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.
ACT.18.PLAIN: Paul remained in Corinth for quite some time before saying goodbye to the brothers. He had his head shaved in Cenchrea to keep a vow he had made, and then he sailed for Syria, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila.

ACT.18.BSB: When they reached Ephesus, Paul parted ways with Priscilla and Aquila. He himself went into the synagogue there and reasoned with the Jews.
ACT.18.KJV: And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.
ACT.18.PLAIN: When they reached Ephesus, Paul parted ways with Priscilla and Aquila. He himself went into the synagogue there and reasoned with the Jews.

ACT.18.BSB: When they asked him to stay for a while longer, he declined.
ACT.18.KJV: When they desired him to tarry longer time with them, he consented not;
ACT.18.PLAIN: When they asked him to stay for a while longer, he declined.

ACT.18.BSB: But as he left, he said, “I will come back to you if God is willing.” And he set sail from Ephesus.
ACT.18.KJV: But bade them farewell, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that comes in Jerusalem: but I will return again to you, if God will. And he sailed from Ephesus.
ACT.18.PLAIN: But as he left, he said, “I will come back to you if God is willing.” And he set sail from Ephesus.

ACT.18.BSB: When Paul had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church at Jerusalem. Then he went down to Antioch.
ACT.18.KJV: And when he had landed at Caesarea, and gone up, and saluted the church, he went down to Antioch.
ACT.18.PLAIN: When Paul had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church at Jerusalem. Then he went down to Antioch.

ACT.18.BSB: After Paul had spent some time in Antioch, he traveled from place to place throughout the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
ACT.18.KJV: And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples. ¶
ACT.18.PLAIN: After Paul had spent some time in Antioch, he traveled from place to place throughout the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.

ACT.18.BSB: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures.
ACT.18.KJV: And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.
ACT.18.PLAIN: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures.

ACT.18.BSB: He had been instructed in the way of the Lord and was fervent in spirit. He spoke and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.
ACT.18.KJV: This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit, he spoke and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.
ACT.18.PLAIN: He had been instructed in the way of the Lord and was fervent in spirit. He spoke and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.

ACT.18.BSB: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him in and explained to him the way of God more accurately.
ACT.18.KJV: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him to them, and expounded to him the way of God more perfectly.
ACT.18.PLAIN: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him in and explained to him the way of God more accurately.

ACT.18.BSB: When Apollos resolved to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him. On his arrival, he was a great help to those who by grace had believed.
ACT.18.KJV: And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brothers wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace:
ACT.18.PLAIN: When Apollos resolved to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him. On his arrival, he was a great help to those who by grace had believed.

ACT.18.BSB: For he powerfully refuted the Jews in public debate, proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.
ACT.18.KJV: For he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publicly, showing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ.
ACT.18.PLAIN: For he powerfully refuted the Jews in public debate, proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.

ACT.19.BSB: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul passed through the interior and came to Ephesus. There he found some disciples
ACT.19.KJV: And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples,
ACT.19.PLAIN: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul passed through the interior and came to Ephesus. There he found some disciples

ACT.19.BSB: and asked them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers?” “No,” they answered, “we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
ACT.19.KJV: He said to them, Have you received the Holy Ghost since you believed? And they said to him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.
ACT.19.PLAIN: and asked them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers?” “No,” they answered, “we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”

ACT.19.BSB: “Into what, then, were you baptized?” Paul asked. “The baptism of John,” they replied.
ACT.19.KJV: And he said to them, To what then were you baptized? And they said, To John’s baptism.
ACT.19.PLAIN: “Into what, then, were you baptized?” Paul asked. “The baptism of John,” they replied.

ACT.19.BSB: Paul explained: “John’s baptism was a baptism of repentance. He told the people to believe in the One coming after him, that is, in Jesus.”
ACT.19.KJV: Then said Paul, John truly baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying to the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.
ACT.19.PLAIN: Paul explained: “John’s baptism was a baptism of repentance. He told the people to believe in the One coming after him, that is, in Jesus.”

ACT.19.BSB: On hearing this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
ACT.19.KJV: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
ACT.19.PLAIN: On hearing this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.

ACT.19.BSB: And when Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.
ACT.19.KJV: And when Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spoke with tongues, and prophesied.
ACT.19.PLAIN: And when Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.

ACT.19.BSB: There were about twelve men in all.
ACT.19.KJV: And all the men were about twelve.
ACT.19.PLAIN: There were about twelve men in all.

ACT.19.BSB: Then Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months, arguing persuasively about the kingdom of God.
ACT.19.KJV: And he went into the synagogue, and spoke boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.
ACT.19.PLAIN: Then Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months, arguing persuasively about the kingdom of God.

ACT.19.BSB: But when some of them stubbornly refused to believe and publicly maligned the Way, Paul took his disciples and left the synagogue to conduct daily discussions in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
ACT.19.KJV: But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spoke evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.
ACT.19.PLAIN: But when some of them stubbornly refused to believe and publicly maligned the Way, Paul took his disciples and left the synagogue to conduct daily discussions in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.

ACT.19.BSB: This continued for two years, so that everyone who lived in the province of Asia, Jews and Greeks alike, heard the word of the Lord.
ACT.19.KJV: And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelled in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
ACT.19.PLAIN: This continued for two years, so that everyone who lived in the province of Asia, Jews and Greeks alike, heard the word of the Lord.

ACT.19.BSB: God did extraordinary miracles through the hands of Paul,
ACT.19.KJV: And God worked special miracles by the hands of Paul:
ACT.19.PLAIN: God did extraordinary miracles through the hands of Paul,

ACT.19.BSB: so that even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were taken to the sick, and the diseases and evil spirits left them.
ACT.19.KJV: So that from his body were brought to the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them. ¶
ACT.19.PLAIN: so that even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were taken to the sick, and the diseases and evil spirits left them.

ACT.19.BSB: Now there were some itinerant Jewish exorcists who tried to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those with evil spirits. They would say, “I bind you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.”
ACT.19.KJV: Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took on them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the LORD Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preaches.
ACT.19.PLAIN: Now there were some itinerant Jewish exorcists who tried to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those with evil spirits. They would say, “I bind you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.”

ACT.19.BSB: Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.
ACT.19.KJV: And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, and chief of the priests, which did so.
ACT.19.PLAIN: Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.

ACT.19.BSB: Eventually, one of the evil spirits answered them, “Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?”
ACT.19.KJV: And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are you?
ACT.19.PLAIN: Eventually, one of the evil spirits answered them, “Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?”

ACT.19.BSB: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them all. The attack was so violent that they ran out of the house naked and wounded.
ACT.19.KJV: And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
ACT.19.PLAIN: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them all. The attack was so violent that they ran out of the house naked and wounded.

ACT.19.BSB: This became known to all the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, and fear came over all of them. So the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honor.
ACT.19.KJV: And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus; and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
ACT.19.PLAIN: This became known to all the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, and fear came over all of them. So the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honor.

ACT.19.BSB: Many who had believed now came forward, confessing and disclosing their deeds.
ACT.19.KJV: And many that believed came, and confessed, and showed their deeds.
ACT.19.PLAIN: Many who had believed now came forward, confessing and disclosing their deeds.

ACT.19.BSB: And a number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books and burned them in front of everyone. When the value of the books was calculated, the total came to fifty thousand drachmas.
ACT.19.KJV: Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men: and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.
ACT.19.PLAIN: And a number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books and burned them in front of everyone. When the value of the books was calculated, the total came to fifty thousand drachmas.

ACT.19.BSB: So the word of the Lord powerfully continued to spread and prevail.
ACT.19.KJV: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed. ¶

ACT.25.KJV: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

ACT.25.BSB: Since I was at a loss as to how to investigate these matters, I asked if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried there on these charges.
ACT.25.KJV: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.
ACT.25.PLAIN: Since I was at a loss as to how to investigate these matters, I asked if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried there on these charges.

ACT.25.BSB: But when Paul appealed to be held over for the decision of the Emperor, I ordered that he be held until I could send him to Caesar.”
ACT.25.KJV: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved to the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar.
ACT.25.PLAIN: But when Paul appealed to be held over for the decision of the Emperor, I ordered that he be held until I could send him to Caesar.”

ACT.25.BSB: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would like to hear this man myself.” “Tomorrow you will hear him,” Festus declared.
ACT.25.KJV: Then Agrippa said to Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, you shall hear him.
ACT.25.PLAIN: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would like to hear this man myself.” “Tomorrow you will hear him,” Festus declared.

ACT.25.BSB: The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the auditorium, along with the commanders and leading men of the city. And Festus ordered that Paul be brought in.
ACT.25.KJV: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus’ commandment Paul was brought forth.
ACT.25.PLAIN: The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the auditorium, along with the commanders and leading men of the city. And Festus ordered that Paul be brought in.

ACT.25.BSB: Then Festus said, “King Agrippa and all who are present with us, you see this man. The whole Jewish community has petitioned me about him, both here and in Jerusalem, crying out that he ought not to live any longer.
ACT.25.KJV: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, you see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
ACT.25.PLAIN: Then Festus said, “King Agrippa and all who are present with us, you see this man. The whole Jewish community has petitioned me about him, both here and in Jerusalem, crying out that he ought not to live any longer.

ACT.25.BSB: But I found he had done nothing worthy of death, and since he has now appealed to the Emperor, I decided to send him.
ACT.25.KJV: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself has appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.
ACT.25.PLAIN: But I found he had done nothing worthy of death, and since he has now appealed to the Emperor, I decided to send him.

ACT.25.BSB: I have nothing definite to write to our sovereign one about him. Therefore I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after this inquiry I may have something to write.
ACT.25.KJV: Of whom I have no certain thing to write to my lord. Why I have brought him forth before you, and specially before you, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.
ACT.25.PLAIN: I have nothing definite to write to our sovereign one about him. Therefore I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after this inquiry I may have something to write.

ACT.25.BSB: For it seems unreasonable to me to send on a prisoner without specifying the charges against him.”
ACT.25.KJV: For it seems to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not with to signify the crimes laid against him.
ACT.25.PLAIN: For it seems unreasonable to me to send on a prisoner without specifying the charges against him.”

ACT.26.BSB: Agrippa said to Paul, “You have permission to speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand and began his defense:
ACT.26.KJV: Then Agrippa said to Paul, You are permitted to speak for yourself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:
ACT.26.PLAIN: Agrippa said to Paul, “You have permission to speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand and began his defense:

ACT.26.BSB: “King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to stand before you today to defend myself against all the accusations of the Jews,
ACT.26.KJV: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before you touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:
ACT.26.PLAIN: “King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to stand before you today to defend myself against all the accusations of the Jews,

ACT.26.BSB: especially since you are acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies. I beg you, therefore, to listen to me patiently.
ACT.26.KJV: Especially because I know you to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: why I beseech you to hear me patiently.
ACT.26.PLAIN: especially since you are acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies. I beg you, therefore, to listen to me patiently.

ACT.26.BSB: Surely all the Jews know how I have lived from the earliest days of my youth, among my own people and in Jerusalem.
ACT.26.KJV: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among my own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;
ACT.26.PLAIN: Surely all the Jews know how I have lived from the earliest days of my youth, among my own people and in Jerusalem.

ACT.26.BSB: They have known me for a long time and can testify, if they are willing, that I lived as a Pharisee, adhering to the strictest sect of our religion.
ACT.26.KJV: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most strait sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
ACT.26.PLAIN: They have known me for a long time and can testify, if they are willing, that I lived as a Pharisee, adhering to the strictest sect of our religion.

ACT.26.BSB: And now I stand on trial because of my hope in the promise that God made to our fathers,
ACT.26.KJV: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God, to our fathers:
ACT.26.PLAIN: And now I stand on trial because of my hope in the promise that God made to our fathers,

ACT.26.BSB: the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to realize as they earnestly serve God day and night. It is because of this hope, O king, that I am accused by the Jews.
ACT.26.KJV: To which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.
ACT.26.PLAIN: the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to realize as they earnestly serve God day and night. It is because of this hope, O king, that I am accused by the Jews.

ACT.26.BSB: Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?
ACT.26.KJV: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?
ACT.26.PLAIN: Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?

ACT.26.BSB: So then, I too was convinced that I ought to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
ACT.26.KJV: I truly thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
ACT.26.PLAIN: So then, I too was convinced that I ought to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

ACT.26.BSB: And that is what I did in Jerusalem. With authority from the chief priests I put many of the saints in prison, and when they were condemned to death, I cast my vote against them.
ACT.26.KJV: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
ACT.26.PLAIN: And that is what I did in Jerusalem. With authority from the chief priests I put many of the saints in prison, and when they were condemned to death, I cast my vote against them.

ACT.26.BSB: I frequently had them punished in the synagogues, and I tried to make them blaspheme. In my raging fury against them, I even went to foreign cities to persecute them.
ACT.26.KJV: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even to strange cities.
ACT.26.PLAIN: I frequently had them punished in the synagogues, and I tried to make them blaspheme. In my raging fury against them, I even went to foreign cities to persecute them.

ACT.26.BSB: In this pursuit I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.
ACT.26.KJV: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
ACT.26.PLAIN: In this pursuit I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.

ACT.26.BSB: About noon, O king, as I was on the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and my companions.
ACT.26.KJV: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.
ACT.26.PLAIN: About noon, O king, as I was on the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and my companions.

ACT.26.BSB: We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice say to me in Hebrew, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
ACT.26.KJV: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking to me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecute you me? it is hard for you to kick against the pricks.
ACT.26.PLAIN: We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice say to me in Hebrew, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’

ACT.26.BSB: ‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked. ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,’ the Lord replied.
ACT.26.KJV: And I said, Who are you, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom you persecute.
ACT.26.PLAIN: ‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked. ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,’ the Lord replied.

ACT.26.BSB: ‘But get up and stand on your feet. For I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness of what you have seen from Me and what I will show you.
ACT.26.KJV: But rise, and stand on your feet: for I have appeared to you for this purpose, to make you a minister and a witness both of these things which you have seen, and of those things in the which I will appear to you;
ACT.26.PLAIN: ‘But get up and stand on your feet. For I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness of what you have seen from Me and what I will show you.

ACT.26.BSB: I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to them
ACT.26.KJV: Delivering you from the people, and from the Gentiles, to whom now I send you,
ACT.26.PLAIN: I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to them

ACT.26.BSB: to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those sanctified by faith in Me.’
ACT.26.KJV: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.
ACT.26.PLAIN: to open their eyes and turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, so they may receive forgiveness of sins and a place among those made holy by faith in me.

ACT.26.BSB: So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.
ACT.26.KJV: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision:
ACT.26.PLAIN: So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.

ACT.26.BSB: First to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, then to everyone in the region of Judea, and then to the Gentiles, I declared that they should repent and turn to God, performing deeds worthy of their repentance.
ACT.26.KJV: But showed first to them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
ACT.26.PLAIN: First to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, then to everyone in the region of Judea, and then to the Gentiles, I declared that they should repent and turn to God, performing deeds worthy of their repentance.

ACT.26.BSB: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me.
ACT.26.KJV: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me.
ACT.26.PLAIN: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me.

ACT.26.BSB: But I have had God’s help to this day, and I stand here to testify to small and great alike. I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen:
ACT.26.KJV: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue to this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:
ACT.26.PLAIN: But I have had God’s help to this day, and I stand here to testify to small and great alike. I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen:

ACT.26.BSB: that the Christ would suffer, and as the first to rise from the dead, would proclaim light to our people and to the Gentiles.”
ACT.26.KJV: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should show light to the people, and to the Gentiles.
ACT.26.PLAIN: that the Christ would suffer, and as the first to rise from the dead, would proclaim light to our people and to the Gentiles.”

ACT.26.BSB: At this stage of Paul’s defense, Festus exclaimed in a loud voice, “You are insane, Paul! Your great learning is driving you to madness!”
ACT.26.KJV: And as he thus spoke for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, you are beside yourself; much learning does make you mad.
ACT.26.PLAIN: At this stage of Paul’s defense, Festus exclaimed in a loud voice, “You are insane, Paul! Your great learning is driving you to madness!”

ACT.26.BSB: But Paul answered, “I am not insane, most excellent Festus; I am speaking words of truth and sobriety.
ACT.26.KJV: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.
ACT.26.PLAIN: But Paul answered, “I am not insane, most excellent Festus; I am speaking words of truth and sobriety.

ACT.26.BSB: For the king knows about these matters, and I can speak freely to him. I am confident that none of this has escaped his notice, because it was not done in a corner.
ACT.26.KJV: For the king knows of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.
ACT.26.PLAIN: For the king knows about these matters, and I can speak freely to him. I am confident that none of this has escaped his notice, because it was not done in a corner.

ACT.26.BSB: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do.”
ACT.26.KJV: King Agrippa, believe you the prophets? I know that you believe.
ACT.26.PLAIN: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do.”

ACT.26.BSB: Then Agrippa said to Paul, “Can you persuade me in such a short time to become a Christian?”
ACT.26.KJV: Then Agrippa said to Paul, Almost you persuade me to be a Christian.
ACT.26.PLAIN: Then Agrippa said to Paul, 'Do you think you can make me a Christian so quickly?'

ACT.26.BSB: “Short time or long,” Paul replied, “I wish to God that not only you but all who hear me this day may become what I am, except for these chains.”
ACT.26.KJV: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only you, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.
ACT.26.PLAIN: Paul replied, 'Whether it takes a short time or long, I pray to God that not only you but everyone listening to me today might become what I am — except for these chains.'

ACT.26.BSB: Then the king and the governor rose, along with Bernice and those seated with them.
ACT.26.KJV: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:
ACT.26.PLAIN: Then the king and the governor rose, along with Bernice and those seated with them.

ACT.26.BSB: On their way out, they said to one another, “This man has done nothing worthy of death or imprisonment.”
ACT.26.KJV: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.
ACT.26.PLAIN: On their way out, they said to one another, “This man has done nothing worthy of death or imprisonment.”

ACT.26.BSB: And Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
ACT.26.KJV: Then said Agrippa to Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed to Caesar.
ACT.26.PLAIN: And Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”

ACT.27.BSB: When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to the Imperial Regiment.
ACT.27.KJV: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band.
ACT.27.PLAIN: When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to the Imperial Regiment.

ACT.27.BSB: We boarded an Adramyttian ship about to sail for ports along the coast of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.
ACT.27.KJV: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
ACT.27.PLAIN: We boarded an Adramyttian ship about to sail for ports along the coast of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.

ACT.27.BSB: The next day we landed at Sidon, and Julius treated Paul with consideration, allowing him to visit his friends and receive their care.
ACT.27.KJV: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go to his friends to refresh himself.
ACT.27.PLAIN: The next day we landed at Sidon, and Julius treated Paul with consideration, allowing him to visit his friends and receive their care.

ACT.27.BSB: After putting out from there, we sailed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us.
ACT.27.KJV: And when we had launched from there, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
ACT.27.PLAIN: After putting out from there, we sailed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us.

ACT.27.BSB: And when we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra in Lycia.
ACT.27.KJV: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
ACT.27.PLAIN: And when we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra in Lycia.

ACT.27.BSB: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.
ACT.27.KJV: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
ACT.27.PLAIN: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.

ACT.27.BSB: After sailing slowly for many days, we arrived off Cnidus. When the wind impeded us, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
ACT.27.KJV: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;
ACT.27.PLAIN: After sailing slowly for many days, we arrived off Cnidus. When the wind impeded us, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

ACT.27.BSB: After we had moved along the coast with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.
ACT.27.KJV: And, hardly passing it, came to a place which is called The fair havens; near to where was the city of Lasea.
ACT.27.PLAIN: After we had moved along the coast with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.

ACT.27.BSB: By now much time had passed, and the voyage had already become dangerous because it was after the Fast. So Paul advised them,
ACT.27.KJV: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,
ACT.27.PLAIN: By now much time had passed, and the voyage had already become dangerous because it was after the Fast. So Paul advised them,

ACT.27.BSB: “Men, I can see that our voyage will be filled with disaster and great loss, not only to ship and cargo, but to our own lives as well.”
