ACT.27.KJV: And said to them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.
ACT.27.PLAIN: “Men, I can see that our voyage will be filled with disaster and great loss, not only to ship and cargo, but to our own lives as well.”

ACT.27.BSB: But contrary to Paul’s advice, the centurion was persuaded by the pilot and by the owner of the ship.
ACT.27.KJV: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.
ACT.27.PLAIN: But contrary to Paul’s advice, the centurion was persuaded by the pilot and by the owner of the ship.

ACT.27.BSB: Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided to sail on, if somehow they could reach Phoenix to winter there. Phoenix was a harbor in Crete facing both southwest and northwest.
ACT.27.KJV: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart there also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lies toward the south west and north west.
ACT.27.PLAIN: Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided to sail on, if somehow they could reach Phoenix to winter there. Phoenix was a harbor in Crete facing both southwest and northwest.

ACT.27.BSB: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had their opportunity. So they weighed anchor and sailed along, hugging the coast of Crete.
ACT.27.KJV: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing there, they sailed close by Crete.
ACT.27.PLAIN: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had their opportunity. So they weighed anchor and sailed along, hugging the coast of Crete.

ACT.27.BSB: But it was not long before a cyclone called the Northeaster swept down across the island.
ACT.27.KJV: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.
ACT.27.PLAIN: But it was not long before a cyclone called the Northeaster swept down across the island.

ACT.27.BSB: Unable to head into the wind, the ship was caught up. So we gave way and let ourselves be driven along.
ACT.27.KJV: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.
ACT.27.PLAIN: Unable to head into the wind, the ship was caught up. So we gave way and let ourselves be driven along.

ACT.27.BSB: Passing to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we barely managed to secure the lifeboat.
ACT.27.KJV: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:
ACT.27.PLAIN: Passing to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we barely managed to secure the lifeboat.

ACT.27.BSB: After hoisting it up, the crew used ropes to undergird the ship. And fearing that they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and were driven along.
ACT.27.KJV: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, under girding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, struck sail, and so were driven.
ACT.27.PLAIN: After hoisting it up, the crew used ropes to undergird the ship. And fearing that they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and were driven along.

ACT.27.BSB: We were tossed so violently that the next day the men began to jettison the cargo.
ACT.27.KJV: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;
ACT.27.PLAIN: We were tossed so violently that the next day the men began to jettison the cargo.

ACT.27.BSB: On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.
ACT.27.KJV: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.
ACT.27.PLAIN: On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.

ACT.27.BSB: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the great storm continued to batter us, we abandoned all hope of being saved.
ACT.27.KJV: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
ACT.27.PLAIN: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the great storm continued to batter us, we abandoned all hope of being saved.

ACT.27.BSB: After the men had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have followed my advice not to sail from Crete. Then you would have averted this disaster and loss.
ACT.27.KJV: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the middle of them, and said, Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.
ACT.27.PLAIN: After the men had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have followed my advice not to sail from Crete. Then you would have averted this disaster and loss.

ACT.27.BSB: But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because you will not experience any loss of life, but only of the ship.
ACT.27.KJV: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship.
ACT.27.PLAIN: But now I urge you to take courage, because not one of you will lose your life; only the ship will be lost.

ACT.27.BSB: For just last night an angel of God, whose I am and whom I serve, stood beside me
ACT.27.KJV: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,
ACT.27.PLAIN: For just last night an angel of God, whose I am and whom I serve, stood beside me

ACT.27.BSB: and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And look, God has granted you the lives of all who sail with you.’
ACT.27.KJV: Saying, Fear not, Paul; you must be brought before Caesar: and, see, God has given you all them that sail with you.
ACT.27.PLAIN: and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And look, God has granted you the lives of all who sail with you.’

ACT.27.BSB: So take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as He told me.
ACT.27.KJV: Why, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.
ACT.27.PLAIN: So take heart, men, for I trust God that it will happen just as he told me.

ACT.27.BSB: However, we must run aground on some island.”
ACT.27.KJV: However, we must be cast on a certain island.
ACT.27.PLAIN: However, we must run aground on some island.”

ACT.27.BSB: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.
ACT.27.KJV: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;
ACT.27.PLAIN: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.

ACT.27.BSB: They took soundings and found that the water was twenty fathoms deep. Going a little farther, they took another set of soundings that read fifteen fathoms.
ACT.27.KJV: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.
ACT.27.PLAIN: They took soundings and found that the water was twenty fathoms deep. Going a little farther, they took another set of soundings that read fifteen fathoms.

ACT.27.BSB: Fearing that we would run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daybreak.
ACT.27.KJV: Then fearing lest we should have fallen on rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.
ACT.27.PLAIN: Fearing that we would run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daybreak.

ACT.27.BSB: Meanwhile, the sailors attempted to escape from the ship. Pretending to lower anchors from the bow, they let the lifeboat down into the sea.
ACT.27.KJV: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under color as though they would have cast anchors out of the bow,
ACT.27.PLAIN: Meanwhile, the sailors attempted to escape from the ship. Pretending to lower anchors from the bow, they let the lifeboat down into the sea.

ACT.27.BSB: But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain with the ship, you cannot be saved.”
ACT.27.KJV: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, you cannot be saved.
ACT.27.PLAIN: But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain with the ship, you cannot be saved.”

ACT.27.BSB: So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and set it adrift.
ACT.27.KJV: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.
ACT.27.PLAIN: So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and set it adrift.

ACT.27.BSB: Right up to daybreak, Paul kept urging them all to eat: “Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense, without taking any food.
ACT.27.KJV: And while the day was coming on, Paul sought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that you have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.
ACT.27.PLAIN: Right up to daybreak, Paul kept urging them all to eat: “Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense, without taking any food.

ACT.27.BSB: So for your own preservation, I urge you to eat something, because not a single hair of your head will be lost.”
ACT.27.KJV: Why I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.
ACT.27.PLAIN: So for your own preservation, I urge you to eat something, because not a single hair of your head will be lost.”

ACT.27.BSB: After he had said this, Paul took bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.
ACT.27.KJV: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.
ACT.27.PLAIN: After he had said this, Paul took bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.

ACT.27.BSB: They were all encouraged and took some food themselves.
ACT.27.KJV: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.
ACT.27.PLAIN: They were all encouraged and took some food themselves.

ACT.27.BSB: In all, there were 276 of us on board.
ACT.27.KJV: And we were in all in the ship two hundred three score and sixteen souls.
ACT.27.PLAIN: In all, there were 276 of us on board.

ACT.27.BSB: After the men had eaten their fill, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.
ACT.27.KJV: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.
ACT.27.PLAIN: After the men had eaten their fill, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.

ACT.27.BSB: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.
ACT.27.KJV: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.
ACT.27.PLAIN: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.

ACT.27.BSB: Cutting away the anchors, they left them in the sea as they loosened the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.
ACT.27.KJV: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves to the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoisted up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.
ACT.27.PLAIN: Cutting away the anchors, they left them in the sea as they loosened the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.

ACT.27.BSB: But the vessel struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves.
ACT.27.KJV: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmovable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.
ACT.27.PLAIN: But the vessel struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves.

ACT.27.BSB: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom.
ACT.27.KJV: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.
ACT.27.PLAIN: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom.

ACT.27.BSB: But the centurion, wanting to spare Paul’s life, thwarted their plan. He commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.
ACT.27.KJV: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:
ACT.27.PLAIN: But the centurion, wanting to spare Paul’s life, thwarted their plan. He commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.

ACT.27.BSB: The rest were to follow on planks and various parts of the ship. In this way everyone was brought safely to land.
ACT.27.KJV: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.
ACT.27.PLAIN: The rest were to follow on planks and various parts of the ship. In this way everyone was brought safely to land.

ACT.28.BSB: Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
ACT.28.KJV: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.
ACT.28.PLAIN: Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.

ACT.28.BSB: The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.
ACT.28.KJV: And the barbarous people showed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
ACT.28.PLAIN: The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.

ACT.28.BSB: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks, and as he laid them on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.
ACT.28.KJV: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
ACT.28.PLAIN: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks, and as he laid them on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.

ACT.28.BSB: When the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “Surely this man is a murderer. Although he was saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”
ACT.28.KJV: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffers not to live.
ACT.28.PLAIN: When the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “Surely this man is a murderer. Although he was saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”

ACT.28.BSB: But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.
ACT.28.KJV: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.
ACT.28.PLAIN: But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.

ACT.28.BSB: The islanders were expecting him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.
ACT.28.KJV: However, they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.
ACT.28.PLAIN: The islanders were expecting him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.

ACT.28.BSB: Nearby stood an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.
ACT.28.KJV: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.
ACT.28.PLAIN: Nearby stood an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.

ACT.28.BSB: The father of Publius was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after praying and placing his hands on him, he healed the man.
ACT.28.KJV: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.
ACT.28.PLAIN: The father of Publius was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after praying and placing his hands on him, he healed the man.

ACT.28.BSB: After this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well.
ACT.28.KJV: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:
ACT.28.PLAIN: After this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well.

ACT.28.BSB: The islanders honored us in many ways and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail.
ACT.28.KJV: Who also honored us with many honors; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.
ACT.28.PLAIN: The islanders honored us in many ways and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail.

ACT.28.BSB: After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island. It had the Twin Brothers as a figurehead.
ACT.28.KJV: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.
ACT.28.PLAIN: After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island. It had the Twin Brothers as a figurehead.

ACT.28.BSB: Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
ACT.28.KJV: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.
ACT.28.PLAIN: Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

ACT.28.BSB: From there we weighed anchor and came to Rhegium. After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli.
ACT.28.KJV: And from there we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:
ACT.28.PLAIN: From there we weighed anchor and came to Rhegium. After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli.

ACT.28.BSB: There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week with them. And so we came to Rome.
ACT.28.KJV: Where we found brothers, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.
ACT.28.PLAIN: There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week with them. And so we came to Rome.

ACT.28.BSB: The brothers there had heard about us and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.
ACT.28.KJV: And from there, when the brothers heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.
ACT.28.PLAIN: The brothers there had heard about us and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.

ACT.28.BSB: When we arrived in Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him.
ACT.28.KJV: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.
ACT.28.PLAIN: When we arrived in Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him.

ACT.28.BSB: After three days, he called together the leaders of the Jews. When they had gathered, he said to them, “Brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was taken prisoner in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.
ACT.28.KJV: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said to them, Men and brothers, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.
ACT.28.PLAIN: After three days, he called together the leaders of the Jews. When they had gathered, he said to them, “Brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was taken prisoner in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.

ACT.28.BSB: They examined me and wanted to release me, because there was no basis for a death sentence against me.
ACT.28.KJV: Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.
ACT.28.PLAIN: They examined me and wanted to release me, because there was no basis for a death sentence against me.

ACT.28.BSB: But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, even though I have no charge to bring against my nation.
ACT.28.KJV: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar; not that I had something to accuse my nation of.
ACT.28.PLAIN: But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, even though I have no charge to bring against my nation.

ACT.28.BSB: So for this reason I have called to see you and speak with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain.”
ACT.28.KJV: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you, and to speak with you: because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.
ACT.28.PLAIN: So for this reason I have called to see you and speak with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain.”

ACT.28.BSB: The leaders replied, “We have not received any letters about you from Judea, nor have any of the brothers from there reported or even mentioned anything bad about you.
ACT.28.KJV: And they said to him, We neither received letters out of Judaea concerning you, neither any of the brothers that came showed or spoke any harm of you.
ACT.28.PLAIN: The leaders replied, “We have not received any letters about you from Judea, nor have any of the brothers from there reported or even mentioned anything bad about you.

ACT.28.BSB: But we consider your views worth hearing, because we know that people everywhere are speaking against this sect.”
ACT.28.KJV: But we desire to hear of you what you think: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.
ACT.28.PLAIN: But we consider your views worth hearing, because we know that people everywhere are speaking against this sect.”

ACT.28.BSB: So they set a day to meet with Paul, and many people came to the place he was staying. He expounded to them from morning to evening, testifying about the kingdom of God and persuading them about Jesus from the Law of Moses and the Prophets.
ACT.28.KJV: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.
ACT.28.PLAIN: So they set a day to meet with Paul, and many people came to the place he was staying. He expounded to them from morning to evening, testifying about the kingdom of God and persuading them about Jesus from the Law of Moses and the Prophets.

ACT.28.BSB: Some of them were convinced by what he said, but others refused to believe.
ACT.28.KJV: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.
ACT.28.PLAIN: Some of them were convinced by what he said, but others refused to believe.

ACT.28.BSB: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: “The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet:
ACT.28.KJV: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spoke the Holy Ghost by Isaiah the prophet to our fathers,
ACT.28.PLAIN: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: “The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet:

ACT.28.BSB: ‘Go to this people and say, “You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.”
ACT.28.KJV: Saying, Go to this people, and say, Hearing you shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing you shall see, and not perceive:
ACT.28.PLAIN: ‘Go to this people and say, “You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.”

ACT.28.BSB: For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.’
ACT.28.KJV: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.
ACT.28.PLAIN: For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.’

ACT.28.BSB: Be advised, therefore, that God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!”
ACT.28.KJV: Be it known therefore to you, that the salvation of God is sent to the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.
ACT.28.PLAIN: So let it be known to you that God's salvation has been sent to the nations, and they will listen.

ACT.28.KJV: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.

ACT.28.BSB: Paul stayed there two full years in his own rented house, welcoming all who came to visit him.
ACT.28.KJV: And Paul dwelled two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in to him,
ACT.28.PLAIN: Paul stayed there two full years in his own rented house, welcoming all who came to visit him.

ACT.28.BSB: Boldly and freely he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.
ACT.28.KJV: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
ACT.28.PLAIN: boldly proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ — and no one stopped him.

ROM.1.BSB: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, and set apart for the gospel of God—
ROM.1.KJV: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated to the gospel of God,
ROM.1.PLAIN: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, and set apart for the gospel of God—

ROM.1.BSB: the gospel He promised beforehand through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures,
ROM.1.KJV: (Which he had promised before by his prophets in the holy scriptures,)
ROM.1.PLAIN: the gospel He promised beforehand through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures,

ROM.1.BSB: regarding His Son, who was a descendant of David according to the flesh,
ROM.1.KJV: Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;
ROM.1.PLAIN: regarding His Son, who was a descendant of David according to the flesh,

ROM.1.BSB: and who through the Spirit of holiness was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.
ROM.1.KJV: And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:
ROM.1.PLAIN: and who through the Spirit of holiness was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.

ROM.1.BSB: Through Him and on behalf of His name, we received grace and apostleship to call all those among the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith.
ROM.1.KJV: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name:
ROM.1.PLAIN: Through Him and on behalf of His name, we received grace and apostleship to call all those among the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith.

ROM.1.BSB: And you also are among those who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.
ROM.1.KJV: Among whom are you also the called of Jesus Christ:
ROM.1.PLAIN: And you also are among those who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.

ROM.1.BSB: To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be saints: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
ROM.1.KJV: To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
ROM.1.PLAIN: To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be saints: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

ROM.1.BSB: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed all over the world.
ROM.1.KJV: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.
ROM.1.PLAIN: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed all over the world.

ROM.1.BSB: God, whom I serve with my spirit in preaching the gospel of His Son, is my witness how constantly I remember you
ROM.1.KJV: For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, that without ceasing I make mention of you always in my prayers;
ROM.1.PLAIN: God, whom I serve with my spirit in preaching the gospel of His Son, is my witness how constantly I remember you

ROM.1.BSB: in my prayers at all times, asking that now at last by God’s will I may succeed in coming to you.
ROM.1.KJV: Making request, if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come to you.
ROM.1.PLAIN: in my prayers at all times, asking that now at last by God’s will I may succeed in coming to you.

ROM.1.BSB: For I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to strengthen you,
ROM.1.KJV: For I long to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift, to the end you may be established;
ROM.1.PLAIN: For I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to strengthen you,

ROM.1.BSB: that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other’s faith.
ROM.1.KJV: That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.
ROM.1.PLAIN: that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other’s faith.

ROM.1.BSB: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, how often I planned to come to you (but have been prevented from visiting until now), in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.
ROM.1.KJV: Now I would not have you ignorant, brothers, that oftentimes I purposed to come to you, (but was let till now,) that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles.
ROM.1.PLAIN: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, how often I planned to come to you (but have been prevented from visiting until now), in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.

ROM.1.BSB: I am obligated both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish.
ROM.1.KJV: I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians; both to the wise, and to the unwise.
ROM.1.PLAIN: I am obligated both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish.

ROM.1.BSB: That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.
ROM.1.KJV: So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also.
ROM.1.PLAIN: That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.

ROM.1.BSB: I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, first to the Jew, then to the Greek.
ROM.1.KJV: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God to salvation to every one that believes; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
ROM.1.PLAIN: I'm not ashamed of the good news about Christ, because it's the power of God that brings salvation to everyone who believes — to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

ROM.1.BSB: For the gospel reveals the righteousness of God that comes by faith from start to finish, just as it is written: “The righteous will live by faith.”
ROM.1.KJV: For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.
ROM.1.PLAIN: In it, God's way of making us right is revealed — a righteousness that is by faith from start to finish, as it's written: 'The just will live by faith.'

ROM.1.BSB: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness.
ROM.1.KJV: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness;
ROM.1.PLAIN: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness.

ROM.1.BSB: For what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.
ROM.1.KJV: Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God has showed it to them.
ROM.1.PLAIN: For what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.

ROM.1.BSB: For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood from His workmanship, so that men are without excuse.
ROM.1.KJV: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:
ROM.1.PLAIN: Ever since the world was created, God's invisible qualities — his eternal power and divine nature — have been clearly seen in the things he made, so no one has an excuse.

ROM.1.BSB: For although they knew God, they neither glorified Him as God nor gave thanks to Him, but they became futile in their thinking and darkened in their foolish hearts.
ROM.1.KJV: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.
ROM.1.PLAIN: For although they knew God, they neither glorified Him as God nor gave thanks to Him, but they became futile in their thinking and darkened in their foolish hearts.

ROM.1.BSB: Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools,
ROM.1.KJV: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,
ROM.1.PLAIN: Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools,

ROM.1.BSB: and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles.
ROM.1.KJV: And changed the glory of the incorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and four footed beasts, and creeping things.
ROM.1.PLAIN: and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles.

ROM.1.BSB: Therefore God gave them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity for the dishonoring of their bodies with one another.
ROM.1.KJV: Why God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonor their own bodies between themselves:
ROM.1.PLAIN: Therefore God gave them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity for the dishonoring of their bodies with one another.

ROM.1.BSB: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is forever worthy of praise! Amen.
ROM.1.KJV: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.
ROM.1.PLAIN: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is forever worthy of praise! Amen.

ROM.1.BSB: For this reason God gave them over to dishonorable passions. Even their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.
ROM.1.KJV: For this cause God gave them up to vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature:
ROM.1.PLAIN: For this reason God gave them over to dishonorable passions. Even their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.

ROM.1.BSB: Likewise, the men abandoned natural relations with women and burned with lust for one another. Men committed indecent acts with other men, and received in themselves the due penalty for their error.
ROM.1.KJV: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompense of their error which was meet.
ROM.1.PLAIN: Likewise, the men abandoned natural relations with women and burned with lust for one another. Men committed indecent acts with other men, and received in themselves the due penalty for their error.

ROM.1.BSB: Furthermore, since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, He gave them up to a depraved mind, to do what ought not to be done.
ROM.1.KJV: And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient;
ROM.1.PLAIN: Furthermore, since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, He gave them up to a depraved mind, to do what ought not to be done.

ROM.1.BSB: They have become filled with every kind of wickedness, evil, greed, and depravity. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, and malice. They are gossips,
ROM.1.KJV: Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers,
ROM.1.PLAIN: They have become filled with every kind of wickedness, evil, greed, and depravity. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, and malice. They are gossips,

ROM.1.BSB: slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, and boastful. They invent new forms of evil; they disobey their parents.
ROM.1.KJV: Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,
ROM.1.PLAIN: slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, and boastful. They invent new forms of evil; they disobey their parents.

ROM.1.BSB: They are senseless, faithless, heartless, merciless.
ROM.1.KJV: Without understanding, covenant breakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful:
ROM.1.PLAIN: They are senseless, faithless, heartless, merciless.

ROM.1.BSB: Although they know God’s righteous decree that those who do such things are worthy of death, they not only continue to do these things, but also approve of those who practice them.
ROM.1.KJV: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.
ROM.1.PLAIN: Although they know God’s righteous decree that those who do such things are worthy of death, they not only continue to do these things, but also approve of those who practice them.

ROM.2.BSB: You, therefore, have no excuse, you who pass judgment on another. For on whatever grounds you judge the other, you are condemning yourself, because you who pass judgment do the same things.
ROM.2.KJV: Therefore you are inexcusable, O man, whoever you are that judge: for wherein you judge another, you condemn yourself; for you that judge do the same things.
ROM.2.PLAIN: You, therefore, have no excuse, you who pass judgment on another. For on whatever grounds you judge the other, you are condemning yourself, because you who pass judgment do the same things.

ROM.2.BSB: And we know that God’s judgment against those who do such things is based on truth.
ROM.2.KJV: But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things.
ROM.2.PLAIN: And we know that God’s judgment against those who do such things is based on truth.

ROM.2.BSB: So when you, O man, pass judgment on others, yet do the same things, do you think you will escape God’s judgment?
ROM.2.KJV: And think you this, O man, that judge them which do such things, and do the same, that you shall escape the judgment of God?
ROM.2.PLAIN: So when you, O man, pass judgment on others, yet do the same things, do you think you will escape God’s judgment?

ROM.2.BSB: Or do you disregard the riches of His kindness, tolerance, and patience, not realizing that God’s kindness leads you to repentance?
ROM.2.KJV: Or despise you the riches of his goodness and forbearance and long-suffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?
ROM.2.PLAIN: Or do you take his rich kindness, patience, and restraint for granted, not realizing that God's kindness is meant to lead you to change your heart?

ROM.2.BSB: But because of your hard and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath against yourself for the day of wrath, when God’s righteous judgment will be revealed.
ROM.2.KJV: But after your hardness and impenitent heart treasure up to yourself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God;
ROM.2.PLAIN: But because of your hard and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath against yourself for the day of wrath, when God’s righteous judgment will be revealed.

ROM.2.BSB: God “will repay each one according to his deeds.”
ROM.2.KJV: Who will render to every man according to his deeds:
ROM.2.PLAIN: God “will repay each one according to his deeds.”

ROM.2.BSB: To those who by perseverance in doing good seek glory, honor, and immortality, He will give eternal life.
ROM.2.KJV: To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honor and immortality, eternal life:
ROM.2.PLAIN: To those who by perseverance in doing good seek glory, honor, and immortality, He will give eternal life.

ROM.2.BSB: But for those who are self-seeking and who reject the truth and follow wickedness, there will be wrath and anger.
ROM.2.KJV: But to them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath,
ROM.2.PLAIN: But for those who are self-seeking and who reject the truth and follow wickedness, there will be wrath and anger.

ROM.2.BSB: There will be trouble and distress for every human being who does evil, first for the Jew, then for the Greek;
ROM.2.KJV: Tribulation and anguish, on every soul of man that does evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile;
ROM.2.PLAIN: There will be trouble and distress for every human being who does evil, first for the Jew, then for the Greek;

ROM.2.BSB: but glory, honor, and peace for everyone who does good, first for the Jew, then for the Greek.
ROM.2.KJV: But glory, honor, and peace, to every man that works good, to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile:
ROM.2.PLAIN: but glory, honor, and peace for everyone who does good, first for the Jew, then for the Greek.

ROM.2.BSB: For God does not show favoritism.
ROM.2.KJV: For there is no respect of persons with God.
ROM.2.PLAIN: For God shows no favoritism.

ROM.2.BSB: All who sin apart from the law will also perish apart from the law, and all who sin under the law will be judged by the law.
ROM.2.KJV: For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law;
ROM.2.PLAIN: All who sin apart from the law will also perish apart from the law, and all who sin under the law will be judged by the law.

ROM.2.BSB: For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but it is the doers of the law who will be declared righteous.
ROM.2.KJV: (For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.
ROM.2.PLAIN: For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but it is the doers of the law who will be declared righteous.

ROM.2.BSB: Indeed, when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature what the law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the law.
ROM.2.KJV: For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law to themselves:
ROM.2.PLAIN: Indeed, when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature what the law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the law.

ROM.2.BSB: So they show that the work of the law is written on their hearts, their consciences also bearing witness, and their thoughts either accusing or defending them
ROM.2.KJV: Which show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;)
ROM.2.PLAIN: So they show that the work of the law is written on their hearts, their consciences also bearing witness, and their thoughts either accusing or defending them

ROM.2.BSB: on the day when God will judge men’s secrets through Christ Jesus, as proclaimed by my gospel.
ROM.2.KJV: In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel.
ROM.2.PLAIN: on the day when God will judge men’s secrets through Christ Jesus, as proclaimed by my gospel.

ROM.2.BSB: Now you, if you call yourself a Jew; if you rely on the law and boast in God;
ROM.2.KJV: Behold, you are called a Jew, and rest in the law, and make your boast of God,
ROM.2.PLAIN: Now you, if you call yourself a Jew; if you rely on the law and boast in God;

ROM.2.BSB: if you know His will and approve of what is superior because you are instructed by the law;
ROM.2.KJV: And know his will, and approve the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law;
ROM.2.PLAIN: if you know His will and approve of what is superior because you are instructed by the law;

ROM.2.BSB: if you are convinced that you are a guide for the blind, a light for those in darkness,
ROM.2.KJV: And are confident that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light of them which are in darkness,
ROM.2.PLAIN: if you are convinced that you are a guide for the blind, a light for those in darkness,

ROM.2.BSB: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, because you have in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth—
ROM.2.KJV: An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, which have the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law.
ROM.2.PLAIN: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, because you have in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth—

ROM.2.BSB: you, then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?
ROM.2.KJV: You therefore which teach another, teach you not yourself? you that preach a man should not steal, do you steal?
ROM.2.PLAIN: you, then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?

ROM.2.BSB: You who forbid adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
ROM.2.KJV: You that say a man should not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? you that abhor idols, do you commit sacrilege?
ROM.2.PLAIN: You who forbid adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?

ROM.2.BSB: You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?
ROM.2.KJV: You that make your boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonor you God?
ROM.2.PLAIN: You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?

ROM.2.BSB: As it is written: “God’s name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.”
ROM.2.KJV: For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written.
ROM.2.PLAIN: As it is written: “God’s name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.”

ROM.2.BSB: Circumcision has value if you observe the law, but if you break the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
ROM.2.KJV: For circumcision truly profits, if you keep the law: but if you be a breaker of the law, your circumcision is made uncircumcision.
ROM.2.PLAIN: Circumcision has value if you observe the law, but if you break the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.

ROM.2.BSB: If a man who is not circumcised keeps the requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision?
ROM.2.KJV: Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?
ROM.2.PLAIN: If a man who is not circumcised keeps the requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision?

ROM.2.BSB: The one who is physically uncircumcised yet keeps the law will condemn you who, even though you have the written code and circumcision, are a lawbreaker.
ROM.2.KJV: And shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfill the law, judge you, who by the letter and circumcision do transgress the law?
ROM.2.PLAIN: The one who is physically uncircumcised yet keeps the law will condemn you who, even though you have the written code and circumcision, are a lawbreaker.

ROM.2.BSB: A man is not a Jew because he is one outwardly, nor is circumcision only outward and physical.
ROM.2.KJV: For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh:
ROM.2.PLAIN: A man is not a Jew because he is one outwardly, nor is circumcision only outward and physical.

ROM.2.BSB: No, a man is a Jew because he is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code. Such a man’s praise does not come from men, but from God.
ROM.2.KJV: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.
ROM.2.PLAIN: No, a man is a Jew because he is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code. Such a man’s praise does not come from men, but from God.

ROM.3.BSB: What, then, is the advantage of being a Jew? Or what is the value of circumcision?
ROM.3.KJV: What advantage then has the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision?
ROM.3.PLAIN: What, then, is the advantage of being a Jew? Or what is the value of circumcision?

ROM.3.BSB: Much in every way. First of all, they have been entrusted with the very words of God.
ROM.3.KJV: Much every way: chiefly, because that to them were committed the oracles of God.
ROM.3.PLAIN: Much in every way. First of all, they have been entrusted with the very words of God.

ROM.3.BSB: What if some did not have faith? Will their lack of faith nullify God’s faithfulness?
ROM.3.KJV: For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect?
ROM.3.PLAIN: What if some did not have faith? Will their lack of faith nullify God’s faithfulness?

ROM.3.BSB: Certainly not! Let God be true and every man a liar. As it is written: “So that You may be proved right when You speak and victorious when You judge.”
ROM.3.KJV: God forbid: yes, let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That you might be justified in your sayings, and might overcome when you are judged.
ROM.3.PLAIN: Certainly not! Let God be true and every man a liar. As it is written: “So that You may be proved right when You speak and victorious when You judge.”

ROM.3.BSB: But if our unrighteousness highlights the righteousness of God, what shall we say? That God is unjust to inflict His wrath on us? I am speaking in human terms.
ROM.3.KJV: But if our unrighteousness commend the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous who takes vengeance? (I speak as a man)
ROM.3.PLAIN: But if our unrighteousness highlights the righteousness of God, what shall we say? That God is unjust to inflict His wrath on us? I am speaking in human terms.

ROM.3.BSB: Certainly not! In that case, how could God judge the world?
ROM.3.KJV: God forbid: for then how shall God judge the world?
ROM.3.PLAIN: Certainly not! In that case, how could God judge the world?

ROM.3.BSB: However, if my falsehood accentuates God’s truthfulness, to the increase of His glory, why am I still condemned as a sinner?
ROM.3.KJV: For if the truth of God has more abounded through my lie to his glory; why yet am I also judged as a sinner?
ROM.3.PLAIN: However, if my falsehood accentuates God’s truthfulness, to the increase of His glory, why am I still condemned as a sinner?

ROM.3.BSB: Why not say, as some slanderously claim that we say, “Let us do evil that good may result”? Their condemnation is deserved!
ROM.3.KJV: And not rather, (as we be slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say,) Let us do evil, that good may come? whose damnation is just.
ROM.3.PLAIN: Why not say, as some slanderously claim that we say, “Let us do evil that good may result”? Their condemnation is deserved!

ROM.3.BSB: What then? Are we any better? Not at all. For we have already made the charge that Jews and Greeks alike are all under sin.
ROM.3.KJV: What then? are we better than they? No, in no wise: for we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin;
ROM.3.PLAIN: What then? Are we any better? Not at all. For we have already made the charge that Jews and Greeks alike are all under sin.

ROM.3.BSB: As it is written: “There is no one righteous, not even one.
ROM.3.KJV: As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one:
ROM.3.PLAIN: As it is written: “There is no one righteous, not even one.

ROM.3.BSB: There is no one who understands, no one who seeks God.
ROM.3.KJV: There is none that understands, there is none that seeks after God.
ROM.3.PLAIN: There is no one who understands, no one who seeks God.

ROM.3.BSB: All have turned away, they have together become worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one.”
ROM.3.KJV: They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that does good, no, not one.
ROM.3.PLAIN: All have turned away, they have together become worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one.”

ROM.3.BSB: “Their throats are open graves; their tongues practice deceit.” “The venom of vipers is on their lips.”
ROM.3.KJV: Their throat is an open sepulcher; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips:
ROM.3.PLAIN: “Their throats are open graves; their tongues practice deceit.” “The venom of vipers is on their lips.”

ROM.3.BSB: “Their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness.”
ROM.3.KJV: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness:
ROM.3.PLAIN: “Their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness.”

ROM.3.BSB: “Their feet are swift to shed blood;
ROM.3.KJV: Their feet are swift to shed blood:
ROM.3.PLAIN: “Their feet are swift to shed blood;

ROM.3.BSB: ruin and misery lie in their wake,
ROM.3.KJV: Destruction and misery are in their ways:
ROM.3.PLAIN: ruin and misery lie in their wake,

ROM.3.BSB: and the way of peace they have not known.”
ROM.3.KJV: And the way of peace have they not known:
ROM.3.PLAIN: and the way of peace they have not known.”

ROM.3.BSB: “There is no fear of God before their eyes.”
ROM.3.KJV: There is no fear of God before their eyes.
ROM.3.PLAIN: “There is no fear of God before their eyes.”

ROM.3.BSB: Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.
ROM.3.KJV: Now we know that what things soever the law said, it says to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God.
ROM.3.PLAIN: Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.

ROM.3.BSB: Therefore no one will be justified in His sight by works of the law. For the law merely brings awareness of sin.
ROM.3.KJV: Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.
ROM.3.PLAIN: Therefore no one will be justified in His sight by works of the law. For the law merely brings awareness of sin.

ROM.3.BSB: But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been revealed, as attested by the Law and the Prophets.
ROM.3.KJV: But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets;
ROM.3.PLAIN: But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been revealed, as attested by the Law and the Prophets.

ROM.3.BSB: And this righteousness from God comes through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe. There is no distinction,
ROM.3.KJV: Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ to all and on all them that believe: for there is no difference:
ROM.3.PLAIN: And this righteousness from God comes through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe. There is no distinction,

ROM.3.BSB: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
ROM.3.KJV: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;
ROM.3.PLAIN: For everyone has sinned and falls short of the glory of God.

ROM.3.BSB: and are justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.
ROM.3.KJV: Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:
ROM.3.PLAIN: and we are made right freely by his grace, through the redemption that came by Christ Jesus.

ROM.3.BSB: God presented Him as the atoning sacrifice through faith in His blood, in order to demonstrate His righteousness, because in His forbearance He had passed over the sins committed beforehand.
ROM.3.KJV: Whom God has set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God;
ROM.3.PLAIN: God presented Him as the atoning sacrifice through faith in His blood, in order to demonstrate His righteousness, because in His forbearance He had passed over the sins committed beforehand.

ROM.3.BSB: He did this to demonstrate His righteousness at the present time, so as to be just and to justify the one who has faith in Jesus.
ROM.3.KJV: To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believes in Jesus.
ROM.3.PLAIN: He did this to demonstrate His righteousness at the present time, so as to be just and to justify the one who has faith in Jesus.

ROM.3.BSB: Where, then, is boasting? It is excluded. On what principle? On that of works? No, but on that of faith.
ROM.3.KJV: Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? No: but by the law of faith.
ROM.3.PLAIN: Where, then, is boasting? It is excluded. On what principle? On that of works? No, but on that of faith.

ROM.3.BSB: For we maintain that a man is justified by faith apart from works of the law.
ROM.3.KJV: Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.
ROM.3.PLAIN: So we conclude that a person is made right with God by faith, apart from keeping the law.

ROM.3.BSB: Is God the God of Jews only? Is He not the God of Gentiles too? Yes, of Gentiles too,
ROM.3.KJV: Is he the God of the Jews only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also:
ROM.3.PLAIN: Is God the God of Jews only? Is He not the God of Gentiles too? Yes, of Gentiles too,

ROM.3.BSB: since there is only one God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that same faith.
ROM.3.KJV: Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.
ROM.3.PLAIN: since there is only one God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that same faith.

ROM.3.BSB: Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith? Certainly not! Instead, we uphold the law.
ROM.3.KJV: Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yes, we establish the law.
ROM.3.PLAIN: Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith? Certainly not! Instead, we uphold the law.

ROM.4.BSB: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather, has discovered?
ROM.4.KJV: What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, has found?
ROM.4.PLAIN: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather, has discovered?

ROM.4.BSB: If Abraham was indeed justified by works, he had something to boast about, but not before God.
ROM.4.KJV: For if Abraham were justified by works, he has whereof to glory; but not before God.
ROM.4.PLAIN: If Abraham was indeed justified by works, he had something to boast about, but not before God.

ROM.4.BSB: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”
ROM.4.KJV: For what says the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness.
ROM.4.PLAIN: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”

ROM.4.BSB: Now the wages of the worker are not credited as a gift, but as an obligation.
ROM.4.KJV: Now to him that works is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.
ROM.4.PLAIN: Now the wages of the worker are not credited as a gift, but as an obligation.

ROM.4.BSB: However, to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the wicked, his faith is credited as righteousness.
ROM.4.KJV: But to him that works not, but believes on him that justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.
ROM.4.PLAIN: But to the person who doesn't rely on works, but simply trusts the God who makes the ungodly right, their faith is counted as righteousness.

ROM.4.BSB: And David speaks likewise of the blessedness of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:
ROM.4.KJV: Even as David also describes the blessedness of the man, to whom God imputes righteousness without works,
ROM.4.PLAIN: And David speaks likewise of the blessedness of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:

ROM.4.BSB: “Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered.
ROM.4.KJV: Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.
ROM.4.PLAIN: “Held in quiet grace are they whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered.

ROM.4.BSB: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him.”
ROM.4.KJV: Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.
ROM.4.PLAIN: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him.”

ROM.4.BSB: Is this blessing only on the circumcised, or also on the uncircumcised? We have been saying that Abraham’s faith was credited to him as righteousness.
ROM.4.KJV: Comes this blessedness then on the circumcision only, or on the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness.
ROM.4.PLAIN: Is this blessing only on the circumcised, or also on the uncircumcised? We have been saying that Abraham’s faith was credited to him as righteousness.

ROM.4.BSB: In what context was it credited? Was it after his circumcision, or before? It was not after, but before.
ROM.4.KJV: How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.
ROM.4.PLAIN: In what context was it credited? Was it after his circumcision, or before? It was not after, but before.

ROM.4.BSB: And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. So then, he is the father of all who believe but are not circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them.
ROM.4.KJV: And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed to them also:
ROM.4.PLAIN: And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. So then, he is the father of all who believe but are not circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them.

ROM.4.BSB: And he is also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised, but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.
ROM.4.KJV: And the father of circumcision to them who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had being yet uncircumcised.
ROM.4.PLAIN: And he is also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised, but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.

ROM.4.BSB: For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not given through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.
ROM.4.KJV: For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.
ROM.4.PLAIN: For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not given through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.

ROM.4.BSB: For if those who live by the law are heirs, faith is useless and the promise is worthless,
ROM.4.KJV: For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect:
ROM.4.PLAIN: For if those who live by the law are heirs, faith is useless and the promise is worthless,

ROM.4.BSB: because the law brings wrath. And where there is no law, there is no transgression.
ROM.4.KJV: Because the law works wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression.
ROM.4.PLAIN: because the law brings wrath. And where there is no law, there is no transgression.

ROM.4.BSB: Therefore, the promise comes by faith, so that it may rest on grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring—not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham. He is the father of us all.
ROM.4.KJV: Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all,
ROM.4.PLAIN: Therefore, the promise comes by faith, so that it may rest on grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring—not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham. He is the father of us all.

ROM.4.BSB: As it is written: “I have made you a father of many nations.” He is our father in the presence of God, in whom he believed, the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not yet exist.
ROM.4.KJV: (As it is written, I have made you a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, even God, who vivifies the dead, and calls those things which be not as though they were.
ROM.4.PLAIN: As it is written: “I have made you a father of many nations.” He is our father in the presence of God, in whom he believed, the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not yet exist.

ROM.4.BSB: Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as he had been told, “So shall your offspring be.”
ROM.4.KJV: Who against hope believed in hope, that he might become the father of many nations, according to that which was spoken, So shall your seed be.
ROM.4.PLAIN: Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as he had been told, “So shall your offspring be.”

ROM.4.BSB: Without weakening in his faith, he acknowledged the decrepitness of his body (since he was about a hundred years old) and the lifelessness of Sarah’s womb.
ROM.4.KJV: And being not weak in faith, he considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Sarah’s womb:
ROM.4.PLAIN: Without weakening in his faith, he acknowledged the decrepitness of his body (since he was about a hundred years old) and the lifelessness of Sarah’s womb.

ROM.4.BSB: Yet he did not waver through disbelief in the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God,
ROM.4.KJV: He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God;
ROM.4.PLAIN: Yet he did not waver through disbelief in the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God,

ROM.4.BSB: being fully persuaded that God was able to do what He had promised.
ROM.4.KJV: And being fully persuaded that, what he had promised, he was able also to perform.
ROM.4.PLAIN: fully convinced that God was able to do what he had promised.

ROM.4.BSB: This is why “it was credited to him as righteousness.”
ROM.4.KJV: And therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness.
ROM.4.PLAIN: This is why “it was credited to him as righteousness.”

ROM.4.BSB: Now the words “it was credited to him” were written not only for Abraham,
ROM.4.KJV: Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him;
ROM.4.PLAIN: Now the words “it was credited to him” were written not only for Abraham,

ROM.4.BSB: but also for us, to whom righteousness will be credited—for us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
ROM.4.KJV: But for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead;
ROM.4.PLAIN: but also for us, to whom righteousness will be credited—for us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.

ROM.4.BSB: He was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification.
ROM.4.KJV: Who was delivered for our offenses, and was raised again for our justification.
ROM.4.PLAIN: He was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification.

ROM.5.BSB: Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
ROM.5.KJV: Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ:
ROM.5.PLAIN: So, since we've been made right by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.

ROM.5.BSB: through whom we have gained access by faith into this grace in which we stand. And we rejoice in the hope of the glory of God.
ROM.5.KJV: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.
ROM.5.PLAIN: through whom we have gained access by faith into this grace in which we stand. And we rejoice in the hope of the glory of God.

ROM.5.BSB: Not only that, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance;
ROM.5.KJV: And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation works patience;
ROM.5.PLAIN: And more than that, we can even take pride in our troubles, because we know that trouble produces endurance;

ROM.5.BSB: perseverance, character; and character, hope.
ROM.5.KJV: And patience, experience; and experience, hope:
ROM.5.PLAIN: perseverance, character; and character, hope.

ROM.5.BSB: And hope does not disappoint us, because God has poured out His love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, whom He has given us.
ROM.5.KJV: And hope makes not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given to us.
ROM.5.PLAIN: And this hope will not disappoint us, because God has poured his love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit he gave us.

ROM.5.BSB: For at just the right time, while we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly.
ROM.5.KJV: For when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly.
ROM.5.PLAIN: For at just the right time, while we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly.

ROM.5.BSB: Very rarely will anyone die for a righteous man, though for a good man someone might possibly dare to die.
ROM.5.KJV: For scarcely for a righteous man will one die: yet peradventure for a good man some would even dare to die.
ROM.5.PLAIN: Very rarely will anyone die for a righteous man, though for a good man someone might possibly dare to die.

ROM.5.BSB: But God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
ROM.5.KJV: But God commends his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
ROM.5.PLAIN: But God shows his love for us in this: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

ROM.5.BSB: Therefore, since we have now been justified by His blood, how much more shall we be saved from wrath through Him!
ROM.5.KJV: Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him.
ROM.5.PLAIN: Therefore, since we have now been justified by His blood, how much more shall we be saved from wrath through Him!

ROM.5.BSB: For if, when we were enemies of God, we were reconciled to Him through the death of His Son, how much more, having been reconciled, shall we be saved through His life!
ROM.5.KJV: For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.
ROM.5.PLAIN: For if, when we were enemies of God, we were reconciled to Him through the death of His Son, how much more, having been reconciled, shall we be saved through His life!

ROM.5.BSB: Not only that, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.
ROM.5.KJV: And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.
ROM.5.PLAIN: Not only that, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.

ROM.5.BSB: Therefore, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death was passed on to all men, because all sinned.
ROM.5.KJV: Why, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed on all men, for that all have sinned:
ROM.5.PLAIN: Therefore, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death was passed on to all men, because all sinned.

ROM.5.BSB: For sin was in the world before the law was given; but sin is not taken into account when there is no law.
ROM.5.KJV: (For until the law sin was in the world: but sin is not imputed when there is no law.
ROM.5.PLAIN: For sin was in the world before the law was given; but sin is not taken into account when there is no law.

ROM.5.BSB: Nevertheless, death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the way that Adam transgressed. He is a pattern of the One to come.
ROM.5.KJV: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam’s transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come.
ROM.5.PLAIN: Nevertheless, death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the way that Adam transgressed. He is a pattern of the One to come.

ROM.5.BSB: But the gift is not like the trespass. For if the many died by the trespass of the one man, how much more did God’s grace and the gift that came by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many!
ROM.5.KJV: But not as the offense, so also is the free gift. For if through the offense of one many be dead, much more the grace of God, and the gift by grace, which is by one man, Jesus Christ, has abounded to many.
ROM.5.PLAIN: But the gift is not like the trespass. For if the many died by the trespass of the one man, how much more did God’s grace and the gift that came by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many!

ROM.5.BSB: Again, the gift is not like the result of the one man’s sin: The judgment that followed one sin brought condemnation, but the gift that followed many trespasses brought justification.
ROM.5.KJV: And not as it was by one that sinned, so is the gift: for the judgment was by one to condemnation, but the free gift is of many offenses to justification.
ROM.5.PLAIN: Again, the gift is not like the result of the one man’s sin: The judgment that followed one sin brought condemnation, but the gift that followed many trespasses brought justification.

ROM.5.BSB: For if, by the trespass of the one man, death reigned through that one man, how much more will those who receive an abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!
ROM.5.KJV: For if by one man’s offense death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.)
ROM.5.PLAIN: For if, by the trespass of the one man, death reigned through that one man, how much more will those who receive an abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!

ROM.5.BSB: So then, just as one trespass brought condemnation for all men, so also one act of righteousness brought justification and life for all men.
ROM.5.KJV: Therefore as by the offense of one judgment came on all men to condemnation; even so by the righteousness of one the free gift came on all men to justification of life.
ROM.5.PLAIN: So then, just as one trespass brought condemnation for all men, so also one act of righteousness brought justification and life for all men.

ROM.5.BSB: For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.
ROM.5.KJV: For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.
ROM.5.PLAIN: For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.

ROM.5.BSB: The law came in so that the trespass would increase; but where sin increased, grace increased all the more,
ROM.5.KJV: Moreover the law entered, that the offense might abound. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound:
ROM.5.PLAIN: The law came in so that the trespass would increase; but where sin increased, grace increased all the more,

ROM.5.BSB: so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness to bring eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
ROM.5.KJV: That as sin has reigned to death, even so might grace reign through righteousness to eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.
ROM.5.PLAIN: so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness to bring eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

ROM.6.BSB: What then shall we say? Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?
ROM.6.KJV: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?
ROM.6.PLAIN: What then shall we say? Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?
