ROM.6.BSB: Certainly not! How can we who died to sin live in it any longer?
ROM.6.KJV: God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?
ROM.6.PLAIN: Certainly not! How can we who died to sin live in it any longer?

ROM.6.BSB: Or aren’t you aware that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?
ROM.6.KJV: Know you not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death?
ROM.6.PLAIN: Or aren’t you aware that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?

ROM.6.BSB: We were therefore buried with Him through baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may walk in newness of life.
ROM.6.KJV: Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.
ROM.6.PLAIN: So through baptism we were buried with him into death, so that just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too can live a brand-new life.

ROM.6.BSB: For if we have been united with Him like this in His death, we will certainly also be united with Him in His resurrection.
ROM.6.KJV: For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection:
ROM.6.PLAIN: For if we have been united with Him like this in His death, we will certainly also be united with Him in His resurrection.

ROM.6.BSB: We know that our old self was crucified with Him so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, that we should no longer be slaves to sin.
ROM.6.KJV: Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that from now on we should not serve sin.
ROM.6.PLAIN: We know that our old self was crucified with Him so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, that we should no longer be slaves to sin.

ROM.6.BSB: For anyone who has died has been freed from sin.
ROM.6.KJV: For he that is dead is freed from sin.
ROM.6.PLAIN: For anyone who has died has been freed from sin.

ROM.6.BSB: Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with Him.
ROM.6.KJV: Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him:
ROM.6.PLAIN: Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with Him.

ROM.6.BSB: For we know that since Christ was raised from the dead, He cannot die again; death no longer has dominion over Him.
ROM.6.KJV: Knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dies no more; death has no more dominion over him.
ROM.6.PLAIN: For we know that since Christ was raised from the dead, He cannot die again; death no longer has dominion over Him.

ROM.6.BSB: The death He died, He died to sin once for all; but the life He lives, He lives to God.
ROM.6.KJV: For in that he died, he died to sin once: but in that he lives, he lives to God.
ROM.6.PLAIN: The death He died, He died to sin once for all; but the life He lives, He lives to God.

ROM.6.BSB: So you too must count yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.
ROM.6.KJV: Likewise reckon you also yourselves to be dead indeed to sin, but alive to God through Jesus Christ our Lord.
ROM.6.PLAIN: In the same way, count yourselves dead to sin but alive to God through Christ Jesus.

ROM.6.BSB: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its desires.
ROM.6.KJV: Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that you should obey it in the lusts thereof.
ROM.6.PLAIN: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its desires.

ROM.6.BSB: Do not present the parts of your body to sin as instruments of wickedness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life; and present the parts of your body to Him as instruments of righteousness.
ROM.6.KJV: Neither yield you your members as instruments of unrighteousness to sin: but yield yourselves to God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness to God.
ROM.6.PLAIN: Do not present the parts of your body to sin as instruments of wickedness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life; and present the parts of your body to Him as instruments of righteousness.

ROM.6.BSB: For sin shall not be your master, because you are not under law, but under grace.
ROM.6.KJV: For sin shall not have dominion over you: for you are not under the law, but under grace.
ROM.6.PLAIN: For sin shall not be your master, because you are not under law, but under grace.

ROM.6.BSB: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? Certainly not!
ROM.6.KJV: What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.
ROM.6.PLAIN: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? Certainly not!

ROM.6.BSB: Do you not know that when you offer yourselves as obedient slaves, you are slaves to the one you obey, whether you are slaves to sin leading to death, or to obedience leading to righteousness?
ROM.6.KJV: Know you not, that to whom you yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants you are to whom you obey; whether of sin to death, or of obedience to righteousness?
ROM.6.PLAIN: Do you not know that when you offer yourselves as obedient slaves, you are slaves to the one you obey, whether you are slaves to sin leading to death, or to obedience leading to righteousness?

ROM.6.BSB: But thanks be to God that, though you once were slaves to sin, you wholeheartedly obeyed the form of teaching to which you were committed.
ROM.6.KJV: But God be thanked, that you were the servants of sin, but you have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you.
ROM.6.PLAIN: But thanks be to God that, though you once were slaves to sin, you wholeheartedly obeyed the form of teaching to which you were committed.

ROM.6.BSB: You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness.
ROM.6.KJV: Being then made free from sin, you became the servants of righteousness.
ROM.6.PLAIN: You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness.

ROM.6.BSB: I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity and to escalating wickedness, so now offer them in slavery to righteousness leading to holiness.
ROM.6.KJV: I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity of your flesh: for as you have yielded your members servants to uncleanness and to iniquity to iniquity; even so now yield your members servants to righteousness to holiness.
ROM.6.PLAIN: I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity and to escalating wickedness, so now offer them in slavery to righteousness leading to holiness.

ROM.6.BSB: For when you were slaves to sin, you were free of obligation to righteousness.
ROM.6.KJV: For when you were the servants of sin, you were free from righteousness.
ROM.6.PLAIN: For when you were slaves to sin, you were free of obligation to righteousness.

ROM.6.BSB: What fruit did you reap at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? The outcome of those things is death.
ROM.6.KJV: What fruit had you then in those things whereof you are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death.
ROM.6.PLAIN: What fruit did you reap at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? The outcome of those things is death.

ROM.6.BSB: But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves to God, the fruit you reap leads to holiness, and the outcome is eternal life.
ROM.6.KJV: But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, you have your fruit to holiness, and the end everlasting life.
ROM.6.PLAIN: But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves to God, the fruit you reap leads to holiness, and the outcome is eternal life.

ROM.6.BSB: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
ROM.6.KJV: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
ROM.6.PLAIN: For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

ROM.7.BSB: Do you not know, brothers (for I am speaking to those who know the law), that the law has authority over a man only as long as he lives?
ROM.7.KJV: Know you not, brothers, (for I speak to them that know the law,) how that the law has dominion over a man as long as he lives?
ROM.7.PLAIN: Do you not know, brothers (for I am speaking to those who know the law), that the law has authority over a man only as long as he lives?

ROM.7.BSB: For instance, a married woman is bound by law to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is released from the law of marriage.
ROM.7.KJV: For the woman which has an husband is bound by the law to her husband so long as he lives; but if the husband be dead, she is loosed from the law of her husband.
ROM.7.PLAIN: For instance, a married woman is bound by law to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is released from the law of marriage.

ROM.7.BSB: So then, if she is joined to another man while her husband is still alive, she is called an adulteress; but if her husband dies, she is free from that law and is not an adulteress, even if she marries another man.
ROM.7.KJV: So then if, while her husband lives, she be married to another man, she shall be called an adulteress: but if her husband be dead, she is free from that law; so that she is no adulteress, though she be married to another man.
ROM.7.PLAIN: So then, if she is joined to another man while her husband is still alive, she is called an adulteress; but if her husband dies, she is free from that law and is not an adulteress, even if she marries another man.

ROM.7.BSB: Therefore, my brothers, you also died to the law through the body of Christ, that you might belong to another, to Him who was raised from the dead, in order that we might bear fruit to God.
ROM.7.KJV: Why, my brothers, you also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ; that you should be married to another, even to him who is raised from the dead, that we should bring forth fruit to God.
ROM.7.PLAIN: Therefore, my brothers, you also died to the law through the body of Christ, that you might belong to another, to Him who was raised from the dead, in order that we might bear fruit to God.

ROM.7.BSB: For when we lived according to the flesh, the sinful passions aroused by the law were at work in our bodies, bearing fruit for death.
ROM.7.KJV: For when we were in the flesh, the motions of sins, which were by the law, did work in our members to bring forth fruit to death.
ROM.7.PLAIN: For when we lived according to the flesh, the sinful passions aroused by the law were at work in our bodies, bearing fruit for death.

ROM.7.BSB: But now, having died to what bound us, we have been released from the law, so that we serve in the new way of the Spirit, and not in the old way of the written code.
ROM.7.KJV: But now we are delivered from the law, that being dead wherein we were held; that we should serve in newness of spirit, and not in the oldness of the letter.
ROM.7.PLAIN: But now, having died to what bound us, we have been released from the law, so that we serve in the new way of the Spirit, and not in the old way of the written code.

ROM.7.BSB: What then shall we say? Is the law sin? Certainly not! Indeed, I would not have been mindful of sin if not for the law. For I would not have been aware of coveting if the law had not said, “Do not covet.”
ROM.7.KJV: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. No, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, You shall not covet.
ROM.7.PLAIN: What then shall we say? Is the law sin? Certainly not! Indeed, I would not have been mindful of sin if not for the law. For I would not have been aware of coveting if the law had not said, “Do not covet.”

ROM.7.BSB: But sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, produced in me every kind of covetous desire. For apart from the law, sin is dead.
ROM.7.KJV: But sin, taking occasion by the commandment, worked in me all manner of concupiscence. For without the law sin was dead.
ROM.7.PLAIN: But sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, produced in me every kind of covetous desire. For apart from the law, sin is dead.

ROM.7.BSB: Once I was alive apart from the law; but when the commandment came, sin sprang to life and I died.
ROM.7.KJV: For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died.
ROM.7.PLAIN: Once I was alive apart from the law; but when the commandment came, sin sprang to life and I died.

ROM.7.BSB: So I discovered that the very commandment that was meant to bring life actually brought death.
ROM.7.KJV: And the commandment, which was ordained to life, I found to be to death.
ROM.7.PLAIN: So I discovered that the very commandment that was meant to bring life actually brought death.

ROM.7.BSB: For sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through the commandment put me to death.
ROM.7.KJV: For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me.
ROM.7.PLAIN: For sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through the commandment put me to death.

ROM.7.BSB: So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.
ROM.7.KJV: Why the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.
ROM.7.PLAIN: So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.

ROM.7.BSB: Did that which is good, then, become death to me? Certainly not! But in order that sin might be exposed as sin, it produced death in me through what was good, so that through the commandment sin might become utterly sinful.
ROM.7.KJV: Was then that which is good made death to me? God forbid. But sin, that it might appear sin, working death in me by that which is good; that sin by the commandment might become exceeding sinful.
ROM.7.PLAIN: Did that which is good, then, become death to me? Certainly not! But in order that sin might be exposed as sin, it produced death in me through what was good, so that through the commandment sin might become utterly sinful.

ROM.7.BSB: We know that the law is spiritual; but I am unspiritual, sold as a slave to sin.
ROM.7.KJV: For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.
ROM.7.PLAIN: We know that the law is spiritual; but I am unspiritual, sold as a slave to sin.

ROM.7.BSB: I do not understand what I do. For what I want to do, I do not do. But what I hate, I do.
ROM.7.KJV: For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I.
ROM.7.PLAIN: I do not understand what I do. For what I want to do, I do not do. But what I hate, I do.

ROM.7.BSB: And if I do what I do not want to do, I admit that the law is good.

ROM.12.PLAIN: Do not let your zeal subside; keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.

ROM.12.BSB: Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.
ROM.12.KJV: Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer;
ROM.12.PLAIN: Be joyful in hope, patient in trouble, and faithful in prayer.

ROM.12.BSB: Share with the saints who are in need. Practice hospitality.
ROM.12.KJV: Distributing to the necessity of saints; given to hospitality.
ROM.12.PLAIN: Share with the saints who are in need. Practice hospitality.

ROM.12.BSB: Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.
ROM.12.KJV: Bless them which persecute you: bless, and curse not.
ROM.12.PLAIN: Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.

ROM.12.BSB: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
ROM.12.KJV: Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep.
ROM.12.PLAIN: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.

ROM.12.BSB: Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but enjoy the company of the lowly. Do not be conceited.
ROM.12.KJV: Be of the same mind one toward another. Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate. Be not wise in your own conceits.
ROM.12.PLAIN: Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but enjoy the company of the lowly. Do not be conceited.

ROM.12.BSB: Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.
ROM.12.KJV: Recompense to no man evil for evil. Provide things honest in the sight of all men.
ROM.12.PLAIN: Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.

ROM.12.BSB: If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.
ROM.12.KJV: If it be possible, as much as lies in you, live peaceably with all men.
ROM.12.PLAIN: If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.

ROM.12.BSB: Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath. For it is written: “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”
ROM.12.KJV: Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place to wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, says the Lord.
ROM.12.PLAIN: Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath. For it is written: “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”

ROM.12.BSB: On the contrary, “If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head.”
ROM.12.KJV: Therefore if your enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing you shall heap coals of fire on his head.
ROM.12.PLAIN: On the contrary, “If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head.”

ROM.12.BSB: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
ROM.12.KJV: Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.
ROM.12.PLAIN: Don't be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

ROM.13.BSB: Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.
ROM.13.KJV: Let every soul be subject to the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.
ROM.13.PLAIN: Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.

ROM.13.BSB: Consequently, whoever resists authority is opposing what God has set in place, and those who do so will bring judgment on themselves.
ROM.13.KJV: Whoever therefore resists the power, resists the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation.
ROM.13.PLAIN: Consequently, whoever resists authority is opposing what God has set in place, and those who do so will bring judgment on themselves.

ROM.13.BSB: For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Do you want to be unafraid of the one in authority? Then do what is right, and you will have his approval.
ROM.13.KJV: For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Will you then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and you shall have praise of the same:
ROM.13.PLAIN: For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Do you want to be unafraid of the one in authority? Then do what is right, and you will have his approval.

ROM.13.BSB: For he is God’s servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not carry the sword in vain. He is God’s servant, an agent of retribution to the wrongdoer.
ROM.13.KJV: For he is the minister of God to you for good. But if you do that which is evil, be afraid; for he bears not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath on him that does evil.
ROM.13.PLAIN: For he is God’s servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not carry the sword in vain. He is God’s servant, an agent of retribution to the wrongdoer.

ROM.13.BSB: Therefore it is necessary to submit to authority, not only to avoid punishment, but also as a matter of conscience.
ROM.13.KJV: Why you must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake.
ROM.13.PLAIN: Therefore it is necessary to submit to authority, not only to avoid punishment, but also as a matter of conscience.

ROM.13.BSB: This is also why you pay taxes. For the authorities are God’s servants, who devote themselves to their work.
ROM.13.KJV: For for this cause pay you tribute also: for they are God’s ministers, attending continually on this very thing.
ROM.13.PLAIN: This is also why you pay taxes. For the authorities are God’s servants, who devote themselves to their work.

ROM.13.BSB: Pay everyone what you owe him: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due.
ROM.13.KJV: Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honor to whom honor.
ROM.13.PLAIN: Pay everyone what you owe him: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due.

ROM.13.BSB: Be indebted to no one, except to one another in love. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.
ROM.13.KJV: Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loves another has fulfilled the law.
ROM.13.PLAIN: Don't owe anyone anything — except to love one another, for whoever loves others has fulfilled the law.

ROM.13.BSB: The commandments “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet,” and any other commandments, are summed up in this one decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
ROM.13.KJV: For this, You shall not commit adultery, You shall not kill, You shall not steal, You shall not bear false witness, You shall not covet; and if there be any other commandment, it is briefly comprehended in this saying, namely, You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
ROM.13.PLAIN: The commandments “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet,” and any other commandments, are summed up in this one decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”

ROM.13.BSB: Love does no wrong to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.
ROM.13.KJV: Love works no ill to his neighbor: therefore love is the fulfilling of the law.
ROM.13.PLAIN: Love does no harm to a neighbor; so love is the fulfilling of the law.

ROM.13.BSB: And do this, understanding the occasion. The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.
ROM.13.KJV: And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.
ROM.13.PLAIN: And do this, understanding the occasion. The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.

ROM.13.BSB: The night is nearly over; the day has drawn near. So let us lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.
ROM.13.KJV: The night is far spent, the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armor of light.
ROM.13.PLAIN: The night is nearly over; the day has drawn near. So let us lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.

ROM.13.BSB: Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.
ROM.13.KJV: Let us walk honestly, as in the day; not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness, not in strife and envying.
ROM.13.PLAIN: Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.

ROM.13.BSB: Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the desires of the flesh.
ROM.13.KJV: But put you on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfill the lusts thereof.
ROM.13.PLAIN: Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the desires of the flesh.

ROM.14.BSB: Accept him whose faith is weak, without passing judgment on his opinions.
ROM.14.KJV: Him that is weak in the faith receive you, but not to doubtful disputations.
ROM.14.PLAIN: Accept him whose faith is weak, without passing judgment on his opinions.

ROM.14.BSB: For one person has faith to eat all things, while another, who is weak, eats only vegetables.
ROM.14.KJV: For one believes that he may eat all things: another, who is weak, eats herbs.
ROM.14.PLAIN: For one person has faith to eat all things, while another, who is weak, eats only vegetables.

ROM.14.BSB: The one who eats everything must not belittle the one who does not, and the one who does not eat everything must not judge the one who does, for God has accepted him.
ROM.14.KJV: Let not him that eats despise him that eats not; and let not him which eats not judge him that eats: for God has received him.
ROM.14.PLAIN: The one who eats everything must not belittle the one who does not, and the one who does not eat everything must not judge the one who does, for God has accepted him.

ROM.14.BSB: Who are you to judge someone else’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. And he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.
ROM.14.KJV: Who are you that judge another man’s servant? to his own master he stands or falls. Yes, he shall be held up: for God is able to make him stand.
ROM.14.PLAIN: Who are you to judge someone else’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. And he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.

ROM.14.BSB: One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.
ROM.14.KJV: One man esteems one day above another: another esteems every day alike. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.
ROM.14.PLAIN: One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.

ROM.14.BSB: He who observes a special day does so to the Lord; he who eats does so to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and he who abstains does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God.
ROM.14.KJV: He that regards the day, regards it to the Lord; and he that regards not the day, to the Lord he does not regard it. He that eats, eats to the Lord, for he gives God thanks; and he that eats not, to the Lord he eats not, and gives God thanks.
ROM.14.PLAIN: He who observes a special day does so to the Lord; he who eats does so to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and he who abstains does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God.

ROM.14.BSB: For none of us lives to himself alone, and none of us dies to himself alone.
ROM.14.KJV: For none of us lives to himself, and no man dies to himself.
ROM.14.PLAIN: For none of us lives to himself alone, and none of us dies to himself alone.

ROM.14.BSB: If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord. So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
ROM.14.KJV: For whether we live, we live to the Lord; and whether we die, we die to the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord’s.
ROM.14.PLAIN: If we live, we live for the Lord; and if we die, we die for the Lord. So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.

ROM.14.BSB: For this reason Christ died and returned to life, that He might be the Lord of both the dead and the living.
ROM.14.KJV: For to this end Christ both died, and rose, and revived, that he might be Lord both of the dead and living.
ROM.14.PLAIN: For this reason Christ died and returned to life, that He might be the Lord of both the dead and the living.

ROM.14.BSB: Why, then, do you judge your brother? Or why do you belittle your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat.
ROM.14.KJV: But why do you judge your brother? or why do you set at nothing your brother? for we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.
ROM.14.PLAIN: Why, then, do you judge your brother? Or why do you belittle your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat.

ROM.14.BSB: It is written: “As surely as I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow before Me; every tongue will confess to God.”
ROM.14.KJV: For it is written, As I live, says the Lord, every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess to God.
ROM.14.PLAIN: It is written: “As surely as I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow before Me; every tongue will confess to God.”

ROM.14.BSB: So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God.
ROM.14.KJV: So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God.
ROM.14.PLAIN: So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God.

ROM.14.BSB: Therefore let us stop judging one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in your brother’s way.
ROM.14.KJV: Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge this rather, that no man put a stumbling block or an occasion to fall in his brother’s way.
ROM.14.PLAIN: Therefore let us stop judging one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in your brother’s way.

ROM.14.BSB: I am convinced and fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone regards something as unclean, then for him it is unclean.
ROM.14.KJV: I know, and am persuaded by the Lord Jesus, that there is nothing unclean of itself: but to him that esteems any thing to be unclean, to him it is unclean.
ROM.14.PLAIN: I am convinced and fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone regards something as unclean, then for him it is unclean.

ROM.14.BSB: If your brother is distressed by what you eat, you are no longer acting in love. Do not by your eating destroy your brother, for whom Christ died.
ROM.14.KJV: But if your brother be grieved with your meat, now walk you not charitably. Destroy not him with your meat, for whom Christ died.
ROM.14.PLAIN: If your brother is distressed by what you eat, you are no longer acting in love. Do not by your eating destroy your brother, for whom Christ died.

ROM.14.BSB: Do not allow what you consider good, then, to be spoken of as evil.
ROM.14.KJV: Let not then your good be evil spoken of:
ROM.14.PLAIN: Do not allow what you consider good, then, to be spoken of as evil.

ROM.14.BSB: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
ROM.14.KJV: For the kingdom of God is not meat and drink; but righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost.
ROM.14.PLAIN: For God's kingdom isn't about food and drink, but about righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

ROM.14.BSB: For whoever serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and approved by men.
ROM.14.KJV: For he that in these things serves Christ is acceptable to God, and approved of men.
ROM.14.PLAIN: For whoever serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and approved by men.

ROM.14.BSB: So then, let us pursue what leads to peace and to mutual edification.
ROM.14.KJV: Let us therefore follow after the things which make for peace, and things with which one may edify another.
ROM.14.PLAIN: So then, let us pursue what leads to peace and to mutual edification.

ROM.14.BSB: Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a man to let his eating be a stumbling block.
ROM.14.KJV: For meat destroy not the work of God. All things indeed are pure; but it is evil for that man who eats with offense.
ROM.14.PLAIN: Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a man to let his eating be a stumbling block.

ROM.14.BSB: It is better not to eat meat or drink wine or to do anything to cause your brother to stumble.
ROM.14.KJV: It is good neither to eat flesh, nor to drink wine, nor any thing whereby your brother stumbles, or is offended, or is made weak.
ROM.14.PLAIN: It is better not to eat meat or drink wine or to do anything to cause your brother to stumble.

ROM.14.BSB: Keep your belief about such matters between yourself and God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves.
ROM.14.KJV: Have you faith? have it to yourself before God. Happy is he that condemns not himself in that thing which he allows.
ROM.14.PLAIN: Keep your belief about such matters between yourself and God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves.

ROM.14.BSB: But the one who has doubts is condemned if he eats, because his eating is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.
ROM.14.KJV: And he that doubts is damned if he eat, because he eats not of faith: for whatever is not of faith is sin.
ROM.14.PLAIN: But the one who has doubts is condemned if he eats, because his eating is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.

ROM.15.BSB: We who are strong ought to bear with the shortcomings of the weak and not to please ourselves.
ROM.15.KJV: We then that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, and not to please ourselves.
ROM.15.PLAIN: We who are strong ought to bear with the shortcomings of the weak and not to please ourselves.

ROM.15.BSB: Each of us should please his neighbor for his good, to build him up.
ROM.15.KJV: Let every one of us please his neighbor for his good to edification.
ROM.15.PLAIN: Each of us should please his neighbor for his good, to build him up.

ROM.15.BSB: For even Christ did not please Himself, but as it is written: “The insults of those who insult You have fallen on Me.”
ROM.15.KJV: For even Christ pleased not himself; but, as it is written, The reproaches of them that reproached you fell on me.
ROM.15.PLAIN: For even Christ did not please Himself, but as it is written: “The insults of those who insult You have fallen on Me.”

ROM.15.BSB: For everything that was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope.
ROM.15.KJV: For whatever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.
ROM.15.PLAIN: For everything that was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope.

ROM.15.BSB: Now may the God who gives endurance and encouragement grant you harmony with one another in Christ Jesus,
ROM.15.KJV: Now the God of patience and consolation grant you to be like minded one toward another according to Christ Jesus:
ROM.15.PLAIN: Now may the God who gives endurance and encouragement grant you harmony with one another in Christ Jesus,

ROM.15.BSB: so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
ROM.15.KJV: That you may with one mind and one mouth glorify God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
ROM.15.PLAIN: so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

ROM.15.BSB: Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.
ROM.15.KJV: Why receive you one another, as Christ also received us to the glory of God.
ROM.15.PLAIN: Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.

ROM.15.BSB: For I tell you that Christ has become a servant of the circumcised on behalf of God’s truth, to confirm the promises made to the patriarchs,
ROM.15.KJV: Now I say that Jesus Christ was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of God, to confirm the promises made to the fathers:
ROM.15.PLAIN: For I tell you that Christ has become a servant of the circumcised on behalf of God’s truth, to confirm the promises made to the patriarchs,

ROM.15.BSB: so that the Gentiles may glorify God for His mercy. As it is written: “Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles; I will sing hymns to Your name.”
ROM.15.KJV: And that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy; as it is written, For this cause I will confess to you among the Gentiles, and sing to your name.
ROM.15.PLAIN: so that the Gentiles may glorify God for His mercy. As it is written: “Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles; I will sing hymns to Your name.”

ROM.15.BSB: Again, it says: “Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people.”
ROM.15.KJV: And again he says, Rejoice, you Gentiles, with his people.
ROM.15.PLAIN: Again, it says: “Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people.”

ROM.15.BSB: And again: “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and extol Him, all you peoples.”
ROM.15.KJV: And again, Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles; and laud him, all you people.
ROM.15.PLAIN: And again: “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and extol Him, all you peoples.”

ROM.15.BSB: And once more, Isaiah says: “The Root of Jesse will appear, One who will arise to rule over the Gentiles; in Him the Gentiles will put their hope.”
ROM.15.KJV: And again, Isaiah says, There shall be a root of Jesse, and he that shall rise to reign over the Gentiles; in him shall the Gentiles trust.
ROM.15.PLAIN: And once more, Isaiah says: “The Root of Jesse will appear, One who will arise to rule over the Gentiles; in Him the Gentiles will put their hope.”

ROM.15.BSB: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you believe in Him, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
ROM.15.KJV: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
ROM.15.PLAIN: May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you trust in him, so that you overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.

ROM.15.BSB: I myself am convinced, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, brimming with knowledge, and able to instruct one another.
ROM.15.KJV: And I myself also am persuaded of you, my brothers, that you also are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish one another.
ROM.15.PLAIN: I myself am convinced, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, brimming with knowledge, and able to instruct one another.

ROM.15.BSB: However, I have written you a bold reminder on some points, because of the grace God has given me
ROM.15.KJV: Nevertheless, brothers, I have written the more boldly to you in some sort, as putting you in mind, because of the grace that is given to me of God,
ROM.15.PLAIN: However, I have written you a bold reminder on some points, because of the grace God has given me

ROM.15.BSB: to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles in the priestly service of the gospel of God, so that the Gentiles might become an offering acceptable to God, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
ROM.15.KJV: That I should be the minister of Jesus Christ to the Gentiles, ministering the gospel of God, that the offering up of the Gentiles might be acceptable, being sanctified by the Holy Ghost.
ROM.15.PLAIN: to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles in the priestly service of the gospel of God, so that the Gentiles might become an offering acceptable to God, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

ROM.15.BSB: Therefore I exult in Christ Jesus in my service to God.
ROM.15.KJV: I have therefore whereof I may glory through Jesus Christ in those things which pertain to God.
ROM.15.PLAIN: Therefore I exult in Christ Jesus in my service to God.

ROM.15.BSB: I will not presume to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me in leading the Gentiles to obedience by word and deed,
ROM.15.KJV: For I will not dare to speak of any of those things which Christ has not worked by me, to make the Gentiles obedient, by word and deed,
ROM.15.PLAIN: I will not presume to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me in leading the Gentiles to obedience by word and deed,

ROM.15.BSB: by the power of signs and wonders, and by the power of the Spirit of God. So from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.
ROM.15.KJV: Through mighty signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit of God; so that from Jerusalem, and round about to Illyricum, I have fully preached the gospel of Christ.
ROM.15.PLAIN: by the power of signs and wonders, and by the power of the Spirit of God. So from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.

ROM.15.BSB: In this way I have aspired to preach the gospel where Christ was not known, so that I would not be building on someone else’s foundation.
ROM.15.KJV: Yes, so have I strived to preach the gospel, not where Christ was named, lest I should build on another man’s foundation:
ROM.15.PLAIN: In this way I have aspired to preach the gospel where Christ was not known, so that I would not be building on someone else’s foundation.

ROM.15.BSB: Rather, as it is written: “Those who were not told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”
ROM.15.KJV: But as it is written, To whom he was not spoken of, they shall see: and they that have not heard shall understand.
ROM.15.PLAIN: Rather, as it is written: “Those who were not told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”

ROM.15.BSB: That is why I have often been hindered from coming to you.
ROM.15.KJV: For which cause also I have been much hindered from coming to you.
ROM.15.PLAIN: That is why I have often been hindered from coming to you.

ROM.15.BSB: But now that there are no further opportunities for me in these regions, and since I have longed for many years to visit you,
ROM.15.KJV: But now having no more place in these parts, and having a great desire these many years to come to you;
ROM.15.PLAIN: But now that there are no further opportunities for me in these regions, and since I have longed for many years to visit you,

ROM.15.BSB: I hope to see you on my way to Spain. And after I have enjoyed your company for a while, you can equip me for my journey.
ROM.15.KJV: Whenever I take my journey into Spain, I will come to you: for I trust to see you in my journey, and to be brought on my way thitherward by you, if first I be somewhat filled with your company.
ROM.15.PLAIN: I hope to see you on my way to Spain. And after I have enjoyed your company for a while, you can equip me for my journey.

ROM.15.BSB: Now, however, I am on my way to Jerusalem to serve the saints there.
ROM.15.KJV: But now I go to Jerusalem to minister to the saints.
ROM.15.PLAIN: Now, however, I am on my way to Jerusalem to serve the saints there.

ROM.15.BSB: For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.
ROM.15.KJV: For it has pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor saints which are at Jerusalem.
ROM.15.PLAIN: For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.

ROM.15.BSB: They were pleased to do it, and indeed they owe it to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual blessings, they are obligated to minister to them with material blessings.
ROM.15.KJV: It has pleased them truly; and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister to them in carnal things.
ROM.15.PLAIN: They were pleased to do it, and indeed they owe it to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual blessings, they are obligated to minister to them with material blessings.

ROM.15.BSB: So after I have completed this service and have safely delivered this bounty to them, I will set off to Spain by way of you.
ROM.15.KJV: When therefore I have performed this, and have sealed to them this fruit, I will come by you into Spain.
ROM.15.PLAIN: So after I have completed this service and have safely delivered this bounty to them, I will set off to Spain by way of you.

ROM.15.BSB: I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.
ROM.15.KJV: And I am sure that, when I come to you, I shall come in the fullness of the blessing of the gospel of Christ.
ROM.15.PLAIN: I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.

ROM.15.BSB: Now I urge you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to join me in my struggle by praying to God for me.
ROM.15.KJV: Now I beseech you, brothers, for the Lord Jesus Christ’s sake, and for the love of the Spirit, that you strive together with me in your prayers to God for me;
ROM.15.PLAIN: Now I urge you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to join me in my struggle by praying to God for me.

ROM.15.BSB: Pray that I may be delivered from the unbelievers in Judea, and that my service in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints there,
ROM.15.KJV: That I may be delivered from them that do not believe in Judaea; and that my service which I have for Jerusalem may be accepted of the saints;
ROM.15.PLAIN: Pray that I may be delivered from the unbelievers in Judea, and that my service in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints there,

ROM.15.BSB: so that by God’s will I may come to you with joy and together with you be refreshed.
ROM.15.KJV: That I may come to you with joy by the will of God, and may with you be refreshed.
ROM.15.PLAIN: so that by God’s will I may come to you with joy and together with you be refreshed.

ROM.15.BSB: The God of peace be with all of you. Amen.
ROM.15.KJV: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
ROM.15.PLAIN: The God of peace be with all of you. Amen.

ROM.16.BSB: I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchrea.
ROM.16.KJV: I commend to you Phebe our sister, which is a servant of the church which is at Cenchrea:
ROM.16.PLAIN: I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchrea.

ROM.16.BSB: Welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her with anything she may need from you. For she has been a great help to many people, including me.
ROM.16.KJV: That you receive her in the Lord, as becomes saints, and that you assist her in whatever business she has need of you: for she has been a succorer of many, and of myself also.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her with anything she may need from you. For she has been a great help to many people, including me.

ROM.16.BSB: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
ROM.16.KJV: Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus:
ROM.16.PLAIN: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,

ROM.16.BSB: who have risked their lives for me. Not only I but all the churches of the Gentiles are grateful to them.
ROM.16.KJV: Who have for my life laid down their own necks: to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles.
ROM.16.PLAIN: who have risked their lives for me. Not only I but all the churches of the Gentiles are grateful to them.

ROM.16.BSB: Greet also the church that meets at their house. Greet my beloved Epenetus, who was the first convert to Christ in the province of Asia.
ROM.16.KJV: Likewise greet the church that is in their house. Salute my well-beloved Epaenetus, who is the first fruits of Achaia to Christ.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Greet also the church that meets at their house. Greet my beloved Epenetus, who was the first convert to Christ in the province of Asia.

ROM.16.BSB: Greet Mary, who has worked very hard for you.
ROM.16.KJV: Greet Mary, who bestowed much labor on us.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Greet Mary, who has worked very hard for you.

ROM.16.BSB: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my fellow countrymen and fellow prisoners. They are outstanding among the apostles, and they were in Christ before I was.
ROM.16.KJV: Salute Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen, and my fellow-prisoners, who are of note among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my fellow countrymen and fellow prisoners. They are outstanding among the apostles, and they were in Christ before I was.

ROM.16.BSB: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
ROM.16.KJV: Greet Amplias my beloved in the Lord.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.

ROM.16.BSB: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and my beloved Stachys.
ROM.16.KJV: Salute Urbane, our helper in Christ, and Stachys my beloved.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and my beloved Stachys.

ROM.16.BSB: Greet Apelles, who is approved in Christ. Greet those who belong to the household of Aristobulus.
ROM.16.KJV: Salute Apelles approved in Christ. Salute them which are of Aristobulus’ household.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Greet Apelles, who is approved in Christ. Greet those who belong to the household of Aristobulus.

ROM.16.BSB: Greet Herodion, my fellow countryman. Greet those from the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
ROM.16.KJV: Salute Herodion my kinsman. Greet them that be of the household of Narcissus, which are in the Lord.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Greet Herodion, my fellow countryman. Greet those from the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.

ROM.16.BSB: Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa, women who have worked hard in the Lord. Greet my beloved Persis, who has worked very hard in the Lord.
ROM.16.KJV: Salute Tryphena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Salute the beloved Persis, which labored much in the Lord.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa, women who have worked hard in the Lord. Greet my beloved Persis, who has worked very hard in the Lord.

ROM.16.BSB: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who has been a mother to me as well.
ROM.16.KJV: Salute Rufus chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who has been a mother to me as well.

ROM.16.BSB: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.
ROM.16.KJV: Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brothers which are with them.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.

ROM.16.BSB: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.
ROM.16.KJV: Salute Philologus, and Julia, Nereus, and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints which are with them.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.

ROM.16.BSB: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ send you greetings.
ROM.16.KJV: Salute one another with an holy kiss. The churches of Christ salute you.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ send you greetings.

ROM.16.BSB: Now I urge you, brothers, to watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles that are contrary to the teaching you have learned. Turn away from them.
ROM.16.KJV: Now I beseech you, brothers, mark them which cause divisions and offenses contrary to the doctrine which you have learned; and avoid them.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Now I urge you, brothers, to watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles that are contrary to the teaching you have learned. Turn away from them.

ROM.16.BSB: For such people are not serving our Lord Christ, but their own appetites. By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the naive.
ROM.16.KJV: For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.
ROM.16.PLAIN: For such people are not serving our Lord Christ, but their own appetites. By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the naive.

ROM.16.BSB: Everyone has heard about your obedience, so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.
ROM.16.KJV: For your obedience is come abroad to all men. I am glad therefore on your behalf: but yet I would have you wise to that which is good, and simple concerning evil.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Everyone has heard about your obedience, so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.

ROM.16.BSB: The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
ROM.16.KJV: And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
ROM.16.PLAIN: The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

ROM.16.BSB: Timothy, my fellow worker, sends you greetings, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my fellow countrymen.
ROM.16.KJV: Timotheus my workfellow, and Lucius, and Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen, salute you.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Timothy, my fellow worker, sends you greetings, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my fellow countrymen.

ROM.16.BSB: I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.
ROM.16.KJV: I Tertius, who wrote this letter, salute you in the Lord.
ROM.16.PLAIN: I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.

ROM.16.BSB: Gaius, who has hosted me and all the church, sends you greetings. Erastus, the city treasurer, sends you greetings, as does our brother Quartus.
ROM.16.KJV: Gaius my host, and of the whole church, salutes you. Erastus the chamberlain of the city salutes you, and Quartus a brother.
ROM.16.PLAIN: Gaius, who has hosted me and all the church, sends you greetings. Erastus, the city treasurer, sends you greetings, as does our brother Quartus.

ROM.16.KJV: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

ROM.16.BSB: Now to Him who is able to strengthen you by my gospel and by the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery concealed for ages past
ROM.16.KJV: Now to him that is of power to establish you according to my gospel, and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery, which was kept secret since the world began,
ROM.16.PLAIN: Now to Him who is able to strengthen you by my gospel and by the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery concealed for ages past

ROM.16.BSB: but now revealed and made known through the writings of the prophets by the command of the eternal God, in order to lead all nations to the obedience that comes from faith—
ROM.16.KJV: But now is made manifest, and by the scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the everlasting God, made known to all nations for the obedience of faith:
ROM.16.PLAIN: but now revealed and made known through the writings of the prophets by the command of the eternal God, in order to lead all nations to the obedience that comes from faith—

ROM.16.BSB: to the only wise God be glory forever through Jesus Christ! Amen.
ROM.16.KJV: To God only wise, be glory through Jesus Christ for ever. Amen.
ROM.16.PLAIN: to the only wise God be glory forever through Jesus Christ! Amen.

1CO.1.BSB: Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,
1CO.1.KJV: Paul called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother,
1CO.1.PLAIN: Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,

1CO.1.BSB: To the church of God in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be holy, together with all those everywhere who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:
1CO.1.KJV: To the church of God which is at Corinth, to them that are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, with all that in every place call on the name of Jesus Christ our Lord, both theirs and ours:
1CO.1.PLAIN: To the church of God in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be holy, together with all those everywhere who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:

1CO.1.BSB: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1CO.1.KJV: Grace be to you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
1CO.1.PLAIN: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

1CO.1.BSB: I always thank my God for you because of the grace He has given you in Christ Jesus.
1CO.1.KJV: I thank my God always on your behalf, for the grace of God which is given you by Jesus Christ;
1CO.1.PLAIN: I always thank my God for you because of the grace He has given you in Christ Jesus.

1CO.1.BSB: For in Him you have been enriched in every way, in all speech and all knowledge,
1CO.1.KJV: That in every thing you are enriched by him, in all utterance, and in all knowledge;
1CO.1.PLAIN: For in Him you have been enriched in every way, in all speech and all knowledge,

1CO.1.BSB: because our testimony about Christ was confirmed in you.
1CO.1.KJV: Even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you:
1CO.1.PLAIN: because our testimony about Christ was confirmed in you.

1CO.1.BSB: Therefore you do not lack any spiritual gift as you eagerly await the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ.
1CO.1.KJV: So that you come behind in no gift; waiting for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ:
1CO.1.PLAIN: Therefore you do not lack any spiritual gift as you eagerly await the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ.

1CO.1.BSB: He will sustain you to the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
1CO.1.KJV: Who shall also confirm you to the end, that you may be blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
1CO.1.PLAIN: He will sustain you to the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

1CO.1.BSB: God, who has called you into fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ our Lord, is faithful.
1CO.1.KJV: God is faithful, by whom you were called to the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord.
1CO.1.PLAIN: God, who has called you into fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ our Lord, is faithful.

1CO.1.BSB: I appeal to you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree together, so that there may be no divisions among you and that you may be united in mind and conviction.
1CO.1.KJV: Now I beseech you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that you be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.
1CO.1.PLAIN: I appeal to you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree together, so that there may be no divisions among you and that you may be united in mind and conviction.

1CO.1.BSB: My brothers, some from Chloe’s household have informed me that there are quarrels among you.
1CO.1.KJV: For it has been declared to me of you, my brothers, by them which are of the house of Chloe, that there are contentions among you.
1CO.1.PLAIN: My brothers, some from Chloe’s household have informed me that there are quarrels among you.

1CO.1.BSB: What I mean is this: Individuals among you are saying, “I follow Paul,” “I follow Apollos,” “I follow Cephas,” or “I follow Christ.”
1CO.1.KJV: Now this I say, that every one of you says, I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas; and I of Christ.
1CO.1.PLAIN: What I mean is this: Individuals among you are saying, “I follow Paul,” “I follow Apollos,” “I follow Cephas,” or “I follow Christ.”

1CO.1.BSB: Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Were you baptized into the name of Paul?
1CO.1.KJV: Is Christ divided? was Paul crucified for you? or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
1CO.1.PLAIN: Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Were you baptized into the name of Paul?

1CO.1.BSB: I thank God that I did not baptize any of you except Crispus and Gaius,
1CO.1.KJV: I thank God that I baptized none of you, but Crispus and Gaius;
1CO.1.PLAIN: I thank God that I did not baptize any of you except Crispus and Gaius,

1CO.1.BSB: so no one can say that you were baptized into my name.
1CO.1.KJV: Lest any should say that I had baptized in my own name.
1CO.1.PLAIN: so no one can say that you were baptized into my name.

1CO.1.BSB: Yes, I also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that I do not remember if I baptized anyone else.
1CO.1.KJV: And I baptized also the household of Stephanas: besides, I know not whether I baptized any other.
1CO.1.PLAIN: Yes, I also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that I do not remember if I baptized anyone else.

1CO.1.BSB: For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel, not with words of wisdom, lest the cross of Christ be emptied of its power.
1CO.1.KJV: For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the gospel: not with wisdom of words, lest the cross of Christ should be made of none effect.
1CO.1.PLAIN: For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel, not with words of wisdom, lest the cross of Christ be emptied of its power.

1CO.1.BSB: For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
1CO.1.KJV: For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but to us which are saved it is the power of God.
1CO.1.PLAIN: The message of the cross sounds foolish to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it's the power of God.

1CO.1.BSB: For it is written: “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise; the intelligence of the intelligent I will frustrate.”
1CO.1.KJV: For it is written, I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent.
1CO.1.PLAIN: For it is written: “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise; the intelligence of the intelligent I will frustrate.”

1CO.1.BSB: Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the philosopher of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?
1CO.1.KJV: Where is the wise? where is the scribe? where is the disputer of this world? has not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?
1CO.1.PLAIN: Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the philosopher of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?

1CO.1.BSB: For since in the wisdom of God the world through its wisdom did not know Him, God was pleased through the foolishness of what was preached to save those who believe.
1CO.1.KJV: For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.
1CO.1.PLAIN: For since in the wisdom of God the world through its wisdom did not know Him, God was pleased through the foolishness of what was preached to save those who believe.

1CO.1.BSB: Jews demand signs and Greeks search for wisdom,
1CO.1.KJV: For the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom:
1CO.1.PLAIN: Jews demand signs and Greeks search for wisdom,

1CO.1.BSB: but we preach Christ crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles,
1CO.1.KJV: But we preach Christ crucified, to the Jews a stumbling block, and to the Greeks foolishness;
1CO.1.PLAIN: but we preach Christ crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles,

1CO.1.BSB: but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.
1CO.1.KJV: But to them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.
1CO.1.PLAIN: but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.

1CO.1.BSB: For the foolishness of God is wiser than man’s wisdom, and the weakness of God is stronger than man’s strength.
1CO.1.KJV: Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men; and the weakness of God is stronger than men.
1CO.1.PLAIN: For the foolishness of God is wiser than man’s wisdom, and the weakness of God is stronger than man’s strength.

1CO.1.BSB: Brothers, consider the time of your calling: Not many of you were wise by human standards; not many were powerful; not many were of noble birth.
1CO.1.KJV: For you see your calling, brothers, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called:
1CO.1.PLAIN: Brothers, consider the time of your calling: Not many of you were wise by human standards; not many were powerful; not many were of noble birth.

1CO.1.BSB: But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.
1CO.1.KJV: But God has chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God has chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty;
1CO.1.PLAIN: But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise, and the weak things of the world to shame the strong.

1CO.1.BSB: He chose the lowly and despised things of the world, and the things that are not, to nullify the things that are,
1CO.1.KJV: And base things of the world, and things which are despised, has God chosen, yes, and things which are not, to bring to nothing things that are:
1CO.1.PLAIN: He chose the lowly and despised things of the world, and the things that are not, to nullify the things that are,

1CO.1.BSB: so that no one may boast in His presence.
1CO.1.KJV: That no flesh should glory in his presence.
1CO.1.PLAIN: so that no one may boast in His presence.

1CO.1.BSB: It is because of Him that you are in Christ Jesus, who has become for us wisdom from God: our righteousness, holiness, and redemption.
1CO.1.KJV: But of him are you in Christ Jesus, who of God is made to us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption:
1CO.1.PLAIN: It is because of Him that you are in Christ Jesus, who has become for us wisdom from God: our righteousness, holiness, and redemption.

1CO.1.BSB: Therefore, as it is written: “Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.”
1CO.1.KJV: That, according as it is written, He that glories, let him glory in the Lord.
1CO.1.PLAIN: so that, as it's written, 'Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.'

1CO.2.BSB: When I came to you, brothers, I did not come with eloquence or wisdom as I proclaimed to you the testimony about God.
1CO.2.KJV: And I, brothers, when I came to you, came not with excellency of speech or of wisdom, declaring to you the testimony of God.
1CO.2.PLAIN: When I came to you, brothers, I did not come with eloquence or wisdom as I proclaimed to you the testimony about God.

1CO.2.BSB: For I resolved to know nothing while I was with you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified.
1CO.2.KJV: For I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
1CO.2.PLAIN: For I made up my mind to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ and him crucified.

1CO.2.BSB: I came to you in weakness and fear, and with much trembling.
1CO.2.KJV: And I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling.
1CO.2.PLAIN: I came to you in weakness and fear, and with much trembling.

1CO.2.BSB: My message and my preaching were not with persuasive words of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit’s power,
1CO.2.KJV: And my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man’s wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power:
1CO.2.PLAIN: My message and my preaching were not with persuasive words of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit’s power,

1CO.2.BSB: so that your faith would not rest on men’s wisdom, but on God’s power.
1CO.2.KJV: That your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.
1CO.2.PLAIN: so that your faith would not rest on men’s wisdom, but on God’s power.

1CO.2.BSB: Among the mature, however, we speak a message of wisdom—but not the wisdom of this age or of the rulers of this age, who are coming to nothing.
1CO.2.KJV: However, we speak wisdom among them that are perfect: yet not the wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world, that come to nothing:
1CO.2.PLAIN: Among the mature, however, we speak a message of wisdom—but not the wisdom of this age or of the rulers of this age, who are coming to nothing.

1CO.2.BSB: No, we speak of the mysterious and hidden wisdom of God, which He destined for our glory before time began.
1CO.2.KJV: But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom, which God ordained before the world to our glory:
1CO.2.PLAIN: No, we speak of the mysterious and hidden wisdom of God, which He destined for our glory before time began.

1CO.2.BSB: None of the rulers of this age understood it. For if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
1CO.2.KJV: Which none of the princes of this world knew: for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
1CO.2.PLAIN: None of the rulers of this age understood it. For if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

1CO.2.BSB: Rather, as it is written: “No eye has seen, no ear has heard, no heart has imagined, what God has prepared for those who love Him.”
1CO.2.KJV: But as it is written, Eye has not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God has prepared for them that love him.
1CO.2.PLAIN: But as it's written: 'No eye has seen, no ear has heard, no mind has imagined the things God has prepared for those who love him.'

1CO.2.BSB: But God has revealed it to us by the Spirit. The Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God.
1CO.2.KJV: But God has revealed them to us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searches all things, yes, the deep things of God.
1CO.2.PLAIN: But God has revealed it to us by the Spirit. The Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God.

1CO.2.BSB: For who among men knows the thoughts of man except his own spirit within him? So too, no one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.
1CO.2.KJV: For what man knows the things of a man, save the spirit of man which is in him? even so the things of God knows no man, but the Spirit of God.
1CO.2.PLAIN: For who among men knows the thoughts of man except his own spirit within him? So too, no one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.

1CO.2.BSB: We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, that we may understand what God has freely given us.
1CO.2.KJV: Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God; that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God.
1CO.2.PLAIN: We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, that we may understand what God has freely given us.

1CO.2.BSB: And this is what we speak, not in words taught us by human wisdom, but in words taught by the Spirit, expressing spiritual truths in spiritual words.
1CO.2.KJV: Which things also we speak, not in the words which man’s wisdom teaches, but which the Holy Ghost teaches; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.
1CO.2.PLAIN: And this is what we speak, not in words taught us by human wisdom, but in words taught by the Spirit, expressing spiritual truths in spiritual words.

1CO.2.BSB: The natural man does not accept the things that come from the Spirit of God. For they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are spiritually discerned.
1CO.2.KJV: But the natural man receives not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness to him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.
1CO.2.PLAIN: The natural man does not accept the things that come from the Spirit of God. For they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are spiritually discerned.

1CO.2.BSB: The spiritual man judges all things, but he himself is not subject to anyone’s judgment.
1CO.2.KJV: But he that is spiritual judges all things, yet he himself is judged of no man.
1CO.2.PLAIN: The spiritual man judges all things, but he himself is not subject to anyone’s judgment.

1CO.2.BSB: “For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct Him?” But we have the mind of Christ.
1CO.2.KJV: For who has known the mind of the Lord, that he may instruct him? But we have the mind of Christ.
1CO.2.PLAIN: “For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct Him?” But we have the mind of Christ.

1CO.3.BSB: Brothers, I could not address you as spiritual, but as worldly—as infants in Christ.
1CO.3.KJV: And I, brothers, could not speak to you as to spiritual, but as to carnal, even as to babes in Christ.
1CO.3.PLAIN: Brothers, I could not address you as spiritual, but as worldly—as infants in Christ.

1CO.3.BSB: I gave you milk, not solid food, for you were not yet ready for solid food. In fact, you are still not ready,
1CO.3.KJV: I have fed you with milk, and not with meat: for till now you were not able to bear it, neither yet now are you able.
1CO.3.PLAIN: I gave you milk, not solid food, for you were not yet ready for solid food. In fact, you are still not ready,

1CO.3.BSB: for you are still worldly. For since there is jealousy and dissension among you, are you not worldly? Are you not walking in the way of man?
1CO.3.KJV: For you are yet carnal: for whereas there is among you envying, and strife, and divisions, are you not carnal, and walk as men?
1CO.3.PLAIN: for you are still worldly. For since there is jealousy and dissension among you, are you not worldly? Are you not walking in the way of man?

1CO.3.BSB: For when one of you says, “I follow Paul,” and another, “I follow Apollos,” are you not mere men?
1CO.3.KJV: For while one says, I am of Paul; and another, I am of Apollos; are you not carnal?
1CO.3.PLAIN: For when one of you says, “I follow Paul,” and another, “I follow Apollos,” are you not mere men?

1CO.3.BSB: What then is Apollos? And what is Paul? They are servants through whom you believed, as the Lord has assigned to each his role.
1CO.3.KJV: Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers by whom you believed, even as the Lord gave to every man?
1CO.3.PLAIN: What then is Apollos? And what is Paul? They are servants through whom you believed, as the Lord has assigned to each his role.

1CO.3.BSB: I planted the seed and Apollos watered it, but God made it grow.
1CO.3.KJV: I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.
1CO.3.PLAIN: I planted the seed and Apollos watered it, but God made it grow.

1CO.3.BSB: So neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but only God, who makes things grow.
1CO.3.KJV: So then neither is he that plants any thing, neither he that waters; but God that gives the increase.
1CO.3.PLAIN: So neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but only God, who makes things grow.

1CO.3.BSB: He who plants and he who waters are one in purpose, and each will be rewarded according to his own labor.
1CO.3.KJV: Now he that plants and he that waters are one: and every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labor.
1CO.3.PLAIN: He who plants and he who waters are one in purpose, and each will be rewarded according to his own labor.

1CO.3.BSB: For we are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s field, God’s building.
1CO.3.KJV: For we are laborers together with God: you are God’s husbandry, you are God’s building.
1CO.3.PLAIN: For we are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s field, God’s building.

1CO.3.BSB: By the grace God has given me, I laid a foundation as an expert builder, and someone else is building on it. But each one must be careful how he builds.
1CO.3.KJV: According to the grace of God which is given to me, as a wise master builder, I have laid the foundation, and another builds thereon. But let every man take heed how he builds thereupon.
1CO.3.PLAIN: By the grace God has given me, I laid a foundation as an expert builder, and someone else is building on it. But each one must be careful how he builds.

1CO.3.BSB: For no one can lay a foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
1CO.3.KJV: For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.
1CO.3.PLAIN: For no one can lay any foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.

1CO.3.BSB: If anyone builds on this foundation using gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw,
1CO.3.KJV: Now if any man build on this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble;
1CO.3.PLAIN: If anyone builds on this foundation using gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw,

1CO.3.BSB: his workmanship will be evident, because the Day will bring it to light. It will be revealed with fire, and the fire will prove the quality of each man’s work.
1CO.3.KJV: Every man’s work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man’s work of what sort it is.
1CO.3.PLAIN: his workmanship will be evident, because the Day will bring it to light. It will be revealed with fire, and the fire will prove the quality of each man’s work.

1CO.3.BSB: If what he has built survives, he will receive a reward.
1CO.3.KJV: If any man’s work abide which he has built thereupon, he shall receive a reward.
1CO.3.PLAIN: If what he has built survives, he will receive a reward.

1CO.3.BSB: If it is burned up, he will suffer loss. He himself will be saved, but only as if through the flames.
1CO.3.KJV: If any man’s work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.
1CO.3.PLAIN: If it is burned up, he will suffer loss. He himself will be saved, but only as if through the flames.

1CO.3.BSB: Do you not know that you yourselves are God’s temple, and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?
1CO.3.KJV: Know you not that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?
1CO.3.PLAIN: Don't you know that you are God's temple, and that God's Spirit lives in you?

1CO.3.BSB: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for God’s temple is holy, and you are that temple.
1CO.3.KJV: If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple you are.
1CO.3.PLAIN: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for God’s temple is holy, and you are that temple.

1CO.3.BSB: Let no one deceive himself. If any of you thinks he is wise in this age, he should become a fool, so that he may become wise.
1CO.3.KJV: Let no man deceive himself. If any man among you seems to be wise in this world, let him become a fool, that he may be wise.
1CO.3.PLAIN: Let no one deceive himself. If any of you thinks he is wise in this age, he should become a fool, so that he may become wise.

1CO.3.BSB: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness in God’s sight. As it is written: “He catches the wise in their craftiness.”
1CO.3.KJV: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, He takes the wise in their own craftiness.
1CO.3.PLAIN: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness in God’s sight. As it is written: “He catches the wise in their craftiness.”

1CO.3.BSB: And again, “The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are futile.”
1CO.3.KJV: And again, The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are vain.
1CO.3.PLAIN: And again, “The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are futile.”

1CO.3.BSB: Therefore, stop boasting in men. All things are yours,
1CO.3.KJV: Therefore let no man glory in men. For all things are yours;
